12688.s: This order directs the Secretary of Defense to transfer excess property within or next to Choctawhatchee National Forest, Florida, to the Secretary of Agriculture for national forest use. It applies only to property that is no longer needed for military purposes. The Secretary of Defense must document each transfer and notify the Secretary of the Interior 30 days before the land is opened to relevant land laws.

12687.s: This order creates the President's Education Policy Advisory Committee. The committee is made up of members appointed by the President and is led by a chairman chosen from among those members. It advises the President on education policy and may review and assess education policy and report when asked. Executive agencies must provide information on education policy matters to the committee when allowed by law.

12686.s: This order creates a presidential commission to review and evaluate aviation security policy options, with special attention to the destruction of Pan American World Airways Flight 103. The commission is also directed to study ways to prevent terrorist acts involving aviation, review how to handle terrorist threats, and look at laws and policies on treatment of families of victims. It must report to the President within 6 months and then end 30 days after the report is submitted.

12685.s: This order lets certain federal employees who work as readers, interpreters, or personal assistants for a handicapped employee be moved into a career or career-conditional job without competition. It applies when their current job is no longer needed, if their agency recommends them, and if they have at least 1 year of satisfactory service in that position under a non-temporary appointment.

12684.s: This order changes how the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability System is administered to match certain changes in the Civil Service Retirement and Disability System. It sets rules for figuring annuities for employees with part-time service and says some part-time service must be counted using the full-time basic pay rate. It also changes the remarriage age for certain surviving spouse annuity rules from 60 to 55, and makes the part-time service rule apply retroactively to April 7, 1986.

12683.s: The order changes how travel time is counted as active duty for members of the uniformed services called to active duty. It applies to travel from home to the first duty station and from the last duty station back home. The travel time must match the allowable time for the approved mode of travel, and it must be figured using uniform regulations and official mileage tables.

12682.s: This order creates a commission to look at other uses for military facilities that are underused or no longer needed by the Department of Defense. The commission must review those facilities and report on ones that could be used as minimum security facilities for nonviolent prisoners, drug treatment facilities for nonviolent drug abusers, or facilities to assist the homeless. The Secretary of Defense must also send the commission lists of active and inactive military facilities that meet those conditions.

12681.s: This order excludes certain subdivisions of the National Preparedness Directorate of the Federal Emergency Management Agency from the federal labor-management relations program. It says these offices have a primary function in intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work. The excluded offices include parts of the Office of Associate Director, the Office of Analysis and Support, the Office of Mobilization Preparedness, the Office of Systems Engineering, the Office of Operations, and the Office of Information Resource Management.

12680.s: This order changes how certain foreign assistance and arms export control duties are assigned within the executive branch. It gives specific functions under several laws and prior executive orders to the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense, the Administrator of the Agency for International Development, and the Chairman of the Export-Import Bank. Some of those duties must be carried out in consultation with other officials, including the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of State.

12679.s: This order adds the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force to level IV of the Executive Schedule. It affects that federal position by placing it in that pay level.

12678.s: This order changes level IV of the Executive Schedule. It adds the Comptroller of the Department of Defense and removes several obsolete positions from the schedule. These changes affect the listed executive positions in the federal government.

12677.s: This order directs the Department of Education to set up a President’s Board of Advisors on Historically Black Colleges and Universities. It also requires federal departments and agencies to make annual plans, reports, and reviews to increase these schools’ participation in federally sponsored programs. The order calls for advice on private sector help, stronger financial management, and better opportunities for students and graduates.

12675.s: This order establishes the National Space Council to help develop and monitor national space policy and strategy. The Council includes the Vice President and several Cabinet and other senior officials, and it advises the President on space policy and related issues. It also creates a private citizens advisory board for the Vice President and requires federal agencies involved in space policy to cooperate with the Council.

12676.s: This order gives the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, working with the Secretary of State, the power to decide how much unobligated money is transferred to the Agency for International Development and which accounts receive it. It also lets the Secretary of Defense, working with the Agency for International Development, transfer and designate unobligated funds from specified accounts. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget may also approve detailing personnel to the Agency for International Development, and Executive Order 12654 is revoked.

12674.s: This order sets ethics rules for executive branch employees. It says they must avoid conflicts of interest, not take improper gifts, not use public office for private gain, and report waste, fraud, abuse, and corruption. It also limits outside earned income for certain full-time presidential appointees, gives the Office of Government Ethics and agency heads duties to issue and enforce ethics rules, and revokes two earlier executive orders.

12673.s: This order delegates many disaster relief and emergency assistance duties to the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency. It leaves certain presidential functions in place, including declaring major disasters and emergencies, declaring emergencies, repairing or replacing Federal facilities, and food coupon and distribution functions. It also delegates some report and other functions from the 1988 disaster relief amendments to the same agency director.

12672.s: This order changes a prior executive order about the Interagency Committee on Handicapped Employees. It adds the Postmaster General of the United States Postal Service, the Chairman of the President's Committee on Employment of People with Disabilities, and any other members the President may designate.

12671.s: This order amends a prior executive order to list the Office of Enforcement, including its headquarters and regional components, in the U.S. Customs Service. It does this because the President found that office's main work includes intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work, and that the labor-management rules in Chapter 71 of Title 5 cannot be applied to it consistently with national security requirements.

12670.s: This order extends the time period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1990. It says that ending this cooperation would be seriously harmful to U.S. non-proliferation goals and could jeopardize the common defense and security of the United States. The order also says Congress was notified of this decision.

12669.s: This order designates the Organization of Eastern Caribbean States as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities covered by that law, and says it does not limit any other rights it may have from international agreements or congressional action.

12668.s: The order creates the President's Commission on Federal Ethics Law Reform, with up to eight members appointed by the President. The commission is to review federal ethics laws, executive orders, and policies and make recommendations for reforms to the President. It must report to the President and give a copy to the Attorney General, and it ends 30 days after its report unless extended.

12666.s: This order adds certain Federal Aviation Administration units to an exclusion from the federal labor-management relations program. It applies to the Federal Air Marshal Branch and to units of Civil Aviation Security Inspectors whose jobs require Federal air marshal functions.

12667.s: This order sets rules for how the National Archives and Records Administration may release Presidential records. It requires notice to the incumbent President and the former President before disclosure, and it gives them a chance to raise a claim of Executive privilege. If Executive privilege is claimed, the Archivist must consult with the Attorney General and the Counsel to the President before deciding whether to disclose the records, unless a final court order says otherwise.

12665.s: This order changes Executive Order 12658 by increasing the President's Commission on Catastrophic Nuclear Accidents from nine members to eleven members. It affects the commission's membership number only.

12664.s: This order establishes a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and certain employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers. The parties must submit final offers for settlement within 30 days after the board is created. The board must then report to the President on the most reasonable offer, and the conditions tied to the dispute cannot change except by agreement during the period stated in the order.

12662.s: The order directs agencies to give notice of certain proposed federal standards-related measures or product approval procedures at least 75 days before the comment due date, except in urgent circumstances. It also establishes a United States Secretariat in the Department of Commerce to help carry out Chapters 18 and 19 of the Free-Trade Agreement and support binational panels and extraordinary challenge committees. The order says the President accepts all decisions of those panels and committees if certain Tariff Act provisions take effect.

12660.s: This order creates the National Microgravity Research Board. The Board is made up of leaders from several federal agencies and is chaired by the NASA Administrator. It is to consult with academia, private industry, and other federal agencies, and it will advise on microgravity research priorities, policy, coordination, and international programs.

12659.s: This order gives the Secretary of Energy the President’s functions under two sections of federal law about the Naval Petroleum and Oil Shale Reserves. It also requires the Secretary of Energy to send the President a full report on the agreements and programs made under this order by June 30, 1991. The delegated authority ends after October 1, 1991.

12661.s: This order delegates several trade and tariff functions to the United States Trade Representative, including matters on state trading regimes, wine trade barriers, steel imports, telecommunications trade, and a uniform fee on imports. It also establishes an Interagency Group on Countertrade and directs U.S. agencies to follow procurement and import sanctions against Toshiba Machine Company, Toshiba Corporation, Kongsberg Trading Company, and Kongsberg Vaapenfabrikk, with listed exceptions. The order also changes how certain mergers, acquisitions, and takeovers are reviewed under the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States and requires reports on semiconductors, fiber optics, superconducting materials, and a National Commission on Superconductivity.

12658.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Catastrophic Nuclear Accidents and names nine members appointed by the President. The commission must study how to fully compensate victims of a catastrophic nuclear accident and make recommendations on liability rules, claim procedures, and handling claims if money is limited. It may ask executive agencies for information and support, and some agencies are directed to help if allowed by law. The commission must submit its final report to Congress and then end two months later.

12657.s: This order tells FEMA to help plan for radiological emergencies at commercial nuclear power plants when state or local governments do not prepare enough or do not take part enough. FEMA may give advice, technical help, and other support for emergency planning, and it may work with the licensee and other federal agencies. It also covers evaluating plans, helping with emergency response, and coordinating public warning, evacuation, shelters, medical services, and communication.

12656.s: This order assigns federal departments and agencies responsibilities for national security emergency preparedness. It says they must plan for continuity of government, emergency operations, resource management, protection of essential facilities, and coordination with state and local governments and the private sector when appropriate. It also gives the National Security Council a central role in policy, and it gives the Secretary of Agriculture duties for agricultural production, food distribution, and related planning in national security emergencies.

12655.s: This order sets up a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and some of its employees represented by the Transportation Communications Union-Carmen Division. The parties must submit final settlement offers to the board, and the board must send the President a report choosing the most reasonable offer. Until 60 days after the board reports, the parties may not change the conditions tied to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

12653.s: This order changes the rules for White House Fellowships. It lets the Commission set the fellowship length, as long as it does not exceed 365 days, and it allows extensions of up to 90 days. The change applies to Fellows with appointments starting on or after September 1, 1987.

12654.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense authority to transfer unobligated funds and set the amounts of those funds for use under the Act. It also gives the Director of the Office of Management and Budget authority to approve detailing personnel to the Agency for International Development.

12652.s: This order returns the administration of the Federal Employees' Compensation Act for Panama Canal Commission employees from the Panama Canal Commission to the Secretary of Labor. It rescinds a section of an earlier executive order and related transfer authorities. The order takes effect on January 1, 1989.

12651.s:
This order gives the Permanent Observer Mission of the Delegation of the Commission of the European Communities to the United Nations the same privileges and immunities as permanent observer missions of states. It also gives similar privileges and immunities to certain diplomatic staff in New York and to their families.

The order extends comparable privileges and immunities to the West Coast Office in San Francisco and to certain officers, employees, and their families. It also extends similar privileges and immunities to certain administrative, technical, and service staff in Washington and to their families.

12650.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and certain employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days after it is created. For 120 days after the board is created, the carrier and the employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute unless both sides agree.

12649.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about reporting on the effects of offsets in international trade. It authorizes the Bureau of Economic Analysis in the Department of Commerce to collect information for a database used to prepare reports to Congress, and says the information should have confidentiality protections.

12647.s: This order designates the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. That gives the agency the privileges, exemptions, and immunities covered by that law. It also amends an earlier executive order to add the agency to listed sections.

12648.s: The order designates the Department of State as the United States Central Authority for the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction. It authorizes the Secretary of State to carry out the lawful acts needed to perform those functions. This affects the federal government’s work under the convention.

12646.s: This order sets up a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and some employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days after it is created. For 120 days after the board is created, neither side may change the conditions that led to the dispute unless both sides agree.

12644.s: The order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and certain employees represented by the Transportation Communications Union-Carmen Division. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days after it is created. From the day the board is created and for 120 days after, the carrier and the employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless both sides agree.

12645.s: This order amends Executive Order 12364 to improve the Presidential Management Intern Program. It changes the number in Section 3(c)(1) from "two hundred" to "four hundred". The change affects the recruitment and selection of employees for careers in public sector management.

12643.s: This order extends the privileges, exemptions, and immunities in the International Organizations Immunities Act to the International Committee of the Red Cross. It also says this does not reduce any privileges, exemptions, or immunities the committee already has or may get through other agreements or laws.

12642.s: This order designates the Secretary of Defense as the President’s designee under Title I of the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act. It also allows the Secretary of Defense to pass any of those duties, powers, or responsibilities to people within the Department of Defense. It affects the Department of Defense and the duties carried out under the Act.

12641.s: This order directs the Administrator of General Services to rename certain National Aeronautics and Space Administration facilities in Mississippi as the John C. Stennis Space Center. After that, those facilities must be called by that name.

12640.s: This order creates the President's Committee on Employment of People with Disabilities and an Advisory Council to support it. The committee gives advice and information on expanding employment opportunities for people who are physically disabled, mentally retarded, and mentally ill, and it works with federal, state, and local agencies. It also sets up an Executive Committee to help run the work, and members serve without compensation. The order replaces an earlier committee on employment of the handicapped and transfers its members, records, property, funds, and pending business to the new committee.

12638.s: This order designates the Department of Justice as the United States Central Authority for the Inter-American Convention on Letters Rogatory and Additional Protocol. It gives the department the job of transmitting and processing letters rogatory and acting in line with the convention’s rules. It also allows the Department of Justice to make additional designations that the convention and protocol allow.

12639.s: This order changes who handles certain foreign assistance and related functions under earlier executive orders. It gives some of those functions to the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense, and the Director of the International Development Cooperation Agency. It also assigns several specific duties under the 1988 foreign operations appropriations law and says some of them must be done in consultation with other officials.

12637.s: This order sets up a government-wide program to improve the quality, timeliness, and efficiency of services provided by the Federal Government. It directs each Executive department and agency to add appropriate functions to the program and to work toward covering all appropriate functions by 1991. It also requires annual productivity plans and reports, and it gives the Office of Management and Budget and the Office of Personnel Management roles in reviewing plans, setting guidance, and supporting training and policy changes.

12636.s: This order sets up a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Chicago and North Western Transportation Company and certain employees represented by the United Transportation Union. The board is to report its findings to the President within 30 days of its creation. While the board is working, neither side may change the conditions that led to the dispute unless both agree.

12635.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of the Government of Panama that are in the United States or under control of people in the United States. It also prohibits certain payments or transfers to the Noriega/Solis regime by United States persons in Panama and by Panama-based entities owned or controlled by United States persons. Payments owed to the Government of Panama must be sent to an account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York for the benefit of the Panamanian people, and the order says it does not block private Panamanian assets or remittances to Panamanian people other than the Noriega/Solis regime.

12633.s: This order amends the Code of Conduct for members of the Armed Forces of the United States to remove gender-specific terms. It also says members who may be captured must get specific training and instruction for combat or captivity. The order updates several parts of the code, including the statements about never surrendering and being responsible for one’s actions.

12634.s: This order delegates certain presidential duties related to assistance and support for peace, democracy, and reconciliation in Central America. It authorizes the Secretary of Defense to transfer unobligated funds from specified accounts and to designate the amounts to be transferred. It also authorizes the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to approve the detailing of personnel to the Agency for International Development.

12631.s: This order creates a Working Group on Financial Markets made up of the Treasury Secretary, the Federal Reserve Chairman, the SEC Chairman, and the CFTC Chairman. The group is directed to review issues raised by the market events around October 19, 1987, and consider actions under existing laws and regulations, including policy coordination and contingency planning. It must also consult with exchanges, clearinghouses, self-regulatory bodies, and major market participants, and report to the President on its progress and any recommended legislative changes.

12632.s: This order excludes certain agencies and subdivisions from coverage under the Federal Labor-Management Relations Program. It says these offices have primary intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work, and that Chapter 71 of Title 5 cannot be applied to them in a way that fits national security needs. It covers listed offices in the Drug Enforcement Administration and the United States Marshals Service.

12630.s: This order tells federal departments and agencies to review how their actions affect private property rights under the Fifth Amendment. It covers regulations, proposed laws, permit conditions, and other actions that could count as a taking, and it tells agencies to try to avoid unnecessary takings and report takings claims and awards. It also says actions for public health and safety should be based on real threats and should not go beyond what is needed. The order does not create a right or benefit that people can enforce in court.

12629.s: This order extends the period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1989. It says ending that cooperation would be seriously harmful to U.S. non-proliferation objectives and could threaten the common defense and security of the United States. It also supersedes Executive Order 12587 on its effective date.

12627.s: This order changes the end date in a prior order about the President’s Commission on Privatization. It replaces March 1, 1988 with March 31, 1988 in that commission’s term.

12628.s: This order designates the United Nations Industrial Development Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. That gives it the privileges, exemptions, and immunities covered by that law, and it is meant to help the United States take part in the organization.

12626.s: This order names the Secretary of Defense as the National Defense Stockpile Manager. It gives the Secretary of Defense most of the President’s functions under the Strategic and Critical Materials Stock Piling Act, with some functions assigned to the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture. It also gives the Secretary of Defense certain functions under two other federal laws and allows the Secretary to pass on these duties as appropriate, while consulting affected agencies.

12625.s: This order establishes the President's Council on Integrity and Efficiency as an interagency committee. It also creates a Coordinating Conference made up of the Council chairperson and one representative from each executive agency not on the Council. The Council is told to find and review weak spots in federal programs and to develop coordinated plans to fight fraud, waste, and abuse and improve economy and efficiency. It also develops policies to help build a trained Office of Inspector General staff, and it revokes Executive Order 12301.

12622.s: This order sets new rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Services Schedule, Senior Executive Service, Executive Schedule, congressional salaries, and salaries for certain judges and other judicial officers. It also sets new monthly basic pay and basic allowances for subsistence and quarters for members of the uniformed services. The uniformed services rates take effect on January 1, 1988, and the other schedules take effect on the first applicable pay period beginning on or after that date.

12624.s: This order amends Executive Order 12537 by changing one number in Section 1. It increases the number of members on the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board from fourteen to sixteen.

12621.s: This order changes a deadline in a previous executive order. It says the Task Force must submit its recommendations to the President no later than January 8, 1988.

12620.s: This order amends an earlier executive order about the Administration of Justice Program. It adds the functions given by Section 534 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to the duties covered by Section 1-201, subsection 6.

12619.s: This order closes all federal executive departments and agencies for the last half of the workday on Christmas Eve, December 24, 1987. Agency heads may keep some offices or employees on duty for national security, defense, or other essential public reasons. It applies only to federal departments and agencies, and it addresses pay and leave rules for federal employees.

12617.s: This order extends the life of the President's Advisory Committee on Mediation and Conciliation. It changes the committee's end date so it will end 60 days after it submits its report to the President and the Director of the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service, or no later than September 30, 1988, unless extended sooner.

12618.s: This order changes a prior order on how federal agencies handle patents and licenses for inventions made with federal assistance. It requires agencies to follow uniform rules for inventions owned by a nonprofit contractor or grantee, under the cited law. For an invention that has not been marketed, the funding agency may decide whether the contractor or grantee has taken enough steps to market it.

12615.s: This order tells federal departments and agencies to use private industry for new commercial work when allowed by law, unless government performance is required by statute or national security, or private costs are unreasonable. It also requires them to identify current commercial activities, study them under OMB rules, and report progress on privatization efforts. The order directs the Office of Management and Budget and the Office of Personnel Management to issue guidance, track progress, and review personnel policies for affected employees.

12616.s: This order uses units and members of the Armed Forces to suppress violence and restore law and order in the area around Atlanta, Georgia. It lets the Secretary of Defense call up National Guard units or members to active duty for an indefinite period and until relieved by orders. It also authorizes the Attorney General to coordinate federal agencies and work with state and local agencies, and it lets the Secretary of Defense decide when federal military forces will be withdrawn.

12613.s: This order prohibits goods and services of Iranian origin from being imported into the United States, including its territories and possessions, after the effective date. It does not apply to Iranian publications and news materials, petroleum products refined from Iranian crude oil in a third country, or some articles that were exported from Iran before the effective date. The Secretary of the Treasury and other federal agencies are directed to take steps needed to carry out the order.

12614.s: This order creates the Presidential Task Force on Market Mechanisms and gives it five members appointed by the President. The task force reviews the condition of the nation’s securities markets, looks for problems that could threaten their short-term liquidity or long-term solvency, and makes recommendations to the President, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Chairman of the Federal Reserve Board. It must submit its recommendations within 60 days and then ends 30 days later.

12611.s: This order changes an earlier executive order to add funds provided in the Joint Resolution Making Continuing Appropriations for the Fiscal Year 1988 to the list of funds covered. It deals with the delegation of certain functions about how those funds are used.

12612.s: This order tells executive departments and agencies to follow federalism principles when making policies that affect the relationship between the national government and the States. It says federal action should stay within clear constitutional authority, give States as much discretion as possible, and use the least preemption needed. It also requires agencies to review proposed policies for federalism effects and to consider costs, burdens, and impacts on State authority.

12609.s: This order extends the time for the President's Commission on Compensation of Career Federal Executives to finish its work. It changes the deadline in a prior order from August 1, 1987 to February 28, 1988.

12610.s: This order continues several federal advisory committees through September 30, 1989. It also says the head of the listed department or agency will carry out most of the President’s duties for those committees under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, except for annual reporting to Congress. The order revokes several executive orders that created committees that had ended or finished their work, and it supersedes Executive Order 12534.

12608.s: This order revokes several older Executive Orders and makes many technical changes to others. It updates agency names, legal citations, and references in a long list of Executive Orders. The changes affect federal agencies and programs covered by those orders, and some people who already received benefits under revoked orders keep those benefits.

12607.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Privatization. The Commission is directed to study privatization efforts, review federal activities and asset holdings, and identify functions that could be moved to the private sector or done more efficiently by private entities. It must also develop a framework for a privatization program and submit its findings and recommendations to the President and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. Federal departments and agencies must provide information to the Commission when requested, and the Commission will end 30 days after its final report is submitted.

12606.s: This order tells executive departments and agencies to consider how their policies and regulations may affect family formation, family stability, parents’ rights, family earnings, and family well-being. It also asks them to think about whether government action should be done by a lower level of government or by the family itself. Agencies must review proposed rules and legislative proposals with these family-related criteria and report on them.

12605.s: This order delegates to the Secretary of Defense the President’s function to approve, modify, or disapprove reports from Naval Reserve and Marine Corps Reserve selection boards. It does not delegate the President’s authority to remove a name from a selection board report. It also allows some of this authority to be passed down to certain Defense Department and Navy officials, and it ratifies prior actions that would have been valid under the order.

12604.s: This order changes the Presidential Board of Advisors on Private Sector Initiatives. It increases the Board’s maximum membership from 30 to 35. It also says the Board will end on July 1, 1989, unless it is extended sooner.

12603.s: This order changes the Presidential Commission on the Human Immunodeficiency Virus Epidemic from 11 members to 13 members. It affects the commission created to study the HIV epidemic.

12602.s: This order changes Section 2(b) of Executive Order 12493. It replaces the phrase “90 days” with “365 days.”

12601.s: This order creates the Presidential Commission on the Human Immunodeficiency Virus Epidemic to investigate the spread of HIV and AIDS in the United States. The commission will advise the President and other officials on the medical, legal, ethical, social, and economic impact of HIV and AIDS, and recommend actions to protect the public, help find a cure, and care for people with the disease. It also reviews education efforts, government responses, research, drug and vaccine development, and legal and ethical issues related to AIDS.

12600.s: This order sets procedures for federal agencies to notify people or entities that submitted confidential commercial information when that information may be released under the Freedom of Information Act. It gives submitters a chance to object to disclosure and requires agencies to consider those objections and give a written explanation if they still plan to release the records. The order also requires prompt notice if a FOIA requester sues to force disclosure, and it says the notice rules do not apply in certain listed cases.

12599.s: This order creates a committee to coordinate United States economic programs and policies for Sub-Saharan Africa. It says those programs should be consistent with the goal of ending hunger in the region through economic growth, policy reform, and private sector development, and that they should be tailored to each country’s needs. It also calls for coordination of food assistance, trade and investment efforts, and a yearly report to the President on the economic condition of Sub-Saharan Africa.

12597.s: This order sets procedures for presidential review of certain Department of Transportation decisions under the Federal Aviation Act. It gives the Secretary of Transportation authority to receive those decisions for the President and sets deadlines for review, notice, and any recommendations for disapproval. It also limits outside departments and agencies to raising only national defense or foreign relations matters in that review process.

12598.s: This order delegates certain presidential functions under the Omnibus Diplomatic Security and Antiterrorism Act of 1986 to the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense. Some of those functions must be carried out in consultation with the Secretary of Labor, and the Secretaries of State and Defense must consult with each other and with other appropriate executive departments and agencies. It also supersedes Executive Order No. 12576.

12596.s: This order allows certain employees in Professional or Administrative Career positions under Schedule B to be converted noncompetitively to a career or career-conditional appointment at GS-9. The employee must meet qualifications and other requirements set by the Director of the Office of Personnel Management. The employing agency must also formally evaluate the employee’s performance and find that it warrants the conversion.

12594.s: This order creates the President’s Volunteer Action Award to recognize outstanding volunteer work by individuals and organizations that help others in society. The award may be given in ten areas, including arts and humanities, education, the environment, health, human services, international volunteering, mobilization of volunteers, public safety, youth, and the workplace. Recipients are recommended to the President by the National Voluntary Service Advisory Council with the White House Office of Private Sector Initiatives.

12593.s:
This order changes the size of an advisory committee that helps efforts to increase private sector support for the arts and the humanities. It removes the cap of “not more than twenty persons” and allows additional members to be added.

It also changes the committee’s end date to September 30, 1989, unless it is extended sooner.

12595.s: This order sets up the White House Conference for a Drug Free America in the Executive Office of the President. The Conference is meant to study drug abuse education, prevention, treatment, and the sale and trafficking of illicit drugs, and to bring in public and private participants. It must review law enforcement, the impact of drug abuse on education, current laws on drug trafficking, and ways to create drug free areas in society. It must also send a report with findings and recommendations to the President and Congress.

12592.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Compensation of Career Federal Executives. The commission is to study pay for career members of the Senior Executive Service and advise the President and the Office of Personnel Management on its findings and recommendations. It also looks at how those pay levels compare with private-sector executives, how they affect hiring and keeping career executives, and whether legislation should be proposed to change the President's authority over SES pay. The commission must report by August 1, 1987, and then ends 30 days after it submits its report.

12591.s: This order directs federal agencies and laboratories to work more closely with universities, state and local governments, and the private sector to move federally funded research into new products and processes. It tells agencies to support research partnerships, help share lab information, and give contractors rights to certain patents, software, engineering drawings, and other technical data in exchange for royalty-free government use. It also creates programs for technology sharing, scientist and engineer exchanges, international science information sharing, and reporting on technology transfer efforts.

12589.s: The order gives the Director of the Office of Personnel Management authority to prepare and send Congress a report on whether Federal employees should be allowed to voluntarily donate annual and sick leave to other Federal employees. It says this would be for medical or family emergencies or other hardship situations. It also gives that Director authority to make rules for a temporary program to transfer unused accrued leave in not more than three cases.

12590.s: This order creates the National Drug Policy Board to coordinate federal drug policy. The Board is made up of cabinet and other senior officials, and it works on illegal drug law enforcement, prevention, education, treatment, rehabilitation, and research. It also sets up two coordinating groups, one for drug enforcement and one for drug abuse prevention and health.

12588.s: This order blocks certain transfers and other dealings in real or personal property in the United States if the property is covered by the order. It applies when the Government of Haiti certifies that it has filed suit to claim the property, believes it is held by Jean Claude Duvalier or people tied to his regime, and cannot post the bond needed to seek a court order. The restriction ends after final judgment, any appeals, and satisfaction of any judgment in the case.

12587.s: This order extends the period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community to March 10, 1988. It says that ending this cooperation would be seriously harmful to U.S. non-proliferation goals and could jeopardize U.S. common defense and security, and it says Congress was notified.

12586.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial and changes how some courts-martial are handled in the armed forces. It gives rules for court-martial jurisdiction over reserve component personnel, including when they may be on active duty or inactive-duty training. It also changes the rules on mental responsibility defenses, mental examinations, and post-trial filing deadlines and review procedures.

12584.s: This order gives the President's Special Review Board more time to submit its findings and recommendations. It changes the deadline in another executive order from February 19, 1987 to February 26, 1987.

12585.s: This order expands eligibility for some former overseas employees to be appointed to competitive service jobs without competition. It adds nonappropriated fund employees, changes the service requirement from 24 months to 18 months, and lets an agency waive a written test if the overseas job was similar enough to the new job. It also changes who can qualify as a family member of an appropriate sponsor and requires eligible people to use this appointment option within three years of returning to the United States, unless a longer time is approved for hardship.

12583.s: This order delegates certain Food for Progress duties from the President to other officials. It lets the Director of the United States International Development Cooperation Agency make agreements with developing countries and send required reports to Congress. It also lets the Secretary of Agriculture waive any minimum tonnage requirements. The work must be coordinated through the Food Aid Subcommittee of the Development Coordination Committee.

12582.s: This order gives expedited naturalization to certain aliens and non-citizen nationals who served honorably on active duty in the Armed Forces during the Grenada campaign. It says the Grenada military operations period ran from October 25, 1983, to November 2, 1983. It also lists the places and areas of service that count for this naturalization exception.

12581.s: This order changes the deadline for the President's Special Review Board to send its findings and recommendations to the President. It affects the Board and updates the date to February 19, 1987.

12580.s: This order sets up how the federal government will carry out the Superfund law for hazardous releases and cleanup. It gives the Environmental Protection Agency, Coast Guard, Federal Emergency Management Agency, Health and Human Services, and other agencies different duties for response, cleanup schedules, enforcement, liability, and litigation. It also creates national and regional response teams and says some actions need consultation or approval from other federal offices, including the Attorney General and the Office of Management and Budget.

12579.s: This order extends the life of the President's Advisory Committee on Mediation and Conciliation. It changes the committee's termination date to December 31, 1987, unless it is extended sooner.

12578.s: This order adjusts basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Administration medical staff, the Senior Executive Service, executive salaries, congressional salaries, and judicial salaries. It also adjusts monthly basic pay and certain allowances for members of the uniformed services. The uniformed services changes take effect on January 1, 1987, and the other changes take effect on the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 1987.

12577.s: This order closes all Executive departments and agencies on Friday, December 26, 1986, and excuses their employees from duty that day. Department and agency heads may keep certain offices open and require some employees to report for duty for national security, defense, or other public reasons. It also treats that day as covered by federal pay and leave rules for United States employees.

12576.s: This order delegates to the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense the power to pay compensation to people who were held in captive status on or before January 21, 1981. It applies to individuals who had been held hostage in Iran and other former hostages. The two departments must consult with each other and with other executive departments and agencies when carrying out these duties.

12575.s: This order creates the President’s Special Review Board to study the future role and procedures of the National Security Council staff. The Board must review how the staff helps develop, coordinate, oversee, and carry out foreign and national security policy, and it must look at the staff’s role in operational activities, including sensitive diplomatic, military, and intelligence missions. The Board will report its findings and recommendations to the President within 60 days, and it ends 30 days after it submits its report.

12574.s: This order creates an experimental program within the President’s Commission on Executive Exchange. Under it, executive agencies may accept voluntary services from private sector participants in the program. The program is limited to fiscal years 1987 through 1989, with no more than ten new participants in any fiscal year, and it cannot displace any government employee. Participants are treated as employees of the assigned agency for some laws and rules, but they are not covered by certain federal pay and benefit laws.

12572.s: This order says that the United States will handle its relations with the Government of the Northern Mariana Islands under the general administrative supervision of the Secretary of the Interior. It applies to matters that are not the program responsibility of another federal department or agency.

12573.s: This order changes the rules for incentive pay for hazardous duty under Executive Order 11157. It says using certain solid fumigant formulations to control burrowing animals outdoors does not qualify for that pay. It also adds a new category for handling chemical munitions and chemical surety material, and says some duties and materials are not included. The chemical munitions change is effective as of October 1, 1985, and the pesticide change is effective right away.

12570.s: This executive order gives the Secretary of State authority to carry out certain functions about transferring and depositing funds for assistance under the Military Construction Appropriations Act, 1987. It also lets the Secretary of Defense designate the accounts from which some unobligated Defense Department funds are transferred. These actions affect the accounts and funds used for assistance related to Central American democracies and the Nicaraguan Democratic Resistance.

12571.s: This order tells federal departments and agencies to carry out the requirements of the Comprehensive Anti-Apartheid Act. It gives specific jobs to the State, Treasury, Commerce, Defense, Transportation, and other agencies for parts of the Act. It also creates an inter-agency committee on South Africa to consult on U.S. policy and monitor implementation.

12569.s: This order sets how the United States will carry out relations under the Compact with the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, and the Republic of Palau. It gives the Secretary of State responsibility for government-to-government relations and for United States representatives in those states. It gives the Secretary of the Interior responsibility for United States assistance and for coordinating and monitoring related programs and economic development planning. It also creates an interagency group and an office in the Department of State to help carry out these duties.

12568.s: This order lets Defense Department officials use hiring preference for qualified spouses of members of the Armed Forces stationed in the same geographic area as a nonappropriated fund activity. The preference applies to wage grade UA-8 and below, equivalent positions, and positions paid at hourly rates.

12567.s: The order designates the Inter-American Investment Corporation, the Commission for the Study of Alternatives to the Panama Canal, and the Pacific Salmon Commission as public international organizations under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It says these organizations are entitled to the privileges, exemptions, and immunities given by that law, and it does not change any privileges or immunities they may already have under treaties or congressional action. It also delegates certain functions for the Inter-American Investment Corporation to the Secretary of the Treasury.

12566.s: The order requires Federal employees in the front seat of a motor vehicle on official business to have a safety belt properly fastened when the vehicle is moving. It directs executive branch agencies to make rules and take other steps to carry out the order, including educating employees about it. It also asks the Secretary of Labor to work with agencies in the Legislative and Judicial branches to encourage safety belt use programs and to report each year on on-the-job belt use by Federal employees.

12565.s: This order sets up a system of financial reporting for executive branch officers and employees. Some employees must file public reports, and others must file non-public confidential reports if their positions are designated for that purpose. The Office of Government Ethics must help set the rules and oversee how agencies carry them out. Existing financial reports that were already kept confidential must stay confidential.

12564.s: This order requires Federal employees to stay away from illegal drugs and says people who use illegal drugs are not suitable for Federal employment. It directs each Executive agency to make a plan for a drug-free workplace, including employee assistance, supervisor training, and ways to identify illegal drug users. It also allows drug testing for employees in sensitive positions, for applicants, and in some other cases, and it calls for discipline or removal for employees who use illegal drugs unless limited exceptions apply.

12563.s: This order establishes a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain employee labor organizations. The parties must submit final settlement offers to the board within 30 days after the board is created. The board must then report to the President and choose the most reasonable offer, and the conditions tied to the dispute may not be changed except by agreement until 60 days after the report.

12562.s: This order sets up a three-member board to investigate disputes between certain railroads and their employees represented by labor organizations. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. While the board is in place and for 30 days after its report, the carriers and employees may not change the conditions tied to the disputes unless both sides agree.

12560.s: This order changes how certain foreign assistance and foreign relations functions are assigned within the government. It gives some of those functions to the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense, and the Director of the International Development Cooperation Agency. It also says some of these duties must be carried out in consultation with other officials, including the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Director of the Arms Control and Disarmament Agency.

12559.s: This order exempts certain parts of the Department of Justice from coverage under the Federal Labor-Management Relations Program. It covers the Office of Enforcement and the Office of Intelligence in the Drug Enforcement Administration, and several offices and divisions in the United States Marshals Service.

12558.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain employees represented by labor organizations. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days after it is created. For 120 days after the board is created, the carrier and the employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute unless both sides agree.

12557.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the Maine Central Railroad Company/Portland Terminal Company and certain employees represented by the Brotherhood of Maintenance of Way Employees. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. While the board is working and for 30 days after its report, the carriers and the employees may not change the conditions that led to the disputes unless both sides agree.

12556.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense the President’s power to choose areas for free mailing privileges. The Secretary of Defense must consult with the Secretary of State, the United States Postal Service, and other Executive agencies as needed, and must tell the Postal Service about any designations or terminations.

12555.s: This order delegates several duties under the cultural property law to the Director of the United States Information Agency, the Secretary of State, and the Secretary of the Treasury. It covers negotiations and extensions of agreements, requests from State Parties, reports to Congress, emergency import restrictions, and the suspension or application of import restrictions. It also designates the Secretary of the Interior to carry out enforcement functions in section 314.

12554.s: This order extends the period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1987. It says Congress was notified of this decision.

12553.s: This order revokes a long list of earlier executive orders that were no longer considered necessary. The revoked orders cover many areas, including military academy examinations, Selective Service rules, railroad and airline labor dispute boards, civil service matters, and tax return inspection rules. It affects the executive orders named in the list and any amendments to them.

12552.s: This order sets up a government-wide program to improve the quality, timeliness, and efficiency of Federal services. It tells each Executive department and agency to review its functions, set productivity goals, and submit yearly productivity plans and reports. It also directs the Office of Management and Budget and the Office of Personnel Management to set guidance, review plans, and support productivity training and employee programs.

12551.s: This order expands the membership of the President's Export Council. It adds five members of the United States Senate and five members of the United States House of Representatives, each to serve a two-year term.

12550.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial and changes rules for military trials and evidence. It says an accused must be brought to trial within 120 days in certain cases, updates rules for mental incompetence, and adds rules on when evidence from involuntary statements or unlawful searches may be used. It also adds a new espionage offense and sets out when that offense can be punished by death.

12549.s: This order sets up a government-wide system for debarment and suspension from federal programs and activities that involve federal financial and nonfinancial assistance and benefits. If one agency debars or suspends a participant, that decision applies across the federal government, and agencies must follow common criteria and due process rules. It also requires a list of excluded individuals and organizations and names certain programs and benefits that are not covered.

12548.s: This order directs the Secretaries of Agriculture and the Interior to set fees for domestic livestock grazing on public rangelands. It gives a formula for figuring the fee and says the yearly change cannot be more than 25 percent up or down from the previous year, with a minimum fee of $1.35 per animal unit month. It also keeps existing rules and practices for the grazing fee formula in effect.

12546.s: This order creates a Presidential Commission to investigate the Space Shuttle Challenger accident. The commission must review the accident, find the probable cause or causes, and make recommendations for corrective or other action. It must give its final report to the President and the NASA Administrator, and it will end 60 days after that report is submitted.

12547.s: This order sets procedures for presidential review of certain Department of Transportation aviation decisions. It lets the DOT withhold those decisions from public disclosure for up to five days after they are sent to the President, and it sends copies to specified departments and agencies for review of national defense or foreign relations issues. Other departments and agencies may raise only national defense or foreign relations matters in this review, and the order says it does not give rights to private parties.

12545.s: This order changes the deadline for the National Commission on Space to submit its plan and recommendations. It extends the time from 12 months to 18 months.

12544.s: This order blocks all property and interests in property of the Government of Libya, its agencies, instrumentalities, controlled entities, and the Central Bank of Libya. It applies to property in the United States, property that later comes into the United States, and property in the possession or control of U.S. persons, including overseas branches. The Secretary of the Treasury may use powers under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to carry it out.

12542.s: This order changes the deadline for the President's Blue Ribbon Commission on Defense Management to submit its conclusions and recommendations on the procurement section of its study. It moves the date from December 31, 1985, to February 28, 1986.

12541.s: This order changes the rules for what counts as “sea duty” under a prior executive order. Duty for less than three months does not count as sea duty, and duty for more than three months under temporary orders to return to the member’s same permanent station also does not count as sea duty. It affects service members covered by the basic allowance for quarters while on sea duty.

12540.s: This order changes certain rates of pay and allowances in Executive Order 12496 by replacing Schedule 7 and Schedule 8. It sets adjusted pay rates for the uniformed services, including monthly basic pay, subsistence allowances, and quarters allowances. The new pay rates take effect on the dates stated in the order.

12538.s: This order bars most petroleum products refined in Libya from being imported into the United States, its territories, or possessions. It applies to petroleum products in certain tariff categories, with an exception for products loaded aboard maritime vessels before the stated cutoff time. The Secretary of the Treasury may issue rules and regulations to carry out the order.

12539.s: This order changes the President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports by increasing its membership from fifteen to eighteen. It affects the council's size and the people who serve on it.

12536.s: This order revokes one section of Executive Order 12293 that deals with appointing the Chairman of the Board of the Foreign Service. It also changes the numbering of another section in that order.

12537.s: This order creates the President’s Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board in the White House Office. The board reviews intelligence work across federal agencies, reports to the President, and may make recommendations to improve intelligence activities.

12535.s: This order prohibits importing South African Krugerrands into the United States. The ban took effect on October 11, 1985. The Secretary of the Treasury may issue rules and regulations to carry out the prohibition.

12534.s: This order continues several federal advisory committees until September 30, 1987. It says the head of each named department or agency will handle the President’s duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for those committees, except for reporting annually to Congress. It also revokes a number of executive orders that had created other committees, and it supersedes two executive orders.

12533.s: This order extends the life of the President's Advisory Committee on Mediation and Conciliation and changes its membership from twelve to thirteen. It says the members other than the Chairman must represent labor and management equally. The committee is set to end on December 31, 1986, unless it is extended sooner.

12531.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the United Transportation Union and certain railroads. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. From the day the board is created and for 30 days after it reports, the railroads and employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute unless both sides agree.

12530.s: This order establishes the Nicaraguan Humanitarian Assistance Office to administer a program of humanitarian assistance to the Nicaraguan democratic resistance. The Office is to be supervised by the Secretary of State and led by a Director named by the President. It may enter grant agreements and contracts, use staff from federal agencies with limits, and receive support through the Department of State. The Director is also given authority to classify information as Top Secret and must help prepare required reports on the program's disbursements.

12529.s: This order changes the name of a presidential advisory commission to "President's Commission on Americans Outdoors." It also extends the time for the commission to finish its work, requiring a report by December 31, 1986. The commission will end 30 days after it submits its report.

12528.s: This order creates the Presidential Board of Advisors on Private Sector Initiatives. The board is to advise the President and the Secretary of Commerce on private sector initiative policies, including public/private partnerships, barriers to private social service programs, and the long-term development of private sector initiatives in the United States. It also says the board may get support from executive agencies and will end two years after the order unless extended.

12527.s: This order amends Executive Order 11252 by repealing Sections 2 and 3. It also renumbers the current Section 4 as Section 2, affecting the Food-for-Peace Program administrative position provisions.

12526.s: This order creates the President’s Blue Ribbon Commission on Defense Management. The Commission is made up of members appointed or designated by the President and is led by a Chairman chosen from among them. It must study defense management and organization, including defense procurement, oversight, and how military forces are planned and used, and report its findings and recommendations to the President and the Secretary of Defense. Executive agencies must provide information to the Commission, and the Secretary of Defense must provide administrative support.

12525.s: This order revokes Executive Order 12470 and rescinds the declaration of economic emergency. It says the export control rules and other administrative actions that were already issued under that order stay in effect until they are changed or revoked by proper authority. It also keeps in force the rules tied to Section 38(e) of the Arms Export Control Act.

12524.s: This order designates listed beneficiary countries as least-developed beneficiary developing countries under the Generalized System of Preferences. Eligible articles imported directly from those countries get duty-free treatment without the usual limits in the trade law. It also changes the list of articles that qualify for GSP benefits and removes one article from some GSP lists. The changes apply to covered imports and entries on or after the dates named in the order.

12523.s: This order gives the Administrator of the Small Business Administration the President's functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for the White House Conference on Small Business Authorization Act, except for the duty to report annually to Congress. The Administrator must carry out those functions under guidelines and procedures set by the Administrator of General Services.

12522.s: This order changes who can set the rules for federal employee relocation expense reimbursement under 5 U.S.C. 5724c. It says each agency will carry out its responsibilities under those rules, and the Director of Central Intelligence will set the rules for the Central Intelligence Agency after consulting with the Administrator of General Services. The order is effective as of October 12, 1984.

12521.s: This order assigns the Office of Management and Budget the job of preparing and sending reports to Congress about offsets. It lets the OMB Director delegate parts of that work to executive departments and agencies, which must provide needed information as allowed by law. It also authorizes the United States International Trade Commission to collect information for the data base used in the first report and says that information should have appropriate confidentiality protections.

12520.s: The order lets the Secretary of Defense make rules for quarters allowances under the Panama Canal Act of 1979. Those rules must follow the Panama Canal Treaty and related agreements.

12519.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences rules for certain imported articles. It modifies the tariff schedules, updates the lists of articles and beneficiary developing countries, and provides staged reductions in duty rates for some new items. Some changes take effect for goods entered on or after the dates listed in the order.

12518.s: This order changes a previous executive order about international investment and trade in services. It updates the order’s name and makes several wording changes, including adding trade in services to one section. The purpose is to help collect, analyze, and share information needed to develop and carry out U.S. policy on trade in services.

12517.s: This order gives the Secretary of State all functions that were given to the President under the United States-India Fund for Cultural, Educational, and Scientific Cooperation Act. It also directs India rupees provided for that law to be allocated to the Secretary of the Treasury for investment. The investment earnings are to be used for the purposes of Title IX of the Act.

12516.s: This order changes who may be selected as Presidential Exchange Executives. It limits them to certain career Federal Executives in the Senior Executive Service or at an equivalent level, including some candidates, and requires that they be assigned for one year to private sector positions. The private sector jobs must offer significant challenge, responsibility, and regular contact with senior private sector officials.

12515.s: This order changes the lists of articles that can get preferential treatment under the Generalized System of Preferences when imported from designated beneficiary developing countries. It updates three parts of the tariff rules to reflect changes made by the Trade and Tariff Act of 1984. The changes affect certain imported articles and apply to entries and withdrawals from warehouse on the dates listed in the order.

12514.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Secretary of the Air Force if one of those offices becomes vacant because of death, disability, or absence. It lists which officers would act in each role and in what order. It also says the President may choose a different officer from the listed group, and that any succession is only temporary.

12513.s: This order declares a national emergency over the policies and actions of the Government of Nicaragua. It prohibits imports into the United States of goods and services of Nicaraguan origin, and it also bans most exports from the United States to Nicaragua, except goods sent to the organized democratic resistance. It bars Nicaraguan air carriers from flights to or from the United States and stops vessels of Nicaraguan registry from entering U.S. ports.

12512.s: This order sets up government-wide policies for the acquisition, management, and disposal of federal real property and public land assets. It directs federal departments and agencies to review their property, set goals, make annual improvement plans, and create internal accountability systems. It gives the Domestic Policy Council, the Office of Management and Budget, and the General Services Administration roles in approving policies, reviewing progress, and managing selected properties. It also directs the Departments of Agriculture and the Interior to improve management of public lands and National Forest System lands, and it revokes Executive Order 12348.

12511.s: This order creates the President's Child Safety Partnership, an advisory committee made up of up to 26 members, including the Attorney General and the secretaries of Health and Human Services and Education. The group must study child safety, look at preventing the victimization of children, and make recommendations to the President. It is also directed to focus on public-private cooperation, including work by service organizations, schools, businesses, charitable organizations, and public safety organizations. The Partnership must report to the President and will end on April 29, 1987, or 60 days after its final report, whichever comes first.

12509.s: This order creates the Technical Review Group on Inertial Confinement Fusion as an advisory committee. The group is told to review the defense inertial confinement fusion program and advise the President and Congress on its findings and recommendations for future work. It must submit an interim report and a final report, and it ends after the final report is submitted.

12510.s: This order changes rules for extra pay for federal workers in non-foreign areas where living costs are higher than in the Washington, D.C., area. It directs the Office of Personnel Management to set and adjust these allowances and to make rules for how they are handled. It also changes the wording in older orders to use “non-foreign areas” instead of “Territories,” and it supersedes Executive Order 12070.

12508.s: This order designates the World Tourism Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities that law provides, and it does not limit any other privileges or immunities it may have under international agreements or congressional action.

12505.s: This order lets some Office of Management and Budget employees have their appointments changed to career or career-conditional status if they meet set service, performance, and qualification requirements. It applies to employees in positions tied to the President’s paperwork reduction and regulatory review and planning programs. Employees who are not converted must be separated when their current appointment ends.

12506.s: This order extends the time period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1986. It says the President made this decision after determining that ending the cooperation would hurt United States nonproliferation objectives and could endanger the common defense and security of the United States, and after notifying Congress.

12504.s: This order sets a process for asking the President to issue a proclamation extending protection against unauthorized duplication of semiconductor chip products. Requests must go through the Secretary of Commerce, who may set regulations after consulting the Secretary of State. The protection applies to foreign nationals, domiciliaries, and sovereign authorities.

12503.s: This order creates a Presidential Commission to review outdoor recreation resources. The Commission will look at public outdoor recreation policies, programs, opportunities, and some privately provided recreation resources, then make recommendations to the President. It may hold public hearings, and its members serve without pay, though some private citizens may get travel expenses. The Commission is to submit its report and recommendations within twelve months and then end after that report is submitted or by March 1, 1986, whichever comes first.

12502.s: This order creates the Chemical Warfare Review Commission. The commission is to review the United States’ chemical warfare posture, with special focus on whether the United States should produce binary chemical munitions. It must report its findings and recommendations to the President on the need to keep a chemical retaliatory stockpile, the adequacy of that stockpile if needed, and whether the United States should produce binary chemical munitions or take other actions. The order also says executive agencies must provide information to the commission, and the commission will end after it submits its report or on September 30, 1985, whichever comes first.

12501.s: This order establishes an Arctic Research Commission and an Interagency Arctic Research Policy Committee. The Commission includes five presidential appointees and is tasked with developing and recommending an integrated national Arctic research policy, reviewing Federal research programs, and reporting each year to the President and Congress. The Interagency Committee, led by the National Science Foundation, is to help carry out Arctic research policy, coordinate Federal agency work, and provide public notice of its meetings and an opportunity for public participation.

12500.s: This order delegates certain foreign assistance functions to the Secretary of State and the Director of the International Development Cooperation Agency. It adds authority for parts of the 1985 foreign assistance and defense laws, including provisions tied to El Salvador, Turkey, and Honduras. It also requires consultation with the Secretary of Defense for one section and with the Secretary of State for another.

12497.s: This order extends the life of the President's Advisory Committee on Mediation and Conciliation. It changes the committee's end date to September 30, 1985, unless it is extended sooner.

12499.s: This order creates the President's Blue Ribbon Task Group on Nuclear Weapons Program Management. The task group is to review how the Departments of Defense and Energy set requirements and provide resources for nuclear weapons research, development, testing, production, surveillance, and retirement, and recommend needed changes. It is to report to the President and the Armed Services Committees of the Senate and House, and it may not include employees of the Department of Defense or the Department of Energy.

12496.s: This order adjusts rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, and Veterans’ Administration medical schedules. It also adjusts pay for members of the Senior Executive Service, the Vice President, Congress, and the judiciary. The order changes monthly basic pay and allowances for members of the uniformed services, and the changes take effect with the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 1985.

12495.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen. The parties must give the board their final settlement offers within 30 days after the board is created. The board must then report to the President with its choice of the most reasonable offer, and the conditions tied to the dispute cannot be changed by the parties except by agreement during the stated period.

12494.s: This order amends an earlier order to define one type of hazardous duty for pay purposes. It says the duty includes members who, as a primary assignment, demolish explosives, render them harmless, or work to do so. It also covers members who train, keep skills current, or develop tools, equipment, or procedures for that work when live explosives are used.

12493.s: This order continues the President's Commission on Executive Exchange and sets its membership, leadership, and terms of service. The Commission runs exchange programs that place selected private sector executives in federal jobs and selected career federal executives in private sector jobs, and it also runs an executive international embassy assignments program. It also oversees an education program, reviews the program's operation, and makes sure it follows federal merit principles. Executive agencies must help the Commission, and Executive Order 12136 is revoked.

12492.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and the union representing some of its employees.
