It also requires the agencies to work with other federal departments on facilities protection, damage assessment, research, resource planning, and getting needed materials, manpower, equipment, supplies, and services.

11093.s: This order gives the Administrator of General Services responsibility to prepare national emergency plans and readiness programs for the General Services Administration. It covers Federal buildings, public utilities, communications, transportation, records, the Federal Register, government supply, stockpiles, industrial reserve plants, and surplus property. It also directs the Administrator to work with the Department of Defense and other agencies on emergency planning, damage assessment, and strategic materials stockpiles.

11092.s: This order gives the Federal Communications Commission emergency preparedness duties for communications services. It requires the Commission to prepare national emergency plans and programs for common carriers, broadcasting facilities, safety and special radio services, radio frequency assignments, and the protection and restoration of facilities. It also covers enforcement, financial aid, research, and cooperation with the Department of Defense and the Office of Emergency Planning.

11091.s: This order directs the Civil Service Commission to prepare national emergency plans and preparedness programs for Federal civilian employees. The plans cover personnel administration, recruiting, reassignment, postattack registration, deferment requests, investigations, salaries, benefits, and training. It also applies to the executive branch and the municipal government of the District of Columbia for employee deferment, and it revokes a prior emergency preparedness order.

11090.s: This order assigns the Civil Aeronautics Board emergency preparedness duties for civil air operations. It tells the Board to prepare national emergency plans and programs for the War Air Service Program, including aircraft distribution, economic regulation, passenger and cargo priorities, accident investigation, and resource planning. It also directs the Board to work with other agencies on emergency transportation plans and to be ready to carry out these functions in an emergency.

11089.s: This order gives the Atomic Energy Commission responsibility for preparing national emergency plans and preparedness programs for atomic energy activities of the federal government. It directs the Commission to plan for continuing or resuming work on nuclear weapons and equipment, reactors, atomic materials, research, public information, foreign liaison, health services, damage assessment, and claims for needed resources during an emergency. It also says these plans must be coordinated with the Department of Defense and the Office of Emergency Planning, and that the President keeps the authority to put emergency plans into effect.

11088.s: This order tells the Secretary of the Treasury to prepare national emergency plans and readiness programs for the Treasury Department. It covers emergency work in areas like money and credit, taxes, financial institutions, customs, Treasury checks, currency, counterfeiting, port security, and protection of the President and Vice President. It also says the Secretary and the Office of Emergency Planning should work together on research and coordination, but only the President can put any emergency plan into effect.

11087.s: This order tells the Secretary of State to prepare national emergency plans and develop preparedness programs for the Department of State and other agencies under his control. It also assigns the Secretary duties for foreign relations during a national emergency, including work with allies and neutral states, foreign assistance, protection or evacuation of Americans abroad, and control of people entering or leaving the United States. The Secretary must work with the Office of Emergency Planning on research and resources evaluation, and the President keeps the authority to put emergency plans into effect.

11086.s: This order amends an earlier order about section 32(h) of the Trading with the Enemy Act. It designates the Jewish Restitution Successor Organization as a successor in interest to deceased persons for those purposes. It also gives the Foreign Claims Settlement Commission the power to carry out the section’s functions, while claims filed earlier by that organization stay with the Attorney General until they are paid or otherwise settled.

11085.s: This order re-establishes the Medal of Freedom as the Presidential Medal of Freedom and sets it in two degrees. It lets the President award it to people who have made an especially meritorious contribution to the security or national interests of the United States, world peace, or cultural or other significant public or private efforts. It also expands the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board to help review recommendations and nominate people for the medal.

11084.s: This order amends a prior order on telecommunications management. It gives the Director of the Office of Emergency Planning the authority to assign radio frequencies to Government agencies and to amend, modify, or revoke those assignments. It also gives that office the authority to let a foreign government build and operate a radio station at the seat of government, with a recommendation from the Secretary of State and consultation with the Attorney General and the Chairman of the Federal Communications Commission.

11083.s: This order allows the House Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1947 to 1963 during the Eighty-eighth Congress. The inspections are for the committee’s study of government activities and how economical and efficient they are. The inspections must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

11082.s: This order allows the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for the years 1947 through 1963. The inspection is for the committee’s study of government activities and must follow Treasury rules on inspecting congressional returns.

11081.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial to update rules for nonjudicial punishment under Article 15. It changes who may impose punishment, how minor offenses are handled, and what punishments may be used for military personnel. It also adds new maximum punishments for correctional custody offenses and sets an effective date for the changes.

11080.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1950 through 1962 open to inspection by the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee’s study of nondiplomatic activities of representatives of foreign governments, and their contractors and agents, in promoting those governments’ interests and trying to influence U.S. policies. The inspection must follow Treasury rules on congressional review of tax returns.

11079.s: This order tells certain federal secretaries to make rules about when members of the armed forces and commissioned officers of the Public Health Service may accept fellowships, scholarships, or grants. The rules apply to awards from corporations, funds, foundations, or educational institutions that are organized mainly for scientific, literary, or educational purposes. It also says the rules should be uniform as much as practical.

11078.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into a labor dispute involving the Boeing Company, some of its employees, and a Rohr Aircraft Corporation plant that works as a Boeing subcontractor. The order says the dispute could lead to a strike affecting a large part of the industry and could imperil national safety. The board must report to the President and then may keep doing other tasks allowed under the law.

11077.s: This order gives the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare the job of carrying out different parts of the Migration and Refugee Assistance Act of 1962. It also assigns the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare responsibility for assistance to Cuban refugee students in the United States who need loans to attend higher education. The order allows the government to carry out these functions without following certain laws on shipping, advance payments, bidding, contracts, and some overseas travel rules, and it says these waivers should be used sparingly.

11094.s: This order assigns several federal agencies to prepare national emergency plans and readiness programs for conditions of national emergency, including an attack on the United States. It gives them duties related to money and credit, banking and other financial institutions, securities markets, small business contracts and loans, and veterans benefits. It also directs them to work with other federal agencies on emergency planning, research, facilities protection, and damage assessment.

11076.s: This order creates the President's Advisory Commission on Narcotic and Drug Abuse. The Commission is to study narcotic and non-narcotic drug abuse, review federal programs, and make recommendations for legislation and better rehabilitation for habitual drug misusers. It also directs several executive departments to help the Commission and provide information. The Commission must submit a final report to the President and then terminate by December 31, 1963.

11075.s: This order sets up how the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 will be carried out. It places the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations in the Executive Office of the President, creates a Trade Expansion Act Advisory Committee, and gives certain duties to the Treasury, Commerce, and Labor Departments. It also changes a prior executive order and revokes several older orders related to trade policy.

11074.s: This order creates the President's Council on Physical Fitness. The Council is to improve physical fitness programs, coordinate federal agency efforts, and get help from citizens, civic groups, private enterprise, and voluntary organizations. It also continues the earlier President's Council on Youth Fitness and revokes three older executive orders.

11073.s: This order sets policy for federal salary administration in the executive branch. It directs agencies to use salary authorities to keep a strong federal workforce, pay employees fairly, and make sure the government gets value for salary spending. It also requires annual reviews and reports on federal pay, gives the Civil Service Commission authority to set higher pay rates in some cases, and sets rules for classification, step increases, and reports from agencies.

11072.s: This order extends the boundaries of the Superior National Forest in Minnesota and the Clark National Forest in Missouri. It adds certain lands to each forest and reserves other United States lands within those boundaries as parts of the forests, subject to valid claims. It affects lands in both states that are described in the order.

11070.s: This order changes the list of communicable diseases used for rules that allow the apprehension, detention, or conditional release of people to help prevent the spread of disease. It adds chickenpox to the list. It also replaces Scarlet Fever and Streptococcic Sore Throat with Hemolytic Streptococcal Infections.

11071.s: This order designates certain foreign countries and territories as economically less developed countries for purposes of parts of the Internal Revenue Code. It covers most foreign countries, certain overseas territories and possessions, Puerto Rico, and all possessions of the United States, with listed exceptions. It also defines which countries and areas count as being within the Sino-Soviet bloc. The Secretary of the Treasury is authorized to issue rules to carry out the order.

11069.s: This executive order changes Executive Order No. 11017 by adding the Secretary of Commerce to the Recreation Advisory Council. It affects the membership of that council by placing the Secretary of Commerce after the Secretary of Defense.

11068.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into a labor dispute between Lockheed Aircraft Corporation and some of its employees represented by the International Association of Machinists. The dispute led to a strike affecting part of the ballistics missile, space vehicle, and military aircraft industry. The board must report to the President and then continue to carry out other duties under the law.

11067.s: This order includes certain lands in Cherokee County, North Carolina, in the Nantahala National Forest. It covers two parcels on both shores of Apalachia Lake, totaling about 166 acres. The order also refers to the transfer of certain rights and land interests in Polk County, Tennessee, and Cherokee County, North Carolina, so those lands can be included in the Nantahala and Cherokee National Forests.

11066.s: This order includes certain lands in Sullivan County, Tennessee, and Washington County, Virginia, in the Cherokee National Forest and the Jefferson National Forest. It says the lands are transferred under an agreement between the Tennessee Valley Authority and the Department of Agriculture. The order covers several parcels and islands in South Holston Lake and other nearby land areas.

11065.s: This order allows certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for 1950 through 1962 to be inspected during the Eighty-seventh Congress. The Senate Committee on Foreign Relations, or a subcommittee it authorizes, may review them under Treasury rules. The inspection is for the committee’s study of nondiplomatic activities of representatives of foreign governments, and their contractors and agents, and attempts to influence U.S. policy and the national interest.

11064.s: This order excuses many federal employees from duty on Monday, December 24, 1962, the day before Christmas Day. It treats that day as a holiday for pay and leave rules. Department and agency heads are told to use a liberal policy on annual leave when it fits the needs of the service, but some employees may still be required to work for public or national security reasons.

11062.s: This order changes a prior executive order so that the Department of Defense is named instead of the Department of the Army, the Department of the Navy, and the Department of the Air Force. It affects the administration of the Defense Mobilization Program and the agency named as a loan guaranteeing agency.

11063.s: This order directs federal departments and agencies to prevent discrimination in housing and related facilities based on race, color, creed, or national origin. It covers the sale, lease, rental, use, or lending for residential property that is owned by the federal government or backed by federal aid or federal loan guarantees. It also creates the President's Committee on Equal Opportunity in Housing to help carry out the order and review agency progress. Federal agencies may issue rules and take enforcement action against violations under the order.

11061.s: This order directs that the flag of the United States be flown at half-staff until interment in memory of Mrs. Anna Eleanor Roosevelt. It applies to federal buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the United States and its territories and possessions, and to U.S. offices and military facilities abroad.

11060.s: This order directs the Director of the Bureau of the Budget to set rates for the reasonable value of hospital, medical, surgical, and dental care and treatment furnished or to be furnished. It also gives the Attorney General authority to prescribe regulations to carry out the Act of September 25, 1962, except for the rate-setting in Section 1.

11059.s: This order designates three international commissions as public international organizations under the International Organizations Immunities Act. They are the Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission, the Great Lakes Fishery Commission, and the International Pacific Halibut Commission. The order gives them the privileges, exemptions, and immunities allowed by that law, except for certain sections, and does not limit any other privileges or immunities they may already have or later receive.

11058.s: This order lets the Secretary of Defense, and some other military officials, order members or units of the Ready Reserve to active duty without their consent until February 28, 1963. It also lets the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of the Treasury extend certain enlistments, duties, and other service periods that expire before that date. No one who was already involuntarily ordered to active duty or had service extended under the 1961 law may be involuntarily ordered to active duty under this order.

11057.s: This order authorizes the Department of State to communicate restricted data and data removed from the Restricted Data category under agreements for cooperation made under the Atomic Energy Act. The communication must be limited to data that the President, or the Atomic Energy Commission and the Department of Defense together, have determined may be shared under the agreement. The Department of State may not make any communication until it has been authorized under the required procedures.

11055.s: This order lets the House Select Committee on Small Business, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain income tax returns from 1950 to 1969. The returns are for organizations exempt from income tax under the listed sections of the tax code. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

11056.s: This order gives the Civil Service Commission authority to make certain findings and to set and revise rates of basic compensation. That authority applies to positions paid under Section 603(b) of the Classification Act of 1949, as amended. It affects federal salaries for those covered positions.

11054.s: The order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into labor disputes between certain maritime employers and employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, AFL-CIO. It says the disputes have led to a strike that could affect the maritime industry, national health and safety, and the flow of necessary perishable products. The board must report to the President and may continue to perform other duties under the law.

11053.s: This order directs the Secretary of Defense to enforce court orders from the United States District Court for the Southern District of Mississippi and the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit. It also lets the Secretary of Defense use United States armed forces if needed. The order allows Mississippi Army National Guard and Air National Guard units to be called into active military service for this purpose.

11052.s: This order sets up Cabinet and interagency committees to oversee the Long Term Arrangement on trade in cotton textiles. It directs the Secretary of State to handle the related negotiations, including bilateral textile agreements, and to lead the U.S. delegation to the Cotton Textiles Committee. It also directs the Commissioner of Customs to take actions needed to carry out the arrangement for cotton textiles and cotton textile products entering the United States or coming out of warehouse for consumption.

11051.s: This order gives the Director of the Office of Emergency Planning a central role in coordinating federal emergency preparedness. It directs the Director to help plan for national emergencies, civil defense, continuity of government, emergency telecommunications, and the use of resources and supplies. It also assigns duties on stockpiling strategic materials, reviewing imports that may threaten national security, and working with state and local governments on emergency planning.

11050.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between REA Express and certain of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the carrier and its employees may not change the working conditions involved except by agreement.

11049.s: The order gives the Secretary of Commerce a role in carrying out the Public Works Acceleration Act. The Secretary is to receive and coordinate proposals from federal agencies, make recommendations to the President about fund allocations, and set rules and procedures for the act. It also says public works jobs should, when practical, give preference to qualified local labor, and federal agencies that receive funds must report to the Secretary and cooperate with him.

11048.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Interior responsibility for the civil administration of Wake Island, including executive, legislative, and most judicial authority there. It gives the Secretary of the Navy the same kind of responsibility for Midway Island. It also keeps certain public lands on the Midway Islands under Navy Department control and says these rules stay in force until Congress provides otherwise or the President changes them.

11047.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense and the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency joint authority to transfer certain functions from the Department of Defense to the Federal Aviation Agency. The transfers are limited to functions related to flight inspection of air navigation facilities. It also allows transfers of appropriations, records, and property needed for those function changes, but it does not require or allow the transfer of civilian or military personnel.

11045.s: This order ends the Guam Island Naval Defensive Sea Area and the Guam Island Naval Airspace Reservation. It also revokes three earlier executive orders, to the extent they still apply.

11044.s: This order sets procedures for coordination on United States arms control and disarmament policy. It requires the Director of the United States Arms Control and Disarmament Agency and other affected agencies to keep each other informed, resolve disagreements through consultation, and refer major unresolved disputes to the President. It also directs the Director to coordinate research, public information, international negotiations, and participation in control systems related to arms control and disarmament. The Secretary of Defense must keep the Director informed about armed forces levels and armaments, and the Director must provide policy statements for that planning.

11046.s: This order sets rules for awarding the Bronze Star Medal to people serving in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, or Coast Guard. It may be given for heroic or meritorious achievement or service not involving aerial flight while fighting an enemy of the United States, during military operations against a foreign force, or while serving with friendly foreign forces in an armed conflict. No more than one Bronze Star Medal may be awarded to one person, but a device may be given for later qualifying service, and the medal may be awarded after death.

11043.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Pan American World Airways and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For that time, and for thirty days after the report, Pan American and its employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute except by agreement.

11041.s: This order keeps the Peace Corps in the Department of State and gives the Secretary of State most of the President’s functions under the Peace Corps Act. It also lets the Secretary of State manage and transfer funds for the Peace Corps and directs the Civil Service Commission on one function under the Act. Some powers, including appointing the Peace Corps Director and Deputy Director, stay with the President.

11040.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between The Belt Railway Company of Chicago and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, The Belt Railway Company of Chicago and its employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

11042.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines) and certain of its employees represented by a labor organization. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the company and its employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute except by agreement.

11039.s: This order changes a previous order about the President's Commission on Campaign Costs. It adds language allowing funds from a corresponding appropriation for fiscal year 1963 and says the Commission will end on November 1, 1962.

11038.s: This order keeps Executive Order 10945 in effect, along with the delegations, rules, regulations, orders, licenses, and other administrative actions under it that were in place on June 30, 1962. It affects the administration of the Export Control Act of 1949.

11036.s: This order changes how foreign currencies earned under Title I of the act may be used. It gives priority to selling those currencies for dollars, unless that would conflict with the law or agreements, and lets the Director of the Bureau of the Budget set how much may be used for Section 104 purposes. It also gives certain presidential duties under Section 104 to the Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Director of the Bureau of the Budget.

11035.s: This order directs the Administrator of General Services to plan, manage, and review federal office space in the United States. It says existing government buildings should be used first, and private space should be rented only when government space is not available and at market rates. It also requires executive agencies to work with the Administrator, report changing space needs early, and review whether some services near the District of Columbia can be moved elsewhere without excessive costs or significant loss of efficiency.

11037.s: This order amends an earlier order about gold holdings. It says people subject to U.S. law may not, without a license, acquire or hold interests in certain gold coin, gold certificates, gold bullion outside the United States, or certain securities tied to gold. The Secretary of the Treasury may issue licenses for gold bullion used for legitimate industry, professional, or artistic needs, and may also allow certain rare coin collectors to hold, sell, or import specified gold coins until January 1, 1963.

11034.s: This order delegates many duties under the Mutual Educational and Cultural Exchange Act of 1961 to the Secretary of State, the Director of the United States Information Agency, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare. It also gives the Secretary of State primary responsibility for government-wide leadership and policy guidance on international educational and cultural affairs. The order keeps some powers with the President, sets rules for hiring, funding, and waivers, and takes effect immediately.

11032.s: This order amends the rules for the Army ration. It removes the words limiting the field ration to times of war or national emergency and changes “Secretary of War” to “Secretary of the military department concerned.” It also lets that secretary set procedures, including increased monetary allowances, to meet special feeding requirements.

11033.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate disputes between American Airlines and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report is made, American Airlines and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the disputes except by agreement.

11031.s: This order extends the Quetico-Superior Committee for four more years, through June 30, 1966. It reappoints three named members to the committee for that same period. The two other committee members will continue to be named by the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of the Interior.

11029.s: This order changes the title of Executive Order 11025 to say it creates a Board of Inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the tactical fighter production industry, which is part of the aircraft industry of the United States. It says there is a labor dispute at Republic Aviation Corporation and between a cafeteria concessionaire and certain employees represented by several unions. The order says the disputes led to a strike that affects a substantial part of the industry and, if it continues, could imperil national safety.

11028.s: This order transfers part of the Clark National Forest in Missouri to the Mark Twain National Forest, and part of the Mark Twain National Forest to the Clark National Forest. It also adds Round Island in Michigan to the Hiawatha National Forest. The order takes effect on July 1, 1962.

11026.s: This order amends a prior order about a labor dispute at Republic Aviation Corporation in Farmingdale, Long Island, New York. It says the dispute is between the company and certain employees represented by several unions, and between the cafeteria concessionaire at that facility and certain employees represented by Local 164.

11027.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate a dispute between the New York Central Railroad Company System, the Pittsburgh and Lake Erie Railroad Company, and certain of their employees represented by the Order of Railroad Telegraphers. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. From the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, the companies and their employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

11025.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into a labor dispute between Republic Aviation Corporation and some of its employees represented by Republic Lodge 1987 of the International Association of Machinists, AFL-CIO. The order says the strike affects a substantial part of the aircraft industry and could imperil national health and safety if it continues. The board must report to the President and may keep working after it submits its report as required by the Labor Management Relations Act.

11024.s: This order exempts Alan T. Waterman from compulsory retirement for age for an indefinite period of time. It affects Dr. Waterman, who was the Director of the National Science Foundation.

11023.s: This order gives the Secretary of Commerce power to handle many Coast and Geodetic Survey officer matters without further action by the President. It covers revoking or approving commissions, making temporary appointments and promotions, deferring retirement, accepting resignations, and ending appointments or promotions. It also lets the Secretary transfer vessels, equipment, stations, and personnel in a national emergency, and use public vessels for certain work with required approvals in some cases.

11022.s: This order creates the President's Council on Aging and sets out which federal officials will serve on it. The Council must study the federal government's responsibilities for problems of the aging, find issues that need coordinated action across agencies, and share information among federal, state, local, and private groups. It must also prepare an annual report to the President. The order also abolishes the earlier Federal Council on Aging.

11021.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Interior responsibility for civil government in all of the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands. It also gives the Secretary of the Interior the executive, legislative, and judicial authority needed for that administration, and lets that authority be carried out by Interior officers or other persons the Secretary designates. The President keeps the power to close parts of the territory for security reasons, and the Secretary of State must be kept informed and handle relations with the United Nations on trust territory matters.

11020.s: This order directs that certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for 1946 through 1962 be open to inspection during the 87th Congress. The Senate Committee on Armed Services, or a subcommittee it authorizes, may inspect them. The inspection is for its investigation of the acquisition, storage, and disposal of strategic and critical materials, and must follow Treasury rules.

11018.s: This order changes the rules for the President's Committee on Employment of the Handicapped. It raises the limit on Vice Chairmen from three to four. It also says the Chairman and Vice Chairmen are appointed by the President, and other members may be appointed from people, including representatives of organizations, who can help the committee reach its goals.

11019.s: This order amends a prior executive order about the Inter-American Development Bank. It says the bank’s designation under the International Organizations Immunities Act should not change the effect of a specific provision in the bank’s articles of agreement. It affects the Inter-American Development Bank and the legal rules that apply to it.

11017.s: This order creates the Recreation Advisory Council to help coordinate federal work on outdoor recreation resources. The council gives policy advice to federal agencies and helps improve cooperation on recreation policies and programs. It also asks federal agencies to share information and assist the council when requested.

11016.s: This order directs military departments to award the Purple Heart to members of the armed forces and certain civilian nationals of the United States who are wounded while serving under competent authority in listed combat situations. It also allows the award to be made posthumously if the person was killed or later died from the wound, and the wound must have required treatment by a medical officer. The order says the Purple Heart goes to the next of kin in posthumous cases, limits most people to one Purple Heart, and allows a Gold Star or other suitable device for later awards.

11014.s: This order delegates to the Secretary of Commerce the President’s functions related to U.S. participation in the New York World’s Fair. It asks other federal departments and agencies, including the Department of State, the United States Information Agency, and the National Science Foundation, to help with planning and providing for that participation. It also says buildings built by the United States for the fair are not “public buildings” under the Public Buildings Act of 1959, and it waives several laws and limits for Commerce’s work on the fair.

11015.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the Chicago and North Western Railway Company and certain employees represented by the Order of Railroad Telegraphers. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For that period, and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and the employees may not change the conditions involved except by agreement.

11012.s: This order changes who can make rules about travel and moving expenses for civilian federal employees who are transferred for permanent duty. It lets the Administrator of General Services set the rates for some reimbursed moving costs within the continental United States, without further presidential approval. It also keeps existing regulations in place until they are replaced and revokes several older executive orders when the new regulations take effect.

11013.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into a labor dispute between ship owners and operators and certain employees in the maritime industry. The dispute has led to a strike that affects a substantial part of the maritime industry and involves trade, commerce, and transportation among the states and with foreign nations. The Board must report to the President and then keep operating for any other duties allowed under the law until the President ends it.

11011.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Trans World Airlines and certain employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, AFL-CIO. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, Trans World Airlines and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute unless they agree to do so.

11010.s: This order changes how the Ryukyu Islands are governed under U.S. control. It sets up a civil administration under the Secretary of Defense, with a High Commissioner and a civilian Civil Administrator, and it changes how the legislative body, Chief Executive, and municipal heads are chosen. It also gives the High Commissioner power to make laws and regulations, veto or annul laws, remove officials, and take full authority in the islands if needed for security.

11009.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial to add rules for prosecuting certain bad check offenses under military law. It says making, drawing, uttering, or delivering a check, draft, or order without enough funds can be punished by court-martial in some cases. It also changes rules for using banking records and proof about returned checks in military cases.

11008.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company, other rail carriers, and certain employees. The board is to report its findings to the President, and no changes may be made in the disputed working conditions except by agreement while the order is in effect. It applies to the listed rail carriers and the railroad labor organizations named in the order.

11007.s: This order sets rules for how government departments and agencies may form and use advisory committees. It says these committees must be authorized by law or formally found to be in the public interest, and they may be used only for advisory purposes unless another law says otherwise. It also sets meeting rules, recordkeeping requirements, limits on industry advisory committees, and rules for when a committee must end unless it is continued in writing.

11006.s: The order creates a board of three members to investigate a dispute between Eastern Air Lines and certain of its employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, EAL Chapter. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, Eastern Air Lines and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

11005.s: This order gives the Interstate Commerce Commission emergency preparedness duties for domestic surface transportation and storage. It tells the Commission to plan for railroad, motor carrier, inland water, and storage needs in an emergency, and to guide states, industries, and other agencies on preparedness measures. It also directs the Commission to work on priorities, resource planning, salvage and rehabilitation, research, and coordination with the Department of Defense. The order says the President keeps the authority to put any emergency plan into effect.

11004.s: The order assigns the Housing and Home Finance Administrator responsibility for emergency planning and preparedness for lodging, housing, and related community facilities. It covers plans for new housing, damaged housing, emergency housing units, community facilities, and the movement of people from areas to be abandoned to areas where housing is available. It also directs work on housing resources, stockpiles, research, and cooperation with the Department of Defense and other agencies during an emergency.

11003.s: This order gives the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency duties for emergency planning and preparedness for the nation’s civil airports, civil aviation facilities, civil aviation services, and civil aircraft other than air carrier aircraft. It also covers planning for resources, priorities, training, damage assessment, monitoring of chemical, biological, and radiological agents, and recovery after attack. The Administrator must work with other agencies, but the President keeps the authority to put any emergency plan into effect.

11002.s: The order tells the Postmaster General to help build a national emergency registration system. It also directs the Post Office Department to plan for registering people and families so it can answer welfare inquiries and help reunite families in civil defense emergencies. The department must train postal employees, handle emergency cards, and keep a way to assess damage to postal service and resources after an attack.

11000.s: This order gives the Secretary of Labor responsibility for emergency preparedness plans and programs for civilian manpower, wages and salaries, worker protection, training, labor-management relations, and critical occupations. It also directs the Secretary to assess manpower resources and needs, develop guidance for using workers in an emergency, and keep a list of critical occupations. The order says emergency plans are part of the Labor Department’s continuing work, but only the President can put those plans into effect.

11001.s: This order gives the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare responsibility for emergency plans and preparedness programs for health services, welfare services, and education. It covers things like public health, health manpower, water supplies, food and drug safety, welfare aid, school instruction, and protection of health, welfare, and education facilities. It also directs the Secretary to work with other federal, state, local, and private groups, and to assess resources, stockpiles, damage, and research needs for emergencies, including an attack on the United States.

10999.s: This order gives the Secretary of Commerce responsibility for preparing national emergency plans and preparedness programs. It covers transportation, certain production and distribution matters, fallout forecasting, census data, economic stabilization, and other emergency planning tasks. It also directs the Secretary to work with other federal agencies, the states, and the Department of Defense on these functions.

10998.s: This order assigns the Secretary of Agriculture to prepare national emergency plans and preparedness programs for food resources, farm equipment, fertilizer, rural fire control, biological, chemical, and radiological defense, and rural defense information and education. It covers planning for production, processing, storage, distribution, salvage, rehabilitation, financial aid, stockpiles, research, and coordination with state and local governments and other agencies. It affects the Department of Agriculture, farmers, food industries, and others involved in these agricultural and rural functions.

10997.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Interior to prepare national emergency plans and preparedness programs for electric power, petroleum and gas, solid fuels, and minerals. It also gives the Secretary duties for priorities and allocations, resource planning, stockpiles, salvage, research, and cooperation with other agencies and the Department of Defense. The order says the Secretary may not put any emergency plan into effect, because that authority is reserved to the President.

10995.s: This order creates a Director of Telecommunications Management in the executive branch. The director coordinates government telecommunications activities, helps set policies and standards, and handles government radio frequency assignments through the Office of Emergency Planning. It also allows advisory committees and says federal departments and agencies must cooperate, while leaving the Federal Communications Commission’s authority in place.

10996.s: This order sets rules for agreements between the Secretary of Defense and state officials about withholding pay from civilian Army National Guard and Air National Guard employees. The withheld pay is for state or state-sponsored retirement, disability, or death benefits programs, if state law allows it and the employees are eligible. It also assigns the Army and Air Force to carry out the withholding and payment procedures and says the United States is not subject to extra state burdens or penalties.

10993.s: This order transfers lands in Michigan from the Marquette National Forest to the Hiawatha National Forest and abolishes the Marquette National Forest. It also changes land descriptions for part of the Nebraska National Forest and for lands in the Wasatch National Forest in Utah. The order further corrects and adds land descriptions in parts of Utah.

10992.s: This order relocates and redefines the exterior boundaries of the Caribbean National Forest in Puerto Rico. It says all U.S. lands within those new boundaries are reserved as part of the forest.

10991.s: This order changes the membership of the commission created by Executive Order No. 10929. It says the commission will have nine members: three chosen from nominees of the carriers, three from nominees of the employees, and three members, including the chairman, without nominations. The commission is for a controversy between certain carriers and certain of their employees.

10994.s: This order sets up the President's Committee on Employment of the Handicapped and an Advisory Council. The committee is directed to help increase employment opportunities for physically and mentally handicapped people by giving information to employers, running public education, and working with federal, state, and local groups. It also changes the earlier committee on employment of the physically handicapped and moves its members, records, property, funds, and pending business to the new committee.

10990.s: This order sets up the Federal Safety Council in the Department of Labor. The council advises the Secretary of Labor on safety for civilian federal employees and employees of the municipal government of the District of Columbia. It also advises on safety programs, work hazards, health risks, and ways to prevent injuries and accidents in federal employment. The order replaces an earlier executive order on the same council.

10989.s: This order amends an earlier rule on extra pay for enlisted members of the uniformed services for sea and foreign duty. It adds certain duty on artificial islands, such as Texas Towers, on the outer Continental Shelf outside U.S. territorial waters. It also covers some time spent ashore or temporarily based ashore, and some duty while based or stationed ashore if it lasts at least eight consecutive days.

10988.s: This order sets rules for employee-management relations in the Federal service. It protects federal employees’ right to form, join, assist, or refuse to join employee organizations, and limits that right when there is a conflict of interest or it would go against law or official duties. It also sets rules for recognizing employee organizations and for consulting with them on personnel policies, working conditions, and grievances. Agencies must issue policies to carry out the order.

10986.s: This order changes the membership of the Interdepartmental Highway Safety Board. It names the Secretary of Commerce as chairman and includes the Secretary of Defense, the Postmaster General, the Secretary of Labor, the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare, the Chairman of the Interstate Commerce Commission, and the Administrator of General Services.

10987.s: This order requires each department and agency to set up a system for reconsidering adverse actions against employees. It says employees may seek review in writing, may ask for a hearing in some cases, and may be accompanied and represented by someone they choose. The order also says appeals should be handled without undue delay and gives the Civil Service Commission rules and review duties. It does not apply to certain agencies named in the order, and some classes of employees may be excluded if the work makes the order inappropriate.

10985.s: This order amends earlier rules on safeguarding official information for national security. It removes several agencies from the lists in Executive Order 10501 and adds the Agency for International Development, the Office of Emergency Planning, the Peace Corps, the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board, the United States Arms Control and Disarmament Agency, and the Federal Maritime Commission. It also says the added agencies are treated as having had authority to classify information or material from the dates they were established.

10984.s: This order amends Selective Service regulations on registration, classification, appeal, and physical examination procedures. It adds a new Class I-Y for registrants qualified for military service only in time of war or national emergency, and changes Class IV-F to cover registrants not qualified for any military service. It also changes rules for duplicate registration and classification notices, appeal board handling, and how local boards and examining stations handle registrants and records during physical examinations.

10983.s: This order designates the Caribbean Organization as a public international organization. It gives the organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also revokes part of Executive Order 10025 that relates to the Caribbean Commission.

10981.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for 1950 through 1961 open to inspection by the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is tied to the committee’s investigation of the administration, operation, and enforcement of the Internal Security Act of 1950 and other internal security laws. The inspection must follow Treasury rules, and the order takes effect when it is filed for publication in the Federal Register.

10980.s: This order creates the President's Commission on the Status of Women. The commission is directed to review sex discrimination and make recommendations on employment, wages, labor laws, civil and property rights, family relations, and services for women as wives, mothers, and workers. Federal departments and agencies are required to cooperate with the commission, and it must submit a final report to the President by October 1, 1963.

10979.s: This order amends an earlier order about the President’s Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service. It says the award may be given to civilian federal officers or employees for achievements that improve government operations or serve the public interest, and lists the kinds of achievements that can qualify. It also says nominations need the concurrence of the employee’s agency head, and generally no more than five awards may be made in one year. People appointed by the President are not eligible unless the Board finds they are serving in a career position.

10982.s: This order sets rules for evacuation payments, assignments, and allotments for civilian employees of Federal agencies in foreign areas. It gives the Secretary of State and the Civil Service Commission power to carry out certain functions under the act. It also limits advance payments to no more than thirty days and sets conditions for extending monetary allowances beyond sixty days. Federal agencies must issue regulations and get prior approval before making payments under the act or this order.

10978.s: This order creates an award program for significant contributions to the Export Expansion Program. It sets up two awards: the President's "E" Award and the President's "E" Certificate of Service. The awards may go to persons, firms, and organizations that help expand the export trade of the United States, and recipients may be allowed to use the emblem in advertising and give employees a pin.

10976.s: This order says that on NASA public work, laborers and mechanics do not have to be limited to eight hours in one day during the national emergency. It also says they must be paid overtime at no less than time and one-half under applicable law. The order applies to laborers and mechanics employed by NASA on public work.

10977.s: This order creates the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal, with ribbons and appurtenances, for members of the Armed Forces of the United States. It applies to personnel who took part after July 1, 1958, in a United States military operation in significant numbers and who met the conditions described by the Joint Chiefs of Staff involving foreign armed opposition or imminent hostile action. The medal is to be awarded under uniform regulations, only when no other United States campaign medal is approved, and only one medal may be given to any one person. It may also be awarded posthumously.

10975.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Pan American World Airways and certain of its employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International. The board members are to be appointed by the President and may not have a financial or other interest in any airline employee group or carrier. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For that period, and for thirty days after the report, Pan American World Airways and its employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

10974.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Campaign Costs. The commission will study the costs of campaigning in presidential elections and prepare recommendations on better ways to finance expenses required of nominees for President and Vice President. It will be made up of up to twelve members from outside the Government, and it may ask people to provide information to help its work.

10973.s: This order divides foreign assistance duties among the Department of State, the Department of Defense, and other agencies. It establishes the Agency for International Development in the Department of State and puts the Office of Small Business there as well. It also assigns foreign assistance funds to the Secretaries of State and Defense and keeps some functions for the President.

10972.s: This order changes a prior executive order that dealt with administration of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act. It removes one exception clause from section 4(d) and deletes paragraph (5) from that section.

10971.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Trans World Airlines and certain employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, Trans World Airlines and its employees cannot change the disputed working conditions except by agreement.

10970.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the power to set maximum per-diem travel allowances for civilian government officers and employees when they are in travel status in foreign areas. It also keeps the existing maximum per-diem allowances in effect until the Secretary of State or the Director of the Bureau of the Budget changes them. The order also amends a prior executive order to cover travel status outside foreign areas.

10969.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Reading Company and certain of its employees represented by the International Organization of Masters, Mates and Pilots, Local No. 14. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report is made, the company and its employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute except by agreement.

10967.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Interior responsibility for the civil administration of Palmyra Island. It gives the Secretary executive, legislative, and most judicial authority for the island, and allows that authority to be carried out through Interior offices or other federal officers and agencies. The Secretary may also give the U.S. District Court for the District of Hawaii additional jurisdiction and judicial duties for this purpose.

10966.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1947 through 1961 open to inspection by the House Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for studies of government activities to judge economy and efficiency. It must follow Treasury rules for inspecting tax returns.

10965.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Trans World Airlines, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, neither Trans World Airlines nor its employees may change the conditions that led to the dispute except by agreement.

10964.s: This order amends rules for classifying, downgrading, and declassifying defense information and material. It sets marking and review rules, adds automatic downgrade or declassification schedules for some information, and keeps special handling rules for restricted data, communications intelligence, and cryptography. It also updates storage and transmission rules for classified material and directs agencies to take prompt action against government personnel who knowingly make unauthorized disclosures.

10962.s: This order allows certain tax returns to be inspected by the Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations. The commission may use the returns for studies and investigations about coordinating and simplifying tax laws and administrative practices. The stated goal is to help create a more orderly and less competitive fiscal relationship between levels of government and reduce the burden of compliance for taxpayers.

10963.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the Pullman Company, the Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul & Pacific Railroad Company, and certain of their employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days, and for that period and thirty days after the report, no changes may be made in the disputed working conditions except by agreement.

10960.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about functions that were tied to the President. It gives authority to receive reports, decide when certain land or property is no longer needed by the United States, and convey that land or property to the State of Hawaii. It affects land or property covered by section 5(e) of the Hawaii statehood act.

10961.s: This order sets up a President’s Committee to help with the National Medal of Science. The committee receives recommendations for the medal from the National Academy of Sciences and other national scientific or engineering groups, then sends its own recommendations to the President. It also sets deadlines for recommendations and awards, and says the National Science Foundation may provide staff and administrative services.

10959.s: This order allows Mr. Maurice L. Kowal to be appointed to a competitive position in the classified civil service of the United States. It lets that appointment be made without following the competitive provisions of the Civil Service Rules and regulations.

10957.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense, and some military secretaries he designates, authority to order units and certain Ready Reserve members to active duty without their consent. It limits that service to no more than 12 straight months and says no more than 250,000 Ready Reserve members may be on active duty without consent at one time. It also lets the Secretary of Defense extend enlistments, appointments, active duty, training duty, obligated service, or other military status that would expire before July 1, 1962, for up to 12 more months.

10958.s: This order delegates federal civil defense functions on stockpiling medical supplies and equipment to the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare, and stockpiling food to the Secretary of Agriculture. It also lets each secretary redelegate those functions to subordinates. The order provides for the transfer of related property, personnel, records, and funds, and it supersedes prior executive orders to the extent they cover these functions.

10955.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the President’s functions under sections 2 and 3 of the 1960 law on assistance for the development of Latin America and the reconstruction of Chile. It also says funds appropriated for those sections are to be treated as allocated to the Secretary of State or to subordinates he designates. This affects the State Department and the use of those funds.

10954.s: This order amends a previous executive order about who may inspect certain tax returns. It says the order applies to inspection by State tax officials of estate and gift-tax returns made under the Internal Revenue Code of 1954. It also says the order is effective as of January 18, 1961.

10956.s: This order changes Executive Order No. 10841, which deals with international cooperation under the Atomic Energy Act of 1954. It says each determination under one paragraph must be referred to the President and, unless he disapproves it, it becomes effective after that referral or at a later time stated in the determination.

10952.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense most civil defense functions under the Federal Civil Defense Act of 1950, under the President’s direction and control. It includes plans for fallout shelters, chemical, biological, and radiological defense, warning systems, emergency help to state and local governments after an attack, and financial contributions to the states. It also gives the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization a role in advising and assisting the President on civil defense policy, coordination, and continuity of government plans.

10951.s: This order extends the deadline for a board of inquiry to report to the President. The board is looking into issues in a labor dispute involving the maritime industry of the United States.

10949.s: The order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into a labor dispute between certain ship owners and operators and their employees represented by several maritime unions. It says the strike affects a substantial part of the maritime industry and could, if it continues, imperil the national health and safety. The board must report to the President and then continue to carry out other duties under the law until the President ends it.

10950.s: This order designates the Secretary of the Interior to approve land selections made by the State of Alaska that include land north and west of the line named in the Alaska Statehood Act. No such selection may be approved without the concurrence of the Secretary of Defense or a designated representative. The Secretary of the Interior may also let certain Interior and Bureau of Land Management officials exercise this authority.

10947.s: This order allows the House Committee on Public Works, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for 1950 through 1961. The inspection is for the committee’s investigation of the policies, procedures, and practices used in administering the Federal-Aid Highway Program. The inspections must follow Treasury rules for congressional review of returns.

10948.s: This order sets up a Presidential commission to look into a dispute between certain carriers in the New York Harbor Carriers' Conference Committee and certain of their employees. The commission is to investigate the carriers' proposal, hold hearings, and make findings and recommendations to the President. Federal departments and agencies are directed to help the commission with information and assistance.

10946.s: This order sets up a commission to develop ways to handle labor problems at missile and space sites. It also calls for local labor committees at each site to help settle disputes before they lead to work stoppages. The order asks federal agencies, labor groups, and employers to work together on grievance and labor problem procedures, and it directs the National Labor Relations Board to use faster procedures where allowed by law.

10945.s: This order delegates the President’s powers under the Export Control Act of 1949 to the Secretary of Commerce, with power to delegate them again. It also sets up the Export Control Review Board, made up of the Secretaries of Commerce, State, and Defense, to review certain export license matters involving national security or major policy issues and make recommendations. The Secretary of Commerce must report on the law’s administration, and the President may issue rules and specific directives. The order also replaces earlier export control actions listed in the order and leaves other existing export control actions in place unless they conflict with it.

10943.s: This order designates the Coffee Study Group as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the group the privileges, exemptions, and immunities allowed by that law. It also says this does not limit any other privileges, exemptions, or immunities the group may have from treaty or congressional action.

10944.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad Company, other carriers, and certain of their employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. From the date of the order and for thirty days after the report, the railroad companies and their employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute unless they agree to do so.

10942.s: This order changes the official description of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration seal. It updates the design details and the words shown on the seal. It affects the agency's official seal.

10941.s: This order sets a line of succession for who will act as Secretary of the Treasury if the Secretary and Under Secretary are dead, resign, absent, or sick. It names the Under Secretary for Monetary Affairs first, then certain Assistant Secretaries and the General Counsel in the order set by the Secretary or by their office dates. It also revokes a 1955 executive order on the same subject.

10940.s: This order creates the President's Committee on Juvenile Delinquency and Youth Crime and a Citizens Advisory Council. The committee is told to review and coordinate federal work on juvenile delinquency and youth crime, encourage cooperation and information sharing, and make recommendations on prevention, treatment, and control. Federal departments and agencies are directed to cooperate with the committee and provide information and assistance.

10939.s: This order applies to top officials in federal departments and agencies, certain presidential appointees, and White House staff. It bars them from outside work or activities that conflict with their duties or create the appearance of using public office for private gain, special treatment, or harm to public trust. It also limits them from taking extra compensation or gifts for work tied to their official role, while allowing some expense reimbursement, charitable or civic participation, and awards for public service. Department and agency heads must issue or review internal rules to maintain high ethical and moral standards.

10938.s: This order creates the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board to advise the President on foreign intelligence activities related to foreign policy, national defense, and security. The board must review the work of the Central Intelligence Agency and other agencies with similar duties and report to the President at least every six months. Its members are to come from outside the government, and the order revokes Executive Order 10656.

10936.s: This order requires federal departments, agencies, and other government bodies to report certain identical bids to the Attorney General. It applies to public bids for buying or selling property or services over $10,000, with an exception for bid proceedings involving only foreign sources and work done outside the United States. The Attorney General may set exemptions and change the $10,000 limit, and may invite state and local governments to send similar reports.

10935.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for 1945 to 1961 open to inspection by the House Committee on Un-American Activities, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for investigations allowed under House rules and must follow Treasury rules for viewing returns.

10934.s: This order establishes the Administrative Conference of the United States. The Conference is set up to help the President, Congress, and federal departments and agencies improve administrative procedures by studying their efficiency, adequacy, and fairness. It includes members from federal agencies, the practicing bar, scholars, and other people with knowledge of federal administrative procedures. Federal departments and agencies are directed to cooperate with the Conference and provide needed information and assistance.

10932.s: This order changes the outside boundaries of several national forests in Illinois, Michigan, Missouri, and Wisconsin. It excludes certain lands from the Chequamegon, Clark, Hiawatha, Huron, Marquette, Mark Twain, Nicolet, Ottawa, and Shawnee National Forests. The lands excluded are described in detail in the order.

10933.s: This order lets Emergency Board No. 136 make its report to the President any day before May 24, 1961. It also says the thirty-day period after the board’s report under the Railway Labor Act is included in this extension of time.

10931.s: This order updates the rules for the President's Council on Youth Fitness. It says the council is made up of several Cabinet officials and the Housing and Home Finance Administrator, with the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare as chairman. It also revokes three earlier orders that amended the same section.

10930.s: This order abolishes the Government Patents Board and the positions created under it. It transfers most of the Board’s functions to the Secretary of Commerce, who may assign them within the Department of Commerce. It also directs the Secretary of Commerce to handle the Board’s property, personnel, records, and funds, while existing actions and rules stay in effect unless changed later.

10929.s: This order creates a Presidential commission to look into a dispute between certain carriers and some of their employees. The commission is to investigate the issues, hold public hearings if needed, and report its findings and recommendations to the President. Federal departments and agencies are directed to cooperate with the commission and provide information and assistance allowed by law.

10928.s: This order abolishes the Committee on Government Activities Affecting Prices and Costs. It also revokes the executive order that created that committee.

10927.s: This order abolishes the President's Committee on Fund-Raising Within the Federal Service and revokes the order that created it. It directs the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission to arrange for certain national voluntary agencies to ask Federal employees and members of the armed forces for donations at their places of work or duty. The order says these solicitations must be voluntary, may be kept confidential, and are limited to set periods and no more than three times a year except in emergency or disaster appeals.

10926.s: This order extends the deadline for an emergency board to report its findings to the President. The board is investigating a dispute between Pan American World Airways, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, PAA Chapter.

10925.s: This order creates the President’s Committee on Equal Employment Opportunity. The Committee is directed to study federal employment practices and recommend steps to stop discrimination in government employment. It also requires government contracts to include nondiscrimination clauses and puts related duties on contractors, subcontractors, and labor unions connected to those contracts.

10924.s: The order creates an agency in the Department of State called the Peace Corps and places it under a Director. It gives the Peace Corps responsibility for training and service abroad by men and women of the United States in new programs of assistance to nations and areas of the world, along with support for existing economic assistance programs. The Secretary of State is directed to delegate needed functions to the Director and provide financing for the Peace Corps from funds available under the Mutual Security Act of 1954.

10922.s: This order changes a previous order that set up a commission to look into a dispute between certain air carriers and their employees. It adds Western Airlines to the air carriers covered by that commission.

10921.s: This order creates a Presidential commission to look into disputes over the flight engineer job, job security for employees in that role, and related union representation rights. The commission covers certain employees and carriers, including Pan American World Airways, American Airlines, Trans World Airways, Eastern Airlines, National Airlines, and Flying Tigers. It is directed to investigate the issues, hold public hearings if needed, and report findings and recommendations to the President. Federal departments and agencies are told to cooperate with the commission and provide information and assistance.

10923.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between Northwest Airlines and certain employees represented by the International Association of Machinists. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, Northwest Airlines and its employees may not change the conditions that led to the disputes unless they agree to do so.

10919.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Pan American World Airways and certain of its employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, PAA Chapter. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, Pan American and its employees may not change the working conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10920.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 10700, which was entitled "Further Providing for the Operations Coordinating Board." It affects that executive order and its amendments.

10918.s: This order creates the President's Advisory Committee on Labor-Management Policy. The committee includes the Secretary of Labor, the Secretary of Commerce, and 19 other members chosen by the President from the public, labor, and management. It is directed to study labor-management policy and advise the President on collective bargaining, industrial peace, wages and prices, living standards, productivity, world competition, and the effects of automation and other technological changes. Federal departments and agencies are told to cooperate with the committee and provide information and assistance.

10917.s: This order abolishes two advisory committees on government organization and management improvement. It transfers the remaining work of one committee to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget and revokes one executive order while deleting a section of another.

10916.s: This order makes certain income, estate, and gift tax returns from 1947 through 1961 open to inspection by the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee’s study of government activities at all levels and its review of the economy and efficiency of government. The inspection must follow the rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

10915.s: This order changes two earlier executive orders to add duties for the Director of the Food-for-Peace Program. The director is put in charge of continuous supervision and coordination of certain government functions, subject to the President’s direction. It applies to officers and agencies handling these food-for-peace and related mutual security functions.

10914.s: This order directs the Secretary of Agriculture to expand and improve the food distribution program throughout the United States. It says more food should be made available to needy families through state and local agencies. The order also calls for a greater variety and quantity of food using existing funds and legal authority.

10913.s: This order updates rules for carrying out the Watershed Protection and Flood Prevention Act. It gives the Secretary of Agriculture responsibilities for approving planning help, setting criteria and standards, coordinating with other federal agencies, and holding public hearings when needed. It also requires notice to state governors and several federal agencies when surveys or field investigations begin, and it sets coordination steps for irrigation, flood protection, watershed protection, and fish and wildlife development.

10911.s: This order says income tax returns made under the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 may be inspected by the Department of Commerce. The inspection must follow rules and regulations set by the Acting Secretary of the Treasury.

10912.s: This order amends a prior order that set up how the International Cultural Exchange and Trade Fair Participation Act of 1956 is carried out. It changes how certain functions are assigned and says the Director of the United States Information Agency may allocate funds to that agency, the Department of State, the Department of Commerce, and other agencies as appropriate. It also covers functions related to liquidating affairs for the Universal and International Exhibition of Brussels, 1958, and updates a reference in the earlier order.

10909.s: This order changes an earlier order about safeguarding classified information within industry. It updates which federal officials count as a “head of a department” and who may issue invitations and requests for people to appear and testify. It also says some invited government workers or service members may get travel expenses and per diem, and it adds authority for a deputy or principal assistant in certain cases.

10908.s: This order allows the Federal Trade Commission to inspect corporate income tax returns filed under the Internal Revenue Code of 1954. The inspection must follow rules set by the Acting Secretary of the Treasury. It affects corporations whose tax returns may be reviewed by the Commission.

10910.s: This order sets up the National Medal of Science as a bronze medal with a set design and a parchment citation for each recipient.
