The President awards it to individuals who deserve special recognition for outstanding contributions to knowledge in the physical, biological, mathematical, or engineering sciences. No more than twenty people may receive the medal in one calendar year. It may also be awarded after death to certain people who met the citizenship or lawful permanent residence rules and died within the past five years.

10907.s: This order says income tax returns made under the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 must be open to inspection by the Renegotiation Board. The inspection must follow the rules and regulations set by the Acting Secretary of the Treasury. It affects income tax returns and the Renegotiation Board.

10905.s: This order changes the definition of who is covered under the earlier order. It also adds rules that bar people subject to U.S. jurisdiction from acquiring, holding, or keeping certain gold coin, gold certificates, gold bullion, and some securities outside the United States unless they have a license. The Secretary of the Treasury may issue licenses for some of this property, including certain holdings acquired before the rule took effect and some gold bullion needed for legitimate use in an industry, profession, or art.

10906.s: This order lets certain people and State and Federal government offices inspect some tax returns, if they follow Treasury rules. It applies to returns for several taxes under the Internal Revenue Code of 1954. It also replaces an earlier order for State tax officials looking at estate and gift-tax returns.

10904.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between certain carriers represented by the New York Harbor Carriers' Conference Committee and certain of their employees represented by the Lighter Captains' Union, Local 996, I.L.A. The board must report its findings to the President within the time set in the order, and no changes may be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose except by agreement during that period and for the period after the report.

10903.s: This order gives the Secretary of State power to issue regulations on several allowance and benefit matters for government personnel on overseas duty. It covers employee definitions, allowances and differentials, travel for dependents, storage and transportation of personal effects, leave rules, quarters allowances, cost-of-living allowances, and unhealthful posts. It also revokes several older executive orders and keeps existing rules in place until they are replaced under this order.

10902.s: This order directs the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization to set up a series of "Emergency Preparedness Orders" for civil-defense and defense-mobilization planning. It says these orders should help executive branch departments and agencies develop plans and programs for national emergencies, including attack on the United States. Department and agency heads are to develop those plans under the Director's policy direction and central program control. The order also says it does not give authority to put any of those plans or programs into effect.

10901.s: This order amends rules for classifying defense information in the executive branch. It lists certain departments and agencies that may classify information, limits some others to classification by the head of the agency without delegation, and says agencies not named do not have that authority unless it is later given to them. It also revokes earlier memoranda from 1953, 1959, and 1960.

10899.s: This order lets the Central Intelligence Agency share certain Restricted Data and data removed from that category for intelligence purposes. The sharing must follow the terms of agreements for cooperation under the Atomic Energy Act. It also says no communication can happen until it is authorized under approved procedures by the Atomic Energy Commission and the Department of Defense.

10900.s: This order gives the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of State many of the President’s duties under the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954. It also assigns parts of the Act to other agencies, including the Department of Agriculture, the Department of State, the Export-Import Bank, the Department of Defense, the United States Information Agency, and others. The order sets rules for how foreign currencies under the Act are to be used and managed. It keeps the President’s reporting duties under section 108.

10897.s: This order gives the Secretary of State authority to make rules for the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System. It also lets the Secretary set regulations for certain Foreign Service staff officers and employees who take part in the system, and for voluntary contributions to the retirement and disability fund. It supersedes a 1948 executive order and says the order is effective as of October 16, 1960.

10898.s: This order creates the Interdepartmental Highway Safety Board to give Federal leadership and coordination on traffic safety for public streets and highways. The Board is made up of several cabinet and agency officials, and agencies may provide alternate members and help staff the Board. It works to guide Federal traffic safety programs, study traffic safety needs, consult with State and local officials and other related interests, and report to the President on national progress in traffic safety.

10895.s: This order says that, for the rules in section 1586, an employee assigned to duty in Alaska or Hawaii will be treated as assigned outside the United States. It applies to civilian employees of the Defense Establishment covered by those rules. The Secretary of Defense must review whether the order should stay in effect and recommend revoking it if needed.

10894.s: This order establishes the President's Committee on Migratory Labor. The committee is made up of certain federal officials and may ask other federal agencies to join its work. It is directed to review the needs of migrant workers and their families, help federal agencies coordinate programs and services, and work with state, local, civic, church, employer, and worker groups to improve their living and working conditions.

10896.s:
This order amends a previous executive order and revokes sections 3 and 7. It also changes the first paragraph of section 5 by removing a proviso and changing punctuation.

It says the amendment does not change acts already done, rights already earned, or cases already started before it took effect. Existing licenses, orders, rules, and regulations under the earlier order stay in effect until the Secretary of the Treasury changes them.

10892.s: This order changes the rules for incentive pay for submarine duty. It says service members attached to an active submarine, including one under construction during builders' trials, can receive this pay. It also covers operators or crew members of operational self-propelled submersibles, including undersea exploration and research vehicles, and for nuclear-powered submarines it includes training and rehabilitation periods after assignment as decided by the Secretary of the Navy.

10893.s: This order divides responsibility for mutual security functions among the Secretary of State, Secretary of Defense, Secretary of the Treasury, Secretary of Commerce, the Development Loan Fund, and the United States Information Agency. It also keeps some functions with the President and says U.S. diplomatic mission chiefs abroad are responsible for coordination and supervision of agency work in their countries. The order covers how funds, personnel, studies, and foreign assistance functions are to be handled under the listed laws.

10891.s: This order creates a Presidential commission to look into a dispute between certain railroad carriers and some of their employees. The commission is directed to investigate the issues, hold public hearings if needed, and report its findings and recommendations to the President. Federal agencies are told to cooperate with the commission, and its work is tied to the controversy between the two sides.

10890.s: This order extends the boundaries of the Dixie National Forest in Utah to include certain federal lands. It also transfers other specified lands from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of the Interior for use, administration, or exchange under land-management laws. The transferred lands are subject to valid existing rights, and 25% of net revenues from grazing and other uses will still go to the counties where the lands are located.

10889.s: This order amends an earlier executive order by adding new presidential duties tied to Alaska and Hawaii. It lets the President handle certain Alaska functions, transfer some Alaska property to the State of Alaska without reimbursement until July 1, 1964, receive reports about Hawaii, decide when certain land or property is no longer needed by the United States, and set procedures for those Hawaii reports. It also replaces certain earlier presidential letters that had authorized other officers to use some of the Alaska authority.

10887.s: This order designates the Department of Commerce to carry out the functions given by the act, except for functions assigned to other agencies or to the President. It also asks other federal departments and agencies, including the Department of State and the National Science Foundation, to cooperate with the Department of Commerce. Any building built under the act will become a public building after the Exposition ends.

10888.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between certain carriers and some of their employees. The board must report its findings to the President, and the carriers and employees may not change the conditions out of which the dispute arose except by agreement during the stated period.

10886.s: This order suspends part of a law that limits how many Navy officers may serve as admiral and vice admiral. The suspension lasts until June 30 of the fiscal year after the national emergency declared in 1950 ends.

10885.s: This order allows Navy vessels that have been removed from the Naval Vessel Register, and are not covered by other law, to be sold at public sale to the highest acceptable bidder. The sale must be advertised for at least 30 days, and each bid must include a cash deposit of at least 10 percent or a deposit bond. No other bond is required. It also replaces Executive Order 10743.

10883.s: This order ends the Air Coordinating Committee. It also revokes two earlier executive orders about that committee. The Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency must make any needed arrangements to wind up the committee's remaining business.

10882.s: This order changes an earlier order about Treasury Department functions. It says the Secretary of the Treasury may issue orders to suspend or discontinue certain discriminating tonnage duties, imposts, and import duties when the required proof is obtained from the Department of State. It also covers partial suspension for foreign vessels and goods when another country gives similar privileges to U.S. vessels and merchandise.

10884.s: This order changes how parts of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954 are carried out. It gives the Secretary of Agriculture the President’s functions under Titles I and IV, unless the order says otherwise. It also says the President keeps the functions tied to reports to Congress and may later name the federal agency or agencies that will handle credit provisions and payments under Title IV agreements.

10881.s: This order changes the rules for travel payments for claimants and beneficiaries of the Veterans' Administration and their attendants. It lets the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs authorize a mileage allowance of up to five cents a mile instead of actual travel expenses, including lodging and subsistence, for travel to or from a Veterans' Administration facility for vocational rehabilitation, counseling, examination, treatment, or care. It also allows reimbursement for ferry fares and bridge, road, and tunnel tolls, and in some cases payment can be made before the travel is finished.

10880.s: This order allows certain federal and District of Columbia government employees in competitive service positions with indefinite or temporary appointments to have those appointments changed to career or career-conditional appointments if they meet the listed service, recommendation, and exam requirements. It also gives some employees who left to enter the armed forces a chance to have their appointments converted after reemployment, if they qualify. The order does not apply to postmasters, rural carriers, or employees serving under overseas limited appointments, and it sets special rules for substitute Postal Field Service employees.

10879.s: This order creates a White House Service Certificate for members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, and Air Force who have been detailed to White House duty for at least one year, other than Presidential Aides. It also creates a White House Service Badge that may be issued to armed forces members detailed to White House duty, other than Presidential Aides, and worn on the uniform during that detail. The certificate may be awarded only once to each person and may be granted after death.

10877.s:
The order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Pennsylvania Railroad Company and certain of its employees represented by railroad labor organizations. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days.

For that time period, and for thirty days after the report, the Pennsylvania Railroad Company and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10876.s: This executive order changes a prior order about inspection of income tax returns by the Senate Committee on the Judiciary. It expands the covered tax return years from 1945 to 1959. It also adds Senate Resolution 238 to the listed Senate resolutions authorizing the inspection.

10878.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate a dispute between the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad Company and other carriers and certain employees represented by the Switchmen's Union of North America, AFL-CIO. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the company, the other carriers, and their employees may not change the conditions out of which the dispute arose except by agreement.

10875.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad and other carriers, and certain of their employees. The disputes involve vacation and holiday rules, health and welfare plans, group life insurance, cost-of-living adjustments in basic wage rates, and a general wage increase. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For thirty days after the report, the railroad, the other carriers, and their employees may not change the working conditions involved except by agreement.

10873.s: This order designates the Inter-American Development Bank as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the bank the privileges, exemptions, and immunities that law provides. It also says this designation does not reduce any other privileges, exemptions, or immunities the bank may have from treaty or congressional action.

10874.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between The Long Island Railroad Company and certain employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For thirty days from the order and for thirty days after the report, neither the company nor its employees may change the conditions tied to the dispute unless they agree.

10871.s: This order opens certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1950 to 1959 to inspection by the House Committee on Public Works, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee’s investigation of the policies, procedures, and practices used in the administration of the Federal-aid highway program. It must follow the rules and regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

10872.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Pan American World Airways and certain of its employees represented by a labor organization. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, Pan American World Airways and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10870.s: The order designates the National Aeronautics and Space Administration facilities at Huntsville, Alabama, as the George C. Marshall Space Flight Center. Those facilities must afterward be called by that name.

10869.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule H for appointments to fourth-class postmaster positions. If the Civil Service Commission cannot certify enough eligible names, or if the pay is too low for regular competitive examinations, it may allow appointments under procedures it prescribes. People appointed under this rule may gain competitive status after a probationary period. It also revokes several older executive orders and regulations about fourth-class postmaster appointments.

10867.s: This order says the United States District Court for the District of Alaska is ready to take over the duties given to it. It ends the jurisdiction of the District Court for the Territory of Alaska. It also ends the terms of the judges, United States attorneys, marshals, and other officers of that territorial court.

10868.s:
This order creates a three-member board to investigate a labor dispute between the New York Central System and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days.

For thirty days from the order, and for thirty days after the board reports, the New York Central System and its employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute except by agreement.

10866.s: This order designates the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It says the organization is entitled to the privileges, exemptions, and immunities given by that law. It also says this designation does not take away any privileges, exemptions, or immunities the organization may have from treaty or congressional action.

10864.s: This order designates the Pan American Health Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities allowed by that law. The designation also includes the Pan American Sanitary Bureau and replaces its earlier designation.

10863.s: This order designates the Attorney General to seize and detain arms, munitions of war, and other articles when they are being exported or removed from the United States in violation of law. It also allows the Attorney General to delegate that authority to a Justice Department officer. The order applies to vessels, vehicles, and aircraft that contain those items or were used to export them.

10865.s: This order sets rules to protect classified defense information released to or within United States industry. It directs certain departments and agencies to make regulations for contracts and other information they must safeguard, and it allows access only when it is clearly consistent with the national interest. It also gives applicants notice, a chance to reply, and a chance to appear before a final denial or revocation, unless national security requires the department head to act without those procedures.

10861.s: This order suspends parts of section 5762 of title 10 that deal with promotions in the Supply Corps, Chaplain Corps, Civil Engineer Corps, Medical Service Corps, and related corps. It does not suspend the parts that require the Secretary of the Navy to give the selection board the number of officers or male officers who may be recommended for promotion. The suspension lasts until June 30 of the fiscal year after the national emergency proclaimed in 1950 ends.

10860.s: This order sets the design for the President of the United States’ coat of arms, seal, and flag. It describes the eagle, shield, stars, and colors to be used, and says the seal must include the coat of arms with the words “Seal of the President of the United States.” It also says these designs are to represent the President exclusively.

10862.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company—Coast Lines and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For that time, and for thirty days after the report is made, neither side may change the working conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10858.s: This order continues the President's Committee for Traffic Safety. The committee is to promote state and community use of the traffic safety Action Program, work with federal, state, and local officials, and encourage uniform traffic laws and balanced traffic-safety programs. It also may use advisory groups and help guide traffic safety education and highway safety efforts.

10857.s: This order says certain federal fish and wildlife functions in Alaska will end, and the same functions will be taken over by the State of Alaska. It also gives the Secretary of the Interior the power to transfer United States property in Alaska tied to those functions to the State of Alaska without reimbursement. The Secretary may pass some of that authority to certain Interior officials, and transfers must follow the Secretary’s policies and procedures.

10859.s: This order revokes Executive Order 10758, which established a career executive program within the civil service system. It also revokes Executive Order 10777, which had amended that program to increase the membership of the Career Executive Board.

10856.s: This order excuses many federal employees from duty for one-half day on December 24, 1959, the day before Christmas. It applies to executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies, including some named offices, unless they are excluded for public reasons or because existing law requires them to stay. It also tells agency heads to use a liberal policy for annual leave over the holiday period when consistent with the needs of the service.

10855.s: This order allows income tax returns from 1945 through 1958 to be open to inspection by the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee it authorizes, during the Eighty-sixth Congress. The inspection is for the committee’s study and investigation of how federal antitrust and anti-monopoly laws apply to professional boxing. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

10854.s: This order extends parts of the Federal Aviation Act of 1958 to certain areas outside the United States and the airspace above them, where the U.S. government has jurisdiction or control under an international treaty, agreement, or other lawful arrangement. It applies only as needed so the Federal Aviation Agency Administrator can carry out Titles III and XII of the act. Before acting under this authority, the Administrator must consult the Secretary of State on foreign relations and the Secretary of Defense on national defense.

10852.s: This order changes a prior executive order by replacing one phrase in section 4(b). The change narrows the wording from "capital grants with respect to projects assisted under Title I of the said act" to "grants under Title I of that act."

10853.s: This order sets rules for paying certain allowances and benefits to government personnel on foreign duty. It applies to overseas teachers and to veterans matters under title 38 of the United States Code. It also lets the Secretary of State and the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs issue the needed regulations, with an effective date no earlier than July 28, 1959.

10851.s: This order extends the boundaries of the Chattahoochee, Kisatchie, Holly Springs, and Ouachita National Forests. It adds certain United States lands in Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Oklahoma that were acquired under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 or Title III of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act. The added lands remain subject to existing leases and other valid rights.

10850.s: This order changes the outer boundaries of several national forests in Alabama, Florida, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, and South Carolina. It removes certain listed lands from the boundaries of those forests, and it also extends some boundaries to include other lands near the Apalachicola, De Soto, and Kisatchie National Forests. The lands affected include areas in private ownership and other lands described in the order.

10849.s: This order approves a seal as the official seal of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. It affects NASA by making the described design its official seal.

10848.s: This order changes the deadline for the Board of Inquiry to report to the President on a labor dispute affecting the steel industry. The report must be submitted on or before October 19, 1959.

10847.s: This order creates the Committee for Rural Development Program. The committee is made up of officials from several federal departments and agencies, and it is meant to give leadership and uniform policy guidance for rural-development work. It also directs federal departments and agencies to cooperate more closely with each other and with state, local, private, and other non-Federal participants in helping rural areas.

10846.s: This order directs that income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1950 through 1959 may be opened for inspection by the Senate Committee on Agriculture and Forestry, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for that committee’s study of the Commodity Credit Corporation and other activities of the Department of Agriculture. The committee must follow Treasury rules for inspecting returns.

10845.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about purchases made outside the United States or the District of Columbia under the Mutual Security Act of 1954. It allows those functions to be carried out without following section 3(b) of a law on defense contracts, but only when the executive or military department says the required clause or compliance with it is impracticable. It affects contracts covered by that purchase authority.

10844.s: This order extends the boundaries of the Wasatch National Forest in Utah to include certain federal lands. The lands were acquired under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 or Title III of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act, and some lands transferred to the Department of Agriculture are also included and reserved as part of the forest. It also revokes part of Executive Order 10046 for those lands.

10843.s: The order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into a labor dispute between steel-producing or steel-fabricating companies and employees represented by the United Steel Workers of America, AFL-CIO. It says the strike affects a substantial part of the steel industry and, if it continues, could endanger national health and safety. The board must report to the President and may continue to perform other duties under the Labor-Management Relations Act until the President ends it.

10842.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into certain labor disputes in the maritime industry. The disputes involve steamship companies, stevedores, marine carpenters, and other employers engaged in related pier activities, along with employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association (Independent). The board must report to the President and then may keep working until the President ends it.

10841.s: This order sets out how certain international cooperation agreements under the Atomic Energy Act are to be handled. It lets the Secretary of Defense and the Atomic Energy Commission make some required security findings together, and sends the matter to the President if they cannot agree. It also says the Secretary of State is responsible for negotiating and entering into the international agreements and for the foreign policy side of that cooperation.

10840.s: This order designates the Federal Aviation Agency as an agency covered by certain parts of the Assignment of Claims Act of 1940. It lets FAA contracts, in the same way as certain other federal contracts, include terms that protect payments made to an assignee from reduction or set-off. It affects contracts of the Federal Aviation Agency and the people or companies receiving assigned payments under those contracts.

10838.s: This order changes one part of an earlier order about the Operations Coordinating Board. It says the Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs will represent the Secretary of State on the board.

10839.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Secretary of State if the Secretary and Under Secretary are dead, resigned, absent, or sick. It says certain officers of the Department of State would act as Secretary of State in the order listed until a successor is appointed or the absence or sickness ends. The President may also direct another officer to act as Secretary of State, and this order replaces Executive Order No. 10791.

10837.s: This order changes Selective Service rules on who counts as a governor or state, and it defines the term "continental United States." It also changes how appeal board areas are set up in some places and how local boards handle permits for registrants to leave the United States. The order also updates rules for registration, classification, physical examinations, induction, and civilian work for men outside the United States and in certain U.S. areas.

10836.s: This order amends a prior executive order to change which presidential powers can be carried out under it. It covers approval of land to be acquired by condemnation, contracts for the purchase of lands, and agreements between the National Capital Planning Commission and officials of Maryland and Virginia. It also covers transitional grants to the State of Alaska and requests for federal agencies to keep providing services or facilities in Alaska for an interim period, along with the funds needed for those services or facilities.

10835.s: This order gives the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission the power to make certain determinations for Presidential awards and honorary recognition. The Chairman may decide which government activity or activities mainly benefit from a civilian officer or employee’s suggestion, invention, superior accomplishment, or other personal effort. The President does not need to approve or ratify those decisions.

10833.s: This order transfers title to a 202-acre tract of land at Sand Island in the Territory of Hawaii, along with the improvements on it, to the Territory of Hawaii. It also keeps certain United States easements and utilities in place, and requires the Territory of Hawaii to relocate the Navy tower and related facilities on the southern shore of Sand Island. The transferred land remains subject to airport zoning laws and other terms listed in the order.

10832.s: This order revokes Executive Order 9887. That earlier order had given certain privileges, exemptions, and immunities to the Preparatory Commission for the International Refugee Organization and the International Refugee Organization. The order says those organizations have ceased to exist.

10831.s: This order creates the Federal Radiation Council and places it in the hands of top officials from Defense, Commerce, Health, Education, and Welfare, and the Atomic Energy Commission. The Council advises the President on radiation matters that affect health and helps coordinate agency steps to protect people from ionizing radiation. It may also get help and information from executive agencies and seek technical advice from other sources.

10830.s: This order approves a seal as the official seal of the President's Council on Youth Fitness. The seal has an open book, a torch, a laurel wreath, and a cloud with rays, with the council's name and date around it. It applies to the President's Council on Youth Fitness.

10829.s: The order directs that the flag of the United States be flown at half-staff until the burial of Fleet Admiral William D. Leahy. This applies to all Federal Government buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the District of Columbia and throughout the United States and its territories and possessions.

10828.s: This order designates the airport being built in Fairfax and Loudoun counties in Virginia as Dulles International Airport. It affects the airport under construction to provide facilities for the District of Columbia and its vicinity, and says it will be known by that name from then on.

10827.s: This order changes how foreign currencies received under the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act are used and managed. It sets which agencies handle different uses of those currencies, including loans, foreign aid, agriculture, defense, scientific information, and other listed purposes. It also gives the Secretary of the Treasury power to write rules for buying, holding, depositing, moving, and selling those foreign currencies, and it keeps report-making to Congress with the President.

10825.s: This order excuses many federal employees from duty all day on Friday, July 3, 1959, before the Fourth of July. It applies to employees in several executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies, including some field services. It does not apply to certain employees needed for national security or other public reasons, or to employees covered by special pay rules. Some employees who are not excused that day may be given another workday off in fiscal year 1960 without loss of pay or leave.

10824.s: This order designates the National Aeronautics and Space Administration as an agency covered by certain contract rules under the Assignment of Claims Act of 1940, as amended. It means NASA contracts can use the same payment assignment protections that apply to the Department of Defense, the General Services Administration, and the Atomic Energy Commission. The rule affects payments to assignees of money due under those contracts during a war or national emergency.

10823.s: This order sets the design of the President of the United States’ coat of arms, seal, and flag. It says the seal must use the coat of arms, and the flag must show the coat of arms on a dark blue background. These designs are to be used only to represent the President. It also replaces an earlier executive order and takes effect on July 4, 1959.

10822.s: This order changes how foreign-aid functions are handled under earlier executive orders. It gives some duties to the Department of State, the Department of Defense, the Development Loan Fund, the Director of the Bureau of the Budget, and several Federal agency heads. It also changes rules for some overseas personnel and revokes or revises several earlier sections and parts of earlier orders.

10821.s: This order changes the rules for when enlisted members of the uniformed services count as on sea duty for additional pay. It defines sea duty for members assigned to certain vessels, ship-based staff, aviation units, landing-craft squadrons, and motor-torpedo-boat squadrons, and it lists some duties that do not count as sea duty. It also says an enlisted member cannot get both sea-duty pay and foreign-duty pay for the same time, and cannot get sea-duty pay and credit for basic allowance for subsistence for the same time except in the stated cases.

10819.s: This order changes an earlier order about the defense mobilization program. It directs several federal departments and agencies, within production areas named by the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization, to develop and promote measures to expand productive capacity and the production and supply of materials and facilities needed for national defense.

10818.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1945 through 1959 open to inspection by the House Committee on Government Operations or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee’s studies of government activities at all levels to determine the economy and efficiency of the government. It must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

10820.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Secretary of the Air Force. If one of those offices is vacant because of death, disability, or absence, named officers in each department may act in that role in the order listed. The President may also choose a different eligible officer from the list, and any acting service is temporary and does not remove the person from their own office. The order also revokes two earlier executive orders.

10817.s: This order honors the memory of Donald A. Quarles, who was the late Deputy Secretary of Defense. It directs that the United States flag be flown at half-staff on Federal Government buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the District of Columbia and across the United States and its territories and possessions until his interment.

10815.s: The order says certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for 1945 through 1959 may be opened for inspection by the Committee on Un-American Activities of the House of Representatives, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for investigations allowed under House rules and must follow Treasury rules on inspecting tax returns by congressional committees.

10816.s: This order changes earlier rules for safeguarding official defense information. It says some departments and agencies without original classification authority are still covered by the declassification rules for defense material. It also lets agency heads allow outside historical researchers to see classified defense information if it is consistent with national defense and the person is trustworthy, and it changes how confidential defense material may be sent within the continental United States.

10814.s: This order lets the Securities and Exchange Commission inspect certain Internal Revenue Service transcript cards and corporate and individual income tax returns. The inspection is for gathering statistical information and for complying with budget-related directives or recommendations. It applies to returns for taxable years ending after the dates listed in the order.

10813.s: The order includes certain lands in Towns County and Union County, Georgia, in the Chattahoochee National Forest. It also includes certain lands in Cherokee County and Clay County, North Carolina, in the Nantahala National Forest. The lands are transferred under agreements between the Tennessee Valley Authority and the Department of Agriculture.

10812.s: This order approves an official flag for the United States Navy. The flag is dark blue with yellow fringe and a central Navy seal design above a scroll that says “UNITED STATES NAVY.” It applies to the United States Navy.

10810.s: This order lets the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs approve payment of travel costs for claimants and beneficiaries traveling with prior authorization to or from a Veterans' Administration facility or other place for vocational rehabilitation, counseling, examination, treatment, or care. It allows payment of actual travel expenses, including lodging and subsistence, or an allowance of up to five cents a mile instead. It also lets an attendant's travel expenses be paid in the same way, and it revokes two earlier executive orders.

10811.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Pan American World Airways and certain of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report is made, Pan American and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10809.s: This order changes Selective Service rules on registration, classification, and local board procedures. It requires registrants to keep an unaltered Registration Certificate in their personal possession, and it changes who may be placed in Class I-D based on service in the National Guard or reserve components. It also requires local boards to post classification reports, says reopening a classification usually cancels an induction or civilian work order, and sets rules for volunteers and unregistered delinquents.

10808.s: This order allows the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, or an authorized subcommittee, to inspect certain tax returns for the years 1945 to 1958. The returns include income, excess-profits, declared-value excess-profits, capital-stock, estate, and gift tax returns. The inspection is tied to the committee’s investigation of the administration, operation, and enforcement of the Internal Security Act of 1950 and other internal security laws, and must follow Treasury rules.

10806.s: This order says certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for 1947 through 1959 may be opened for inspection by the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee’s studies of government activities and its search for economy and efficiency in government. The inspection must follow the rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

10805.s: This order excepts the Central Intelligence Agency from several parts of the Government Employees Training Act. It lists the sections and language that do not apply to the agency. It also amends Executive Order 10800 by changing references from section 5 and section 5(b) to section 4 and section 4(b).

10807.s: This order creates the Federal Council for Science and Technology. It includes representatives from several federal departments and agencies and is chaired by a member chosen by the President. The Council advises the President and federal agencies on science and technology issues, recommends policies, and helps coordinate federal research and scientific programs. Federal agencies on the Council must help it with information, studies, and staff, and the order revokes one older executive order and amends another.

10804.s: This order gives the United States Civil Service Commission the President’s authority to make rules under the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act. It also revokes three earlier executive orders as they apply to certain employees, with exceptions for some workers serving with an international organization and for rights and benefits already vested under those orders.

10803.s: This order changes the term rules for members of the International Development Advisory Board, including the chairman. It says each member may be appointed for a term of no more than three years and may be reappointed for one or more additional terms of up to three years each. It also says the terms should be set to reduce many members’ terms ending at the same time.

10801.s: This order changes a previous order on inspection of certain tax returns by the Senate select committee on labor-management relations. It extends the years covered from 1945 to 1957 to 1945 to 1959 and allows the committee to act during the Eighty-fifth Congress and as long as it is authorized to act during the Eighty-sixth Congress.

10802.s:
This order creates a committee to review federal programs and activities that affect prices and costs. The committee includes representatives from several federal agencies and advises the President on how those programs affect price levels and costs.

Federal departments and agencies involved in procurement, stockpiling, price supports, rate regulation, subsidies, and similar programs must review their work and may change their administrative actions or recommend changes in law. Those agencies must also cooperate with the committee and provide assistance when needed.

10800.s: This order tells department heads to review their employee training needs, make plans to meet those needs, and set up training programs and controls. It also tells them to encourage employee self-development and to use training facilities and services from other departments when practical. The order gives department heads and the Civil Service Commission certain authority under the Government Employees Training Act.

10799.s: This order amends a prior executive order to expand one part of its rules from paragraphs (a) through (j) to paragraphs (a) through (k). It also adds the National Science Foundation, and any other agencies the Bureau of the Budget designates, to handle activities under section 104(k). The Director of the Bureau of the Budget must divide $5,100,000 for translation of publications and scientific cooperation among the National Science Foundation and any other designated agencies.

10798.s: This order sets the official flag design for executive agencies, including the flag’s proportions, sizes, and star placement. It applies to national flags and union jacks made or bought for executive agencies, with limited exceptions for troops and camp colors. It also says older flags and jacks may be used until they are unserviceable, and it revokes Executive Order No. 2390.

10797.s: This order gives the Director of the Bureau of the Budget the President’s authority under parts of the Federal Aviation Act of 1958. It covers transfers of records, property, personnel, and unexpended appropriations tied to changes in duties and agencies under that law. It also revokes an earlier executive order, with that revocation taking effect when the repeal of the Airways Modernization Act of 1957 takes effect.

10796.s: This order changes the membership of the Air Coordinating Committee. It names one representative from each listed federal agency and says the representative from the Federal Aviation Agency will be the chairman. It also revokes Executive Order No. 10754.

10794.s: This order sets up a Canal Zone Merit System for hiring, reappointment, reinstatement, re-employment, and retention in Canal Zone jobs. It says the system must be based on merit and qualifications, apply uniformly, and follow civil service standards. It also creates a Canal Zone Board of Appeals to hear employee appeals and gives the Secretary of the Army authority to issue regulations and exclude some employees or positions under the act.

10795.s: This order designates the Intergovernmental Maritime Consultative Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It says the organization is entitled to the privileges, exemptions, and immunities given by that law. It also says this designation does not reduce any privileges, exemptions, or immunities the organization may have or later get by treaty or congressional action.

10793.s: This order transfers certain Army functions at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory to the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. It does not transfer functions that relate mainly to military operations or weapon system development programs. It also transfers government-owned property used by the laboratory, except equipment tied to those military programs, and directs the agencies to make the needed record and administrative changes.

10792.s: This order excuses many federal employees from duty all day on Friday, December 26, 1958, the day after Christmas. It also treats that day as a holiday for federal pay and leave rules. Agency heads may exclude some employees for public reasons, and they are told to use a liberal policy on annual leave when the needs of the service allow it.

10791.s: This order sets a line of succession for who will act as Secretary of State if the Secretary of State and the Under Secretary of State die, resign, are absent, or are sick. It names three Department of State officers to serve in a set order until a successor is appointed or the absence or sickness ends. It also revokes prior presidential orders naming officers to do this job.

10789.s: This order lets the Department of Defense and several other federal agencies make and change contracts for national defense work, and it allows advance payments in some cases. It also sets rules for records, public access, yearly reports to Congress, and nondiscrimination in contracts. The order bars certain contracting methods, such as cost-plus-a-percentage-of-cost contracts, and keeps other legal limits on bonds, profits, and competitive bidding in place.

10787.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of the Interior. The lands may be used, managed, or exchanged under the Taylor Grazing Act and other land laws, subject to valid existing rights. It also keeps 25 percent of net grazing and other use revenues going to the counties where the lands are located. The transfer covers listed land projects in California, Montana, New Mexico, and Texas.

10788.s: This order suspends compliance with certain statutory provisions about employment in the Canal Zone. It does not change the rules on how much compensation can be paid to people in skilled, technical, clerical, administrative, executive, or supervisory jobs there. Those pay rules still apply to workers employed directly or indirectly by the United States Government or by a company partly or fully owned by the government.

10786.s: This order transfers all functions of the Airways Modernization Board to the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency. It also transfers the board’s records, property, facilities, employees, and remaining funds to the Federal Aviation Agency. The Director of the Bureau of the Budget may direct any other needed steps for the transfer.

10785.s: This order changes the membership of the President's Council on Youth Fitness. It makes the Secretary of the Interior the chairman and keeps the council made up of several cabinet officials and the Housing and Home Finance Administrator. It also amends an earlier executive order that created the council and listed its members.

10784.s: This order says certain functions under the Mutual Security Act of 1954 may be carried out without following several listed laws. It also allows certain purchases made outside the continental United States to be made without following some other listed laws. For some cost-type contracts with nonprofit institutions, the order says amendments and changes may be made with or without consideration.

10783.s: This order transfers certain Defense Department functions to the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. It covers the United States scientific satellite project, called Project VANGUARD, and certain space-related projects of the Advanced Research Projects Agency and the Department of the Air Force. It also directs transfers of money, records, property, facilities, and civilian personnel tied to those functions.

10782.s: This order amends Executive Order No. 10773. It changes the words "Defense and Civilian Mobilization" to "Civil and Defense Mobilization" in titles of officers, agencies, or bodies, and adds the words "as amended" after "1958" in section 1.

10781.s: This order suspends part of section 5764(a) of title 10 that deals with promotion zones for male officers in the line of the Navy who are not restricted in the performance of duty. The suspension lasts until June 30 of the fiscal year after the national emergency proclaimed in 1950 ends.

10780.s: This order suspends part of a federal law on promotions for officers in the Supply Corps, Chaplain Corps, Civil Engineer Corps, and Medical Service Corps. The suspension lasts until June 30 of the fiscal year after the national emergency ends. It does not change the rule for the Medical Corps or the part about women officers appointed under section 5590.

10778.s: This order allows William K. Harris to be appointed to a competitive position in the Department of the Navy without following the competitive provisions of the Civil Service Act and Rules. It affects that single appointment and the Department of the Navy.

10779.s: This order directs federal departments and agencies to work with state and local authorities on air pollution control. It says they should take practical steps, as allowed by law, to prevent or reduce air pollution caused by federal activities, including industrial and manufacturing processes run or controlled by the federal government and the destruction of foodstuffs or other materials ordered by federal regulators.

10776.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense the President’s power to set rules and regulations that change the standards and requirements for induction into the armed forces. The Secretary may give that authority to certain Defense Department officials. No one may be inducted for training and service unless they meet the standards set under these rules.

10777.s: This order changes the Career Executive Board so it has seven members. Four members are appointed by the President from private life, and three represent executive agencies, including the Commission and two other agencies the President chooses. No more than four members may belong to the same political party, and the President designates the chairman from among the members.

10775.s: This order changes the airspace reservation over the Las Vegas Project in Nevada. It expands the reservation to include the air space above an additional area at the western boundary, including all the air space above the Atomic Energy Commission's test-site area. The added area was previously part of restricted air space over the Las Vegas Bombing and Gunnery Range.

10774.s: This order tells the Civil Service Commission to write rules to protect retirement, insurance, and other civil-service rights for certain federal employees, presidential appointees, and elected officers who go to work for the International Atomic Energy Agency. It says some of these people can keep retirement and life insurance coverage, may get re-employment at their former pay and status, and can receive service credit and restored sick leave when they return to federal service. It also gives certain federal employees a right to appeal if re-employment is denied.

10773.s: This order gives the Director of the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization the functions that were transferred to the President under Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958, and it moves certain other presidential functions to that Director as well. It changes references in prior executive orders from the old defense mobilization offices to the new office and director, and it creates a Defense and Civilian Mobilization Board to advise the Director. It also revokes several earlier executive orders, while keeping earlier actions and agreements in force.

10772.s: This order changes part of a previous executive order about the fitness of American youth. It creates the President's Citizens Advisory Committee on the Fitness of American Youth. The Chairman of the Council may choose the members, and one member is named as the committee chairman.

10771.s: This order changes who oversees the Saint Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation. The Secretary of Defense is put in charge of the parts that directly concern construction of the Saint Lawrence River navigation project, and that role ends when construction is finished. The Secretary of Commerce keeps supervision over the Corporation’s general policies, operation and maintenance of the Seaway, needed services and facilities, and vessel and cargo measurement rules and tolls. The Department of Commerce must also help encourage traffic and full use of the Seaway.

10769.s: This order designates the International Hydrographic Bureau as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. That means it is entitled to the privileges, exemptions, and immunities given by that law. The order also says this designation does not reduce any privileges, exemptions, or immunities the bureau already has or may get by treaty or congressional action.

10768.s: This order ends the airspace reservation over part of the Aleutian Islands, Alaska, including territorial waters west of the 167th meridian west longitude. It also revokes Executive Order No. 7138 in full.

10770.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between American Airlines and certain employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International. The board must report its findings to the President. For a period after the order and after the board reports, American Airlines and its employees may not change the conditions out of which the dispute arose except by agreement.

10767.s: This order extends the existence of the Quetico-Superior Committee for four more years, until June 30, 1962. It affects the committee and keeps it in place for that time.

10765.s: This order sets rules for awarding life-saving medals under the Medals of Honor Act. It says applications must be filed with the Interstate Commerce Commission and must include detailed evidence and affidavits about the incident. The Commission may investigate cases, review the evidence, and make recommendations for approval. It also sets time limits for filing and replaces earlier medal regulations.

10766.s: This order gives the Director of the Bureau of the Budget the President’s power to approve regulations about renting substandard housing for members of the uniformed services. It also lets the Director approve changes to those regulations and ask for reports from the Secretaries named in the law.

10764.s: This order suspends the eight-hour work limit for laborers and mechanics employed by the Civil Aeronautics Administration on public work that is essential to national defense. Their pay must still be figured on an eight-hour day, and overtime must be paid at not less than time and one-half for hours over eight in a day. The order stays in effect until the President terminates or revokes it.

10761.s: This order says the government should re-examine how the Buy American Act applies to petroleum products. It directs agencies to prefer domestic petroleum products unless a domestic product is unavailable or its cost is unreasonable, and to treat complying petroleum products the same as domestic ones in bid prices. It also requires contracts for imported crude petroleum or petroleum products refined from imported crude petroleum to include a promise to follow the Voluntary Oil Import Program.

10760.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a labor dispute between Trans World Airlines and certain of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, TWA and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10759.s: This order amends a previous executive order about who can make rules for certain presidential functions. It gives authority over regulations for travel and moving expenses for civilian officers and employees who are transferred for permanent duty, including family travel, household goods, and house trailers or mobile dwellings.

10757.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a labor dispute between several airlines and certain employees represented by the International Association of Machinists. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For that period, and for thirty days after the report is made, the airlines and the employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10758.s: This order establishes a career executive program within the civil service system. It creates a Career Executive Board to help identify, select, place, train, and retain civil-service executives and to advise on related rules and practices. An employee can join the program only if the President designates that person as a career executive, and the order revokes a prior executive order.

10756.s: This order directs that the United States flag be flown at half-staff until interment as a mark of respect for The Honorable Frederick M. Dearborn, Jr., who was Special Assistant to the President. It applies to all buildings, grounds, and naval vessels of the Federal Government in the metropolitan area of the District of Columbia and the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.

10755.s: This order transfers a tract of land in California from the Department of the Navy to the Housing and Home Finance Agency for defense-housing purposes. The land is excluded from Naval Petroleum Reserve No. 2, but oil, gas, and other mineral rights stay with the Navy. Existing permits, easements, rights-of-way, and other rights already granted on the land continue until they end.

10754.s: This order changes how members of the Air Coordinating Committee are named. The heads of the member agencies designate their members, and the President designates one additional non-voting member who serves as chairman.

10753.s: This order sets a line of succession for the Department of the Interior if the Secretary dies, resigns, is absent, or is sick. It says the Under Secretary, certain Assistant Secretaries in order of service, and then the Solicitor will act as Secretary of the Interior until a successor is appointed or the Secretary returns. It also replaces an earlier order with the same subject.

10752.s: This order names the Secretary of the Interior to carry out most of the President’s powers under a 1935 law that regulates interstate and foreign commerce in petroleum and its products. It does not include the powers in section 4 of that law. The Secretary may also make rules inside the Department of the Interior to administer the law. This order replaces several earlier executive orders.

10751.s: This order changes the airspace reservation above the Hanford Engineer Works in Richland, Washington. It updates the boundary description for that reserved airspace. The change excludes certain landmarks useful in air navigation, so pilots can follow those landmarks without flying within the reservation.

10750.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate a dispute between Eastern Air Lines and certain of its employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. From the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, Eastern Air Lines and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10749.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Eastern Air Lines and certain of its employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, EAL Chapter. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For that time, and for thirty days after the report, Eastern Air Lines and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10748.s: This order appoints Honorable Edward I. P. Tatelman, a Magistrate in the Canal Zone, as Special Judge in one specific case. He is authorized to perform the duties of a judge of the United States District Court for the District of the Canal Zone and to sign the needed papers and records in that case.

10747.s: This order gives the Secretary of State, or a designee, the power to make certain decisions for the United States on requests from Japan for reduction of sentence or parole for Japanese war criminals. It says the Secretary of State should generally accept Japan's recommendations if they come with findings from a responsible non-political board and if the board has considered the relevant matters, including the trial record. It also revokes two earlier executive orders and abolishes the Clemency and Parole Board for War Criminals, with its records sent to the Department of State.

10745.s: This order changes the rules for converting some career-conditional federal appointments to career appointments. It applies to employees entitled to veteran preference who have a compensable service-connected disability of 10 percent or more, if they received their career-conditional appointment before January 1, 1958 and their agency recommends the conversion by December 31, 1958. If they are not certified under this section, their appointment is to be converted when they meet the service requirement for a career appointment.

10746.s: This order changes an earlier executive order on how the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954 is administered. It updates which parts of section 104 apply and makes a new rule for certain loans made by the Export-Import Bank of Washington. It also sets how foreign currencies under Title I are to be used for those loans.

10744.s: This order excuses many federal employees from duty for one-half day on December 24, 1957, and for one-half day on December 31, 1957. It applies to employees of executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies, including the General Accounting Office and the Government Printing Office, with some exceptions for special public reasons, existing law, or national security reasons. Each half day is treated as a holiday for compensation and leave rules.

10743.s: The order says Navy vessels that have been removed from the Naval Vessel Register and are not covered by any other law may be sold at public sale to the highest acceptable bidder. They must be advertised for sale for at least 30 days, and each bid does not have to include a payment bond. It also replaces Executive Order No. 9986 on the sale of Navy vessels.

10741.s: This order establishes the Trade Policy Committee and names the government officials who make it up. The committee is to advise the President on basic trade policy issues and on reports from the United States Tariff Commission. Government agencies are required to give the committee information when it asks for it, and recommendations from the Trade Agreements Committee must go through the Trade Policy Committee before reaching the President.

10740.s: This order changes who serves on the President's Council on Youth Fitness. It names the Secretary of the Interior as chairman and includes the Secretaries of Defense, Agriculture, Labor, and Health, Education, and Welfare on the council. It also updates an earlier executive order to match these changes.

10742.s: This order changes earlier executive orders about foreign-aid functions under the Mutual Security Act. It directs the Secretary of State to set up the International Cooperation Administration in the Department of State and puts transferred offices, personnel, facilities, and agencies under the Secretary’s direction and control. It also creates a Development Loan Committee and revokes two subsections of a prior order.

10739.s: This order amends an earlier order about incentive pay for hazardous duty by adding a definition for “duty as human test subject in thermal stress experiments.” It says this means duty performed by members exposed as human thermal experimental subjects in thermal stress experiments under the supervision of a laboratory designated by the Secretary concerned. The amendment is effective as of September 1, 1957.

10738.s: This order says estate and gift tax returns under the 1939 and 1954 Internal Revenue Codes may be inspected by state officials, bodies, or commissions that are lawfully in charge of state tax laws. The inspection must follow the rules and regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

10736.s: This order approves a seal as the official seal of the Department of the Navy. The seal includes a ship, an anchor, and an American bald eagle, with the words "DEPARTMENT OF THE NAVY" and "UNITED STATES OF AMERICA." It applies to the Department of the Navy.

10737.s: This order sets rules for states to get federal help after a major disaster or when one is threatened. A governor must ask for assistance and provide information about the damage, state and local resources, and the federal help needed. If the President decides the disaster qualifies, federal assistance can be given under an agreement with the state, and the aid can end by notice or after one year unless extended in some cases.

10734.s: This order amends a prior order about the Atomic Energy Community Act of 1955. It transfers many functions of the Atomic Energy Commission to the Housing and Home Finance Administrator, but the Commission keeps certain duties over property disposal, some compensation and eligibility decisions, and some responsibilities under section 57a. It also allows the Administrator to reimburse the Federal Housing Commissioner from the Community Disposal Operations Fund.

10735.s: This order changes the Selective Service Regulations for draft registration, classification, and induction. It adds rules for medical, dental, and allied specialist categories, changes who can be placed in Class IV-F, and sets how calls for men are made from the Secretary of Defense down to state and local boards. It also requires classified registrants to keep their local board informed of changes in status, address, physical condition, and any professional degree. The order revokes Part 1650 of the regulations.

10732.s: This order changes an earlier order that assigned some presidential duties to the Secretary of the Interior. It adds authority over approval of certain bonds for the Territory of Hawaii and over certain drug and marihuana matters in the Virgin Islands, with consultation from the Department of the Treasury. It also removes one Alaska road, trail, and tolls item and allows the Secretary of the Interior to pass some of this authority to the Under Secretary of the Interior.

10733.s: This order amends a prior order on the Government Contract Committee. It changes the committee membership and provides for an Executive Vice Chairman who will assist the Chairman and Vice Chairman in carrying out the committee's functions.

10731.s: This order gives the Director of the Bureau of the Budget the President’s authority to arrange transfers of records, property, and personnel under the Airways Modernization Act of 1957. It applies to transfers tied to changes in functions made under that law.

10730.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of Defense to bring any or all units of the National Guard and Air National Guard in Arkansas into active military service for an indefinite period. It directs the Secretary of Defense to help enforce United States District Court orders about enrollment and attendance at public schools in the Little Rock School District. It also allows the use of other armed forces if needed and lets the Secretary of Defense delegate that authority to the Secretary of the Army or the Secretary of the Air Force.

10729.s:
This order creates a White House official called the Special Assistant to the President for Personnel Management. That official helps the President with civilian personnel management, sets and reviews policies and standards for executive departments and agencies, and works to improve coordination in personnel management.

The order also requires the Civil Service Commission or its chairman to consult with that official on certain functions related to personnel management. It revokes a 1953 executive order on related personnel-management functions.

10728.s: This order sets rules for fund-raising campaigns within the executive branch, including the armed forces. It limits solicitations, requires them to be organized under uniform standards, and preserves each giver’s choice of agency and whether to keep a gift confidential. It also establishes the President’s Committee on Fund-Raising within the Federal Service to review the program and approve eligible national voluntary agencies.

10727.s: This order designates the Preparatory Commission of the International Atomic Energy Agency, the International Atomic Energy Agency, and the Universal Postal Union as public international organizations under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It makes them entitled to the privileges, exemptions, and immunities given by that law. The order also says this does not reduce any privileges, exemptions, or immunities they may already have or later get by treaty or congressional action.

10725.s: This order suspends a Marine Corps rule that set a service-in-grade requirement for officers of the grade of captain to be considered by a selection board for promotion to the next higher grade. It applies to Marine Corps captains and lasts until June 30, 1958. It also replaces Executive Order No. 10546.

10726.s: This order suspends compliance with certain statutory provisions about employment in the Canal Zone. It does not change the parts of those provisions that limit the pay of people in skilled, technical, clerical, administrative, executive, or supervisory jobs there. Those pay limits apply to people employed directly or indirectly by a branch of the United States Government or by a corporation partly or wholly owned by the government.

10724.s: This order sets up a Career Executive Committee made up of five members. The committee must study the civil service system and develop recommendations, proposed laws, executive orders, and regulations for a Career Executive Program. The program is meant to improve the selection, pay, and use of top career civil servants and to make civil service a more attractive career for able men and women. Only career civil servants would be eligible, and selections and promotions are to be based on merit without political tests.

10723.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between certain railroad carriers and some of their employees represented by the International Organization of Masters, Mates and Pilots, Inc. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days, and during that time and for thirty days after the report, no changes may be made in the conditions that led to the dispute except by agreement.

10722.s: This order amends the rules for the President's Committee on Government Employment Policy. It says the committee has seven members: four from federal agencies and three public members appointed by the President. The President also designates the chairman and vice-chairman, and members serve at the President's pleasure.

10721.s: This order directs that the flag of the United States be flown at half-staff on Federal Government buildings, grounds, and naval vessels. It applies in the District of Columbia and throughout the United States and its Territories and possessions until interment, as a mark of respect for the memory of The Honorable Walter F. George.

10720.s: This order changes who has direction and control over certain matters handled by the Federal Facilities Corporation. It replaces the Secretary of the Treasury with the Administrator of General Services in section 4 of a prior executive order. It also requires the Secretary of the Treasury to assign and deliver certain certificates and other documents to the Administrator of General Services.

10719.s: This order restores a parcel of land from the Schofield Barracks Military Reservation to the Territory of Hawaii. The land is to be used for public-school purposes only, and the Territory gets a right-of-way along certain roads. The United States keeps easements for existing utilities and utility lines, and the land reverts to Army control if it is used for other purposes and that use continues after notice to stop.

10717.s: This order creates an honorary award for distinguished civilian service in the Federal Government. The President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service is given to civilian officers or employees for exceptionally meritorious or outstanding service connected to their official work. The award is selected by the President with advice from a five-member board, and no more than five awards may be made in any one year.

10718.s: This order delegates to the Secretary of State the authority to set the rates or tariffs of fees for official services at U.S. embassies, legations, and consulates. It also lets the Secretary decide what counts as an official service and make any needed differences for each post. Existing fee rates and related rules stay in place unless changed under this delegated authority, and the Secretary’s actions must be published in the Federal Register.

10715.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 9775, which had established the Federal Committee on Highway Safety. It affects that committee by ending the order that created it.

10714.s: This order changes several Selective Service rules. It adds a registration exception for certain foreign press representatives and updates classification rules for registrants with dependents, members of the Ready Reserve, conscientious objectors, and some people with foreign military service. It also changes procedures for local boards, appeals, physical examinations, and transfers.

10713.s: This order sets up the U.S. administration of the Ryukyu Islands and puts those powers under the Secretary of Defense, with foreign relations handled by the Secretary of State. It creates a civil administration led by a High Commissioner, keeps the Ryukyuan central government, and provides for an elected legislature and a Ryukyuan Chief Executive. It also lays out court powers, lets the High Commissioner veto or annul laws, remove officials, and issue laws or regulations when needed, while requiring protection of basic liberties.

10716.s: This order puts the Director of the United States Information Agency in charge of coordinating the functions under the Act, and lets the director advise the President and handle some reports and funding for those functions. It also gives some of the Act’s functions to the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Commerce, with the State Department handling the Universal and International Exhibition of Brussels, 1958. The President keeps the power to appoint certain officers, send periodic reports to Congress, and waive limits in the Act. It also extends rules for coordination abroad to United States agencies and personnel involved in carrying out the Act.

10712.s: This order allows the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect certain tax returns for the years 1945 through 1957. The returns covered are income, excess-profits, declared-value excess-profits, capital-stock, estate, and gift tax returns. The inspection is for the committee’s study of the anti-trust and antimonopoly laws of the United States.

10711.s: The order restores two parcels of land from the Lualualei Military Reservation to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii.
