The order allows some temporary appointments and gives the Commission power to grant civil service status in certain cases. It revokes earlier executive orders on federal hiring, but says it does not affect existing reemployment rights.

9693.s: This order directs the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation to take possession and control of transportation systems, plants, and facilities used by towing and transportation companies in New York Harbor and nearby waters. It applies to the companies listed in the order and includes the property used with those operations. The systems and facilities are to be operated under the existing employment terms when possession is taken, and the Director may ask for protection and other help from the Secretaries of War and the Navy.

9690.s: This order amends a prior order so the Secretary of Agriculture is authorized and directed to take possession of and operate the plants and facilities of the Los Angeles Union Stockyards Company. It applies the earlier order to those plants and facilities in and around Los Angeles, California.

9688.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules by adding a new Schedule B category. It makes positions assigned only to Navy Communications Intelligence activities part of that category.

9689.s: This order moves the Surplus Property Administration’s domestic disposal functions to the War Assets Corporation and transfers foreign surplus property functions to the Secretary of State and the Department of State. It also creates a War Assets Administrator to take over certain surplus property functions from the War Assets Corporation on March 25, 1946. The order transfers related records, property, personnel, funds, and obligations to the agencies that receive the functions.

9686.s: This order gives the Housing Expediter authority to make plans and programs to increase the supply of housing of all kinds, especially homes for sale or rent at moderate prices for World War II veterans and their immediate families. It also lets the Housing Expediter issue orders and directions to other executive agencies, and those agencies must carry them out. The order tells federal agencies to use their emergency powers to help deal with the housing emergency and to work with other levels of government and other groups.

9687.s: This order revokes several earlier executive orders that set rules for paying losses to officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States serving in foreign countries because foreign currencies changed in value against the American dollar. It applies to the agencies concerned at the close of the pay period ending or current on January 31, 1946.

9685.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to take possession of certain plants and facilities used in the production, processing, transportation, sale, and distribution of livestock, meat, meat products, and by-products. It applies where strikes or other labor disturbances are interrupting those operations and, according to the order, affecting the war effort. The Secretary may also hire workers, use other federal agencies for help, and operate the plants until their prior productive efficiency is restored.

9683.s: This order restores the punishment limits that had been suspended for certain violations of Articles of War 58, 59, 61, and 86. Those articles cover desertion, aiding or advising another to desert, absence without leave, and misbehavior of sentinels.

9682.s: This order directs executive branch departments and agencies to give the Anglo-American Committee records, documents, and other information related to its study, unless the material is confidential and would harm U.S. interests. It also allows government officers and employees to share personal knowledge with the Committee, with approval from their department heads. The Secretary of State may assign State Department and Foreign Service staff to work with the American member of the Committee, and the Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy may provide transportation and other available government facilities.

9680.s: This order abolishes the United States of America Typhus Commission as of June 30, 1946. The commission had been created to protect members of the armed forces from typhus fever and to prevent its introduction into the United States. It also says the Secretary of War will supervise the winding up of the commission’s affairs and the handling of its records, scientific data, and material.

9684.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate disputes between the railroad companies and some of their employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For thirty days after the report, the companies and their employees may not change the conditions that led to the disputes unless they agree.

9679.s: This order gives the United States Representative and Chief of Counsel power to proceed before United States military or occupation tribunals against other Axis adherents in proper cases. It also lets the Chief of Counsel name a Deputy Chief of Counsel to help organize and conduct prosecutions of atrocities and war crimes. If the current Representative and Chief of Counsel leaves office, those duties and powers go to a Chief of Counsel for War Crimes appointed by the United States Military Governor for Germany or a successor.

9678.s: This order changes an earlier civil service order to extend the time for applying for its benefits. It says a person who leaves a covered civil service job for active military or naval service must be reinstated to their old job or a similar one in the same department or agency, if they meet the listed conditions. Those conditions include honorable discharge, applying within the stated time, a recommendation from the department or agency head, and passing a suitable noncompetitive examination.

9676.s: This order changes the rules for issuing non-necessity certificates under section 124(d) of the Internal Revenue Code. It says an application must be filed before February 15, 1946 to get one. It affects people and businesses seeking these certificates.

9675.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the two railway companies and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. Until then, and for thirty days after the board reports, the companies and their employees may not change the conditions tied to the disputes except by agreement.

9674.s: This order creates a Director of Liquidation in the Office for Emergency Management to help with the orderly winding up of temporary federal war agencies. The Director works with a Liquidation Advisory Committee made up of representatives from several agencies. The Director is to help agencies make liquidation plans, receive reports, set uniform practices, and advise them on personnel, property, accounts, space, and records.

9672.s: This order creates the National Wage Stabilization Board in the Department of Labor. It gives the new board the powers and duties of the National War Labor Board for wage and salary stabilization, dispute cases, arbitrators, and certain industry commissions. It also transfers the War Labor Board’s personnel, records, property, funds, and obligations to the new board and ends the National War Labor Board.

9673.s: This order transfers the functions of the Office of Production Research and Development from the Civilian Production Administration to the Department of Commerce. It also transfers the personnel, records, property, and funds mainly connected to those functions, and puts them under the supervision and direction of the Secretary of Commerce. The Director of the Bureau of the Budget may take the steps needed to carry out the transfer.

9671.s: This order restores several parcels of land in Honolulu, Oahu, to the possession, use, and control of the Government of the Territory of Hawaii. The lands had been set aside for United States government uses, including an agricultural experiment station and a site for a United States Marine Hospital. The order says the land is now needed by the Territory of Hawaii for use as home sites for the people of Hawaii.

9670.s: This order sets aside certain lands in Henry, Benton, Humphreys, and Decatur counties, Tennessee, for use by the Department of the Interior. The land is reserved as a refuge and wildlife management area for migratory birds and other wildlife. It says the reservation will be known as the Tennessee National Wildlife Refuge.

9668.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules. It changes a rule to cover receivers of insolvent national banks and other financial institutions appointed by the Comptroller of the Currency, along with the employees of those receivers. Their salaries must be paid from the funds of the insolvent institutions.

9669.s: This order transfers certain U.S. air-navigation, air-traffic-control, communications, and weather facilities in Tehran, Abadan, and Jask, Iran, from the War Department to the Administrator of Civil Aeronautics in the Department of Commerce. It also transfers related U.S. property, operating and maintenance functions, and some funds tied to those facilities.

9666.s: This order directs the Coast Guard to operate under the Department of the Treasury instead of as part of the Navy. Some Coast Guard vessels, facilities, and personnel may keep operating with the Navy if the Secretary of the Treasury and the Secretary of the Navy agree. The Coast Guard may also continue certain air-sea rescue, weather station, and navigational aid work under Navy directional control. It also revokes the earlier order that put the Coast Guard under the Navy.

9667.s: This order revokes Executive Order 9074, which had directed the Secretary of the Navy to take action needed to protect vessels, harbors, ports, and waterfront facilities. It changes that previous direction and affects the Navy's authority under that earlier order.

9665.s: This order transfers most functions of the Smaller War Plants Corporation to the Reconstruction Finance Corporation. It sends the remaining functions to the Department of Commerce and moves related board duties to the Secretary of Commerce or the Reconstruction Finance Corporation board. It also transfers some personnel, property, records, assets, liabilities, and administrative funds connected to those functions.

9663.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Texas & New Orleans Railway Company and Hospital Association of the Southern Pacific Lines in Texas and Louisiana and certain of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. During that time, and for 30 days after the report, no changes may be made in the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

9664.s: This order continues the duties of the Committee on Fair Employment Practice under the conditions set in the National War Agencies Appropriation Act, 1946. The committee is to investigate discrimination in industries that help produce military supplies or help the shift to a peacetime economy. It must also make findings and recommendations and report to the President.

9662.s: This order restricts competition in civil-service examinations for the Correctional Officer job in the Bureau of Prisons, Department of Justice. It limits those exams to people entitled to preference under the Veterans' Preference Act of 1944 during the war and for five years after it ends, as long as such people are available.

9660.s: This order gives the Chief of Counsel authority to prepare and prosecute charges of war crimes against the major leaders of Japan and their principal agents and accessories. It lets the Chief of Counsel select needed personnel, and it allows federal departments and agencies to help by providing staff and making approved expenditures. It also allows the Chief of Counsel to receive compensation and expenses authorized by the Secretary of War and to work with foreign governments when needed.

9661.s: This order directs the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation to take possession of and control the transportation system, plants, and facilities of The Great Lakes Towing Company. It says the system will be operated under the employment terms in effect when possession is taken, and that property in the Director’s possession cannot be attached without written consent. The order also lets the Director end this control when it is no longer needed and allows the Navy to be asked for protection, equipment, manpower, or other services.

9658.s: This order directs the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation to take possession and control of the Capital Transit Company’s transportation system, plants, and facilities in Washington, D.C. It says this is because a labor dispute is interrupting operations and could delay the war effort. The system is to be operated under the employment terms already in effect when possession is taken, and the Director may request protection and other help from the Secretary of War.

9657.s: This order appoints Henry F. Grady to head the United States group that will join other Allied Governments in observing the upcoming elections in Greece. It authorizes the Secretary of State and the Secretary of War to help him with personnel and expenses, and lets him cooperate with foreign governments as needed.

9656.s: This order transfers the Shipbuilding Stabilization Committee and its related functions, records, property, personnel, and funds to the Department of Labor. The Secretary of Labor will supervise and direct the committee and fill any vacancies in its appointive membership. Existing regulations and directives for the transferred functions stay in effect unless later changed or revoked by proper authority.

9655.s: This order sets rules for commissioned officers and employees of the Public Health Service. It covers rank, titles, appointments, pay and allowances, leave, promotions, separation, retirement, uniforms, decorations, and discipline. It also sets requirements for applying and being examined for appointment in the Regular Corps and Reserve Corps.

9654.s: This order adopts and ratifies the capture of the German steamship Milwaukee as prize by Captain J. F. Devlin of the War Shipping Administration. It covers the ship, its engines, boilers, furniture, tackle, apparel, spare parts, equipment, contents, and property on board.

9653.s: This order changes parts of the Civil Service Rules in Schedules A and B. It adds or revises rules for certain government jobs, including part-time workers, students, clerks, messengers, janitors, housekeepers, seasonal field assistants, consultants, and some positions in the Panama Canal area, postal service, Agriculture Department, and other agencies. Several of these jobs are limited to certain pay levels, time periods, or approval by the Commission.

9652.s: This order lets the Secretary of State appoint certain military personnel to civilian jobs in the Department of State after they are released from active military duty. It applies to people working on activities moved to the Department of State by two earlier executive orders, and the appointments are subject to Civil Service Commission fitness tests and war service rules.

9651.s: This order amends an earlier order on wage, price, and production controls during the shift from war to peace. It tells the Stabilization Administrator when wage or salary increases may be approved to correct pay problems, help full production in essential industries, or match earlier standards. It also says employers may put a wage increase into effect first and later ask for approval, and that the Price Administrator may consider such increases when reviewing price ceilings.

9650.s: This order discontinues several named defensive sea areas, including areas near Portland, Portsmouth, Boston, Narragansett Bay, New London, New York Harbor, Delaware Bay and River, Chesapeake Bay-Norfolk, Charleston Harbor, and Buzzards Bay and Vineyard Sound. It affects the coastal areas and harbors named in the order.

9659.s: This order extends trust periods and other limits on selling certain Indian lands that would expire during calendar year 1946. The extension lasts 25 more years from the date the trust would otherwise end. It applies to tribal and individual Indian lands, except cases where Congress has kept the authority to extend the trust period for itself.

9649.s: This order ends the Office of Fishery Coordination and the office of Fishery Coordinator. It directs the Secretary of the Interior, through the Fish and Wildlife Service or other Interior agencies, to wind up the office’s affairs. It also allows use of the office’s personnel, records, property, and funds for that work and for functions given under Food Directive No. 2.

9648.s: This order ends the Matagorda Bay Defensive Sea Area, which had been set aside for national defense. It affects that sea area and removes the special defense status created by the earlier executive order.

9646.s: This order sets the design for the President of the United States’ coat of arms, seal, and flag. It also revokes part of a 1916 executive order about the President’s flag. These designs are to be used only to represent the President of the United States.

9647.s: This order sets rules for giving public notice before a foreign trade agreement is negotiated. It says the Secretary of State must publish notice at least 30 days before an agreement is concluded, and interested persons may present their views to the Committee for Reciprocity Information. It also revokes part of a prior executive order about that committee.

9644.s: This order lets the Civil Service Commission give certain disabled veterans a competitive classified civil-service status or a probational status. It applies to veterans serving under a war-service indefinite appointment who can show a service-connected disability of at least 10 percent. It also sets a one-year trial period for some of these appointments and directs the Commission to make needed rules.

9645.s: This order ends the authority given to the Secretary of War to designate a military commander for the Territory of Hawaii and to let that commander set a military area and use certain powers there. It says the change does not affect actions already taken under the earlier order. It also does not affect past offenses, convictions, or penalties for violations of rules issued by that military commander.

9643.s: The order ends the Office of Surplus Property in the Department of Commerce. It transfers the office’s personnel, records, property, contracts, obligations, and funds, plus related Commerce resources, to the Reconstruction Finance Corporation. The transfer is for use in connection with surplus property disposal functions.

9642.s: This order changes the rules for clothing in kind or cash allowances for enlisted personnel of the Navy, the Coast Guard, the Naval Reserve, and the Coast Guard Reserve. It sets new fiscal year 1946 allowance amounts for enlisted men in other ratings and for those within 30 days of enlistment or reporting for active duty.

9641.s: This order lets certain Navy combatant vessels that have been removed from the Navy Register be sold at public sale to the highest acceptable bidder. The sale can happen even if the bid is below the vessels’ appraised value, as long as they have been advertised for sale for at least thirty days. It applies to battleships, cruisers, aircraft carriers, destroyers, and submarines.

9639.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate certain plants and facilities used in transporting, refining, and processing petroleum and petroleum products. It says the action is needed because strikes and other labor disturbances are interrupting operations and could delay the war effort. It affects the plants, facilities, property, employees, and management at the listed companies and locations.

9637.s: This order sets rules for awarding the Medal for Merit, which may be given only by the President or at his direction. It says the medal may be awarded to civilians of nations prosecuting the war, including civilians of foreign nations, for exceptionally meritorious conduct or courageous acts in support of the war. It also creates a Medal for Merit Board to review proposals and make recommendations to the President, and it replaces an earlier order and board.

9636.s: This order says that when certain holidays fall on a Sunday, federal executive departments, independent agencies, and government-owned or government-controlled corporations must be closed to public business the next Monday. It also says employees who would normally be excused from work on those holidays are excused on that Monday instead. For pay and leave rules, that Monday is treated as a holiday, with special rules for employees whose workweek includes Sunday and Monday.

9638.s: This order creates the Civilian Production Administration in the Office for Emergency Management and ends the War Production Board. It transfers the Board’s functions, staff, records, property, and funds to the new Administration, led by a President-appointed administrator. The Administration is directed to help shift from wartime production to peacetime production, including managing scarce materials and limiting some manufacturing where materials or facilities are not enough.

9634.s: This order directs the Secretary of State and the Secretary of the Interior to jointly recommend fishery conservation zones in areas of the high seas next to the coasts of the United States. It also directs them to recommend rules for the administration, regulation, and control of fishery resources and fishing activities in those zones.

9635.s: This order reorganizes the Navy Department to better group military, administrative, and business functions, and it lets the Secretary of the Navy shift duties among offices and bureaus. It defines the "naval establishment" to include naval sea, air, and ground forces, the Marine Corps, and, in time of war or when the President directs, the Coast Guard. It also sets the duties and succession of the Chief of Naval Operations and revokes two earlier executive orders.

9632.s: This order transfers the United States’ jurisdiction over mineral deposits in the Dupre Strip in Jefferson Parish, Louisiana, from the War Department to the Department of the Interior. The Secretary of the Interior is directed to take action to protect the United States from loss from drainage or threatened drainage of oil and gas deposits. The Department of the Interior’s authority is subject to the War Department’s primary jurisdiction over the lands for river and harbor improvements. Any money received from minerals extracted from the Dupre Strip must be paid into the Treasury and credited to miscellaneous receipts.

9633.s: This order places the natural resources of the subsoil and sea bed of the continental shelf beneath the high seas next to U.S. coasts under the control of the Secretary of the Interior for administrative purposes. It says this does not affect later decisions by law or court decree about ownership or control of that subsoil and sea bed between the United States and the states, within or outside the three-mile limit.

9630.s: This order ends the Foreign Economic Administration and moves its duties to other federal agencies. It transfers many foreign economic, export control, food, trade, and procurement functions to the Department of State, the Reconstruction Finance Corporation, the Department of Commerce, and the Department of Agriculture. It also places the disposal of surplus property in foreign areas under the Department of State and abolishes the Army-Navy Liquidation Commissioner.

9631.s: This order ends the Office of Censorship after it continues only to wind up its work until November 15, 1945. It also ends the Censorship Policy Board right away. The office’s property, records, remaining personnel, and unused funds are to be transferred for liquidation, and the order says it does not affect certain proceedings or forfeitures already started under the First War Powers Act.

9629.s: This order changes Executive Order 9492 by replacing the words "one year" with "eighteen months" in section 2(c). It applies to rules for non-military and non-naval transportation on Army and Navy air transports.

9628.s: This order lets a veteran who has won the Congressional Medal of Honor be appointed to the classified position of Contact Representative in the Veterans Administration. The appointment can be made without following the Civil Service Rules, if the Administrator of Veterans Affairs recommends the person to the Civil Service Commission. It applies to people entitled to veteran's preference who meet those requirements.

9626.s: This order appoints Francis Biddle as the United States member and John J. Parker as the alternate member of the International Military Tribunal. It says the member may receive compensation and expense allowances set by the Secretary of State, while the alternate member serves without compensation but may receive expense allowances. It also authorizes the Secretary of State, Secretary of War, Attorney General, and Secretary of the Navy to provide assistance and assign personnel, including members of the armed forces.

9625.s: This executive order revokes Executive Order 9294 of January 4, 1943. That earlier order had further defined the functions and duties of the Office of Defense Transportation.

9622.s: This order revokes Executive Order 9103 from March 18, 1942. That earlier order had set uniform control over the publication and use of federal statistical information that could give aid and comfort to the enemy.

9621.s: This order transfers some Office of Strategic Services functions to a new Interim Research and Intelligence Service in the Department of State, and moves the rest to the Department of War. It also transfers related personnel, property, records, and funds, with some military and naval personnel able to continue their duties if allowed. The Office of Strategic Services is terminated, and the Interim Research and Intelligence Service is to be abolished at the end of 1945.

9620.s: This order abolishes the Office of Economic Stabilization and the office of Economic Stabilization Director. It transfers their functions, records, property, personnel, and funds to the Office of War Mobilization and Reconversion. It also moves the Economic Stabilization Board to that office to advise the Director of War Mobilization and Reconversion.

9619.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules by adding one private secretary to the Executive Assistant to the Postmaster General. It affects the civil service job list for that office.

9617.s: This order transfers the functions, agencies, records, property, and funds of the War Manpower Commission to the Department of Labor and ends that commission. It also transfers the National War Labor Board and the Retraining and Reemployment Administration to the Department of Labor, placing them under the Secretary of Labor. Some functions of the Procurement and Assignment Service are transferred to the Federal Security Administrator instead. The Department of Labor is also directed to help with employment service and unemployment compensation work, with some services subject to Social Security Board approval.

9618.s: This order appoints Edwin G. Arnold as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration. He is to serve without additional compensation and take over the functions, duties, and authority given by earlier executive orders. The earlier executive orders are amended accordingly.

9616-A.s: This order creates a special temporary Public Health Service position called Chief Public Health Adviser on the staff of the United States High Commissioner of the Philippine Islands and Chief Public Health Service Representative for the Far Eastern Area, including the Philippine Islands. It also says a commissioned officer assigned to that job will hold the grade of Assistant Surgeon General while serving in it.

9616.s: This order moves the functions, powers, duties, personnel, records, property, and funds of the United States High Commissioner to the Philippine Islands from the Secretary of the Interior to that office. It also gives the High Commissioner delegated authority over United States matters in the Philippine Islands and puts United States civilian offices there under his supervision. The order sets rules for how United States departments and Commonwealth officials are to make official representations, and it covers staff hiring, pay, leave, transfers, retirement credit, and certain military privileges for employees and their families.

9615.s: This order says the time limits for recommending the Distinguished Flying Cross do not apply in certain cases. It covers acts or achievements done between December 7, 1941, and the end of hostilities in the present war, if the recommendation is started within six months after that date.

9614.s: This order ends the War Refugee Board in the Executive Office of the President. It directs the Secretary of the Treasury to liquidate the Board’s activities and obligations, wind up its affairs, and use its personnel, property, records, and unspent money as needed. It also directs the Secretary to separate the Board’s personnel and dispose of its property and records.

9613.s: This order withdraws public lands of the United States that contain deposits of radio-active mineral substances from sale and other disposal under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands and the deposits for the use of the United States. It also reserves certain lands already acquired by the United States from sale, and says later leases or permits for those lands must let the United States enter, mine, and remove those mineral substances.

9612.s: This order changes earlier rules on bringing coffee into the United States from countries in the Inter-American Coffee Agreement. It says those rules are suspended when Article VI of that agreement is not in force. It also directs the Secretary of State to notify the Secretary of the Treasury when Article VI becomes inoperative because of action by the Inter-American Coffee Board or because the agreement expires.

9611.s: This order re-establishes the Advisory Board on Just Compensation for the limited purpose of setting fair and equal standards, rules, and formulas for the War Shipping Administration. The board is to help determine just compensation for vessels requisitioned under the act of June 6, 1941. It gives the board the same power and authority it had under Executive Order 9387, and the War Shipping Administration must provide assistance and follow its determinations as that order provides.

9609.s: This order authorizes the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics to acquire, use, and dispose of real property, temporary use rights, and personal property tied to that property. It applies to property the committee deems necessary for military, naval, or other war purposes.

9610.s: This order authorizes the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs, or another Veterans' Administration officer acting for the Administrator, to use powers under the Second War Powers Act of 1942. It allows the agency to acquire, use, and dispose of real property and related personal property that is needed for military, naval, or other war purposes. It applies to property the agency deems necessary for those purposes.

9608.s: This order transfers some overseas information functions from the Office of War Information and the Office of Inter-American Affairs to a new Interim International Information Service in the Department of State. It also moves certain functions of the Office of War Information to the Bureau of the Budget. The order then ends the remaining functions of the Office of War Information and later abolishes both that office and the Interim International Information Service, with their remaining personnel, records, property, and funds moved to the Department of the Treasury for final liquidation.

9607.s: This order revokes Executive Order 9301, which had set a minimum wartime workweek of forty-eight hours. It affects that wartime workweek requirement.

9606.s: This order adopts and ratifies the capture of the German motor vessel "Caribia" made as a prize by Captain J.F. Devlin of the War Shipping Administration. It also covers the ship’s engines, boilers, furniture, tackle, apparel, spare parts, equipment, contents, and property on board.

9604.s: This order directs the government to promptly release and share certain scientific and industrial information obtained from the enemy, as long as national military security allows it. It extends the Publication Board’s authority and procedures to cover declassification, release, and publication of that information. It also keeps final release decisions with the Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy.

9605.s: This order revokes paragraph 4 of Executive Order No. 9279. It allows voluntary enlistments in the armed forces of the United States.

9603.s: This order says plants, mines, facilities, and other property taken by the United States under listed executive orders must be returned to the owners as soon as practicable. The officer holding and operating the property for the government must decide the timing in each case, with approval from the Director of Economic Stabilization. It also changes any earlier order that conflicts with this one.

9602.s: This order directs the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation to take possession of and control the Illinois Central Railroad Company's transportation system, plants, and facilities. It allows the system to be operated to support the war effort, and says the terms and conditions of employment in effect when possession is taken will stay in place. It also lets the Director request protection, equipment, manpower, and other services from the Secretary of War.

9601.s: This order revokes Executive Order 9240, as amended, which dealt with overtime wage compensation. It takes effect on the date of the order.

9599.s: This order directs federal agencies to help move the economy from war to peace while keeping prices, wages, materials, and facilities under control. It calls for aid to increase production, convert war plants and facilities, place war workers and returning service men and women in jobs, and support prices during the transition. It also gives agencies authority to adjust wage and price controls and to help free business from wartime controls as reconversion continues.

9600.s: This order changes the rules for overtime wage compensation on customary holidays. It says no extra pay is due for holiday work except time and one-half pay for work on the listed holidays.

9597.s: This order changes the rules for overtime wage compensation under an earlier executive order. It says no premium wage is paid for work on customary holidays, except time-and-one-half pay for work on the listed holidays. It affects workers who perform work on New Year’s Day, Thanksgiving Day, the Fourth of July, Christmas Day, Labor Day, V-J Day, and either Memorial Day or one other holiday of greater local importance.

9595.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the United States Rubber Company plants and facilities in or around Detroit, Michigan. It says the plants were needed for the war effort and were being interrupted by a labor disturbance. The Secretary of War may keep current employment terms in place, allow management to keep its functions as much as possible, and work with other federal agencies to protect the plants and people there. Possession and operation must end within 60 days after the plants' productive efficiency is restored.

9596.s: This order revokes Executive Order 9528, which had changed the order of succession for officers who could act as Secretary of the Navy. It affects the succession order for that Navy position.

9593.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the Springfield Plywood Corporation plants and facilities in Springfield, Oregon. It says the plants make materials needed for the war effort and that labor disturbances have interrupted their operation. The Secretary of War may keep the plants running, continue management as much as possible, and use federal help to protect the plants, workers, and their families. Possession and control must end after the plants’ productive efficiency is restored.

9592-A.s: This order changes an earlier order about the Los Angeles Shipbuilding and Drydock Corporation shipyard in Los Angeles, California. It says the Secretary of the Navy shall end government possession and operation of the shipyard when he decides it can be run privately in an efficient way that still fits the needs of the war effort.

9592.s: This order extends rules from Executive Order 9001 to contracts made by the Office of War Information and to certain contracts made by the Office of Alien Property Custodian. It allows those agencies to hire people or organizations for special services without following civil service and classification laws. It also lets the heads of those agencies, and people they choose, carry out the powers given under the earlier order.

9591.s: This order changes parts of the Foreign Service Regulations. It sets the fee for issuing a card or certificate of identity and registration at $1.00, revokes one listed item, and changes the wording from "office forms" to "official forms." It also changes "disbursing officers" to "disbursing agents" and revokes one subdivision in another section.

9590.s: This order lets the Secretary of Commerce create several Coast and Geodetic Survey ribbons and medals. They are for commissioned officers, ship officers, and crew members who gave distinguished, meritorious, or good conduct service, or who served in certain war zones or during a set defense service period. It also limits each person to one ribbon of each type and allows devices for later similar awards.

9589-A.s: The order authorizes the Petroleum Administrator to take possession of the butadiene plant in Houston and operate it, or arrange for its operation, for the war effort. It also allows the administrator to use property and assets tied to the plant, continue or hire workers, and take other steps needed to run the plant and produce its products. Federal agencies are directed to cooperate, and the order says possession and operation end after the plant’s productive efficiency is restored.

9589.s: This order restricts civil service competition for the position of Veterans' Relations Adviser and certain Veterans Administration jobs to people who are entitled to preference under the Veterans' Preference Act of 1944. That restriction applies as long as those preferred applicants are available and during the present war and for five years after it ends.

9588.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the two railroad companies and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the companies and their employees may not change the conditions that led to the disputes except by agreement.

9586.s: This order establishes the Medal of Freedom with ribbons and other parts for people who performed a meritorious act or service that helped the United States in a war, or helped a nation fighting with the United States against a common enemy. It says the medal is not for a U.S. citizen for acts or service done within the continental United States or for a member of the armed forces of the United States. It also says the medal may be given posthumously and that no person may receive more than one Medal of Freedom, though a later qualifying act may be marked with a device to wear with the medal.

9585.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate the Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company plants and facilities in Akron, Ohio, if needed for the war effort. It says the plants had interruptions from strikes and other labor disturbances, and that these interruptions could delay the war effort. The Secretary of the Navy may hire workers and agents, use the company’s rights needed to run the plants, and work with other federal agencies. The order also says management may continue its functions as much as possible, and possession will end after productive efficiency is restored.

9584.s: This order suspends compliance with certain employment provisions for the Canal Zone. It applies to the sections named in the War Department, Naval, and Military Appropriation Acts, 1946. The suspension lasts during the continuance of any wars in which the United States is now engaged.

9583.s: This order amends rules for clothing in kind or cash allowances for enlisted personnel in the Navy, Coast Guard, Naval Reserve, and Coast Guard Reserve. It sets new fiscal year 1946 amounts for chief petty officers, cooks, stewards, band members, and enlisted men in other ratings. It also changes the allowance amounts for those who are more than 30 days from enlistment or reporting for active duty and those within 30 days of enlistment or reporting for active duty.

9587.s: This order changes rules for shipping household goods and personal effects for certain civilian officers and employees. It lets an employee choose a different shipping method if they pay the difference, and it allows limited express shipment of some items needed right away at the new station. It also sets rules for paying travel costs for the immediate family of civilian officers and employees who are transferred for permanent duty, including spouse, children in certain cases, and dependent parents.

9577-A.s: This order authorizes the Petroleum Administrator to take possession of and operate the Texas Company plants and facilities in and around Port Arthur, Texas. It says this is because a labor disturbance threatened to interrupt production needed for the war effort. The order also directs federal agencies to cooperate, and it says control must end within 60 days after the plants’ productive efficiency is restored.

9582.s: This order restores one parcel of land from the Upolu Point Military Reservation to the Government of the Territory of Hawaii for aeronautical purposes. The land must remain available, without charge, for United States airplanes and airships to take off and land, and for temporary government use as needed by military authority. It also reserves another parcel on the island of Hawaii for military purposes as part of the Upolu Point Military Reservation.

9580.s: This order changes how leave pay is figured for employees of the Panama Canal and the Panama Railroad Company on the Isthmus of Panama. It says paid leave must be paid at the same rate the employee would have received while on duty, and travel leave must be paid at that same rate. It also says cash payment for leave taken in money must match the compensation the employee would have received if still in service, and it applies only to leave taken or commuted on or after the date of the order. It does not reduce the rate of payment for leave earned before that date.

9581.s: This order changes a prior executive order about wage and salary adjustments for employees covered by the Railway Labor Act. It gives the Territorial War Labor Board for the Territory of Hawaii jurisdiction over voluntary wage and salary adjustments for those employees in Hawaii.

9578.s: This order approves Civil Service Commission regulations under the Federal Employees Pay Act of 1945. The regulations set overtime pay rules for civilian officers and employees in the executive branch, with several listed exceptions. They also require a 40-hour basic workweek and set procedures for overtime, compensatory time off, and pay calculations.

9579.s: This order changes the rules for people who served in the armed forces and want the benefits of a prior civil service order. It says they must notify the Civil Service Commission within 90 days after their service ends, or within 90 days after hospitalization after discharge if it lasts no more than one year. It affects those service members who are on civil service registers or lists.

9577.s: This order ends the War Food Administration and the office of War Food Administrator. It transfers their functions, duties, powers, records, property, personnel, funds, and agencies to the Secretary of Agriculture. Existing orders, rules, and regulations on those matters stay in effect unless changed or revoked by the Secretary of Agriculture.

9575.s: This order declares the commissioned corps of the Public Health Service to be a military service and a branch of the land and naval forces of the United States during the present war. It makes the corps subject to the Articles for the Government of the Navy, including trial and punishment for violations. Officers detailed to the Army, Navy, or Coast Guard are subject to the laws of the service they are assigned to.

9576.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Erie Railroad Company and certain employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen. The board members must not have a financial or other interest in any railway employee organization or carrier. During the period stated in the order, the Erie Railroad Company and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute unless they agree to do so.

9574.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the Diamond Alkali Company plants and facilities in or around Painesville, Ohio. It applies to the plants, related property and assets used with them, and to people working there or seeking work there. The order says the plants should be run under the current employment terms, with management continuing as much as possible, and federal agencies must help. Possession and operation must end after the Secretary of War decides the plants have returned to their prior productive efficiency.

9572.s: This order approves and confirms the actions taken since March 21, 1942, to take possession of the Toledo, Peoria & Western Railroad and operate it for the United States. It also authorizes the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation to continue holding and operating the railroad. The order affects the railroad and the officers and agents carrying out its operation.

9573.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Georgia and Florida Railroad and certain of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days, and no change in the conditions behind the dispute may be made by the railroad or its employees except by agreement during that time and for thirty days after the report.

9571.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to acquire land under Cerritos Channel in California, along with any personal property on or used with it, and to dispose of that property under the Second War Powers Act. It applies to land partly within Los Angeles and Long Beach. It also requires the Secretary to take action to protect the United States from loss from drainage of oil and gas from the land. Royalties from oil and gas taken from the land must be paid into the Treasury.

9569.s: This order allows the Office of Price Administration to inspect certain corporation statistical transcript cards prepared from corporation income and declared value excess profits tax returns. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury. It applies to returns for taxable years ending after June 30, 1943, and before July 1, 1944.

9570.s: This order directs the Office of Defense Transportation to take possession and control of the Scranton Transit Company’s transportation system, plants, and facilities in and about Scranton, Pennsylvania. It says the action is needed because labor disturbances are interrupting operations and could delay the war effort. The system is to be operated under the terms and conditions of employment in effect when possession is taken, and control ends when it is no longer needed for the war effort.

9568.s: This order sets up a process for reviewing certain scientific and technical information kept from the public for national military security. It lets the Director of War Mobilization and Reconversion review this information and recommend what can be released for publication. The War or Navy Secretary makes the final decision on whether security allows release. It also creates a Publication Board and committees to help with this work.

9567.s: This order changes the rules for what property the Alien Property Custodian can cover under earlier orders. It applies to property in the United States owned or controlled by a designated enemy country or national, including Germany and Japan and their nationals. For enemy countries other than Germany or Japan, certain cash, currency, deposits, credit instruments, foreign exchange, and securities are not included unless the Custodian decides they are needed to protect other property of that same country or national.

9566.s: This order revokes Executive Order 9090, which had established an airspace reservation over portions of Ulster and Dutchess Counties, New York. It affects the airspace reservation in those counties.

9564.s: This order authorizes the Petroleum Administrator to take possession of and operate the Humble Oil and Refining Company plants and facilities in Ingleside, Texas. It says the plants are needed for the war effort and that a labor disturbance could interrupt their operation. Federal agencies are directed to cooperate, and the order says control of the plants must end after productive efficiency is restored.

9565.s: This order authorizes the Petroleum Administrator to take possession of and operate the plants and facilities at the Cabin Creek Oil Field in Dawes, West Virginia, and any related property used with them. It also allows the Administrator to keep workers employed, use the company’s contractual rights, and take other steps needed to run the site and produce its products. Federal agencies are directed to help the Petroleum Administrator carry out the order.

9562.s: This order ends the Office of Civilian Defense and abolishes its functions, except for parts that are transferred elsewhere. It transfers some of the office’s property and related duties to the Department of Commerce, and assigns the Secretary of the Treasury to wind up the office’s remaining affairs. It also lets the Director of the Bureau of the Budget direct any further steps needed to carry out the order.

9563.s: This order changes the rules for meals on vessels in the Panama Canal and adjacent waters. It requires vessels to provide meals without charge to pilots, extra deck hands, and other Panama Canal personnel on duty during regular meal hours while the vessel is transiting the Canal. If a vessel cannot provide those meals, the Panama Canal may furnish them at the vessel’s expense.

9561.s: This order changes a prior rule on allowances for enlisted men who are not furnished quarters or rations in kind. It raises the daily subsistence allowance where no Government messing facilities are furnished from $1.80 to $2.25.

9560.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the Mary-Leila Cotton Mills plants and facilities in Greensboro, Georgia. It also lets him use related property, employ people, and take other steps needed to run the plants for the war effort. He may also provide protection for the plants and the people working there. The possession and operation must end within 60 days after the plants’ earlier productive efficiency has been restored.

9559.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the plants and facilities of the Gaffney Manufacturing Company in Gaffney, South Carolina. It says the plants were needed for the war effort and had been interrupted by a labor disturbance. The Secretary of War may also keep or hire workers and take steps needed to protect the plants and the people there.

9556.s: This order lets the Secretary of War, the Under Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Under Secretary of the Navy handle certain court-martial functions and powers that were held by the President. It covers some cases under the Articles of War and the Navy articles, but not cases that end in death or loss of life. The President keeps the power to do these things himself, and the order stays in effect until Title I of the First War Powers Act of 1941 ends.

9555.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Illinois Central Railroad Company and certain employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the railroad company and its employees may not change the conditions at issue except by agreement.

9557.s: This order amends a prior order on extra pay for enlisted men of the Navy and Coast Guard who are specially qualified to use arms. It says they may receive additional compensation if they are stationed where they may be required to use those arms, including some temporary duty away from their usual ship or station. The pay is set at different monthly amounts for five classes, and the order takes effect May 1, 1945.

9554.s: This order directs the federal government to take possession of certain plants, facilities, and transportation systems owned or operated by motor carriers in and about the City of Chicago if labor disturbances have interrupted or are about to interrupt them. It says these systems are to be operated for the war effort, under the terms and conditions of employment in place when possession is taken, and with some wage increases paid only from net operating revenue. The Director may also request protection and other help from the Secretary of War. It does not apply to any motor carrier transportation system already in government possession under a prior order.

9552.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the Cocker Machine and Foundry Company plants and facilities in Gastonia, North Carolina. It says the plants are needed for the war effort and that a labor disturbance is interrupting their operation. The Secretary of War may continue workers, arrange protection for the plants and people there, and must end control within 60 days after the plants’ productive efficiency is restored.

9551.s: This order directs the transfer of the United States’ right, title, and interest in the water and sewerage systems in the cities of Panama and Colon to the Republic of Panama. It also allows the Governor of The Panama Canal to keep operating and maintaining the systems, or parts of them, for Panama after the transfer, under terms agreed to by both sides. For parts of the systems in certain areas of Colon, the United States may continue operating and maintaining them for as long as it uses those areas and Panama lets the United States use those parts without charge.

9553.s: This order creates a board to investigate a dispute between the River Terminal Railway Company and certain employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen. The dispute is described as one that could interrupt interstate commerce in Ohio and deprive the state of essential transportation services. The board must report to the President within thirty days, and the company and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute, except by agreement, during that time and for thirty days after the report.

9550.s: This order applies the same aerial flight rules used for certain military and Public Health Service personnel to commissioned officers of the Coast and Geodetic Survey when they are serving under that service. It also gives the Director of the Coast and Geodetic Survey the duties and obligations that the order places on naval personnel officials for Coast and Geodetic Survey personnel.

9548.s: The order directs the Secretary of the Interior to take possession of certain anthracite mines and run them if needed for the war effort. It says this is because labor disturbances are interrupting or could interrupt mine operations and the coal is needed for the war effort. It also directs federal agencies to help, says workers at the mines must be protected, and lets mine management keep working where possible.

9546.s: This order allows the Federal Security Agency to inspect statistical transcript punch cards made from individual income tax returns for certain tax years. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

9547.s: This order names Associate Justice Robert H. Jackson as the United States representative and chief counsel for preparing and prosecuting charges of atrocities and war crimes before an international military tribunal. It applies to leaders of the European Axis powers and their principal agents and accessories. It also lets him pick needed personnel and work with foreign governments to carry out these duties.

9545.s: This order restores a parcel of land from the Aiea Military Reservation to the use of the Territory of Hawaii. The land remains subject to rights-of-way reserved to the United States. It affects a described tract on the Island of Oahu, Territory of Hawaii.

9543.s: This order designates the Reconstruction Finance Corporation to handle certain bonds, notes, and other securities connected to loans made to the Seaboard Airline Railway Company and the Seaboard-Bay Line Company. It allows the agency to sell, exchange, dispose of, or extend the maturity of those securities, and requires the money raised to be paid to the Secretary of the Treasury.

9544.s: The order directs the Secretary of War to take full control of a public airport on certain lands leased to the City of Redmond, Oregon. It says the airport area covers 1,520 acres. The order stays in force during the unlimited national emergency and for six months after it ends.

9542.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate the plants and facilities of United Engineering Company, Ltd. in San Francisco. It says the plants are needed for the war effort and that strikes and labor disturbances are interrupting their operation. The Secretary of the Navy may hire employees and agents, use other federal agencies, and keep operating the plants until productive efficiency is restored.

9540.s: This order authorizes the Petroleum Administrator to take possession of and operate the Cities Service Refining Corporation plants and facilities in and around Lake Charles, Louisiana. It also directs federal agencies to help carry out the order and requires protection for the plants, workers, and their families and homes. The order says the company’s management may keep its management role as much as possible, and possession and operation must end when no longer needed for the war effort.

9541.s: This order transfers the Office of Surplus Property in the Treasury Department to the Department of Commerce. It also moves related records, property, funds, contracts, and personnel used in those disposal duties, as the two secretaries determine. Treasury and Commerce are directed to provide each other materials, supplies, equipment, work, and services to help carry out the order.

9538.s: This order lets the Civil Service Commission certify certain people for probational appointment if they were on an eligible list, entered the armed forces during the listed dates, left under honorable conditions, and are still qualified for the job. It also requires that they ask for restoration or certification within the stated time limit. The order does not apply if the eligible list expired before they entered the armed forces and the Commission had not already sustained objections to their certification because of draft status.

9537.s: This order changes the Foreign Service regulations so that clerks and other Foreign Service employees shall be appointed by the Secretary of State, or by authorized subordinates. It also allows those appointments to be made under rules the Secretary of State may prescribe.

9536.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Interior to take possession of certain bituminous coal mines and operate them, or arrange for their operation, for the war effort. It covers the mines and related property, assets, and facilities used with them, and it directs federal agencies to help carry out the order. The Secretary must make employment available, provide protection for workers and job seekers as needed, and may seek changes in employment terms through the National War Labor Board.

9539.s: This order reinstates Avra M. Warren in the Foreign Service of the United States. His reinstatement would take effect when the Senate confirms his nomination to a position in Class I.

9535.s: This order changes the National War Labor Board by increasing the number of public members from four to eight. It also revokes two earlier orders that provided for associate members and alternate public members, and no more than four of the public members may vote on any one matter.

9534.s: This order makes the Federal Loan Administrator and the War Food Administrator additional members of the Economic Stabilization Board. It amends the earlier order that created that board.

9533.s: This order changes the name of the customs port of entry of Marshfield, Oregon, to Coos Bay, Oregon. It also keeps in force earlier orders that extended the port limits to include North Bend, Oregon, and all points on Coos Bay, with the new name used in those orders.

9532.s: This order changes the name of the Office of the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs to the Office of Inter-American Affairs. It puts a Director at the head of the office, appointed by the President, to carry out the office’s duties under the President’s direction and in line with U.S. foreign policy. Wallace EL Harrison is appointed as the Director.

9531.s: This order changes the customs field organization. It abolishes Customs Collection District Number 46 in Omaha, revokes Omaha, Nebraska, as a customs port of entry in that district, and makes Omaha a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District Number 39. It also extends District Number 39 to cover Nebraska and Council Bluffs, Iowa, and extends District Number 47 in Colorado to include Wyoming.

9530.s: This order exempts Harry F. Hawley, a Foreign Service Officer of Class III, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for as long as is needed, but not beyond the duration of the present emergency.

9528.s: This order changes the order of officers who may act as Secretary of the Navy when the Secretary is temporarily absent. It names the Under Secretary of the Navy, the Assistant Secretary of the Navy for Air, the Assistant Secretary of the Navy, and the Commander in Chief, United States Fleet, and Chief of Naval Operations in that order. If all of those are absent, the Vice Chief of Naval Operations and the Chief of Staff, United States Fleet, are next in line.

9529.s: This order reinstates Paul H. Alling in the Foreign Service of the United States in Class II. His reinstatement takes effect when the Senate confirms his nomination to that class.

9527.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to end possession, use, and operation of the plants, facilities, and other property of York Safe and Lock Co. in York County, Pennsylvania. It affects the property that had been taken over to produce war material, and it says the plants will be operated privately in a way that is consistent with the war effort.

9526.s: This order changes a long list of earlier orders that withdrew public lands for military and other federal uses during the national emergency and war. It says those lands will stay withdrawn unless ordered otherwise, but the special wartime jurisdiction will end six months after the unlimited national emergency ends. After that, jurisdiction will go back to the Department of the Interior and any other federal department or agency with an interest on record.

9525.s: This order changes a prior rule on clothing for enlisted Navy, Coast Guard, Naval Reserve, and Coast Guard Reserve personnel. It lets certain enlisted men who returned to the United States from overseas as patients receive clothing in kind if they lost clothing through no fault of their own and have not been reimbursed. If they later file a claim for lost personal property, the value of the clothing must be deducted from that claim.

9524.s: This order amends earlier rules on aerial flights and increased pay for certain Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, National Guard, and Public Health Service personnel. It updates who can be required to take regular and frequent aerial flights, including some medical officers, student aviators, and other listed personnel. It also changes how those orders are issued, how long they stay in force, and how some actions are reported for confirmation.

9523.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the plants and facilities of the American Enka Corporation near Enka, North Carolina. It also covers related real or personal property used with those plants. The order says this is needed because labor disturbances threaten to interrupt operations and delay the war effort.

9522.s: This order transfers the Tomah Radio School property at Tomah, Wisconsin, from the Department of the Interior to the Veterans' Administration. It covers the 378 acres of land and all improvements on the property.

9520.s: This order names Ronald Ransom as Vice Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. He is set to serve for four years from August 6, 1944, unless his service as a Board member ends sooner.

9519.s: This order extends the rules of Executive Order No. 9001 to the Office of War Mobilization and Reconversion, the Office of Contract Settlement, the Surplus Property Board, and the Retraining and Reemployment Administration. It applies to contracts made or to be made by those agencies. It also lets their leaders and designated staff carry out the same functions and powers given by that earlier order to the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Chairman of the United States Maritime Commission.

9521.s: This order revokes a long list of older executive orders about the duties and business of Foreign Service officers and employees. It says the Secretary of State’s regulations will replace those orders when they cover the same subject matter. The Secretary of State must identify which orders or parts are being superseded and publish the regulations in the Federal Register.

9518.s: This order designates and authorizes A. R. de Jesus, an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico, to act as Judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico. He may perform the judge’s duties and sign needed papers and records without extra compensation when the judge is absent, ill, or otherwise legally disabled during the current calendar year.

9517.s: This order returns a tract of land in Kapiolani Park, in Honolulu, to the jurisdiction of the Territory of Hawaii. The land had been transferred to the United States for a United Service Organization club building reservation, but the clubhouse was not built and no plans existed for it. It affects that parcel of land in Waikiki.

9516.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and control the transportation system of the Bingham and Garfield Railway Co. It also covers related real or personal property used with that system. The Secretary of War may operate it for the effective prosecution of the war, and must end that possession and control within sixty days after it is no longer needed for that purpose.

9515.s: This order changes the rules for navigation in the Panama Canal and nearby waters by setting maximum speeds for vessels in different areas. It gives different speed limits for places like Gatun Lake, Gaillard Cut, and the locks, and some limits depend on the length of the vessel. Vessels in Canal Zone waters must follow these speed limits.

9514.s: This order changes an earlier order about the Foreign Service. It lets the Secretary of State issue regulations, orders, and instructions about the duties and business of Foreign Service officers and employees. The authority does not apply when another law gives the President specific power to make rules on a particular subject.

9513.s: This order extends the service or training periods of people inducted under the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940 who have been or may be assigned to the Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard. Their service is extended for the length of any war the United States is in, plus six months after the war ends, unless they are discharged sooner.

9510.s: This order transfers eight named commissioned officers from the Coast and Geodetic Survey to the service and jurisdiction of the War Department. While under the War Department, they keep serving under their Coast and Geodetic Survey commissions and are part of the active military forces of the United States. They are to return to the Coast and Geodetic Survey when the present national emergency ends.

9509.s: This order sets rules for the uniforms and insignia worn by commissioned officers of the Public Health Service, including different rules for male and female officers and for those serving with the Army. It says when officers on active duty must appear in uniform and lets the Surgeon General set when uniforms are worn in peace time. It also limits when inactive reserve and retired officers may wear uniforms, except for ceremonial occasions or if authorized.

9508.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate certain Montgomery Ward plants and facilities in several states. It says the facilities may be run under the terms then in effect and in line with National War Labor Board directive orders. It also directs federal agencies to cooperate and says possession and operation must end after the Secretary of War finds that productive efficiency has been restored.

9511.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of the Cleveland Electric Illuminating Company’s properties in and around Cleveland, Ohio, and any related real or personal property used with them. It also allows the Secretary of War to operate those properties as needed for the successful prosecution of the War. Possession must end within sixty days after the Secretary of War decides it is no longer needed for that purpose.

9507.s: This order changes the Foreign Service fee schedule by removing several listed fees and wording about Chinese certificates and travel certificates for use in China. It also revokes two sections of the Foreign Service Regulations. In addition, it revokes Executive Order 8566, but says that revocation does not bring back the earlier Executive Order 7224-A.

9506.s: This order changes the conditions for getting a classified civil service status. A person can no longer get that status just because his name was reached on a civil service register; he must be regularly selected for appointment from a certificate issued by the Civil Service Commission for probational appointment and enter on duty from that certificate.

9505.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the plants and facilities of Cudahy Brothers Company in Cudahy, Wisconsin. It also lets him take related property and assets, continue or hire workers, and do what he thinks is needed to process, sell, and distribute the products. The Secretary of War must operate the plants under the War Labor Disputes Act and the National War Labor Board directive, and he must end possession and control within 60 days after productive efficiency is restored.

9504.s: This order revokes Dunkirk, New York, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District Number 9 (Buffalo). The change takes effect at the close of business on December 31, 1944.

9503.s: This order says a disabled veteran who completes a training course prescribed by the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs may be appointed to the job for which the training was received in a federal executive branch department, agency, or independent establishment. The appointment is allowed without regard to the Civil Service Rules and War Service Regulations if the employing agency recommends the veteran, the Civil Service Commission finds the training adequate, and the veteran passes any noncompetitive exam the Commission requires.

9502.s: This order creates two special temporary positions in the Public Health Service: Associate Chief of the Bureau of State Services and Chief Medical Officer for the War Shipping Administration. Commissioned officers assigned to these jobs will hold the grade of Assistant Surgeon General while they serve in them. The positions will end when the present war ends or when the declared emergency ends, whichever comes first.

9500.s: This order extends the trust periods for Indian lands, whether tribal or individual, that would otherwise expire during calendar year 1945. The extension lasts 25 more years from the date the trust would have expired. It does not apply to cases where Congress has specifically kept the authority to extend the trust period for those lands.

9501.s: This order sets rules for recalling retired commissioned officers of the Public Health Service to active duty. The Surgeon General may require some retired officers to take a medical exam and may return them to active duty if they have recovered or are physically able to serve. In time of war, officers retired for age may be recalled, and their duty cannot go past the last day of the sixth month after the war ends. Officers placed on permanent "waiting orders" are treated as retired officers under this order.

9499.s: This order makes income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, and capital stock tax returns open to inspection by the Department of Commerce. It applies to returns made under the Internal Revenue Code for 1941 and later years, subject to conditions set in a Treasury decision.

9497.s: This order changes earlier rules on leave for some alien employees of The Panama Canal and the Panama Railroad Company. It lets the Governor grant sick and rest leave to alien employees who are not already entitled to leave under other employment rules, with a limit of 24 days in any one year and 60 days total. It also corrects another section so that U.S. citizens and certain alien employees paid above set rates are entitled to leave privileges under that order.

9498.s: This order changes a prior order about certain Public Health Service hospitals for the care and treatment of insane persons. It allows payments to be made, in advance or by monthly reimbursement, from the appropriation for Saint Elizabeths Hospital to help operate and maintain those hospitals. The Federal Security Administrator may make these payments when deemed necessary and proper.

9495.s: This order extends the rules of Executive Order 9177 to the United States Maritime Commission and the Administrator of the War Shipping Administration. It lets those agencies carry out the functions and powers that order gave to the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Agriculture, and the Reconstruction Finance Corporation, within the limits set by that order. It applies to articles entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after August 1, 1944.

9496.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of certain plants and facilities in or near Toledo, Ohio, and to operate them for the war effort. It applies to listed companies whose operations were interrupted or threatened by a labor disturbance. The Secretary of War may also keep management in place as much as possible, protect the plants and workers, and use other federal agencies to help. Possession and operation must end within 60 days after the plants’ prior productive efficiency is restored.

9494.s: This order authorizes the Civil Service Commission to give classified civil-service status to three named employees in the Antitrust Division of the Department of Justice. It says this can be done without following the competitive provisions of the Civil Service Rules.

9493.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of the Lord Manufacturing Company’s plant and facilities in Erie, Pennsylvania, and any related property used with them. It lets the Secretary operate them, or arrange for their operation, to keep producing and distributing the company’s products for the war effort. The order says this control ends when the Secretary decides the plants can be operated in a way that is consistent with the effective prosecution of the war.

9492.s: This order lets the War and Navy departments allow non-military and non-naval passengers and cargo on Army and Navy air transports on foreign routes if the travel is certified as in the national interest and important enough to justify air travel. It says armed forces and United Nations air-transport needs for the war effort come first. It also requires reasonable charges for this transportation and limits it when United States civil air carriers can handle the traffic.

9491.s: This order sets rules for issuing payment certificates under section 124(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. It says the Chairman of the War Production Board, or a representative, may issue a certificate when the United States has made a payment for an emergency facility because a contract was ended or because expected future contracts did not happen. It also allows the certifying authority to require proof about the payment and to issue extra rules for applications and other administrative matters.

9489.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to name a military commander for the Territory of Hawaii. The commander may treat all or part of Hawaii as a military area and may set rules that can exclude people, limit travel, impose curfews, regulate enemy aliens, control firearms, and restrict newspapers, radio, and other information. It also lets the commander control certain ports, travel facilities, and cargo quotas in Hawaii.

9490.s: This order transfers certain functions, powers, and duties of the Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy under section 124 of the Internal Revenue Code to the Chairman of the War Production Board. It also transfers some related funds, records, property, and civilian personnel used mainly to carry out those functions. The order covers changes to necessity certificates and certification under section 124, and it amends any earlier executive orders that conflict with it.
