9488.s: This order transfers records, property, funds, and personnel from the Office of War Mobilization and two other wartime agencies to other offices created by law. It also moves the functions, powers, and duties of the Office of War Mobilization to the Director of the Office of War Mobilization and Reconversion when that Director takes office. The changes affect the employees, records, equipment, and funds of the named agencies.

9486.s: This order transfers certain certification duties from the Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy to the Chairman of the War Production Board. It applies to certificates saying an emergency facility is no longer necessary for national defense during the emergency period. The change affects the officials who handle these certifications.

9487.s: This order sets rules for issuing "Non-Necessity Certificates" for emergency facilities under section 124(d) of the Internal Revenue Code. It says the Chairman of the War Production Board, or a representative, will decide whether an emergency facility is no longer needed for national defense and will issue the certificate on proper application. The order also says applications must be filed with the War Production Board in Washington, D.C., or another office named by the certifying authority.

9484.s: This order directs the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the Farrell Cheek Steel Company plants and facilities in and around Sandusky, Ohio. It says the plants were needed for the war effort and were being interrupted by a labor disturbance. The Secretary of War is also allowed to continue or hire workers, use company rights and assets as needed, and provide protection for the plants and for people employed or seeking employment there.

9485.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to give back possession of the Remington Rand plant in Southport, New York. The Navy had been operating that part of the plant under a prior order to produce essential war materials. It also directs the Secretary to issue any needed orders to carry out the transfer.

9483.s: This order authorizes and directs the Secretary of the Interior to take possession of certain mines, collieries, and preparation facilities listed in the order. It also directs the Secretary to operate them and handle the coal produced, prepared, or handled by them. Federal agencies are directed to cooperate, and the Secretary may end possession after productive efficiency is restored.

9481.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to take possession of certain listed mines, collieries, and coal preparation facilities and to operate them or arrange for their operation. It says this is because strikes and other labor disturbances are interrupting operations and may delay the war effort. It also applies to the property used with those mines and to the employees and management working at them.

9482.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to take possession of certain listed mines, collieries, and preparation facilities and to operate them or arrange for their operation. It says this is because strikes and other labor disturbances were interrupting operations and could delay the war effort. The Secretary is also directed to work with other federal agencies and to let existing management continue its functions as much as possible.

9480.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the plants and facilities of Twentieth Century Brass Works, Inc. in and around Minneapolis, Minnesota. It says the plants are used for war work and that operations were being interrupted by a labor disturbance. The Secretary of War may also continue employment, protect the plants and workers, and take other steps needed to run the facilities.

9479.s: This order changes a prior order to let the Governor of The Panama Canal contract with the Panama Railroad Company to operate certain piers and a dock at the Atlantic terminal and several piers at the Pacific terminal. The piers are owned by The Panama Canal. The work would be done with the company’s funds and on terms the Governor considers fair to both sides.

9478.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to take possession of certain coal mines, collieries, and preparation facilities in Pennsylvania and West Virginia and to operate them during the war. It says this is because strikes and other labor disturbances were interrupting production and could delay the war effort. The Secretary must operate them under existing employment terms, protect employees as needed, and allow management to keep doing its managerial work as much as possible. Possession must end after the mines’ productive efficiency is restored.

9476.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to take possession of certain coal companies’ mines, collieries, and preparation facilities in Pennsylvania and operate them during the war. It says this is because strikes and other labor disturbances were interrupting production and could delay the war effort. The Secretary is to keep the facilities running under the current employment terms, coordinate with federal agencies, and end possession within sixty days after productive efficiency is restored.

9477.s: The order directs the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the Cleveland Graphite Bronze Company plants and facilities in Cleveland, Ohio. It says the plants were needed for the war effort and that labor interruptions were delaying their operation. The Secretary of War must keep the current employment terms in place, allow management to keep its functions as much as possible, and provide protection for the plants, workers, and their families and homes. Possession and operation must end within 60 days after the plant’s prior productive efficiency has been restored.

9475-A.s: This order lets the Secretary of War take over and run two Hughes Tool Company plants in Houston, Texas. It says the plants make items needed for the war effort and were facing a labor disturbance that could slow production. The Secretary of War may also use related property, keep or hire workers, and provide protection for the plants and people there. Control must end within 60 days after production returns to its earlier level.

9475.s: This order abolishes the Office of Rubber Director and transfers its authority and functions to the Chairman of the War Production Board. It also gives the Rubber Reserve Company responsibility for buying, selling, storing, transporting, researching, developing, and testing synthetic and natural rubber and related products, and for operating certain synthetic rubber plants under the Chairman’s direction. Some personnel, property, records, funds, and other resources of the War Production Board are to be transferred to the Rubber Reserve Company.

9474.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Interior to take possession of and operate the mines, collieries, and preparation facilities of two coal companies in Pennsylvania. It says the move is needed because strikes and other labor disturbances are interrupting operations and could delay the war effort. The Secretary must operate the mines under the current employment terms, protect employees as needed, and work with federal agencies and other designated helpers.

9472.s: This order sets up awards for United States ships and some foreign ships operated for the United States Maritime Commission or the War Shipping Administration. It allows a citation and plaque for ships that served in outstanding action against attack or in gallant action in marine disasters or other emergencies at sea, and it gives citation ribbon bars to the master and crew on board at the time. It also creates the Merchant Marine Meritorious Service Medal for masters, officers, and crew who are officially commended for meritorious service, and it authorizes a distinctive service ribbon bar for certain merchant marine personnel who served between September 8, 1939, and December 6, 1941.

9473.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of the International Nickel Company plants and facilities in and around Huntington, West Virginia. It says the plants are needed for the war effort and that labor disturbances have interrupted operations. The Secretary of War may operate the plants, keep management in place as much as possible, and direct federal agencies to help carry out the order.

9471.s: This order ends the Division of Central Administrative Services in the Office for Emergency Management. Its functions are to be stopped or transferred to other federal agencies, as decided by the Director of the Bureau of the Budget. The order also allows personnel, records, property, funds, and obligations of the Division to be transferred or otherwise disposed of under law or executive order.

9470.s: This order sets a uniform method for deciding the bond amounts for collectors of customs. The bond must be at least 10% of the average monthly collections in the district from the previous fiscal year, with a minimum of $10,000 and a general maximum of $100,000 unless the Secretary of the Treasury decides otherwise. The bonds must be in multiples of $1,000, and they must be reviewed at least every two years.

9468.s: This order lets commissioned officers of the Coast and Geodetic Survey be transferred to the War or Navy Department and returned to the Coast and Geodetic Survey when directed. While serving under the War or Navy Department, they remain under their Coast and Geodetic Survey commissions and are part of the active military or naval forces of the United States. It also says they must be returned when the present national emergency ends, unless they are returned sooner.

9467.s: This order changes employment rules for workers of the Panama Canal and the Panama Railroad Company on the Isthmus of Panama. It keeps preference for citizens of the United States or the Republic of Panama, sets limits and exceptions for some alien employees, and changes rules for passes, medical care, and leave. It also says some leave may be paid out in cash when service ends, and it revokes two earlier executive orders.

9466.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate the listed plants and facilities near San Francisco, California. It says the plants were needed for the war effort and that labor disturbances were causing or could cause interruptions in their operation. The Secretary of the Navy may also keep management working as much as possible and take steps to protect the plants and the people working there or seeking work there.

9465.s: This order changes an earlier rule about clothing for enlisted personnel of the Navy, Coast Guard, Naval Reserve, and Coast Guard Reserve. It says those in other training may receive clothing in kind up to a set value and a temporary issue of Government-owned clothing up to a set net value. The change is effective July 1, 1944.

9464.s: This order transfers the use, possession, and control of 4.4 acres in the Nantahala National Forest from the Department of Agriculture to the Tennessee Valley Authority. The land is in Nantahala Township, Swain County, North Carolina. The transfer is subject to any rights of Swain County or North Carolina to rights-of-way for public roads.

9463.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate five plants and facilities in San Francisco. It covers their property and other assets used with the plants, and allows the Secretary to keep or hire workers and use company rights as needed. The plants are to be run under the War Labor Disputes Act and the terms of certain War Labor Board orders. Control must end within 60 days after the Secretary finds that production has returned to its earlier level.

9462.s: The order directs the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation to take possession of and operate the motor carrier transportation systems listed in the order. It says this is to keep those systems running for the war effort and applies to the carriers named on the list, including their property and assets. The systems are to be managed under the employment terms in effect when possession is taken, and the Director is to follow the National War Labor Board directive. Wage increases already covered by that directive may be paid only from the system’s net operating revenue.

9461.s: This order abolishes the Executive Committee on Commercial Policy. It affects that committee and ends its continued existence under earlier presidential actions.

9460.s: This order sets rules for glider flights by officers, warrant officers, nurses, and enlisted men in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard. It says some personnel who are qualified or in training and who are ordered to take part regularly and frequently in glider flights must complete certain flights during set time periods. It also gives special rules when glider equipment or towing aircraft are not available, when military operations make flights impossible, or when a person is unable to fly because of an aviation accident.

9459.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession and control of the Philadelphia Transportation Company’s transportation systems. It includes the company’s real and personal property and other assets used with those systems. The systems may be used for war emergency purposes, and control ends when the Secretary of War decides it is no longer needed for that purpose.

9458.s: This order changes rules for aerial flights by enlisted men in the Army Air Forces, Navy, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard. It says enlisted men who are qualified aircraft pilots or observers must be required to take part regularly and frequently in aerial flights. It also says enlisted men who are not qualified pilots or observers may be required to do so. These orders stay in effect until they are revoked and must be reported to the proper military officials.

9455.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, and capital stock tax returns open to inspection by the Select Committee to Investigate the Federal Communications Commission, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The returns cover the years 1939 to 1944 and may be used to carry out House Resolution 21, subject to the stated Treasury conditions.

9456.s: This order suspends compliance with certain employment rules for the Canal Zone found in three 1945 appropriations acts. The suspension lasts during any war the United States is then engaged in.

9454.s: This order appoints and commissions certain members of the Army Nurse Corps and certain female dietetic and physical-therapy personnel of the Army Medical Department as officers in the Army of the United States. It applies to those on active duty on June 22, 1944, and gives them commissioned grades based on the relative rank they held on that date.

9452.s: This order lets the Secretary of State set regulations, orders, and instructions for the duties and business of Foreign Service officers and employees, as long as they do not conflict with the Constitution, U.S. law, or other executive orders or proclamations. It also lets the Secretary set the form and publication method for those rules, but it does not change legal requirements for publication in the Federal Register.

9453.s: This order directs the Administrator of the Foreign Economic Administration to carry out functions about spending funds and providing supplies and services for the United States role in the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration. It also lets the United States representative on the Council designate alternates and members for the Council, committees, and subcommittees. All U.S. government activities for this participation must follow the foreign policy of the United States as defined by the Secretary of State.

9450.s: This order amends Foreign Service rules for how examinations are given and how the Foreign Service Officers' Training School is run. It creates a Board of Examiners made up of State, Commerce, Agriculture, and State Department officials, along with the Chief Examiner of the Civil Service Commission. It also puts the Training School under a board whose decisions must be approved by the Secretary of State.

9451.s: This order revokes paragraph 2 of Executive Order 9243. That paragraph had provided for priority classifications between executive departments and agencies, and the revocation takes effect July 1, 1944.

9448.s: This order lets the Select Committee to Investigate the Federal Communications Commission, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain income, excess-profits, and capital stock tax returns. The returns are for the years 1932 through 1938 and must be inspected under rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury so the committee can carry out House Resolution 21.

9449.s: This order changes the rules for paying losses caused by foreign currency changes for U.S. officers, enlisted men, and employees in foreign countries. It says that for people serving under the War or Navy Departments, no losses shall be paid, with certain listed exceptions. It also changes any other parts of the earlier order that conflict with these new rules.

9447.s: This order amends rules for clothing allowances for enlisted personnel of the Navy, the Coast Guard, the Naval Reserve, and the Coast Guard Reserve. It changes the cash clothing allowance amounts for fiscal year 1945 and updates when those payments may be made. It also changes how credits are handled for clothing issued in kind and for people who change status or reenlist.

9445.s: This order names the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico to act as judge of the United States District Court for Puerto Rico in the case of United States v. Julio Trinidad Geigel. It also lets him sign the needed papers and records for that case without extra commission. The order says the regular district judge had disqualified himself from acting in the case.

9446.s: This order sets rules for paying travel expenses for Veterans' Administration claimants and beneficiaries who travel with prior authorization for examination, treatment, or care. It allows payment of actual necessary travel costs, including lodging and subsistence, or an allowance of 3 cents per mile instead. If an attendant is needed, that person may also be allowed travel expenses on a similar basis.

9444.s: This order says certain income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, and capital stock tax returns may be inspected by the Special Committee on Un-American Activities of the House, or a duly authorized subcommittee. The inspection must follow rules and regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

9443.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the plants and facilities of Hummer Manufacturing Division of Montgomery Ward & Company in Springfield, Illinois. It also lets the Secretary use related property, keep or hire workers, and take other steps needed to run the plants for the war effort. The Secretary must follow the current employment terms and the National War Labor Board order dated April 14, 1944, and must end control within sixty days after productivity is restored.

9442.s: This order waives a federal rule that had limited federal officers and employees from holding certain state, territorial, or municipal offices. It allows Eugene E. Dickerson, the postmaster at Warmsprings, Montana, to also serve as Secretary to the Superintendent of the Montana State Hospital and Registrar of Vital Statistics. The same waiver also applies to future postmasters in that position while the Warmsprings post office is on the hospital grounds.

9441.s: This order suspends the eight-hour work limit for laborers and mechanics employed by the Veterans' Administration on public work within the United States that is essential to the prosecution of the war. It applies during the emergencies proclaimed on September 8, 1939, and May 27, 1941. Their wages and overtime pay must still be computed under existing law.

9440.s: This order lets the Reconstruction Finance Corporation place orders for materials, supplies, equipment, work, or services that a requisitioned federal agency can supply, provide by contract, or obtain by contract. It extends the same authority to any designated subsidiary or controlled agency or corporation of the Reconstruction Finance Corporation. It also says any conflicting executive order or proclamation is superseded to the extent of the conflict.

9438.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to take possession of and operate Montgomery Ward and Company plants and facilities in Chicago, including the mail order house, the retail store, and the Schwinn Warehouse. It also lets the Secretary use the company’s assets and exercise its contractual or other rights to carry out the order. The Secretary may take steps to protect the plants and the people employed or seeking work there. Control of any plant or facility must end within sixty days after the Secretary finds that productive efficiency has been restored.

9439.s: This order sets a monthly stipend of sixty dollars for student nurses transferred to Federal hospitals in the continental United States, excluding Alaska. The stipend applies for the training period needed for graduation. That training period cannot go beyond what the student nurse’s original school requires for graduation, and it may end earlier if the service needs it.

9436.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take over and operate the plants and facilities of the two Ken-Rad corporations in Owensboro, Kentucky. It says there is a threatened interruption because of a labor disturbance, and that this could delay the war effort. The Secretary of War may also provide protection for the plants and for people employed or seeking employment there.

9437.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 9165, which had provided for the protection of essential facilities from sabotage and other destructive acts. It also says this does not end any facility security functions of the War Department or stop needed cooperation on facility security between the War Department and any agency named in that earlier order.

9435.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of Jenkins Brothers’ plants and facilities in Bridgeport, Connecticut, and to operate them if needed. It says this is because a labor disturbance threatened to interrupt the plant’s operation and delay the war effort. The Secretary must run the plants under the current terms of employment and the National War Labor Board order, and may provide protection for the plants and workers. The possession and operation must end after productive efficiency is restored to its former level.

9434.s: This order sets aside a tract of land in the Canal Zone as a naval reservation called Naval Radio Station, Summit, Canal Zone. It places the area under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy, but keeps it subject to the civil jurisdiction of the Canal Zone Government. Naval authorities must pay the costs of the transfer, and Panama Canal personnel and equipment may enter the area to carry out necessary operations and protect Canal facilities.

9433.s: This order extends the limits of the customs ports of entry at Durham and Reidsville in North Carolina and Friday Harbor in Washington. It adds specific land areas around Durham and Reidsville and includes all points on Roche Harbor on San Juan Island. The order takes effect 30 days after it was signed.

9432.s: This order directs the Under Secretary of the Interior to do the Secretary of the Interior’s duties when the Secretary is absent or sick. It also directs Assistant Secretary Michael W. Straus, or his successors, and in his absence or sickness Assistant Secretary Oscar L. Chapman, or his successors, to do those duties when both the Secretary and the Under Secretary are absent or sick.

9431.s: This order changes Foreign Service rules on where diplomatic and consular officers may live while assigned to Foreign Service posts. It also says Foreign Service offices must stay open for the public during hours set by the Secretary of State, except for certain local holidays. Officers and employees of the Foreign Service must follow official duty hours set by law, the President, or the Secretary of State.

9430.s: This order makes certain corporation statistical transcript cards from income and declared value excess-profits tax returns open to inspection by the Office of Price Administration. The inspection must follow the rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury for similar cards for earlier taxable years.

9428.s: This order lets certain former Fingerprint Classifiers in the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Department of Justice, acquire a competitive classified civil-service status. It applies to people appointed between August 21, 1939, and June 3, 1941, if they had at least one year of continuous satisfactory service, left voluntarily without prejudice, are United States citizens, and are not otherwise disqualified under the Civil Service rules or laws.

9429.s: This order changes which office handles applications for Necessity Certificates. The Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy will decide certain older applications, while the Chairman of the War Production Board will decide other applications filed after December 17, 1943. It also says some certificates may be issued only if the Chairman first determines the facilities are clearly necessary for the war effort and that private financing is in the Government’s advantage.

9427.s: This order creates a Retraining and Reemployment Administration in the Office of War Mobilization. It gives the Administration general supervision over government work on retraining and reemploying people discharged or released from the armed services or other war work. It also directs the agency to develop programs for vocational training, job placement, help for those workers and their families, and care for wounded and disabled people, including physical and occupational therapy and resumed education.

9425.s: This order sets up the Surplus War Property Administration in the Office of War Mobilization. It gives the new office general supervision over how surplus war property is handled, moved between government agencies, and disposed of. The order also directs how different kinds of surplus property should be assigned, including consumer goods, industrial property, ships, food, and property sent outside the United States.

9426.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of certain water and power plants, facilities, and related property of the Department of Water and Power of the City of Los Angeles in California and Nevada. It applies to places where strikes or labor disturbances have occurred or are threatened, and it directs federal agencies to cooperate. The Secretary of War may let existing management continue as much as possible and must end possession and control within sixty days after the plants are restored to their prior level of efficiency.

9424.s: This order creates a separate register in the United States Patent Office for recording the Government’s rights and interests in patents and patent applications. Federal departments and agencies, including Government-owned or Government-controlled corporations, must send licenses, assignments, and other interests to be recorded. The register is open to inspection, except for entries or documents that are kept secret by the agency that submits them.

9423.s: This order transfers the War Relocation Authority and its functions to the Department of the Interior. It also moves the agency’s records, property, personnel, and unused funds to that department. The Director’s functions are transferred to the Secretary of the Interior, and the order takes effect immediately.

9422.s: This order approves the Army Air Forces’ use of 6,120.25 pounds of optical glass. The glass had been acquired by the Treasury Department’s Procurement Division and was stored with the Army Air Forces.

9421.s: This order designates Marriner S. Eccles as Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. He is to serve in that role for four years starting February 1, 1944.

9420.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate certain textile plants and facilities in and about Fall River, Massachusetts. It applies to the named companies and any additional nearby textile plants or installations linked to them where strikes have occurred or are threatened. Federal agencies must cooperate, and the plants are to be run under the terms and conditions of employment already in effect when possession is taken.

9419.s: This order establishes the Bronze Star Medal, with ribbons and other parts, for people serving in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard. It may be awarded for heroic or meritorious achievement or service in connection with military or naval operations against an enemy of the United States, and it can be given posthumously. Only one Bronze Star Medal may be awarded to a person, though a device may be added for later qualifying service.

9418.s: This order lets the War Food Administration place orders for materials, supplies, equipment, work, or services that certain federal agencies can supply, arrange by contract, or obtain by contract. It also lets the War Food Administrator name a constituent agency or corporation to use these same powers. Any conflicting executive order or proclamation is superseded to the extent of the conflict.

9417.s: This order creates a War Refugee Board in the Executive Office of the President. The board is responsible for helping rescue, transport, maintain, and provide relief for victims of enemy oppression, and for setting up temporary places of refuge. It also directs other departments and agencies to help the board and lets it work with foreign governments, private groups, and international organizations.

9416.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate the plants and facilities of York Safe & Lock Company in York County, Pennsylvania. It says the plants are to be used to produce essential war material for the United States. The Secretary of the Navy may hire employees and agents and use the company’s existing rights as needed to carry out the order.

9414.s: This order sets rules for annual and sick leave for civilian officers and employees of the United States, the District of Columbia, and certain covered corporations. It says how leave is earned, used, carried over, and charged, and it sets rules for court leave, sick leave, leave without pay, and advance sick leave. It also gives agency heads responsibility for administering these leave accounts and for making supplemental rules for employees with 24-hour shifts or other uncommon tours of duty.

9415.s: This order transfers six named Coast and Geodetic Survey officers to the service and jurisdiction of the War Department. While under the War Department, they remain commissioned in the Coast and Geodetic Survey, serve as part of the active military forces of the United States, and are subject to Army laws and orders where applicable. They are to be returned to the Coast and Geodetic Survey when the present national emergency ends.

9412.s: This order takes federal possession and control of railroad carriers and related facilities in the continental United States. The Secretary of War is directed to manage and operate them to keep transportation service continuous and uninterrupted. It also says existing contracts stay in effect, workers keep certain rights, and the Secretary may end federal control when it is no longer needed to prevent a break in service.

9411.s: This order sets a daily hospital rate for dependents of naval and Marine Corps personnel. It also sets rates for hospital and dispensary services outside the continental United States and in Alaska for other people covered by the law. It gives a price for each out-patient treatment, examination, or consultation, and a per diem rate for in-patient treatment.

9410.s: This order makes the Selective Service System a separate agency under the supervision and direction of the Director of Selective Service. It delegates to the Director certain functions, powers, and duties of the President under the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940 and Public Law 197, except for sections 3 and 4 of that law. The Director must consult with the Chairman of the War Manpower Commission on matters tied to the law and on coordination with the Chairman’s policies and programs.

9409.s: This order changes the makeup of the War Manpower Commission in the Office for Emergency Management. It says the Commission will include a chairman appointed by the President, representatives from listed agencies, a joint maritime representative, and the Director of Selective Service. It also revokes part of a previous executive order.

9408.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take immediate possession of and operate the Point Breeze plants and facilities of Western Electric Company in and near Baltimore, Maryland. It also lets him take over other related installations there if needed, and to take steps to protect the plant and people working or seeking work there. The order says management may keep its managerial functions as much as possible, and the takeover ends within sixty days after the plant’s prior productive efficiency has been restored.

9406.s: This order transfers some duties over Necessity Certificates from the Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy to the Chairman of the War Production Board. It applies to certificates for facilities needed for national defense and sets rules for which applications each office will handle. It also says certain regulations will govern those certificates and allows the Chairman to consult the War Department, Navy Department, and other agencies. It transfers related civilian personnel, property, records, and some funds to the War Production Board.

9405.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to change one listed job category under the Department of Agriculture. It covers positions in the Federal Intermediate Credit Banks, the Production Credit Corporations, the Federal Land Banks, the Banks for Cooperatives, and joint officers and employees for those institutions.

9407.s: This order changes the Foreign Service fee rules. It says there is no fee for services done for the official use of the Government of the United States, for certain notarial services tied to forms or documents for a U.S. department or agency, and for notarial services for members of the armed forces of the United States or civilian employees of the Government of the United States. It affects people who use these Foreign Service services for those government and military-related purposes.

9404.s: This order authorizes the Governor of The Panama Canal, or an acting officer, to acquire, use, and dispose of real property and personal property. It applies to property that is deemed necessary for military, naval, or other war purposes.

9403.s: This order directs the Secretary of War to give back possession of thirteen leather manufacturing plants in Salem, Peabody, and Danvers, Massachusetts, to the people who had them before the government took control. It says the plants’ productive efficiency had been restored. It also allows the Secretary of War to require information about how the plants were operated while the government had possession and control.

9401.s: This order suspends the eight-hour limit for laborers and mechanics employed by the Department of Agriculture, including the War Food Administration, on public work in the United States that is marked as essential to the prosecution of the war. It applies during the emergencies named in the order. Their pay must still be figured on an eight-hour basic day, with overtime paid at time and one-half for hours over eight in a day.

9400.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate the shipyard of the Los Angeles Shipbuilding and Drydock Corporation in Los Angeles, California. It says the shipyard is to be used to construct, convert, and repair vessels needed by the United States. The Secretary of the Navy may hire help and take steps needed to carry out the order, and the takeover will end within sixty days after the President determines the shipyard will be privately operated efficiently in a way consistent with the war effort.

9399.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate part of Remington Rand, Inc.’s plant in Southport, New York. It is to be used to produce war materials for the United States Navy Department and War Department. The order also says the President will end possession within 60 days after he decides the plant can be privately operated in a way consistent with the war effort.

9397.s: This order directs federal agencies, when they set up new permanent account number systems for individual persons, to use Social Security Act account numbers. It also directs the Social Security Board to assign numbers to people who need one and have not already been assigned one. Federal agencies and the Social Security Board must keep that personal information confidential.

9396.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to issue a citation in the President’s name to Army units and Army of the Philippine Commonwealth units for outstanding performance of duty in action. It also allows those units to display a streamer, emblem, or guidon band set by the Secretary of War. Officers and enlisted men assigned to a cited unit may receive a device to wear on their uniforms.

9398.s: This order extends the trust periods on Indian lands, whether tribal or individual, that would otherwise expire during calendar year 1944. It extends those trust periods for 25 more years from the date they would have expired. It does not apply to any case where Congress has specifically kept the power to extend the trust period.

9395-B.s: The order lets the Secretary of War take possession of and operate several leather plants in Salem, Peabody, and Danvers, Massachusetts. It says the plants may be used to make war materials for government contracts or other war needs. The order also says plant management should keep handling its own management functions as much as possible, and workers should be hired under existing collective bargaining contracts as needed.

9395-A.s: This order changes the rules for the National War Labor Board by allowing the President to appoint alternate public members for terms he sets. No more than four alternate public members may hold office at one time, and each would be paid $9,000 a year. When called by the Board, they may sit and vote, but no more than four public members, regular or alternate, may vote in any one case.

9394.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to add "Fourth-class postmasters in the Hawaiian Islands" to Subdivision VII of Schedule A. It affects those postmaster positions in the Hawaiian Islands under the civil service rules.

9395.s: This order gives enlisted Marine Corps personnel, including the Marine Corps Women's Reserve, who are regularly detailed as messmen the same extra compensation given to Navy enlisted personnel in similar roles. The Secretary of the Navy will set the rules for the number of messmen and the conditions for getting this extra pay. It replaces an older 1906 order and is effective as of November 1, 1943.

9393.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Interior to take possession of coal mines where a strike or stoppage has happened or is threatened, and to run them or arrange for them to be run. It also says the government should make work available, protect employees and people seeking work, and keep customary working conditions and grievance procedures. The order says workers may keep their labor organization membership, bargain collectively, and take concerted action so long as it does not interfere with mine operations.

9392.s: This order transfers certain powers, functions, and duties from the Secretary of Agriculture to the War Food Administrator. It covers duties under two earlier executive orders, matters tied to labor and manpower, and matters tied to agencies, personnel, property, and records. The War Food Administrator is also made the chairman of a committee set up under one earlier order and the United States member of the Combined Food Board. The War Food Administrator and the Secretary of Agriculture stay on the War Production Board.

9390.s: This order transfers the use, possession, and control of certain lands in the Nantahala National Forest from the Department of Agriculture to the Tennessee Valley Authority. The lands are in Swain County, North Carolina, and the transfer is for the purposes stated in the Tennessee Valley Authority Act of 1933. The order keeps any rights-of-way for public roads held by Swain County or North Carolina, and it also keeps a Southern Railway Company right-of-way for one of the tracts.

9391.s: This order transfers the use, possession, and control of certain lands in the Cherokee National Forest in Tennessee from the Department of Agriculture to the Tennessee Valley Authority. The lands are to be used for concrete or steel lined underground water diversion tunnels from the Ocoee No. 3 and Apalachia Dams to their power houses. Some rights of way and Forest Service rights are reserved, including access, surface structures, patrol, and forest product harvesting on the named strips.

9388.s: The order sets up a Special Emergency Board of three members to reconsider wage adjustment claims for nonoperating railway employees. The board must recommend any wage changes within the limits of the Act of October 2, 1942, and the related executive orders. The board must report by November 15, 1943, and its recommendations on wage and salary changes become effective 15 days after the report is filed unless the Economic Stabilization Director directs otherwise.

9387.s: This order sets up an Advisory Board on Just Compensation for the War Shipping Administration. The board must make fair and general standards, rules, and formulae to guide payment for vessels that are requisitioned, purchased, chartered, or insured by the Administration. The War Shipping Administration will use those standards when determining compensation for each vessel.

9386.s: This order sets rules for allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Survey, and Public Health Service when they are not given quarters or rations in kind. It also covers enlisted men of the first, second, and third grades who have dependents and are not provided public quarters for those dependents. The order gives different allowance rates for duty, travel, detentions, and certain locations, and it replaces earlier executive orders on this subject.

9389.s: This order changes how four federal offices are organized and managed. It lets the directors of the Office of Scientific Research and Development, the Office of the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs, and the Office of Defense Transportation handle their own internal organization and management. It also lets the Director of Civilian Defense delegate authority to agencies, officials, or personnel he designates, and lets some of these offices appoint committees or advisory committees.

9385.s: This order moves certain work on procuring and developing food, food machinery, and other food facilities in foreign countries from the War Food Administration and the Commodity Credit Corporation to the Foreign Economic Administration. It also transfers related personnel, records, property, funds, contracts, assets, and liabilities that are mainly tied to those functions. The order says the Foreign Economic Administration must follow certain directives on procurement, and it does not change some existing authority over priorities, allocations, or general policy.

9383.s: This order requires Federal civil agencies working in Puerto Rico or the Virgin Islands to send current reports to the Secretary of the Interior. It also gives the Secretary of the Interior power to make recommendations to those agencies to coordinate their work, cut unessential Federal activities, and help insular agencies take on more civil administration. The order does not apply to United States District Judges, United States Attorneys, or United States Marshals.

9382.s: This order revokes Westby, Montana, as a customs port of entry. It also extends the customs port of entry limits for Nogales, Arizona, and Douglas, Arizona, to include additional described territory. The changes take effect on October 1, 1943.

9381.s: This order amends an earlier order about stabilizing the national economy. It updates references to the Public Debt Act of 1943 and changes rules under Title II on wage increases and salary decreases. It also lets the National War Labor Board make exemptions for small total wage increases and removes one paragraph from Title II.

9379.s: This order creates a Special Emergency Board of three members to consider what wage adjustments, if any, should be made for employees of the Pacific Electric Railway Company of Los Angeles, California. The board must report to the President and also file copies with the Economic Stabilization Director, the National War Labor Board, and the Commissioner of Internal Revenue. The Economic Stabilization Director must then report on the effect of the recommendations on the general stabilization program, and the wage and salary changes become effective unless the Director directs otherwise.

9380.s: This order creates the Foreign Economic Administration in the Office for Emergency Management of the Executive Office of the President. It brings together several offices and their functions, powers, duties, personnel, property, records, funds, contracts, assets, liabilities, and capital stock into the new administration. The Administrator may set up offices, bureaus, or divisions and may assign them functions, and the administration must follow the foreign policy of the United States as defined by the Secretary of State.

9378.s: This order changes a prior executive order so the United States Civil Service Commission can set special rules for recruiting, placing, and changing the status of federal employees. It also covers dismissals because of a reduction in force. The rules apply to departments, independent establishments, and other federal agencies, except postmaster positions in all classes of post offices.

9376.s: This order reinstates John W. Bailey, Jr. in the Foreign Service of the United States in Class III. His reinstatement takes effect when the Senate confirms his nomination to that class.

9375.s: This order directs the War Shipping Administrator to take over and run the Atlantic Basin Iron Works plant in Brooklyn, New York. It says the plant's operation was threatened by a labor disturbance and that the war effort would be delayed if the interruption continued. The plant is to be used as needed to produce war materials, and the Secretary of War may provide protection for the plant and the people working there.

9377.s: This order directs the War Shipping Administrator to give back possession of the Atlantic Basin Iron Works plant in Brooklyn, New York, to Atlantic Basin Iron Works, Incorporated. It says the plant’s productive efficiency, as it was before the government took possession, has been restored.

9373.s: The order transfers control of certain functions, powers, and property for the Grand River Dam Project and the Norfork Dam Project to the Secretary of the Interior. It also directs the Secretary to integrate the power facilities of the Grand River, Norfork, and Denison projects, connect them with other utility systems, and arrange sales and exchanges of electric energy. The energy may be sold to war plants and establishments, public bodies and cooperatives, and other persons, in that order of preference.

9372.s: This order lets certain people be excepted from the classification of "alien enemy" if the Attorney General, the Commissioner of Immigration and Naturalization, or a District Director certifies after investigation that they are loyal to the United States. People covered by the order may apply for naturalization. It replaces Executive Order No. 9106 from March 20, 1942.

9371.s: This order changes the leave rules for government employees. It says that if an employee’s active service ends because a statute expires, and the employee still has accumulated or current accrued leave, the employee may be granted leave without pay or furlough for up to 12 months. It is effective as of August 23, 1943.

9369.s: This order names the Secretary of the Interior as the liquidating agent for the Office of the Bituminous Coal Consumers' Counsel. He is directed to take custody of the office's records and files, preserve them, and make them available to government agencies aiding the war effort. He is also directed to approve certain vouchers for obligations the office incurred before its statutory expiration, and to transfer needed office equipment and other property.

9370.s: This order authorizes the Director of Economic Stabilization to issue directives when the National War Labor Board says its orders have not been followed. It allows federal agencies to withhold priorities, benefits, privileges, or contracts from a non-complying employer, and it lets agencies seek action against a non-complying labor union. It also allows the War Manpower Commission to change or cancel draft deferments or employment privileges for non-complying individuals.

9368.s: This order extends a suspension of the eight-hour law to laborers and mechanics employed by the Department of the Interior on public works in the Territory of Alaska. It applies only to work the Secretary of the Interior designates as essential to the prosecution of the war. The work remains subject to the conditions and limitations in the earlier executive order.

9367.s: This order says government officers and employees may not directly or indirectly instruct people to prepare for Civil Service Commission exams or Foreign Service exams. It allows government agencies to use government facilities and federal staff for training and testing disabled members or former members of the armed forces, and for educational or training programs open only to members or former members of the armed forces. It also says a violation can be cause for removal from government service.

9366.s: This order puts the Secretary of the Interior in charge of selling and distributing electric power made at the Denison Dam Project that is not needed to run the project. It directs the Secretary of War to complete, maintain, and operate the project, and it sets a preference order for sales to war plants, public bodies and cooperatives, and other persons. It also transfers certain authority and related property for the Grand River Dam Authority project in Oklahoma and the Norfork Project in Arkansas and Missouri to the Secretary of the Interior.

9365.s: This order establishes the Women's Army Corps Service Medal. It may be awarded, under rules set by the Secretary of War, to members of the Women's Army Corps for honorable service in the Women's Army Auxiliary Corps.

9364.s: This order sets a cap on how many women can be enlisted or appointed in the Women's Army Corps. It says the total number may not exceed two hundred thousand.

9363.s: This order moves some court-martial functions, duties, and powers from the Secretary of War and the Judge Advocate General to the Under Secretary of War, the Assistant Secretary of War, and the Assistant Judge Advocate General in charge of military justice matters. It lets those officials act on those matters without extra approval, unless the Secretary of War sets regulations that require it. The Secretary of War and the Judge Advocate General may still use their own powers if they choose.

9362.s: This order transfers a tract of land in Wahiawa, on the Island of Oahu in Hawaii, from the Federal Communications Commission to the Navy Department. The land and the buildings on it are to be used as a naval radio station site or for other naval purposes. It also includes any easement rights for the tract.

9361.s: This order ends the Board of Economic Warfare and creates an Office of Economic Warfare in the Office for Emergency Management. It transfers the board’s work, money, property, records, and staff to the new office, and also transfers several corporations and related functions to it. It also says the Office of War Mobilization may coordinate federal activities on foreign supply, foreign procurement, and other foreign economic affairs.

9360.s: This order suspends the eight-hour limit for laborers and mechanics employed by the Department of the Interior on public works within the United States that are designated as essential to the prosecution of the war. It applies during the stated emergencies. Their pay must still be based on an eight-hour day, with overtime paid at time and one-half for hours over eight in a day.

9359.s: This order suspends compliance with certain employment rules for the Canal Zone found in three 1944 appropriation acts. The suspension lasts while any war the United States is now engaged in continues.

9358.s: This order puts the Civil Service Commission in charge of civil service laws as they apply to attorney positions in the classified civil service, while Congress considers whether to continue the Board of Legal Examiners. It lets the Commission set the rules and procedures for recruiting and examining applicants and for selecting, appointing, promoting, and transferring attorneys. It also says Executive Order 8743, as amended, stays in effect unless changed by this order or a later order.

9357.s: This order transfers the functions, powers, and duties of the Public Works Administration and the Commissioner of Public Works to the Federal Works Administrator. It also transfers the agency’s records, property, personnel, and unused funds. Any personnel found to be more than needed may be moved to other government jobs or separated from service.

9356.s: This order sets rules for giving clothing in kind or cash clothing allowances to enlisted personnel of the Navy, Coast Guard, Naval Reserve, and Coast Guard Reserve. It also sets a quarterly maintenance allowance for some enlisted men and says when that allowance starts and who cannot get it. The order does not apply to enlisted members of the Women's Reserve of the Naval Reserve and the Women's Reserve of the Coast Guard Reserve, who get a special quarterly clothing allowance instead.

9355.s: This order changes the clothing allowance rules for members of the Naval Reserve and the Coast Guard Reserve. It sets different clothing-in-kind limits for Naval Reserve members in flight training and in other training leading to a commission, and it says some members who do not finish flight training may get the cash allowances allowed under the order. It also says temporary Coast Guard Reserve members on part-time or intermittent active duty may be issued clothing in kind instead of cash clothing allowances.

9354.s: This order adds the Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission as an additional member of the Economic Stabilization Board. It also amends Executive Order 9250 to reflect that change.

9353.s: This order directs that the Norfork Project be completed, maintained, and operated under the Secretary of War and the Chief of Engineers. It requires the electric energy generated there to be delivered to the Federal Works Administrator, who is authorized to sell it and arrange for transmission and distribution. The order also lets the Administrator allocate transmission and distribution lines for this purpose and says the money from these sales goes to the U.S. Treasury.

9352.s: This order sets rules for the entry of alien seamen into the United States. It requires crew lists and certain identity papers for many seamen arriving on vessels, and it limits when they may land or get shore leave. It also gives some exemptions for certain seamen entering as passengers or workaways, and for returning residents who were lawfully admitted for permanent residence.

9351.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate the Howarth Pivoted Bearings Company plant in Philadelphia. It says the plant is needed to produce war materials required by the United States. The Secretary may hire employees and use the company's existing rights as needed to carry out the order.

9350.s: This order lets the Administrator of the War Shipping Administration keep using certain powers over foreign merchant vessels lying idle in U.S. waters, including the Philippine Islands and the Canal Zone. Those powers include buying, requisitioning, chartering, using, or taking title to or possession of the vessels. It also approves the Administrator’s later actions on those matters after June 30, 1942.

9349.s: The order directs the Secretary of the Navy to give back the plants of Milford Ordnance Company, Inc. and Sussex Ordnance Company in Milford, Delaware. It says the plants will be privately operated in a way consistent with the war effort.

9348.s: This order changes the rules for what household goods and personal effects may include when certain civilian officers and employees have their transportation expenses paid. It says groceries, provisions, wines, liquors, animals not needed for official duties, birds, and automobiles are not allowed, except that groceries and provisions may be included during Government rationing of foods.

9347.s: This order creates an Office of War Mobilization in the Executive Office of the President. It also creates a War Mobilization Committee made up of top war and economic officials, with the Director as chairman. The office is directed to make unified plans and policies for using the nation’s resources and manpower for war needs, and to coordinate federal agencies involved in production, procurement, distribution, and transportation of supplies.

9346.s: This order establishes a new Committee on Fair Employment Practice and ends the old fair employment committee once the new one is appointed. It says there shall be no discrimination in war industries or in government employment because of race, creed, color, or national origin. It also requires government contracts and war production training programs to be handled without that discrimination, and it lets the committee receive and investigate complaints.

9345.s: This order says certain income, excess-profits, and declared value excess-profits tax returns for 1939 and later years may be inspected by the Naval Affairs Investigating Committee of the House of Representatives, or an authorized subcommittee. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury. It applies to the committee and to the tax returns covered by the order.

9344.s: This order changes the name of the Alley Dwelling Authority to the National Capital Housing Authority. It also updates the earlier executive order that set up that authority to match the new name. The change takes effect on June 1, 1943.

9343.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over a 35-acre tract of land on Government Island, California, to the Navy Department for the duration of the emergency. It also transfers the Federal Works Agency’s rights over buildings and other facilities on a 15-acre tract to the Navy Department, with some limited use still allowed for Building No. 22. The order lets the Federal Works Agency transfer some personnel, machinery, equipment, and tools to the Navy Department for Coast Guard use, and says these rights and items will return to the Federal Works Agency when the emergency ends.

9341.s: This order directs the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation to take control of the American Railroad Company of Porto Rico’s property and operate the railroad. It says the railroad was interrupted by a labor dispute and was needed to move supplies and food for the armed forces and civilian population during the war. The National War Labor Board must decide the labor dispute, and the order says existing health, safety, security, and employment laws still apply to railroad employees.

9342.s: This order changes a prior order that set up a defensive sea area. It defines the area to include United States territorial waters of Narragansett Bay, the Sakonnet River, Providence Harbor, and their tributaries, with boundary lines set in several places, including across the Taunton River and the Seekonk River.

9340.s: The order directs the Secretary of the Interior to take over coal mines where strikes have happened or are threatened, along with property and other assets used to run them. He is to operate the mines or arrange for their operation and do what is needed for coal production, sale, and distribution. The order also says workers may keep their labor memberships, bargain collectively, and seek protection, and that the takeover ends when it is no longer needed for the war program.

9339.s: This order transfers the Civil Air Patrol, along with its functions, duties, and powers, from the Office of Civilian Defense to the Department of War. It also transfers related property, civilian and military personnel, and some available funds to the Department of War. The Secretary of War is to supervise and direct the work under this order.

9337.s: This order lets the Secretary of the Interior withdraw or reserve public lands and other lands owned or controlled by the United States, to the same extent the President could do so. It also lets the Secretary modify or revoke those withdrawals or reservations. Orders under this authority must have prior approval from the Director of the Bureau of the Budget and the Attorney General, and lands under another department or agency need that department or agency head's concurrence.

9338.s: This order abolishes the Office of Defense Health and Welfare Services. It transfers that office’s functions, duties, powers, personnel, property, records, and funds to the Federal Security Agency and the Federal Security Administrator. The transferred work is to be handled through the Office of Community War Services or other offices in the agency.

9335.s: This order adds the Chairman of the War Manpower Commission, the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation, and the Petroleum Administrator for War to the War Production Board. It changes the membership of that board by adding those officials.

9336.s: This order authorizes the Office of Lend-Lease Administration and the War Shipping Administration to make financing arrangements with the War Department, the Navy Department, and the Maritime Commission. These arrangements can include guaranties, indemnification agreements, and agreements to provide funds tied to certain loans, discounts, advances, contracts, guaranties, or commitments. It also allows these offices to delegate this authority and requires them to keep records of the arrangements, with some data available for public inspection.

9334.s: This order creates a War Food Administration within the Department of Agriculture by combining several food-related agencies and their powers. It transfers certain food, labor, manpower, personnel, property, records, and funds to the War Food Administrator, who is appointed by the President and reports directly to him. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps some named roles and shares some authority with the War Food Administrator for matters covered by the order.

9333.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules for the Inland Waterways Corporation. For the duration of the war and six months after, all positions in or under that corporation are covered by this rule.

9331.s: This order sets rules for awarding the Medal for Merit, which may be given only by the President or at his direction. It may be awarded to certain civilians of nations prosecuting the war and other friendly foreign nations who have shown exceptionally meritorious conduct in outstanding services, and foreign civilians need prior approval from the Secretary of State. It creates a Medal for Merit Board made up of the Secretary of State, the Secretary of War, and the Secretary of the Navy to review proposals and make recommendations to the President.

9332.s: This order creates a Solid Fuels Administration for War within the Department of the Interior. The Secretary of the Interior serves as the Administrator, and the office is meant to help conserve, develop, and use solid fuels for the war effort. It gives the Administrator authority to issue directives to the solid fuels industries, gather information, and work with other federal departments and agencies. It also transfers the work, records, property, and funds of the former solid fuels coordination office to the new administration.

9329.s: This order designates Emory B. Land as Chairman of the United States Maritime Commission. It changes who will lead that commission.

9330.s: This order moves certain fiscal duties for the Office of Price Administration and the War Production Board to those agencies. It also transfers field personnel recruitment and field job classification work to the United States Civil Service Commission. The order says personnel, records, property, and some unspent funds tied to these functions may also be transferred.

9328.s: The order directs agencies to put ceiling prices on commodities that affect the cost of living and to prevent further price increases, profiteering, and excessively high prices. It also directs agencies to stop further wage or salary increases except when needed to correct substandard living conditions or make certain allowed adjustments. The order gives the War Manpower Commission power to limit new hiring in some cases, and it tells federal, state, and local authorities to work to keep utility and carrier rates from rising.

9327.s: This order creates a committee to handle government problems in congested production areas that have grown because of the war and lack enough services or facilities. The committee can name these areas, work with state and local governments, and coordinate federal agencies that deal with congestion there. It also sets up area directors and advisory councils to help carry out the order. The order stays in effect until Title I of the First War Powers Act, 1941 ends.

9325.s: This order lets the Alien Property Custodian pay necessary expenses from funds in his custody or control for carrying out his duties. It also lets him recover those expenses from specific property or other property tied to the former owner, and it says this power is not limited by claims or lawsuits about the property. The Office of Alien Property Custodian must submit budget estimates to the Bureau of the Budget, and after April 30, 1943, it may not spend beyond the amounts approved.

9326.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over the oil and gas deposits in a tract of land in California from the War Department to the Department of the Interior. The Secretary of the Interior is to take action to protect the United States from loss from drainage or threatened drainage of oil and gas from the land. The Department of the Interior’s jurisdiction is subject to the War Department’s primary jurisdiction for flood control and navigation, and royalties from oil and gas from the land must be paid into the Treasury of the United States.

9322.s: This order consolidates several food production and distribution agencies within the Department of Agriculture into one Administration of Food Production and Distribution. It places that new administration under an Administrator appointed by the President and directly responsible to him. The order also transfers certain powers, personnel, property, records, and funds from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Administrator. It applies to the agencies and functions named in the order.

9324.s: This order amends the Army Manual for Courts-Martial. It changes rules on military court records, oaths, notarial powers, and the use of official seals and forms. It also says commissioned officers and persons with similar rank are excepted from the jurisdiction of special courts-martial.

9321.s: This order lets the Attorney General acquire, use, and dispose of real property, temporary use of property, and other interests in property. It also covers personal property on that land or used with it when it is needed for military, naval, or other war purposes.

9320.s: This order changes a prior order about the Toledo, Peoria and Western Railroad. It lets the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation use net cash earnings from running the railroad to pay lawful obligations and preserve the railroad’s property, corporate organization, franchises, rights, and other assets. The money may not be used for executive salaries beyond what is needed for those purposes or for dividends, and the advances do not have to be repaid until the railroad’s compensation claim is finally settled.

9319.s: This order changes a prior order about the Petroleum Administration for War. It lets the Administrator appoint a Deputy Administrator, with the President’s approval, and delegate powers to that person. The Deputy Administrator reports to the Administrator and acts for the Administrator when the Administrator is absent.

9318.s: This order reinstates Maxwell M. Hamilton in the Foreign Service of the United States in Class I. His reinstatement takes effect when the Senate confirms his nomination to that class.

9316.s: This order changes a prior order about requisitioning property needed for national defense. It requires the War Production Board to send the President reports on operations under the act of October 16, 1941 once every six months.

9317.s: This order directs the Treasury Department’s Procurement Division to make quinine sulfate available from its stocks. The quinine sulfate is for use by the Army and the Navy. It also says the sales and delivery terms must be mutually satisfactory to the Procurement Division and the buyers and users.

9315.s: This order transfers all functions, duties, and powers given to the President by section 4 of a 1936 act to the Secretary of Agriculture. It affects the President and the Secretary of Agriculture.

9314.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 8955. That earlier order had extended the Classification Act of 1923 to certain positions in the War Department and the Navy Department and set a salary differential for them.

9313.s: This order extends the rules in Executive Order 9231 to the construction of Red Mountain Chromite Road near Seldovia in the Territory of Alaska. The road is being built by the Department of the Interior. The extension is subject to the same conditions and limits in the earlier order.

9312.s: This order gives the Office of War Information responsibility for the federal program of radio, press, publication, and related foreign propaganda activities. It says foreign propaganda in areas of actual or projected military operations must be coordinated with military plans and approved by the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Parts carried out in a theater of military operations are subject to the theater commander, and the office’s authority does not extend to the Western Hemisphere, except the United States and Canada.

9310.s: This order transfers the nutrition functions of the Office of Defense Health and Welfare Services to the Department of Agriculture. It also transfers the personnel, property, and records mainly used for those functions, along with some unspent funds. The Secretary of Agriculture will supervise and direct these duties through agencies in the department he designates.

9311.s: This order sets aside about 374.64 acres of land in Holt County, Missouri for the Department of the Interior. It adds that land to the Squaw Creek National Wildlife Refuge, subject to valid existing rights. The order says this is to further the purposes of the Migratory Bird Conservation Act.

9309.s: This order limits when federal agencies can ask for selective service deferment of employees. It sets up review and agency committees to decide which jobs are key positions and to handle deferment requests, appeals, and reports. It also says agencies may grant or deny an employee’s request to leave for voluntary service in the armed forces based on the rules in the order.

9308.s: This order revokes Gastonia, North Carolina’s designation as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District Number 15. It affects the customs port status of Gastonia in North Carolina.

9306.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to give back possession of the Triumph Explosives plants in Elkton, Maryland, to Triumph Explosives, Incorporated. The plants had been under Navy control to help produce war materials. The order says the President determined the plants would be privately operated in a way consistent with the war effort.

9307.s: This order changes the annual leave rules for Government employees. It defines accumulated leave and lets eligible permanent employees earn current annual leave, carry unused leave into later years, and accumulate extra leave during the national emergency declared on September 8, 1939. Departments and agencies must adjust leave records to make the changes work back to that date.

9305.s: This order transfers four named commissioned officers from the Coast and Geodetic Survey to the War Department. While under War Department control, they serve under their Coast and Geodetic Survey commissions and are subject to Army laws, regulations, and orders as applicable. The order also returns two other named officers to the Coast and Geodetic Survey, and says the four transferred officers will be returned when the present national emergency ends.

9304.s: This order designates and authorizes Martin Travieso, an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico, to act as Judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico. He may perform the judge’s duties and sign necessary papers and records during the judge’s absence, illness, or other legal disability in the current calendar year, without extra compensation.

9303.s: This order changes Foreign Service fee rules for notarial and other services given to officials of foreign governments who give free reciprocal courtesies to officers of the United States, including military and naval officers. For those services, no fee is charged. It also revokes sections V-49 through V-52 of the Foreign Service Regulations and deletes the words "in the handwriting of the officer" from section V-54(d).

9302.s: This order transfers certain duties from the Attorney General and the Department of Justice to the Commissioner of Internal Revenue. It covers deciding Internal Revenue taxes and penalties from violations of the National Prohibition Act before the repeal of the Eighteenth Amendment, and handling compromises of that liability before any suit. It also makes Justice Department files and records available to the Commissioner for these functions.

9301.s: This order sets a minimum work week of 48 hours for the duration of the war at plants, factories, and other places of employment, unless a different minimum is set for a particular case. Federal departments and agencies must require their contractors to follow this rule and must help enforce it. The Chairman of the War Manpower Commission decides how to apply the order and can issue rules to carry it out. It does not change other laws or agreements on hours, wages, or overtime.

9300.s: This order creates an interdepartmental committee in the Department of Justice to deal with complaints of subversive activity by executive branch employees. The committee will review complaints, receive investigative reports from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and advise departments on what action to take. Federal departments and agencies must refer covered complaints to the FBI and report back on what they do in those cases.

9298.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules by adding the Solicitor of the Post Office Department to Schedule A. It also says that for the Tax Court of the United States, each member may have two private secretaries or confidential assistants.

9299.s: This order sets rules for wage and salary changes for employees covered by the Railway Labor Act. It says such changes cannot be made except under this order and related approval procedures. It also applies special review rules to proposed changes and directs certain boards and agencies to handle pending and future applications.

9296.s: This order changes the reporting rules for the War Department, the Navy Department, and the United States Maritime Commission. Instead of reporting all contracts and purchases to the President, they must keep complete data on them and make some of it available for public inspection, except for restricted, confidential, or secret contracts or purchases. It also applies to other government departments and agencies that were or may be covered by Executive Order 9001.

9297.s: This order changes the customs field organization. It expands the customs ports of entry for Portland, Maine, and Bangor, Maine, and moves Council Bluffs, Iowa, from one customs district to another. It also extends the Omaha, Nebraska, customs port of entry to include Council Bluffs and certain Nebraska townships.

9295.s: This order changes the rules for allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men. It says enlisted men on duty where emergency conditions justify such allowances may receive them at rates not to exceed the amounts listed, as determined by the head of the department concerned. It is effective as of January 1, 1943.

9293.s: This order sets aside a tract of land in the Canal Zone as a military reservation called Quarry Heights Military Reservation. It places the reservation under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of War, while still subject to the civil jurisdiction of Canal Zone authorities. It also replaces a 1936 order and releases any land covered by that earlier order that is not included in this new reservation.

9292.s: The order withdraws public lands in Stillwater County, Montana, and sets them aside as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also says lands in Petroleum Reserve No. 40 stay subject to primary use for oil and gas development. It is unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

9294.s: This order gives the Office of Defense Transportation more duties over local passenger transportation equipment, including buses, streetcars, trolley coaches, ferryboats, and similar vehicles. It tells the office to help plan transportation for moving people to and from war plants and other needed services, and to review or approve certain contracts for buying, leasing, requisitioning, or using that equipment. It also says domestic transportation in U.S. territories and possessions is within the office's authority, and it does not apply to military and naval movements in certain special operations.
