8857.s: This order sets aside land and water on Uganik Island and the western part of Kodiak Island, Alaska, as the Kodiak National Wildlife Refuge. It is meant to protect brown bears and other wildlife and to serve as a refuge and breeding ground for them. The order also limits settlement and other land disposal in the area, with some exceptions for existing rights, a shore strip, livestock use, hunting, trapping, and future Indian reservations.

8856.s: This order allows the Postal Service to appoint temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers for part-time or intermittent holiday or seasonal work without following the Civil Service Rules. It applies to Postal Service employees needed from November 15, 1941, to January 15, 1942.

8854.s: This order revokes a 1939 order that had reserved certain lands near Sitka, Alaska for a magnetic and seismological observatory site. It also withdraws those lands, plus an adjoining tract, from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. The land is reserved for use by the United States Coast and Geodetic Survey, Department of Commerce, as an observatory site.

8855.s: This order exempts certain jobs from a salary schedule for some positions not covered by the Classification Act. It applies to consultants, experts, specialists, attorneys, and similar positions that are paid on a per diem basis or for part-time service. It covers people paid from public works or other emergency funds handled by the Secretary of the Interior or the Federal Works Administrator through the Commissioner of Public Works.

8852.s: This order transfers the United States Coast Guard for the District of Honolulu, Territory of Hawaii, along with its organization, personnel, and equipment, from the Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of the Navy. It makes the Coast Guard operate as part of the Navy and subject to Navy control during the unlimited national emergency proclaimed on May 27, 1941.

8853.s: This order sets up the Manila Bay Defensive Sea Area in the territorial waters of Manila Bay, its approaches, and tributaries, for national defense. Vessels not under United States Naval or other United States authorized supervision may not enter or navigate there except in daylight with good visibility and after getting specific permission. Ships in the area must follow any further instructions from United States Navy or other United States authority, and those who disobey may be detained, attacked, or prosecuted.

8851.s: This order transfers the United States Coast Guard Ship Redwing from the Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of the Navy. It says the ship will operate as part of the Navy and be subject to Navy control during the unlimited national emergency proclaimed on May 27, 1941.

8850.s: This order authorizes the Commandant of the Coast Guard to take over foreign merchant marine training ships that are lying idle in waters within the United States. The ships may be purchased, chartered, or requisitioned for use in training Coast Guard cadets and merchant marine personnel. The Commandant is also directed to operate, repair, equip, and man the ships, and to pay just compensation to the owners.

8843.s: This order directs the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to regulate and, when needed, prohibit certain credit transactions. It mainly covers installment credit used to buy or carry consumers' durable goods, except a residential building in its entirety. It can also reach other consumer credit and loans to prevent evasion, and it affects banking institutions and people using or extending that credit.

8849.s: This order allows Margaret Patterson to be appointed as Assistant Historical Aide at the Andrew Johnson National Monument. It says she may be appointed without following the Civil Service Rules.

8847.s: This order withdraws public lands in a described area of Alaska from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the land for use by the War Department as an aerial bombing and gunnery range, subject to valid existing rights.

8848.s: This order suspends the eight-hour limit for laborers and mechanics employed by the War Department on certain public works in the United States needed for national defense. It applies to cantonments, air fields, fortifications, and other public works that the Secretary of War specifies as needing more than eight hours of work per day. It also says workers must be paid a basic eight-hour day rate, with overtime at not less than time and one-half for hours over eight in a day.

8846.s: This order revokes a 1910 license to build, maintain, and run an electric street railway system between the City of Panama and certain points in the Canal Zone. It affects the company that succeeded Henry T. Cook and had announced it was ending all service and tearing down the line. After the revocation, the authority to operate the railway in the Canal Zone ends at once.

8845.s: This order revokes Grand Rapids, Michigan, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 38. It takes effect at the close of business on the thirtieth day after the date of the order.

8844.s: This order changes a previous exemption for Harry T. Edwards, a senior technologist in the Bureau of Plant Industry at the Department of Agriculture. It extends his exemption from compulsory retirement for age for one more year, until October 31, 1942.

8841.s: This order restores certain public lands in Nebraska to the status they had under an earlier executive order. The lands are reserved for classification and for deciding the most useful purposes for them under the land program, including conservation and development of natural resources. It applies to the public lands in the listed areas, with some parts excluded because they are in Fort Robinson reservations.

8840.s: This order creates the Office of the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs in the Executive Office of the President. The office is to work on cultural and commercial relations between the American republics and to help with hemisphere defense. It may work with other government agencies, make contracts, and use funds and personnel for these duties.

8842.s: This order sets within-grade salary increases for employees covered by the salary schedule in Executive Order No. 6746. It sets different increment amounts for grades 1 to 7, 8 to 12, 13 to 16, and 17 to 19, and says employees may move up one increment after the required service period if their performance, conduct, and other conditions are met. It also lets department or agency heads give an additional increase for especially meritorious service, within available appropriations.

8839.s: This order creates an Economic Defense Board to help develop and coordinate policies and programs to protect and strengthen U.S. economic relations for national defense. The Board includes top officials from several departments, and it can also add other members with the President's approval. It advises the President, coordinates department and agency actions, studies related laws, and works with existing agencies on economic defense matters.

8837.s: This order sets rules for overtime pay for certain per-annum field service employees in the War Department, Navy Department, Coast Guard, and The Panama Canal. If their overtime work is essential and directly connected to other overtime work, they may be paid one and one-half times their regular rate for hours over forty in a workweek. It also says overtime should be kept to the absolute minimum, and that some employees should not be required or allowed to work overtime if it would harm their health or efficiency.

8838.s: This order changes a prior order about transferring certain vessels between the Navy Department and the Department of Commerce. It replaces the United States Navy Vessel Jamestown with the United States Navy Vessel Argus in that transfer.

8835.s: This order exempts Charles A. Appel, a chief accountant and auditor in the Bureau of Internal Revenue, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him and extends his service until October 31, 1942.

8836.s: This order exempts Paul Bartsch from compulsory retirement for age for one year. He was a curator at the United States National Museum, Smithsonian Institution, and the exemption applies through August 31, 1942.

8834.s: The order designates the Honorable Robert H. Todd, Jr., to serve as Acting Judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico. He may perform the judge’s duties and sign necessary papers and records when the judge is absent, ill, or otherwise legally unable to serve. He is to do this without extra compensation during the current calendar year.

8831.s: This order withdraws the described public land in Florida from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the land for the use of the War Department for military purposes, subject to valid existing rights. It also takes precedence over Executive Order No. 6964 for that land, but does not revoke it.

8832.s: This order changes Executive Order No. 8389 by adding a new subdivision to Section 3. The new subdivision lists "China, and Japan" with the date June 14, 1941.

8830.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for use by the War Department as a training center, subject to valid existing rights. It says this order takes precedence over Executive Order No. 6910 for these lands, but does not rescind or revoke that order for them.

8829.s: This order exempts William D. Terrell from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him as Chief, Field Division, Engineering Department, Federal Communications Commission.

8828.s: This order exempts Louis Loebl, a special agent in the Federal Bureau of Investigation, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. It applies only to him and extends through September 30, 1942.

8827.s: This order further exempts Harry T. Edwards, a senior technologist in the Bureau of Plant Industry at the Department of Agriculture, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and extends his earlier exemption.

8826.s: This order extends the Civil Service Retirement Act to James Edgar Smith, Patrick J. Farrell, and John McChord. They are employees of the Interstate Commerce Commission. The commission says they served faithfully and honorably for 34, 40, and 27 years.

8824.s: This order sets the grades and ratings of enlisted men in the Regular Army, including selective service trainees, for fiscal year 1942. It keeps them the same as in a prior order, except for the maximum number of enlisted men in the 7th grade. That maximum must be limited so the total with men above Grade Seven and authorized flying cadets does not exceed the Army’s enlisted pay strength covered by the Military Appropriation Act, 1942.

8825.s: This order exempts Bernard S. Kroger, a foreman of plate printing at the Bureau of Engraving and Printing in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It affects only him and extends his service until August 31, 1942.

8821.s: This order sets aside about 20 acres in Nevada at the Boulder City Airport site for naval aviation purposes. The land is placed under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy. The order says this reservation takes precedence over earlier reservations and withdrawals for that land, but it does not rescind or revoke them.

8820.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by adding rules on nationality, passports, registration, and protection abroad. It tells Foreign Service officers what duties they must carry out for American nationals, including handling passport services and registration abroad. It also cancels certain parts of the regulations and revokes several earlier executive orders.

8822.s: This order changes a prior order about the Office of Civilian Defense. It adds the American Red Cross to the organizations invited to name a representative to serve on the Board for Civilian Protection.

8819.s: This order excludes a tract of public land in Nevada from the Humboldt National Forest. It reserves that land for townsite purposes and says it will be disposed of under the listed federal laws. The land is described as the East Mountain City Townsite, which is occupied as a townsite.

8817.s: This order sets rules for paying certain employees of the War Department, Navy Department, Coast Guard, and The Panama Canal instead of giving them annual leave they cannot take. It applies when their services cannot be spared without hurting national defense, and it covers employees who would lose leave under existing law and regulations. It also allows some employees in construction, manufacturing, processing, or similar work to get this payment for current annual leave, subject to the limits in the order.

8816.s: This order suspends the Saturday half-holiday rules for certain civil employees of the War Department and its field services, and for certain civil employees of the Coast Guard and its field services. It applies to employees working in the Canal Zone, Puerto Rico, and the Territory of Alaska, and lasts for the duration of the national emergency.

8818.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by adding rules for documenting merchandise imported into the United States. It tells consular officers to help enforce U.S. laws on invoice certification, may require a power of attorney for agents signing invoices, and must help customs and tariff officials when asked. It also limits how consular officers answer questions about tariff acts or customs regulations and revokes two earlier executive orders.

8814.s: This order tells the Secretary of War to give back control of the Inglewood plant of North American Aviation, Inc. The plant had been taken over to produce aircraft and other materials for U.S. contracts and to protect workers returning to the plant. The order says the plant will now be privately operated in a way consistent with the needs of national defense.

8813.s: This executive order revokes part of Power Site Reserve No. 759 in New Mexico. It removes the reserve from the listed lands in Township 11 South, Range 20 West, under the New Mexico Principal Meridian.

8815.s: This order revokes Lancaster, Minnesota’s designation as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 34 (Dakota). It applies to Lancaster, Minnesota, and takes effect at the close of business on the thirtieth day after the date of the order.

8812.s: This order suspends compliance with certain statutory provisions about some kinds of employment in the Canal Zone. The suspension takes effect July 1, 1941, and lasts during the continuing unlimited national emergency declared on May 27, 1941.

8811.s: The order lets the Director of the Office of Government Reports keep employed people who worked there on June 30, 1941. It says certain vacant jobs after that date must be filled under the Civil Service Rules. People kept in their jobs may get competitive classified civil service status on January 1, 1942 if they are still employed, and the order also covers people who left for active military or naval service.

8810.s: This order further exempts Hubert K. Bishop from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to Bishop, who was Chief of the Division of Construction in the Public Roads Administration of the Federal Works Agency.

8809.s: This order establishes a Good Conduct Medal for the Army of the United States. It may be awarded to enlisted men who complete three years of active Federal military service, are recommended by their commanding officers, and show exemplary behavior, efficiency, and fidelity.

8808.s: This order establishes the American Defense Service Medal and says it may be awarded with suitable appurtenances. It applies to personnel of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard who served during the limited emergency proclaimed on September 8, 1939, or the unlimited emergency proclaimed on May 27, 1941.

8807.s: This order creates the Office of Scientific Research and Development in the Executive Office of the President. It gives the office duties over scientific and medical research related to national defense, including coordinating research, mobilizing scientific and medical personnel, and helping with contracts and agreements. It also creates advisory groups and committees to assist the Director in these tasks.

8806.s: This order requires 900,000 men to be inducted into the land forces of the United States between July 1, 1941, and June 30, 1942. It directs the Secretary of War to request up to that number and induct them. It also directs the Director of Selective Service to oversee the selection of men and make enough available to fill those requests.

8805.s: This order exempts Samuel A. Cottrell, an auditor in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. It affects only him and extends his earlier exemptions.

8804.s: This order exempts James E. Harper, Chief of the Employee Relations Section in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age for three more months. It applies only to him and extends a previous exemption.

8802.s: This order says there shall be no discrimination in defense industries or government hiring because of race, creed, color, or national origin. It directs government departments and agencies to run defense training programs without discrimination and to put this rule into defense contracts. It also creates a committee to receive and investigate complaints and to recommend further steps.

8801.s: This order exempts Archie W. Davis from compulsory retirement for age for one year. Davis was an assistant mail, file and record clerk in the Immigration and Naturalization Service at the Department of Justice. It affects him only and extends through July 31, 1942.

8803.s: This order changes parts of the Civil Service Rules by adding and revising jobs that are listed in Schedule A. It covers some people working in foreign countries, the Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico, certain Pacific island possessions, the Philippine Islands, and some jobs in Canada and Mexico. It also adds special assistants to the Secretary of State, certain Weather Bureau agents, all positions in or under the Inland Waterways Corporation until June 30, 1943, and certain Federal Works Agency field agents.

8800.s: This order amends the list of basic exchange rates used for paying losses sustained by officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States in foreign countries when foreign currencies rise against the American dollar. It adds Surinam under the Netherlands possessions at a basic rate of 40.19 cents to the florin, effective January 1, 1941.

8799.s: This order changes the Volunteer Participation Committee in the Office of Civilian Defense. It raises the committee size from not more than twenty members to not more than forty-five members. It affects the committee within the Office for Emergency Management of the Executive Office of the President.

8798.s: This order transfers three Coast and Geodetic Survey vessels to the Navy Department, along with their equipment and supplies except surveying equipment. It also transfers three Navy vessels to the Department of Commerce, Coast and Geodetic Survey, except for ordnance equipment. After the present national emergency ends, the vessels are to be returned to their original departments.

8797.s: This order suspends the eight-hour limit for laborers and mechanics employed by the War Department on certain public works needed for national defense. It applies to construction of cantonments, air fields, fortifications, and other public works in the Canal Zone, Puerto Rico, and the Territory of Alaska. The suspension lasts for the duration of the emergencies proclaimed on September 8, 1939 and May 27, 1941.

8796.s: This order exempts George Cook, a plate printer in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending July 31, 1942.

8794.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Oregon from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. The lands are reserved for the War Department for military purposes. It covers both public and non-public lands in the areas described.

8795.s: This order changes a prior executive order creating Power Site Reserve No. 661 to allow Lane County, Oregon, to build a road over a specific parcel of land in the reserve. The road must be stopped without cost to the United States or its licensees if the Secretary of the Interior finds it conflicts with project works authorized by the United States.

8792.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Florida from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department for military purposes. It also replaces an earlier withdrawal order for any of the same lands that were affected.

8791.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the Department of the Navy to use in connection with a Marine Corps combat and training area. It also supersedes an earlier temporary withdrawal for the lands affected.

8790.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from all forms of appropriation under the public land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the Department of the Navy for a Marine Corps combat and training area. The order says the described areas, including both public and non-public lands, total 2,395.82 acres and supersede an earlier withdrawal for any affected lands.

8793.s: This order withdraws the listed lands in Oklahoma from all forms of appropriation under the public land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department for military purposes, subject to valid existing rights.

8789.s: This order revokes part of a 1940 order for the Alaska lands named here. It withdraws those public lands from appropriation under the public land laws, including the mining laws, and reserves them for the War Department for military purposes. The lands are in several areas on Kodiak Island and Unalaska Island, subject to valid existing rights.

8788.s: This order withdraws a piece of public land in Alaska from all forms of appropriation under the public land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves that land for the War Department to use for military purposes.

8786.s: This order withdraws public lands on Amaknak Island, Alaska, from the public-land laws, including the mining laws, and reserves them for the Navy Department for naval aviation purposes. It applies subject to valid existing rights and some prior land uses, including land set aside for native birds, Alaska native fishing rights, and lighthouse purposes. The reservation stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

8785.s: This order prohibits many transactions involving certain foreign countries and their nationals unless the Secretary of the Treasury authorizes them. It covers transfers of credit, foreign exchange, gold or silver, securities, and other dealings with property connected to those countries. It also requires people and businesses involved in these transactions to keep records and provide reports when required.

8787.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 3151, which had reserved a tract of land at the head of Passage Canal (Portage Bay), Alaska, for the Navy Department. It restores that land to its former status as withdrawn for town-site purposes under Executive Order No. 1919½.

8783.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use for stock-watering purposes. It applies to the listed land in Mount Diablo Meridian, subject to valid existing rights.

8782.s: This order sets aside three islands in Gatun Lake in the Canal Zone as a military reservation. The reservation is placed under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of War. The War Department must pay the costs of creating the reservation, including surveys and canceling any agricultural licenses or other permits in the area.

8784.s: This order revokes parts of earlier executive orders that created Public Water Reserves in California and New Mexico. It applies only to the specific lands listed in those states.

8781.s: This order requires executive civil service employees whose fingerprints are not already on file to be fingerprinted. It also requires fingerprinting before any original appointment or reinstatement to an executive civil service job. The fingerprints are to be sent to the Federal Bureau of Investigation for checking criminal records and for permanent filing.

8780.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the Department of State to use in connection with the Rio Grande Canalization project. The order keeps valid existing rights in place and allows livestock to cross the lands for watering, with one stated exception.

8779.s: This order excludes a five-acre tract in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. The land is described as a cemetery site on the west side of the southern peninsula of High Island. It restores that tract to entry under the applicable public-land laws.

8778.s: This order further exempts Percy Nicholls, a heat transmission engineer in the Bureau of Mines, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending June 30, 1942.

8776.s: This order withdraws a 40-acre tract of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets the land aside under the Department of the Interior for use as a radio relay station site for Federal and State cooperative forest-protection work. It also revokes an earlier withdrawal of that tract.

8777.s: This order allows Dr. Harold C. Bryant to be appointed Superintendent of Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona in the National Park Service, Department of the Interior. It says the appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

8774.s: This order changes an earlier order about coffee imports from countries that are not signatories of the Inter-American Coffee Agreement. It lets coffee from those countries be entered for consumption in the United States up to the unfilled balance of the total quota for the quota year ending September 30, 1941. The order keeps the maximum allocation for mocha type coffee in place.

8775.s: This order transfers a tract of land in the Virgin Islands from the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of the Navy. The land is to be used for the establishment, construction, and operation of aviation facilities at the Naval Air Station in St. Thomas, and it is subject to valid existing rights.

8773.s: This order directs the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate North American Aviation’s Inglewood plant. The plant is to be used to produce aircraft and other materials under its contracts with the United States, and the Secretary of War may make needed contract and compensation adjustments. It also directs the Secretary of War to hire needed employees and take steps to protect workers returning to the plant. The President will end federal possession and operation when he decides the plant can be privately operated in a way that meets national defense needs.

8772.s: This order exempts Clarence H. Branscombe, an assistant supervising engineer in the Public Buildings Administration, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on August 31, 1942.

8771.s: This order authorizes the United States Maritime Commission to purchase, requisition, charter, or take over foreign merchant vessels that are lying idle in waters within the jurisdiction of the United States, including the Philippine Islands and the Canal Zone. The Commission may use, operate, charter, lease, document, repair, equip, and man those vessels for national defense and other directed uses, but it may not transfer, charter, or lease a vessel to a belligerent government without the President's approval. The Commission must pay the owners just compensation for any vessel taken or for its use.

8770.s: This order sets aside about 6,884 acres in Musselshell County, Montana, for the Department of the Interior to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for people to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge. It also bars entry into the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8768.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules to list all positions in the Federal Bureau of Investigation under Schedule A. It affects FBI positions and changes how they are covered under the civil service rules.

8767.s: This order directs certain Coast Guard officers and enlisted men to operate as part of the Navy and follow the orders of the Secretary of the Navy. It applies to the number needed to man and operate certain naval vessels, as agreed upon by the Chief of Naval Operations and the Commandant of the Coast Guard. Those Coast Guard personnel, while serving on those naval vessels, are subject to the laws for the government of the Navy.

8769.s: This order transfers certain lands in Florida between the Department of Agriculture and the Department of the Interior. Some land is moved to Agriculture for use, administration, and disposition under the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act, and some land is moved to the Interior’s Fish and Wildlife Service as part of the Welaka Fish Hatchery. It also transfers land to widen the right-of-way for Quail Farm Road. The changes affect lands in the Town of Beecher and Putnam County, Florida.

8766.s: This order sets what documents aliens must show when entering the United States. It requires different papers for nonimmigrants and immigrants, with some special rules for transit, short visits, border crossings, and certain people from Canada, Newfoundland, Mexico, Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone, American Samoa, and Guam. It also lets the Secretary of State waive some passport or visa requirements in emergencies and gives the Secretary of State and the Attorney General power to make more rules.

8764.s: This order allows John H. Dillon to be appointed to a classified Navy Department job as Junior Administrative Officer, serving as Confidential Assistant to the Secretary of the Navy in Washington, D.C. It says the appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

8763.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands in several Wisconsin counties to the Department of the Interior. It reserves those lands, along with some intermingled public lands, as a refuge and breeding ground for native birds and other wildlife, and for research on wildlife and related forest resources. The lands may remain available to the State of Wisconsin for use and management under a cooperative and license agreement.

8762.s: This order exempts Frank L. Hess, a principal mineral technologist in the Bureau of Mines, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending September 30, 1942.

8760.s: The order directs the Civil Service Commission to refuse civil service examinations and certification to some people employed in the civilian executive branch of the federal government. It applies to anyone who is, or was within three months of the exam date, in that kind of job unless their department or office gives written assent. That assent must be based on a finding that the person can render better service for the government in the job sought.

8761.s: This order exempts Edward P. Davis, a topographic engineer in the Geological Survey, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, ending June 30, 1942.

8759.s: This order amends a prior order on allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Survey, and Public Health Service. It adds an exception for enlisted men assigned to duty in countries where emergency conditions justify such allowances during the present national emergency. The allowances are to be paid at the discretion and determination of the head of the department concerned.

8758.s: This order sets conversion factors for administering quotas on coffee imports under the Inter-American Coffee Agreement. It says one bag of 60 kilograms of coffee equals 132.276 pounds of coffee, and one pound of roasted coffee equals 1.2 pounds of raw green coffee.

8756.s: This order amends a previous order on the National Guard. It adds several listed units to the units being called into active military service of the United States. The order affects the members of those named units.

8755.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Alaska from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the area for use by the War Department as a demolition and practice bombing range. The areas described, including both public and non-public lands, total 18,600 acres, and the order is subject to valid existing rights and certain existing reservations and classifications for power purposes.

8757.s: This order creates the Office of Civilian Defense within the Office for Emergency Management. It gives the office a director and sets up a board and a volunteer committee to help coordinate civilian defense work, plan protection measures, and support civilian participation. It affects federal, state, local, territory, and District of Columbia governments, along with volunteer and other advisory groups involved in defense activities.

8753.s: This order changes the rules for license tags on motor vehicles in the Canal Zone. It requires each licensed vehicle to carry a metal tag at the rear with the license number in large numerals, and the tag must stay legible. When vehicle lights are required, the tag must be illuminated so it can be seen from at least 60 feet, except on vehicles operated officially by the armed forces of the United States.

8754.s: This order exempts Frederick A. Sterling, the Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary to Sweden, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption may last for as long as needed, but not more than five years from August 31, 1941.

8751.s: This order creates the Division of Defense Aid Reports within the Office for Emergency Management of the Executive Office of the President. It puts an Executive Officer in charge, appointed by the President. The division is to clear transactions and reports, coordinate requests for aid under the Act, keep records, and prepare reports for the President. It may hire needed staff and get supplies and services within the funds the President allocates.

8752.s: This order amends Executive Order 8712 by revoking paragraph 11. It changes the rules governing the exportation of articles and materials named in proclamations issued under section 6 of the July 2, 1940 law.

8750.s: This order exempts Alphonso L. Graham, an assistant storekeeper at the United States Maritime Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending June 30, 1942.

8748.s: The order approves Civil Service Commission rules that set up efficiency-rating boards of review in departments and independent establishments with employees covered by the Classification Act of 1923. The boards consider appeals of efficiency ratings, with written appeals generally due within 90 days, though the deadline can be waived for good reasons. Hearings are to be informal, and employees may appear with a representative. The boards can adjust a rating or leave it unchanged, and their decisions are sent in writing to the department head and the employee.

8749.s:
The order sets apart certain waters in and around Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, as a naval defensive sea area for national defense. It also sets apart the airspace over those waters and over the Guantanamo Naval Reservation as a naval airspace reservation.

Only public vessels of the United States and vessels engaged in Cuban trade may enter the sea area unless the Secretary of the Navy authorizes it. Only public aircraft of the United States may enter the airspace reservation unless the Secretary of the Navy authorizes it.

8747.s: This order exempts Louis A. Simon from compulsory retirement for age for six more months. It affects Simon, who was the Supervising Architect of the Public Buildings Administration in the Federal Works Agency.

8746.s: This order amends a prior executive order to extend its rules to property in which Greece or any Greek national has had any direct or indirect interest. It also changes the date used in the definitions of “Greece” and “national” of Greece to April 28, 1941.

8745.s: This order exempts Charley R. Davis, a special agent in the Federal Bureau of Investigation, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and extends his service until August 31, 1942.

8744.s: This order lets some government employees gain classified civil service status for transfer to another classified civil service job. It applies to people whose positions were covered into the classified civil service and who were involuntarily separated because of a reduction in force, an abolished position, or the liquidation of their agency. They must meet listed service, recommendation, examination, and transfer timing requirements.

8742.s: This order revokes part of the 1910 coal land withdrawal in Montana. It restores the listed lands in several townships and ranges to the area covered by the revocation, with a few exceptions named in the order. It affects the specific lands described under the Montana Meridian.

8743.s: This order puts most executive civil service offices and positions into the classified civil service, with some exceptions for temporary and already excepted positions. It also creates a Board of Legal Examiners to set rules for recruiting, examining, appointing, promoting, and transferring attorneys in the classified service. The order says some attorney positions may be filled by noncompetitive examination, and it sets rules for recalled employees and for people who left for military or naval service.

8741.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5623 of May 15, 1931, which had withdrawn public lands in California while a resurvey was pending. It takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey of those lands is filed.

8739.s: This order revokes a 1934 order that had reserved a tract of land in Alaska for joint use by the Department of Agriculture and the Alaska Game Commission. It withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for the Alaska Game Commission to use as a headquarters site for administering Alaska game laws.

8740.s: This order puts the positions of Counsel and Assistant Attorney in the Alley Dwelling Authority into the competitive classified civil service. It also adds the Executive Officer of the Alley Dwelling Authority to Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules.

8738.s: This order limits how much coffee from countries that are not signatories to the Inter-American Coffee Agreement may be entered for consumption in the United States. It sets quotas for Mocha and other Arabica coffee, and it sets a limit for other coffee types based on amounts already entered. The order affects coffee imports from those countries.

8737.s: This order sets aside land in the Canal Zone as a military reservation called Fort Gulick Military Reservation. It puts the reservation under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of War, and it includes a 100-foot corridor connecting the reservation to the Bolivar Highway. The order also says the military must pay the costs of the transfer, limits sewage discharge into Gatun Lake’s drainage basin, and keeps certain Panama Canal uses and public access through the corridor.

8736.s: This order revokes part of a 1929 withdrawal of public land in Alaska for naval purposes. It applies to a described tract of land that is part of the Cold Bay-Dolgoi Island Naval Reservation and covers not more than 18 acres. The Secretary of the Navy must provide access to and from the tract under rules he sets.

8735.s: This order allows five named attorneys in the Office of the Administrator of the Federal Security Agency to get a competitive classified status without following the Civil Service Rules. It affects those five employees and is based on a recommendation from the Federal Security Administrator, with the Civil Service Commission agreeing.

8734.s: This order creates an Office of Price Administration and Civilian Supply in the Executive Office of the President. It puts an Administrator in charge and gives that office duties related to prices, rents, supplies, and the use of materials and commodities for civilian use. The office is also directed to study prices and civilian needs, make findings, and work with other government agencies.

8733.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Oklahoma from settlement, sale, entry, or other disposal. It reserves the land for use with the Canton Dam and Reservoir project on the North Canadian River under the War Department. One parcel may also be used by the Secretary of the Interior for Indian school, agency, and other Indian administrative purposes if that does not interfere with the project.

8732.s: This order temporarily withdraws a described parcel of public land in Arkansas from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for use with construction of the Nimrod Dam and Reservoir on the Fourche La Fave River, under War Department supervision. It applies to the listed land, subject to valid existing rights, and replaces an earlier withdrawal for that land.

8731.s: This order amends a prior order to allow alternate members to be appointed to the National Defense Mediation Board. An alternate may serve when the regular member they stand in for is unavailable and may do the duties of a Board member on a division assigned by the Chairman. Alternate members receive compensation and expenses while serving, the same as regular members.

8730.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to add certain classified positions in the Custodial Service and in the Division of Equipment and Supplies under the Fourth Assistant Postmaster General. It lets unskilled personnel from the unclassified laborer register move up to those classified positions through non-competitive examination, subject to Civil Service Commission approval. It does not give those employees classified status or make them eligible to transfer to classified positions in other parts of the federal service.

8729.s: This executive order corrects wording in three earlier executive orders about naval defensive sea areas and naval airspace reservations. It changes the phrase about territorial waters to say they are between the extreme high-water marks and the three-mile marine boundaries.

8727.s: This order changes the Army’s manual for courts-martial rules on punishments. It says that when a sentence does not include dishonorable discharge, pay forfeitures and other deductions cannot take more than two-thirds of the accused person’s pay in any month. It also says “base pay” means only the minimum base pay set by statute and does not include specialists’ pay or extra pay for special qualifications or decorations.

8726.s: This order exempts Harry U. Wagner, an assistant collector of customs in Denver, Colorado, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending March 31, 1942.

8728.s: This order exempts Ernest C. Steward, a resident job superintendent for The Alley Dwelling Authority for the District of Columbia, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends June 30, 1942.

8724.s: This order restores the Homestead Field Military Reservation land on Molokai to the use of the Territory of Hawaii. It says the War Department may remove its improvements and installations there if that has not already been done.

8725.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Florida from all forms of appropriation under the public land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use in connection with aerial gunnery ranges, subject to valid existing rights. The withdrawal takes precedence over earlier executive orders covering some of the same lands, but it does not revoke them.

8723.s: This order revokes part of an earlier 1917 power site reserve in Oregon. It removes the reserve from the listed lands in the Willamette Meridian. The change affects the specific tracts named in the order.

8722.s: This order modifies a 1917 executive order to allow Lane County, Oregon, to build a road over certain land in Oregon. The road may be used only until the Secretary of the Interior finds it conflicts with project works authorized by the United States. If that happens, the road use must stop without liability or expense to the United States or its licensees.

8721.s: This order amends a previous executive order to extend its rules to property in which Yugoslavia or any Yugoslav national has had any interest, direct or indirect, on or since March 24, 1941. It also changes the date used in the definitions of “Yugoslavia” and “National” of Yugoslavia to March 24, 1941. The order affects property tied to Yugoslavia and its nationals.

8720.s: This order allows Watson B. Miller to be appointed as Assistant Administrator of the Federal Security Agency without following the Civil Service Act’s competitive rules. He must still show the Civil Service Commission that he has the required qualifications for the job.

8719.s: This order suspends compliance with certain statutory provisions about some kinds of employment in the Canal Zone. The suspension lasts during the national emergency proclaimed in 1939.

8718.s: This order sets apart part of Subic Bay in the Philippine Islands as a naval defensive sea area for national defense. It also sets apart the airspace over that water and over the Subic Bay Naval Reservation as a naval airspace reservation. Vessels other than public vessels of the United States may not enter the sea area, and aircraft other than public aircraft of the United States may not enter the airspace, unless the Secretary of the Navy authorizes it.

8717.s: This order sets apart the waters around the eastern portion of Kodiak Island, Alaska, as a naval defensive sea area for national defense. It bars any vessel or other craft, except public vessels of the United States, from entering unless the Secretary of the Navy authorizes it. The Secretary of the Navy is to enforce the order and may make regulations to carry it out.

8715.s: This order changes the rules for radio communication in and around the Panama Canal. It gives the Governor of the Panama Canal control over radio use for most vessels in Canal Zone waters, and it requires vessels approaching the Canal to send certain information by radio through a designated shore station. It also limits vessel radio use, including rules on broadcasting, power, testing, tuning, and keeping a radio operator on watch during transit.

8714.s: This order sets who will carry out the duties of the Secretary of the Treasury if the Secretary is absent or sick. It says the Fiscal Assistant Secretary, a senior Assistant Secretary on duty, or the General Counsel for the Treasury Department will act in that role, depending on which offices are also unavailable, and it revokes a 1933 executive order.

8716.s: This order creates the National Defense Mediation Board in the Office for Emergency Management. The board is made up of members appointed by the President, with public, employee, and employer representatives. It can help settle labor disputes between employers and employees in production or transportation of materials needed for national defense, including by negotiation, voluntary arbitration, hearings, and recommendations. Employers and employees in those industries are told to try to settle disputes without interrupting production or transportation.

8712.s: This order sets rules for exporting certain articles and materials named in proclamations under the 1940 defense law. It requires export licenses for those items unless a general license applies, and gives the Secretary of State and the Administrator of Export Control roles in handling the licenses and lists of covered goods. It also says export licenses are not transferable, may be revoked, and must be returned if revoked or expired.

8711.s: This order amends Executive Order 8389 to extend its provisions to property in which Hungary or any Hungarian national has had any interest, direct or indirect, since March 13, 1941. It changes the date used in the definitions of "Hungary" and "national" of Hungary to March 13, 1941.

8713.s: This order sets rules for exporting certain articles and materials named in a March 4, 1941 proclamation. It puts the Administrator of Export Control in charge of listing the covered forms, publishing those lists, and issuing export licenses unless the export would be harmful to national defense. The order also says licenses are not transferable, can be revoked without notice, and must be returned if revoked or expired.

8710.s: This order keeps Ales Hrdlicka, Curator of Physical Anthropology in the United States National Museum, from being required to retire for age for one more year. It applies only to him and extends his earlier age-retirement exemption until March 31, 1942.

8709.s: The order changes the name of the Wyoming National Forest to Bridger National Forest. It affects the forest in Wyoming and says the new name honors Jim Bridger, who was associated with the early exploration and development of the region.

8708.s: This order reserves certain public lands in Independence County, Arkansas, for use by the State of Arkansas Game and Fish Commission in connection with the Independence County Wildlife Refuge. The lands are placed under the jurisdiction of the Department of the Interior, subject to conditions set by the Secretary of the Interior. It also supersedes a prior temporary withdrawal for some of the same lands.

8706.s: This order changes the rules for suspending Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, and National Guard personnel from flying. It says a commanding officer shall suspend anyone under his command who he thinks is unfit for flying, and it sets out when that suspension can be ordered, reported, confirmed, or revoked. It also says that if the suspension was for sickness or injury incurred in line of duty and later removed, the suspension is treated as if it never started, and the person may be entitled to increased pay for flying if the listed requirements are met.

8705.s: This order amends Civil Service Rules on election conduct, reductions in force, and pay for employees who are appointed or serving in violation of the law or rules. It says people in the executive civil service may not use official power to interfere with elections, and competitive classified employees may not take part in political management or campaigns. It also gives military preference in reductions in force and says the government shall not pay the salary or wages of certain employees after the Civil Service Commission sends instructions and those instructions are not carried out.

8707.s: This order changes civil service rules for reinstatement and transfer. It lets a person who was separated without prejudice, after at least six months of satisfactory service in a position with a probationary period longer than six months, be reinstated if qualified or able to qualify through a non-competitive examination. It also allows a probationer with at least six months of satisfactory service in such a position to be transferred to another part of the service, with the new position requiring completion of probation if it also has a probationary period longer than six months.

8703.s: This order adds additional rules for exporting certain articles and materials named in the March 4, 1941 proclamation. It covers jute, lead, borax, and phosphates, including the listed forms of those materials. It also applies earlier export rules to those items and amends a prior executive order to include them.

8704.s: This order sets rules for allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Survey, and Public Health Service when they are not given quarters or rations in kind. It gives payment rules for duty stations, travel status, and temporary detentions during travel. It also replaces earlier executive orders on this subject, with a later effective date for quarters allowance within the continental United States.

8702.s: This order adds a list of articles and materials, including cadmium, carbon black, coconut oil, copra, cresylic acid and cresols, fatty acids from vegetable oils under export control, glycerin, palm-kernel oil and palm kernels, pine oil, petroleum coke, shellac, and titanium, to export regulations. It says the existing regulations from July 2, 1940 apply to the export of these items. It also amends a previous executive order to include these articles and materials.

8701.s: This order amends a prior executive order to extend its provisions to property in which Bulgaria or any Bulgarian national has had any interest, direct or indirect, on or since March 4, 1941. It changes the date used in the definitions of "Bulgaria" and "national" of Bulgaria to March 4, 1941.

8700.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6667, which had withdrawn public lands in Colorado pending a resurvey. It takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey of the lands involved is filed.

8699.s: This order covers certain Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation positions into the competitive classified civil service. It does not apply to positions excepted from competitive requirements under Schedule A. Employees in covered positions, and some people employed by the corporation on February 1, 1939 who stayed employed continuously, may acquire classified civil service status.

8698.s: This order exempts Harry L. Mickey, a messenger in The White House Office, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending April 30, 1942.

8696.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands and improvements in Valencia and Bernalillo Counties, New Mexico, from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior. The lands were acquired by the United States in connection with the Cuba-Rio Puerco Project. The Secretary of the Interior is authorized to administer the lands through the Commissioner of Indian Affairs for the exclusive use of the Pueblo Indians, under conditions set for the land-conservation and land-utilization program.

8697.s: This order transfers certain lands and improvements in Sandoval County, New Mexico, from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of Agriculture. The land is to be used, managed, and disposed of under the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act. Grazing facilities on the land must be made available to Pueblo Indians for up to 400 cattle units yearlong.

8694.s: This order adds extra export rules for certain articles and materials named in the President’s February 25, 1941 proclamation. It covers beryllium, graphite electrodes, and aircraft pilot trainers. It also makes earlier export regulations apply to those items and amends Executive Order 8640 to include them.

8693.s: This order adds export rules for certain articles and materials named in the President’s February 25, 1941 proclamation. It includes belladonna products, atropine products, sole leather bends, backs, and sides, and belting leather. It says the listed items are subject to existing export regulations and updates Executive Order 8640 to include them.

8695.s: This order extends the limits of the customs port of entry of Jonesport, Maine, in Customs Collection District No. 1. It adds the towns of Beals, Jonesboro, Roque Bluffs, and Machiasport in Maine. The order becomes effective on the thirtieth day after it is signed.

8692.s: This order exempts Edgar M. Cohee, a chief office clerk in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending April 30, 1942.

8691.s: This order affects a 40-acre tract of public land in Oregon. It withdraws the land from settlement, location, sale, or entry, and reserves it for use by the Forest Service as a fire-lookout station for the Siskiyou National Forest. It also revokes an earlier withdrawal for that tract.

8690.s: This order further exempts John M. Terwilliger, a chief clerk in the Office of the Collector of Internal Revenue in Detroit, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on February 28, 1942.

8689.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by adding rules for civil vessels and aircraft. It sets out what consular officers must or may do for entry and clearance, wrecked or lost vessels, surveys, bottomry bonds, and transfers of vessels abroad. It also cancels certain chapters and sections of the Foreign Service Regulations.

8687.s: This order adds a new exception to Civil Service Rules for certain Food and Drug Administration specialists. It allows professional, technical, or scientific specialists to work intermittently for short periods, up to a total of 60 days in one year, as Standards Committee members or as consultants on food standards and enforcement of the Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act.

8688.s: This order sets rules for allowances for quarters for enlisted men of the first, second, and third grades of the Army of the United States who are on active duty and have dependents. It applies when public quarters are not provided and available for their dependents. Philippine Scouts covered by the order may receive actual lodging expenses, up to fifty cents a day.

8686.s: This order transfers named officers and employees from the United States Maritime Commission to the Interstate Commerce Commission. It says they were employed in administering laws that were repealed, and that their retention by the Maritime Commission is not necessary for other duties.

8684.s: This order sets aside the waters around Culebra Island, Puerto Rico, as a naval defensive sea area for national defense. It also sets aside the airspace over those waters and the island as a naval airspace reservation for national defense. Only public vessels and public aircraft of the United States may enter, unless the Secretary of the Navy authorizes it. People who violate the order may face penalties under the Criminal Code or the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938.

8685.s: The order reserves and sets apart federal land in Arizona and California for the Department of the Interior to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It says lands later acquired in those areas will also become part of the refuge, but the reservation is subject to use for the Colorado River Storage Project. It also makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter there, except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8682.s: This order sets up naval defensive sea areas and naval airspace reservations around Palmyra, Johnston, Midway, Wake, and Kingman Reef. It bars most people, vessels, and aircraft from entering those areas unless the Secretary of the Navy allows it. The Secretary of the Navy is responsible for enforcing the order and may make rules to carry it out.

8683.s: This order sets up naval defensive sea areas and naval airspace reservations around the islands of Rose, Tutuila, and Guam in the Pacific Ocean for national defense. It bars most people, vessels, and aircraft from entering these areas unless the Secretary of the Navy authorizes it. The Secretary of the Navy is to enforce the order, work with local law enforcement officers of the United States, and may prescribe needed regulations.

8681.s: The order creates a naval defensive sea area in part of Kaneohe Bay and a naval airspace reservation over that water for national defense. It bars most people, vessels, and aircraft from entering those areas unless the Secretary of the Navy authorizes it. The Secretary of the Navy is to enforce the order and may make rules to carry it out. Violations are subject to penalties under the Criminal Code and the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938.

8679.s: This order allows the first appointments to two assistant director positions in the Naval Civilian Police Corps of the Navy Department to be made without following the Civil Service Act’s competitive rules. The appointments still must meet the required qualifications before the Civil Service Commission.

8678.s: This order places certain lands in Puerto Rico under the control of the Navy Department, the War Department, and the United States Public Health Service. It assigns land for use with the United States Naval Air Station in San Juan, as a United States Engineer Depot for national-defense purposes, and as a quarantine station or site for a Marine hospital, or both. It also says this order replaces two earlier executive orders about Miraflores Island and other lands in Puerto Rico.

8680.s: This order sets up naval defensive sea areas around Kiska and Unalaska and naval airspace reservations over those islands and waters for national defense. It bars people, vessels, and aircraft from entering those areas unless authorized by the Secretary of the Navy, with exceptions for public vessels and public aircraft of the United States. The Secretary of the Navy is to enforce the order and may make regulations to carry it out.

8677.s: This order directs the land and naval forces of the United States to help control vessels in the territorial waters of the United States and the Canal Zone when the Secretary of the Treasury or the Governor of the Panama Canal asks for assistance. It also says a request from the Governor of the Panama Canal must be approved by the designated commanding officer while a related executive order is in force.

8676.s: This order exempts Alexander W. Weddell, the Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to Spain, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption can last for as long as needed, but not more than five years from April 30, 1941.

8675.s: This order authorizes the Director of Selective Service to set up or designate civilian work of national importance for people who are found to be conscientiously opposed to combatant and non-combatant military service. The Director must assign people to that work and decide which agencies, organizations, or individuals may provide civilian direction. The Director may also use federal, state, territorial, and private services and supplies, and may issue rules to carry out the order.

8674.s: This order changes the rules for allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men in certain services. It says enlisted men of the Navy and Marine Corps serving in the office of the Naval Attache and Naval Attache for Air at the American Embassy in Havana, Cuba, and who are not given quarters or rations in kind, will receive a per diem allowance instead. The allowance is $3.00 in place of subsistence and $1.00 in place of quarters.

8673.s: This order designates the Massanutten Unit of the George Washington National Forest in Virginia as the Robert Fechner Memorial Forest. It honors Robert Fechner, the first Director of the Civilian Conservation Corps. The lands inside the memorial forest, including later land added within its boundaries, keep national-forest status, and the Forest Service must manage them to reflect the memorial designation.

8672.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by adding a new chapter on navigation. It lets the Secretary of State issue general instructions for Foreign Service officers about civil vessels and aircraft, seamen, and documents carried by vessels, aircraft, and seamen. It also cancels several listed sections of the Foreign Service Regulations.

8671.s: This order directs the Treasury Department’s Procurement Division to use tungsten ore it had bought under a 1939 law. The ore may be sold or otherwise used for defense production purposes. The amount and the buyers or users are to be requested from time to time by the Office of Production Management.

8670.s: This order exempts Clarence E. Ingling, Chief of Files in The White House Office, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him and extends through April 30, 1942.

8668.s: This order adds new export rules for certain articles and materials named in the February 4, 1941 proclamation. It covers petroleum and gas well equipment and parts, petroleum refining machinery, radium, uranium, and calf and kip skins. It says the export rules from July 2, 1940 apply to these items, and it amends Executive Order 8640 to include them.

8667.s: This order sets aside certain U.S.-owned land in McHenry County, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge. It also limits entry to the refuge under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8669.s: This order sets new regulations for exporting iron and steel, including certain forms, conversions, and derivatives covered by earlier export rules. It also changes some prior regulations for ferro-alloys and says these rules apply to the exportation of iron and steel, replacing Executive Order 8607.

8665.s: This order sets aside about 440 acres of U.S.-owned land in Barnes County, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there, or to enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8664.s: This order sets aside lands in Emmons County, North Dakota, as the Sunburst Lake National Wildlife Refuge. It reserves the area for the Department of the Interior to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8666.s: The order sets aside federal land in Slope County, North Dakota, for the Department of the Interior to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there, or to enter except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8663.s: The order sets aside federal land in Barnes County, North Dakota, as the Stoney Slough National Wildlife Refuge for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also bars people from hunting, trapping, capturing, disturbing, or killing birds or wild animals in the refuge, and from entering it except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8662.s: This order sets aside federal land in Slope County, North Dakota, as the Stewart Lake National Wildlife Refuge. It gives the Department of the Interior use of the land as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8661.s: This order sets aside about 640 acres in Emmons County, North Dakota, for the Department of the Interior to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful to pursue, hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal in the refuge. It also bars people from entering the refuge unless allowed under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8660.s: The order sets aside federal land in Towner County, North Dakota, as the Snyder Lake National Wildlife Refuge for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there, or to enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8658.s: The order sets aside federal land in Nelson County, North Dakota, as the Prairie Lake National Wildlife Refuge. It is to be used by the Department of the Interior as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The order also makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8659.s: The order sets aside about 800 acres of U.S.-owned land in Grant County, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful to pursue, hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal there. People also may not enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8657.s: This order extends the Classification Act of 1923, as amended, to certain Navy Department jobs in the Professional and Scientific Service, the Subprofessional Service, and the Clerical, Administrative and Fiscal Service. It applies to these positions in British Guiana, Trinidad, Antigua, St. Lucia, Jamaica, Bermuda, The Bahamas, and Newfoundland, and it sets up a salary differential for them.

8655.s: This order revokes part of a prior order for a tract of public land on Woody Island in Alaska. It then withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for the Department of Commerce as an addition to an air-navigation site. The reservation stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

8654.s: This order revokes Molson, Washington’s designation as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 30. It takes effect at the close of business on January 31, 1941.

8656.s: This order exempts Ovilup H. George, a chief pipefitter and fire chief at the Government Printing Office, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, ending February 28, 1942.

8652.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Utah from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws, subject to valid existing rights. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use for aerial bombing and gunnery range purposes. The lands are in the listed areas and total about 262,200 acres.

8651.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Oregon from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use as an aerial bombing and gunnery range. The order also says it takes precedence over some earlier withdrawals, and some lands will return if the Secretary of the Interior gives notice that they are needed for reclamation purposes.

8650.s: This order changes the name of the Kellys Slough Migratory Waterfowl Refuge in Grand Forks County, North Dakota, to Kellys Slough National Wildlife Refuge. It also adds certain United States lands in that county to the refuge, subject to valid existing rights. The refuge is enlarged to include all lands owned or controlled by the United States in the described area.

8648.s: This order changes the name of the Killcohook Migratory Bird Refuge to the Killcohook National Wildlife Refuge. It also adds about 5 acres of land and water in Salem County, New Jersey, to the refuge, subject to valid existing rights. The added lands are under the primary jurisdiction of the Director of Procurement and may be disposed of under the cited law.

8647.s: This order sets aside certain U.S.-owned lands in Arizona and California as the Havasu Lake National Wildlife Refuge for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also says lands later acquired in the area will become part of the refuge. The order makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there, or to enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior. The refuge is subject to use for the Parker Dam Project.

8646.s: This order withdraws about 57,215 acres of public land in Dona Ana County, New Mexico, and sets it aside for the Department of the Interior to conserve and develop natural wildlife resources. It also makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior. Land within the Jornada Experimental Range stays subject to the Department of Agriculture for range research, and land in New Mexico Grazing District No. 4 stays subject to that grazing law and its rules.

8645.s: The order sets aside federal land in Cheyenne County, Colorado, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge. People may enter only under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior, and the reservation is called the Kit Carson National Wildlife Refuge.

8644.s: This order sets aside about 360 acres of federal land in Uinta County, Wyoming, as the Evanston National Wildlife Refuge. It is for the Department of the Interior to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The order makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there, or to enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8649.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from all forms of use under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the Department of State for the Rio Grande Canalization project. The order also says valid existing rights still apply, and livestock may cross the lands for watering purposes.

8642.s: This order changes a prior order about certain public lands in Alaska. It allows entry of the tract of land commonly known as the old town of Kodiak, Alaska, under the cited law. It affects that specific tract of land reserved for town-site purposes.

8641.s: This order adds a new parole rule for people convicted of breaking the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940 or its regulations. It lets the Attorney General parole some of those people for military service, non-combatant service, work of national importance under civilian direction, or other special service under the Act. The Attorney General may set terms, supervise parolees, and revoke parole if they do not follow the rules.

8640.s: This order sets additional rules for exporting certain articles and materials named in earlier presidential proclamations. It allows the Secretary of State to issue general licenses for those exports, except where the Neutrality Act of 1939 forbids it. It also says some earlier export rules will not apply to the general licenses covered here.

8639.s: This order revokes the designation of Unalaska, Alaska, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 31. It takes effect at the close of business on January 15, 1941.

8638.s: This order lets certain employees of the Rural Electrification Administration apply for competitive classified civil-service status. It applies to people who were employed there on October 16, 1936, were not then eligible because they did not have enough service, and have worked there continuously until the date of the order. They must be recommended by the Secretary of Agriculture, pass Civil Service Commission tests, and meet citizenship and other civil-service requirements.

8637.s: This order exempts Joshua G. Hefty, a topographic engineer with the International Boundary Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending January 31, 1942.

8636.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. The lands are reserved for the War Department for military purposes as an aviation base, subject to valid existing rights. It affects the public lands in the listed areas.

8643.s: This order changes a prior order about land in the Virgin Islands. It transfers a tract of land near Bourne Field and the Botanical Garden in St. Thomas from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of the Navy for aviation facilities at the Naval Air Station. The entrance road from the main road to the Botanical Garden must stay open to the public when the garden is open, and employees of the garden must have free access over that road at all times.

8634.s: This order lets certain Federal Works Agency employees who were detailed from the Public Works Administration to the Office of Buildings Manager seek a competitive classified civil service status or an unclassified status under the Labor Regulations. To qualify, they must have served satisfactorily, pass any non-competitive fitness tests set by the Civil Service Commission, and not be disqualified under civil service rules, the Civil Service Act, or other orders or statutes.

8635.s: This order revokes part of the 1910 coal land withdrawal in Montana. It applies to the listed lands in the Montana Meridian, with a few small exceptions named in the order. It affects the federal coal land withdrawal for those areas.

8633.s: This order puts certain National Guard units and members into active military service of the United States. They are to serve for twelve consecutive months unless sooner relieved, starting on dates later announced by the Secretary of War. While they are in federal service, they are relieved from duty in their state National Guard units. It also directs that certain officers and warrant officers be ordered to active duty and given appointments or commissions as described in the order.

8631.s: This order sets new rules for exporting copper, brass and bronze, zinc, nickel, and potash. It also says these materials include certain ores, metals, scrap, alloys, compounds, and some manufactured forms listed in the order. The earlier export rule from July 2, 1940, is changed to match these classifications, and other listed regulations also apply to these exports.

8632.s: This order creates a Division of Defense Housing Coordination in the Office for Emergency Management and a Coordinator of Defense Housing appointed by the President. The Coordinator is to help coordinate defense housing work among federal housing agencies and other public and private groups. The order covers housing programs tied to national defense activities and directs the Coordinator to track needs, help avoid shortages and duplication, and report to the President.

8629.s: This order creates the Office of Production Management in the Executive Office of the President. It gives the office duties to increase, coordinate, and regulate production and supply for national defense, including raw materials, production facilities, purchases, and priorities.
