It covers items marked "secret," "confidential," or "restricted" in certain military, naval, and related places and activities. Under the law it cites, making photos, sketches, maps, or similar images of those items without permission is unlawful.

8380.s: This order changes the name of the Cold Springs Reservation in Umatilla County, Oregon, to Cold Springs National Wildlife Refuge. It adds about 80 acres of land to the refuge and states that the enlarged refuge includes lands owned or controlled by the United States in the described area. The order also says most of the reserved lands were withdrawn for reclamation purposes and may still be used for reclamation and related purposes.

8379.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by setting rules for record books, archives, and codes in Foreign Service establishments. It requires different offices to keep specific record books, and it says the Secretary of State may issue instructions on how they are kept and may define what counts as an official document. It also cancels certain earlier regulations and revokes three prior executive orders.

8378.s: This order reserves the airspace over a part of the District of Columbia for national defense, other government purposes, and public safety. No one may fly a civil aircraft in that airspace without special permission from the Civil Aeronautics Authority. Anyone who violates the order is subject to the penalties in the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938.

8376.s: This order places certain lands in New Mexico under the control of the Secretary of the Interior because they have become useless for military purposes. It says the lands may be disposed of as provided by law. It also revokes two earlier executive orders that had reserved the lands for military use.

8377.s: This order changes Executive Order No. 8356 by replacing the word "Federal" with "Foreign" in section 5. It affects the rules of precedence for Foreign Service officers and other officers of the United States Government.

8374.s: This order exempts Charles F. Markey, an assistant foreman at the Government Printing Office, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him because he was set to reach the retirement age in May 1940. The exemption ends on May 31, 1941.

8375.s: This order exempts James F. Rogers, Chief Educationist in the Office of Education, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends May 31, 1941.

8372.s: This order changes a prior order that had withdrawn certain lands in Alaska. It allows the Secretary of the Interior to issue a coal prospecting permit to the Alaska Matanuska Coal Company for the listed lands.

8373.s: This order designates and authorizes the Honorable Angel R. de Jesus, an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico, to act as Judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico. He may perform the judge’s duties and sign needed papers and records when the judge is absent, ill, or otherwise legally unable to serve during the current calendar year.

8370.s: This order allows Edith M. Watkins to be appointed to a classified position in the Department of Justice without following the Civil Service Rules. It says this is so she can be assigned to an administrative position that requires civil service status.

8369.s: This order further exempts Louis A. Simon, the supervising architect of the Public Buildings Administration, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It affects only him and extends a previous exemption.

8368.s: This order exempts Ales Hrdlicka from compulsory retirement for age for one more year, ending March 31, 1941. It applies to his job as Curator of Physical Anthropology in the United States National Museum, Smithsonian Institution.

8371.s: This order changes a prior executive order to add Attorney General Robert H. Jackson to a committee on civil service personnel. The committee is directed to study how to recruit, test, select, promote, transfer, remove, and reinstate personnel for the positions covered by the order, and to report recommendations to the President.

8366.s: This order designates Marriner S. Eccles as Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. It says he will serve in that role for four years, starting February 1, 1940.

8367.s: This order extends the limits of the customs port of entry of Savannah, Georgia, to include an additional area. It affects the customs port of Savannah, which is the headquarters port of Customs Collection District Number 17. The order says it becomes effective thirty days after it was signed.

8365.s: This order allows Mrs. Rose S. Rutledge to be appointed to a clerical position in the Department of Agriculture without meeting the Civil Service Rules requirements. It says she is the widow of a former junior clerk in the Department of Agriculture who died, leaving his widow and one child without adequate means of support.

8363.s: This order changes a prior executive order about Civil Service Rule II. It says the second proviso will also apply to people in positions that were covered into the classified, competitive civil service by an earlier order, and it changes section 3 of that order to match.

8364.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5346 of May 9, 1930, which had withdrawn public lands in Minnesota while a resurvey was pending. It becomes effective when the official plat of the resurvey of the lands involved is filed.

8362.s: This order allows Archie L. Hardy to be appointed to a clerical job in the Social Security Board without following the usual Civil Service Rules. It is meant to let him return to the Social Security Board under a civil-service status he would have had if he had not resigned to take temporary work in the Department of Labor.

8361.s: This order amends a prior order about public lands in South Dakota that had been withdrawn for a grazing project. It changes the authority named for the project and limits the withdrawal to the lands listed in the order. The rest of the lands that were part of the earlier withdrawal are excluded.

8360.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules to allow certain classified jobs in the Custodian Service and at the Coast Guard Depot in Curtis Bay, Maryland, to be filled by promoting unclassified laborers under the Labor Regulations, with Commission approval. It says those laborers may move up through noncompetitive examination to classified positions. It also says this does not give them classified status or make them eligible to transfer to classified positions in other parts of the federal service.

8358.s: This order revokes a 1925 executive order that had temporarily withdrawn public lands in Arizona for classification. The earlier order was in place while the Smithsonian Institution examined certain Indian ruins on those lands.

8357.s: This order sets rules for officers chosen by the Secretaries of Commerce and Agriculture to serve abroad or in the Department of State. It says the Secretary of State may give them commissions, assign them to offices, and place them under the Secretary of State’s jurisdiction while they are on assignment. It also says their duties are limited to their special missions or, for liaison officers, to matters of interest to their own departments.

8359.s: This order revokes part of a 1921 order that had withdrawn land in Alaska for lighthouse purposes. It applies only to the parcel called Parcel 26, now designated as U.S. Survey No. 1626, on Mitkof Island in Wrangell Strait.

8355.s: This order transfers certain national-forest lands in Idaho from the Idaho National Forest to the Salmon National Forest. It says the transfer does not give national-forest status to any publicly owned lands that did not already have that status, and it does not remove any publicly owned lands from national-forest status.

8354.s: This order sets apart a tract of land in the Canal Zone as a military reservation called Fort Kobbé Military Reservation. It puts the area under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of War, subject to the order’s conditions and limits. The area stays under civil jurisdiction of the Canal Zone Government except when it is placed under Army authority, and Panama Canal personnel and Panama Railroad Company employees must be allowed access for certain purposes.

8353.s: This order restores a parcel of land near Kuhio Wharf at the port of Hilo, Hawaii, to the possession, use, and control of the Government of the Territory of Hawaii. The land had previously been set aside as a site for a Custom House at Hilo. It applies to the specific parcel described in the order.

8352.s: This order changes the Foreign Service Regulations on attachés and consular officers. It says attachés are assigned and commissioned through their departments and the Secretary of State, and that they work under the general supervision of the chief of mission. It also gives consular officers duties related to Social Security Board activities abroad and requires them to send reports and information through the Department of State.

8350.s: This order exempts Alexander E. Twomey, a quarterman blacksmith at the Navy Yard in Boston, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, ending February 28, 1941.

8351.s: This order extends Sims Ely’s exemption from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. It affects Sims Ely, who was serving as City Manager of Boulder City, Nevada.

8349.s: This order exempts Thomas E. McElree, a principal administrative assistant in the Engineer Department at Large, War Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on February 28, 1941.

8347.s: This order transfers the use, possession, and control of certain public lands in Alabama to the Tennessee Valley Authority for the purposes named in the Tennessee Valley Authority Act of 1933. It applies to two described parcels in the Huntsville Meridian. It also revokes a previous order for those lands.

8348.s: This order exempts John E. White, a chauffeur in the Post Office Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending February 28, 1941.

8345.s: This order further exempts Fred C. Bailey, Fleet Manager in the United States Maritime Commission’s Maintenance and Repair Division, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one more year, ending March 31, 1941.

8343.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Alaska from settlement, sale, entry, and other appropriation. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use for military purposes in connection with an Air Corps station. Lands already under existing public-purpose reservations are not covered for as long as those reservations stay in force.

8344.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry for classification and in aid of legislation. It covers Kodiak, Whale, Uganik, Spruce, Sitkalidak, and Aiaktalik Islands, including adjacent islands, rocks, and pinnacles within two miles of their shores, with some land excluded from the withdrawal. The withdrawal is subject to valid existing rights and to existing withdrawals and reservations made for public purposes, and it stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

8342.s: This order revokes an earlier public land withdrawal for the land described here in Oklahoma. It temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for flood-control purposes connected to the Fort Supply Dam and Reservoir project. The reservation stays in place until the President or Congress revokes it.

8340.s: This order exempts Frank E. Gass, a correspondence clerk at the Smithsonian Institution, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending February 28, 1941.

8339.s: This order authorizes the Civil Service Commission to give competitive classified civil-service status to certain employees assigned to the Wage and Hour Division of the Department of Labor. It applies to employees from several former agencies who were serving in that division on May 15, 1939, if they are certified for satisfactory service, pass any required noncompetitive examination, are U.S. citizens, and are not disqualified under Civil Service Rule V.

8338.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Wyoming pending a resurvey. It applies to the listed townships and takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

8337.s: This order places certain lands in Puerto Rico under the control and jurisdiction of the Navy Department, the War Department, and the United States Public Health Service. Some land is set aside for a naval air station, one parcel is for a United States Engineer Depot, and part of Miraflores Island is for a quarantine station, a Marine hospital, or both. It also requires a common right-of-way for the different activities and revokes an earlier order reserving Miraflores Island for quarantine or a Marine hospital.

8336.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 3355 of November 19, 1920. That earlier order had temporarily withdrawn certain lands in Alaska for use by the Forest Service as a dock site for the administration of the Chugach National Forest.

8335.s: This order extends the customs port of entry of Charleston, South Carolina to include all points in Charleston Harbor and points on the Ashley and Cooper Rivers and their tributaries within ten miles of the city limits. It affects customs operations in those areas and takes effect thirty days after the order is signed.

8334.s: This order lets the Archivist of the United States make the first appointments to certain professional and sub-professional jobs in the Franklin D. Roosevelt Library. Those appointments can be made without following the Civil Service Act and rules.

8332.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal order for the land described here. It withdraws that public land in Mississippi from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for use in connection with the project to improve the flood channel of the Big Black River. The land is to be used under the supervision of the War Department, and the reservation stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

8333.s: This order changes the rules for the Army ration. It revokes the Reserve Ration and revises the Field Ration, including what foods it may contain and when it may be issued. It affects Army personnel using these rations, especially in war, national emergency, training, and operations in the theater of operations.

8331.s: This order adds listed lands and water areas in Minnesota and Wisconsin to the Upper Mississippi River Wildlife and Fish Refuge. The added areas are to be used as a breeding place for migratory and other wild birds, game and fur-bearing animals, fish, and other aquatic life, and for the conservation of wild flowers and aquatic plants. The land remains under the primary jurisdiction of the War Department for Mississippi River navigation work, and people may not hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wildlife in the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8330.s: This order temporarily withdraws a small area of public land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves that land for flood-control work connected to the Lowell Creek flood-control project. The order applies to the unsurveyed public land described in Alaska and stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

8329.s: This order waives Civil Service Rule IX time limits so Van C. Brodrick can be reinstated as a rural carrier at the post office in Marysville, Kansas. It says he had been dropped from the roll on the mistaken ground that he was unavailable for duty, and that he was in fact available for duty.

8328.s: This order further exempts Henry Clarke Hill, the Warden of the United States Penitentiary in Lewisburg, Pennsylvania, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for up to six months starting March 1, 1940.

8326.s: This order exempts William S. Garland, a civil engineer in the Navy Department’s Bureau of Aeronautics, from compulsory retirement for age for six more months. It extends his earlier exemption through July 31, 1940.

8327.s: This order exempts Dr. Mary B. Harris, the Warden of the Federal Reformatory for Women in Alderson, West Virginia, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends March 31, 1941.

8325.s: This order temporarily withdraws a parcel of public land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for use by the War Department for military purposes. The order stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

8324.s: This order abolishes Customs Collection District No. 48 for Utah and Nevada. It also revokes Salt Lake City, Utah, as a customs port of entry and extends Customs Collection District No. 28 to include Utah and Nevada.

8321.s: This order sets aside a tract of land owned by the United States near Jones Point in Alexandria, Virginia, for military purposes. The land will be known as the Battery Cove Military Reservation. The tract is described as about 39.93 acres.

8322.s: This order exempts John M. Terwilliger, a chief clerk in the Treasury Department in Detroit, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It affects only him and delays his automatic separation from service until February 28, 1941.

8319.s: This order changes the name of the Necedah Migratory Waterfowl Refuge to Necedah National Wildlife Refuge. It also transfers 39.09 acres in Juneau County, Wisconsin, from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior and adds those lands to the refuge. It makes it unlawful for any person to hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, or kill birds or other wild animals in the area, or to enter there except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8320.s: This order amends the description of the Aiea Military Reservation in the Territory of Hawaii. It says the updated description follows a recent survey of the lands under the control of the United States Government. The reservation is divided into three lots and totals 8.471 acres.

8318.s: This order makes certain income, profits, capital stock, and employment tax returns open to inspection by the Senate Committee on Education and Labor, or a duly authorized subcommittee. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury. The committee was authorized to investigate violations of free speech and assembly rights and undue interference with the right of labor to organize and bargain collectively.

8317.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to add a new rule for The National Archives. It allows certain classified positions there to be filled by promoting unclassified laborers appointed under the Labor Regulations, with Commission approval. It also says unskilled laborers at The National Archives may advance through noncompetitive examination, but they will not get classified status or be eligible to transfer to classified jobs in other parts of the federal service.

8316.s: This order allows the first appointment to a specific Assistant to the Assistant Administrator position in the Wage and Hour Division without following the competitive civil service rules, if the person meets the required qualifications. The person appointed to that job will not get competitive classified civil service status from the appointment. It also revokes part of a 1938 executive order for the Director of Regional Offices and the Chief of Policies and Standards Section positions.

8314.s: This order exempts John Kieley, an Assistant to the Secretary of the Treasury, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending December 31, 1940.

8315.s: This order changes Customs Collection District No. 38 in Michigan. It revokes Grand Haven, Michigan, as a customs port of entry and designates Muskegon, Michigan, as a customs port of entry. The change takes effect thirty days after the order.

8312.s: This order exempts David D. Caldwell, an attorney in the Department of Justice, from compulsory retirement because of age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending January 31, 1941.

8313.s: This order allows Henry Schneider to be appointed as an Investigator in the Alcohol Tax Unit of the Bureau of Internal Revenue, Treasury Department. It says the appointment can be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

8311.s: This order exempts Alexander McKeon, a deputy surveyor of customs in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending December 31, 1940.

8310.s: This order exempts Louis C. Vogt, Assistant Superintendent of Planning at the Government Printing Office, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending January 31, 1941.

8309.s: This order exempts Harry J. Morrison, a senior highway engineer in the Public Roads Administration, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on December 31, 1940.

8308.s: This order exempts Gerrit S. Miller, Jr., from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him as Curator of Mammals in the United States National Museum, Smithsonian Institution.

8306.s: This order sets license taxes in the Canal Zone for peddlers, runners who solicit sales to vessels, retail tobacco sellers, and sellers of soda water, aerated waters, or ice cream. It says no one may do those businesses without a valid license, and some applications may be denied based on the applicant’s character. It also says licenses can be canceled for rule or law violations, and people who do those businesses without a license can be fined or jailed.

8307.s: This order changes the Foreign Service Regulations to tell Foreign Service officers to protect and promote American agricultural, commercial, and financial interests abroad. It requires them to guard American rights in trade and navigation, report discrimination against American interests, and help create demand for American products. It also directs them to answer trade inquiries, assist American citizens and business firms, support American chambers of commerce, and report on economic developments in their districts.

8305.s: This order revokes an earlier reservation of certain public lands in Alaska that had been set aside for the Bureau of Biological Survey. It then withdraws and reserves those lands for the War Department for military purposes, subject to existing rights and the conditions in the cited acts. The order also says part of the land remains subject to the Alaska Railroad right-of-way.

8304.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 2552 from March 21, 1917. That earlier order had withdrawn public land in Alaska for lighthouse purposes.

8303.s: This order waives an old rule that generally barred Federal officers and employees from holding certain state, territorial, or municipal offices. It lets Huntington Cairns, an Assistant General Counsel at the United States Treasury Department, accept and hold a job on the Maryland Tax Revision Commission without extra pay.

8302.s: This order exempts Frank Burke, an agent in the Secret Service Division of the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending December 31, 1940.

8300.s: This order changes a Civil Service Rule about how an officer chooses a person for the first vacancy. It says the officer must choose from not more than the top three certified people, or from the register, and use merit and fitness as the only basis. The Civil Service Commission can object to one or more certified people for reasons listed in another rule, and for highly confidential jobs in the State, War, and Navy Departments for other approved reasons.

8299.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use for stock-watering purposes, subject to valid existing rights.

8301.s: This order directs Carroll L. Wilson, a Special Assistant to the Secretary of Commerce, to perform the duties of the Director of the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce when that director is sick or absent. It stops being effective at the close of May 31, 1940.

8297.s: This order amends the Tariff of United States Foreign Service Fees in the Foreign Service Regulations of the United States. The change takes effect on January 1, 1940, and affects United States foreign service fees.

8298.s: This order sets rules for Foreign Service officers handling commissions to take testimony in criminal cases involving foreign documents. It also sets fees and mileage for witnesses, counsel, interpreters, and translators, and says when those costs are paid by the United States or by the party asking for the commission. If the United States is not paying, the party must deposit enough money in advance to cover the expected fees and expenses.

8296.s: The order changes the name of the Pathfinder Wildlife Refuge in Wyoming to Pathfinder National Wildlife Refuge. It also adds certain public lands in Natrona County to the refuge, subject to valid existing rights. The added lands remain subject to use by the Department of the Interior for irrigation and incidental purposes in connection with the North Platte project.

8295.s: This order revokes part of two earlier executive orders that created Public Water Reserves Nos. 41 and 92. It applies only to certain public lands in California and Arizona. The lands are the ones described in the order, including land near South Cove Spring and North Cove Spring in Arizona.

8293.s: This order suspends the eight-hour limit for government workers doing authorized work at or near Midway Island and Wake Island. It applies to people employed by the Government on that work, including laborers and mechanics. The work is connected to building naval aviation facilities and harbor development there.

8294.s: The order appoints Admiral William D. Leahy, Governor of the Territory of Puerto Rico, as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration. It says he will serve without additional compensation and will carry out the functions, duties, and authority given to that office. It also amends earlier executive orders to reflect this change.

8292.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by adding rules for legal services. It tells diplomatic representatives and consular officers what to do in extradition matters, how to authenticate foreign extradition papers, when they may perform notarial acts, and when they may serve certain legal papers or deliver documents about fraudulent naturalization. It also bars Foreign Service officers from doing private legal services or making agreements with local attorneys, cancels several old regulation sections, and revokes Executive Order No. 7470.

8291.s: This order closes several federal departments, agencies, the Government Printing Office, and the Navy Yard and Naval Stations in the District of Columbia on December 23 and December 30, 1939. It also excuses federal employees in the District of Columbia and in the field service of executive departments and other government agencies from duty on those days, except for workers excluded for special public reasons or by existing law.

8290.s: This order directs that Franklin B. Atwood, a Foreign Service officer, be retired on an annuity. It says he was found to be permanently and totally disabled for useful and efficient service because of disease, not because of vicious habits, intemperance, or willful misconduct. The retirement applies to him under the Foreign Service retirement law.

8289.s: This order reserves public lands and lands the United States acquires in Socorro County, New Mexico, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It covers about 60,267 acres and is for use by the Department of the Interior. Private lands inside the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control of them.

8287.s: This order further exempts Arthur H. Chase, a senior ordnance engineer in the Navy Department, from compulsory retirement for age. It extends that exemption for one more year, ending November 30, 1940.

8286.s: This order exempts Hugh J. Murray, a master mechanic at the Navy Yard in Washington, D.C., from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending November 30, 1940.

8285.s: This order allows George K. Briggs to be appointed as Executive Assistant to the Director of the Bureau of Marine Inspection and Navigation in the Department of Commerce. It says he may be appointed without following Civil Service Rules and without being given a classified status.

8284.s: This order sets the duties of the Librarian Emeritus of the Library of Congress. Those duties are to help increase the Library of Congress collections through gifts of money and materials, and to increase trust funds and other endowments that support its chairs, consultantships, concerts, and other aids and services.

8283.s: This order changes a Civil Service rule for employees whose positions are moved into the classified, competitive service. It says they may get the rights of a competitive appointee if they meet set service, test, and disqualification requirements. It also applies to incumbents of certain positions covered by a prior executive order, and those who do not meet the requirements may be separated from service unless kept by certification.

8282.s: This order exempts John S. Biggs, an attorney-examiner at the Federal Trade Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on November 30, 1940.

8281.s: This order amends earlier Army rules for the grades and ratings of enlisted men in the Regular Army. It sets maximum numbers for each enlisted grade and for specialist ratings. It applies to enlisted men and flying cadets, and it takes effect on November 8, 1939.

8279.s: The order directs Dr. John W. Finch, the Director of the Bureau of Mines, to do the duties of the Under Secretary of the Interior, the First Assistant Secretary of the Interior, or the Assistant Secretary of the Interior when those officials are absent or sick. It also lets him perform the duties of the Secretary of the Interior during the absence or sickness of the Secretary, the Under Secretary, the First Assistant Secretary, and the Assistant Secretary from November 1 to November 30, 1939.

8278.s: This order withdraws public land and water in the eastern part of Kodiak Island, Alaska, from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves that area for the Department of the Navy for naval purposes. It also replaces a prior 1937 order and stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

8277.s: This order transfers certain lands in Oklahoma, along with improvements on them, from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of War for use as a military reservation. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps the jurisdiction needed to finish acquiring lands that are still in process of acquisition.

8276.s: This order extends the trust periods for Indian lands, whether tribal or individual, that would otherwise expire during calendar year 1940. The extension is for 25 more years from the date the trust would have expired. It does not apply to any case where Congress has specifically kept the authority to extend the trust period for those lands.

8280.s: This order changes a Civil Service Rule for classified positions in the field service of the War Department. It lets unclassified laborers appointed under the Labor Regulations be promoted into those positions, with Commission approval. It says those promoted workers do not get classified status and are not eligible for transfer to classified jobs in other parts of the federal service.

8275.s: This order exempts Harvey J. Zimmerman, Chief Statistician in the Bureau of the Census, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in his job for one more year, ending October 31, 1940.

8273.s: This order lets appointments to positions under the United States Coronado Exposition Commission be made without following the competitive requirements of the Civil Service Act and Rules. It affects appointments to those positions under the commission.

8274.s: This order exempts Edward A. Neill, Chief Mechanic at the Naval Hospital in Washington, D.C., from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and extends his service through December 31, 1940.

8271.s: This order changes Section 6 of an earlier order about foreign and domestic aircraft entering the Canal Zone and flying there. It allows the Secretary of State or the Civil Aeronautics Authority, with the agreement of the Secretary of War, to waive all or part of Sections 2, 3, 4, and 5 for certain classes of flights.

8270.s: This order exempts Edward M. Nevils, a Production Manager at the Government Printing Office, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends October 31, 1940.

8269.s: This order changes the basic exchange rates used to pay losses to officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States in foreign countries when foreign currencies rise in value against the American dollar. It says the change takes effect on December 1, 1939. For the period from October 1, 1939, to November 30, 1939, it sets the monetary unit for Danzig as the reichsmark and the basic exchange rate as 23.77.

8272.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to add temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers for part-time or intermittent work in the Postal Service. The work is for holiday or seasonal business from November 15, 1939, to January 15, 1940.

8268.s: This order exempts George W. Stose, a principal scientist (geologist) in the Geological Survey, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending October 31, 1940.

8266.s: This order exempts certain positions from Executive Order No. 6746. It applies to consultants, experts, specialists, attorneys, and similar positions that are intermittently employed on a per diem basis or on an annual basis at part-time rates, and who are paid from the public works fund or other emergency funds administered by the Secretary of the Interior during fiscal years 1940 and 1941.

8267.s: This order changes the rules for vehicles in the Canal Zone that carry inflammable or combustible liquids in bulk. It adds safety requirements for tank trucks, including bumpers, vents, valves, drag chains, and grounding during filling or unloading. It also sets a penalty for violating these rules, including a fine, jail time, or both.

8265.s: This order lets Dr. John W. Finch, the Director of the Bureau of Mines, carry out the duties of the Under Secretary of the Interior, the First Assistant Secretary, or the Assistant Secretary when those officials are absent or sick. It also lets him do the duties of the Secretary of the Interior during that same period if the Secretary and certain other Interior officials are absent or sick.

8264.s: This order allows Master Sergeant Morris Swett, United States Army, Retired, to be appointed as a junior librarian in the Field Artillery School at Fort Sill, Oklahoma. It says the appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

8263.s: This order exempts William F. Mackenzie, an examiner of merchandise in the United States Customs Service, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It affects only him and lets him stay in service through September 30, 1940.

8262.s: This order exempts Samuel A. Cottrell, an auditor in the Bureau of Internal Revenue, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending September 30, 1940.

8261.s: This order changes rules for paying losses caused by foreign currencies becoming more valuable compared with the American dollar. It clarifies what counts as the area around a ship’s station and who is included as a member of a ship’s company. It also changes when Navy employees can get foreign service pay adjustment and sets limits on that adjustment.

8260.s: This order exempts James L. Hughes from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to Hughes, who was serving as District Director of the Immigration and Naturalization Service in Gloucester City, New Jersey, in the Department of Labor.

8259.s: This order exempts Harry T. Edwards, a senior technologist in the Bureau of Plant Industry at the Department of Agriculture, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on October 31, 1940.

8258.s: This order changes a Civil Service rule about which jobs can be kept out of the competitive classified service. It covers certain people employed in a foreign country, the Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico when public need requires, some Pacific island possessions, and U.S. citizens in a confidential job in the Philippine Islands. It does not apply to people employed in Canada or Mexico for the Immigration and Naturalization Service or to people employed in any foreign country by the Bureau of Customs.

8256.s: This order exempts Maurice C. Latta, the Executive Clerk in the White House Office, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and lasts until October 31, 1940.

8257.s: This order lets the Civil Service Commission allow immediate appointments without the usual competitive civil service rules when there is a public emergency tied to the neutrality of the United States or the Federal Government’s preparedness program. It says this can be used only in unusual and compelling circumstances, and people appointed this way do not get classified civil service status.

8254.s: This order directs the Coast Guard to increase its active enlisted strength by up to 2,000 men through voluntary enlistments. It also allows the Coast Guard’s facilities to be increased, repaired, modernized, enlarged, and equipped as needed to carry out added duties and support the larger force. The Director of the Bureau of the Budget may waive or change certain apportionments for Coast Guard appropriations for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1940.

8255.s: This order transfers control and jurisdiction over certain U.S. lands in Sandoval County, New Mexico, from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior. The Secretary of the Interior may administer the lands through the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. The lands are to be used for the benefit of Indians the Secretary of the Interior designates, under conditions that fit the land-conservation and land-utilization program.

8253.s: This order exempts Walter I. Swanton, an associate engineer in the Bureau of Reclamation, from compulsory retirement for age. It allows him to stay in service for one more year, ending September 30, 1940.

8251.s: This order sets the airspace above the Canal Zone, including nearby territorial waters, apart as a military airspace reservation. Foreign and domestic aircraft may enter or pass through only under required authorization and rules, and military, naval, and other public aircraft of the United States are exempt. It also gives the Governor power to enforce the order and issue detailed regulations, and it sets penalties for violations.

8250.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 2006 of July 30, 1914. It returns certain land in the Canal Zone at Darien from the Secretary of the Navy to the control and jurisdiction of the Governor of The Panama Canal.

8252.s: This order further exempts Samuel J. Gompers, the Chief Clerk in the Department of Labor, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. The exemption runs until September 30, 1940.

8249.s: This order says the United States is neutral in the war between Germany and Canada. It makes the regulations in Executive Order 8233 apply equally to Canada to help enforce U.S. neutrality.

8247.s: This order directs the Attorney General to increase the personnel of the Federal Bureau of Investigation by up to 150 people. It says this is for the additional duties the Department of Justice will have during the national emergency. It also allows the Department of Justice to waive or change its monthly or other spending apportionments for certain appropriations for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1940.

8248.s: This order sets up divisions within the Executive Office of the President and defines what each one does. It covers the White House Office, the Bureau of the Budget, the National Resources Planning Board, the Liaison Office for Personnel Management, and the Office of Government Reports, with an emergency office if needed. It also gives rules for budget work, internal procedures, and how some offices will handle information, personnel, and reports.

8246.s: The order says there is an emergency endangering the lives of American citizens in foreign countries. It directs the Secretary of the Treasury, when asked by the Secretary of State, to transfer up to $500,000 from certain foreign affairs funds for their protection. Any reimbursements from American citizens who receive relief are to be credited back to the funds used.

8244.s: This order increases the enlisted strength of the active Regular Army by voluntary enlistments and allows the use of reserve officers if needed. It also authorizes an increase in the enlisted strength of existing active National Guard units and the commissioned strength needed for command. The Department of War may waive or change how some of its funds are apportioned if needed to carry out the order.

8243.s: This order says the United States is neutral in the war between Germany and the Union of South Africa. It applies the same neutrality enforcement rules to the Union of South Africa that already applied under Executive Order No. 8233. It is meant to make the United States’s neutrality rules more effective under the treaties, the law of nations, and the earlier proclamation.

8242.s: This order allows Miss Charlotta Gallap to be transferred from the Tennessee Valley Authority to a classified job at the Federal Communications Commission. She would serve as private secretary to the Chairman at a salary of $2,900 a year, without following the Civil Service Rules.

8241.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6774 of June 30, 1934, which had withdrawn public lands in Washington pending a resurvey. It takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey of the lands involved is filed.

8240.s: This order changes how a 1889 executive order is read so it includes sections 4, 5, and 6 of land in South Dakota as part of the Fort Meade Wood and Timber Military Reservation. It also changes a 1925 order as needed to match that land description. This affects the Fort Meade reservation and the Meade District of the Black Hills National Forest.

8245.s: This order increases the enlisted strength of the Regular Navy and the Marine Corps. It raises the Regular Navy limit to 145,000 men and the Marine Corps to 25,000 men through voluntary enlistments. It also lets the Secretary of the Navy call certain retired officers, reserve members, and aviation cadets to active duty, and waives or changes some Navy spending apportionments if needed.

8238.s: This order extends the limits of the customs port of entry of Baltimore, Maryland, to include Sparrows Point, Maryland. It becomes effective thirty days after the date of the order.

8239.s: This order revokes part of two earlier executive orders that created Power Site Reserve No. 165 and Power Site Reserve No. 241. It applies to the specific lands listed in Idaho under the Boise Meridian.

8236.s: This order makes certain income tax withholding returns open to inspection by the Department of National Revenue in Ottawa, Canada. The purpose is to help the United States Treasury Department administer the tax convention between the United States and Canada. The inspection must follow rules and regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

8235.s: This order allows Mrs. Coey Custer Jones to be appointed to a classified job in the Public Health Service without following the usual Civil Service rules. It says she is the widow of a Public Health Service medical officer who died, leaving her and three children without enough support.

8237.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to add one confidential assistant to each member of the Civil Aeronautics Authority and to the Administrator. It also says that, in each case, the private secretary position exempt by statute from competitive civil service requirements must be filled by a classified civil service employee.

8234.s: This order sets rules for vessels passing through the Panama Canal in any war when the United States is neutral. Canal authorities may inspect belligerent or neutral vessels, except public vessels, and may place armed guards on them and take control during passage. Public vessels of belligerent or neutral nations may pass only after their commanding officer gives written assurance that U.S. rules, regulations, and treaties will be obeyed.

8233.s: This order directs U.S. departments and offices to enforce the country’s neutrality during the war between Germany and France; Poland; and the United Kingdom, India, Australia, and New Zealand. It assigns duties to the War Department, Navy Department, Treasury Department, Commerce Department, Department of Justice, and the Governor of the Panama Canal. It also requires all departments and offices to help enforce neutrality in their own activities and to assist one another.

8231.s: This order exempts Edward M. Weeks, a letter engraver at the Bureau of Engraving and Printing in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age for six more months. It applies only to him and extends his exemption through February 29, 1940.

8232.s: This order gives the Army officer commanding U.S. troops in the Canal Zone exclusive authority over the operation of the Panama Canal and the government of the Canal Zone. It also says the Governor of the Panama Canal must follow that officer’s orders on matters affecting the Canal Zone.

8230.s: This order says certain tax returns made under the Internal Revenue Code may be open to inspection if the Treasury’s rules are followed. It applies to income, excess-profits, capital stock, estate, gift, and employment tax returns.

8229.s: This order allows the Board of Commissioners of the District of Columbia to promote Lieutenant Harry R. Lohman to captain in the Metropolitan Police Force. It says the promotion may be made without regard to his standing on the civil service register of eligibles.

8228.s: This order exempts William T. Andrews, an engineer revenue agent in the Bureau of Internal Revenue, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending September 30, 1940.

8224.s: This order exempts John P. Dunlop, an economic analyst in the Bureau of Mines at the Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one additional year, ending September 30, 1940.

8226.s: This order changes the annual leave rules for temporary Government employees who later get indefinite, emergency, probational, or permanent appointments in the same department or agency without a break in service. It says they are entitled to 2½ days of annual leave for each full month of service before that appointment, and then 2⅙ days per month after that, with leave credited or charged as needed.

8222.s: This order exempts certain positions from Executive Order No. 6746. The exempted jobs include consultants, experts, specialists, attorneys, and similar positions. It applies to people hired part time or on a per diem basis who are paid from public works or other emergency funds handled by the Federal Works Administrator.

8223.s: This order changes a prior Alaska land reservation so certain town-site lands in Nenana can be used by the Alaska Road Commission for aviation field purposes. It reserves and sets apart the south half of Block 38 and all of Block 45 for that use. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

8221.s: This order changes how the Civilian Conservation Corps is run. It phases out reserve officers on active duty with the Corps and says no new reserve officers will be ordered to that duty, with limited short extensions in some cases. It also lets the Corps director carry out projects on county, municipal, and private land, and asks several department heads to help the director with the program.

8220.s: This order revokes parts of two earlier executive orders that had withdrawn certain lands in Oregon for power-site use. It applies only to the specific land descriptions listed under the Willamette Meridian. The rest of those earlier orders is not changed.

8219.s: This order gives the Secretary of Agriculture the authority to exercise all rights of the United States that come from owning stock in the Commodity Credit Corporation. It replaces an earlier order that had given that role to the Secretary of the Treasury.

8218.s: This order exempts Herbert Vansant, a senior civil engineer in the War Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending August 31, 1940.

8216.s: This order revokes an earlier reservation of Harbor Island and three islets in Sitka Harbor, Alaska, that had been set aside for the Revenue Cutter Service. It withdraws the listed public land and water in Sitka Bay from settlement, location, sale, or entry, and reserves it for the Department of the Navy for naval purposes. The reservation stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

8217.s: This order further exempts George Middleton, a senior commodity specialist with the United States Tariff Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for six months and ends March 31, 1940.

8215.s: This order changes the employment rules for employees of The Panama Canal and the Panama Railroad Company on the Isthmus of Panama. It gives some United States citizens free transportation to the United States when their service ends, including to New York, another U.S. port, or a port of embarkation in certain cases. In some cases, employees must pay any cost over $50 or any excess over the cost to the port of embarkation.

8213.s: This order exempts Erastus S. Hawkins, a deputy collector of customs in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and delays his automatic separation from service until July 31, 1940.

8214.s: This order changes how time limits for reinstatement under the Civil Service Rules are counted for certain former federal employees. It applies to employees who were separated between June 30, 1932, and July 26, 1937, solely because of section 213 of the Economy Act. It gives them extra time eligibility for reinstatement, subject to the other Civil Service Rules requirements.

8212.s: This order reinstates James J. Murphy, Jr. in the Foreign Service of the United States in Class III. His reinstatement takes effect when the Senate confirms his nomination to that class.

8210.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by setting rules for diplomatic and consular officers. It defines who counts as diplomatic and consular officers and describes how they are appointed, present credentials, begin duty, and get official recognition. It also cancels several older regulation sections and revokes Executive Order No. 5661.

8209.s: This order exempts William M. Smith from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to Smith, a Special Assistant to the Chief of the Bureau of Yards and Docks in the Navy Department, and ends October 31, 1940.

8211.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5633 of May 28, 1931, which had withdrawn public lands in California pending a resurvey. The change takes effect when the official filing of the plat of the resurvey for those lands is made.

8208.s: This order exempts Mrs. Frances S. Nichols from compulsory retirement for age. It lets her stay in her job as Editorial Assistant at the Bureau of American Ethnology, Smithsonian Institution, for one more year ending August 31, 1940.

8206.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6432, which had withdrawn public lands in Wyoming while a resurvey was pending. It takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey of the lands involved are filed.

8207.s: This order further exempts Dr. George F. Bowerman, the Librarian of the Free Public Library of the District of Columbia, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending September 30, 1940.

8205.s: This order lets the first Assistant Administrator of the Federal Security Agency and one private secretary or confidential assistant be appointed without following the competitive civil service rules, if the Civil Service Commission sets the needed qualifications. It also amends the civil service rules to add two private secretaries or confidential assistants to the Administrator of the Federal Security Agency.

8204.s: This order exempts Michael E. Gorman, an Examiner of Indian Inheritance in the Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for six months, ending February 29, 1940.

8203.s: The order transfers certain lands in Monroe County, Wisconsin, from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of War. The lands, along with improvements on them, are to be used as a military reservation. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps any jurisdiction needed to finish acquiring lands that are still in process of acquisition.

8202.s: This order tells the Federal Power Commission to receive applications for permits for facilities at the U.S. border that transmit electric energy between the United States and foreign countries. It also covers applications to export or import natural gas to or from foreign countries. The commission is to send each application to the President with a recommendation, after getting the views of the Secretary of State and the Secretary of War.

8200.s: This order revokes part of an earlier order that had withdrawn public lands in Wyoming pending a resurvey. It applies to one named township in the Sixth Principal Meridian and takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

8198.s: This order suspends the law that limits certain workers on U.S. contracts to eight hours of labor in one day. It applies to work on naval aviation bases at or near Midway Island, Johnston Island, Palmyra Island, Kodiak, Alaska, and Sitka, Alaska. It affects people doing that work under contracts with the United States.

8199.s: This order revokes earlier coal land withdrawals for the listed lands in New Mexico. It removes those lands from the coal land withdrawal areas created in 1910, 1911, 1915, and 1917. The change affects the specific townships, sections, and tracts named in the order.

8197.s: This order sets rules for foreign governments to request the services of U.S. officers and employees with special scientific, technical, or professional qualifications. Those requests must go through diplomatic channels to the Secretary of State, and the request may be denied if the United States cannot comply or if compliance is not in the public interest. The order also requires the Secretary of State to keep uniform records and share a completed form with the lending agency after each detail or assignment.

8196.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by adding new rules for attachés and for relations with other U.S. departments abroad. It sets rules for official calls and visits between naval officers and Foreign Service officers, and it directs consular officers to help with quarantine duties, stranded Coast Guard personnel, and some Veterans' Administration activities abroad. It also cancels several parts of the Foreign Service Regulations and revokes two earlier executive orders.

8195.s: This order exempts Frederick S. Jackson, a Civil Engineer and Superintendent of Construction in the War Department, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for nine more months, ending April 30, 1940.

8194.s: This order places the Federal Fire Council under the jurisdiction and control of the Federal Works Agency. It says the Council’s functions will be carried out under the direction and supervision of the Federal Works Administrator, and it names the Commissioner of Public Buildings as chairman of the Council’s governing body.

8193-A.s: This order assigns radio frequencies to Government radio stations and classes of stations. It sets rules for how those frequencies may be used, including approval requirements, priority, experimental use, and interference limits. It also defines several terms used in the order and says some frequencies may be used in the Canal Zone and in communication with non-Government stations.

8193.s: This order revokes part of a 1932 order that had withdrawn public lands in Colorado while a resurvey was pending. It applies to the listed townships and takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

8192.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of a 12.5-acre piece of land in Alaska from the 1917 order. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for use by the Forest Service as an addition to an existing administrative site.

8191.s: This order places the Goethals Memorial Commission under the jurisdiction and control of the War Department. Its functions are to be carried out under the direction and supervision of the Secretary of War.

8190.s: This order places the Committee for Reciprocity Information under the control of the Department of State. Its work is to be carried out under the direction and supervision of the Secretary of State, who will choose the chairman from the committee’s members. The Executive Committee on Commercial Policy will keep selecting certain members of the Committee for Reciprocity Information.

8188.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 4539 of November 6, 1926, for the rest of the public lands in Utah that were covered by it. It becomes effective when the official plat of the resurvey of those lands is filed.

8187.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules by adding a new paragraph to Schedule A. It covers all positions in the Federal Bureau of Investigation during the stated period, except fingerprint classifiers.

8186.s: This order transfers all powers, rights, privileges, and duties that had been moved to the Secretary of the Treasury to the Federal Works Administrator. It also requires the Secretary of the Treasury to take needed steps to carry out the order, including transferring all stock of the United States Housing Corporation held by the Secretary of the Treasury as trustee. The order supersedes a prior executive order and takes effect July 1, 1939.

8185.s: This order changes how the Board of Foreign Service Personnel is staffed. It says the Commerce and Agriculture officers on that board will sit only when matters of interest to their departments are being considered, such as commercial attaches, agricultural attaches, or related training. It also adds those officers to the School Board for the Foreign Service Officers' Training School and changes the Board of Examiners for the Foreign Service to include them. The order kept the existing rules for foreign service examinations and became effective on July 1, 1939.

8189.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations and adds rules for how offices are transferred, how government property is handled, and how reports are made. It also sets rules for Foreign Service quarters, where diplomatic and consular officers may live, office hours, leave, and the use of the coat of arms and the flag. The order cancels several parts of the Foreign Service Regulations and revokes five earlier executive orders.

8183.s: This order closes executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies in the District of Columbia for all day on Monday, July 3, 1939. It also excuses Federal employees in the District of Columbia and in the field service of the Executive departments and other government agencies from duty that day, except for employees excluded for special public reasons or where absence would conflict with existing law.

8184.s: This order changes the use of certain land and buildings in Hampton Bays, Suffolk County, New York. It keeps the land for a wildlife refuge, but makes that use subject to the Treasury Department’s use of the property for Coast Guard purposes. The primary use of the property remains with the Department of Commerce for lighthouse purposes.

8182.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations under Executive Order No. 6166. It applies to the disbursement function used by United States Marshals under the Department of Justice and to the disbursement function for the Postal Service. These changes are delayed until June 30, 1940.

8181.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by adding new rules on immunity, powers, and privileges for diplomatic and consular officers. It says diplomatic immunity cannot be waived except with the Secretary of State’s consent, and it limits asylum, customs courtesies, and tax exemptions to what treaty, law, or reciprocity allows. It also says diplomats and consular officers may not use their official position to avoid just obligations, and it cancels some older regulations and revokes a prior executive order.

8180.s: This order sets September 1, 1939, as the effective date for elections by retired Foreign Service officers to receive reduced annuities. It applies to retired officers who choose that option under the law. A portion of the annuity would continue after the officer's death for the life of the surviving widow.

8178.s: This order revokes part of an 1875 executive order that had reserved land for lifesaving purposes. It applies to a described parcel of public land in Florida.

8179.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules about probationary employees and promotions. It says a person separated during probation may be reinstated under certain conditions, including different rules for involuntary separation and voluntary resignation. It also says a person must have received absolute appointment, and that an employee during probation cannot be promoted without prior Commission approval.

8177.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations to cover retirement benefits for Foreign Service officers, ambassadors and ministers promoted from the classified Foreign Service, some State Department appointees, and other officers named in the order. It also lets Foreign Service officers make optional extra deposits into the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability Fund, within stated limits. The order cancels certain sections of the Foreign Service Regulations.

8175.s: This order revokes part of a 1914 Executive Order that created Public Water Reserve No. 18. The change applies only to the listed land in Wyoming.

8176.s: This order sets the grades and ratings for enlisted men of the Regular Army for fiscal year 1940. It limits how many enlisted men may be in each grade and in each specialist rating. It also says the number of privates must fit within the Army’s enlisted pay strength and the number of authorized flying cadets.

8174.s: This order changes the boundary description of a tract of public land in Alaska. The tract is used as a headquarters site for administering the Alaska game laws. The new description is made to match a survey called "U.S. Survey No. 2264, Alaska."

8173.s: The order reserves about 804.71 acres and part of Talcot Lake in Minnesota for use by the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It says the area will be known as the Talcot Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. Any private lands in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control of them.

8171.s: The order transfers certain lands in New York from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of War. The lands are to be used as military reservations. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps any jurisdiction needed to finish acquiring lands that are still in process of acquisition.

8172.s: This order removes certain tracts of land in Alaska from the Chugach and Tongass National Forests and restores them to entry under the public-land laws. The lands listed are occupied for trade and manufacturing purposes or as homesites. It affects the named sites in the two forests.

8170.s: This order allows A. Sidney Johnson to be appointed as a deputy commissioner of customs in the Bureau of Customs, Treasury Department, in Washington, D.C. It says the appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

8169.s: This order revokes part of Executive Order No. 6153 for one named township in Colorado. The revocation applies to public lands in that township that had been withdrawn pending a resurvey. It takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

8168.s: This order revokes an 1898 reservation of certain lands in Alaska that had been set aside for an agricultural experiment station. It then reserves those lands for the United States Coast and Geodetic Survey in the Department of Commerce to use as a magnetic and seismological observatory site.

8167.s: This order sets aside federal lands and waters in Griggs County, North Dakota as the Sibley Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, or kill birds or other wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. It reserves the area for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife.

8166.s: This order sets aside about 1,678 acres in Mountrail County, North Dakota, as the Shell Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. The land is reserved for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife, subject to valid rights. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or enter within the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8165.s: This order sets aside about 5,587 acres of United States land and water in Towner County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture. It creates the Rock Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there, or to enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8164.s: This order reserves about 1,020 acres of federal land and water in Benson County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal in the refuge. It also bars people from entering the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8163.s: This order sets aside federal land in Walsh County, North Dakota, as the Pioneer Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. The land is reserved for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It is unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8162.s: The order sets aside lands owned or controlled by the United States in Dickey County, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal in the refuge. It also bars entry into the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8160.s: This order sets aside certain United States-owned lands in Mountrail County, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for any person to hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal in the refuge. It also says people may not enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8161.s: This order adds about 11,135 acres of land and water in Burleigh and Kidder Counties, North Dakota, to the Long Lake Migratory Bird Refuge. Any private land in the area becomes part of the refuge if the United States gets title or control of it. It also makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, or kill birds or other wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8159.s: The order sets aside federal land in Nelson County, North Dakota as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It says people may not hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge. It also says no one may enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8157.s: This order reserves about 480 acres of U.S.-owned land in McLean County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal in the refuge. It also bars entry into the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8158.s: The order sets aside federal lands and waters in Williams County, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, wilfully disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal in the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. It also revokes an earlier order for these lands.

8156.s: This order sets aside federal land in Morton County, North Dakota, as the Lake Patricia Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. It makes the land a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or enter birds or wild animals in the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8155.s: This order sets aside about 1,800 acres of federal land and water in McLean County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there, or to enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8154.s: This order sets aside 3,064.51 acres in Dunn County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it, except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. The area is to be known as the Lake Ilo Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

8153.s: This order sets aside about 3,113 acres of federal land and water in Kidder County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there, or to enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. It also revokes part of a 1934 order as to the lands covered here.

8151.s: This order sets aside about 1,840 acres in Barnes County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8152.s: This order reserves about 635 acres of federal land and water in Richland County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal in the refuge. People may enter only under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8150.s: This order sets aside federal lands and waters in McLean and Ward Counties, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It applies to lands owned or controlled by the United States within the described area. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8149.s: This order reserves certain federal lands and waters in McHenry County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal in the refuge. It also bars entry except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8148.s: This order sets aside 1,977.48 acres of land in Towner County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it, unless allowed under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. The area is to be known as the Brumba Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

8147.s: This order set aside about 2,980 acres of U.S. land and water in Walsh County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals inside the refuge. It also bars entry there unless allowed under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8146.s: This order reinstates Paul H. Alling in the Foreign Service of the United States in Class IV. His reinstatement takes effect when the Senate confirms his nomination to that class.

8144.s: This order revokes part of a 1910 executive order that created Petroleum Reserve No. 7 in Utah. It removes the reserve status from the listed lands in many townships and sections in Utah. The change affects only those described lands; the rest of the reserve is not mentioned here.

8145.s: This order changes the name of the Nine-Pipe Reservation in Lake County, Montana, to the Nine-Pipe Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. It also adds certain United States lands to the refuge, subject to valid rights. The refuge is enlarged to include the lands described in the order.

8142.s: This order exempts Thomas A. Jaggar, Jr., a Principal Scientist in the National Park Service, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. It applies only to him and extends his exemption through July 31, 1940.

8143.s: This order sets part of Pearl Harbor and its entrance channel in Hawaii as a defensive sea area for national defense. It says only public vessels of the United States may enter or move within that area unless the Secretary of the Navy gives permission. Anyone who breaks the order can face penalties under the law.

8141.s: This order transfers the use, possession, and control of certain lands in Jackson County, Alabama, from the War Department to the Tennessee Valley Authority. The lands include the Widows Bar Lock and Dam, along with the lock, buildings, and other improvements on them. The transfer becomes effective when the Guntersville Dam is completed.

8140.s: The order restores three parcels of land from the Punchbowl Hill Military Reservation to the Territory of Hawaii for road purposes. It also reserves two other parcels as part of the military reservation for military purposes. The changes affect land in the Territory of Hawaii and the Punchbowl Hill Military Reservation.

8139.s: This order exempts James E. Harper, Chief of the Division of Appointments in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, ending June 30, 1940.

8137.s: This order lets certain employees of the General Accounting Office stay in service beyond the earlier authorized date. Their service may continue, but not past June 30, 1940.

8138.s: This order revokes part of a 1910 executive order that had created a coal land withdrawal in Montana. It restores the listed lands in Montana to their former status under that withdrawal. The change affects the specific townships and sections named in the order.

8136.s: This order gives the Attorney General, or the Assistant Attorney General in charge of the Claims Division, the powers the President had under parts of the Trading with the Enemy Act. It also approves past actions taken by the Attorney General and the Department of Justice on these matters. The Secretary of the Treasury must sell certain securities and deposit the proceeds in the Treasury for the account of the Attorney General, Alien Property Bureau. Earlier executive orders that gave these powers to other officials are replaced by this order.

8135.s: This order sets rules for appeals from decisions of the Auditor General of the Philippines to the President of the United States. It requires appeals to be in writing, filed with the Office of the United States High Commissioner to the Philippine Islands within thirty days, and sent to the Auditor General for a response. The High Commissioner may end the appeal by agreeing with the Auditor General, or send the case onward if the decision is found to be erroneous.

8134.s: This order changes the rules for pay and job classification in agencies that are operated in whole or in part from emergency funds. Agency heads may choose to classify employee positions and set pay either under the salary schedule in Executive Order No. 6746 or under the Classification Act of 1923, as amended. It applies to employees now in service and to those appointed later.

8132.s: This order exempts Miss Lilian M. Lamb, a junior administrative assistant in the Navy Department, from compulsory retirement for age. It allows her to stay in service for one year, until June 30, 1940.

8133.s: This order changes a prior executive order about the Civilian Conservation Corps. It asks the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Agriculture, and the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs to work with the Corps director. Each of them must appoint a representative to meet with the director and help carry out the law under his direction.

8131.s: This order opens certain income, excess-profits, and capital stock tax returns for inspection by the Special Committee on Un-American Activities of the House of Representatives, or an authorized subcommittee. The returns covered are for the calendar year 1932 and later taxable years. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

8130.s: This order transfers the lands in the Pocatello and Portneuf Divisions of the Cache National Forest in Idaho to the Caribou National Forest in Idaho.
