It says no publicly owned lands are to gain national-forest status if they did not already have it, and no publicly owned lands are to lose national-forest status.

8129.s: The order sets aside certain federally owned or controlled land in Benson County, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal in the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8128.s: This order reserves certain lands and waters in McLean County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal there. It also bars people from entering the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8127.s: The order reserves certain lands and waters in Bottineau and Rolette Counties, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge. People may enter only under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8126.s: This order sets aside about 480 acres of federal land in Emmons County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there. It also bars entry into the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8125.s: This order reserves certain federal land in Grand Forks County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. The area is called the Little Goose Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

8124.s: This order sets aside federal land in Oliver County, North Dakota, as the Lake Oliver Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. It gives the Department of Agriculture use of the area as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It bars people from hunting, trapping, capturing, disturbing, or killing birds or wild animals there, or entering the refuge, except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8123.s: This order sets aside about 320 acres of United States land in Burleigh County, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal there, or to enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. The area will be known as the Lake Moraine Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

8122.s: This order sets aside United States land in Eddy and Nelson Counties, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8121.s: This order sets aside federal land and water in Kidder County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. The area is named the Hutchinson Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

8120.s: The order reserves about 160 acres of United States land in Stutsman County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there. It also bars people from entering the refuge unless allowed under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8119.s: This order reserves certain lands and waters in Burleigh County, North Dakota for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there, or to enter the refuge unless allowed under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8118.s: This order sets aside about 640 acres of U.S.-owned or controlled land in Emmons County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there, or to enter the refuge unless allowed by rules from the Secretary of Agriculture.

8117.s: This order sets aside about 2,784 acres in Dickey County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it, unless allowed under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. The area is called the Dakota Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

8116.s: This order sets aside about 800 acres of U.S.-owned or controlled land in Hettinger County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal in the refuge. It also bars entry into the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8115.s: This order sets aside about 453 acres of federal land and water in Burleigh County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals inside the refuge. Entry is allowed only under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8114.s: This order reserves certain lands and waters in McLean County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, wilfully disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal in the refuge. It also bars people from entering the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8113.s: This order sets aside federal lands and waters in Pierce County, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or enter there except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. It also revokes an earlier order for these lands.

8112.s: This order sets aside about 640 acres of federal land in LaMoure County, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal in the refuge. People may enter only under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8111.s: This order sets aside federal land in Cavalier County, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals within the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. The area is to be known as the Billings Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

8110.s: This order sets aside certain federally owned or controlled land in Emmons County, North Dakota as the Appert Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. It is to be used by the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8109.s: This order corrects the land description of the Waianae-Kai Military Reservation in the Territory of Hawaii after a new survey found errors. It also extends the Territorial Government road right-of-way through Tract No. 1 from 40 feet to 60 feet wide. The changes affect the military reservation lands and the road right-of-way there.

8107.s: This order changes an existing rule on allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men who are not given quarters or rations in kind. It updates one exception to cover Naval Missions to Brazil, Peru, and Colombia instead of only Brazil and Peru. It affects enlisted men of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Survey, and Public Health Service.

8105.s: This order exempts Herbert E. Lucas, a special agent in the Bureau of Internal Revenue, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, ending May 31, 1940.

8106.s: This order keeps Frank B. Bourn from being forced to retire for age for one more year, ending June 30, 1940. It applies to him as Chief of the Supplies and Accounts Division in the Office of the Secretary of War, War Department.

8104.s: This order sets aside certain lands in Washington as the Little Pend Oreille Wildlife Refuge for the Department of Agriculture. It is for a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife, and private lands in the area become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control. It also bars hunting, trapping, capturing, willful disturbance, killing, or entry in the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8102.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It places those lands under the control of the War Department for use as a military reservation. Lands in existing public-purpose reservations are exempt while those reservations remain in effect.

8103.s: The order transfers land in the Virgin Islands from the control of the Secretary of the Interior to the control of the Secretary of the Navy. The land is to be used for the establishment, construction, and operation of aviation facilities near the existing Naval Air Station, St. Thomas. Parts of the area now used as an Agricultural Station will stay available to the Department of the Interior until the Secretary of the Interior says they are no longer needed for that use.

8101.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for use of the War Department as a target range for the Wyoming National Guard. The reservation stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

8100.s: This order adds a described piece of public land in Mississippi to the Homochitto National Forest. It says the land is included and reserved as part of the forest, subject to valid existing rights. It also revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn that land for classification.

8099.s: This order puts the Veterans' Administration in charge of administering and paying the benefits created by the law. It covers certain Army officers, warrant officers, and enlisted men who are called into active military service for more than 30 days and who suffer disability or death in line of duty from disease or injury. For retirement benefits, the Secretary of War, or someone he designates, decides whether a disability exists and whether it was incurred in line of duty.

8098.s: This order revokes a previous order that had withdrawn public lands in Colorado while a resurvey was pending. It affects those lands in Colorado. It takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

8097.s: This order further exempts Charles J. Carlton, a letterer and grainer at the Navy Yard in Washington, D.C., from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one more year, ending April 30, 1940.

8096.s: This order exempts William C. Shambaugh, a blacksmith instructor in the War Department’s Medical Department at Large, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending August 31, 1940.

8094.s: This order exempts Zeke Johnson, a custodian at Natural Bridges National Monument, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and ends on April 30, 1940.

8095.s: The order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands in New Mexico from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior. The Secretary of the Interior may use those lands with the Taylor Grazing Act and the land-conservation and land-utilization program. It also reserves other public-domain lands for the Department of Agriculture for the Hope Land Use Adjustment Project, and those lands cannot be sold, exchanged, or granted without approval from the Secretary of the Interior. The order says it does not apply to mineral resources on those lands.

8093.s: This order revokes a 1933 order that had withdrawn public lands in California pending a resurvey. It applies to the rest of the lands covered by that earlier order and takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

8092.s: This order changes Schedule B of the Civil Service Rules to add certain classified positions in the field service of the Department of Agriculture. It allows unclassified laborers appointed under the Labor Regulations to be promoted to those positions, with approval from the Civil Service Commission. It also says those promoted workers do not get classified status and cannot be transferred to classified jobs in other branches of the Federal service.

8091.s: This order changes a prior 1915 order that had reserved certain Alaska lands for townsite purposes. It allows specific lots in the Federal Addition to Seward Townsite to be used by the Bureau of Public Roads in the Department of Agriculture for road building projects. The lands are reserved and set apart for that use until the order is revoked by the President or by Congress.

8089.s: This order revokes part of a prior withdrawal for certain public lands in Oklahoma. The land is temporarily withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserved for the War Department for flood-control purposes. The reservation stays in place until the President or Congress revokes it.

8090.s: This order restores two adjoining parcels of land from the Nozaleda Military Reservation in Manila to the Commonwealth of the Philippines. It says the land is no longer needed for the reservation and that restoring it is in the public interest. The parcels together total 1,470 square meters, more or less.

8087.s: This order removes certain homesite tracts in Alaska from the Chugach and Tongass National Forests. It restores those tracts to entry under the public-land laws. The tracts are listed in the order and include homesites on Kenai Lake, Revillagigedo Island, Wrangell Island, Wrangell Narrows, and Mountain Point Group.

8086.s: This order sets aside certain U.S.-owned or controlled land in Addison County, Vermont, as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and other wildlife. The land stays under the Department of Agriculture for use as the United States Morgan Horse Farm, and the refuge must remain subject to that use. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8085.s: This order temporarily withdraws a 40-acre parcel of land in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for use by the Forest Service as a ranger station connected to the Gunnison National Forest. The withdrawal stays in place until the President or Congress revokes it.

8083.s: This order extends the Civil Service Retirement Act to certain federal employees in Schedule A or Schedule B positions, and to some employees in other excepted positions if they were appointed under Civil Service Rule II. It also covers employees who have been given classified status while serving in those positions. The order changes Civil Service Rule II so some excepted positions may be filled like classified positions, but the person appointed to one of those jobs will not get protection against removal under those rules.

8084.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by adding rules on marriages, births, deaths, and estates. It forbids Foreign Service officers from celebrating marriages, lets consular officers act as official witnesses in some cases, and requires them to record births of American children abroad and report deaths of Americans abroad. It also sets out duties for consular officers in handling the personal property and estates of Americans who die abroad, cancels several older regulation sections, and revokes Executive Order No. 170.

8081.s: This order reserves about 197 acres of land on Bath House Island, Bird Island, Round Island, and Anclote Keys in Pasco and Pinellas Counties, Florida. It sets the land aside for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife, subject to valid existing rights. It also revokes part of an 1886 executive order that reserved some of the same land as the Anclote Keys Lighthouse Reservation.

8082.s: This order says Mrs. Esther H. Soter may be appointed to a classified position in the Federal Trade Commission without following the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of a former FTC employee who died, leaving her and three children without adequate means of continued support.

8079.s: This order changes the name of the customs port of entry of Mars Hill, Maine, to Bridgewater, Maine. It also includes the townships of Bridgewater, Blaine, Mars Hill, and Easton within the limits of the customs port of Bridgewater. The change takes effect thirty days after the order is signed.

8080.s: This order revokes Fair Haven, New York’s designation as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 8 (Rochester). It becomes effective thirty days from the date of the order.

8078.s: This order changes the fee schedule for U.S. Foreign Service services. It adds a $10 fee for issuing a Chinese certificate, sets no fee for preparing an application and administering the oath for a limited entry certificate, and sets no fee for granting that certificate. It also changes the fee for certifying copies of documents to $2.00, with an exception for documents that may be furnished without charge.

8077.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations for dealings with foreign governments. It says diplomatic representatives must handle direct correspondence with the government they are assigned to, and consular officers may do so when there is no diplomatic representative and it is necessary. It also lets diplomatic and consular officers temporarily represent foreign interests with approval from the Department of State, but they may not accept an office for a foreign government. The order cancels several listed sections of the regulations.

8076.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by adding new rules for how diplomats, consuls general, and consular officers work within the service. It gives diplomatic representatives general supervision over consular officers and sets rules for how consuls general supervise consular offices, inspect them, and share information. It also sets the order of rank for Foreign Service and consular officers and cancels several older regulation sections.

8075.s: This order exempts Glenn S. Smith, a chief engineer with the Geological Survey in the Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on April 30, 1940.

8074.s: This order exempts George K. Larrison from compulsory retirement for age for three months. It applies to his work as Hawaiian Homes Representative in the Office of the Secretary, Division of Territories and Island Possessions, Department of the Interior.

8073.s: This order exempts Newton C. Lammond, a senior clerk in the War Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends June 30, 1940.

8072.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Washington from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for use by the Navy Department for naval aviation purposes. The withdrawal is temporary and stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

8071.s: This order creates the Federal Interdepartmental Safety Council as an advisory agency on the safety of federal employees. The Council is made up of officers and employees from federal departments and the government of the District of Columbia, and they serve without extra pay. It is to share information on accident prevention and health conservation, make recommendations and forms for safe practices, and, when asked, conduct surveys or investigations and report the results. The Division of Labor Standards in the Department of Labor is asked to cooperate with the Council.

8069.s: This order revokes the designation of Gateway, Montana, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 33. The change takes effect at the close of business on March 31, 1939.

8068.s: This order changes the navigation rules for the Panama Canal and adjacent waters. It exempts vessels transiting and re-transiting the canal for repairs at Panama Canal drydocks or shops from tolls, but they still must pay for pilotage, towage, and other related services. It also says vessels that go through the locks at one end and return to the start pay tolls for a single passage, and if they carry cargo or passengers, the toll rate for laden vessels applies.

8070.s: This order exempts Sims Ely, the City Manager of Boulder City, Nevada, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on March 31, 1940.

8067.s: The order reserves certain lands in Chesterfield County, South Carolina, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Any private land in the area can become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control of it. It makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, willfully disturb, kill, or enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8066.s: This order confirms and ratifies the appointments of Walter Kearney and Stanley D. Zaveckas to competitive classified positions in the United States Despatch Agency in the Department of State in New York. It says their appointments were made without following the competitive civil service rules. The order was issued on the recommendation of the Acting Secretary of State.

8065.s: This order sets aside about 40,500 acres in Wisconsin as the Necedah Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. It reserves the land for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Private lands in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control. It also makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8063.s: This order allows initial appointments to certain executive jobs in the Railroad Retirement Board without following the competitive Civil Service Rules, if the required qualifications are first established before the Civil Service Commission. The positions include controller, chief of plans and procedure, director of research, chief inspector, assistant chief inspector, assistant director of employment and claims, director of employment service, and regional directors. It affects appointments to those Railroad Retirement Board positions.

8064.s: This order designates Fairbanks, Alaska, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 31, with headquarters at Juneau, Alaska. It also discontinues Seward, Alaska, as a customs port of entry in that district. The order takes effect thirty days from the date of the order.

8062.s: This order sets a new fee schedule for officers of the United States Court for China. It lists fees for the clerk and marshal for filing cases, appeals, probate matters, marriage ceremonies, service of papers, sales of property, and other court services. It also says this new schedule replaces the earlier fee schedule for that court.

8060.s: This order exempts Fred C. Bailey, a Fleet Manager in the United States Maritime Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, ending March 31, 1940.

8061.s: This order moves a tract of land in Christiansted, St. Croix, in the Virgin Islands from the Department of the Interior to the Treasury Department. The property is to be used for post-office purposes. It also changes a 1931 order about the same property so this transfer can take effect.

8058.s: This order exempts Ales Hrdlicka, Curator of Physical Anthropology in the United States National Museum, Smithsonian Institution, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending March 31, 1940.

8059.s: This order transfers the use, possession, and control of certain public lands in Alabama to the Tennessee Valley Authority. It also transfers certain lands the United States had acquired and placed under the control of the War Department, for the purposes stated in the Tennessee Valley Authority Act of 1933.

8057.s: This order transfers certain lands and the improvements on them from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior. The lands are to be used and administered as part of the Appomattox Court House National Historical Monument in Virginia.

8056.s: This order changes a Civil Service Rule for certain classified positions in the Ordnance Department at Large and in the Chemical Warfare Service at Large at Edgewood Arsenal, Maryland. It says those jobs may be filled by promoting unclassified laborers, with approval from the Civil Service Commission.

8055.s: The order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands in the Fort Peck Indian Reservation in Montana from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior. It also authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to administer those lands through the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. The lands are to be used for the benefit of Indians the Secretary designates, under conditions that carry out the land-conservation and land-utilization program.

8054.s: This order places a parcel of land in the Townsite of Wrangell, Alaska, under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Treasury. The land is to be used as a site for Federal buildings.

8053.s: This order revokes part of two earlier executive orders that created Public Water Reserves Nos. 14 and 15. It applies only to the listed lands in California and Oregon, including a parcel in San Bernardino Meridian and lands in Willamette Meridian near a spring.

8052.s: This order designates the Honorable Angel R. de Jesus, an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico, to act as judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico. He may do this and sign needed papers and records when the judge is absent, ill, or otherwise legally disabled, and he will receive no extra compensation.

8050.s: This order exempts Robert F. Whitehead, a Solicitor in the Patent Office at the Department of Commerce, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for four months and ends on June 30, 1939.

8049.s: This order exempts George W. Patterson, the head chemist at the U.S. Naval Powder Factory in Indian Head, Maryland, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. His exemption runs until March 31, 1940.

8048.s: This order exempts John G. Crane, Superintendent of the Garbage Reduction Plant of the Government of the District of Columbia, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and applies only to him.

8051.s: This order limits how many red cedar shingles from Canada may be admitted to entry during the first six months of 1939. It sets the limit at 1,051,168 squares. The order says it will stop having force and effect when the trade agreement from November 15, 1935 ends.

8046.s: This order exempts Louis A. Simon from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. Simon was the supervising architect of the Public Buildings Branch of the Procurement Division in the Treasury Department.

8047.s: This order further exempts Edward B. Russ, Chief of the Stenographic Section at the Department of State, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year ending February 29, 1940.

8045.s: This order authorizes Frederick Morgan Davenport to be appointed to a classified position in the Civil Service Commission. It also designates him as a member and chairman of the Council of Personnel Administration, effective when he accepts the appointment.

8044.s: This order suspends part of Executive Order No. 7916 for certain civil service positions, including some that are not practical to fill by competitive exam, highly confidential jobs, professional and scientific jobs, Inland Waterways Corporation positions, and certain administrative and technical positions. It defines what counts as administrative and technical positions under the order. It also creates a committee to study how civil service personnel are recruited, tested, selected, promoted, transferred, removed, and reinstated, and to report recommendations to the President.

8043.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to list many federal jobs that are excepted from competitive examination. It covers positions in several departments, including private secretaries, chauffeurs, interpreters, local physicians and dentists, temporary legal staff, and certain workers in the field, overseas, or in special service areas. It also sets conditions for some of these exceptions, such as limits on term, location, pay, or approval by the Civil Service Commission.

8042.s: This order allows initial appointments to certain positions under the Air Safety Board, Civil Aeronautics Authority without following the competitive requirements of the Civil Service Rules. It applies to the Executive Officer, Technical Adviser, and several division and section chiefs. The order says each person must still meet the required qualifications before the Civil Service Commission.

8041.s: This order exempts Henry Clarke Hill, the warden of the United States Northeastern Penitentiary in Lewisburg, Pennsylvania, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption can last for up to one year starting March 1, 1939.

8040.s: This order sets rules for extra pay for enlisted Navy men who are specially qualified to use the arms they may be required to use. It applies when they are stationed where they may need to use those arms, including some temporary duty away from their ship if their commanding officer keeps them in their usual battle stations. It also replaces an earlier 1922 order on the same subject.

8039.s: This order withdraws certain federal lands in Arizona from settlement, sale, or entry and sets them aside for wildlife conservation and the protection of public grazing lands and natural forage resources. It says mineral prospecting, mining, leasing, and patenting may continue under the law. The range is to be called the Kofa Game Range, and the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture share authority over wildlife matters, while surplus forage may be available for domestic livestock.

8038.s: This order withdraws the described lands in Arizona from settlement, location, sale, or entry and sets them aside for wildlife conservation and development, as well as for protecting and improving public grazing lands and natural forage resources. It also says mineral resources may still be prospected, located, developed, mined, entered, leased, or patented under the applicable laws. The range is to be known as the Cabeza Prieta Game Range, and it places management of wildlife, grazing lands, and some other lands under the officials named in the order.

8037.s: This order sets aside certain lands in Jasper and Jones Counties, Georgia, as the Piedmont Wildlife Refuge for the Department of Agriculture. It is for birds and other wildlife, and private lands in the area can become part of the refuge if the United States gets title or control of them. The order makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

8036.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations of the United States. It cancels several listed sections of those regulations and revokes several earlier executive orders. It affects the Foreign Service rules covered by those sections and orders.

8035.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules for certain classified positions in the Ordnance Department at Large and the Chemical Warfare Service at Edgewood Arsenal, Maryland. It allows unskilled laborers from the unclassified laborer register to advance by noncompetitive examination to those classified positions, subject to Civil Service Commission approval. It does not give those promoted employees classified status or make them eligible for transfer to classified jobs in other parts of the Federal service.

8033.s: This order changes who serves on the Alley Dwelling Authority. It designates the Director of Planning of the National Capital Park and Planning Commission as a member in place of the Executive Officer of that commission, and it updates a prior order to match.

8034.s: This order establishes the Federal Real Estate Board with representatives from several executive departments and agencies. It asks the Treasury Department to keep a current record of all Federal real estate and asks departments and agencies to share information about real property they control, including land not being used for their own purposes. The board is to review surplus Federal real property, advise on possible new Federal property acquisitions, and study communities affected by lost tax revenue from land bought by the Federal Government.

8032.s: This order exempts Mrs. Cora M. Armstrong, a senior clerk in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending January 31, 1940.

8031.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 4130 of January 22, 1925. That earlier order had withdrawn public land for use as a fish hatchery in Oregon.

8030.s: This order transfers a described area in Saguache County, Colorado, from the Cochetopa National Forest to the Rio Grande National Forest. It says the transfer is not meant to give any public lands national-forest status they do not already have, or to remove any lands from national-forest status.

8028.s: This order changes the title of the officer who has the immediate supervision of the National Youth Administration from Executive Director to Administrator. It affects the person appointed to oversee that agency.

8029.s: This order sets document rules for aliens entering the United States. It requires nonimmigrants and immigrants to present passports and visas, with some listed exceptions for certain travel, temporary visits, children, and returning residents. It also lets certain U.S. officials issue or waive documents in some cases, and it covers aliens coming from the Canal Zone, American Samoa, and Guam.

8027.s: This order lets the Administrator of the Wage and Hour Division make initial appointments to certain listed jobs in the Department of Labor without following the competitive Civil Service Rules. It applies to positions such as section chiefs, regional directors, territorial representatives, and special assistants. People appointed this way do not get competitive classified civil-service status just from these appointments.

8026.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations under another executive order. It also delays other related provisions of that order until June 30, 1939. The delay applies to the function of disbursement now exercised by United States Marshals under the Department of Justice.

8024.s: This order exempts Percy A. Baker from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him in his job as superintendent of buildings and grounds at Ellis Island in the Immigration and Naturalization Service.

8025.s: This order exempts Cloyd A. McIlvaine, Executive Secretary of The Panama Canal, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and delays his automatic separation from service until February 29, 1940.

8022.s: This order closed certain federal offices in the District of Columbia all day on December 24, 1938, and December 31, 1938. It also excused federal employees in the District of Columbia and in the field service of executive departments and other government agencies from duty on those days, except for workers excluded for special public reasons or where absence would conflict with existing law.

8023.s: This order changes a 1927 order that had withdrawn public lands in Alaska for town-site purposes. It allows the entry of the part of that land that has been subdivided for town-site purposes, on behalf of settlers, under the cited law.

8021.s: The order revokes an earlier withdrawal for a tract of public land in Wyoming and then sets that land aside for use by the Forest Service as a fire-lookout station. It bars settlement, location, sale, or entry on the tract, subject to valid existing rights. The withdrawal stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

8020.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It does this for flood-control purposes connected to the Tanana River and Chena Slough flood-control project under War Department supervision. It affects the public lands in the areas described in the order.

8019.s: This order exempts George M. Lewis, a clerk in the Office of the Collector of Taxes for the Government of the District of Columbia, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending December 31, 1939.

8017.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6672, which had withdrawn public lands in Wyoming pending a resurvey. It becomes effective when the official plat of the resurvey of the lands involved is filed.

8018.s: This order changes how currency-appreciation losses are figured for disbursing officers of the Navy and Marine Corps, except naval attaches. It says the amount will be based on the disbursing officer’s average cost rate. It also makes this rule retroactive to April 1, 1934, for certain prior credits, and says no loss will be payable if the foreign currency has fallen to or below the basic rate when payment becomes due.

8015.s: This order corrects the land description for the Union Slough Migratory Waterfowl Refuge in Iowa. It changes the legal description of the lands reserved for that refuge. It affects the listed parcels of land in the specified townships and ranges.

8016.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by adding rules for negotiating, signing, and ratifying treaties. It says when diplomatic agents may negotiate treaties, how treaty texts and signatures should be arranged, and how ratifications should be exchanged and reported. It also cancels Sections IX-1 to IX-7 of Part I of the regulations.

8014.s: This order removes certain lands in Alaska from military use and places them under the control of the Secretary of the Interior. It applies to tracts at the Circle, Hot Springs, Fort St. Michael, and Iditarod Military Reservations. It also revokes earlier orders that had reserved those lands for military purposes.

8013.s: This order adds about 573.60 acres in Day County, South Dakota, to the Waubay Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. The land is reserved for the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands in the area will become part of the refuge when the United States gets title or control of them.

8011.s: This order exempts Arthur H. Chase, a senior ordnance engineer in the Navy Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending November 30, 1939.

8012.s: This order allows Miss Sarah Wilson Reed to be appointed to a classified position in the Navy Department without meeting the usual Civil Service Rules requirements. It says she is the daughter of Clyde Reed, who retired from the Navy Department because of permanent and total disability, and that the order was issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Navy.

8010.s: This order revokes an earlier temporary withdrawal for certain public lands in California near Cache Creek and sets them aside as reservoir sites. It applies to the listed tracts, totaling 3,039 acres, and keeps the lands closed to settlement, location, sale, or entry unless the President or Congress revokes the reservation.

8008.s: This order changes the name of the Big Lake Reservation in Arkansas to the Big Lake Migratory Bird Refuge. It also adds certain lands that the United States has acquired to the refuge, subject to valid existing rights. The order says the added area is 442.27 acres, more or less.

8009.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California, Idaho, Oregon, and Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use, subject to valid existing rights. The order lists the specific land parcels in each state.

8006.s: This order lets the Special Joint Congressional Committee investigating the Tennessee Valley Authority inspect certain income and excess-profits tax returns. The returns covered are for taxable years from 1925 through 1937 and must be inspected under Treasury rules.

8007.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules to cover temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers for part-time or intermittent work in the Postal Service. The work is for holiday or seasonal business during the stated period.

8005.s: This order makes certain tax returns open to inspection under rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury. It applies to income, excess-profits, and capital stock tax returns, estate and gift tax returns filed after June 16, 1933, and returns under Title IX of the Social Security Act. It also covers returns made under the listed revenue laws and their amendments.

8004.s: This order withdraws a public land area in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, or other appropriation. It reserves the land for the exclusive use of the Navy Department for naval purposes. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

8002.s: This order exempts Harry Peale, an architect in the Office of the Quartermaster General, War Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for six months and ends July 31, 1939.

8003.s: This order revokes parts of earlier executive orders that created Public Water Reserves Nos. 12, 24, and 114. The revocation applies only to the listed lands in Wyoming, Arizona, and California. It affects the specific land sections named in the order.

8001.s: This order transfers certain lands in Putnam County, Florida, from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Department of Commerce, Bureau of Fisheries. It reserves the lands, together with any improvements on them, for use as a fish hatchery. The reservation is to be known as the Welaka Fish Hatchery.

8000.s: This order corrects and updates the boundaries of the Molokai Lighthouse Reservation in Hawaii. It adds a strip of land for lighthouse purposes and includes a portion of the lighthouse plot that the Territory of Hawaii needs for landing field purposes. It also gives United States Lighthouse Service agents a right of way over certain roadways, and allows Territory of Hawaii agents to enter the premises and use the Government Survey Triangulation Station "Kalawao".

7998.s: This order establishes the Interdepartmental Committee on Printing and Processing. It includes representatives from several federal departments and agencies, each chosen by the head of that department or agency. The committee is to make rules for uniform policies and procedures for the efficient and economical use of printing and processing in the executive branch.

7997.s: This order exempts Andrew M. Smith from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him as Assistant Chief of the Division of Bookkeeping and Warrants at the Treasury Department.

7996.s: This order exempts Wallace Streater, a senior attorney in the Bureau of Internal Revenue, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him and delays his automatic separation from service until November 30, 1939.

7995.s: This order exempts William S. Garland, a civil engineer in the Navy Department’s Bureau of Aeronautics, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on January 31, 1940.

7994.s: This order changes the Okefenokee Wildlife Refuge in Georgia by removing certain lands from it. The lands excluded are listed in Ware County, Georgia, in the 8th and 9th districts.

7999.s: The order transfers the records, files, equipment, and other property of the Office of the Administrator of the Census of Partial Employment, Unemployment and Occupations to the Secretary of Commerce. It also says four employees who served with merit may be appointed to classified civil service positions without the usual competitive requirements, if they establish the needed qualifications before the Civil Service Commission.

7993.s: The order withdraws certain islands and parts of islands in the Gulf of Mexico in Florida from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets them aside as a refuge and breeding ground for great white herons, other migratory birds, and other wildlife. Public lands in the area become part of the refuge when private rights end, and private lands become part of it when the United States acquires title or control. The order also replaces earlier withdrawals for the covered lands.

7992.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 3674 from 1922. That earlier order had withdrawn lands in Wyoming for the use and occupancy of the DuBois Rifle Club for rifle practice.

7991.s: This order exempts P. Julian Latham, a principal civil engineer in the United States Coast Guard, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and affects only him.

7990.s: This order names Aubrey Williams, Deputy Administrator of the Works Progress Administration, as a member of the Interdepartmental Committee to Coordinate Health and Welfare Activities. It also changes the earlier order that listed the committee’s members.

7989.s: This order exempts Francis T. Leahy, a deputy collector of customs in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and ends on October 31, 1939.

7987.s: This order names Dr. Thomas Parran, the Surgeon General of the United States Public Health Service, as a member of the Interdepartmental Committee to Coordinate Health and Welfare Activities. It also changes an earlier executive order that had named the committee members.

7988.s: This order exempts Miss Ada Tanner, a junior administrative assistant in the Office of the Treasurer of the United States, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on October 31, 1939.

7986.s: This order transfers certain national-forest lands in Idaho from the Lemhi National Forest to the Salmon National Forest and the Challis National Forest. It also transfers some lands from the Targhee National Forest to the Salmon National Forest. The order says it is not meant to give national-forest status to public lands that did not already have it, or to remove that status from public lands.

7985.s: This order reserves the airspace over certain areas in Maryland for national-defense purposes. The areas include Aberdeen Proving Ground, parts of Fort Hoyle and Edgewood Arsenal Military Reservations, and parts of Bush River, Gunpowder River, and Chesapeake Bay. When two named sections are not being used or needed for national-defense purposes, they may be released for civil aircraft crossings by agreement. People who fly aircraft in the reserved airspace in violation of the order or the Air Commerce Act of 1926 are subject to penalties.

7984.s: This order extends the trust periods for Indian lands, whether tribal or individual, that would otherwise expire during calendar year 1939. The extension lasts for 25 more years from the date the trust would have expired. It does not apply to any case where Congress has specifically kept the power to extend the trust period.

7983.s: This order sets apart certain United States-owned lands on Breton Island, Freemason Islands, Old Harbor Islands, Errol Island, and part of the Chandeleur Islands off the coast of Louisiana. It makes them a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife under the Department of Agriculture. The order also keeps valid existing rights, allows oil and gas recovery on the island areas, and revokes earlier executive orders for some of these islands.

7981.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to allow certain classified positions in the Ordnance Department at Large, War Department, to be filled by promoting unclassified laborers, with approval from the Civil Service Commission. It says unskilled laborers on the unclassified laborer register may advance to those classified positions after a noncompetitive examination. It also says this promotion does not give them classified status or make them eligible for transfer to classified positions in other parts of the Federal service.

7982.s: This order exempts Herman G. A. Brauer, a senior commercial policy analyst at the United States Tariff Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and applies only to him.

7980.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations under Executive Order No. 6166. It also delays other related provisions for the function of disbursement now carried out by United States Marshals under the Department of Justice until December 31, 1938.

7978.s: This order exempts George Middleton, a senior commodity specialist at the United States Tariff Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending September 30, 1939.

7979.s: This order sets apart a tract of land in the Canal Zone as a military reservation called Cerro Pelado Ammunition Depot Military Reservation. It places the area under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of War. The reservation covers 278.6 acres, and the land stays subject to the civil jurisdiction of the Canal Zone Government.

7977.s: This order adds land and water in Wakulla County, Florida to the St. Marks Migratory Bird Refuge. It also says private land in the area becomes part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to it. The order makes it unlawful for anyone to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals in the refuge, or to enter there except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

7975-A.s: This order names several independent establishments and agencies that must follow section 6 of Executive Order No. 7916. It applies to the Civil Aeronautics Authority, Civil Service Commission, Farm Credit Administration, General Accounting Office, Government Printing Office, Interstate Commerce Commission, The Panama Canal, Railroad Retirement Board, Securities and Exchange Commission, Social Security Board, United States Housing Authority, United States Maritime Commission, and Veterans' Administration.

7976.s: This order sets aside about 1,334.61 acres in Kossuth County, Iowa, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also says that any private land in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to it. The reservation is called the Union Slough Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7975.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands in New Mexico from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps any jurisdiction needed to finish acquiring lands now in process of acquisition. The Secretary of the Interior is authorized to administer the lands through the Commissioner of Indian Affairs for the benefit of Indians he designates, under conditions that fit the land-conservation and land-utilization program.

7973.s: This order exempts Joseph H. Wheat, a topographic engineer in the Geological Survey, from compulsory retirement for age. It applies to him for one year, ending September 30, 1939.

7972.s: This order sets rules for paying losses to officers, enlisted men, and other employees of the United States serving in foreign countries when foreign currencies rise in value against the American dollar. It explains how to figure those losses, when different rates apply, and how payment may be made in foreign currency or United States currency. It also lists basic exchange rates for many countries and directs the Secretary of State to review those rates each year and submit needed changes for approval.

7974.s: This order exempts Alfred R. Gould from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to Gould, an artistic operator of a geometric lathe in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing at the Treasury Department.

7971.s: This order sets aside about 7,500 acres in Seneca County, New York, as the Montezuma Migratory Bird Refuge. It gives the land to the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Private lands in the area become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control of them.

7970.s: This order sets the grades and ratings for enlisted men in the Regular Army for fiscal year 1939. It also limits how many enlisted men may serve in each grade and in each specialist rating. The number in the lowest grade is set so the total does not exceed the Army pay strength covered by the Military Appropriation Act, 1939.

7968.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations by adding new rules for Foreign Service accounts, collections, and fees. It requires officers to keep separate records, render monthly accounts, report when there are no transactions, and follow rules for handling public money, deposits, and special accounts. It also sets out fee rules for diplomatic and consular services, including passports, visas, certificates, and other official services.

7969.s: This order revokes part of a 1920 executive order that created Power Site Reserve No. 730. It applies to the listed lands in Oregon under the Willamette Meridian.

7967.s: This order reserves certain lands in Edmunds, Washington County, Maine, as an addition to the Moosehorn Migratory Bird Refuge. Private lands in the area would become part of the refuge when the United States acquires title or control. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there, or to enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

7966.s: The order sets aside certain lands in Lyon and Trigg Counties, Kentucky, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and other wildlife. Private lands in the area become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control. It is unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or wild animals there, or to enter except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

7965.s: This order approves regulations to carry out a U.S.-Mexico agreement on stolen or embezzled motor vehicles, trailers, airplanes, and their parts. It sets out the papers needed when either country asks for the detention and return of that property. It affects the United States and the United Mexican States, and people claiming the property.

7963.s: This order allows the Administrator of the Wage and Hour Division to make initial appointments to certain named executive positions in the Department of Labor without following the competitive civil service rules. The appointments are still subject to the Civil Service Commission finding the required qualifications in each case. People appointed under this order do not gain competitive classified civil service status from the appointment.

7962.s: This order amends a prior executive order to let the Secretary of the Treasury award the Distinguished Flying Cross to Lieutenant Richard L. Burke of the United States Coast Guard. It makes that award possible even though the time limits in the earlier order would normally apply.

7960.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal for certain public lands in Montana along the Tongue River. It then withdraws those lands from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves them for reservoir sites. The reservation stays in place until the President or Congress revokes it.

7959.s: This order transfers certain officers and employees from the Department of Commerce and the Interstate Commerce Commission to the Civil Aeronautics Authority. It also transfers unexpended appropriations, along with the related obligations, to that Authority. In addition, it transfers real and personal property, including official records, that had been used for the air commerce and airmail duties described in the order.

7961.s: This order revokes part of a 1914 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Alaska for townsite purposes. It covers specific land in the Seward Meridian described in the order. The vacant, unreserved public lands in the released area are open to qualified ex-service men under Alaska homestead laws for ninety-one days beginning on the sixty-third day after the order, and after that they are open to the general public under applicable public land laws.

7958.s: This order exempts Samuel J. Gompers, Chief Clerk in the Department of Labor, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends September 30, 1939.

7957.s: This order sets aside 138.51 acres in Tillamook County, Oregon for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also revokes an earlier public lands reservation for those same lands, because they were declared surplus to the Department of Commerce's needs. The area is to be known as the Cape Meares Migratory Bird Refuge.

7956.s: This order allows appointments to certain government positions to be made without following the Civil Service Rules. It applies to departments, independent establishments, and agencies whose pay comes from funds allotted by the Federal Emergency Administrator of Public Works under the Public Works Administration Appropriation Act of 1938, or from earlier appropriations still available for similar allotments. It lasts until February 1, 1939.

7954.s: This order exempts Frank S. Smith, a special agent of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending September 30, 1939.

7955.s: This order changes a prior rule about paying losses to U.S. officers, enlisted men, and employees in foreign countries when foreign currency rises against the American dollar. It removes Austria and the schilling from the list, and says losses for employees in the former state of Austria will be figured using the basic rate for the German reichsmark starting September 1, 1938.

7953.s: This order sets aside lands and waters in Lake and Obion Counties, Tennessee, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Any private land in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control of it. The refuge is called the Lake Isom Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7952.s: This order revokes a 1930 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Arizona pending a resurvey. It applies to the remaining lands covered by that earlier order and takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7951.s: The order revokes a prior withdrawal for a 20-acre tract of public land in Arkansas. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for use by the State of Arkansas as a site for a forest-fire lookout tower.

7950.s: This order exempts William H. Egberts from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to his work as chief preparator in anthropology in the United States National Museum, Smithsonian Institution.

7949.s: This order exempts Stephen W. Hamilton, a deputy collector of customs in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him and extends his service until August 31, 1939.

7948.s: This order exempts Charles L. Parker, a Deputy Marshal for the Canal Zone, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending August 31, 1939.

7946.s: This order limits the amount of red cedar shingles that may be imported from Canada during the last six months of 1938. The limit is 864,881 squares. It affects imports of red cedar shingles from Canada.

7947.s: This order designates Del Bonita, Montana, as a customs port of entry. It places it in Customs Collection District No. 33, with headquarters at Great Falls, Montana. The order takes effect thirty days after the date of the order.

7945.s: This order exempts Edward M. Weeks, a letter engraver in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. It applies only to him and extends his prior exemptions through August 31, 1939.

7944.s: This order changes an earlier rule that barred federal officers and employees from holding certain state or local offices. It lets employees of the Division of Grazing, with approval from the Secretary of the Interior, accept appointments as deputy fire wardens and deputy fish and game wardens under state law. Their service in those roles must be unpaid and must not interfere with their federal duties.

7942.s: This order lets certain examiner and expert positions in the Department of Justice, Treasury, Labor, Commerce, the Securities and Exchange Commission, and the Federal Trade Commission be filled without following Civil Service Rules. It applies to jobs needed to carry out their work under Public Resolution No. 113, and the pay for these positions comes from funds allocated to those departments and commissions.

7940.s: This order transfers certain land in the Coronado National Forest to the Secretary of the Treasury. The land is to be used for a customs-immigration inspection station, and any valid existing rights remain in place. If the land stops being used for that purpose, it will go back to being part of the Coronado National Forest.

7941.s: This order reserves land on Gardiners Island in Suffolk County, New York, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The area is called the Fort Tyler Migratory Bird Refuge. The land had been declared surplus by the War Department, and the Director of Procurement may dispose of it under the law named in the order.

7939.s: This order revokes part of a prior order that withdrew public lands in Wyoming pending a resurvey. It applies to the listed townships in the Sixth Principal Meridian. The change becomes effective when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7938.s: This order corrects the land description in a 1921 order that withdrew public land for the Warm Springs Bay Lighthouse Reserve in Alaska. It says the correction must match Alaska Survey No. 1649 and is subject to valid existing rights. The land involved is 9.97 acres.

7937.s: This order sets apart part of West Sister Island in Ohio for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It says this reservation is subject to valid existing rights. The Bureau of Lighthouses may still go across the island and use any landing wharf to tend and maintain aids to navigation. It revokes an 1838 order for the parts covered by this reservation.

7936.s: This order exempts Thomas A. Jaggar, Jr., a Principal Scientist in the National Park Service, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending July 31, 1939.

7934.s: The order transfers certain custodial and maintenance employees from the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works to the United States Housing Authority. It applies to employees in the field service who were on duty on November 1, 1937, had substantially continuous duty, and were certified as having worked on housing or slum-clearance projects. The order says these employees do not automatically get competitive civil service status, though some may become eligible if they meet the stated pay limit and civil service rule.

7935.s: This order exempts J. Humbird Smith, a market master in the Department of Weights, Measures and Markets of the Government of the District of Columbia, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year.

7933-A.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, and capital stock tax returns open to inspection by the Special Committee on Un-American Activities of the House of Representatives, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The returns covered are for 1932 and later taxable years through the fiscal year ending November 30, 1938. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

7932.s: This order exempts Ulysses S. Shewmaker from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It affects him as an administrative assistant in the Treasury Department and delays his automatic separation from service until September 30, 1939.

7931.s: This order exempts Marion C. Hargrove, a purchasing officer for the Government of the District of Columbia, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on November 30, 1939.

7930.s: This order further exempts William H. Griffin, a senior engineer in the Geological Survey at the Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one more year, ending July 31, 1939.

7929.s: This order exempts Ernest P. Rands, a technical adviser in the General Land Office, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending July 31, 1939.

7928.s: This order designates St. Petersburg, Florida, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 18, which has headquarters at Tampa, Florida. It takes effect thirty days after July 14, 1938.

7925.s: The order withdraws about 5.60 acres of public land in Alfalfa County, Oklahoma from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets the land aside for the Department of Agriculture as an addition to the Salt Plains Wildlife Refuge. It also revokes a prior order for this land.

7926.s: The order sets aside certain U.S.-owned or controlled lands in Limestone, Madison, and Morgan Counties, Alabama, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wild life. It says the lands are subject to existing valid rights and the Tennessee Valley Authority’s use of the area. The reservation is to be known as the Wheeler Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7923.s: This order sets apart federal lands within and around Ruby Lake in Nevada as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It applies to lands owned or controlled by the United States in the described area, and private lands can become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease. The reservation is to be known as the Ruby Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7924.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn public lands in Alaska pending legislation. It opens certain vacant, unreserved public lands to entry under Alaska homestead laws for qualified ex-service men for a limited period, subject to the stated terms and conditions. After that period, the lands are to be subject to appropriation by the general public under applicable public-land laws.

7922.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Treasury to assemble a Coast Guard Personnel Board every year. It applies to the Secretary of the Treasury and the Coast Guard personnel board process.

7921.s: This order extends the existence of the Quetico-Superior Committee for four more years, from June 30, 1938 to June 30, 1942. It affects the committee created by Executive Order No. 6783.

7919.s: This order allows Mrs. Eleanor J. Townsend to be appointed to a classified position in the Securities and Exchange Commission. Her appointment may be made without following the Civil Service rules.

7917.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations under Executive Order No. 6166. It also delays related rules for disbursement work done by United States Marshals under the Department of Justice, by officers and employees of the United States in foreign countries, and by Postal Service officers and employees. The delays last until September 30, 1938, for some functions and until June 30, 1939, for Postal Service disbursement work.

7918.s: This order revokes part of an earlier order that had excepted certain initial appointments in the Bureau of Motor Carriers, Interstate Commerce Commission, from competitive civil service requirements. It applies to the remaining initial appointments that had not yet been made.

7916.s: This order brings most Executive civil service jobs, including jobs in U.S.-owned or U.S.-controlled corporations, into the competitive classified civil service unless they are policy-determining, specially exempted, or filled by Senate-confirmed appointment. It also sets rules for current workers in those jobs to gain classified status, or be separated if they do not qualify. The order requires departments to set up personnel supervision offices, creates a Council of Personnel Administration, and revokes Executive Order No. 5612.

7914.s: This order exempts David A. Brodie, the farm superintendent at St. Elizabeths Hospital, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, ending July 31, 1939.

7915.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules for federal jobs, with the changes set to take effect on February 1, 1939. It bars executive civil service workers from using their authority to affect elections and stops questions or discrimination based on political or religious opinions. It also sets rules for who is in the classified service, when examinations are required, and who may be appointed or removed from federal positions.

7913.s: This order lets certain employees of the General Accounting Office keep working past June 30, 1938. Their service may continue, but not beyond June 30, 1939.

7912.s: This order exempts John H. Thomas from compulsory retirement for age for one more year, until September 30, 1939. It applies to Thomas, who served as Assistant Solicitor and a member of the Board of Appeals in the Department of the Interior.

7909.s: This order ends all powers, rights, and duties of the Special Mexican Claims Commission. It says the Commission has completed its work before the time set for it to finish.

7911.s: This order transfers title to two parcels of public land in the Territory of Hawaii. The land is at Kaalawai, Kapahulu, in the District of Honolulu on the Island of Oahu. The order says the land is needed to build a causeway so people can have a safe way to travel along the coast where the land is located.

7907.s: This order sets aside certain lands and waters in Princess Anne County, Virginia, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Private lands in the area become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to them or leases them. The reservation is named the Back Bay Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7908.s: This order transfers the United States’ right, title, and interest in certain lands to the Secretary of Agriculture. The lands are to be used, managed, and disposed of under Title III of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act and related Title IV provisions. It does not apply to lands in national forests or certain wildlife, waterfowl, migratory bird, or research refuges, and it limits sale, exchange, or grant of some reserved lands without approval from the Secretary of the Interior.

7906.s: This order changes a previous order that abolished the National Emergency Council. It extends the date for abolishing the Council and transferring its funds, records, and property to June 30, 1939, unless the President abolishes it sooner. It affects the National Emergency Council and its funds, records, and property.

7905.s: This order allows Mrs. Lucile Ensminger to be appointed to a classified position in the Navy Department without following the Civil Service Rules. It says she is the widow of Charles Lee Ensminger, who died in the line of duty on December 13, 1937. The order was issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Navy.

7903.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands in Rhode Island from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior. It also authorizes the Secretary of the Interior, through the National Park Service, to administer the lands as part of the Beach Pond Project, with some parcels, burial lots, highways, and rights of way excepted.

7904.s: This order exempts Charles H. Hastings from the rule requiring automatic retirement at age. It lets him continue in service until December 1, 1938.

7902.s: This order sets aside lands and waters in Becker County, Minnesota, as the Tamarac Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. It reserves the area for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Private lands in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease. It also says the order does not change the status of tribal Indian lands in the White Earth Indian Reservation.

7901.s: This order authorizes the Attorney General to sell certain property held under the Trading with the Enemy Act on public exchanges without giving prior advertisement. The property includes shares of stock, bonds, notes, and other beneficial interests listed on public exchanges. It applies to sales to any individual, corporation, partnership, or association, on terms and in amounts the Attorney General decides.

7900.s: This order authorizes John Monroe Johnson, an Assistant Secretary of Commerce, to do the duties of the Secretary of Commerce when the Secretary is absent or sick. It also authorizes Richard C. Patterson, Jr., to do those duties if both the Secretary and Johnson are absent or sick.

7899.s: This order allows Miss Amy G. Maher to be appointed as a technical adviser in the Social Security Board without following the civil service rules. It affects that appointment and the Social Security Board.

7898.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from use under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands so they can be added to Yosemite National Park once all privately owned land in the area has been turned over to the United States. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

7896.s: This order changes an earlier rule that had barred certain federal officers and employees from holding local government jobs. It allows officers or employees of the Police or Prison Departments of the territorial and municipal governments of the Virgin Islands to be appointed as deputies or other employees in the office of the United States Marshal for the Virgin Islands.

7897.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn public lands in Colorado pending a resurvey. It applies to the townships in the New Mexico Principal Meridian listed in the order. It takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7895.s: This order adds private lands that the United States has acquired or leased since the Hart Mountain Antelope Refuge was established to the refuge. It also says any private lands later acquired or leased within that area will become part of the refuge.

7894.s: This order gives the Attorney General the President’s powers under section 12 of the Trading With the Enemy Act. It affects the Attorney General and concerns the powers given to the President by that law.

7892.s: This order exempts Dr. George F. Bowerman from the rule that requires some civilian employees to leave service when they reach retirement age. It lets him stay in service as Librarian of the Free Public Library of the District of Columbia until October 1, 1939.

7891.s: This order restores certain lands of the Hawaii Agricultural Experiment Station to the Government of the Territory of Hawaii for highway purposes. The lands are within the limits of a realigned right-of-way in Honolulu. It affects land under the control of the United States Department of Agriculture and the Territory of Hawaii.

7890.s: This order exempts Stanley Searles from the rule that would require civilian federal workers to leave service at the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until July 1, 1939.

7893.s: The order restores the Upolu Point Military Reservation in the Territory of Hawaii to the territory for aeronautical purposes. It says the land must still be available at all times, without charge, for the takeoff and landing of airplanes and airships of the United States, and for temporary occupation and maintenance when needed by military authority. It also reserves another parcel of land on the island of Hawaii for military purposes.

7889.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 7520, which had withdrawn lands for use as a target range for the War Department and the Arizona National Guard. It affects those lands and their use for that target range.

7888.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be classified while a decision is made about whether to reserve them for national monument purposes. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

7887.s: This order extends the Civil Service Retirement Act to certain federal employees who are appointed without competitive examination under section 10 of Civil Service Rule II. It applies only to those who are citizens of the United States and does not cover employees whose work is intermittent or paid on a per diem when-actually-employed basis.

7886.s: This order revokes part of one 1924 executive order and part of a 1928 executive order that had withdrawn public lands in New Mexico pending a resurvey. It applies to the lands in Townships 7 and 8 South, Range 5 West, in the New Mexico Principal Meridian. The order takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7884.s: This order removes the Toiyabe Division of the Nevada National Forest and the Santa Rosa Division of the Humboldt National Forest from those forests. It then reestablishes them as the Toiyabe National Forest and says they will be designated and administered under that name.
