7885.s: This order places Block 27 in the Townsite of Anchorage, Alaska, under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Treasury. It is to be used as a site for Federal buildings.

7882.s: This order reserves Oyster Bed Island and nearby spoil bank land in Chatham County, Georgia, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The land stays subject to existing valid rights and to use by the Department of Commerce and the War Department for lighthouse work and river and harbor improvement. The area is named the Tybee Migratory Bird Refuge.

7883.s: This order revokes part of a prior withdrawal of public lands in California for a specific tract in Mt. Diablo Meridian. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved to provide material for the construction and maintenance of public roads and other public projects under federal agencies.

7881.s: This order revokes part of a 1916 executive order that created Power Site Reserve No. 533. It applies to the lands described in the Willamette Meridian in Washington.

7880.s: This order changes the sick leave rules for government employees who are transferred or reappointed without a break in service. It says they must be credited with accumulated sick leave and charged for sick leave advanced beyond what they had earned at the time of transfer or reappointment. It also defines a "break in service" as separation from service for one or more work days.

7879.s: This order changes the rules for annual leave for government employees. It says an employee who is transferred or reappointed without a break in service between permanent, emergency, or indefinite jobs in a government agency will keep accumulated and current leave, or be charged for any leave advanced. It also defines a "break in service" as being separated from service for one or more work days.

7878.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules for certain Public Health Service jobs in the Treasury Department. It keeps some hospital, sanatorium, preventive medicine, and treatment or convalescence positions outside competitive civil-service rules. It also removes the position of attendant at quarantine stations from the excepted class, and current workers in that job may get civil-service status under the rules.

7877.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6814 and Executive Order No. 6895-A. It says the revocation does not affect any act done, right accrued, or suit or proceeding started before the revocation, and penalties, forfeitures, and liabilities under those orders may still be enforced.

7875.s: This order transfers a specific parcel of land in Hot Springs, New Mexico, from the Department of the Interior to the Treasury Department. The land is to be used as a site for a federal building. It also modifies an earlier order about land with hot springs or springs with curative properties so this transfer can take effect.

7874.s: This order waives Civil Service Rule IX time limits so Mrs. Jessie Scott Arnold can be reinstated to a classified position in the Federal Trade Commission. It says she has served in the War Department and the Federal Trade Commission, and that the order was recommended by the Federal Trade Commission.

7873.s: This order exempts Edwin C. E. Lord from a retirement rule for federal civilian workers who reach the automatic retirement age. It allows him to stay in service until June 1, 1939.

7872.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules to add some administrative or custodial jobs in the field service of the United States Housing Authority. The jobs must relate to managing or maintaining Federal low-rent housing projects, and the Civil Service Commission must think they cannot be filled well through open competitive examination. No position can be filled under this rule unless it is clearly shown to be in the best interests of the service.

7871.s: This order exempts Thomas G. Shearman from the automatic retirement rule for federal civilian service. It lets him stay in service until June 1, 1939.

7870.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 3345 of October 23, 1920. That earlier order had temporarily withdrawn public lands in Arizona for national-monument classification.

7868.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands and improvements from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior for administrative purposes. The lands are ones acquired or being acquired in connection with designated projects, and some are near existing Indian reservations. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps whatever jurisdiction is needed to finish buying lands still in process of acquisition. The Secretary of the Interior is authorized to administer the lands through the Commissioner of Indian Affairs and to make rules needed to carry out the order.

7869.s: This order allows the Special Committee to Investigate Lobbying Activities of the United States Senate, or an authorized subcommittee, to inspect certain income, excess-profits, and capital stock tax returns. The inspection is for investigations of lobbying activities and any other matter or proposal affecting legislation that the committee is authorized to investigate, and it must follow Treasury rules.

7867.s: This order temporarily withdraws a described parcel of public land in Claiborne Parish, Louisiana from settlement, location, sale, and entry. It reserves the land for use by the Department of Agriculture for reforestation, forestation, soil erosion control, and other land use activities connected to the Claiborne Parish Project. It also says mineral activities on the land are not restricted under the applicable laws.

7866.s: The order revokes part of a previous withdrawal for a specific piece of public land in Washington County, Arkansas. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, and entry and sets it aside for use by the Department of Agriculture. The land is to be used for reforestation, forestation, soil erosion control, and other land use activities tied to the Northwest Arkansas Project. Mineral prospecting, mining, leasing, and patenting are still allowed under the law.

7865.s: This order sets document rules for aliens entering the United States, including non-immigrants and immigrants. It says they generally must have unexpired passports and the proper visas or travel documents, with some listed exceptions and waiver cases. It also lets certain officials in the Canal Zone, American Samoa, and Guam issue these documents, and it authorizes the Secretary of State and Secretary of Labor to make needed rules.

7864.s: This order sets aside federal land in Dare County, North Carolina, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Private land in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires or leases it. Land used as Coast Guard stations stays under the Treasury Department’s primary jurisdiction and can still be used for Coast Guard purposes.

7863.s: This order exempts Frank B. Bourn from the rule that would require his automatic retirement when he reaches the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until July 1, 1939. It affects Bourn and the War Department position he held.

7862.s: This order changes the name of the naval reservation in the Canal Zone to "Naval Radio Station, Balboa, Canal Zone." It assigns the area to use as a naval radio station and to other naval uses the Secretary of the Navy may determine.

7861.s: This order exempts Clarence E. Aiderman from the rule that would require certain government workers to retire at the set age. It lets him stay in service until June 1, 1939. The order applies only to him.

7859.s: This order exempts Edward M. Kennard from the rule that requires some federal civilian employees to retire at the set age. It lets him stay in service until May 1, 1939. It affects Kennard, who worked in the Department of Justice.

7860.s: This order revokes an earlier reservation of the named land for military purposes. It temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry, and reserves it for the use of the War Department for river and harbor purposes. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

7858.s: This order authorizes the Attorney General to reject all bids made at a public auction in Savannah, Georgia, for two pieces of real estate. The bids included bids made by Jake Fine. It applies to the property at Jones and Whitaker Streets and the property at 413 E. 36th Street.

7857.s: This order transfers two parcels of land in San Juan, Puerto Rico, from the United States to the people of Puerto Rico. The land was described as no longer needed for the purposes of the United States and had been under the control of the Treasury Department and the Department of the Navy. The order applies to the lands within the municipality of San Juan, Puerto Rico.

7856.s: This order says only the Secretary of State may grant and issue passports in the United States. It says passports may be issued only to people who owe allegiance to the United States, and it gives rules for minors and for family members who may be included on one passport. It also requires passport applicants to file a written application with personal details, a photo, an oath of allegiance, and supporting witness information.

7855.s: This order revokes a prior 1929 order that had temporarily withdrawn certain public lands in Colorado for classification and in aid of proposed legislation. It applies to the listed lands under the Sixth Principal Meridian, totaling 4,320 acres.

7854.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6055 of February 28, 1933, which had withdrawn public lands in Colorado while a resurvey was pending. It becomes effective when the official plat of the resurvey of those lands is filed.

7852.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules to list seaman, deck-hand, fireman, and mess department employees on vessels, as well as lamplighters in the Lighthouse Service. It also says the people already holding those jobs may get competitive classified civil service status under Civil Service Rule 37.

7853.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules to list certain Bureau of Air Commerce jobs outside the competitive civil service. It covers the Director of Air Commerce, two Assistant Directors of Air Commerce, and up to ten consulting aeronautical experts in certain fields. Employees in Bureau of Air Commerce jobs covered by this change may get competitive classified status under Civil Service Rule II.

7851.s: This order names Charles V. McLaughlin, the Assistant Secretary of Labor, as a member of the Interdepartmental Committee to Coordinate Health and Welfare Activities. It takes the place of Edward F. McGrady, who resigned, and changes the earlier committee order accordingly.

7850.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6087 of March 28, 1933, which had withdrawn public lands in Colorado pending a resurvey. It becomes effective when the official plats of the resurvey of those lands are filed.

7849.s: This order says certain tax returns may be opened for inspection under rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury. It covers income, excess profits, and capital stock tax returns, estate and gift tax returns filed after June 16, 1933, and returns under Title IX of the Social Security Act. It also applies to returns made under the listed acts as amended.

7848.s: This order names the Secretary of the Treasury as the official to receive certain capital stock from the Reconstruction Finance Corporation, the Secretary of Agriculture, and the Governor of the Farm Credit Administration. It also authorizes and directs the Secretary of the Treasury to use all rights that come with that stock on behalf of the United States.

7847.s: This order temporarily withdraws two tracts of land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for the use of the Navy Department. The order stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

7845.s: This order sets rules for annual leave for civilian officers and employees of the United States, the District of Columbia, and certain corporations covered by the law. It says who gets leave, how much leave they can earn or carry over, when leave can be used, and how leave is charged for Sundays, holidays, and part days. It also leaves out several groups, including temporary construction workers paid by the hour, some Post Office Department employees, and certain part-time or intermittent workers.

7844.s: This order exempts John G. Honey from the rule that requires certain federal civilian workers to retire at the set retirement age. It lets him stay in service until July 1, 1939.

7846.s: This order sets sick leave rules for civilian officers and employees of the United States, the District of Columbia, and certain corporations. It says sick leave with pay may be used for sickness, injury, pregnancy and confinement, or when family illness or exposure to contagious disease makes leave necessary, and it sets rules for earning, advancing, and documenting that leave. It also says the rules do not apply to several listed groups, including certain school, police, fire, postal, and temporary workers.

7842.s: This order exempts James Robertson from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service until June 1, 1939.

7841.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in Alaska from settlement, sale, entry, or other disposal. It reserves the land for use by The Alaska Railroad. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

7843.s: This order exempts William J. Maries, a post office inspector in the Post Office Department, from the retirement rule for automatic separation because of age. It lets him stay in the service until April 1, 1939.

7839.s: This order revokes part of a prior order for two housing or slum-clearance projects in Puerto Rico, one in San Juan and one in Caguas. It transfers the projects, along with related assets, contracts, records, funds, and certain employees, from the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works to the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration. The Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration is to supervise, control, and administer the projects and the transferred property and funds.

7840.s: This order extends the limits of the customs port of entry of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. It adds Brooklawn, West Deptford, National Park, Paulsboro, Greenwich, and Tinicum to that customs area. The order becomes effective thirty days from the date it was signed.

7838.s:
This order creates a revolving supply fund for the Works Progress Administration, with a limit of $25,000,000. The fund can be used to buy, repair, distribute, and rent materials, supplies, equipment, and tools for Works Progress Administration projects, including projects of the National Youth Administration.

It also sets rules for reimbursing the fund for items used on approved projects and for charging the fund for items no longer needed to finish a project. The Administrator must report the remaining inventory and any balance left when the fund is closed must go back to the appropriation under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1937.

7836.s: This order revokes parts of earlier orders that created Public Water Reserves Nos. 77, 82, 85, and 12. It applies only to the listed lands in New Mexico and Wyoming.

7837.s: This order sets rules for cash relief for people covered by the July 8, 1937 act. Applicants must file for relief in a form set by the Governor of The Panama Canal and provide proof of eligibility, service, and economic status. The monthly amount is based on years of service, cannot be more than $25, and may be changed by the Governor. Payments start after the employee leaves Panama Canal service and are made monthly or more often as the Governor allows.

7834.s: This order exempts Charles W. Franks from the rule that requires some government workers to retire at the automatic retirement age. It lets him stay in service until September 1, 1940.

7833.s: The order sets aside about 1,200 acres of federal land in Phillips County, Montana, for the Department of Agriculture. It makes the area a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife, subject to valid existing rights. It also says the order does not change how the oil and gas deposits in the area are handled under the mineral leasing law.

7835.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn and reserved public lands in Alaska for townsite purposes. It says those lands will be open to qualified ex-service men under the homestead laws for Alaska for a set period beginning on the sixty-third day after the order, and then they will be open to the general public under applicable public land laws.

7832.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5923, which had withdrawn public lands in Oregon while a resurvey was pending. The revocation takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey of those lands is filed.

7831.s: This order changes a prior rule on allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men who are not given quarters or rations in kind. It expands one listed exception to include Naval Missions to Brazil and Peru, affecting enlisted men in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Survey, and Public Health Service.

7829.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5428 of August 20, 1930. That earlier order had temporarily withdrawn and reserved certain land in Montana for classification and in aid of legislation.

7830.s: This order revokes part of a 1930 order that had withdrawn public lands in Arizona while a resurvey was pending. It applies to one township in the Gila and Salt River Meridian. The order takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey for that township is filed.

7827.s: This order allows Thomas D. Quinn to be appointed as Administrative Assistant to the Attorney General in the Department of Justice. It removes that position from the Civil Service Rules requirements for this appointment.

7828.s: This order reserves Canton Island and Enderbury Island and places them under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Interior for administrative purposes. It affects those two islands and gives the Secretary of the Interior authority over them for administration.

7826.s: This order amends the consular regulations on when American seamen may be discharged in a foreign port by consular officers upon payment of wages. It adds a new case for vessels that are wrecked, destroyed, lost, stranded, or condemned as unfit for service.

7824.s: This order exempts Louis A. Simon from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in federal service until June 1, 1939. Simon is identified as the supervising architect of the Public Buildings Branch of the Procurement Division in the Treasury Department.

7825.s: This order exempts Harry H. Little from the rule that required his automatic retirement for age. It lets him stay in service until April 1, 1939.

7822.s: This order limits the amount of red cedar shingles imported from Canada that may be entered during the first six months of 1938. It sets that limit at 916,246 squares. It affects importers of red cedar shingles from Canada.

7821.s: This executive order designates Emory S. Land as Chairman of the United States Maritime Commission. It affects the person named in the order and the Commission.

7819.s: This order exempts George W. Patterson from the compulsory retirement rule for civilian federal workers. It allows him to stay in service until April 1, 1939, at the U.S. Naval Powder Factory in Indian Head, Maryland.

7817.s: This order designates and authorizes Honorable Martin Travieso, an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico, to act as Judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico. He may perform the judge’s duties and sign needed papers and records when the judge is absent, ill, or otherwise legally unable to serve during the current calendar year.

7818.s: This order designates Port St. Joe, Florida, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 18, with headquarters at Tampa, Florida. It takes effect thirty days after February 17, 1938.

7816.s: This order transfers parts of Amaknak Island in Alaska to the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy for naval uses. The land may still be used by the Department of Agriculture and Alaska natives for the purposes it was originally set aside for, as long as that use does not interfere with naval activities. It also changes the earlier executive orders for that land.

7814.s: This order revokes a 1926 withdrawal order for one described piece of public land in Wisconsin. The earlier order had temporarily withdrawn certain lands in Michigan and Wisconsin pending classification and legislation.

7815.s: This order changes the civil service rules for some civilian jobs at the United States Military Academy at West Point. It keeps certain positions outside competitive civil service, but places the chapel organist and choirmaster in the classified civil service.

7812.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6179 of June 16, 1933, which had withdrawn public lands in Utah while a resurvey was pending. It affects those Utah public lands and takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7811.s: This order changes the civil service rule for appointing unclassified laborers. It says a person with unclassified competitive status, or who is eligible for that status through a competitive exam, may be reinstated to a similar Federal job if separated without delinquency or misconduct. The reinstatement is subject to a physical examination and other listed limits.

7813.s: This order changes the rule for reduced tolls on vessels in ballast without passengers or cargo. To get the reduced rate, the fuel on board for the vessel’s own use must not be more than 125 percent of the volume of its engine room, as shown on its Panama Canal Tonnage Certificate. It takes effect on March 1, 1938.

7810.s: This order revokes the 1875 executive order that established the Baird Fish Hatchery on the McCloud River in California. It affects the fish hatchery established by that earlier order.

7808.s: This order revokes part of Power-Site Reserve No. 661 in Oregon. It removes the reserve from the listed lands in the Willamette Meridian.

7809.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules for certain Public Health Service investigation stations. It removes the exception for positions at stations where workers are engaged in Rocky Mountain spotted fever work. After this change, only people employed in leprosy, yellow fever, and psittacosis investigation stations remain in the excepted class.

7807.s: This order revokes part of a 1917 executive order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 621. It applies to the described lands in the Willamette Meridian in Oregon.

7806.s: This order sets aside three parcels of land in the Canal Zone as a military reservation called Fort William D. Davis Military Reservation. It places the reservation under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of War, while civil jurisdiction stays with the Canal Zone Government. It also says military authorities may not build any structure within 200 feet of the Panama Canal banks, and The Panama Canal may use some areas for cattle pasturage when they are not needed for troops.

7805.s: This order corrects the description of the western boundary line in Executive Order No. 6897 from 1934. That earlier order transferred certain lands off the southern coast of California to the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy. The correction changes the western longitudinal limit to 118°36'30" W.

7804.s: This order reserves a part of Walkalua-Waho Beach Reserve in Kaneohe, Oahu, for the use of the Lighthouse Service in the Department of Commerce. The land is described by survey boundaries and is about 3,365 square feet. It affects the use of that public land in Hawaii.

7803.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal for a tract of public land in Washington. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for use by the Forest Service as a fire lookout station for the Chelan National Forest. The withdrawal stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

7802.s: This order exempts Nathan C. Grover from the law that would require his automatic retirement for age. It lets him stay in civilian service as chief hydraulic engineer in the Geological Survey, Department of the Interior, until February 1, 1939.

7801.s: This order reserves certain United States lands in Blaine County, Montana, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It applies to 1,160 acres, and any private land in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control of it.

7800.s: This order transfers part of military reservation No. 1 at Cuzco Hills, Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, from the control of the Secretary of War to the control of the Secretary of the Navy. It covers the land north of a specified east-west line, but it does not include the portion already transferred for a lighthouse depot or existing rights of certain telegraph and cable companies.

7799.s: This order adds lands in Bottineau and McHenry Counties, North Dakota, to the Lower Souris Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. It covers lands acquired or to be acquired by the United States, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands in the listed areas would become part of the refuge when the United States acquires title to them or leases them.

7798.s: This order transfers a described portion of the Boise Barracks Military Reservation in Idaho from the War Department to the Veterans' Administration. The land is described by boundary lines and contains about 110 acres. It affects that parcel of land and the federal agencies in control of it.

7796.s: This order changes an earlier rule that barred most federal officers and employees from holding state, territorial, or municipal offices. It lets some Department of the Interior employees hold those offices if the Secretary approves and the work is connected to Interior programs. It also lets some state, territorial, and municipal officers or employees serve in the Department of the Interior when the Secretary thinks it is needed, with civil-service rules still applying when required.

7795.s: This order sets aside the Huron Islands group in Michigan for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The reservation is subject to valid existing rights and to uses by the War Department and the Department of Commerce for quarrying stone, building breakwaters, and maintaining the Huron Island Light Station. It also revokes the 1905 order that established the Huron Islands Reservation.

7797.s: This order sets rules for how alien seamen may enter the United States. Some bona fide seamen may be admitted temporarily without passports or visas if they meet certain listed conditions and the Secretary of Labor allows it. Masters of maritime vessels sailing for a U.S. port must submit a list of alien crew members for visa, and seamen not on a visaed crew list may not land without permission from the Secretary of State, except in the Virgin Islands.

7794.s: This order corrects the land description for one parcel covered by Executive Order No. 6050 of February 27, 1933. The parcel is near Juneau, Alaska, and was part of the land placed under the control of the Secretary of War for use as a site for the Army radio receiving station at Juneau. The order changes only the legal description of that parcel.

7793.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn public lands in Colorado pending a resurvey. The revocation applies only to the described township in the Sixth Principal Meridian. It takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey for that township is filed.

7791.s: This order exempts Edward B. Russ from a retirement rule that would normally separate certain government workers when they reach the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until March 1, 1939.

7792.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands in New Mexico from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior for administrative purposes. The lands are connected to projects near existing Indian reservations and include the Zia-Santa Ana, Laguna, Acoma, Jemez, and Isleta projects. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps jurisdiction as needed to finish buying lands that are still being acquired. The Secretary of the Interior is authorized to administer the lands through the Commissioner of Indian Affairs and make rules for carrying out the order.

7789.s: This order exempts David H. Hahn from a law that would otherwise require automatic separation at retirement age. It lets him stay in civilian service in the War Department until February 1, 1939.

7790.s: This order changes a prior order and transfers certain lands in the Virgin Islands from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of the Navy for aviation facilities. It covers two land areas, including parcels "A" and "C," and says the transfer is subject to valid existing rights. Part of the land now used by the Civilian Conservation Corps Camp V-1 stays available for that use until the Secretary of the Interior says it is no longer needed. The entrance road to the Botanical Garden must stay open to the public when the garden is open, and employees must have free access on that road at all times.

7788.s: This order exempts Joseph J. McGuigan from the rule that certain Canal Zone employees must retire at age sixty-two after enough service. It lets him stay in service until May 17, 1939, and then until his successor is appointed and qualified.

7786.s: This order changes the rules for awarding the Distinguished Flying Cross. It says members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard may be eligible when they take part in an aerial flight as part of their duties. It also says the Secretaries of War, the Navy, and the Treasury will make the award for their departments and may issue extra rules for them.

7787.s: This order revokes parts of two earlier executive orders that had withdrawn land in Montana for Temporary Power-Site Withdrawal No. 20 and Power-Site Reserve No. 20. It applies to the listed lands in Principal Meridian, Township 3 North, Range 6 West, in the sections named in the order.

7784-A.s: This order changes who serves on the Alley Dwelling Authority. It designates the Architect of the Capitol as a member in place of the Director of Housing of the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works.

7785.s: This order amends an earlier rule on paying losses to officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States in foreign countries when foreign currencies rise against the American dollar. It changes the basic rate for the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics and makes the change effective as of July 1, 1937.

7784.s: This order sets aside land in Aransas and Refugio Counties, Texas, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It says the land is reserved for use by the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private land in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to it or leases it.

7783.s: This order changes an earlier land reservation so the Alaska Road Commission can use certain Talkeetna townsite lots for aviation-field purposes. It also sets apart a public land tract in Alaska for that same use. The order stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

7782.s: This order exempts Harry C. Dorsey, a filing clerk for the Municipal Court of the District of Columbia, from the compulsory retirement rule for age. It lets him stay in service until January 1, 1939.

7780.s: This order reserves about 33,400 acres in Cameron Parish, Louisiana, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It covers lands acquired or to be acquired by the United States within the described area, subject to existing valid rights. Private lands in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to them or leases them.

7781.s: This order amends a prior executive order about a tract of land in Alaska that was excluded from the Chugach National Forest and restored to entry under the public-land laws. It changes the metes-and-bounds description of that tract so it matches U.S. Survey No. 2267, Alaska.

7779.s: This order amends an earlier executive order on representation and post allowances. It adds allowance rules for Foreign Service officers detailed as inspectors when they are outside the United States, with the amounts and conditions to be set by the Secretary of State. It also renumbers one paragraph and makes the order effective immediately.

7778.s: This order lets the Civil Service Rule IX examination requirements be waived so Bernard J. Kinnahan can be appointed to a classified position in the Post Office Department. It applies to that appointment and refers to his service in the department in a position excepted from civil service requirements.

7777.s: This order exempts Charles Earle, a gardener's helper in the National Park Service, from the rule on compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service until January 1, 1939. He had already been exempted for one year by a previous executive order.

7776.s: This order changes a previous order that would have abolished the National Emergency Council on December 31, 1937. It extends the date for the council to be abolished, and for its funds, records, and property to be transferred, to June 30, 1938 unless the President ends it sooner.

7775.s: This order transfers certain land in Richmond County, North Carolina, from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of Commerce. It reserves the land for use by the Bureau of Fisheries as a fish hatchery called the McKinney Lake Fish Hatchery. The order excepts a 15-acre tract and a perpetual easement for ingress and egress.

7774.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations under Executive Order No. 6166 until June 30, 1938. It applies to provisions of that earlier order that were not already carried out by December 31, 1937. The Secretary of the Treasury, with the President’s approval, may make any of those changes effective between December 31, 1937, and June 30, 1938.

7772.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5711 of September 14, 1931. That earlier order had temporarily withdrawn and reserved certain land in Montana for classification and in aid of legislation.

7771.s: This order removes several listed homesite tracts in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It restores those lands to entry under the public-land laws. The tracts are identified as homesites on several islands and along Glacier Highway.

7773.s: This order modifies a prior Alaska land withdrawal order. It authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to issue a coal prospecting permit to Frank Colobuffalo for certain lands in Alaska.

7769.s: This order exempts Walter H. Beal from a law that would normally require certain federal civilian workers to retire at the set retirement age. It lets him stay in service until July 1, 1938.

7770.s: This order withdraws Nunivakchak and Krigegak Islands in Hazen Bay from settlement, location, sale, or entry, subject to valid existing rights. It sets them apart for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The area is to be known as the Hazen Bay Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7768.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6124, which had withdrawn public lands in Colorado pending a resurvey. The revocation takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7767.s: This order extends the limits of the customs port of entry of Buffalo, New York. It adds the city of Lackawanna, the east bank of the Niagara River between Buffalo and Tonawanda, and the cities of Tonawanda and North Tonawanda to that customs area.

7766.s: This order amends rules for paying losses to U.S. officers, enlisted men, and employees in foreign countries when foreign currency changes affect their pay and allowances. It changes how those losses may be calculated in places with special currency rules or limits on converting local currency into foreign exchange. The amendments apply back to July 1, 1933, for one part and February 1, 1936, for another part.

7764.s: This order sets aside about 143,110 acres in Cameron Parish, Louisiana, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The lands are reserved for use by the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to them.

7765.s: This order restores certain lands in Washington to the control of the Secretary of the Interior. It also revokes the earlier order that had withdrawn those lands for the use of the Navy Department.

7763.s: This order closed several federal offices and government agencies in the District of Columbia all day on Friday, December 24, 1937. It also excused federal employees in the District of Columbia and in the field service from duty that day, except for those excluded for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law.

7762.s: This order exempts John W. Woermann from the rule that would require his automatic separation from civilian service when he reaches the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until February 1, 1939.

7761.s: This order extends the limits of the customs port of entry of Wilmington, North Carolina. It adds the Township of Northwest and parts of the Townships of Wilmington and Cape Fear that are outside the city of Wilmington.

7759.s: This order revokes two earlier executive orders about petroleum moved in interstate commerce. One had created the Federal Petroleum Agency No. 1, and the other had required reports of loadings and discharges of petroleum and petroleum products. Those orders were replaced by two later executive orders.

7760.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal for certain public lands in Nebraska and temporarily withdraws vacant, unappropriated, and unreserved public lands in the area from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are reserved for use by the Department of Agriculture for forestation, soil erosion, flood control, and other land-use work connected to the Pine Ridge Project. It says mineral resource activity on the lands is still allowed under the applicable laws.

7758.s: This order makes part of East Texas Field a designated area and applies federal regulations to petroleum and petroleum products there. It covers people who produce, refine, process, manufacture, store, ship, or transport petroleum or petroleum products in or from that area. It also creates Federal Tender Board No. 1 in Kilgore, Texas, to issue certificates of clearance and administer the rules, and it requires applications and monthly reports on approved forms.

7757.s: This order sets rules for enforcing the law on petroleum and petroleum products moved in interstate commerce. It lets the Secretary of the Interior designate areas, set up boards, and issue certificates of clearance called "Tenders" for certain shipments. It applies to people and businesses that produce, refine, store, transport, or handle petroleum and petroleum products in those areas.

7756.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Interior the President’s powers under the 1935 petroleum law, except for the powers kept under section 4. It says any regulation under section 5(a) that can be punished by fine or imprisonment must be approved by the President first. It also allows the Secretary to set up a Petroleum Conservation Division to help administer the law, work with oil- and gas-producing states on conservation laws, and keep the President informed for duties under section 4.

7755.s: This order exempts Charles H. Hastings from a rule that would otherwise require his automatic retirement at the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until July 1, 1938.

7754.s: This order exempts Luther S. Cannon from the rule that would separate him from federal service when he reaches retirement age. It lets him stay on as Chairman, Board of Review (Processing Tax), Treasury Department, until February 1, 1939.

7752.s: The order transfers certain lands in Washington County, Rhode Island, from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of Commerce, Bureau of Fisheries. It reserves the land for use as a fish hatchery, subject to valid existing rights. The tract is about 26 acres and is to be known as the Arcadia Fish Hatchery.

7753.s: This order exempts Frank L. Boyd from the law that would normally require retirement at the set age. It lets him stay in civilian service until December 1, 1938. Boyd was a district supervisor in the Alcohol Tax Unit of the Bureau of Internal Revenue.

7751.s: This order exempts Wendell W. Mischler from the law that requires certain civilian employees to retire at the automatic separation age. It lets him keep serving as secretary to the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States for as long as his services are needed.

7749.s: This order adds lands and waters in Wakulla, Jefferson, and Taylor Counties, Florida to the St. Marks Migratory Bird Refuge. It covers about 31,445 acres and says private lands in the area become part of the refuge when the United States gets title or a lease. The land is reserved for use by the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights.

7747.s: The order sets the water around San Clemente Island, California as a defensive sea area for national defense. Vessels or other craft may not travel there unless the Secretary of the Navy authorizes them. People who break the order can face penalties under the law.

7748.s: This order withdraws a described area in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the area, subject to valid existing rights, for the Navy Department for present and future naval purposes. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

7746.s: This order changes a civil service rule about certain jobs outside the United States. It covers people employed in a foreign country, in the Virgin Islands, in certain Pacific island possessions, and some U.S. citizens employed in a confidential capacity in the Philippine Islands. It does not apply to people employed in a foreign country contiguous to the United States in the service of the Immigration and Naturalization Service in the Department of Labor.

7745.s: This order exempts Arthur Snow from the rule that requires civilian employees to stop serving when they reach the retirement age for automatic separation. It lets him stay in service until December 1, 1938.

7743.s: This order transfers control and jurisdiction over about 3,186.997 acres in Dona Ana County, New Mexico, from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of the Interior. The land was acquired by the United States through the Resettlement Administration and is to be used for conservation purposes in connection with the Taylor Grazing Act.

7742.s: This order adds certain public lands in Alaska to the Tongass National Forest. It says the lands are added subject to valid existing rights. The lands total 2,311.93 acres.

7744.s: This order directs the Solicitor of the Department of Labor to perform the duties of Secretary of Labor when both the Secretary and the Assistant Secretary are absent. It affects the Department of Labor and the person serving as Solicitor.

7740.s: This order revokes part of an earlier withdrawal for a tract of public land in California. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for use by the War Department for military purposes. The reservation stays in place until the President or Congress revokes it.

7741.s: This executive order revokes part of Reservoir Site Reserve No. 17 in California. It removes the reserve status from the specific lands listed in the order. The rest of the reserve is not mentioned as being changed.

7739.s: This order revokes Executive Order 6752, which had added positions at the National Soldiers' Home at Johnson City, Tennessee, to an exception in the Civil Service Rules. The revocation takes effect on January 1, 1938. It also says some employees at the Veterans' Administration Facility in Mountain Home, Tennessee, who were appointed after June 28, 1934 and do not have civil-service status, may acquire that status under the Civil Service Rules, except for certain positions already covered by paragraphs 11 and 12.

7738.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules to allow temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers for part-time or intermittent work in the Postal Service. It applies to holiday or seasonal business from November 15, 1937, to January 15, 1938.

7735.s: This order exempts Mrs. Olive H. Jarrett from the rule that requires some federal civilian workers to retire at a set age. It lets her stay in service as a clerk in the American Consulate General at Mexico, Mexico until January 1, 1939.

7734.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal for certain public lands in New Mexico and then temporarily withdraws the vacant, unappropriated, and unreserved lands in that area. It sets the land aside for use by the Department of Agriculture for soil-erosion control and other land use work connected to the Taos Project. It does not restrict prospecting, mining, leasing, or patenting of mineral resources under the applicable laws.

7733-A.s: This order exempts Margaret M. Hanna from the rule that would automatically separate her from service at the retirement age. It lets her stay in service for as long as needed, but not beyond the close of business on December 31, 1938.

7733.s: This order exempts Robert Dickens, a quarterman modelmaker at the Navy Yard in Washington, D.C., from the rule that requires some civilian employees to retire at a set age. It lets him stay in service until November 1, 1938.

7732.s: This order transfers housing and slum-clearance projects, funds, property, records, and some employees from the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works to the United States Housing Authority. It applies to projects under construction, related assets and contracts, unspent balances for those projects, and certain administrative funds. It also covers employees who were serving on the effective date and were certified as having worked on housing or slum-clearance work.

7730.s: This order exempts Marvin M. McLean, an associate attorney in the Department of the Interior, from the rule that requires automatic retirement at a set age. It lets him stay in federal service until December 1, 1938.

7728.s: This order exempts Miss Mary M. O'Reilly from the rule that required some civilian federal employees to retire at a set age. It lets her stay in service until November 1, 1938.

7729.s: The order updates rules for diplomatic officers when sending condolences, congratulations, and similar messages, using Department of State rules. It also changes consular rules for the shipment and discharge of seamen on U.S. merchant vessels in foreign ports and for American-owned vessels abroad. The revised rules cover how seamen are shipped, discharged, paid, documented, and how shipping articles are handled, and they set duties for masters and consular officers.

7727.s: This order exempts Harry D. Myers from the rule that requires civilian employees to retire at the set retirement age. It lets him stay in service until November 1, 1938.

7725.s: This order exempts Matthew J. Munster from the rule that requires automatic separation at retirement age for certain federal civilian workers. It lets him stay in service as chief marine engineer in the Immigration and Naturalization Service until November 1, 1938.

7726.s: This order exempts George T. Summerlin from the rule that requires retirement at the set age. It lets him stay in the Foreign Service for as long as needed, but not beyond the close of business on November 30, 1942.

7724.s: This order sets aside federal land in Chaves County, New Mexico as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Private land inside the area can become part of the refuge if the United States gets title to it or leases it. The refuge will be known as the Bitter Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7723.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be classified as to whether it is suitable for wildlife refuge purposes. It applies to the public lands in the described area and stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

7722.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal order for one tract of public land in Alabama. It then withdraws that tract from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for the use, possession, and control of the Tennessee Valley Authority, subject to valid existing rights. The reservation stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

7721.s: This order adds about 5,000 acres in Pacific County, Washington, to the Willapa Harbor Migratory Bird Refuge. The land is reserved for use by the Department of Agriculture, subject to existing valid rights. Any private land in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to it or leases it.

7720.s: This order sets aside lands in Jefferson County, Idaho, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The refuge applies to lands the United States has acquired or will acquire in the described area, subject to existing valid rights. Private lands in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to them or leases them.

7719.s: This order adds specific public land in Arkansas to the Ouachita National Forest, subject to valid existing rights. It also replaces a temporary withdrawal of that same land made by an earlier executive order.

7718.s: This order makes income tax withholding returns, Form 1042B, open to inspection by the Department of National Revenue in Ottawa, Canada. It applies to returns filed for the 1937 calendar year and later years. The inspection is for the U.S. Treasury Department to help administer the tax convention between the United States and Canada.

7717.s: This order changes a prior order about the Civilian Conservation Corps. It asks the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Agriculture, the Secretary of Labor, and the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs to work with the Director of the Corps and each appoint a representative to confer with him and help carry out the law.

7716.s: This order extends the trust periods for Indian lands, whether tribal or individual, that would otherwise expire during calendar year 1938. The extension is for 25 years from the date each trust would have expired, except in cases where Congress has specifically kept that power for itself.

7715.s: This order sets up rules to carry out the Marihuana Tax Act of 1937 in the Virgin Islands. It requires people there who import, make, sell, give away, or otherwise handle marihuana to register with the Commissioner of Finance and pay the special taxes when required. It also lets the Governor of the Virgin Islands make regulations and inspect and take action to enforce the law.

7713.s: This order sets aside federal land in Hill County, Montana as the Lake Thibadeau Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. The land is withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserved for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Private land inside the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control of it.

7714.s: This order exempts Charles R. Torbet from the rule that required automatic retirement at the set age. It lets him stay in his job as engineer-in-charge of the House Wing of the U.S. Capitol Building until October 1, 1938.

7712.s: This order changes the Tariff of United States Consular Fees. It adds a $1 fee for taking an application for, and issuing, a travel certificate for use in China.

7711.s: This order designates John D. Biggets as the administrator for a census of partial employment, unemployment, and occupations. It directs him to conduct the census and issue a report of findings when it is done. It also lets him hire temporary employees, set their pay, and make needed spending for the work, with total allocations not to exceed $5,000,000.

7710.s: This order allows Dr. Winfred Overholser to be appointed Superintendent of St. Elizabeths Hospital in the Department of the Interior without following the Civil Service Rules. It affects the appointment to that hospital post and says the order was recommended by the Secretary of the Interior.

7709-A.s: This order abolishes the National Emergency Council as of December 31, 1937. Any remaining unused funds for the council must be transferred back to the appropriation made by the 1937 act. Its records, papers, equipment, and other property must be transferred to the Bureau of the Budget.

7709.s: This order exempts Lee C. Corbett from the rule that required automatic retirement at the set age. It lets him stay in federal service until February 1, 1938.

7708.s: This order waives a rule that had barred Federal employees from holding office under a state, territorial, or municipal government. It allows Roger John Traynor to hold a position as Consulting Expert in the Office of the Secretary of the Treasury while also serving as a Consulting Tax Counsel for the State Board of Equalization of California.

7707.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in California for the tracts listed in the order. It then temporarily withdraws those lands from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves them for use of the War Department for military purposes. The reservation stays in place until the President or Congress revokes it.

7706.s: This order extends the customs port of entry limits for Chester, Pennsylvania. It adds Lower Chichester Township, Marcus Hook Borough, Trainer Borough, Upland Borough, Parkside Borough, Eddystone Borough, and Ridley Township to that port area.

7705.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in the San Bernardino Meridian from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use. The order applies to the listed sections in Township 14 South, Range 5 East.

7704.s: This order exempts George C. Havenner, a liaison officer at the Government Printing Office, from the rule that required certain government workers to retire at age. It lets him stay in service until October 1, 1938.

7703.s: This order designates Jeanne Kavanagh of Iowa to sign the President’s name on land patents. It applies to land patents handled through the Department of the Interior.

7702.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules to list two assistants to the Secretary in the office of the Secretary of Agriculture. It affects the office of the Secretary of Agriculture and how its assistants are classified under the civil service rules.

7701.s: This order limits the amount of red cedar shingles that may be imported from Canada during the last six months of 1937. The limit is 892,373 squares. It affects people and businesses importing those shingles from Canada.

7698.s: This order excludes certain lands in New Mexico from the Carson National Forest. The lands are in T. 25 N., R. 8 E., section 2, tracts 37, 38, and 39, totaling 8.89 acres.

7699.s: This order abolishes Nome, Alaska, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 31. The change takes effect thirty days after the date of the order.

7697.s: This order transfers a portion of Bolling Field in the District of Columbia from the War Department to the Navy Department. It also keeps the land description for the Navy-held area and says the Army must vacate the part transferred to the Navy as soon as practicable after its new facilities are far enough along to meet its needs. The order affects land and facilities at Bolling Field and the Army and Navy departments.

7696.s: This order sets the grades and ratings for enlisted men in the Regular Army for fiscal year 1938. It also limits how many enlisted men may be in each grade and specialist rating. The limits apply to enlisted men in the Regular Army.

7695.s: This order revokes part of a prior order for certain public lands in Washington. It then temporarily withdraws those tracts from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves them for use by the War Department for military purposes. The reservation stays in place until the President or Congress revokes it.

7694.s: This order revokes a previous order that had withdrawn public lands in Wyoming pending resurvey. It applies to the remaining lands covered by that earlier order and takes effect when the official filing of the resurvey plats is made.

7693.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal for certain public lands in Washington and applies to the area listed in the order. It temporarily withdraws vacant, unappropriated, and unreserved public lands there from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are set aside for use by the Department of Agriculture for reforestation, forestation, soil erosion control, and other land use activities connected to the Northeast Washington Project. It does not stop prospecting, mining, leasing, or patenting mineral resources under the applicable laws.

7692.s: This order exempts Robert C. Merritt from a law that would require civilian workers to leave service at the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until September 1, 1938.

7690.s: This order exempts Stephen B. Soulé from the rule that would require automatic separation at retirement age. It lets him continue in service until September 1, 1938. The order applies to Soulé and the Department of the Interior position he held as senior hydraulic engineer.

7691.s: This order sets aside certain islands in the Snake River in Idaho as the Snake River Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. It withdraws those islands from settlement, location, sale, or entry, and reserves them for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Islands that later come under United States control in the area would become part of the refuge.

7689.s: This order appoints the Secretary of the Interior as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, in place of Ernest Gruening, who resigned. The Administrator may appoint an Assistant Administrator and delegate some powers for the efficient operation of the Administration in Puerto Rico. It also amends earlier executive orders on the Administration.

7688.s: This order changes the Federal Board of Surveys and Maps. It adds the Division of Maps and Charts in the National Archives to the list of organizations that can be members of the Board.

7687.s: This order extends the Civil Service Retirement Act to certain federal employees on the Isthmus of Panama. It applies to U.S. citizen federal employees there who are not covered by the Canal Zone Retirement Act and whose jobs are not intermittent or of uncertain duration.

7685.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 4699 of August 1, 1927, which had withdrawn public lands in California pending resurvey. It takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey of those lands is filed.

7686.s: This order changes an earlier order that transferred certain lands in the Virgin Islands from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of the Navy for aviation facilities. It leaves out the east beach and bath-house fronting on Lindbergh Bay from that transfer. The excepted area is to be described later by survey approved by the Secretary of the Interior, and its use during seaplane operation will be governed by Navy regulations.

7684.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6288 for the remaining public lands in Wyoming that were being withheld pending resurvey. It affects those remaining lands and takes effect when the official resurvey plat is filed.

7683.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6192, which had withdrawn public lands in California pending resurvey. It affects those public lands in California and becomes effective when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7681.s: This order sets aside lands in Spokane County, Washington, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It covers 12,774 acres, more or less, and applies to lands acquired or to be acquired by the United States, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands in the area become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to them or leases them.

7682.s: This order exempts Milton F. Colburn, a carpenter at St. Elizabeths Hospital in the Department of the Interior, from the rule that requires retirement at the set age. It allows him to stay in service until August 1, 1938.

7680.s: This order enlarges the Elk Refuge in Teton County, Wyoming by adding federal lands in the listed areas. Private lands inside those areas would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to them. It also replaces earlier temporary land withdrawals for some of the affected lands and revokes the order that established the Flat Creek Reservation.

7679.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules by adding a new exemption to Schedule A. It covers the chief and two assistant chiefs of the Foreign Service Buildings Office.

7678.s: This order reserves about 2,680 acres in the Apache National Forest in Apache County, Arizona, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Any private land in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to it or leases it. The land stays in the Apache National Forest, and its use as a bird refuge must not interfere with forest conservation purposes.

7677.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal for certain public lands in Colorado. It then temporarily withdraws vacant, unappropriated, and unreserved public lands in the area from settlement, location, sale, or entry and sets them aside for use by the Department of Agriculture. The lands are to be used for soil erosion and flood control and other land use work connected to the Weld County Project. It does not stop prospecting, mining, leasing, or patenting mineral resources under the law.

7677-A.s: This order calls selected reserve officers from the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard to active duty for service with the Civilian Conservation Corps. It also lets the Corps director undertake projects on county and city lands and on privately owned land, subject to limits in the law. The Secretaries of War, Agriculture, the Interior, and Labor are asked to cooperate with the director and appoint representatives to help carry out the law.

7676.s: This order sets the boundaries of the Balboa and Cristobal divisions of the District Court in the Canal Zone, and it divides the Canal Zone into matching subdivisions. It also says the towns of Balboa and Cristobal include the town sites and other settlements in those subdivisions. The Governor must provide places for District Court sessions in Balboa and Cristobal, and must appoint magistrates and constables for each town.

7675.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal for certain public lands in New Mexico. It then temporarily withdraws vacant, unappropriated, and unreserved public lands in that area from settlement, location, sale, or entry, and sets them aside for use by the Department of Agriculture for soil erosion control and other land use activities connected to the Mills Project. The order says mineral resources may still be prospected, located, developed, mined, entered, leased, or patented under the law.

7674.s: This order revokes an earlier temporary withdrawal for certain public lands in North Dakota. It then temporarily withdraws vacant, unappropriated, and unreserved public lands in the listed area from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves them for use by the Department of Agriculture for soil erosion control and other land use work in the Little Missouri Project. The order does not stop prospecting, mining, leasing, or patenting mineral resources under the law.

7673.s: This order revokes part of an earlier withdrawal of public lands in North Dakota. It temporarily withdraws vacant, unappropriated, and unreserved public lands in the listed area from settlement, location, sale, or entry, and sets them aside for the Department of Agriculture for soil erosion control and other land use work connected with the Billings Project. It does not restrict prospecting, mining, leasing, or patenting mineral resources under the applicable laws.

7671.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in South Dakota and sets them aside for use by the Department of Agriculture. The lands are to be used for reforestation, forestation, soil erosion control, and other land utilization activities connected with the Fort Sully Project. It also says the order does not restrict mineral prospecting, locating, developing, mining, entering, leasing, or patenting under applicable laws.

7672.s: This order revokes part of a previous withdrawal for certain public lands in Oregon and temporarily withdraws the listed vacant public lands from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are reserved for use by the Department of Agriculture for soil erosion control and other land use work connected to the Central Oregon Land Project. It does not stop prospecting, mining, leasing, or patenting mineral resources under the law.

7670.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Arkansas from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets those lands aside for the Department of Agriculture to use for reforestation, forestation, soil erosion control, and other land use activities connected to the Boston Mountain Project. It does not restrict prospecting, mining, leasing, or patenting of mineral resources under applicable law.

7669.s: This order revoked an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Colorado for the area listed in the order. It then temporarily withdrew vacant, unappropriated, and unreserved public lands in that area from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserved them for use by the Department of Agriculture for soil erosion control and other land use activities tied to the Southern Otero Project. It says valid existing rights are preserved, and mineral prospecting, mining, leasing, and patenting may continue under applicable laws.

7668.s: This order reinstates George T. Summerlin to his former position as a Foreign Service officer of Class I. His reinstatement takes effect after the Senate confirms his nomination and he takes the oath of office.

7667.s: This order exempts William H. Griffin from the rule that would require his automatic retirement for age. It lets him stay in civilian service with the Geological Survey, Department of the Interior, until August 1, 1938.

7666.s: This order exempts Albert F. Woods from compulsory retirement for age and lets him stay in service until September 1, 1938. It applies to his civil service job as principal pathologist in the Bureau of Plant Industry at the Department of Agriculture.

7665.s: This order corrects the boundary description of the Kawaihae Lighthouse Reservation in the Territory of Hawaii. It also excepts a strip of land about sixty feet wide for the Territory of Hawaii to use for road purposes. The order says the net area of the reservation is 9.524 acres, more or less.

7664.s: This order adds land in Michigan to the Seney Migratory Waterfowl Refuge and takes some other land out of the refuge. Private land in the added area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to it or leases it. The land removed from the refuge remains under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of Agriculture.

7663.s: This order extends the boundaries of the Uinta National Forest in Utah to include the listed lands. It covers 42,365.41 acres. The order says existing legal rights and other public uses on those lands are not to be interfered with, and it replaces earlier withdrawals and reservations for stock-driveway purposes.

7662.s: This order revoked part of a previous withdrawal of public lands in Arkansas and then temporarily withdrew vacant, unappropriated, and unreserved public lands in the area for the Department of Agriculture. The lands are to be used for reforestation, forestation, soil erosion and flood control, and other land use activities tied to the Magazine Mountain Project. The order says mineral prospecting, leasing, mining, and related activities are still allowed under the applicable laws.

7661.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to add certain classified positions in the field service of the Navy Department and the Marine Corps. It allows unclassified laborers on the laborer register to move into those positions through promotion and noncompetitive examination, with approval of the Commission. The promotion does not give them classified status or make them eligible for transfer to classified positions in other parts of the federal service.

7660.s: This order exempts certain positions from Executive Order No. 6746 of June 21, 1934. The positions include consultants, experts, specialists, attorneys, and similar jobs that are paid by the day or on an annual basis for part-time service. It applies to people paid from the public works fund or other emergency funds handled by the Secretary of the Interior and the Administrator of Public Works during fiscal years 1938 and 1939.

7659.s: This order exempts Walter B. Luna from the rule that requires retirement at the prescribed age. It lets him stay in service until March 1, 1938.

7658.s: This order restores a parcel of land in Honolulu, Oahu, from the Fort De Russy Military Reservation to the Territory of Hawaii. The land is to be used for improving the territory’s highway system. The United States keeps the right to build a railroad on the land from Fort De Russy Military Reservation to the existing Honolulu Rapid Transit and Land Company line.

7657.s: This order exempts George C. DeHart from a retirement rule that would otherwise separate him from civilian service when he reaches the retirement age. It allows him to stay in service until August 1, 1938. The order affects DeHart, who is an assistant purchasing officer with the United States Coast Guard store in Brooklyn, New York.

7656.s: This order changes Potash Reserve No. 7 in New Mexico by removing certain selected lands from the reserve and adding different base lands in their place. It is part of an exchange of lands under federal law, without mutual reservations of potash and associated minerals. The change takes effect when fee title to the base lands is revested in the United States.

7654.s: This order allows Jacob Oblock to be appointed as an elevator operator in the Custodial Service of the Post Office Department without following the Civil Service Rules. It says he had serious injuries while working as a laborer in that service and has been unable to return to his former job.

7655.s: This order sets aside federal land in Canyon County, Idaho, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Private land in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to it or leases it. It also says the land use remains subject to reclamation work by the Department of the Interior, and it revokes an earlier order for part of the area.

7653.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5603, which had withdrawn public lands in Wyoming pending resurvey. It takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed for the lands covered by that earlier order.

7651.s: This order changes a 1926 reserve order for Reservoir Site Reserve No. 17 in California. It allows the Federal Power Commission to issue licenses and amendments for power projects with transmission lines on the lands listed in the order. If the land is later needed for reservoir purposes, the licensees must remove their project works at their own expense within 30 days after notice from the Secretary of the Interior.

7652.s: This order revokes part of a 1933 order that had temporarily withdrawn certain public land in California. The land had been set aside for classification and for deciding whether it should be included in a national monument. It applies only to the public land described in the order.

7650.s: This order sets aside lands and waters in Washington County, Maine, as the Moosehorn Migratory Bird Refuge. It gives the Department of Agriculture the area to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife, subject to existing valid rights. Private lands in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to them or leases them.

7649.s: This order says funds made available under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1937 must be spent and managed under earlier presidential orders, rules, and regulations for the 1935 and 1936 relief acts, as far as they apply. It makes an exception for rates of pay and eligibility for employment.

7648.s: This order waives a federal rule for Douglas Armstrong, who is Director of Police for the Municipality of St. Croix, Virgin Islands. It allows him to be appointed to and hold the office of United States Marshal for the Virgin Islands.

7647.s: The order withdraws certain public land in Idaho from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for use as a rifle range by the Nampa Rod and Gun Club. The range would be under the supervision of the War Department, and the use must respect valid existing rights. One part of the land is still subject to an earlier reclamation withdrawal, and rifle range operations must not interfere with that withdrawal.

7646.s: This order exempts Hoffman Philip from the rule requiring retirement at the set age. It lets him stay in service for as long as needed, but not past the close of business on October 31, 1937.

7645.s: This order exempts George G. Hedgcock from the law that required automatic separation from government service at retirement age. It lets him stay in service until January 1, 1938. Hedgcock was a senior pathologist in the Bureau of Plant Industry at the Department of Agriculture.

7643.s: This order sets aside lands and waters in Kent County, Delaware as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It applies to land and water already acquired or to be acquired by the United States, subject to existing valid rights. Private lands in the area would become part of the refuge when the United States acquires title to them or leases them.

7642.s: This order exempts Burton Smith from the rule that ends civilian service when a person reaches the retirement age for automatic separation. It lets him stay in service until January 1, 1938.

7641.s: This order transfers to the Secretary of the Treasury the powers, rights, privileges, and duties that had been given to the Secretary of Labor under a 1918 executive order. It also lets the Treasury Secretary use those powers through the Director of Procurement, including signing deeds, contracts, and other conveyance papers. The Secretary of Labor must also help carry out the order, including transferring all stock of the United States Housing Corporation held in trust to the Secretary of the Treasury as trustee.

7640.s: This order sets June 21, 1937, as the effective date of the Bituminous Coal Code and of section 3 of the Bituminous Coal Act of 1937. It applies to the code created under that act and the forms of acceptance for membership in the code.

7639.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations under Executive Order 6166. It also delays other related provisions tied to section 4 of that order until December 31, 1937. The Secretary of the Treasury, with the President’s approval, may still make some of those changes effective between June 30, 1937, and December 31, 1937.

7638.s: This order exempts William F. Staley from the rule requiring automatic separation at retirement age. It lets him stay in service until August 1, 1938.

7637.s: This order exempts John H. Thomas from the rule requiring retirement at the automatic separation age. It lets him stay in service until October 1, 1938. The order applies to him in the Department of the Interior.

7636.s: This order changes an earlier rule that generally barred federal officers and employees from holding state, municipal, or other local offices. It allows a state, county, or municipal officer to serve as a district advisor under the Act of June 28, 1934, if the person is elected by qualified voters of a grazing district and appointed by the Secretary of the Interior. The service is paid on a per diem basis for intermittent duty when the Secretary of the Interior thinks it is needed for grazing on public lands.

7633.s: The order allows William R. Benham to be appointed to a competitive classified position in the Department of Justice without following the Civil Service Rules. It says the appointment is recommended by the Attorney General of the United States.

7632.s: This order designates several places in Texas, Washington, Montana, North Dakota, Minnesota, Michigan, and Vermont as customs ports of entry. It also detaches the townships of Highgate and Franklin in Vermont from the customs port of St. Albans. The order designates Highgate Springs, Vermont, as a customs port of entry and includes the Township of Highgate within it.

7635.s: This order exempts Edward M. Weeks from the law on compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in federal service until September 1, 1938. Weeks is a letter engraver in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing at the Treasury Department.

7630.s: This order lets certain employees of the General Accounting Office keep working past June 30, 1937, through a later date. It applies only to the employees whose continued service had already been allowed by a prior executive order, and it cannot extend beyond June 30, 1938.

7631.s: This order revokes part of the 1914 order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 451. It removes that reserve status from the listed lands in Arizona.

7628.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal for a specific tract of public land in Arkansas. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry for classification, subject to valid existing rights. The withdrawal stays in place until the President or Congress revokes it.

7627.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6120, which had withdrawn public lands in California pending resurvey. It applies to those lands and becomes effective when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.
