7629.s: This order exempts William T. Marshall from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service until August 1, 1938.

7626.s: This order reinstates Robert F. Kelley in the Foreign Service of the United States in Class III. His reinstatement takes effect when the Senate confirms his nomination to that class.

7625.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5144, which had withdrawn public lands in certain townships in New Mexico while a resurvey was pending. The revocation takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7624.s: This order adds a tract of public land in Alaska to the Tongass National Forest. The land is included subject to valid existing rights. The tract is described as containing about 3,800 acres.

7623.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain lands in the Umatilla Federal Irrigation Project in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for the Department of Agriculture as an addition to an existing agricultural field station. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

7621.s: This order revokes part of the 1911 order that had withdrawn certain lands in Utah for Power Site Reserve No. 178. It applies only to the listed parcels of land in Salt Lake Meridian.

7622.s: This order revokes an earlier order that reserved a tract of land in Unalaska for public water use. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for use by the United States Indian Service Hospital at Unalaska. The reservation stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

7619.s: This order allows J. V. Taylor to be appointed as Senior Soil Conservationist in the Soil Conservation Service, Department of Agriculture. It says the appointment may be made without following the civil service rules and without classified status.

7618.s: This order abolishes Vineyard Haven, Massachusetts, as a customs port of entry. It affects Customs Collection District No. 4 in Massachusetts and takes effect immediately.

7620.s: This order revokes a 1909 order that withdrew land in Montana for Temporary Power Site Withdrawal No. 17. It also partially revokes a 1910 order for Power Site Reserve No. 17, for the land described as the east half of the southeast quarter of section 2 in township 9 south, range 10 west.

7617.s: This order increases the money available for assistance for educational, professional, and clerical persons, women’s projects, and miscellaneous work projects under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1936. It says the added amounts will be transferred from another clause in the same act and changes the amounts available for several classes of public projects.

7616.s: This order revokes part of a prior withdrawal for certain public lands in Wyoming. It then temporarily withdraws vacant, unappropriated, and unreserved public lands in the described area from settlement, location, sale, or entry, and sets them aside for the Agriculture Department for soil erosion control and other land use work connected to the Thunder Basin Project. It does not restrict prospecting, locating, developing, mining, entering, leasing, or patenting mineral resources under the law.

7615.s: This order revokes a 1933 executive order that had withdrawn certain public lands in New Mexico pending resurvey. It affects the public lands in the listed township, and it takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7614.s: This order excludes four homesite tracts in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest and restores them to entry under the public-land laws. The tracts are on Prince of Wales Island and Revillagigedo Island, and the order says they are occupied as homesites.

7613.s: This order exempts James Robertson from a rule that requires certain civilian workers to leave service at the retirement age. It lets him stay in the service until June 1, 1938. The order applies only to James Robertson and the service he holds with the Navy Department.

7612.s: This order exempts Charles H. Pierce from the rule requiring retirement at a set age. It lets him stay in civilian service in the Patent Office until June 1, 1938.

7611.s: This order exempts Harry C. Armstrong from the rule that requires civilian federal workers to retire at the automatic separation age. It lets him stay in service until May 1, 1938.

7609.s: This order changes the rules for appointing employees paid from emergency funds. It says appointments or reappointments to those positions cannot last beyond the date when the emergency appropriation ends. It applies to executive departments, independent establishments, and emergency agencies.

7610.s: This order amends the description of homesite No. 20 in Executive Order No. 6966, which excluded certain tracts of land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest and restored them to entry under the public-land laws. The amended homesite is east of the Alaska Railroad near Lawing and is 3.96 acres.

7608.s: This order revokes a 1931 executive order that had withdrawn public lands in Nevada while a resurvey was pending. It affects those public lands in Nevada and takes effect when the official resurvey plat for the township is filed.

7606.s: This order designates Joseph P. Kennedy as Chairman of the United States Maritime Commission. It affects the leadership of that commission.

7607.s: This order transfers the Moapa Division of the Dixie National Forest to the Nevada National Forest. It says the change will not give national-forest status to any publicly owned lands that did not already have it, and it will not remove any publicly owned lands from national forest status. The order becomes effective July 1, 1937.

7605.s: This order revokes two earlier orders that had withdrawn certain public lands in New Mexico while they were pending resurvey. It applies to the listed townships under the New Mexico Principal Meridian. The order takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7604.s: This order partially revokes Executive Order No. 6473 for two townships in Wyoming. It ends the withdrawal of the public lands in Townships 12 and 13 North, Range 97 West, under the Sixth Principal Meridian. The change takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7603.s: This order revokes part of Executive Order No. 6795 for one township in Wyoming. It lifts the withdrawal of the public lands in that township, pending resurvey, and becomes effective when the official plat of resurvey is filed.

7602.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 7261-A of December 31, 1935. It affects the instructions to diplomatic officers of the United States.

7601.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands to provide material for the construction and maintenance of public roads and other public projects. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

7599.s: This order changes two earlier executive orders that withdrew public lands in certain states. It excludes from those orders any lands found by later surveys that would otherwise become part of a school-land grant to the states named in the earlier orders.

7598.s: This order exempts Harry M. Reynolds from the rule that required automatic separation at retirement age. It lets him continue in service until April 1, 1938. It applies to Reynolds, who is a wireman in the Office of the Architect of the Capitol.

7597.s: This order exempts Harry O. Bailey from the rule requiring retirement at the automatic separation age. It lets him stay in service until July 1, 1937, at the Office of the Architect of the Capitol.

7596.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain vacant, unappropriated public lands in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for use by the War Department for military purposes. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

7594.s: This order sets aside the described land on Jones Island in Washington for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also revokes an earlier order for lighthouse purposes as it applies to that land. The refuge is to be known as the Jones Island Migratory Bird Refuge.

7595.s: This order sets aside about 145 acres of Matia Island in Washington for the Department of Agriculture. It makes the land a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife, subject to valid existing rights. It also revokes an earlier order that reserved the same land for lighthouse purposes.

7593.s: This order sets aside land in Charlton, Clinch, and Ware Counties, Georgia, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It applies to lands acquired or to be acquired by the United States, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires the title or leases them.

7592.s: The order allows Mrs. Etta May Gilley to be appointed to a position in the Postal Service without regard to her competitive standing on the civil service register. It says she is the wife of a retired Postal Service clerk and does not have enough means to support herself and her two small children.

7590.s: This order revokes part of a 1933 withdrawal of public lands in a township in California. It applies to sections 1, 2, and 12 in that township in San Bernardino Meridian. The order takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7591.s: This order exempts Reinhardt Thiessen from the usual retirement rule for civilian service. It lets him stay in service until June 1, 1938. Thiessen was a senior research chemist in the Bureau of Mines at the Department of the Interior.

7589.s: This order revokes part of a 1928 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Wyoming from use while a resurvey was pending. It applies to the listed townships in the Sixth Principal Meridian and takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7588.s: This order restores a parcel of land at Kahauiki, Oahu, to its previous status for use by the Territory of Hawaii. The land is to be used in connection with extending Middle Street by diverting Kahauiki Stream and providing a road to Mokumoa Island. It affects the described parcel of land and the Territory of Hawaii.

7587.s: This order lets certain National Labor Relations Board employees get competitive civil service status if they meet the rules in Civil Service Rule II. It does not apply to attorneys, examiners, regional directors, or an executive secretary. It affects employees who were transferred under the National Labor Relations Act and now hold positions covered by the Civil Service Act and rules.

7586.s: This order exempts William Gerig from the rule that requires certain government workers to retire at the set retirement age. It lets him stay in service until April 1, 1938.

7585.s: This order partly revokes a 1933 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Wyoming. It applies to townships 14 and 15 north, B. 97 west, under the Sixth Principal Meridian. The revocation takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7583.s: This order sets aside lands in Marshall County, Minnesota as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It covers about 55,170 acres and places the lands under the use of the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to them.

7584.s: This order designates the customs station of Ajo, Arizona, as a customs port of entry. It places it in Customs Collection District No. 26, with headquarters at Nogales, Arizona, effective thirty days from the date of the order.

7582.s: This order exempts George W. Hutchison from the compulsory retirement rule for age. It lets him stay in service until June 1, 1938. He is the chief engineer of the ship Fathomer in the Coast and Geodetic Survey, Department of Commerce.

7581.s: This order exempts Louis A. Simon from a law that would otherwise require his retirement for age. It lets him stay in government service until June 1, 1938.

7579.s: This order revokes a 1929 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Colorado’s listed townships pending a resurvey. It applies to the townships in the Sixth Principal Meridian named in the order. The change takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7580.s: This order exempts Frank Hahn from the rule requiring retirement at the set age. It lets him stay in service until May 1, 1938. It applies to Frank Hahn, a senior administrative assistant in the Geological Survey.

7578.s: This order excludes four homesite tracts in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It restores those tracts to entry under the public-land laws. The tracts are listed as homesites in the Auke Lake, Triangle, Inner Lagoon, and Bostwick Bay areas.

7576.s: This order restores some land from the Schofield Barracks Military Reservation to the Territory of Hawaii for road purposes. It also sets aside other parts of the Honolulu-Waialua Road, also called Kamehameha Highway, as part of the military reservation for military purposes. The affected lands are within the Schofield Barracks area in Hawaii.

7575.s: This order limits the amount of red cedar shingles that may be imported from Canada into the United States during the first six months of 1937. The limit is set at 1,048,262 squares. It affects imports of red cedar shingles from Canada and the U.S. producers represented by the industry group that requested the limit.

7574.s: This order exempts Edward M. Kennard from the rule that would require him to leave federal civilian service at the retirement age. It lets him stay in his job as Chief of the Budget and Accounting Section of the Division of Accounts in the Department of Justice until May 1, 1938.

7577.s: This order amends the rules for diplomatic and consular officers. It says they may not ask for or accept any present, decoration, medal, order, testimonial, office, or title from any king, prince, or foreign state. It also says any such item given by a foreign government must go through the Department of State and cannot be delivered unless Congress authorizes it.

7573.s: This order designates and authorizes Adolph G. Wolff, an associate justice of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico, to serve as acting judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico. He may perform the duties of that judge and sign necessary papers and records when the judge is absent during the current calendar year.

7571.s: This order exempts John G. Honey from a law that would normally end civilian service when a person reaches the retirement age for automatic separation. It lets him stay in service until July 1, 1938.

7570.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about rules for appointing employees paid from emergency funds. It says those rules no longer apply to appointments made by the United States Employees' Compensation Commission.

7568.s: This order exempts Clarence W. Perley from the rule that requires civilian federal workers to retire at the automatic separation age. It lets him stay in service until September 1, 1937. The order applies only to Perley, who was Chief of the Classification Division at the Library of Congress.

7569.s: This order exempts Carl F. Jeansen from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in civilian service with the Navy Department until April 1, 1938.

7567.s: This order exempts Charles J. Evans from compulsory retirement under the cited law. It lets him stay in government service until March 1, 1938.

7566.s: This order exempts William M. Beaman from a rule that would otherwise require automatic separation from civilian service at the retirement age. It allows him to stay in service until March 1, 1938. The order applies to Beaman, a senior topographic engineer in the Geological Survey, Department of the Interior.

7565.s: This order exempts Joseph W. Austin from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service until March 1, 1938. He is a foreman carpenter in the United States Capitol Building under the office of the Architect of the Capitol.

7563.s: This order sets aside about 11,500 acres in Chariton County, Missouri, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Private lands in the area can become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to them or leases them. The refuge is to be known as the Swan Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7562.s: This order sets aside 10,775.61 acres of land in Glenn and Colusa Counties, California, for the Department of Agriculture. It makes the area a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The refuge is to be known as the Sacramento Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7564.s: This order extends the customs port of entry of Saint Paul, Minnesota. It adds the territory within the limits of South Saint Paul and West Saint Paul, Minnesota, to that port’s area.

7561.s: This order revokes the earlier withdrawal of public lands for one township in Wyoming, T. 47 N., R. 84 W. It takes effect when the official plat of the township’s resurvey is filed.

7560.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6082, which had withdrawn public lands in a township in Wyoming while a resurvey was pending. It applies to the township described in the order. The revocation takes effect when the official filing of the plat of resurvey is made.

7558.s: This order revokes an earlier public land withdrawal for certain tracts in Lincoln County, Nevada. It then withdraws those tracts from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves them for the Soil Conservation Service to use for erosion control demonstrations. The order says some of the land will be known as the Pahranagat Valley Area and some as the Panaca Area.

7557.s: This order changes a prior order by moving the Resettlement Administration’s powers, functions, and duties to the Secretary of Agriculture. It also transfers the agency’s funds, personnel, property, records, and equipment to the Department of Agriculture under the Secretary’s control. The Secretary’s actions since January 1, 1937 under certain orders are confirmed and ratified.

7556.s: This order removes several named homesite tracts in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest and restores them to entry under the public-land laws. The lands are described as homesites in the Mud Bay, Fritz Cove, Wrangell, Triangle, and Herring Bay groups. It affects the listed tracts on Revillagigedo Island, Wrangell Island, and near Auke Bay and George Inlet.

7555.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal for one tract of public land in California. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry, and reserves it for use by the Forest Service as an administrative site for the Lassen National Forest. The withdrawal stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

7554.s: This order changes the loan rules for the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration. It says loans may be made to help pay for the purchase of farm land and necessary equipment by farmers, farm tenants, croppers, farm laborers, or stockmen. It also allows loans for other purposes needed for rural rehabilitation or relief in stricken agricultural areas.

7552.s: This order exempts William H. Long from the rule requiring automatic separation at retirement age. It lets him stay in service until August 1, 1937.

7553.s: This order increases the amounts available for several classes of public projects under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1936. The increase is $124,500,000, taken from unexpended balances transferred from the 1935 relief appropriation. It affects projects for highways, public buildings, parks, public utilities, flood control, education-related assistance, women's projects, miscellaneous work projects, the National Youth Administration, and rural rehabilitation and relief for farmers and livestock growers.

7550.s: This order revokes an earlier civil service exemption for one tobacco examiner position in the Customs Service at the port of Chicago. It says the Treasury Department was already filling that position the same way other competitive classified positions are filled. The revocation affects that one position in the Civil Service Rules.

7551.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules by revoking subdivisions (c), (d), and (e) of a rule in Schedule A. After the change, the rule covers the Director of the Bureau of Prisons, up to three Assistant Directors, and members of the Board of Parole.

7549.s: This order designates Coast Guard vessels to patrol waters frequented by seal herds and sea otter. Those vessels are to enforce the act named in the order.

7547.s: This order changes part of an earlier rule on paying losses to officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States in foreign countries when foreign currencies change in value against the American dollar. It updates the monetary unit and basic rate for Ethiopia from "M. T. Dollar" to "lira" and from "33.42" to "5.20."

7548.s: This order directs several federal departments and the Federal Communications Commission to carry out the United States’ duties under the Convention for Safety of Life at Sea. It confirms an arrangement that gives the Department of Commerce responsibility for issuing certificates, while the Commission has final authority over matters involving radio on ships. It also directs the named agencies to perform the duties they are already authorized by law to carry out under the convention.

7546.s: This order transfers several Indian Subsistence Homesteads projects from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of the Interior. It also transfers the related property, contracts, rights, records, and other interests tied to those projects. The Secretary of the Interior is authorized to administer the property and to use the powers and functions previously given to the Secretary of Agriculture for these projects.

7545.s: This order exempts William H. Ramsey from the law on compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in civilian service in the Department of Justice until February 1, 1938.

7544.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal for certain public lands in New Mexico. It then temporarily withdraws those lands from settlement, location, sale, or entry, subject to valid existing rights. The land is reserved for use by the Forest Service as the Espanola administrative site for the Santa Fe National Forest.

7543.s: This order amends diplomatic and consular regulations. It changes rules for Foreign Service officers appointed or promoted during a Senate recess, office supply requests, exequaturs, naval and consular visits, fees for some U.S.-owned vessels, seamen’s extra wages and relief, and the handling of wrecked or stranded vessels. It affects Foreign Service officers, consular officers, naval officers, seamen, and owners of certain vessels.

7542.s: This order transfers certain files and records of the United States Railroad Administration to three agencies. Claims records from a fire in Minnesota go to the General Accounting Office, freight rate and related surplus records go to the Interstate Commerce Commission, and original payroll and personnel records go to the United States Civil Service Commission. The physical transfer is to be completed by February 15, 1937.

7540.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6550 of January 6, 1934. That earlier order required reports on the allocation and obligation of emergency funds to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget.

7539.s: This order revokes part of a 1928 order that had withdrawn public lands in certain Wyoming townships. It applies to the townships named in the order and takes effect when the official plats of resurvey are filed.

7541.s: The order sets aside about 625.62 acres in Washington for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also allows the Department of War and the Department of the Treasury to use rights-of-way for roads, telephone lines, and transmission lines to the Willapa Bay Light Station or nearby properties they control. The earlier reservation of these lands for lighthouse purposes is revoked for these lands.

7538.s: This order reserves about 2,926.87 acres in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana as an addition to the Delta Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. The land is set aside for the Department of Agriculture to use for wildlife conservation purposes, subject to valid existing rights. It also says the land remains under the primary jurisdiction of the War Department and can still be used by that department for work on Mississippi River navigation.

7537.s: This order says certain public lands in Alaska that are reserved for lighthouse purposes, and are not in national forests, may be leased for furfarming. The Secretary of the Interior may make the leases, but the Secretary of Commerce must approve them and the leases cannot interfere with lighthouse use. It also supersedes a 1929 executive order.

7536.s: This order revokes part of a 1931 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Wyoming, specifically in townships 41, 42, 43, and 44 North, Range 85 West of the sixth principal meridian. It becomes effective when the official filing of the plats of resurvey for those townships is made.

7535.s: This order revokes a 1933 order that had withdrawn public lands in certain townships in California. It applies to the townships described in the order and becomes effective when the official plats of resurvey are filed.

7534.s: This order removes a tract of land in Arizona from the Sitgreaves National Forest. It then reserves that land for townsite purposes under federal land laws. The land is described as 3.35 acres.

7533.s: This order exempts James E. Tibbitts from a rule requiring automatic retirement at the set age. It allows him to stay in his job as administrative assistant in the Navy Department until February 1, 1938.

7532.s: This order sets aside about 8.42 acres in Hampton Bays, New York, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The land is reserved subject to valid existing rights. It also says the property may still be used by the Department of Commerce for lighthouse purposes without interference.

7531.s: This order exempts Charles Earle, a gardener's helper in the National Park Service, from the rule that would separate him from service at the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until January 1, 1938.

7530.s: This order transfers the powers, functions, and duties of the Resettlement Administration to the Secretary of Agriculture. It also moves the agency’s funds, personnel, property, records, and equipment to the Department of Agriculture. The Secretary of Agriculture is to supervise and control them, and the order takes effect on January 1, 1937.

7529.s: This order revokes a 1930 order that had withdrawn public lands in two Nevada townships pending a resurvey. It takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed for those townships.

7528.s: This order revokes a 1930 order that had withdrawn public lands in a township in Colorado while a resurvey was pending. It takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey for that township is filed.

7527.s: This order changes a prior order that reserved land at Copper Center, Alaska, for the joint use of the Department of the Interior and the Department of Agriculture for educational and agricultural experiment-station purposes. It removes the listed lands from that reservation. The change takes effect when the approved plat is officially filed.

7526.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations under Executive Order No. 6166 until June 30, 1937. It applies to provisions tied to section 4 that were not already carried out by December 31, 1936. The Secretary of the Treasury, with the President’s approval, may make any of these changes effective between those dates.

7524.s: This order sets aside lands and waters in Mason County, Illinois, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It places the area under the use of the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Any private land in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to it or leases it.

7525.s: This order exempts Robert W. Shumate from the rule that required certain federal workers to be separated at retirement age. It lets him stay in his job as a carpenter at the National Institute of Health until January 1, 1938.

7523.s: This order revokes a previous reservation of lands in Oregon that had been set apart as the Hart Mountain Game Range. It withdraws certain public lands in Lake County, Oregon, from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves them for the Department of Agriculture. The land is to be used as a range and breeding ground for antelope and other species of wildlife.

7522.s: This order revokes part of a 1935 executive order for certain lands in Nevada and withdraws those lands from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets them aside for wildlife conservation and development, and for protecting and improving public grazing lands and natural forage resources. The order also allows mineral activities under the law and puts the area under the joint control of the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture for wildlife matters, with some grazing land under the Secretary of the Interior and some land under the Secretary of Agriculture.

7521.s: This order directs the Coast Guard to help keep channels and harbors open to navigation by using ice-breaking operations when needed and practical. It says the work should meet the reasonable demands of commerce. It also directs the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Secretary of Commerce to cooperate and provide vessels that are available and suitable for this service.

7520.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public land in Arizona from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for use by the War Department as a target range for the Arizona National Guard. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

7519.s: This order exempts Herbert A. Smith, a senior forester in the Forest Service at the Department of Agriculture, from the rule requiring retirement at a certain age. It allows him to stay in service until January 1, 1938.

7518.s: This order exempts Frank E. Singleton from the rule requiring automatic retirement at the set age. It lets him stay in service until January 1, 1938. It affects Singleton and the Department of Agriculture position he held.

7517.s: This order exempts André Fourchy from the law that would require certain government workers to retire at the set retirement age. It lets him stay in service as an associate civil engineer with the United States Coast Guard, Treasury Department, until January 1, 1938.

7516.s: This order exempts Elton A. Gongwer from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service until January 1, 1938. It applies to Gongwer, an investigator at the General Accounting Office.

7513.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Roosevelt and Pike National Forests to the Arapaho National Forest in Colorado. It covers lands in parts of those forests described by boundary lines, including lands in Clear Creek County. It says it does not remove national forest status from land that already has it or give national forest status to public lands that did not already have it. The order takes effect on January 1, 1937.

7514.s: This order sets aside federal lands in Anne Arundel and Prince Georges Counties, Maryland, for the Department of Agriculture. The lands are to be used as a wildlife experiment and research refuge, and private lands in the area will be added if the United States acquires title or a lease. The refuge is named the Patuxent Research Refuge.

7511.s: This order revokes a 1931 withdrawal of public lands in one township in Wyoming. It applies to that township and takes effect when the official resurvey plat is filed.

7510.s: This order withdraws 6,159.40 acres of public land in Washington from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets the land aside for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife, subject to valid existing rights. Some of the land is also subject to use by the Department of the Interior for the Columbia Basin Reclamation Project and related purposes. The refuge is to be known as the Lenore Lake Migratory Bird Refuge.

7508.s: This order designates Carrabelle, Florida, as a customs port of entry. It applies to Customs Collection District No. 18 in Florida and takes effect on the date it was signed.

7509.s: This order withdraws the listed lands in Montana from settlement, location, sale, or entry and sets them aside for wildlife conservation and the protection of public grazing lands and natural forage resources. It also says mineral prospecting, development, mining, leasing, and patenting may continue under the applicable laws. The range is to be under joint control of the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture for wildlife matters, with rules for protection, administration, and the removal of surplus game animals. The order says the forage is to support sharptail grouse, antelope, and other wildlife, while also being available for domestic livestock under Interior's rules.

7507.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6075, which had withdrawn public lands in a township in Colorado pending a resurvey. It takes effect when the official filing of the plat of resurvey for that township is made.

7505.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal for certain public land tracts in California. It then temporarily withdraws those tracts from settlement, location, sale, or entry for classification and in aid of legislation, while subject to valid existing rights.

7506.s: This order revokes two earlier executive orders that had withdrawn certain public lands in Colorado while a resurvey was pending. It applies to the listed townships in Colorado. The order takes effect when the official plats of resurvey are filed.

7504.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal for a 40-acre tract of public land in Arizona. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for use by the Bureau of Plant Industry as an experiment station to study plant diseases.

7503.s: This order amends and corrects the boundary description of the Kuwaaohe Military Reservation in Hawaii. It also describes the reservation as a tract of 322.5 acres, more or less, and says the land is set aside for military purposes subject to private rights and public roads and rights-of-way.

7501.s: This order changes the name of the Santa Barbara National Forest in California to Los Padres National Forest. It affects the national forest and the name used for it.

7502.s: The order revokes an earlier withdrawal for a tract of public land in California. It then temporarily withdraws that tract from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for use as an administrative site for Federal and State cooperative forest protection work, subject to valid existing rights.

7500.s: This order changes a rule on Army rations. It lets the Secretary of War give extra food allowances in special cases when local conditions, the small size of a detachment, or the kind of work makes the normal allowance not enough. The total extra allowance must stay below the money allowance for enlisted men when rations are not furnished and Government messing facilities are provided.

7499.s: This order closed several federal offices in the District of Columbia at 1 p.m. on December 24, 1936, and for the entire day on January 2, 1937. It also excused many federal employees from duty on those days, with some exceptions for special public reasons or when existing law required them to work. Field service employees were also excused for the entire day on December 26, 1936, and shift workers were given shorter duty hours on December 24 and no duty on January 2 and December 26 where covered.

7498.s: This order authorizes the Alaska Railroad to use or charter ocean-going or coastwise vessels to carry passengers and freight to and from the Territory of Alaska. It says this service is for the present interruption in shipping and may continue as long as the Secretary of the Interior thinks necessary. It also directs the railroad to keep the current commercial passenger and freight charges for this added service.

7496.s: This order transfers certain recreational demonstration project property, records, personnel, and remaining funds from the Resettlement Administration to the Secretary of the Interior. The Secretary of the Interior must also take on the outstanding obligations connected with those projects. Through the National Park Service, the Secretary is authorized to complete and administer the projects and to set rules needed to carry out the transferred duties.

7497.s: This order changes rules for Foreign Service officers who want to marry a person of foreign nationality. They must get permission from the Secretary of State first, and an officer who marries an alien without advance approval is treated as guilty of insubordination and separated from the Service. A request to marry an alien must include the officer’s resignation, and no person married to an alien may take the Foreign Service entrance examinations.

7495.s: This order designates Orange, Texas, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 21 (Sabine). It affects customs operations in Orange, Texas, starting on the date of the order.

7494.s: This order exempts Davis B. Levis from compulsory retirement for age. It continues him in the service until December 1, 1937.

7493.s: This order puts the administrative acts of the Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration under the control and supervision of the Secretary of the Interior. It applies until further order. It also amends two earlier executive orders about the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration.

7492.s: This order exempts Albert F. Woods from the rule that would require automatic separation from civilian service at retirement age. It lets him stay in service until September 1, 1937, in his job with the Department of Agriculture.

7490.s: This order revokes part of a 1926 executive order that created Reservoir Site Reserve No. 17. It applies to the lands described in the order in the Pacific Slope Basins in California.

7491.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for use by the War Department as a target range. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

7489.s: The order reserves and sets apart certain public lands in Teton County, Wyoming for the Department of Agriculture as an addition to the Elk Refuge. It also replaces earlier temporary withdrawals for elk refuge classification on those lands, subject to valid existing rights.

7487-A.s: This order authorizes and directs R. Walton Moore, Assistant Secretary of State, to perform the duties of the Secretary of State. It applies during the Secretary of State’s absence.

7487.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules for temporary Postal Service workers. It covers temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers needed for part-time or intermittent work in the Postal Service for holiday or seasonal business from November 15, 1936, to January 15, 1937.

7486.s: This order revokes part of a 1926 order that had withdrawn public lands in the surveyed portion of a township in Utah. It applies to that township and becomes effective when the official plat of resurvey is filed.

7485.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 2124, which had established the Ediz Hook Reservation in Washington for the protection of native birds. It affects the reservation area described as about 83 acres near Port Angeles.

7484.s: This order reserves Sea Horse Key, about 154.46 acres in the Gulf of Mexico, for use by the Department of Agriculture as a headquarters for the Cedar Keys Bird Refuge. It makes the area part of the Cedar Keys Bird Refuge. The order also revokes an 1851 reservation of the land for lighthouse purposes, subject to valid existing rights.

7482.s: This order designates Morehead City, North Carolina, as a customs port of entry. It applies to Customs Collection District No. 15 in North Carolina and takes effect on the date it was signed.

7483.s: This order lets the Senate special committee investigating wool production, transportation, and marketing inspect certain income, profits, and capital stock tax returns. The returns covered are those made under several revenue laws and the National Industrial Recovery Act. Inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

7481.s: This order creates the Interdepartmental Committee to Coordinate Health and Welfare Activities and names its members. The committee is told to help coordinate federal health and welfare work, continue existing agreements, and study ways to improve coordination among government agencies.

7480.s: This order exempts Adolph Kress from a law that would otherwise require him to leave federal service at the retirement age. It lets him stay on as chief lithographer in the Geological Survey of the Department of the Interior until July 1, 1937.

7478.s: This order exempts Adrian J. Pieters from the rule that requires certain federal employees to retire at the prescribed age. It lets him stay in service until December 1, 1937.

7477.s: This order exempts William McNeir from compulsory retirement under the cited law. It lets him stay in civilian service until May 1, 1937.

7476.s: This order sets aside about 103.06 acres in Green Bay, Wisconsin, known as Long Tail Point Island, for the Department of Agriculture. It makes the area a refuge and breeding ground for migratory waterfowl and other wildlife, subject to valid existing rights. It also revokes an 1847 order that had reserved the land for lighthouse purposes.

7475.s: This order exempts George G. Hedgcock from the rule that requires some federal workers to retire at a set age. It lets him stay in service until July 1, 1937. It affects Hedgcock, who was a senior pathologist in the Bureau of Plant Industry at the Department of Agriculture.

7474.s: This order extends the limits of the customs port of entry of Brownsville, Texas. It adds a strip of land along 14th Street Road and land around the Brownsville Navigation District, including the turning basin for vessels. This affects the customs area in Brownsville and the added territory.

7473.s: This order exempts Harry Planert from the rule that requires some civilian government workers to be separated at the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until November 1, 1937.

7472.s: This order changes a prior order so Mrs. Ruth Hampton can get classified civil service status from her appointment as Assistant Director of the Division of Territories and Island Possessions in the Department of the Interior. It affects her position and the civil service rules that applied to her appointment.

7471.s: This order temporarily withdraws the described land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for the Interior Department to use as a gaging station site, subject to valid existing rights.

7469.s: This order increases the money available under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1936 for assistance for educational, professional, and clerical persons and for women's projects. It moves the added money from the amounts set aside for public buildings and public utilities. The order also lists the updated amounts available for several classes of public projects under the Act.

7470.s: This order sets rules for authenticating certified copies of public records from foreign countries or their political subdivisions. It also lays out how U.S. consular and diplomatic officers must handle commissions in criminal cases, including taking testimony, using interpreters or stenographers, and returning the commission to court. The order also provides rules for fees and compensation in these cases.

7468.s: This order exempts James W. Sims from the compulsory retirement rule for age. It lets him stay in the civil service as a senior naval architect in the Navy Department until March 31, 1937.

7467.s: This order transfers the Military Reservation known as Benton Field in Alameda, California, to the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy. The land includes two parcels totaling about 1,075.70 acres. The order says this is done in the interest of national defense.

7466.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to buy the Peaks of Otter land tract in the Jefferson National Forest near Bedford, Virginia. It allocates funds for that purchase and directs that the money be transferred for the Department of Agriculture to use. The order says the land is within the forest and that work there is needed to help protect nearby forest lands from fire, floods, soil erosion, plant pests, and disease.

7465.s: This order names who will perform the duties of the Secretary of Agriculture when the Secretary is absent or sick. It gives that role first to the Under Secretary of Agriculture, then to the Assistant Secretary of Agriculture, and then to the Chief of the Weather Bureau if both of the others are absent or sick. It also replaces Executive Order No. 6596.

7464.s: This order extends the trust period for Indian lands, whether tribal or individual, if it would have expired on December 31, 1936 or during 1937. In those cases, the trust period is extended for 25 more years from the date it would otherwise expire. It does not apply where Congress has specifically kept the power to extend the trust period for those lands.

7462.s: This order places Flag Island in Florida under the control of the Secretary of the Interior for disposition under the cited law. It also revokes an earlier executive order that had reserved that land for military purposes.

7461.s: This order places certain lands at the entrance of Mobile Bay in Alabama under the control of the Secretary of the Interior for disposition under the act named in the order. It also revokes a previous order that had reserved those lands for military purposes.

7463.s: This order abolishes Fort Pierce, Florida, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 18 (Florida). The change takes effect thirty days from the date of the order.

7460.s: This order designates Henry A. Wiley as Chairman of the United States Maritime Commission. It affects the United States Maritime Commission and the person named in the order.

7459.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules. It covers certain Public Health Service attendants in hospitals, quarantine stations, sanatoriums, and similar places where registers are impracticable. It also covers employees working on preventive medicine problems with a cooperating State, county, municipality, incorporated organization, or individual, and employees assigned to classified positions while receiving treatment or convalescing at Government sanatoriums.

7458.s: This order transfers the administration of loans and contracts from the Rural Electrification Administration created in 1935 to the Rural Electrification Administration established by the Rural Electrification Act of 1936. It also transfers the records, property, unspent funds, officers, and employees of the earlier administration to the newer one. People moved under this order do not automatically get competitive classified status, but some may qualify if they meet the stated conditions.

7456.s: This order exempts Lemuel W. Bean from the rule that requires civilian workers to be separated when they reach the retirement age. It lets him stay in service as a customs agent in the Bureau of Customs, Treasury Department, until October 1, 1937.

7457.s: This order exempts Bernard H. Lane, an editor with the Geological Survey in the Department of the Interior, from the rule that requires retirement at the set age for automatic separation from service. It lets him stay in service until October 1, 1937.

7455.s: This order exempts Henry W. Langheim from the compulsory retirement rule for federal civilian service. It lets him stay in service until October 1, 1937.

7454.s: This order revokes two earlier executive orders that had withdrawn public lands in two Arizona townships pending resurvey. It applies to the townships named in those orders. The order takes effect when the official plats of resurvey are filed.

7453.s: The order revokes an earlier withdrawal for a tract of public land in California. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for use as a lookout station for Federal and State cooperative forest-protection work, subject to valid existing rights.

7452.s: The order reserves and sets aside about 4,266.62 acres in Minnesota and Wisconsin for the Upper Mississippi River Wild Life and Fish Refuge. The lands are to be used by the Department of Agriculture as a breeding place for wild birds, game and fur-bearing animals, fish, other aquatic life, wild flowers, and aquatic plants, subject to valid existing rights.

7451.s: This order transfers control and jurisdiction of a part of the San Diego Barracks in San Diego, California, from the Secretary of War to the Secretary of the Navy. The property is a military reservation block in San Diego. It is done in the interest of the national defense.

7450.s: This order excuses certain federal employees in the District of Columbia from duty until 1 p.m. on Wednesday, September 23, 1936. It applies to employees of executive departments, independent establishments, other government agencies, the Government Printing Office, and the Navy Yard and stations who want to join citizens in honoring Civil War veterans at the Grand Army of the Republic parade. It does not apply to employees excluded for special public reasons or to those whose absence would conflict with existing law.

7449.s: This order amends diplomatic and consular rules on government property, private messages, office locations, naval aircraft visits, legal process, fees, and other consular duties. It requires detailed inventories of government property, sets rules for handling gifts from foreign governments, and limits when consular officers may serve legal papers. It also changes rules for Chinese visa documents, Foreign Service pay, and several consular fee items.

7448.s: This order revokes two earlier land withdrawals in Alaska for the described tracts of land. It then withdraws those lands from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves them for use by the War Department as a receiving station for the Alaska Communication System at Anchorage, Alaska.

7447.s: This order gives the United States High Commissioner to the Commonwealth of the Philippine Islands certain duties in extradition cases. He must receive requests from the Commonwealth for the extradition of fugitives found in foreign countries and send them to the Secretary of State, with some requests allowed to go directly to an American ambassador or consular officer. He is also authorized to receive requests from foreign governments for extradition from the Commonwealth and send those requests to the Chief Executive of the Commonwealth.

7446.s: This order changes part of a prior order about appointments paid from emergency funds. It says that a person moving from one executive department, independent establishment, or administrative agency to another through a Civil Service Commission certificate will not be covered by those two paragraphs. Such a person may not be paid more than the certificate allows and may not be promoted or get a pay raise for six months after starting the job.

7445.s: This order exempts Miss Mary M. O'Reilly from the rule that requires certain federal workers to retire at the set retirement age. It lets her stay in service as Assistant Director of the Mint until November 1, 1937.

7444.s: This order exempts Harry D. Myers from the law on automatic retirement for age. It lets him stay in service until November 1, 1937. Myers is a vice consul and clerk in the American Consulate General at Panama.

7441.s: This order revokes earlier withdrawals of certain public lands in Oregon and then temporarily withdraws some of those lands again. The lands are reserved for use by the Forest Service as lookout stations connected to the Siskiyou National Forest. It also revokes two other orders that had withdrawn different Oregon lands for the same purpose.

7440.s: This order exempts Charles B. Sornborger from a retirement rule that would otherwise separate him from civilian service when he reaches the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until October 1, 1937. It applies to Sornborger, an assistant chief clerk and appointment clerk at the Department of Justice.

7442.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are reserved for use by the War Department as an enlargement of a target range used by the New Mexico National Guard. It also modifies earlier executive orders as needed to make this order effective.

7438.s: This order exempts George S. Rice from the rule that would require his retirement at the usual retirement age. It lets him stay in civilian service as chief mining engineer in the Bureau of Mines until October 1, 1937.

7439.s: This order changes the Consular Regulations to expand what consular officers report to the Department of State and other government offices. It requires reports on commerce, industry, transportation, and foreign firms, and says officers should send voluntary reports on matters that may help American business concerns or the Government. It also says consular officers are not authorized to act as arbitrators in trade disputes or as agents.

7437.s: This order reserves about 706.94 acres in Trempealeau County, Wisconsin, for the Department of Agriculture. The land is set aside as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife, subject to valid existing rights. It will be known as the Trempealeau Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7436.s: This order changes the rules for emergency crop loans made through the Farm Credit Administration. It sets a $200 limit for most loans to one borrower and a $400 limit for loans for the production of winter wheat, counting earlier loans under the same rules. It also says applicants must show they cannot get the loan from another source, and farmers with small cash needs get preference.

7434.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6123, which had withdrawn public lands in a township in Colorado while a resurvey was pending. It takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7435.s: The order sets aside public lands in Nevada as the Winnemucca Migratory Bird Refuge. It withdraws the land from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The reservation is subject to valid existing rights, and the land may still be used by the Department of the Interior for irrigation and other incidental purposes.

7432.s: This order allows Mrs. Gertrude Pullman Evans to be appointed to a classified job in the Navy Department without following the Civil Service Rules. It says she is the widow of Captain Franck Taylor Evans and was left without adequate means of continued support.

7433.s: This order amends rules for youth employment on projects under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 and 1936. It says the Works Progress Administration will determine the maximum and minimum hours, conditions of employment, and monthly earnings for young people eligible for National Youth Administration benefits and employed on National Youth Administration and Works Progress Administration projects, other than student-aid projects. For part-time work, monthly earnings may not be more than 50% of the schedule set in Executive Order No. 7046.

7431.s: This order exempts George C. Havenner from a law that would normally require retirement at the automatic separation age. It lets him stay in service until October 1, 1937. The order applies only to him.

7430.s: The order revokes a prior withdrawal for a tract of public land in Oregon. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for use by the Forest Service as a lookout site for the Siskiyou National Forest. Valid existing rights are not affected.

7428.s: This order exempts William E. Cotton from the law on compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in his federal job as principal veterinarian in the Bureau of Animal Industry until October 1, 1937.

7429.s: This order adds certain lands in Utah to the Uinta National Forest, subject to valid existing claims. It says the new reservation replaces an earlier temporary withdrawal for those lands that was made by Executive Order No. 6910.

7427.s: This order revokes a Civil Service Rules exception for certain jobs at the United States Naval Academy, including baker helpers, coffeemen, firemen, linenmen, pantrymen, dish pantrymen, scullions, utility men, waiters, head waiter, and assistant head waiter. Those positions are returned to the competitive classified service. Current workers in those jobs may acquire an appropriate civil-service status under a civil service rule.

7426.s: This order names Ronald Ransom as Vice Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. He is to serve in that role for four years.

7425.s: This order withdraws certain lands in Wyoming from settlement, sale, entry, or other appropriation. It reserves the land for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and other wildlife, subject to valid existing rights. The reservation is also subject to the Department of the Interior’s use of the land for irrigation and incidental purposes. It also replaces an earlier withdrawal and revokes a prior order that had established the Pathfinder Bird Refuge.

7424.s: The order transfers about 430 acres in Pope County, Illinois, from the Resettlement Administration to the Department of Agriculture. The land is to be used as a soil conservation experimental station.

7423.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules by removing one paragraph from Schedule B and rewriting another. It applies to certain positions in the Bureau of Indian Affairs in Washington, D.C., and in the field, where applicants are of one-fourth or more Indian blood and are not already excepted from examination under Schedule A.

7422.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules to add a new temporary worker category for the forest service. It covers guards, scalers, field assistants for reconnaissance parties, foremen on road or trail construction, and telephone operators hired during fire danger season or when special work needs extra help. These employees may serve only as long as needed and not beyond the usual field season, and appointments should come from eligible registers when practicable.

7420.s: This order exempts William T. Marshall from the rule that requires some federal civilian workers to leave service at the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until August 1, 1937.

7419.s: This order exempts Charles Lee Cooke from compulsory retirement for age. It allows him to stay in service until August 1, 1937.

7421.s: This order sets the procedure for filling vacancies for postmasters in first, second, and third class post offices when a vacancy happens because of death, resignation, removal, or the end of a term. The Postmaster General may recommend the incumbent or a promoted postal employee if the Civil Service Commission finds that person eligible, or the Commission may hold an open competitive examination and certify the results. Only people who have been bona fide patrons of the office for at least one year may take the exams, and people who have passed their sixty-seventh birthday are generally barred unless they are already in the postal service or fall under the military preference rule. It also gives military preference to some World War, Spanish-American War, and Philippine insurrection veterans and supersedes prior orders on postmaster appointments.

7418.s: The order authorizes the United States to acquire the Yorktown Hotel property inside Colonial National Historical Park in Virginia. It sets aside money for that land purchase and says the land can be used for Emergency Conservation Work. The work includes tree planting, fire breaks, flood control, seeding, trail and building construction, and restoring historical earthworks. It says the land acquisition will help protect the park and provide employment for unemployed citizens of the United States.

7417.s: This order reserves certain lands in Idaho as the Minidoka Wildlife Refuge for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and other wildlife. It withdraws those lands from settlement, location, sale, entry, or other appropriation, subject to valid existing rights. The reservation is subject to the Department of the Interior’s use of the land for irrigation and incidental purposes.

7416.s: This order revokes part of a prior order that had allowed settlement on certain public lands in Alaska. It keeps that permission for the listed tracts and changes another order so those tracts can be entered under the homestead laws as extended to Alaska.

7415.s: This order revokes parts of earlier orders that had withdrawn certain public lands in Nevada and Utah for use by the Department of Commerce as air-navigation sites. It applies only to the lands listed in the order that are no longer required for that purpose.

7414.s: This order sets the grades and ratings for enlisted men of the Regular Army during fiscal year 1937. It also sets maximum numbers for each grade and for each specialist rating, and says the total number of enlisted men in those grades and ratings may not go over the limits listed.

7413.s: This order exempts Edward M. Weeks from the law on automatic retirement for age. It allows him to stay in service until September 1, 1937. The order applies to him as a civilian employee of the Bureau of Engraving and Printing in the Treasury Department.

7411.s: This order makes certain income, profits, and capital stock tax returns open to inspection by the Senate Committee on Education and Labor or an authorized subcommittee. The inspection is for an investigation into violations of the rights of free speech and assembly and interference with the right of labor to organize and bargain collectively.

7410.s: This order sets rules for sick leave for civilian officers and employees of the United States, the District of Columbia, and certain corporations covered by the law. It says sick leave with pay may be granted for sickness, injury, pregnancy and confinement, or certain family and contagious disease situations. It also sets how sick leave is earned, carried over, advanced, charged, and documented, and lists groups of employees who are not covered.

7409.s: This order sets rules for annual leave for civilian officers and employees of the United States, the District of Columbia, and certain corporations covered by the law. It sets how leave is earned, used, charged, and carried over, and it limits leave for some employees while excluding several groups from the rules. It also ratifies earlier temporary leave rules and revokes other leave rules that conflict with these regulations.

7408.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule II for people already holding a job when that job is moved into the competitive classified civil service. It allows them to get competitive civil service status if they were appointed at least 60 days before the change, are recommended by their department head, pass any noncompetitive fitness tests, and are U.S. citizens who are not disqualified under other civil service rules or laws. It affects current employees in positions that become subject to competitive examination, along with their department heads and the Civil Service Commission.

7407.s: This order reserves a described area of land in the Canal Zone as the Quarry Heights Military Reservation. It places the reservation under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of War, while keeping it subject to the civil jurisdiction of Canal Zone authorities. It also replaces earlier orders on the same reservation and releases any land covered by those older orders that is not included here.

7406.s: This order changes two earlier power site reserves in Colorado only as needed so the Secretary of the Interior can approve two right-of-way applications for a railroad company. The railroad route described runs from a point in one section to another point in Colorado.

7405.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules to add a new job category for certain workers in areas outside the continental limits of the United States. It lets the War Department hire any person in those areas, except the Canal Zone and Alaska, when the Secretary of War thinks the best interests of the service require it.

7404.s: This order amends Civil Service Rules to let the Navy Department hire people in areas outside the continental limits of the United States, except the Canal Zone and Alaska. It applies when the Secretary of the Navy thinks the best interests of the service require it.

7402.s: This order changes an earlier order that had temporarily withdrawn certain public lands in some states. It allows the Secretary of the Interior to withdraw the listed public land tracts in California for reclamation purposes under the law named in the order.

7403.s: This order changes a rule about paying losses to officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States in foreign countries when foreign currencies change against the American dollar. It says the rule also applies while they are serving on United States vessels stationed in foreign waters, and a vessel is considered stationed there from its first arrival in a foreign port or jurisdiction if it stays sixty or more consecutive days in foreign waters.

7401.s: This order exempts Henry Blackwood from the rule that would have required his automatic retirement for age. It allows him to stay in civilian service in the Customs Service, Treasury Department, until July 1, 1937.

7400.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to add a new category to Schedule A. It covers local veterinarians paid on a fee basis or part-time basis when the Civil Service Commission thinks making registers is impracticable.

7399.s: This order reserves a tract of land in the Canal Zone for use as a naval reservation called U.S. Naval Radio Station, Summit, Canal Zone. It places the land under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy, while still subject to the civil jurisdiction of the Canal Zone Government. The reserved tract contains 249.63 acres.

7398.s: This order directs Charles O. Gregory, the Solicitor of Labor, to perform the duties of Secretary of Labor when the Secretary and the Assistant Secretary are absent. It affects the Department of Labor during those absences.

7396.s: This order says money under the 1936 relief act must be spent and managed under earlier orders, rules, and regulations from the 1935 relief act, except for pay rates and eligibility for employment. It also lets the Works Progress Administration keep providing relief and work relief on useful projects under the 1936 act. The agency may make its own rules as needed, so long as they do not conflict with the order.

7397.s: This order establishes the Federal Fire Council as an advisory agency on protecting Federal employees and property from fire. It sets up a governing body, names who will serve on it, and says members serve without extra pay. The Council may develop standards and procedures, conduct surveys and other investigations, review plans for new construction, study Federal buildings and property, and keep a record of fire losses on Government property.

7395.s: This order exempts Miss Jessie McL. Watson from the rule requiring automatic retirement at age. It lets her continue serving in the Library of Congress until August 1, 1937.

7394.s: This order exempts Benjamin F. Taylor from compulsory retirement under the cited law. It lets him stay in service until August 1, 1937.

7393.s: This order amends Civil Service Rule Schedule A to add one special assistant to the Secretary in the Office of the Secretary. It affects the Civil Service Rules and the Office of the Secretary.

7391.s: This order adds about 22,870 acres in Georgia and South Carolina to the Savannah River Wildlife Refuge. The land is reserved for the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights and future use for navigation. Private lands in the area become part of the refuge when the United States acquires title to them or leases them.

7390.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations under Executive Order No. 6166 that were not already carried out before June 30, 1936. It also delays related provisions tied to section 4 of that order until December 31, 1936. The Secretary of the Treasury, with the President's approval, may make any of those changes effective between June 30, 1936, and December 31, 1936.

7388.s: This order changes a prior order on public lands so the Secretary of the Interior can withdraw certain tracts of public land in New Mexico for reclamation purposes. It applies to the public lands described in the order.

7389.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule IX on reinstatement. It says a person with classified civil service status, or eligibility for it through competitive examination, who is separated without delinquency or misconduct from a civilian Federal job may be reinstated if the Commission gives a certificate, subject to limits.

7386.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal for one tract of public land in Colorado. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for use by the Forest Service as an administrative site for the Arapaho National Forest, subject to valid existing rights and an outstanding power-site reservation.

7387.s: This order reserves a tract of land in the Canal Zone for use as a naval reservation called Naval Station, Balboa, Canal Zone. It places the area under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy, while keeping it subject to the civil jurisdiction of Canal Zone authorities. It also replaces two earlier executive orders that set aside sites in the Canal Zone for naval reservations.

7384.s: This order appoints Thomas Neblett and Rose Turlin as members of the National Advisory Committee of the National Youth Administration. It amends an earlier order to add their names to the committee.

7385.s: This order exempts John V. Shea from the rule that requires some federal workers to retire at a certain age. It lets him stay in service until July 1, 1937. Shea is identified as a senior clerk in the Division of Supply at the Treasury Department.

7383.s: The order adds about 900 acres in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana, to the Delta Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. The land, along with buildings, pipe lines, and wharves on it, is set aside for the Department of Agriculture, but the Treasury Department may still use it for quarantine purposes.

7382.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 7357 and partly revokes a 1912 order that withdrew certain public lands in Arizona. It affects Lots 1 to 14 and NW¼SE¼ of Section 36 in Township 23 South, Range 24 East, Gila and Salt River Meridian. It is meant to allow title to the described lands, if not otherwise reserved or withdrawn, to vest in the State of Arizona, subject to existing valid mining claims.

7380.s: This order exempts Vincent Pierro from the rule requiring automatic retirement at the retirement age. It lets him stay in federal service as a laborer with the White House Buildings and Grounds until June 1, 1937.

7381.s: This order transfers possession and control of part of Tract No. 2 at the Charleston Quartermaster Intermediate Depot in Charleston, South Carolina, back to the War Department. The land is to be used for military purposes for as long as the President thinks it is needed. The order says this is to help maintain and supervise the adjoining Charleston Ordnance Depot.

7379.s: The order changes the fee schedule for U.S. consular visa services for aliens. It sets fees for immigration visas, passport visas, and visas for alien crew lists, and it says some transit certificate services are free. It also says no fee is collected for certain foreign government officers and their immediate family, armed forces, or state, district, or municipal members.

7377.s: This order transfers control and jurisdiction of part of the former United States Naval Destroyer and Submarine Base at Squantum, Massachusetts, to the Secretary of the Navy. The land is about 468 acres of fast and tide lands south of the described boundary line. It affects land that had been under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of War.

7378.s: This order adds the listed lands in Utah to the Cache National Forest. It says the reservation will not interfere with existing legal rights or public uses on lands already appropriated or reserved for public purposes other than classification, flood control, or watershed protection. It also replaces earlier withdrawals and reservations of these lands for classification, flood control, and watershed protection.

7375.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 4289 from 1925. That earlier order had withdrawn and reserved certain land in Arizona for use by the War Department as an emergency landing field for airplanes connected to the Army Air Service.

7376.s: This order revokes a 1933 order that had withdrawn public lands in townships 9 and 10 south, range 8 west, in New Mexico, while a resurvey was pending. It becomes effective when the official plats of resurvey for those townships are filed.

7374.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6499, which had withdrawn certain public lands in New Mexico pending a resurvey. The change applies to the township named in the order and takes effect when the official resurvey plat is filed.

7373.s: This order withdraws certain lands in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, or entry and sets them aside for wildlife conservation and development, and for the protection and improvement of public grazing lands and natural forage resources. It says mineral prospecting, mining, leasing, and patenting may continue under applicable laws. The range is to be managed by the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture for wildlife purposes, with some lands also available for grazing under the stated rules.

7371.s: This order changes the pay rules for the emergency conservation work program. It says that, under rules set by the Director, no more than 6% of any Civilian Conservation Corps Company may get a cash allowance of $45 a month, and no more than an additional 9% may get $36 a month. The allowances are for rewarding energetic effort and outstanding leadership.

7370.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules for the United States Military Academy at West Point. It excludes the civilian instructor positions for wrestling, boxing, and gymnastics from the listed civil service paragraph, while leaving the other covered professors, instructors, teachers, and the librarian position in place.

7372.s: This order changes the numbering of a new subdivision added to Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules, from XXV to XXVI. It affects the Civil Service Rules and the section created by Executive Order No. 7228.

7368.s: This order reserves Jarvis Island, Baker Island, and Howland Island and places them under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Interior for administrative purposes. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

7369.s: This order changes an earlier rule that generally barred federal officers and employees from holding state or local offices. It allows certain Indian Service employees in medical or sanitary jobs to hold similar state, county, or municipal positions if the Secretary of the Interior agrees. Their outside work cannot interfere with their federal duties, and full-time employees cannot get extra pay for it.

7367.s: This order allows Mrs. Eva Sweeney to be appointed to a classified job in the Department of Agriculture without following the Civil Service Act and rules. It says she is the widow of John P. Sweeney, who worked in the department, and that she was left with six minor children and without adequate means of support.

7366.s: This order lets the first appointments to certain Social Security Board jobs be made without following the competitive Civil Service Act and rules. The positions include regional office managers and secretaries or clerks for board members, the executive director, the coordinator, the general counsel, and bureau directors. People named for these jobs still have to show the Civil Service Commission that they have the needed qualifications.

7365.s: This order says the Second Export-Import Bank of Washington, D.C., will stop being an agency of the United States on June 30, 1936. Its stockholders must wind up and liquidate its remaining business, property, and affairs under District of Columbia law. The bank's remaining funds must be sent to the Treasury of the United States, and its records must be transferred to the Export-Import Bank of Washington.

7364.s: This order adds certain public lands in Nevada to the existing Charles Sheldon Wildlife Refuge. It withdraws those lands from settlement, sale, entry, and other appropriation, subject to valid existing rights. The lands are reserved for the Department of Agriculture, and this order replaces an earlier temporary withdrawal for those lands.

7362.s: This order revokes part of two earlier orders that had withdrawn certain public lands in Wyoming from use while a resurvey was pending. It applies to the listed townships in the sixth principal meridian area and takes effect when the official plats of resurvey are filed.

7361.s: This order amends a previous order about Carson National Forest land in New Mexico. It adds about 37,000 acres in the Rio Pueblo de Taos watershed to the land withdrawn from entry or other disposition. The change affects land within the Carson National Forest described in the order.

7360.s: This order partially revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn certain public lands in two New Mexico townships pending a resurvey. The revocation applies to those townships and takes effect when the official plats of resurvey are filed.
