7359.s: This order adds certain lands in Wisconsin to the Nicolet National Forest. The lands are subject to existing valid claims. It also replaces an earlier temporary withdrawal for those lands.

7363.s: This order changes a prior order that had withdrawn public land in certain states. It allows the exchange, sale, or leasing of lands covered by that order if valid existing rights are protected, the Secretary of the Interior decides the lands are fit for that use, and they are not needed for any public purpose.

7357.s: This order partially revokes a 1912 withdrawal of certain public lands in Arizona. It applies to Lots 1 to 14 and NW¼ SE¼ of Section 37 in Township 23 South, Range 24 East, Gila and Salt River Meridian. The order says this is to allow title to the lands not otherwise reserved to vest in the State of Arizona, subject to valid existing claims.

7356.s: This order transfers a portion of the Camp Eagle Pass Military Reservation in Eagle Pass, Texas, to the Treasury Department. The land is to be used by the Public Health Service. The transfer covers a tract of 52,500 square feet.

7358.s: This order reinstates Earl L. Packer and Vinton Chapin in the Foreign Service of the United States. Their reinstatement would take effect when the Senate confirms their nominations to the listed classes. Packer is named as a Foreign Service officer, Class IV, and Chapin as a Foreign Service officer, Class VI.

7355.s: This order revokes a 1933 order that had withdrawn public lands in a township in Colorado while a resurvey was pending. It takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey for that township is filed.

7354.s: This order changes an earlier order to allow the Alaska Road Commission to use one townsite lot in Nenana for airport purposes. The land is set apart for that use, but it stays under the earlier reservation for any other purpose. If the land is no longer needed for the airport use, it remains subject to the earlier order.

7353.s: This order excludes a 3.30-acre tract of land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest. It restores that land to entry under the public-land laws. The tract is identified as a homesite near mile post No. 20 and Lakeview Station on the Alaska Railroad.

7352.s: This order removes several homesite tracts in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It restores those lands to entry under the public-land laws. The tracts are identified by lot numbers or locations in Alaska, including sites on Revillagigedo Island, Wrangell Island, Chichagof Island, and near Auke Lake.

7350.s: This order lets the Special Committee Investigating Old Age Pension Organizations inspect income, profits, and capital stock tax returns. It applies to returns made under the Revenue Act of 1934, the National Industrial Recovery Act, the Revenue Act of 1932 as amended, and prior Revenue Acts. The inspection must follow the rules and regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

7351.s: This order says Mrs. Lucille Coy Dailey may be appointed to a position in the classified civil service without following the Civil Service Rules. It says she is the widow of a United States Navy radioman who died in the U.S.S. Macon disaster, and that she was left without adequate means of continued support.

7348.s: This order exempts Harvey A. Harding from the rule requiring retirement at the automatic separation age. It lets him stay in service until May 1, 1937. It affects Harding, who was an adviser to the Comptroller of the Tennessee Valley Authority.

7347.s: This order changes rules for separate contracts on foundations for housing projects supervised by the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works and paid for with funds from the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It requires the contractor building the superstructure to do at least 15% of the project directly, without subcontracting, using the same way of calculating the amount as before.

7346.s: This order allows William J. Butler to be appointed to the position of Park Ranger in the National Park Service. It says this appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

7345.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to use allocated funds to acquire real property or an interest in it. The land may be acquired by purchase, condemnation, or other means for game bird and animal refuges and for migratory bird sanctuaries and refuges.

7343.s: This order revokes part of Power Site Reserve No. 191 in Utah. It removes the reserve status from the listed lands and unsurveyed portions near Fremont River.

7344.s: This order revokes a 1932 order that had withdrawn public lands in one township in Colorado while a resurvey was pending. It will take effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed for that township.

7342.s: This order says a provisional organization for the Railroad Retirement Board should be set up right away under the Railroad Retirement Act of 1935. It allows the first appointments to certain executive jobs on the Board to be made without the usual competitive civil service process. People chosen for those jobs still have to show that they have the needed qualifications.

7341.s: This order adds described lands in Modoc and Siskiyou Counties, California, to the Tule Lake Wildlife Refuge. The land is reserved for the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. It also says the land may still be used by the Department of the Interior for reclamation purposes and is subject to a land exchange law.

7340.s: This order lets the Administrator of the Works Progress Administration make and adopt an official seal for the agency. The seal must be a design the Administrator approves.

7339.s: This order temporarily withdraws a described piece of public land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for use of the Reindeer Service in the Department of the Interior. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it, and it is subject to valid existing rights.

7338.s: This order names the Honorable Martin Travieso, an associate justice of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico, to act as judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico. He may perform the judge’s duties and sign needed papers and records when the judge is absent during the current calendar year.

7337.s: This order changes a prior order that had temporarily withdrawn public lands in certain states. It allows the Secretary of the Interior to withdraw the listed public land tract in Oregon for reclamation purposes. It affects the described land and other public lands covered by the earlier order.

7336.s: This order exempts Frank Hahn from a rule that would require some civilian employees to leave service when they reach retirement age. It keeps him in service until May 1, 1937. The order affects Frank Hahn, who worked for the Geological Survey in the Department of the Interior.

7335.s: This order revokes a 1930 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Nevada pending a resurvey. It becomes effective when the official plat of the resurvey of that township is filed.

7334.s: This order raises the spending limit for the Civilian Conservation Corps under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It increases the limit from $600,000,000 to $700,000,000.

7333.s: This order changes parts of Executive Order 7070 about hiring employees paid from emergency funds. It says those parts do not apply to transfers of people who, at the time of transfer, are working part time or are paid under Executive Order 7046 or any change to it.

7332.s: This order changes an older rule that kept most federal officers and employees from holding state, municipal, or other local offices. It lets National Park Service employees, with approval from the Secretary of the Interior, accept appointments as deputy sheriffs in the states or territories where they are on duty. Their work as deputy sheriffs must be unpaid and must not interfere with their National Park Service duties.

7331.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Montana from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The lands are to be used by the War Department in connection with the Fort Peck Dam and Reservoir project. It applies to the specifically described lands listed in the order, including about 914.87 acres.

7330.s: This order changes an earlier order on public lands in certain states. It lets the Secretary of the Interior withdraw listed public lands in California for reclamation purposes. The order applies to the specific tracts named in the document.

7329.s: The order authorizes the United States to acquire privately owned land near Petersburg National Military Park in Virginia. It says the land will be used for Emergency Conservation Work, including tree planting, fire break maintenance, seeding, sodding, trails, buildings, and restoration of historical earthworks. It also says the work will help protect the park from insect infestation, fire, and soil erosion, and provide employment for unemployed citizens of the United States.

7327.s: This order revokes a prior order that had withdrawn public lands in one township in New Mexico while a resurvey was pending. It takes effect when the official resurvey plat for that township is filed.

7328.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6267, which had withdrawn public lands in two townships in New Mexico pending resurvey. It becomes effective when the official plats of resurvey for those townships are filed.

7326.s: This order revokes part of a 1932 order that had withdrawn public lands in one township in Colorado while a resurvey was pending. It becomes effective when the official plat of resurvey for that township is filed.

7325.s: This order revokes part of a 1914 order for a tract of land in Alaska identified as Survey No. 2158, containing 26.16 acres. It then withdraws and reserves that tract for town-site entry under the act of March 3, 1891.

7323.s: This order creates a Committee of Industrial Analysis to finish a summary of the results and accomplishments of the National Recovery Administration and prepare a final review for the President. The committee includes the Secretary of Commerce as chairman, along with the Secretaries of Agriculture and Labor, and other people the President may appoint. It also creates a Division of Industrial Economics to help the committee and makes certain records, equipment, and property from the National Recovery Administration available to them.

7324.s: This order designates George L. Berry as Coordinator for Industrial Cooperation. He is to arrange and supervise conferences of industry, investors, labor, and consumers, and report to the President on ways to help provide employment and improve industrial, commercial, and labor standards as they affect employment. He serves without salary, may hire staff and incur necessary expenses, and the Secretary of Commerce must provide space and equipment for his work.

7321.s: This order authorizes the heads of departments and independent establishments to issue temporary rules on annual and sick leave. Those rules must follow the law and apply in their own departments and establishments until uniform regulations are put out under the two acts.

7320.s: This order revokes the earlier military withdrawal of 680 acres of public land in North Dakota. It then withdraws the land from settlement, sale, entry, or other use under the public-land laws. The land is reserved for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife.

7322.s: This order lets the House of Representatives managers in the impeachment of Judge Halsted L. Ritter inspect tax returns. The inspection must follow rules and regulations approved by the President and the Secretary of the Treasury.

7319.s: This order amends rules for student-aid projects under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It says these projects give financial help to needy young people so they can stay in primary school, high school, college, or graduate school in exchange for part-time work on useful projects. It also sets payment limits for primary and high school students, college students, and graduate students.

7317.s: This order exempts Milton L. Leffler from the rule requiring retirement at the age set for automatic separation from service. It lets him continue serving in the Federal Trade Commission until May 1, 1937.

7318.s: This order allows Louis Hunter Gwinn to be appointed as a Customs Agent in the Customs Service of the Treasury Department without following the Civil Service Rules. It affects Mr. Gwinn and the Customs Service job he may fill.

7316.s: This order reserves a United States-owned area in Charleston County, South Carolina, as an addition to the Cape Romain Migratory Bird Refuge. The land includes Bull Island and the buildings on it, and it is subject to valid existing rights. It places the area under the use of the Department of Agriculture.

7315.s: This order exempts William Gerig from the rule that required certain federal civilian workers to retire at the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until April 1, 1937.

7314.s: This order exempts Miss Mary G. Wilmarth, a chief scientific aid in the Geological Survey, from the rule requiring automatic separation at retirement age. It lets her continue in service until May 1, 1937.

7313.s: This order revokes a 1905 order that reserved a tract of land in Alaska for a lighthouse depot. It also excludes several described tracts in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest and restores them to entry under the public-land laws. The land includes homesites on Revillagigedo Island, Prince of Wales Island, Kupreanof Island, Chichagof Island, and Mitkof Island.

7312.s: This order changes rules for certain United States employees stationed in foreign countries where local laws limit converting local currency into foreign exchange. It lets their net salary and net allowances be converted in another country and allows reimbursement for losses, but not more than would have been reimbursable under the set conversion rules.

7310.s: This order exempts W. H. Moran from the rule that requires some government workers to retire at the set age. It allows him to stay in service until January 1, 1937.

7311.s: This order revokes part of a prior order that had withdrawn public land in Arkansas and some other states. It applies to certain public lands in Arkansas that were classified as chiefly valuable for recreational use. The land described adds up to 520 acres.

7309.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It affects the listed land in the Fairbanks Meridian, subject to valid existing rights, until the President or Congress revokes it.

7308.s: This order exempts Carl F. Jeansen from a rule requiring automatic retirement at age. It allows him to keep working in civilian service with the Navy Department until April 1, 1937. The order says he had already been exempted for one year before this extension.

7307.s: This order exempts Luther L. Browning from the rule requiring automatic retirement at the retirement age. It lets him stay in his job at the Government Printing Office until November 1, 1936.

7305.s: This order sets aside money for the Farm Credit Administration to make loans to farmers in the United States, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico for crop production and livestock feed. It says no loan may be more than $200, and borrowers must show they cannot get the loan from another source. The loans must be secured by a first lien on crops or livestock, and they bear interest at 5½ per centum per annum.

7304.s: This order changes civil-service rules to allow certain employees of the Bureau of the Census in the Department of Commerce to be appointed as collectors of cotton statistics. It applies when their total pay is not more than $540 a year. It says these appointments are meant to fall under civil-service rules for similar part-time and intermittent federal jobs.

7303.s: This order withdraws a 40-acre tract of public land in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry, subject to valid existing rights. It reserves the land for use by the Forest Service as a lookout station for the Siskiyou National Forest. It also revokes an earlier withdrawal order for that tract.

7302.s: The order transfers certain lands in the Virgin Islands from the control of the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of the Navy. The lands are to be used to establish, build, and operate aviation facilities. It also keeps two areas out of the transfer: the east beach and bath house fronting on Lindbergh Bay, and the existing golf house and its connected recreational facilities.

7300.s: This order exempts Henry C. Stuart from the rule that required certain government workers to retire at the set retirement age. It allows him to stay in service until March 1, 1937. He was serving as assistant collector of customs in the Bureau of Customs, Treasury Department, in New York, New York.

7301.s: This order adds about 3,880 acres in Cherry County, Nebraska, to the Niobrara Reservation for the use of the Department of Agriculture. The land is subject to valid existing rights. Any private land in the area will become part of the reservation if the United States acquires title to it or leases it.

7299.s: This order reserves Kure (Ocean) Island and the surrounding reef and places them under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy for naval purposes. It applies to the island, which is under the sovereignty of the Territory of Hawaii.

7298.s: This order sets rules for how executive orders and proclamations must be written, reviewed, filed, published, and distributed. It requires proposed orders and proclamations to go through the Bureau of the Budget, the Attorney General, and the Division of the Federal Register before they are sent to the President. It also requires signed originals and copies to be sent to the National Archives, and it does not apply to treaties, conventions, protocols, or other international agreements.

7297.s: This order lets the Secretary of State, as chairman of the National Munitions Control Board, grant licenses for exporting tin-plate scrap. The licenses must follow conditions and rules that the Secretary finds necessary to give fair and equal consideration to all producers of this commodity.

7296.s: This order amends an earlier rule on wages, hours, and working conditions under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It lets the Administrator of the Works Progress Administration require workers to make up lost time, without extra pay, if the Administrator believes it will speed up the work program.

7295.s: The order sets aside certain public lands in Montana as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also allows part of the land to be used as a shooting area under a cooperative agreement or lease with the Montana State Game Commission or another approved agency. The reservation is subject to the Department of the Interior using the land for irrigation and other incidental purposes, and to any existing valid rights.

7293.s: This order sets rules for quarters and subsistence allowances for enlisted men in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Survey, and Public Health Service when they are not given quarters or rations in kind. It gives different daily allowance amounts for duty at stations and for travel, including special rules for certain places and for detention during travel. It also replaces several earlier executive orders on the same subject.

7292.s: This order sets aside about 365 acres in Charles Mix County, South Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It also says any private land in the described area will become part of the refuge if the United States gets title to it or leases it. The refuge is to be known as the Lake Andes Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7291.s: This order exempts Charles J. Evans, an appraiser of merchandise in the Bureau of Customs, from the rule requiring retirement at a set age. It lets him stay in the service until March 1, 1937.

7289.s: This order changes a previous order that had temporarily withdrawn public lands in certain states. It lets the Secretary of the Interior withdraw the listed public land tracts in California for reclamation purposes.

7288.s: This order transfers a portion of the Mayaguez Barracks Military Reservation in Mayaguez, Puerto Rico, from the War Department to the Treasury Department for Federal building purposes. If the land stops being used for that purpose and the Treasury Department gives formal notice, control and jurisdiction return to the War Department.

7286.s: This order exempts Charles Holzman, a clerk at the United States Soldiers' Home in Washington, D.C., from the rule requiring automatic retirement at age. It allows him to stay in service until March 1, 1937.

7287.s: This order sets how members of the Central Statistical Board are selected. Six members are designated by certain federal officers from among officials or employees under their direction, and seven members are elected by the Chairman and the six designated members. It also sets terms of membership and says vacancies are filled in the manner described in the order.

7285.s: This order sets an official flag for the Vice President of the United States. It says the flag must follow the plan and design that go with the order.

7284-B.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5709, which had withdrawn public lands in a township in California while a resurvey was pending. It becomes effective when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7284-A.s: This order revokes part of a 1932 order that had withdrawn public lands in a township in Wyoming while a resurvey was pending. It becomes effective when the official plat of the resurvey for that township is filed.

7284.s: This order revokes a 1933 order that had withdrawn public lands in township 4 north, range 18 west of the New Mexico principal meridian, pending resurvey. It affects those public lands in New Mexico and becomes effective when the official plat of resurvey is filed.

7283.s: This order revokes a 1931 order that had withdrawn public lands in certain townships in New Mexico while a resurvey was pending. It affects the public lands in Townships 24 and 25 North, Ranges 10 and 11 West of the New Mexico principal meridian. The order takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7282.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5920, which had withdrawn public lands in townships 21 and 22 south, range 3 east of the New Mexico principal meridian, pending a resurvey. It becomes effective when the official filing of the plats of resurvey for those townships is made.

7281.s: This order designates Marriner S. Eccles as Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. He is to serve in that role for a four-year term.

7280-B.s: This order revokes part of a prior order that had withdrawn public lands in a township in Wyoming pending a resurvey. It applies to that township and becomes effective when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7280-A.s: This order revokes part of a 1927 order that had withdrawn public lands in a township in Wyoming while a resurvey was pending. The revocation applies to that township and takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7280.s: This order states that the Federal Housing Administration was created under the National Housing Act and that a Federal Housing Administrator was appointed. It also validates and confirms that creation. It affects the Federal Housing Administration and the Federal Housing Administrator.

7279.s: This order revokes part of an earlier order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Arizona, specifically the township named in the order, while a resurvey was pending. The revocation takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7278.s: This order exempts William H. Ramsey, a senior attorney in the Department of Justice, from the rule that requires certain government workers to retire at the set age. It lets him stay in service until February 1, 1937.

7277.s: This order says the Under Secretary of the Interior must do the Secretary of the Interior’s duties when the Secretary is absent or sick. If both the Secretary and Under Secretary are absent or sick, the First Assistant Secretary, or the Assistant Secretary if needed, must do those duties instead.

7275.s: This order revokes part of a 1931 order that had withdrawn public lands in one township in Wyoming pending a resurvey. It takes effect when the official filing of the plat of resurvey for that township is made.

7276.s: This order allows Lewis R. Barrett to be appointed as Recreation Coordinator in the National Capital Parks of the National Park Service, Department of the Interior. It says the appointment may be made without following the civil-service rules and without giving him a classified status.

7274.s: This order changes a prior order that withdrew public land in certain states. It excludes lands that are now, or later become, part of grazing districts established under the act of June 28, 1934, as long as they remain in those districts.

7273.s: This order exempts Benjamin W. Kumler from a rule that would require automatic separation from civilian service at the retirement age. It allows him to stay in service until February 1, 1937. It affects Kumler and the United States Civil Service Commission position he holds.

7272.s: This order revokes a 1930 order that had withdrawn public lands in two Colorado townships while a resurvey was pending. It takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed for those townships.

7271.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Wyoming while a resurvey was pending. It affects the lands listed in the order and takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7269.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6287, which had withdrawn public lands in two New Mexico townships pending a resurvey. It applies to those public lands and takes effect when the official plats of resurvey for those townships are filed.

7268.s: The order directs the Secretary of the Treasury to have a suitable number of Coast Guard vessels cruise along the coast during severe weather when service needs allow. These vessels are to be ready to help distressed navigators as needed. The Commandant of the Coast Guard will assign the vessels for this duty from time to time.

7270.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal for certain public land tracts in Oregon. It then temporarily withdraws those tracts from settlement, location, sale, or entry, and reserves them for use by the Forest Service as lookout stations for the Siskiyou National Forest. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

7267.s: This order changes a prior order that had temporarily withdrawn public land in certain states for classification and other purposes. It lets the Secretary of the Interior withdraw listed tracts of public land in Montana, Nevada, and Wyoming for use by the Department of Commerce to maintain air-navigation facilities. The order lists the land tracts and the acreage in each state.

7266.s: This order changes an earlier order so the Secretary of the Interior can withdraw public lands in a specific area in Wyoming for use as a stock driveway. It affects the public lands in that area and sets out the land description in the order.

7265.s: This order changes an earlier 1912 withdrawal of certain public lands in California as power-site reserve No. 322. It allows the State of California to use the listed land for federal and state cooperative forest-protection work. The state must give up its use of the land and remove any improvements within 60 days after notice from the Secretary of the Interior if the land is needed for storage for power or irrigation purposes.

7264.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5807, which had withdrawn public lands in a township in Colorado while a resurvey was pending. The revocation takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7263.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Treasury authority to act on the United States’ interests or claims under the bankruptcy law named in the order. It applies to the United States, any agency of the United States, and any corporation, other than the Reconstruction Finance Corporation, that is mostly owned by the United States.

7262.s: This order amends the earlier order that created the Federal Board of Surveys and Maps. It sets up a board made up of representatives from listed government agencies to coordinate map-making and surveying work, standardize results, and avoid duplication. The members are appointed by their agency heads and serve without extra pay. The board must also keep an information office in the United States Geological Survey and give advice on map and survey data to the public and to government agencies.

7261-A.s: This order adds a rule about who may act as hostess at a diplomatic mission when the head of the mission’s wife is not present. It allows only the head of mission’s daughter, mother, or sister, or the wife of the counselor or highest ranking secretary who has a wife present at the post, to serve in that role.

7261.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations under section 4 of Executive Order No. 6166 until June 30, 1936. It applies to actions not already carried out before December 31, 1935, under earlier executive orders. The Secretary of the Treasury, with the President’s approval, may make any of these changes effective between December 31, 1935, and June 30, 1936.

7260.s: This order keeps the Executive Committee on Commercial Policy in place and says it will continue its current work to coordinate the commercial policy of the United States. It sets the committee’s permanent members as representatives from the Department of State, Treasury, Agriculture, Commerce, the United States Tariff Commission, and the Agricultural Adjustment Administration. It also says the committee may add other government representatives with the President’s approval, and that the chairman will be a State Department representative appointed by the Secretary of State.

7259.s: This order allows Frank P. Fallowfield to be appointed as an engineer in the Office of the Chief of Engineers, War Department. It says the appointment may be made without following civil-service rules and without giving him a classified status.

7257.s: This order amends civil-service rules for positions in Alaska that cannot be filled from existing registers, except those in the Customs Service. It also allows former employees who served in excepted positions in Alaska to be reinstated at any time if the appointing officer recommends it and the Civil Service Commission approves it.

7258.s: This order exempts Irvin P. Disney from the rule requiring retirement at the automatic separation age. It lets him stay in service until April 1, 1936. Disney was an examiner of interferences in the United States Patent Office in the Department of Commerce.

7255.s: This order exempts Elton A. Gongwer from a law that requires certain civilian employees to be separated when they reach retirement age. It allows him to stay in service until January 1, 1937.

7256.s: This order changes an earlier order that had temporarily withdrawn certain public lands in some states. It lets the Secretary of the Interior withdraw specific tracts of public land in Oregon for reclamation purposes. The land described totals about 880 acres.

7254.s: This order excludes a tract of land in Alaska, occupied as a homesite, from the Tongass National Forest. It restores that land to entry under the applicable public-land laws.

7252.s: This order ends the National Recovery Administration and the office of its administrator. It moves the Division of Review, the Division of Business Cooperation, and the Advisory Council to the Department of Commerce, and it moves the Consumers' Division to the Department of Labor. It also says people transferred by the order do not get civil service status, and new appointments may be made without regard to the Civil Service Rules and Regulations.

7251.s: This order assigns radio frequencies to Government radio stations and classes of stations. It lists certain Government experimental stations, independent receiving stations, and rules for when Government stations may use other frequencies for short periods or for experimental operations. It also allows some Government mobile stations to use certain frequencies in exercises or when communicating with non-Government stations, and it says departments must notify other departments before closing a station that is serving them.

7250.s: This order exempts T. Warren Allen from the law requiring certain government workers to retire at the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until January 1, 1937. Allen is identified as a principal highway engineer in the Bureau of Public Roads, Department of Agriculture.

7249.s: This order closes several federal offices in the District of Columbia at 1 p.m. on December 24, 1935, and December 31, 1935. It also excuses federal employees in the District of Columbia and in the field service from duty at those times, except for workers excluded for special public reasons or when their absence would conflict with existing law. For shift workers, the order says they are excused after four hours of work on those dates.

7248.s: This order exempts Andrew Fourchy, an associate civil engineer with the United States Coast Guard, from the rule that requires civilian employees to retire at the set age. It lets him stay in service until January 1, 1937.

7247.s: This order exempts Nelson H. Darton, a senior scientist (geologist) with the Geological Survey in the Department of the Interior, from the rule that requires automatic separation at retirement age. It lets him continue in service until January 1, 1937.

7246.s: This order sets aside about 24,630 acres in Schoolcraft County, Michigan, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Private lands in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to them. It also excludes the public lands in this area from a prior order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Michigan and other states.

7245.s: This order sets aside about 2,200 acres in Day County, South Dakota, as the Waubay Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. It makes the area a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife under the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Any private lands in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires the title or a lease. It also removes the public lands in this area from a previous land-withdrawal order.

7244.s: This order revokes two earlier orders that had withdrawn public lands in two New Mexico townships pending a resurvey. It takes effect when the official plats of resurvey for those townships are filed.

7243.s: This order allows Herbert J. Wollner to be appointed as consulting chemist in the Treasury Department without following the civil-service rules. It affects that appointment in the Treasury Department.

7242.s: This order sets rules for highways, vehicles, and traffic in the Canal Zone. It requires motor vehicle operators and motor vehicles to be licensed, sets license classes and fees, and gives the Governor authority to make and change regulations. It also covers exams, renewals, suspensions, tourist permits, and rules for carrying passengers for hire.

7241.s: This order changes civil-service rules for certain temporary special employees. It removes informers and posse men from the listed positions and adds some special employees in the Bureau of Narcotics. It also limits these appointments to exceptional and unusual cases and says they must be reported to the Civil Service Commission after appointment.

7240.s: This order revokes a 1932 order that had withdrawn public lands in a township in Arizona while a resurvey was pending. It takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7239.s: This order directs that the records, papers, and property of one Railroad Retirement Board be transferred to another Railroad Retirement Board created under the Railroad Retirement Act of 1935. It affects the Railroad Retirement Board and the materials it held.

7237.s: This order adds certain temporary National Park Service jobs to the civil-service rules outside the District of Columbia. The jobs include fire guards, smoke chasers, fire lookout observers, telephone operators, and field assistants in type mapping, insect and tree-disease control, and other protection work or surveys. These workers may be hired only as long as absolutely necessary, and not beyond the usual field season, with appointments made from eligible registers when practical.

7238.s: This order further exempts Thomas M. Thurston from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service until December 1, 1936.

7236.s: This order abolishes the customs ports of entry in Charlotte, North Carolina; Little Rock, Arkansas; and Dubuque, Iowa. It affects the customs collection districts named in the order, and takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

7235.s: This order changes an earlier order withdrawing public lands in certain states. It allows the sale or leasing of lands the Secretary of the Interior decides are proper for that use and not needed for any public purpose. It also says the withdrawal will not block recognition or allowance of bona fide non-metalliferous mining claims.

7234.s: This order lets the Canal Zone Postal Service issue deposit money orders for people who want to deposit savings in post offices there, and no fee is charged. It sets different interest rates for deposit money orders issued before and after certain dates, and says interest is paid when the orders are paid but will not accrue for more than 3 years. It also lets the Governor make detailed rules and revokes four earlier executive orders.

7232.s: This order exempts Frederick D. Henry from a law that would otherwise require automatic separation from service at the retirement age. It lets him stay in his position as Chief Clerk at Freedmen's Hospital until December 1, 1936.

7233.s: This order sets rules for investigations under section 22 of the Agricultural Adjustment Act. It lets the Secretary of Agriculture start preliminary investigations on his own or when asked by an interested party, and it lets him set how such requests must be filed. If the President directs further action, the United States Tariff Commission must investigate, hold hearings, hear from interested people, and make a report with its findings and recommendations. It also covers public notice, confidential information, and how hearing records are handled.

7231.s: This order allows William J. Shaw to be appointed as an inspector in the Customs Service of the Treasury Department in San Francisco, California. His appointment can be made without following the civil-service rules.

7230.s: This order exempts Davis B. Levis from the rule that requires automatic separation at retirement age. It lets him stay in service as vice consul and clerk in the American consulate general at Paris until December 1, 1936.

7229.s: The order reserves about 8,000 acres of land in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana, for the Department of Agriculture. It sets the land apart as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The land is reserved subject to valid existing rights and is to be known as the Delta Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7228.s: This order puts most jobs at the National Training School for Boys into the classified civil service, and future appointments must follow civil-service law and rules. It leaves out the Superintendent, physician-psychiatrist, cottage officers, cottage matrons, and unskilled laborers, who are handled separately. Unskilled-laborer jobs must be filled under labor regulations, and current workers in affected jobs do not get civil-service status unless the Board of Trustees recommends them within 1 year and they pass any required fitness tests.

7226.s: This order changes a rule on wages, hours of work, and conditions of employment under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It lets Works Progress Administration officials exempt certain projects, parts of projects, workers, or activities, and says wage rates will be set based on local wage conditions by the agency supervising the project.

7224-A.s: This order sets document rules for aliens seeking entry into the Philippine Islands. In general, they must show a passport or other travel document and a valid passport visa, or a transit certificate if they are passing through. It also gives the U.S. High Commissioner power to waive these requirements in some cases and says no visa or transit certificate may be granted if entry would be contrary to public safety.

7225.s: This order lets the Treasury Department’s Director of Procurement, and certain staff he names in writing, certify and approve vouchers and disbursement schedules under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It applies to payments for materials, supplies, equipment, transportation charges, and related overhead, or to reimburse the Work Relief Supply Fund for those purchases. The vouchers must have proof that the items were received by the department or agency charged for them.

7224.s: This order changes the rules for commutation of rations and quarters by adding the American Legation in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, to the list. It also adds a special table entry for that legation with subsistence and quarters amounts. The change affects enlisted men connected with that legation.

7223.s: This order puts the jobs of junior assistant to technician in the Civilian Conservation Corps under the competitive classified civil service. The first exam for each camp is limited to enrollees of the Civilian Conservation Corps, and current workers whose duties match these jobs may qualify by passing a noncompetitive exam. Future appointments must follow civil-service rules, and workers who do not qualify for retention may be replaced within 60 days after the eligible list is set.

7222.s: This order reserves about 10,108 acres in Wakulla County, Florida, for the Department of Agriculture as an addition to the St. Marks Migratory Bird Refuge. It applies subject to valid existing rights. Any private lands in the area will become part of the refuge when the United States gets title or a lease to them.

7221-A.s: This order exempts Miss Caledonia McCall from a rule that would require automatic separation from civilian service after reaching retirement age. It allows her to stay in service in the Office of the Register of the Treasury until November 1, 1936.

7221.s: This order sets aside about 7,790 acres in Aitkin County, Minnesota, as a refuge and brooding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The land is reserved for the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands inside the described area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to them.

7220.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal for a specific tract of public land in California. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for use as a powder-storage site connected to the Stanislaus National Forest. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

7218.s: This order revokes part of a 1932 order that had withdrawn public lands in a township in Colorado while a resurvey was pending. The revocation applies to that township and takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7219.s: This order changes an earlier reservation of certain lands at Nenana, Alaska, so the vacant parts of listed townsite blocks can be used for an airport. The airport is to be built by the Alaska Road Commission. The lands stay reserved for the townsite except for this airport use, and if they are no longer needed for that use, they remain subject to the earlier order.

7217.s: This order exempts Carleton W. Sturtevant from the rule that would require him to retire because of age. It lets him stay in federal service until May 1, 1936. It applies only to Sturtevant, who is a principal engineer in the War Department.

7215.s: This order changes control of certain government-owned land between the War Department and the Navy Department. It sets North Island in California, Ford Island in Hawaii, and part of Bolling Field in the District of Columbia for naval reservations, and it sets the Naval Air Station in Sunnyvale, California, for an Army reservation. It also says the Army and Navy must vacate the listed areas as soon as practicable, with some existing installations left in place or moved only under certain conditions.

7214.s: This order sets aside about 3,654 acres in Bailey County, Texas for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The land is subject to valid existing rights. Private lands in the listed areas would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to them.

7213.s: The order designates Coast Guard vessels to patrol the territorial waters of the United States. They are to enforce the Northern Pacific Halibut Act and the convention for preserving halibut fisheries in the Northern Pacific Ocean and the Bering Sea.

7212.s: This order adds certain lands in Wabasha County, Minnesota, and Buffalo County, Wisconsin, to the Upper Mississippi River Wild Life and Fish Refuge. The lands are set aside for the Department of Agriculture to use as a breeding place for migratory birds, other wild birds, game animals, fur-bearing animals, fish, other aquatic animal life, wild flowers, and aquatic plants. The lands remain subject to valid existing rights and to the War Department’s use of them for improving navigation in the Mississippi River.

7211.s: This order changes a prior order to let the Secretary of the Interior withdraw certain public land tracts in Idaho and Utah. The land is to be used by the Department of Commerce to maintain air-navigation facilities.

7210.s: This order amends civil-service rules by adding a new Schedule A category for the office of the United States High Commissioner to the Philippine Islands. It covers junior messengers and under clerks with a salary range of $180 to $250 a year in that office.

7209.s: This order changes the civil-service rules to allow temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers for part-time or intermittent work in the Postal Service. It applies to work connected with the current holiday or seasonal business and lasts until February 1, 1936.

7208.s: This order exempts George G. Hedgcock from a law that requires retirement after reaching the automatic separation age. It lets him stay in civilian service with the Department of Agriculture until November 1, 1936.

7206.s: This order extends trust periods on Indian allotted or tribal lands in Oklahoma that would expire during calendar year 1936. The extension lasts 10 years from the date the trust would otherwise expire. It does not apply to cases where Congress has kept the power to extend the trust period on tribal or individual Indian lands.

7207.s:
This order adds an Executive Secretary office to the Quetico-Superior Committee. The office is to be held by a committee member selected by the committee, and the committee sets the pay.

It also says the committee’s work on conserving natural resources is within the scope of the National Industrial Recovery Act and the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It authorizes funds, as determined by the President, for the committee’s administrative expenses, travel and per diem, and the Executive Secretary’s compensation.

7205.s: This order exempts William McNeir from the rule that required some federal civilian workers to retire at a set age. It lets him stay in service until November 1, 1936. McNeir was Chief of the Bureau of Accounts in the Department of State.

7204.s: This order changes the rules for workers on a federal relief project who get free board and lodging in camps or lodging houses near the project site. Their monthly earnings are reduced by a charge set by the supervising agency, but the deduction cannot be more than $15 a month for each worker.

7203.s: This order changes a wage rule in a prior executive order about work under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It says the monthly earnings schedule for a county, or sometimes a township, will be based on the 1930 population of the largest municipality in that county or township. The Works Progress Administrator or people he designates may decide whether the schedule applies to a township.

7201.s: This order lets the named people be appointed to positions in the Federal Communications Commission without regard to their standings on the Civil Service registers for professional positions. It says they passed the Civil Service examinations for those jobs and had served under temporary appointments for more than a year. The order says their services should be retained in the interest of good administration and economy.

7202.s: This order appoints five people as members of the Prison Industries Reorganization Board, including Joseph N. Ulman as chairman. It also says board members may be paid necessary expenses for attending and traveling to meetings, and Louis N. Robinson will be paid $25.00 per day for attending meetings.

7199.s: This order directs John Monroe Johnson, the Assistant Secretary of Commerce, to perform the duties of the Secretary of Commerce when the Secretary and another Assistant Secretary are absent. It affects the Department of Commerce and applies only during those absences.

7200.s: This order changes the work of the Resettlement Administration. It gives the agency authority to run approved projects for rural rehabilitation, relief in hard-hit farming areas, and resettlement of destitute or low-income families from rural and urban areas. It also lets the agency start and administer approved projects for soil erosion, stream pollution, seacoast erosion, reforestation, forestation, flood control, and other useful projects.

7197.s: This order changes part of an earlier rule on appointments of employees paid from emergency funds. It says those paragraphs do not apply when certain workers move to full-time jobs in the Resettlement Administration. It covers people who are part-time or per diem federal employees, or who are paid partly by the federal government and partly by a state or local government.

7198.s: The order directs Charles West, the Under Secretary of the Interior, to perform the duties of the Secretary of the Interior when the Secretary is absent or sick. It affects the Department of the Interior and names who will serve in that role during those times.

7196.s: This order exempts Wendell W. Mischler from the compulsory retirement rule for age. Mischler is the secretary to the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States. It lets him stay in service until December 1, 1937.

7195.s: This order puts the positions of junior assistant to technician in the administration of the Civilian Conservation Corps into the competitive classified civil service. It says the first examination for each Civilian Conservation Corps camp must be limited to enrollees of the Civilian Conservation Corps. It also revokes part of Executive Order No. 6126 where it conflicts with this order.

7194.s: This order creates the Prison Industries Reorganization Administration and a five-member board appointed by the President. It directs the agency to study prison industries in the states, political subdivisions, and the District of Columbia, and to recommend projects to reorganize them. It also allows the agency to recommend loans or grants and to oversee approved projects aimed at reducing competition with private industry, eliminating idleness, and providing rehabilitation for inmates.

7193.s: The order designates George L. Berry as Coordinator for Industrial Cooperation. He is to supervise conferences of industry, labor, and consumers on industrial recovery, unemployment, and business and labor standards. He is also to coordinate and report to the President on National Recovery Administration personnel matters and receive certain proposed provisions from the Federal Trade Commission for the President's review.

7192.s: This order gives the Federal Trade Commission the President’s authority to approve certain trade practice provisions in voluntary agreements under the National Industrial Recovery Act. The Commission may do this only if the agreements include labor provisions that meet section 7(a) of that law and after those labor provisions are approved by the President.

7191.s: This order excludes certain homesite tracts in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It restores those tracts to entry under the applicable public-land laws. The change affects the listed homesites in places such as Auke Bay, Kuiu Island, Tee Harbor, Wrangell, and George Inlet.

7190.s: This order changes a previous order about acquiring land on Isle Royale for emergency conservation work. It replaces one funding reference with another, saying the work will use funds appropriated or made available by the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935.

7189.s: This order excludes a 3.11-acre tract of land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest. It restores the land to entry under the applicable public-land laws. The tract is described as a homesite near Snow River on the Seward Highway.

7188.s: This order exempts Miss Mary M. O'Reilly from the rule requiring automatic separation at retirement age. It allows her to stay in her job in the Treasury Department until November 1, 1936.

7186.s: This order increases the spending limit for loans or grants under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 from $900,000,000 to $1,700,000,000. It applies to projects for States, Territories, Possessions, their subdivisions and agencies, municipalities, the District of Columbia, and self-liquidating projects of public bodies.

7187.s: This order exempts Albert S. Hitchcock from the rule that would require his automatic separation from federal service at retirement age. It allows him to stay in service until October 1, 1936. The order applies to Hitchcock, who is the principal botanist in the Bureau of Plant Industry at the Department of Agriculture.

7185.s: This order reserves certain lands in Buffalo County, Wisconsin, for use by the Department of Agriculture as part of the Upper Mississippi River Wild Life and Fish Refuge. The lands are to be used as a breeding place for migratory birds, other wild birds, game animals, fur-bearing animals, fish, other aquatic animal life, wild flowers, and aquatic plants. The order says the reservation is subject to valid existing rights and to the War Department’s use of the land for improving navigation in the Mississippi River.

7184.s: This order exempts James E. Ives, a senior physicist in the Public Health Service, from the rule that required certain civilian employees to retire at the automatic separation age. It allows him to stay in service until October 1, 1936.

7183-A.s: This order directs the Secretary of War to proceed with construction of the Bluestone Reservoir Project on New River in West Virginia. The project is described as serving power development, flood control, navigation, agriculture, sanitation, and power production. It also allocates funds for the project and for buying and clearing land needed for it.

7182.s: This order changes Executive Order No. 7098 so it applies to one described parcel of public land in Nevada. It also revokes that earlier order for a different described parcel of public land in Nevada. Both parcels are listed as 200 acres.

7183.s: This order adds about 1,847 acres of land in Garden County, Nebraska, to the Crescent Lake Wildlife Refuge. The land is reserved for the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private land in the described areas would become part of the refuge when the United States gets title or a lease to it.

7180.s: This order sets rules for loans made by the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration. The loans may help farmers, farm tenants, croppers, or farm laborers buy farm land and needed equipment for farm and rural community products. The loans may go to individuals or approved associations and similar groups, with conditions on membership, supervision, interest rates, repayment terms, and what can happen if a loan is not repaid.

7181.s: The order allows the first appointments to certain executive jobs in the Bureau of Motor Carriers to be made without the Civil Service Act’s competitive hiring rules. It says the people chosen must still show the Civil Service Commission that they have the needed qualifications. It affects the listed positions in that bureau.

7179.s: This order excludes a tract of land on the north shore of Tenakee Inlet on Chichagof Island, Alaska, from the Tongass National Forest. The land is described as being occupied as an Indian settlement and contains 16.71 acres, more or less.

7178.s: This order withdrew certain public lands in Nevada and Oregon from settlement, sale, location, or entry and set them aside for wildlife conservation and for the protection and improvement of public grazing lands and natural forage resources. It placed the preserve under the joint jurisdiction of the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture for rules on protection, administration, and the removal of surplus game animals. It also barred hunting, trapping, disturbing wildlife, damaging government property, starting fires, and entering or using the preserve except under the rules, while allowing fishing in line with state law and those rules.

7177.s: This order revokes part of a 1926 executive order that set aside a reservoir-site reserve in California. The change applies to the specific land described in Mount Diablo Meridian, Township 35 North, Range 8 West, section 21, southeast quarter of the northeast quarter.

7176.s: This order returns certain lands on the east slope of Punchbowl in Honolulu, Oahu, to the Government of the Territory of Hawaii. The lands had been set aside for a United States Marine Hospital and for an experiment station, but they were no longer needed for those uses. The order says the land is needed by the Territory of Hawaii for highway construction.

7175.s: This order revokes part of a 1927 order that had withdrawn public lands in certain townships in Colorado. It applies to townships 50 and 51 North, ranges 2, 3, and 4 East of the New Mexico principal meridian. The revocation takes effect when the official plats of resurvey are filed.

7173.s: This order sets aside about 110,000 acres in Arkansas as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It places the land under the use of the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands inside the area become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to them.

7174.s: This order changes a previous executive order so it also applies to several additional United States agencies and instrumentalities. It covers the Agricultural Adjustment Administration, Commodity Credit Corporation, Federal Coordinator of Transportation, Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works, Federal Emergency Relief Administration, National Recovery Administration, and Tennessee Valley Authority. It also changes the date for part of the rule for these agencies from September 15, 1935 to October 15, 1935.

7172.s: This order adds about 37,000 acres in Beaverhead County, Montana, to the Red Rock Lakes Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. The land is reserved for the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private land in the area would become part of the refuge when the United States acquires title or a lease to it.

7171.s: This order sets aside land in Burke and Mountrail Counties, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It says the land is for use by the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands inside the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to them.

7170.s: The order sets aside about 40,000 acres in Bottineau and McHenry Counties, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It places the land under the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or leases them.

7169.s: This order sets aside about 23,103 acres in Brown County, South Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Private lands in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to them. The refuge is called the Sand Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7168.s: This order reserves lands in Foster and Stutsman Counties, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It says private lands in the area will become part of the refuge when the United States acquires title or a lease to them. The refuge is to be known as the Arrow-wood Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7167.s: This order exempts Joseph L. Smith from the rule that requires some civilian workers to retire at the set retirement age. It lets him stay in service until August 31, 1936. The order applies only to Smith and his position as a mechanician in the Senate Office Building under the Office of the Architect of the Capitol.

7166.s: The order exempts Miss Annie N. Travis, a senior clerk in the Treasury Department, from the rule that requires retirement at the set age. It allows her to stay in government service until March 1, 1936.

7165.s: This order requires written decisions on overassessments of income, profits, estate, and gift taxes that are allowed in excess of $20,000 to be prepared. It also says those decisions must be open to public inspection. The Secretary of the Treasury is to prescribe the regulations for this public inspection.

7164.s: This order sets rules for student-aid projects funded under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It says these projects help needy young people stay in high school, college, or graduate school in exchange for part-time work on useful projects. It also places student-aid projects under the National Youth Administration and lets eligible young people work on Works Progress Administration projects under set pay and hour limits.

7162.s: This order exempts Daniel L. Hazard, a mathematician under the Coast and Geodetic Survey in the Department of Commerce, from the rule that requires retirement at the automatic separation age. It lets him stay in service until March 1, 1936.

7161.s: This order sets aside about 40,000 acres in Renville and Ward Counties, North Dakota, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. Private lands inside the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to them. The refuge is to be known as the Upper Souris Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7160.s: This order sets aside lands in Bennett County, South Dakota, as the Lacreek Migratory Waterfowl Refuge. The lands are to be used by the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to them.

7155.s: This order exempts Wilbur John Carr, an Assistant Secretary of State, from the rule that requires retirement at a set age. It allows him to stay in federal service for as long as needed, for up to five years from October 31, 1935.

7159.s: This order appoints Laurence J. Martin of Virginia as Acting Administrator of the National Recovery Administration. He replaces James L. O'Neill, who resigned.

7158-A.s: This order tells leaders of federal departments and agencies to report cases where contractors, subcontractors, or government officers require or allow a person to work more than 8 hours in one calendar day on certain public works. Those reports must go up the chain and then be sent to the Department of Justice for action. It also replaces an earlier order from 1906 on the same subject.

7158.s: This order opens certain income, profits, and capital-stock tax returns to inspection by the Senate Committee on Interstate Commerce and any authorized subcommittee. The access is for an investigation of interstate railroads and their affiliates, including financing, reorganizations, mergers, and other matters. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

7157.s: This order sets rules for wages of unattached workers on projects funded by the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. The Works Progress Administration may exempt some projects or classes of work where workers are given subsistence in a federally supervised camp, and may pay those workers monthly earnings of up to $25 in addition to subsistence. The order says this exemption cannot be used if it would create different wage scales for workers at the same location doing the same kind of work.

7156.s: This order sets aside lands in Holt County, Missouri, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wild life. The lands are to be used by the Department of Agriculture and are subject to valid existing rights. Private lands in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease to them. The refuge is called the Squaw Creek Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7154-A.s: This order sets aside about 24,100 acres in Burke and Ward Counties, North Dakota, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The lands are reserved for the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease. The refuge is called the Des Lacs Migratory Waterfowl Refuge.

7153.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5681, which had withdrawn public lands in a township in California. The revocation takes effect when the official filing of the plat of resurvey for that township is made.

7154.s: This order creates the Camden Board of Arbitration to handle a labor dispute at the Camden, New Jersey, yard of the New York Shipbuilding Corporation. The board is to investigate the disputed issues, hear evidence, make findings, and prepare arbitration awards on wages, work rules, and working conditions. It also asks the company and the union to file agreements to follow the board’s awards, end the strike, and keep the plant operating under the old agreement until a new one is reached.

7152.s: This order gives the Temporary Government of the Virgin Islands new duties to run approved relief and work relief projects to increase employment. It also lets the government carry out remaining work from earlier Virgin Islands projects and transfer assets and records from the Resettlement Administration. The order allows spending on supplies, travel, rent, vehicles, printing, and other incidental expenses, and it lets the Governor hire staff and use volunteer or local help, with a preference for people receiving relief when practical.

7151.s: This order sets up a $3,000,000 special fund in the Treasury Department called the "Work Relief Supply Fund." The fund is for buying and distributing materials, supplies, and equipment through the Treasury Department’s Procurement Division. Departments and agencies that request these items must reimburse the fund at prices set by the Director of Procurement, with approval from the Secretary of the Treasury. The fund is subject to audit, and any surplus must be handled as the order directs.

7150.s: This order amends a prior order to make its budget rules apply to several additional U.S. agencies and instrumentalities. Those agencies are the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, Federal Surplus Relief Administration, Export-Import Bank of Washington, Second Export-Import Bank of Washington, D.C., Reconstruction Finance Corporation, and Electric Home and Farm Authority. It also changes the date when one part of that prior order applies to these agencies.

7148.s: This order sets aside about 23,700 acres in Sheridan and Roosevelt Counties, Montana, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The land is reserved for the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands inside the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or a lease.

7149.s: This order asks executive departments and other government agencies to help the Senate Committee on Interstate Commerce and any authorized subcommittee. It says they should give access to relevant records, papers, and information when the public interest allows, and make their experts available when reasonably possible without interrupting normal business.

7147.s: This order revokes part of a 1929 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in two townships in Colorado while a resurvey was pending. The revocation will take effect when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

7146.s: This order changes an earlier order that temporarily withdrew public land in certain states. It authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to withdraw listed tracts of public land in California, Montana, and Nevada for use by the Department of Commerce. The land is to be used for the maintenance of air-navigation facilities.

7144.s: This order removes a tract of land on Chichagof Island, Alaska, from the Tongass National Forest. The land is described as being occupied as an Indian settlement.

7145.s: This order removes certain homesite tracts in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It restores those tracts to entry under the public-land laws. The land listed includes homesites on Revillagigedo Island and Kuiu Island.

7142.s: This order sets aside land in Cherry County, Nebraska, as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The land is to be used by the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. Private lands in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title to them or leases them.

7143.s: This order sets rules for loans made by the Resettlement Administration. The loans may help farmers, farm tenants, croppers, and farm laborers buy farm land and needed equipment, and may also be used for approved rural rehabilitation or relief projects in stricken agricultural areas. Loans may go to individuals or approved agencies and cooperative associations, with interest set between 3 percent and 5 percent a year and loan terms up to 40 years.

7140.s: This order allows Mrs. Ruth Hampton of Illinois to be appointed as Assistant Director of the Division of Territories and Island Possessions in the Department of the Interior. It says the appointment may be made without following civil-service rules and without giving her a classified status.

7141.s: This order designates Harvey M. Hutchinson, an associate justice of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico, to perform the duties of the judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico. He may sign needed papers and records as acting judge when the judge is absent during the current calendar year.

7138.s: This order sets aside the airspace over certain military and naval reservations and other listed areas for government use. Civil aircraft are forbidden to operate in those airspaces unless they get special permission from the government department in charge. People who violate the order or the Air Commerce Act of 1926 are subject to the penalties in that law.

7139.s: This order designates the Electric Home and Farm Authority, a District of Columbia corporation, as an agency of the United States. It lets that agency continue the functions and business of the Delaware Electric Home and Farm Authority, Inc., as allowed by its charter. It also rescinds a prior order about who would vote the company’s stock and directs that the stock be voted jointly by the trustees of the District of Columbia corporation.

7137.s: This order changes civil service rule II on appointments without examination. It allows certain excepted positions in schedule A, schedule B, or other excepted positions to be filled without examination or with a noncompetitive examination. If those positions are filled as classified positions are filled, the person appointed may be eligible for transfer, reinstatement, or promotion in the classified service. It also says people in these excepted positions do not get the removal protection of the rules, and some excepted-by-law positions do not get Civil Service Retirement Act benefits just from that employment.

7136.s: This order revokes part of a 1910 executive order that had created Coal Land Withdrawal, New Mexico No. 1. It applies only to the listed lands in New Mexico. The rest of the earlier order is not changed by this action.

7134.s: This order excludes a small tract of land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest. It restores that homesite to entry under the public-land laws. The land is Homesite No. 26 on the south shore of the Kenai River.

7135.s: This order temporarily withdraws a tract of land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for use by the Department of War as a site for a radio station. The area is tide land on the Gastineau Channel and contains 227.09 acres, more or less.

7133.s: This order revokes a 1931 executive order that had withdrawn public lands in a township in California while a resurvey was pending. The revocation takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

7132.s: This order revokes part of Executive Order No. 5098, which had withdrawn public lands in Wyoming while a resurvey was pending. The revocation applies to the listed townships and takes effect when the official plats of resurvey are filed.

7131.s: This order revokes part of a 1928 order that had withdrawn public lands in Wyoming pending a resurvey. It applies to the listed townships in Wyoming and takes effect when the official resurvey plats are filed.

7130.s: This order sets rules for rural electrification projects financed by the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 and overseen by the Rural Electrification Administration. It allows loans for projects of private corporations, associations, cooperatives, States, Territories, Possessions, municipalities, and the District of Columbia, and it gives the Administrator control over loan contracts and how projects are carried out. It also sets wage and hour rules, gives preference to workers from the public relief rolls, and requires workers to be certified by the United States Employment Service or approved by the Rural Electrification Administration.

7129-A.s: This order requires reports about loading and unloading petroleum and petroleum products moved in interstate or foreign commerce. It applies to the master, owner, or authorized agent of certain vessels that take on petroleum or petroleum products at ports in Texas or Louisiana. It also applies when those vessels unload such cargo at any port in the United States. The reports must be sent to the Division of Investigations in the Department of the Interior.

7128.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, entry, or other form of appropriation. It reserves those lands to conserve the public interests and to help with future legislation. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

7129.s: This order authorizes the United States to acquire privately owned land on Isle Royale in Lake Superior, using purchase, condemnation, or other means. It says the land is needed to help protect nearby public lands from disease, forest fires, floods, soil erosion, and plant pests. It also says the acquisition will provide work for unemployed citizens of the United States.

7127.s: This order puts the lands and improvements in the named military reservations in Alaska under the control of the Secretary of the Interior. The Secretary may keep parts of those reservations for the Alaska Road Commission and dispose of the rest as allowed by law. The order says these reservations are no longer needed for military purposes.

7126-A.s: This order revokes part of a previous executive order for certain public lands in Alaska. It changes the status of the listed lands in the Seward Meridian area, which had been temporarily withdrawn from settlement and other forms of appropriation.

7126.s: This order asks several federal housing and farm credit agencies to send their yearly estimates for administrative expenses to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget. It also says they should not make administrative spending commitments after September 15, 1935, unless the Director approves the estimates first.

7125.s: This order changes the rules for hiring workers on projects under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It says only people certified for assignment by the United States Employment Service may be employed on those projects. It also lets the Works Progress Administrator, or someone he designates, change that rule for a project or part of a project.

7124.s: This order changes a prior order about appointments of employees paid from emergency funds. It says transfers of Federal Emergency Relief Administration employees working in Massachusetts, Ohio, Louisiana, Georgia, and North Dakota will not be covered by paragraphs 3 and 4 of the earlier order.

7123.s: This order appoints named people to serve as members of the National Advisory Committee of the National Youth Administration. The members serve without compensation, except for necessary transportation expenses and an allowance of twenty-five dollars for each calendar day they are necessarily away from home while doing the committee’s work.

7122.s: This order exempts Mrs. Frances N. Westcott from the rule that required retirement at a set age for certain government civilian workers. It lets her stay in service until January 1, 1936.

7121.s: This order extends the existence of the National Labor Relations Board until September 1, 1935. It changes an earlier order by replacing the date "August 1, 1935" with "September 1, 1935."

7120-A.s: This order exempts William H. Nelson, a park ranger at Yosemite National Park, from the rule requiring automatic retirement at a set age. It lets him stay in service until August 1, 1936.

7120.s: This order recreates the office of Adviser on Consumers' Problems and places that adviser on the National Emergency Council.
