It also creates a Consumers' Division within the National Recovery Administration to work on consumer problems, public policy, research, and information sharing. The order transfers certain consumer-related functions, records, and county council oversight to that division.

7119.s: This order changes a rule under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It lets the Works Progress Administration Administrator exempt certain projects, parts of projects, or activities. For those projects, the agency in charge will set wage rates based on local wage conditions.

7118.s: This order corrects a mistake in Executive Order No. 7082 about land in Montana connected to Blackfeet National Forest. It changes the township section number from 26 to 36 in that earlier order.

7117.s: This order changes the wage rules for work done under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It lets the Works Progress Administrator, or people he designates, redefine regions when needed to avoid unequal wage rates among similar workers. It also says that when a project covers more than one wage schedule, the highest applicable schedule must be used, and local earnings may be adjusted up or down by no more than 10 percent.

7116.s: This order adds certain lands in the Wichita National Forest in Oklahoma to the Wichita National Game Preserve for use by the Department of Agriculture, subject to valid existing rights. It makes it unlawful in the area to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds, or to take or destroy nests or eggs. It also bars people from entering or using the area except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture, and from cutting, burning, or destroying natural growth or damaging U.S. property.

7114.s: This order changes an earlier order to let the Secretary of the Interior withdraw certain public land in Montana. The land is to be used by the Department of Commerce to maintain air-navigation facilities.

7115.s: This order lets the Special Committee to Investigate Lobbying Activities of the United States Senate, and any authorized subcommittee, inspect certain income, excess-profits, and capital stock tax returns. The inspection is for investigating lobbying activities connected with the holding company bill or any other matter affecting legislation. The committee must follow rules and regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury and approved by the President.

7112.s: This order temporarily withdraws a described piece of public land in Montana from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for public use under the cited law.

7113.s: This order exempts George E. Ladd from the compulsory retirement rule for federal civilian workers. It lets him stay in service until August 1, 1936.

7111.s: This order changes an earlier order that had removed restrictions on certain payments, transfers, and deliveries of property under the Trading with the Enemy Act and the Settlement of War Claims Act. It keeps those restrictions in place for payments to certain German nationals, German organizations, and people or groups with a substantial interest in them. It also covers heirs, representatives, creditors, successors, and assigns of those persons, with limited exceptions stated in the order.

7110.s: This order revokes part of Executive Order No. 5534 for certain lands in Montana. Those lands will not become subject to disposal under the laws for public lands until a later date and after notice is announced.

7107.s: This order exempts certain jobs from Executive Order No. 6746 until June 30, 1937. It applies to consultants, experts, specialists, attorneys, and similar positions paid from funds administered by the Rural Electrification Administrator, when they are hired part time or on a per diem basis.

7105.s: This order changes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in California so a forest-exchange application can be approved. It allows the Secretary of the Interior to patent 110 acres of the withdrawn land to Michigan-California Lumber Co. in exchange for lands of equal value within the boundaries of a national forest in that state. The land was previously withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, or entry pending resurvey.

7106.s: This order reserves about 66,717 acres in Harney County, Oregon, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife, subject to valid existing rights. It excludes parts of the Frenchglen townsite from the reservation. It makes hunting, trapping, disturbing wildlife, cutting natural growth, careless fire use, and damaging government property unlawful within the refuge.

7104.s: This order directs executive departments and other government offices to cooperate with the Board created by the act of June 18, 1934. It also requires them to provide records, papers, and information the Board asks for, and to temporarily detail officers, experts, or engineers to help with the Board’s work on foreign-trade zones.

7103.s: This order changes a Civil Service rule for some government workers whose duties take only part of their time or are needed only for short periods. It allows additional government employment for such a person under similar conditions, with Civil Service Commission approval. It also requires reports to list the employee’s name, job duties, pay rate, and place of employment.

7101.s: This order appoints Charles W. Taussig as Chairman of the National Advisory Committee of the National Youth Administration. He is to serve without compensation, except for necessary travel expenses and a $25 daily allowance when he is away from home for the committee's work.

7102.s: This order exempts certain positions from Executive Order No. 6746 on salary classification. The positions include consultants, experts, specialists, attorneys, and similar jobs. It applies to people who are paid on a per diem basis or on an annual basis for part-time service from public-works or other emergency funds.

7100.s: This order extends the Science Advisory Board under the National Research Council from July 31, 1935, to December 1, 1935. It keeps the board’s present membership, powers, and duties in place during that time.

7099.s: This order exempts Charles Lee Cooke from the rule that required some federal civilian workers to retire at the set retirement age. It lets him stay in service until August 1, 1936.

7098.s: This order amends a prior land withdrawal order to let Nevada select certain public lands in the state. It also allows the Secretary of the Interior to patent those lands to Nevada under the 1926 act.

7097.s: This order allows the Senate Committee on Agriculture and Forestry, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect certain income, excess-profits, and capital-stock tax returns. The inspection is for an investigation into the causes of the rapid decline in the price of cotton on the cotton exchanges around March 11, 1935. It affects returns made under the Revenue Act of 1934, the National Industrial Recovery Act, the Revenue Act of 1932 as amended, and earlier revenue acts.

7096.s: This order appoints five people to serve as members of the Executive Committee of the National Youth Administration. They are to serve without additional compensation. It affects the named officials and the committee they will serve on.

7095.s: This order amends the civil-service rules to include certain confidential positions in the Philippine Islands when they are filled by United States citizens. It also keeps the rule covering some jobs in foreign countries, Guam, Samoa, and the Virgin Islands, while saying the exception does not apply to certain Immigration and Naturalization Service employees in a foreign country contiguous to the United States.

7094.s: This order exempts Miss Jessie McL. Watson from the rule requiring retirement for age. It lets her stay in the service until August 1, 1936. It applies to her work as a reviser in the Catalogue Division of the Library of Congress.

7093.s: This order exempts Benjamin F. Taylor, Chief of the Application Division in the Copyright Office of the Library of Congress, from the rule that requires automatic separation at retirement age. It continues him in service until August 1, 1936.

7092.s: This order lets the heads of agencies set up under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 choose how to classify employee positions and set pay. They may use either the salary schedule in Executive Order No. 6746 or the Classification Act of 1923, as amended. It applies to employees now working in those agencies and to future appointments.

7091.s: This order changes a prior order so the National Steel Labor Relations Board will continue "until further order" instead of ending on July 1, 1935. It affects the board and its continued work under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

7090.s: This order changes an earlier order to keep the National Labor Relations Board in existence until August 1, 1935 instead of July 1, 1935. It affects the National Labor Relations Board and the policy carried out under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

7089.s: This order changes Executive Order No. 7084 so the Textile Labor Relations Board will continue "until further order" instead of ending on July 1, 1935. It affects the Textile Labor Relations Board and the time it stays in place.

7087.s: This order transfers all lands in the Clearwater National Forest in Idaho that lie south and east of the described line to the Lolo National Forest. It does not remove any land from national-forest status, and it does not place any public lands into national-forest status if they did not already have that status.

7085-A.s: This order revokes part of two earlier orders that had withdrawn certain public lands in California and Nevada. It applies to the specific townships and sections listed in the order. The lands affected are in California and Nevada.

7088.s: This order adds a tract of land to the Tongass National Forest in Alaska. The tract is 553.70 acres, more or less. It says existing legal rights, public-land uses, and land reserved for a public purpose are not to be interfered with by this withdrawal.

7086.s: This order creates the National Youth Administration within the Works Progress Administration. It sets up a National Advisory Committee and an Executive Committee, and puts the agency under the general supervision of the WPA Administrator and the immediate supervision of an Executive Director. The agency is to run approved projects that provide relief, work relief, and employment for people who are no longer in regular attendance at a full-time school and are not regularly employed.

7084.s: This order continues the Textile Labor Relations Board until July 1, 1935. The board may mediate disputes between employers and employees in the textile industry that could interfere with the purposes of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The Secretary of Labor must approve the board’s staffing, spending, and rules.

7085.s: This order continues the National Steel Labor Relations Board until July 1, 1935. The board may mediate disputes between employers and employees in the iron and steel industry under the direction of the Secretary of Labor. The board must get the Secretary of Labor’s approval to hire staff, set pay, and take on financial obligations, and no officer or employee may be paid more than $25 per day.

7083.s: This order sets rules for projects funded in whole or in part by the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935, except certain work relief projects run by State Emergency Relief Administrations. It says projects must use one of four methods: force account, fixed price contract, limited fixed price contract, or management contract. It also sets rules for contracts, worker pay, reporting, inspections, and limits on who may be employed on the projects.

7082.s: This order transfers lands in the Blackfeet National Forest in Montana to the Kootenai and Flathead National Forests. It moves lands on one side of a described line to the Kootenai National Forest and lands on the other side to the Flathead National Forest, with some listed tracts eliminated from the Blackfeet National Forest. The order says the Blackfeet National Forest is discontinued as a separate administrative entity.

7080.s: This order exempts Curtis F. Marbut from compulsory retirement for age and lets him stay in federal service until July 1, 1936. It applies to him as a principal soil scientist in the Department of Agriculture.

7081.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6497 from December 15, 1933. That earlier order had amended Executive Order No. 6247, so this action affects that earlier set of executive orders.

7078.s: This order revokes a 1919 order that had withdrawn a tract of public land in Colorado. The land had been reserved for use by the Forest Service as a ranger station for the White River National Forest.

7079.s: This order temporarily withdraws about 16 acres of land in the Territory of Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for the Department of the Interior as a school site at Pilot Point (Ugashik), Alaska, for use by the Office of Indian Affairs.

7077.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations under Executive Order No. 6166. It postpones them until December 31, 1935, unless the Secretary of the Treasury, with the President’s approval, makes any of them effective sooner. It affects the provisions tied to section 4 of that earlier order.

7076.s: This order extends existing executive orders issued under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. It also extends the authority and activities of any agency created under that law until April 1, 1936, as long as they stay within the law as amended. It does not allow approval or enforcement of codes of fair competition, or any other action not authorized by Title I.

7074.s: This order reestablishes the National Labor Relations Board and keeps it in existence until July 1, 1935. It keeps the board’s existing personnel and employees at their current grades and salaries. The board is told to carry out the powers, functions, and duties set out in the earlier order, as allowed under the National Industrial Recovery Act and Senate Joint Resolution No. 113.

7075.s: This order ends the National Industrial Recovery Board and creates an Administrator of the National Recovery Administration to carry out Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. It also creates a Division of Review and a Division of Business Cooperation to study the work of the codes, review their effects, and help trade and industrial groups keep fair competition standards. The order says the administration should cut staff to the number needed to do its work, and it changes earlier orders and rules as needed to make this order effective.

7072.s: This order exempts John V. Shea, a senior clerk in the Treasury Department’s Division of Supply, from the rule that requires automatic retirement at the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until July 1, 1936.

7073.s: This order reestablishes the National Emergency Council as an agency within the Government. It gives the council the duties it was already authorized to perform, plus any additional duties the President assigns under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It also allows the Executive Director to use voluntary services, with state consent to use state and local officers and employees, and to appoint employees without regard to civil-service laws.

7071.s: This order exempts Ozni P. Hood from the law that would require his retirement for age. It lets him stay in civilian service until July 1, 1936. Hood was Chief of the Technologic Branch and Chief Engineer in the Bureau of Mines at the Department of the Interior.

7070.s: This order sets rules for hiring and reappointing employees whose pay comes from emergency funds. It says such appointments must be labeled temporary or emergency, and emergency appointments cannot go past the end of the emergency appropriation or June 30, 1937. It also limits contact between agencies about transferring employees, and it restricts salary increases for transferred employees paid from emergency funds unless the President approves them.

7069.s: This order revokes part of the 1912 order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 325 in California. It removes the reserve status from the listed lands under Mount Diablo Meridian.

7068.s: This order appoints four people to the Advisory Committee on Allotments. The members are to represent the Business Advisory Council, farm organizations, organized labor, and the American Bankers' Association. They will serve without compensation, except for necessary travel expenses and a $25 daily allowance when away from home for committee work.

7067.s: This order abolishes Orange, Texas, as a customs port of entry in customs collection district no. 21, which has headquarters at Port Arthur, Texas. The change takes effect 30 days after the order is signed.

7066.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5942, which had withdrawn certain public lands in New Mexico. The revocation applies to the listed townships and becomes effective when the official plats of resurvey are filed.

7065.s: This order creates the National Resources Committee within the Government. The committee is to collect plans, data, and information for the planned development and use of land, water, and other national resources, and it may work with federal, state, local, and private agencies. It also requires executive agencies to notify the committee about proposed federal land and land research projects before major field activities begin. The order abolishes the National Resources Board and transfers its personnel, property, records, rights, and funds to the new committee.

7063.s: This order lets certain temporary employees of the General Accounting Office keep working past June 30, 1935. It applies to employees appointed under the Emergency Appropriation Act of 1934 and those paid from emergency funds under the National Industrial Recovery Act, and their service may continue until no later than June 30, 1937.

7062.s: This order adds several places to the list of unhealthful posts in the Foreign Service. The places were former consular office locations, including Boma, Muscat, Mersin, Mombasa, Sandakan, Santa Rosalia, and Zanzibar. It affects Foreign Service posts at those locations.

7064.s: This order lets the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works keep doing the functions it was allowed to do under Title II of the National Industrial Recovery Act after June 16, 1935. It also lets the agency make loans or grants for projects for states, territories, possessions, municipalities, and the District of Columbia, and carry out slum-clearance or low-cost housing projects. The order also allows the Administrator to use volunteer services, use State and local officers and employees with State consent, and hire workers without following civil service laws, with workers chosen from those receiving relief when practicable.

7061.s: This order makes Edwin Sheddan Cunningham’s retirement effective on December 31, 1935. It applies to Mr. Cunningham, a Foreign Service officer from Tennessee.

7060.s: This order sets rules for who may be employed on projects funded by the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It says workers must be registered with designated employment offices and have been receiving public relief in May 1935, with some later-eligible persons also allowed to be added. It also says eligible workers stay eligible even if they take other public or private jobs, and that workers on these projects must be accepted or rejected based only on their fitness for the work.

7059-A.s: This order changes the name of the Luquillo National Forest in Puerto Rico to the Caribbean National Forest. It affects the federal forest there by giving it a new official name.

7059.s: This order revokes a 1906 executive order that had set aside certain land and water areas in Alaska for a salmon hatchery. It declares those areas to be part of the Tongass National Forest, including Yes Lake, Yes Bay, Back Bay, and nearby strips of land.

7058.s: This order authorizes the Federal Housing Administrator to make and adopt a seal for the Federal Housing Administration. It also says certified copies of the agency’s books, records, papers, documents, agreements, orders, rules, and regulations can be used in evidence the same as the originals. The Administrator, or someone he designates, may certify copies of these records when needed.

7056.s: This order changes a previous executive order so the Advisory Committee on Allotments includes the Deputy Administrator of the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works. It affects the membership of that committee.

7057.s: This order creates the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration in the Department of the Interior and appoints Ernest H. Gruening as its administrator. The agency is directed to run approved projects for relief, work relief, and increasing employment in Puerto Rico. It also authorizes spending for supplies, travel, vehicles, printing, and other expenses, and lets the administrator acquire and dispose of property when needed.

7055.s: This order allows Fred S. Gilbert to be appointed as an elevator operator in the custodial service of the Post Office Department. It says this appointment may be made without following the civil-service rules.

7054.s: This order exempts Finis D. Morris from a law that would otherwise require him to leave civilian service when he reaches the retirement age for automatic separation. It lets him stay in service until September 1, 1935.

7053.s: This order revokes part of an earlier 1915 order that had withdrawn certain lands in Alaska. It then rewithdraws and reserves those lands for town-site purposes. The affected lands are the parts described in the Alaska Railroad Terminal Reserve.

7051.s: This order allows Guy C. Hanna to be appointed as a non-attorney member of the Committee on Enrollment and Disbarment in the Treasury Department. It says the appointment may be made without following civil-service rules and without giving him classified status.

7050.s: This order exempts Charles Y. Dixon from the law that would require automatic retirement after reaching the retirement age. It lets him stay in his civilian job in the War Department until June 1, 1936.

7049.s: This order places four unsurveyed tracts in Alaska, each known as "Post Cemetery," under the control of the Secretary of the Interior. The tracts are in former military reservations and are to be handled as provided by law.

7047.s: This order changes a previous order that withdrew certain public lands in Alaska. It now allows settlement on those lands.

7048.s: This order amends an earlier order about vacant public land in Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oregon, South Dakota, Utah, and Wyoming. It makes the withdrawal rules apply to lands that later have prior entries, selections, or claims canceled or released, or prior withdrawals revoked unless the revocation says otherwise. It also lets the Secretary of the Interior accept title to base lands in land exchanges under the 1934 act.

7046.s: This order sets wage, hour, and employment rules for work projects financed under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935. It gives monthly pay schedules by region, job type, and city size, and it sets maximum work hours for many workers, with some exceptions for certain projects and employees. It also says workers must be at least 16, gives preference to people from the public relief rolls, and limits most projects to one member of a family group unless the Works Progress Administration allows otherwise.

7045.s: The order changes how two tracts of public land in California are managed. One tract is withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserved for the Department of Agriculture to use as a fire lookout site for the Trinity National Forest. The other tract is also withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserved for classification and other purposes.

7044.s: This order revokes a previous order that changed the location of the land office for the Linkton land district in Oregon from Lakeview to Klamath Falls. It affects the land office for that district.

7042.s: This order exempts Benjamin A. Omohundro from the rule that would have required his automatic separation from civilian service at retirement age. It lets him stay in service until June 1, 1936.

7041.s: This order transfers property, records, contracts, rights, and other interests tied to Section 208 from the Secretary of the Interior and related agents to the Resettlement Administration. It also transfers all personnel now employed under Section 208 to that agency.

7043.s: This order waives a civil-service time limit to allow Mrs. Fern A. Black to be reinstated to a clerical position in the Los Angeles post office. It says she had worked there from July 11, 1918, to March 31, 1920, resigned to be married, and later lost her husband, which left her without adequate means of support for herself and two minor children.

7040.s: This order appoints Perry R. Taylor of Pennsylvania as Executive Officer of the Rural Electrification Administration. He is to carry out the administration’s functions and duties until an Administrator is appointed and qualified. The appointment ends when the Administrator takes office.

7039.s: This order lets the Special Committee Investigating the Munitions Industry of the U.S. Senate inspect certain income and profits tax returns and capital stock tax returns. The committee is investigating the manufacture of and traffic in arms, munitions, and other implements of war. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

7038.s: This order changes a previous withdrawal of oil-shale lands. It allows the Secretary of the Interior to issue sodium permits and leases under the General Leasing Act for lands covered by that earlier order. It affects the withdrawn lands containing oil-shale deposits.

7037.s: This order creates the Rural Electrification Administration in the Government and names an Administrator to lead it. It directs the agency to run a program of approved projects for the generation, transmission, and distribution of electric energy in rural areas. It also allows the Administrator to hire staff, spend money for operating needs, and acquire property if needed for these duties.

7036-D.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Plumbing Contracting Division and certain employees in parts of Lake County and all of Porter County, Indiana. The agreement applies in the region named in the order. The National Industrial Recovery Board may grant exceptions or exemptions from the agreement if needed to carry out the act, the code, or to avoid hardship.

7036-C.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division and certain employees in the Travis County, Texas region. It says the agreement complies with the National Industrial Recovery Act and the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement if needed.

7036-B.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and their painter, paperhanger, and decorator employees in parts of Allegheny County, Pennsylvania. It does not apply to the listed towns, boroughs, and the City of McKeesport, and the National Industrial Recovery Board may grant exceptions or exemptions if needed.

7036.s: This order extends the trust periods on allotments made to Indians of the Yakima Reservation, Washington, that would otherwise expire during 1935. Each covered trust is extended for 10 more years from the date it would have expired.

7036-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and their painter, paperhanger, and decorator employees in Hamilton County, Ohio, and Kenton and Campbell Counties, Kentucky. It applies to the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the construction industry. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement, with or without conditions, if needed to carry out the Act or avoid undue hardship.

7035-C.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division and certain employees in the Region of Centre and certain parts of Clearfield Counties, Pennsylvania. The agreement was reviewed and found to comply with the National Industrial Recovery Act and the Construction Industry code. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement if needed.

7035-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and painter, paperhanger, and decorator employees in the Montclair, Bloomfield, and nearby New Jersey area. It applies to the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the construction industry. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement if needed to carry out the act or avoid undue hardship.

7035-B.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the Construction Industry and their employees in a region of Texas. The region includes Smith, Upshur, Rusk, Henderson, Wood, Gregg, Cherokee, Anderson, and Van Zandt Counties. It also allows the National Industrial Recovery Board to make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement if needed to carry out the act or avoid undue hardship.

7035-D.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the construction industry and certain employees in the Denver area and nearby region. It says the agreement was found to comply with the National Industrial Recovery Act and the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement if needed to carry out the act or avoid undue hardship.

7035.s: The order sets aside Goat Island in Oregon for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for wild birds and animals. It also revokes an earlier withdrawal of that island from public land use. Within the refuge, hunting, trapping, disturbing, killing, cutting vegetation, starting or leaving fires, and damaging U.S. property are unlawful.

7034.s: This order sets up new government offices to handle applications for work projects, review them, and advise on how funds should be allotted. It also creates the Works Progress Administration, which is responsible for carrying out the work relief program and moving as many people as possible from relief rolls to work or private employment. The order directs federal offices to help with payments, purchasing, reporting, and other administration of the program.

7033-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Tile Contracting Division and certain tile setter employees in parts of Pennsylvania, Ohio, and West Virginia. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement if needed to carry out the Act or avoid undue hardship.

7033.s: This order changes the boundaries of the Cibola National Forest in New Mexico by removing a described parcel of land. It allows the Secretary of the Interior to dispose of that land under the act of March 1, 1907.

7032.s: This order temporarily withdraws two unnamed islands in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the islands for use by the Department of Commerce for lighthouse purposes. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

7031.s: This order puts all positions in the United States Railroad Administration that existed on that date into the classified civil service. Future appointments to those jobs must follow civil-service laws and rules. Employees already in those positions do not automatically gain civil-service status, but they may be appointed to classified civil service jobs if they get a recommendation and pass any noncompetitive fitness tests required.

7030.s: This order exempts Charles H. Deetz from the compulsory retirement rule for federal civilian service. It lets him stay in service until May 1, 1936. It applies only to Deetz and the retirement rule named in the order.

7029.s: This order allocates $400,000 to the Department of Agriculture for emergency conservation work. It authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to use certain services and personnel powers for this work. It also allows the acquisition of real property, if necessary, by eminent domain, and says supplies must be acquired under the Treasury and Post Office Act rules.

7028.s: This order transfers certain property, records, contracts, and personnel from the Federal Emergency Relief Administration to the Resettlement Administration. It also lets the Resettlement Administration's administrator manage that property and use the powers tied to it. The order transfers and allocates certain remaining appropriated funds to the Resettlement Administration for the same purposes they were first set aside for.

7026.s: The order revokes a prior withdrawal for a 40-acre tract of public land in California. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for use as a lookout station for Federal and State cooperative forest-protection work.

7027.s: This order creates the Resettlement Administration as a government agency and names Rexford G. Tugwell as its administrator. It directs the agency to run projects to resettle destitute or low-income families from rural and urban areas and to establish communities in rural and suburban areas. It also assigns the agency projects for soil erosion, stream pollution, seacoast erosion, reforestation, forestation, and flood control, and allows it to make loans to certain farmers, farm tenants, croppers, and farm laborers for farm land and equipment.

7025.s: This order appoints Charles Edison to the National Industrial Recovery Board to fill a vacancy caused by the retirement of A. D. Whiteside. It also directs that Edison be given leave without pay from his job as State Director for the National Emergency Council for New Jersey while he serves on the board.

7025-A.s: This order approves a supplementary code of fair competition for the Heavy Construction and Railroad Contractors Subdivision of the construction industry. It also amends the larger construction code to include this addition. The National Industrial Recovery Board may review the section on mutual agreements within 60 days if it may interfere with collective bargaining.

7024-A.s: This order appoints Frank C. Walker as Executive Director of the National Emergency Council. He is to carry out the functions and duties given to that office by earlier executive orders and any additional duties set by the President.

7024.s: This order restores certain lands on the southeast slope of Punchbowl, Honolulu, to the possession, use, and control of the Government of the Territory of Hawaii. The land had been set apart for use by the United States Treasury Department for a Marine-Hospital site, and the Territory needed it for the New Punchbowl Road.

7022.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry. It also changes the previous approval of that code so it now includes the code as amended. It affects the distilled spirits rectifying industry.

7023.s: This order withdraws public lands in Beaverhead County, Montana, and sets them apart for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for wild birds and animals. It revokes part of a prior order for that area. It also makes it unlawful there to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or enter for any purpose except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture, and to damage natural growth, start or leave fires unattended, or injure federal property.

7021.s: This order authorizes the Governor of the Panama Canal to contract with the Panama Railroad Company to operate certain Panama Canal piers. The piers are at the Atlantic Terminal and the Pacific Terminal, and they are owned by the Panama Canal. The company would run the piers with its own funds under terms the Governor considers fair to both sides.

7020.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry. It changes the earlier approval of that code to include the code as amended. It affects the wine industry and those covered by the code.

7019.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Brewing Industry. It also changes the earlier approval of that code so it includes the code as amended. The changes affect the brewing industry.

7018.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry. It also changes the earlier approval so the code is approved in full as amended. This affects the distilled spirits industry and the Federal Alcohol Control Administration’s review of the code.

7017.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry. It also changes the earlier approval of that code so it now includes the code as amended.

7016.s: The order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverages Importing Industry. It changes the earlier approval of that code to include the code as amended. This affects the alcoholic beverages importing industry.

7015.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry. It also changes the earlier approval of that code so it now includes the code as amended. It affects the alcoholic beverage wholesale industry.

7014.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry. It also changes the previous approval so the code is approved in full as amended. The order affects businesses in the alcoholic beverage wholesale industry.

7013.s: This order changes office hours for diplomatic and consular offices. It says they should be open on weekdays and Saturdays, with some changes allowed for local customs, weather, or service needs, and it lists holidays when offices may be closed or do only urgent work. It also changes the rule on official precedence to say the order of precedence is among consular officers.

7012.s: This order changes rules for diplomatic officers and consular officers. It sets when drafts on the Secretary of State are to be drawn, and lets the Secretary of State change that timing in his discretion. It also lets consular officers, after investigating a rescue, pay money to a ship master or rescuing crew members if they are judged deserving of a reward.

7010-I.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the construction industry and their painter, paperhanger, woodfinisher, and decorator employees in the Rochester, New York region and nearby townships. It also lets the National Industrial Recovery Board make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement, with or without conditions, if needed to carry out the Act, the code, or the agreement, or to avoid undue hardship.

7010-H.s: A complaint was filed about pig iron being imported into the United States under conditions said to threaten the Code of Fair Competition for the Iron and Steel Industry. After reviewing the complaint and a report from the National Industrial Recovery Board, the order says the facts do not justify further investigation. It directs that no further action be taken and that the complainant be notified.

7010-B.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and employees in the plastering and lathing contracting division of the construction industry in California. It allows the National Industrial Recovery Board to make exceptions and exemptions from the agreement when needed. The agreement’s operation is stayed for most of the region, except in certain metropolitan districts and cities of 10,000 people or more, until the Board finds the sponsors are truly representative.

7010-D.s: This order approves an agreement between employer members of the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division and their painter, paperhanger, and decorator employees in Otsego County, New York. It adopts the National Industrial Recovery Board’s report, recommendations, and findings on that agreement. The Board may also provide exceptions or exemptions from the agreement, with or without conditions, if needed to carry out the law or avoid undue hardship.

7010-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and employees in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the Construction Industry in California. It also lets the National Industrial Recovery Board make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement if needed. The order stays the agreement for most of the region, except in certain metropolitan districts and in cities with 10,000 people or more and nearby areas, until the Board finds the sponsors are truly representative.

7010-F.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Electrical Contracting Division and electrical employees in the Miami area and part of Dade County, Florida. It says the National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement if needed to carry out the Act or to avoid undue hardship.

7010-E.s: This order approves a change to a collective bargaining agreement for the painting, paperhanging, and decorating division in the Omaha, Nebraska, and Council Bluffs, Iowa, region. It changes the date in the agreement from April 1, 1935, to April 1, 1936. The order also allows the National Industrial Recovery Board to make exceptions, exemptions, revisions, or a stay in operation if needed.

7010-G.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the painting, paperhanging, and decorating division and certain employees in the Colorado Springs area and nearby places in Colorado. It says the National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement, with or without conditions, if needed to carry out the act or avoid undue hardship.

7009.s: This order extends the trust period on lands held in trust for the use and benefit of the Torres-Martinez Band of Mission Indians in California. It applies to lands whose trust period would have expired during 1935 and extends that period for 10 more years from the date it would otherwise end.

7008.s: This order exempts Milton L. Leffler from a law that would otherwise require automatic separation from government service at the retirement age. It allows him to stay in service until May 1, 1936, while he serves as a Special Expert at the Federal Trade Commission.

7006.s: This order exempts David E. Roberts from the compulsory retirement rule for federal civilian service. It lets him stay in service until May 1, 1937. The order applies to Roberts, who was Assistant Chief, Division of Fine Arts, Library of Congress.

7003.s: This order changes the Central Statistical Board so its chairman is the chief executive officer and may not do any private business, vocation, or employment. It also lets the Board collect, analyze, and publish certain data and prepare current statistical and economic summaries for use within the Government. Records, papers, property, and employees from the office of the Economic Adviser to the National Emergency Council are transferred to the Board, but the employees do not get permanent civil service status.

7001.s: This order extends the trust periods on allotments made to Indians of the Crow Reservation, Montana, that would have expired during 1935. It extends each trust period for 10 more years from the date it would otherwise expire. The extension is subject to the act of June 18, 1934, and the order would stop if a majority of adult Indians voting at an election choose to apply that act to the reservation.

7002.s: The order allows Mrs. Mattie Lowe Sartor to be appointed as a clerk in the Oklahoma City Post Office without following the civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of Elmer Sartor, who died while serving in a motorcycle escort during a visit of the Postmaster General to Oklahoma. The order is recommended by the Postmaster General.

7000.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry. It also changes the earlier approval of that code so the full code is approved as amended. The order affects the distilled spirits industry and the Federal Alcohol Control Administration's approved rules for it.

6998.s: This order exempts Harry O. Bailey, Superintendent of Meters in the Office of the Architect of the Capitol, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service until April 1, 1937. The order affects Bailey and the retirement rule for civilian service in the United States Government and the municipal government of the District of Columbia.

6999.s: This order transfers certain powers over Codes of Fair Competition for the wheat flour milling, feed manufacturing, country grain elevator, malt, and southern rice milling industries from the Secretary of Agriculture to the National Industrial Recovery Board. It says those powers cannot be used, without the Secretary of Agriculture’s written approval, to control prices, brokerage fees, credits and financial charges, commission rates, purchasing arrangements, marketing quotas, or plant capacity. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps the authority to appoint one or more representatives to the Code Authority for those codes.

6997.s: This order sets rules for the sale, importation, and manufacture of alcoholic beverages in the Canal Zone. It makes it unlawful to sell or import alcoholic beverages there except under a license or written authority, and it forbids making alcoholic beverages in the Canal Zone. It also says the rules do not apply to alcoholic liquors for sacramental, scientific, pharmaceutical, industrial, or medicinal purposes, and violations can bring fines, jail, or loss of a license.

6996-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the painting, paperhanging, and decorating division and their painter, paperhanger, and decorator employees in Hill County, Montana. It says the agreement was found to comply with the National Industrial Recovery Act and the Construction Industry code. It also allows the National Industrial Recovery Board to grant exceptions or exemptions from the agreement when needed to carry out the act or avoid undue hardship.

6996.s: This order revokes parts of two earlier executive orders that had affected certain lands in Wyoming. The change applies only to the lands listed in the order, across several townships and ranges.

6995.s: This order revokes parts of two earlier executive orders that had created coal land withdrawals in Montana. It applies only to the listed lands in the Montana Meridian area.

6994.s: This order retires John A. Gamon, a Foreign Service officer, effective June 30, 1935. It says he was found totally disabled for useful and efficient service because of disease, and not because of vicious habits, intemperance, or willful misconduct. He is to receive an annuity under the cited law.

6992-B.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division and certain employees in the region of Cascade County, Montana. It also lets the National Industrial Recovery Board make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement, with or without conditions, when needed to carry out the law or avoid undue hardship.

6992-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and painter, paperhanger, decorator, and woodfinisher employees in the Erie County region, including North Tonawanda, Gowanda, and Perrysburg. It applies to employers and employees covered by that agreement. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement, with or without conditions, to carry out the Act or avoid undue hardship.

6992.s: This order amends Veterans Regulation No. 10 to define who counts as a “veteran of any war.” It includes certain officers, enlisted men, and Army or Navy nurses who served in World War I, the Spanish-American War, the Philippine Insurrection, or the Boxer Rebellion. It also says that for hospitalization, some people who served overseas as Army contract surgeons are included.

6991.s: This order changes Veterans Regulation No. 6 to let the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs keep providing hospital and domiciliary care, including medical treatment, to certain people already admitted under earlier laws. It applies to those properly admitted under the laws in effect before March 20, 1933. They may keep receiving care until they can be discharged without putting their health or life at risk.

6990.s: This order changes rules for disability and death pensions for veterans. It says pension awards generally cannot start before the later of the veteran’s separation, death, the event that caused the pension, or the date the application was received. If an application is incomplete, the Veteran’s Administration must ask for the needed evidence, and if it is not sent within one year, pension may not be paid on that application. It also says pension to a dependent mother or father continues until death or remarriage, and a claim denied before can be treated as a new claim if new and material evidence is provided.

6989.s: This order changes pension rules for the surviving widow, children, and dependent mother or father of a person who died from an injury or disease linked to active military or naval service. It sets monthly pension rates for different family members and limits the total pension that can be paid under each part. It also allows the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs to pay dependents of an incompetent veteran who disappears, up to the amount of pension the veteran was receiving.

6988-A.s: This order approves an added code section for the Highway Contractors Subdivision of the General Contractors Division of the construction industry. It also amends the Construction Industry code to include that supplement. The National Industrial Recovery Board may review the section on “Mutual Agreements” within 60 days if it may unfairly interfere with collective bargaining.

6988.s: Three domestic producers of pearl essence filed a complaint saying imports were being brought into the United States on terms or under conditions that could make the Code of Fair Competition for the Chemical Manufacturing Industry ineffective or seriously endanger it. After reviewing the complaint and a report from the National Recovery Administration, the order says the facts do not warrant further investigation. It directs that no further action be taken on the complaint and that the complainants be notified.

6987.s: This order sets document rules for aliens seeking admission into the Philippine Islands. It requires passports or similar travel documents and valid passport visas, with some exceptions for certain passengers, seamen, and people traveling in transit. It also lets the Governor General waive these requirements in some cases and bars visas or transit certificates if entry would be contrary to public safety. It authorizes certain officials in the Canal Zone, American Samoa, and Guam to issue passport visas and transit certificates for travel to the Philippine Islands.

6986.s: This order sets document rules for aliens who want to enter the United States. Non-immigrants and immigrants generally must show unexpired passports or other travel documents, along with the needed visas, unless they fit one of the listed exceptions. It also lets certain officials issue these documents for people coming from the Canal Zone, American Samoa, and Guam, and it gives the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Labor power to make added rules.

6985-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Mason Contractors Division and certain employees in the St. Louis region of Missouri. The agreement covers bricklayer, stone mason, bricklayers' tender, and stone mason's helper employees. It also allows the National Industrial Recovery Board to make exceptions or exemptions if needed to carry out the Act, the code, or the agreement, or to avoid undue hardship.

6985.s: This order exempts Lyster H. Dewey from the rule that would require him to retire at the set age. It lets him stay in federal service until October 1, 1935. It affects Dewey, a senior botanist in the Department of Agriculture.

6984.s: This order exempts Luther L. Browning from the rule that required certain government workers to retire at the set retirement age. It lets him stay in service until April 1, 1936.

6984-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the electrical contracting division and their electrician employees in Allegheny County and part of Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania. It also allows the National Industrial Recovery Board to make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement. The order stays the agreement for the rest of the region outside Allegheny County until the board makes required findings.

6982.s: This order removes two specific home site tracts in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It restores those tracts to entry under the public-land laws. The land affected is identified as home sites on Revillagigedo Island.

6983.s: This order authorizes the Federal Emergency Relief Administrator, and the Director of the Land Program if authorized by that Administrator, to buy property or take it through eminent domain. It applies to real or personal property used for projects or programs financed under the National Industrial Recovery Act or related appropriations. It also lets them sell, lease, or administer property acquired or built for those projects.

6980-C.s: This order makes the East Texas Field a designated area under the earlier regulations. It applies those rules to petroleum and petroleum products from that area and to people who produce, refine, store, ship, or transport them. It also sets up Federal Tender Board No. 1 to issue certificates of clearance and administer the regulations for that area.

6980-B.s: This order sets rules for moving petroleum and petroleum products from designated areas. It requires a certificate of clearance, called a "Tender," before those products can be shipped or transported in interstate commerce from those areas. The Secretary of the Interior is to designate areas, set up boards to review applications, and issue further regulations. People who produce, refine, transport, store, or handle petroleum in those areas must keep records and let authorized people inspect their property and books.

6980-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and employees in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the construction industry. It applies to operations in Manhattan and the Bronx, but not in Richmond. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement when needed.

6981.s: This order removes certain restrictions on payments, transfers, and deliveries of money or property under Public Resolution 53, the Trading with the Enemy Act, and the Settlement of War Claims Act of 1928. It says Germany is in arrears on payments under a debt-funding agreement and keeps the restrictions in place for certain payments to German nationals, people living in Germany, some German organizations, and related heirs or representatives. It also says the Attorney General will determine nationality, residence, domicile, or other qualifications for some claimants, and the Secretary of the Treasury will determine them for claims tied to the German, Austrian, and Hungarian Special Deposit Accounts.

6980.s: This order revokes part of a 1932 order that had withdrawn public lands in a township in New Mexico. The revocation applies to the lands in that township and takes effect when the official plat of resurvey is filed.

6979.s: This order designates the Secretary of the Interior to carry out most of the President’s powers and duties under the 1935 petroleum commerce law. It does not apply to the powers in section 4 of that law. Any regulation under section 5(a) that carries a fine or imprisonment cannot take effect unless the President approves it.

6978.s: This order waives a civil service rule that required an absolute appointment before a transfer. It allows Archibald Oden to be retransferred to the position of Special Assistant to the Secretary of the Navy. It applies to Mr. Oden and involves the United States Civil Service Commission.

6977.s: This order revokes a 1929 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Colorado. The revocation applies to sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 of Township 10 South, Range 86 West of the sixth principal meridian, and becomes effective when the official plat of resurvey is filed.

6976.s: This order exempts Joseph W. Austin from the rule that requires some federal workers to retire at the set retirement age. It lets him stay in service until March 1, 1937. It applies to Austin, who was a foreman carpenter in the United States Capitol Building.

6975.s: This order exempts Charles J. James from the compulsory retirement rule for civilian service. It lets him stay in service until March 1, 1936.

6974-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Electrical Contracting Division of the construction industry and certain employees in parts of Oregon and Washington. It also lets the National Industrial Recovery Board make exceptions or exemptions if needed, including with conditions, to carry out the law, the code, or the agreement, or to avoid undue hardship.

6974.s: This order exempts Jacob L. Nuber from compulsory retirement for age and lets him stay in federal service until March 1, 1936. It applies to his position in the Treasury Department and overrides the normal retirement rule for him.

6973-B.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division and certain employees in the Rochester, Minnesota area and nearby. It also allows the National Industrial Recovery Board to make exceptions or exemptions from the agreement when needed to carry out the law, the code, or to avoid undue hardship.

6973-A.s: A complaint was filed saying certain watches, watch movements, and parts were being imported into the United States under conditions that could affect the President's Reemployment Agreement. After reviewing the complaint and a report from the National Recovery Administration, the President found there was not enough reason for more investigation. He directed that no further action be taken and that the complainant be notified.

6973.s: This order withdraws a tract of public land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets the land aside for the joint use and occupancy of the Department of Agriculture and the Alaska Game Commission as a headquarters site for administering Alaska game laws. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6972.s: This order revokes part of a 1917 order that had reserved certain land in Alaska for town-site purposes and for work tied to railroad lines. It applies to the described portion of land in the Fairbanks Meridian.

6971.s: This order changes a prior order that had withdrawn certain Arizona lands for use as a rifle range by the Tucson Rifle Club and the University of Arizona Rifle Club. It allows a public highway to be built across the listed tracts of land in Arizona.

6970.s: This order changes a civil-service rule for the Public Health Service. It covers attendants in hospitals, quarantine stations, sanatoriums, and similar places where registers are not practical, as well as certain workers in rural sanitation and plague-suppressive work. It also covers employees in classified positions while they are being treated or recovering at Government sanatoriums.

6969.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the cigarette, snuff, chewing, and smoking tobacco manufacturing industry. It applies to that industry and its employers. It also directs a study of wages and hours of labor of employees and requires a report to the National Industrial Recovery Board.

6968.s: This order extends the trust period for certain land allotments made to Indians of the Crow Creek band of Sioux in South Dakota. It applies to allotments whose trust period would expire during 1935 and extends them for 10 more years.

6967-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the tile contracting division and certain employees in parts of Pennsylvania and New Jersey. It applies to the region listed in the order. The National Industrial Recovery Board may grant exceptions or exemptions, with or without conditions, if needed to carry out the law, the code, or the agreement, or to avoid undue hardship.

6967.s: This order changes veterans pension rules for certain people who served in the military or naval service between August 13, 1898, and July 4, 1902, and left the continental United States for Guam, Cuba, or Puerto Rico. It also covers the widow, if she remains unmarried, and dependents of a person to whom a pension was being paid on March 19, 1933. The order sets pension rules and limits, including exceptions for wilful misconduct, fraud, and some other cases.

6965.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Brewing Industry. It changes the earlier approval of that code so it now includes the code as amended.

6966.s: This order excludes three tracts of land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest and restores them to entry under the applicable public-land laws. The tracts are home sites near Lakeview Station, Moose Pass, and Lawing, with areas of 5.00 acres, 4.89 acres, and 3.86 acres.

6964-B.s: This order amends the Code of Fair Competition for the Paper and Pulp Industry. It changes the minimum wages for workers in the Northern, Central, and Southern Zones, with different hourly rates for male and female workers. It also sets weekly minimum wages for employees described in another section of the code.

6964-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the painting, paperhanging, and decorating division and certain employees in the region of Knox County, Indiana. It says the agreement was found to comply with the National Industrial Recovery Act and the Construction Industry code. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions to carry out the act or avoid undue hardship.

6964.s: This order temporarily withdraws public lands in the listed states from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are reserved for classification and for deciding the best uses for the Land Program and for conserving natural resources. Public lands already under an existing reservation for a public purpose are exempt while that reservation stays in force.

6962.s: This order extends the trust periods on allotments made to Indians of the Colville Reservation in Washington that would otherwise expire during 1935. Each trust period is extended for 10 more years from the date it would have expired. The extensions are subject to the act of June 18, 1934. If a majority of the adult Indians of the reservation vote to apply that act to the reservation, this order stops being in effect.

6961.s: This order extends the trust periods on allotments made to Indians of the Klamath Reservation, Oregon, that would otherwise expire during 1935. Each trust period is extended for 10 more years from the date it would have expired. The extension is subject to the act of June 18, 1934, and the order would stop applying if a majority of the adult Indians voting under that act vote to apply it to the reservation.

6960.s: This order reserves a 1.96-acre area in Salem County, New Jersey, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a headquarters for the Killcohook Migratory Bird Refuge. The area is subject to valid existing rights and to the Department of Commerce’s use of the Finns Point Rear Light Station. It bars hunting, trapping, capturing, disturbing, or killing wild animals or birds there, and it also bans damaging natural growth or United States property.

6959.s: This order excludes several named home site tracts of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It restores those tracts to entry under the applicable public-land laws. The land is described as occupied as home sites and identified by surveys, plats, and field notes.

6958.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, entry, or other appropriation. It reserves those lands for the exclusive use of the Department of the Navy in connection with the Hawthorne Ammunition Depot. It also changes an earlier order so these lands are excluded from it.

6957.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, entry, or other appropriation. The lands are reserved for classification and to aid future legislation. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6956.s: This order amends a prior order that created Federal Prison Industries, Inc. It corrects the names of two people named as members of the first Board of Directors. The change affects the board members listed in that earlier order.

6955-A.s: This order changes an earlier order about rules for administering paragraph 2 of Section III of the Wool Textile Code. It gives the Wool Textile Work Assignment Board responsibility for administering that paragraph under the principles set out in the earlier order until 30 days after the Board submits its report to the President.

6954.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry. It also changes the earlier approval so the code is approved in full as amended. The order affects the distilled spirits rectifying industry.

6955.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Automobile Manufacturing Industry. It changes the code’s expiration date to June 16, 1935, and says work over forty-eight hours in any week must be paid at time and one-half. It also authorizes industry members to make agreements about fall announcements of new passenger automobile models and fall automobile shows, and it confirms and continues the rules for settling labor controversies.

6953-B.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and certain employees in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the construction industry in Natrona County, Wyoming. It also lets the National Industrial Recovery Board make exceptions or exemptions, with or without conditions, if needed to carry out the law, the code, or the agreement, or to avoid undue hardship.

6953.s: This order exempts certain jobs from Executive Order No. 6746. The jobs include consultants, experts, specialists, attorneys, and similar positions paid on a per diem or part-time annual basis from public works or other emergency funds.

6953-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the Construction Industry and certain employees in the Wheeling, West Virginia area and nearby places. It applies to the employers and employees covered by that agreement. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions, with or without conditions, if needed to carry out the law or avoid hardship.

6952-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Auto Rebuilding and Refinishing Trade. It also stays certain sections of the code until the National Industrial Recovery Board gives further orders.

6952.s: This order transfers $30,000,000 to the Federal Emergency Relief Administration from money earlier set aside for the Federal Civil Works Administration. The money is to be available during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1935. It affects those two federal programs and the funds they use.

6951.s: This order allows Mrs. Myrtle K. Brockway to be appointed to a clerical position in the General Accounting Office without following the civil-service rules. It affects only her appointment to that job.

6950.s: This order extends by one and a half years the period when certain candidates can be appointed as Foreign Service officers. It applies to candidates whose names were on the eligible list on March 20, 1934.

6949-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Mason Contractors Division and certain employees in parts of Tulsa, Rogers, Craig, Ottawa, Creek, and Osage Counties in Oklahoma. The agreement covers the region named in the order, with some areas of Creek and Osage Counties excluded. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions if needed.

6949.s: This order says that approving, agreeing to, or working under a Code of Fair Competition does not mean the government or anyone in industry gives up any constitutional right. It also changes past code approval orders and makes this rule a condition for future code approvals.

6948-B.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and employees in the painting, paperhanging, and decorating division of the construction industry. It applies in parts of Utah, including Utah, Salt Lake, Davis, Weber, Cache, and part of Boxelder County. The National Industrial Recovery Board may grant exceptions or exemptions, with or without conditions, when needed.

6948-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Motor Vehicle Maintenance Trade. It also stays some parts of the code for members of the Motor Vehicle Retailing Trade for 60 days where they conflict with that trade’s code. Other listed rules are stayed until further order, and one provision about choosing members of the National Code Authority is stayed until that authority is organized.

6947-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the painting, paperhanging, and decorating division and certain employees in the Region of Concord, New Hampshire. It says the agreement was found to comply with the National Industrial Recovery Act and the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions, with or without conditions, if needed to carry out the act or avoid undue hardship.

6948.s: This order changes the location of a 10-foot-wide right-of-way between Round Top Military Reservation and Sugar Loaf Military Reservation on the island of Oahu, Hawaii. It restores one strip of land to its previous status for use by the Territory of Hawaii. It also reserves a different 10-foot-wide strip as a right-of-way in connection with the defensive works of Oahu.

6946-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and employees in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the construction industry in Passaic and Bergen Counties, New Jersey. It also lets the National Industrial Recovery Board make exceptions or exemptions if needed, with or without conditions.

6946.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets the land aside for the joint use of the Department of Agriculture, the Bureau of Biological Survey, and the Alaska Game Commission as a headquarters site for administering Alaska game laws. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6945-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Plastering and Lathing Contracting Division of the construction industry and certain employees in the Dallas County, Texas region. It also adopts the report and findings of the National Industrial Recovery Board. The Board may grant exceptions or exemptions, with or without conditions, if needed to carry out the Act, the code, or the agreement, or to avoid hardship.

6945.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry. It also changes the earlier approval of that code so the whole code is approved as amended. It applies to the distilled spirits rectifying industry.

6944.s: This order transfers all lands in the Uinta National Forest that lie east of a described line to the Wasatch National Forest. It affects those lands in Utah and changes which national forest manages them.

6943.s: This executive order revokes a 1929 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Montana. The revocation applies to the land areas listed in the order and becomes effective when the official plats of resurvey are filed.

6942.s: This order makes citation changes in the Consular Regulations and adds Mérida, Mexico, to the list of unhealthful posts. It replaces rules on ship’s papers, consular fees, marine protests, navigation notices, and other consular duties. The changes mainly affect consular officers, masters of U.S. vessels, and seamen.

6940.s: This order extends the trust period on lands held for the use and benefit of the Pala Band of Mission Indians of California. It applies to lands whose trust period would expire during 1935 and extends that trust for ten more years from the date it would otherwise end.

6938.s: This order changes a prior order so the Secretary of the Interior can withdraw a described parcel of public land in Idaho. The land is to be used by the Department of Commerce to maintain air-navigation facilities, and it remains subject to an existing power transmission line reservation.

6939.s: This order extends the trust period for allotments made to Indians of the Spokane Reservation, Washington, when that trust period would otherwise end during 1935. The extension lasts for ten years from the date the trust would otherwise expire. It is subject to the act of June 18, 1934, and would stop being in effect if that act is made applicable to the reservation by the election described in that act.

6936.s: This order announces cost of living index figures for the periods ending June 30, 1928, and December 31, 1934. It says the December 31, 1934 index was 18.8 percent lower than the base period. It also says the reduction used to figure the compensation of officers and employees for January 1, 1935, through June 30, 1935, is 5 percent.

6935-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division and certain employees in the St. Paul, Minnesota area and nearby places. It applies to the employers and employees covered by that agreement. The National Industrial Recovery Board may make exceptions or exemptions, with or without conditions, if needed to carry out the act, the code, or the agreement, or to avoid undue hardship.

6935.s: This order places Wake Island, Kingman Reef, and Johnston and Sand Islands, along with the reefs around them, under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy for administrative purposes. It also keeps Johnston and Sand Islands available for use by the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for native birds.

6933.s: This order exempts Mrs. Maud Brackett Pattin from the rule requiring retirement at a set age. It lets her stay in government service until August 1, 1935. It applies to her job with the War Department in Mexico City.

6934.s: This order abolishes Sioux City, Iowa, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 44, which has headquarters at Des Moines, Iowa. It takes effect thirty days after the date of the order.

6932.s: This order exempts Henry C. Stuart from the rule that would require his automatic separation from service when he reaches retirement age. It lets him stay in service until March 1, 1936.

6931.s: This order exempts Thomas J. Brady from the retirement rule for civilian service after reaching the automatic separation age. It keeps him in service until January 1, 1936. Brady is a Deputy Collector of Customs in charge in the Bureau of Customs, Treasury Department, at Cape Vincent, New York.

6930.s: This order changes the deadline for the Cotton Textile, Silk Textile, and Wool Textile Work Assignment Boards to present recommendations under Executive Order No. 6878. The boards do not have to submit those recommendations before January 1, 1935, but they must do so within a reasonable time after that date. In the meantime, they must send monthly reports of their activities and progress to the Secretary of Labor.

6929-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and certain employees in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division in the Dade County, Florida region. It also lets the National Industrial Recovery Board make exceptions and exemptions, with or without conditions, if needed to carry out the act, the code, or the agreement, or to avoid undue hardship.

6929.s: This order gives the Federal Emergency Administrator of Public Works authority to handle securities bought under certain parts of the National Industrial Recovery Act and the Emergency Appropriation Act. It lets the administrator sell, assign, transfer, and deliver those securities and use the money as required by those laws. It also lets the administrator change or waive some rules and make new rules under section 209, but any rule that carries a fine or prison term must be approved by the President first.

6928.s: This order changes the rules for reimbursing officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States for losses caused by changes in foreign currency values. It says who counts as being “in service in foreign countries” and how their salary and allowances are figured for payment. It also sets basic exchange rates for many foreign currencies and says how employees are to be paid in foreign currency.

6927-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the retail meat trade. It defines which meat sales and establishments are covered by the code. It also sets up an 11-person Code Authority and stays some provisions until similar rules are added or further order is made.

6927.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations covered by section 4 of Executive Order No. 6166. It pushes those changes, and related provisions, to June 30, 1935. It also allows the Secretary of the Treasury, with the President’s approval, to make any of those changes effective between December 31, 1934, and June 30, 1935.

6925-A.s: This order cancels the approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade. It says that after the cancellation, most transportation work in that trade will be covered by the trucking industry code, and construction work will be covered by the construction industry code.
