6925.s: This order removes several named home site tracts in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It restores those tracts to entry under the public-land laws. The tracts are in places including Auke Bay, Tee Harbor, Wrangell, Revillagigedo Island, Meyers Chuck, and Admiralty Island.

6926.s: This order extends the trust period for certain Indian allotted lands in the Otoe Reservation, Oklahoma, and other Indian reservations in Oklahoma not specifically named, if the trust period was set to expire during calendar year 1935. It extends the trust for a period of ten years, but it does not apply where Congress has specifically kept the authority to extend the trust period for tribal or individual Indian lands.

6924.s: This order sets aside land in Hyde County, North Carolina, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and wild animals. Some of the land may also be used as a shooting area, and the waters of Mattamuskeet Lake may be used for fishing under permit or license. It bans hunting, trapping, disturbing wildlife, taking nests or eggs, cutting natural growth, and damaging U.S. property in the refuge.

6923.s: This order excludes certain lands in South Dakota from the Harney National Forest. It applies to Townships 3 and 4 South, Range 6 East, and the east half of Townships 3 and 4 South, Range 5 East, in the Black Hills meridian.

6922.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry. It also changes the previous approval of that code so it now includes the code as amended. This affects the alcoholic beverage wholesale industry and the Federal Alcohol Control Administration’s approved code.

6920-B.s: This order concerns a complaint about imports of quebracho tanning extract into the United States. It says the complaint did not warrant further investigation under Section 3(e) of the National Industrial Recovery Act. It directs that no further action be taken and that the complainants be notified.

6920-C.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and employees in the painting, paperhanging, and decorating division of the construction industry. It applies to the region of Greenwich, Connecticut, except for part of East Port Chester described in the order. The agreement was found to comply with the National Industrial Recovery Act and the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry.

6920-A.s: This order stops any further action on a complaint about menthol imports under the National Industrial Recovery Act. It says the complaint did not warrant more investigation, and the complainants are to be notified.

6920.s: This order closes several federal offices in the District of Columbia at 1 P.M. on December 24, 1934, and at 1 P.M. on December 31, 1934. It excuses federal employees in the District of Columbia and in the field service from duty at those times, except for workers excluded for special public reasons or where absence would conflict with existing law.

6918.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about the Board of Surveys and Maps. It adds the Tennessee Valley Authority to the list of organizations that may have membership on the Board.

6919.s: This order exempts T. Warren Allen from a rule that would require some federal civilian workers to leave service when they reach retirement age. It lets him stay in his job as principal highway engineer in the Bureau of Public Roads until January 1, 1936. It affects Allen and applies under the retirement rule for federal civilian service.

6917.s: This order creates a District of Columbia corporation called Federal Prison Industries, Inc. It gives the corporation power over industrial operations in federal penal and correctional institutions, and it directs the transfer of certain funds, property, assets, and equipment to it. It also says federal departments and government-owned or government-controlled corporations must cooperate with the corporation and buy its products or services when required or allowed by law.

6916.s: This order changes civil-service rules for unclassified laborers who want to be reinstated. It keeps the normal 1-year limit, but lets the Commission waive that limit for longer periods based on prior service, and with no time limit for those with 5 years or more of service. People separated for more than 5 years must still meet other eligibility conditions and pass a thorough physical examination.

6914.s: This order exempts Carl F. Jeansen from the rule that would require his retirement at the automatic separation age. It allows him to stay in civilian service in the Navy Department until March 31, 1936. It applies only to Jeansen.

6913.s: This order sets rules for qualified people in the Virgin Islands to obtain narcotic drugs from registered manufacturers and dealers in the continental United States for legitimate medical purposes. It requires approval by the Commissioner of Health of the Virgin Islands, and approved orders must be used within 2 months. The order also requires records and reports on narcotic drugs in the islands and puts enforcement responsibility on the Governor of the Virgin Islands.

6911.s: The order allows the current Director of the Bureau of Navigation and Steamboat Inspection to appoint one private secretary. That appointment does not have to follow the civil-service rules.

6912.s: This order temporarily withdraws a described piece of public land in Arkansas from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be classified for its suitability for wild life refuge purposes, and the order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

6910-B.s: This order allocates money from a 1935 relief appropriation to the Federal Emergency Relief Administration and the Emergency Conservation Fund. It provides funds for buying submarginal lands in stricken agricultural areas, administering those lands, and establishing and maintaining Civilian Conservation Corps camps. It also allows certain spending for personal services, rent, printing, and binding as needed, and revokes an earlier executive order.

6910-A.s: This order transfers $10,000,000 from the Emergency Conservation Fund to the War Department. It also allows funds to be transferred to the Department of Agriculture for use in carrying out earlier executive orders on emergency conservation work. The order affects the Treasury, the War Department, and the Department of Agriculture.

6910.s: This order temporarily withdraws all vacant, unreserved, and unappropriated public land in certain states from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for classification and for deciding the most useful purpose for them, including conservation and development of natural resources. It does not affect existing rights.

6908.s: This order temporarily withdraws a parcel of land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry while legislation is pending. It applies to the described land and is subject to valid existing rights. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6909.s: The order temporarily withdraws unreserved and unappropriated public lands in Custer, Fall River, Jackson, and Pennington Counties, South Dakota. The lands may not be settled on, located, sold, or entered while they are set aside for classification and use as a grazing project under the submarginal land program. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6906.s: This order appoints Colonel Frank P. Douglas of Oklahoma as a special commissioner and member of the Textile Labor Relations Board. It takes the place of James A. Mullenback, who resigned, and says Douglas will receive travel and subsistence expenses plus $40 per day.

6907.s: This order makes $140,000 available to the Federal Coordinator of Transportation from the National Industrial Recovery appropriation. The money is for studies, data collection, and plans about railroad labor conditions and relations, including pensions and retirement insurance, unemployment insurance, and wages.

6905.s: The order appoints Francis I. Biddle as Chairman of the National Labor Relations Board and sets his salary at $10,000 a year. It also says the board may appoint and retain officers and employees and incur financial obligations only with the approval of the Secretary of Labor, but the Secretary may not review the board's findings or orders in specific cases.

6904.s: The order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the construction industry and certain employees in the Omaha, Nebraska and Council Bluffs, Iowa region and nearby area. It applies to the members of that division and the journeyman painter, paperhanger, and decorator employees covered by the agreement.

6903.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverages Importing Industry. It changes the previous approval of that code so it now includes the code as amended, affecting the alcoholic beverages importing industry.

6902.s: This order temporarily withdraws a parcel of land in Idaho from settlement, location, sale, entry, permit, or lease. It reserves that land as a source of material for the construction and maintenance of public highways. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6901.s: This order reserves a tract of public land in Alaska for joint use by the Department of Agriculture and the Alaska Game Commission. It is set aside as a headquarters site for administering Alaska game laws. The order applies to the public land within the listed boundaries and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6900.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry. It changes the earlier approval of that code so it now includes the code as amended, affecting the wine industry.

6899.s: This order exempts Thomas M. Thurston from the rule that would require his automatic retirement at the retirement age. It lets him stay in his government job until December 1, 1935.

6898.s: The order lets the Secretary of Agriculture hire extra personnel for conservation work on wildlife refuges without following civil service rules. These hires may be made in the District of Columbia or elsewhere, within the funds already allocated. It applies to temporary positions connected to the conservation work authorized by the March 31, 1933 act.

6897.s: This order transfers San Clemente Island and a nearby rocky island in California from the Secretary of Commerce to the Secretary of the Navy for naval purposes. It also keeps the Department of Commerce’s right to select sites for aids to navigation and related facilities. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6896.s: This order transfers San Miguel Island and Prince Island, California, from the control of the Secretary of Commerce to the control of the Secretary of the Navy for naval purposes. It also keeps some sites for the Department of Commerce to use for aids to navigation and related facilities. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6895-A.s: This order changes a prior order that required silver to be delivered to the United States Mints. It says certain silver on hand at the close of business on November 7, 1934, is permanently exempt from delivery. It also says silver made in good faith into certain articles after that date, before it is first required to be delivered, is permanently exempt.

6895.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Automobile Manufacturing Industry. It changes the code’s expiration date from November 3, 1934 to February 1, 1935, unless the emergency ends earlier by proclamation or joint resolution. It affects the automobile manufacturing industry.

6894.s: This order allows Mrs. Helen K. Stebbins to be appointed as a senior stenographer at the Navy Yard in New York without following the civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of a United States Navy chief pharmacist's mate who died in the line of duty, and that she is represented as qualified for the job.

6893.s: This order exempts James P. Fenton from the rule that would require his automatic retirement for age. It lets him stay in his job as a Marine Engineer in the Immigration and Naturalization Service until November 1, 1935.

6892-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Electrical Contracting Division of the construction industry and certain employees in the Detroit, Michigan region and its metropolitan district. It says the agreement was found to comply with the National Industrial Recovery Act and the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry.

6892.s: This order amends Schedule A of the civil-service rules by adding a new subdivision called "National Railroad Adjustment Board." It allows one private secretary or confidential clerk for each member of that board.

6891.s: This order revokes part of a prior executive order that had set aside certain lands in Arizona and Nevada as the Boulder Canyon Wild Life Refuge. The revocation applies only to the described land in Arizona. The land is listed as about 640 acres.

6890.s: This order temporarily withdraws a tract of public land on Kodiak Island, Alaska, from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is set aside for the Smithsonian Institution to use in archaeological investigations. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6889-A.s: This order puts the members and duties of the Executive Council into the National Emergency Council and ends the separate Executive Council. It also says the Industrial Emergency Committee will keep its duties but serve as a sub-committee of the National Emergency Council. The order sets out the Council’s role in presenting business to the President, coordinating federal agencies, and advising the President and the Executive Director.

6889.s: This order transfers lands from the Selway National Forest to the Lolo, Bitterroot, Clearwater, and Nezperce National Forests in Idaho. It says the transfers are not meant to give public lands national-forest status if they did not already have it, or to remove lands from national-forest status. It also says the Selway National Forest will stop being a separate administrative entity.

6888.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in South Dakota from settlement, location, sale, or entry for classification. The lands are to be reviewed to decide whether they should be included in the Harney National Forest. It affects the listed public lands and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6887.s: This order transfers certain land, buildings, and improvements at the Naval Station in St. Thomas to the control of the Secretary of the Interior for use in running the government of the Virgin Islands. It also transfers certain equipment and furnishings to the Secretary for the same use. The land, buildings, and improvements must be kept in good repair and returned to the Secretary of the Navy when needed for naval uses.

6886.s: This order transfers the Mondeaux unit from the Nicolet National Forest to the Chequanegon National Forest. It affects the land covered by that forest unit in Wisconsin.

6885-A.s: This order approves an amended Code of Fair Competition for the Builders Supplies Trade. It also changes the earlier approval so it covers the code as amended. The order applies to the builders supplies trade under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6885.s: This order changes the rules for the Army and Navy General Hospital at Hot Springs, Arkansas. It keeps the hospital under the Secretary of War and says it is for treating diseases that the hot springs waters are known to help, with the War Department to announce which diseases and how to get admitted. It also sets who may be treated there, how the hospital staff is organized, and the charges for subsistence and medicine for different patients.

6884.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in North Dakota from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be classified for their suitability for migratory bird refuge purposes. It affects the listed public lands and anyone seeking to settle, buy, or enter them.

6883-B.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Electrical Contracting Division of the Construction Industry and certain employees in Cook County, Illinois. It affects the employers and employees covered by that agreement.

6883-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the construction industry and certain employees in the Wilmington, Delaware area and its metropolitan district. It applies to the employers and employees covered by that agreement.

6883.s: This order temporarily withdraws unappropriated and unreserved public lands within the boundaries of the proposed Everglades National Park in Florida. It keeps those lands from settlement, location, sale, or entry for classification for the proposed park. The withdrawal applies subject to valid existing rights and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6881.s: This order changes the boundary between the Cochetopa and Gunnison National Forests in Colorado. It transfers lands of the Cochetopa National Forest north and west of the described line to the Gunnison National Forest, and lands of the Gunnison National Forest south and east of that line to the Cochetopa National Forest. It says it does not give national forest status to land that did not already have it, or remove that status from any publicly owned land.

6882.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Tusayan National Forest to the Prescott National Forest. It also transfers certain lands from the Prescott National Forest to the Tonto National Forest. The order says it does not give any publicly owned lands national-forest status if they did not already have it, and it does not remove any publicly owned lands from national-forest status.

6880.s: This order changes a rule on when officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States can be paid for losses caused by changes in foreign currency values. It limits that rule to people attached to and serving on board United States vessels in foreign waters for at least 60 straight days.

6879.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Plumbing Contracting Division of the Construction Industry and certain employees in Denver, Colorado, and nearby areas. It applies to the employers and employees covered by that agreement. The order adopts the National Industrial Recovery Board’s report, recommendations, and findings and makes the agreement approved.

6878.s: This order sets rules for Cotton, Silk, and Wool Textile Work Assignment Boards and has them share a common chairman. It also directs the boards to study work assignment practices in representative plants and recommend a permanent plan for those industries. The plan would limit increases in work assignments unless an employer gets approval, and it lets employees ask for an investigation of existing assignments. Decisions by the district chairman could be appealed to the Textile Work Assignment Board, and that board would have final say.

6877.s: This order creates a Wool Textile Work Assignment Board with a chairman and representatives of employers and employees in the wool textile industry. The board is given power to administer the Code rule on work assignments and to make rules for doing that. It says employers may not increase the number of machines or other equipment handled by workers unless there is a compensating change, and the board may investigate claims that work loads were improperly increased since July 1, 1933, and require a reduction.

6876.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Textile Industry. It also changes the earlier approval of parts of that code so the approved parts are covered in their amended form.

6874.s: This order changes the civil-service rules to allow temporary clerks, earners, and laborers for part-time or intermittent work in the Postal Service. It applies to work connected with the present holiday or seasonal business, from this date to February 1, 1935.

6875.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Silk Textile Industry. It changes the approved code so the amended parts are approved in full, under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6872.s: This order lets George S. Ridner be appointed in the Treasury Department as an investigator in the Alcohol Tax Unit without following the civil service rules. It says he had worked in Treasury enforcement before, was removed after a conviction on extortion charges, and later received a full and unconditional pardon. It also says he would be assigned to investigate violations of internal-revenue laws relating to liquor.

6873.s: This order exempts James S. Goldsmith from the rule requiring retirement at the set age. It lets him continue serving as superintendent of buildings and labor of the United States National Museum until November 1, 1935. It applies only to him.

6871.s: This order approves a committee report on amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Garment Industry. It stays the effective date of those amendments until December 1, 1934, and extends the work of the committee that is reviewing protests from parts of the cotton garment industry. It also tells the National Industrial Recovery Board to appoint another committee to study competition between prison labor, sheltered workshops, and the cotton garment industry.

6870-A.s: This order changes the rules for the Puerto Rican Needlework Commission. It replaces a three-person commission with a four-member commission appointed by the National Industrial Recovery Board. The new commission includes one member for the needlework industry in Puerto Rico, two members for related industries in the continental United States, and one impartial chairman.

6869.s: This order requires executive departments and independent establishments to send the Treasury Secretary monthly statements of certain bonds, notes, shares, and other debts or interests they hold for the United States, along with certain liabilities of the United States. It also requires corporations in which the U.S. government has a proprietary interest to file monthly statements of their assets, liabilities, capital, and surplus. The Treasury Secretary must publish a combined monthly statement and may set the forms and rules for these reports.

6868.s: This order designates three officials as the “Alley Dwelling Authority” to carry out the District of Columbia Alley Dwelling Act. The Authority may make rules, appoint an executive officer, and must send an annual report to the President. It also sets aside $500,000 from an existing allocation for low-cost housing and slum-clearance projects in the District of Columbia as the “Conversion of Inhabited Alleys Fund.”

6867.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California and Idaho from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use. The order applies to the specific parcels listed in the two states.

6866.s: This order changes a Civil Service rule about how people are certified for federal jobs. It says certifications must be made without regard to sex unless sex is specified in the request.

6865.s: This order exempts William McNeir from the rule that requires civilian federal workers to retire at the set retirement age. It allows him to stay in service until November 1, 1935.

6864.s: This order exempts Herman H. B. Meyer from the rule requiring automatic retirement at a certain age. It lets him stay in his job as Director of the Legislative Reference Service at the Library of Congress until November 1, 1935.

6863.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It applies to lands in townships 7 south, ranges 12 and 13 west of the New Mexico principal meridian, and lasts until revoked by the President or by Congress.

6862.s: This order exempts George G. Hedgcock from the rule that required certain civilian employees to retire at the set age. It lets him stay in service until November 1, 1935. The order applies only to Hedgcock, who was a senior pathologist in the Bureau of Plant Industry at the Department of Agriculture.

6861.s: This order delays certain amendments to Articles III and IV of the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Garment Industry until October 15, 1934. It directs the National Industrial Recovery Board to appoint three impartial people to hear protests, investigate the facts, and make recommendations. The board must send those recommendations to the President, who will make a final decision by October 15, 1934.

6860-A.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers and certain employees in the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the construction industry. It covers workers in Philadelphia County, Delaware County, and parts of Chester and Montgomery counties in Pennsylvania. The order says the agreement meets the rules of the National Industrial Recovery Act and the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry.

6860.s: This order amends earlier orders about the Industrial Emergency Committee and names its members. The committee is directed to make recommendations to the President on relief, public works, labor disputes, industrial recovery, and related agricultural recovery problems, and to study and coordinate those matters. It also extends Donald R. Richberg’s leave of absence so he can serve in several listed roles.

6859.s: This order creates the National Industrial Recovery Board to administer the provisions of title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act under the President’s direction. It appoints members and advisers to the board. The board may set administrative policies and manage its personnel, subject to approval by the Industrial Emergency Committee.

6857.s: This order exempts Herman M. Underwood from the law requiring automatic retirement at the retirement age. It lets him stay in civilian service in the War Department until February 1, 1935. It applies only to him.

6858.s: This order creates the Textile Labor Relations Board in the Department of Labor. The board is directed to investigate complaints of discrimination in taking men back to work after the textile strike, and to investigate alleged violations in the textile industry involving hours of work, pay, and other working conditions. It also can hold hearings, make findings, conduct or certify elections for collective bargaining, and help settle labor disputes by voluntary arbitration. The order abolishes three earlier textile labor boards and directs the Bureau of Labor Statistics and the Federal Trade Commission to study hours, earnings, working conditions, labor costs, profits, and investments in the textile industries.

6856.s: This order revokes part of two earlier executive orders that had created power-site reserves in Arizona. It removes the reserve status from the specifically described lands in Gila and Salt River Meridian. The change affects those listed parcels of land.

6855.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Petroleum Industry. It says production quotas for each state are to be divided within the state, and if quotas are not set or a state goes over its quota, the President may regulate shipments of petroleum or petroleum products in interstate commerce out of that state. It also says any person who produces more than the quota assigned to them commits an unfair trade practice under the code.

6854.s: This order lets the Civil Service Commission waive age limits for certain people who were separated from the Prohibition Bureau or the Alcoholic Beverage Unit of the Department of Justice. It applies to those separated between June 10, 1933, and December 31, 1933, so they can take the civil service examinations tied to the Emergency Appropriation Act for fiscal year 1935.

6853.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be used in connection with the Duck Valley Indian irrigation project. It affects the listed lands and anyone who might try to settle, claim, buy, or enter them.

6852.s: This order revokes part of a 1932 withdrawal of public lands in a township in Colorado. It opens those lands first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat, subject to valid rights and existing withdrawals. After that, the lands are open to the general public under any applicable public-land law.

6851.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public land in Idaho from settlement, location, sale, or entry for use by the War Department for target-range purposes. It is subject to valid existing rights and to first-form reclamation withdrawal. The land must be vacated by the War Department if it is needed for the further development of the Minidoka project, Idaho.

6850.s: This order amends rules for paying losses to officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States in foreign countries when foreign currency has appreciated against the American dollar. It sets how to calculate losses for different groups, including employees under the War and Navy Departments and employees traveling abroad under official orders. It also applies to certain losses from July 15, 1933, and makes the amendment retroactive to April 1, 1934.

6849.s: This order excludes certain tracts of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. The lands were occupied under Forest Service permits and will be subject to disposal under public-land laws under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

6847-A.s: This order ends the stay on the provisions of Section 1 of Article IX of the Code of Fair Competition for the Wheat Flour Milling Industry. It affects the wheat flour milling industry, while the rest of the June 9, 1934 order stays in force unless changed here.

6848.s: This order corrects the description of Fort William D. Davis Reservation in the Canal Zone and changes part of its boundaries. It sets out two parcels of land for the reservation, totaling about 1,480 acres. All other conditions of the 1919 order stay in effect unless changed by this order.

6847.s: This order exempts John L. Summers from the rule that would automatically separate some government workers when they reach retirement age. It lets him stay in service until October 1, 1935. Summers is a senior administrative officer in the Treasury Department.

6846.s: This order revokes part of a 1929 executive order that had withdrawn public lands in one township in Colorado. The revocation applies to that township and takes effect when the official plat of resurvey is filed.

6845.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in two townships in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The withdrawal lasts while those townships are resurveyed, and it stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6844.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. Part of the land is set aside for the Department of Agriculture to use as a fire-lookout site for the Lassen and Plumas National Forests. The remaining lands in the section are also temporarily withdrawn for classification and in aid of legislation.

6843.s: This order temporarily withdraws public lands in one township in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The withdrawal lasts while the township is resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it. Valid existing rights are still protected.

6842.s: This order temporarily withdraws a piece of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be used for lookout station purposes connected with cooperative forest-protection work, subject to valid existing rights. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

6841.s: The order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Montana from settlement, location, sale, entry, permit, or lease. It reserves those lands for use by the War Department in connection with Fort Peck Dam, Federal Project No. 30. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6840.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry for the Cotton Textile Industry in connection with the Department of Labor. The Board is directed to look into complaints from workers and problems facing employers in the cotton textile, wool, rayon, silk, and allied industries. It may also help with voluntary arbitration in labor disputes and must report its findings and recommendations to the President.

6839.s: This order directs the Department of Agriculture and the Agricultural Adjustment Administration to give the Federal Trade Commission records and information it asks for. The material is for a milk inquiry and covers the purchase, sale, processing, and distribution of milk and other dairy products. It also covers information about companies and associations engaged in handling milk or other dairy products in interstate commerce.

6837.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Automobile Manufacturing Industry. It changes the code’s expiration date to November 5, 1934, or an earlier date if the national emergency is declared ended.

6836.s: This order changes a previous executive order about the Industrial Emergency Committee. It appoints Donald R. Richberg as director of that committee and gives him leave from his job as general counsel of the National Recovery Administration until October 1, 1934, with pay, so he can carry out those duties and any others the President assigns.

6835.s: This order changes the civil-service rules for one job category. It adds six special agents in the Division of Investigations, Office of the Secretary, to investigate fraudulent entries and other criminal matters.

6838.s: The order lets the Civil Service Commission set rules for a special reemployment list for temporary jobs in the Bureau of the Census. It applies to people who passed civil-service exams and worked there temporarily or on probation for 6 months or more with good records. The list is for temporary work only in connection with the pending agricultural census, and it can be given priority over other eligible lists when the Secretary of Commerce asks.

6834.s: This order exempts Post Wheeler from the retirement rule for civilian service in the United States Government. It lets him stay in service for as long as needed, but not more than two months from August 6, 1934.

6833.s: This order revokes a 1912 order that had withdrawn all public lands on Near Island in Alaska for use as a temporary pasture and animal-quarantine station. It then withdraws the island from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for the joint use and occupancy of the Department of Agriculture and the Alaska Game Commission as a headquarters site for administering Alaska game laws.

6832.s: This order makes $200,000 available to the National Mediation Board from an existing appropriation. The money is for expenses of the National Railroad Adjustment Board during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1935, as approved by the National Mediation Board. It also says the amount spent must be reimbursed if Congress later makes an appropriation for those expenses.

6831.s: This order designates Mahukona, Hawaii, as a customs port of entry in customs collection district no. 32, with headquarters at Honolulu. The designation takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

6830.s: This order allows Fred W. Beltz to be appointed as Assistant Deputy Commissioner in the Alcohol Tax Unit of the Bureau of Internal Revenue in the Treasury Department. It says this appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

6829.s: This order gives the Federal Alcohol Control Administration more of the powers and duties under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act for industries that mainly produce or distribute alcoholic beverages. It lets the agency write rules for changes, exceptions, or exemptions to codes of fair competition for those industries, while the President keeps the power to approve any code or amendment. It also says general executive orders about codes of fair competition do not apply to those codes unless they say so specifically.

6828.s: This executive order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Garment Industry. It also changes an earlier approval so the code is approved in its amended form. The approval takes effect 14 days after the order unless good cause is shown to the Administrator before then.

6826.s: This order directs that the flags on the White House and public buildings in the District of Columbia and Illinois be placed at half mast on the day of Henry T. Rainey's funeral service. It applies to the White House and public buildings in those places.

6827.s: This order temporarily withdraws one town-site lot in Anchorage, Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves that lot, along with the improvements on it, for the War Department for use by the Signal Corps. It also revokes a prior order for a different Anchorage town-site lot in the same block.

6824.s: This order waives a rule that had barred federal officers and employees from holding state or municipal offices. It applies to Robert H. Jackson, who was appointed to a federal job and also to a New York state commission. The order says his work on the state commission will be in the public interest and will not stop him from doing his federal duties.

6825.s: This order exempts C. Frank Wittenauer from the rule that requires certain civilian employees to retire at the set age. It lets him stay in service as a picture engraver at the Bureau of Engraving and Printing until September 1, 1935.

6822.s: This order temporarily withdraws a parcel of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be used by the Department of Agriculture in connection with the administration of the Mono National Forest. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6823.s: This order allocates $1,000,000 to the Secretary of Labor for use by the United States Employment Service. The money may be used as needed for the National Reemployment Service and for similar purposes to meet the demands of the Public Works Program.

6821.s: This order exempts Ingild Povelsen from the rule requiring some government workers to retire at a set age. It lets him stay in service until September 1, 1935.

6819.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The withdrawal is connected to waterworks projects for the city of Rawlins and is subject to valid existing rights. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6820.s: This order allocates $65,000 to the Secretary of Agriculture to control the infestation of the Japanese beetle at St. Louis, Missouri. It says the infestation is a menace to the stricken agricultural area of the Mississippi Valley and westward. The Secretary of Agriculture may spend the money on people, materials, equipment, and assistance needed for control, through agencies the Secretary designates.

6818.s: This order revokes a previous order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Arizona. It applies to the specific lands described in the order, totaling 160 acres.

6817.s: This order temporarily withdraws a specific piece of public land in Idaho from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The Department of Agriculture may use the land as an administrative site to store explosives for the administration of the Challis National Forest. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6815.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Idaho, New Mexico, and Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use. The order applies only to the public lands described in the document and is subject to valid existing rights.

6814.s: This order requires people who own, possess, or control silver in the continental United States to deliver it to the United States Mint, with several listed exceptions. It says silver coins, certain low-fineness silver, some silver used for industry, art, or other listed uses, and some foreign or licensed silver do not have to be delivered. The order also says the silver will be coined into silver dollars or added to the nation’s monetary stocks, and that costs for transporting the silver may be reimbursed.

6812.s: This executive order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry. It also changes earlier approvals of that code so they include the code as amended. The order affects the distilled spirits rectifying industry and the Federal Alcohol Control Administration's submitted amendment.

6813.s: This order approves an agreement between certain employers in the Mason Contractors Division and certain employees in New York City and part of Long Island. It applies to the people covered by that agreement and approves the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6811.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry. It also changes the President’s previous approval of that code to include the code as amended. It affects the distilled spirits industry and the parties involved in the hearings on the amendment.

6810-A.s: This order changes rules for diplomatic and consular officers. It says drafts on the Secretary of State are to be drawn 10 days after sight, with acceptance waived and endorsements by procuration excepted. It also lets a consular officer pay the master or rescuing boat’s crew a reward of $5 to $25 after investigating the rescue, without first referring the matter to the Department of State. The officer must send an account of the payment with vouchers to the Department right away.

6810.s: This order changes a rule about paying losses caused by changes in foreign currency value for officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States in foreign countries. It adds coverage for time spent while traveling through a foreign country or to or from that post. The change is retroactive to April 1, 1934.

6809.s: This order adds specific lands in South Dakota to the Black Hills National Forest. It says the addition covers 1,556.39 acres. It also says the withdrawal does not interfere with legal rights in lands already appropriated under public-land laws or reserved for a public purpose, as long as those rights or reservations remain in force.

6808.s: This order removes a tract of land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest and restores it to entry under the public-land laws. The land is described as a home site and is about 4.04 acres.

6807.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It applies to the listed townships and lasts until the land is resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6806.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Tusayan National Forest to the Kaibab National Forest in Arizona. The lands are those lying north and east of a detailed boundary line described in the order. It also eliminates specific tracts from the Tusayan National Forest and says the transferred lands will be managed as part of the Kaibab National Forest.

6805.s: This order temporarily withdraws a described parcel of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be used by the Department of Agriculture in connection with the administration of Cleveland National Forest, subject to valid existing rights.

6804.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain town site lots in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lots for the Department of Agriculture to use as a warehouse and construction shop for the Bureau of Public Roads. The site is for forest highway projects in Alaska, and the withdrawal stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

6803.s: This order revokes part of a previous order that had withdrawn public lands in one township in Arizona. It opens those lands first to entry under the homestead or desert-land laws by qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat. After that, the lands may be opened to the general public under the public-land laws that apply.

6802.s: This order revokes an earlier reservation of a tract of land in Alaska that had been set aside for the Department of Agriculture as an agricultural experiment station. It then withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for the joint use of the Department of Agriculture and the Alaska Game Commission as a headquarters site for administering Alaska game laws.

6801-B.s: This order adds the listed lands in Utah to the Wasatch National Forest. It says the withdrawal will not interfere with existing legal rights or public uses of land already legally reserved or appropriated. It also says no Federal funds may be used to buy privately owned land in the area until payment is provided from the receipts of the Wasatch National Forest.

6801-A.s: This order adds specific lands in Utah to the Uinta National Forest. It says the change must not interfere with any legal rights already in place or with land already set aside for a public purpose. It also says no federal funds may be used to buy privately owned land in the area until provision is made to pay for those purchases from the Uinta National Forest’s receipts.

6801.s: This order designates Felix Cordova Davila, an associate justice of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico, to act as judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico. He may perform the judge’s duties and sign needed papers and records when the judge is absent during the current calendar year.

6799.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the lands for classification and for conservation development and protection of natural resources. The order applies subject to valid existing rights and rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

6800.s: This order excludes several tracts of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest and restores them to entry under the public-land laws. The tracts are described as occupied home sites on Prince of Wales Island, Chichagof Island, and Eagle River Landing.

6797.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, permit, or lease. It reserves those lands to control the supply and distribution of potash and to aid legislation. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6798.s: This order temporarily withdraws a piece of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be used for lookout-station purposes in connection with cooperative forest-protection work. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6796.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Utah from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for flood-control work by the Department of Agriculture. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6795.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It applies to the listed townships and lasts while they are resurveyed, subject to valid existing rights.

6794.s: This order approves amendments to the code of fair competition for the alcoholic beverages importing industry. It also changes the earlier approval of that code to include the code as amended. The order says interested parties were given notice and a chance to be heard.

6793.s: This order allocates $15,000,000 from an emergency appropriation to the Secretary of Agriculture. The money is for planting forest protective strips in the Plains region to help with drought conditions. The Secretary of Agriculture may spend the funds on staff, seed and planting stock, land, technical investigations, fencing, and rent, and may use designated agencies and, with local consent, state and local officers and employees.

6792.s: The order directs the Postmaster General and other Postal Service officers he designates to hold public hearings on foreign air-mail and ocean-mail contracts made before June 16, 1933. The parties to those contracts may appear or be represented at the hearings. After reviewing the evidence, the Postmaster General must report to the President within 6 months on whether any of the contracts should be modified or canceled and in what way. He may also hire attorneys, technical experts, clerks, and other employees to carry out the order.

6791.s: This order announces cost of living index figures for the 6 months ending June 30, 1928, and June 30, 1934. It says the 1934 index was 20.2 percent lower than the base period. It also says the percentage of reduction for the compensation of officers and employees for July 1, 1934, through December 31, 1934, is 5 percent.

6790.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the auction and loose-leaf tobacco warehouse industry. It says the code was applied for, hearings were held, and the code fits the law. One section is stayed for 20 days so interested parties can raise objections, and it will take effect after that unless changed.

6789.s: This order authorizes The Alaska Railroad to charter vessels and do what is needed to operate them for transporting passengers and freight to and from accessible parts of the Territory of Alaska. It says the service is to provide normal transportation during the transportation emergency and continue until normal transportation facilities are restored. It also directs The Alaska Railroad to keep present passenger and freight charges in place for this added service.

6787.s: This order amends an earlier order about buying forest lands for emergency conservation work. It lets the Secretary of Agriculture use part of the money allotted to protect, improve, and administer the lands bought under that order until regular Department of Agriculture funds are available for that work.

6788.s: This order amends earlier executive orders about the Federal Alcohol Control Administration. It names six people as the present members of that administration.

6786.s: The order transfers certain lands in the Klamath National Forest in California to the Shasta National Forest. It says this change does not give national-forest status to public lands that did not already have it, and does not remove any public lands from national-forest status. The order takes effect July 1, 1934.

6785.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Interior the power to act for the President under subdivisions (a) and (b) of section 9 of the National Industrial Recovery Act. It covers the functions and powers given to the President by those parts of the law.

6784.s: This order places the positions created under the act for the District of Columbia-Virginia Boundary Commission outside the classified civil service. It lets the commission make appointments to those positions without following the civil-service rules. It applies to the positions created under that act and reflects the temporary nature of the work.

6783.s: This order creates the Quetico-Superior Committee to advise federal departments and agencies and the State of Minnesota on a proposed wilderness sanctuary in the Rainy Lake and Pigeon River watersheds. The committee is also to make recommendations from time to time as it sees fit. It includes named members and two members chosen by the Secretaries of Agriculture and the Interior, and it serves for 4 years without pay.

6782.s: This order revokes part of an earlier executive order that had created public water reserve no. 49 in Montana. It applies only to the described lands in Montana Meridian. Those lands will not be open for disposal under public land laws until a later date and notice are set and announced.

6781.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in township 18 north, range 5 west of the Gila and Salt River meridian in Arizona from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands stay withdrawn while they are resurveyed, subject to valid existing rights. The order remains in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6780.s: This order changes rules for paying losses to officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States in foreign countries when foreign currencies rise in value against the American dollar. For employees traveling in foreign countries under official orders who are not assigned to a foreign post, any part of their salary not converted for spending abroad cannot be counted in the loss. The change applies back to April 1, 1934.

6779.s: This order changes the rules for applications for licenses to land or operate submarine cables in the United States. It authorizes and directs the Federal Communications Commission to receive those applications and to advise the President on granting or revoking the licenses after getting approval from the Secretary of State. It also says the order takes effect when the Federal Communications Commission is organized.

6778.s: This order lets the Chairman of and Director for the Federal Alcohol Control Administration choose an acting chairman and an acting director from among the Administration’s members. They would serve when the Chairman and Director are absent or unable to serve because of illness.

6777.s: This order creates the National Resources Board and sets up an advisory committee and a technical committee to help it work. The board must prepare and give the President a plan for using land, water, and other national resources, and it must report on land and water use by December 1, 1934. It also transfers the powers, records, people, equipment, and funds of the National Planning Board to the new board and abolishes the Committee on National Land Problems.

6776.s: This order cancels Executive Order No. 6096, also called Veterans Regulation No. 8, as of its original date. It is about yearly renewable term insurance.

6774.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in township 25 north, range 18 east of the Willamette meridian in Washington from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It applies while a resurvey of that township is pending, subject to valid existing rights. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6775.s: This order updates rules for when the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs may provide hospital or domiciliary care, including medical treatment, to certain veterans and other eligible people. It lists different groups of veterans who may receive care, including some with service-related injuries or diseases, some with no adequate means of support, and some retired officers and enlisted men. It also allows payment or apportionment of travel expenses and limits certain pension, compensation, or retirement payments while a disabled veteran is receiving care.

6772.s: This order places the secretary position for the aviation commission in the unclassified service. It lets the aviation commission choose who is appointed to that job at its discretion.

6773.s: This order exempts Carleton W. Sturtevant from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in civilian service until November 1, 1935. It applies to Sturtevant, a principal engineer in the War Department.

6771.s: This order directs the remaining members of the National Recovery Review Board to take steps to end the board before July 1, 1934. It says the board will cease to exist on that date. It affects the board and its remaining members.

6769.s: This order sets the rental and subsistence allowance rates for officers of the various services who are entitled to them for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1935. It sets one subsistence allowance at 57 cents per day. It also sets one rental allowance for one room at $19 per month.

6770.s: This order creates an Industrial Emergency Committee made up of the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Labor, the Administrator for Industrial Recovery, the Administrator of Federal Emergency Relief, and a director chosen by the President. The committee must make recommendations to the President on relief, public works, labor disputes, and industrial recovery, and study and coordinate related problems. It also appoints Donald R. Richberg as director of the committee and as executive secretary of the Executive Council and Executive Director of the National Emergency Council.

6765.s: This order allocates $325,000 for an addition to the Executive Office Building and for its furnishings and equipment. It gives the Secretary of the Interior the money to spend through the National Park Service during fiscal year 1935.

6767.s: This order changes rules for people or businesses bidding to supply goods or services to U.S., state, municipal, or other public authorities. It says a bidder may quote a price up to 15 percent below the price filed under an approved code of fair competition if the bidder also files a copy of the lower bid after bids are opened. The Administrator for Industrial Recovery may lower that 15 percent limit for a trade or industry if needed to stop destructive price cutting, but not below 5 percent, and must study the order and report back within 6 months.

6762.s: This order temporarily withdraws a parcel of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is set aside for lookout station purposes in connection with cooperative forest-protection work. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6761.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Arkansas from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be classified for their suitability for wildlife refuge purposes. It applies to the specific areas listed in the order and stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

6760.s: This order revokes a 1917 order that had withdrawn public lands in a described area in New Mexico while title was being determined. It applies to the listed sections and townships, and it takes effect when the official survey plats are filed.

6759.s: This order exempts George E. Ladd from the retirement rule for automatic separation because of age. It lets him stay in the service until August 1, 1935. The order applies to Ladd, who was an associate economic geologist in the Bureau of Public Roads, Department of Agriculture.

6758.s: This order puts all positions in the Farm Credit Administration into the classified civil service, so future appointments must follow civil-service laws and rules. It does not change the Governor’s authority to appoint employees for emergency crop production loans, or to appoint experts and attorneys, or the Land Bank Commissioner’s appointment authority. People already in affected jobs do not automatically get classified civil-service status, but some employees in those positions could be appointed after passing noncompetitive fitness tests.

6756-C.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the wholesale fresh fruit and vegetable distributive industry. It says the code was applied for, noticed, and heard under the National Industrial Recovery Act, and that it fits the law's requirements. It also says the continued participation of four named trade groups depends on changes to their by-laws that satisfy the Secretary of Agriculture and the Administrator for Industrial Recovery.

6756-E.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry. It also changes the President’s earlier approval of that code to include the code as amended. The order applies to the distilled spirits rectifying industry and follows hearings and notice to interested parties.

6756-F.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Brewing Industry. It also changes the earlier approval of that code to include the amended version. The order affects the brewing industry and the parties involved in the review and hearings.

6756-G.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry. It changes the earlier approval of that code to include the code as amended. The order applies to the alcoholic beverage wholesale industry and to interested parties involved in the hearing process.

6756-D.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry. It also changes the President’s earlier approval of that code to include the code as amended. The order says notices were given and hearings were held for interested parties.

6756-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Needlework Industry in Puerto Rico. It gives Puerto Rican needlework businesses exemptions from several other fair competition codes and sets rules for labeling goods made partly in Puerto Rico and partly in the continental United States. It also requires contractors and manufacturers to make up any wage shortfalls for homeworkers and makes them responsible for delivering those wages. The order creates a Puerto Rican Needlework Commission to study the code and recommend changes, and it sets a process for piece rates to be reviewed and approved.

6756-A.s: This order offers agreements to members of certain service trades that have not yet been codified and are later designated by the Administrator for Industrial Recovery. A member who displays the NRA insignia shows agreement to follow labor standards approved by the Administrator. In any locality where 85% of a designated trade propose a local code of fair trade practices and it is approved, no member may display the insignia unless they also follow that local code. The Administrator may add rules, exceptions, and changes to carry out the order.

6756.s: This order lets the Treasury Department fill certain emergency and temporary jobs without following civil-service rules. Those jobs are for carrying out the Emergency Banking Act of 1933, the Gold Reserve Act of 1934, and the Silver Purchase Act of 1934. It affects appointments to those positions in the Treasury Department.

6755.s: This order designates Gastonia, North Carolina, as a customs port of entry. It places Gastonia in customs collection district no. 15, with headquarters at Wilmington, North Carolina.

6754.s: This order extends the limits of the customs port of Belfast, Maine, to include the adjoining town of Searsport, Maine. The change takes effect 30 days after the date of the order and affects customs collection in that area.

6753.s: This order exempts Mrs. Maud Brackett Pattin from the rule that required some federal and District of Columbia civilian workers to retire at the set retirement age. It lets her stay in service until February 1, 1935.

6752.s: This order amends the civil-service rules to add positions in the National Soldiers' Home at Johnson City, Tennessee to Schedule A, Subdivision XVIII. It affects those positions by placing them under the added rule in the civil service system.

6751.s: This order creates the National Steel Labor Relations Board in the Department of Labor. The board is given power to investigate labor complaints in the iron and steel industry, mediate disputes, and handle voluntary arbitration. It can also hold secret ballot elections to choose employee representatives and access payroll and other records needed for those elections.

6750-C.s: This order sets rules for apprentice training programs under Codes of Fair Competition. It allows an apprentice to be paid less than the minimum wage or work longer hours only if the employer gets a certificate from an agency approved by the Secretary of Labor. It defines an apprentice as someone at least 16 years old with a written contract for at least 2,000 hours of continuous work and approved training, and it sets up a committee to advise the Secretary of Labor.

6750-A.s: This order gives the Administrator for Industrial Recovery the power to make agreements under section 4(a) of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The agreements may be made with people in a trade or industry in Puerto Rico, Hawaii, or Alaska. The Administrator may do this if he thinks the agreements will help carry out the policy of the act for interstate or foreign commerce and meet the act’s requirements.

6750-B.s: This order approves a new chapter for plastering and lathing contracting in the construction industry. It also changes the earlier approval of the construction industry code so that it includes this chapter. The order affects plastering and lathing contractors within the construction industry.

6750.s: The order sets a process for public notice before foreign trade agreements are concluded. It says the Secretary of State must give notice at least 30 days before an agreement is made, and the notice must be sent to the press and published in certain government publications. People who want to share their views may present them to the Committee for Reciprocity Information, which sets the form, place, and time for those views.

6749.s: This order allocates $1,500,000 from an appropriation for "Petroleum Administration" to the Secretary of the Interior. The money is for administering and enforcing section 9(c) of the National Industrial Recovery Act and the Code of Fair Competition for the Petroleum Industry. It also covers other purposes related to regulating commerce in petroleum.

6748.s: This executive order creates the National Longshoremen's Labor Board in connection with the Department of Labor. The board may investigate issues tied to the longshoremen's strike on the Pacific Coast and labor problems related to it, hear complaints about discrimination or discharge, and act as a voluntary arbitrator if asked. It may also hire up to 15 employees and report its findings and recommendations to the President through the Secretary of Labor.

6747.s: This order allocates funds to several agencies to help stricken agricultural areas. It provides money for Civilian Conservation Corps camps, loans to farmers for seed, feed, freight, and summer fallowing, and grants to states. It also gives money to buy land to increase employment and to buy, sell, give, or transport seed, feed, and livestock.

6746.s: This order sets a salary schedule for employees in emergency agencies and other agencies paid in whole or in part from emergency funds, unless they are in one of the listed exempt groups. It also says employees in executive departments and independent establishments paid from emergency funds are to be classified under the Classification Act, but the heads of those agencies may choose either that law or this salary schedule. The order allows Civil Service Commission review of some classifications and supersedes three earlier executive orders.

6745.s: This order directs that certain vacancy savings for fiscal years 1934 and 1935 be withheld from appropriation and fund accounts and put into a reserve account called "Reserve for Impounded Savings." The money can be released only if the President waives the impoundment. It applies to executive departments, independent establishments, and the municipal government of the District of Columbia, and it affects civil positions that are vacant.

6744-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the cigar manufacturing industry. The code became effective on the date of the order, but some parts were delayed until June 25, 1934, and some waiting periods were delayed until the Administrator gave further orders. It also delayed the rules for filing prices and discounts until arrangements were made for confidential treatment and sharing them with members of the industry and customers willing to pay the cost.

6744-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the retail tobacco trade and makes it effective on the date of the order, with some parts delayed. It applies to cigars, cigarettes, smoking tobacco, chewing tobacco, and snuff. It says wilfully destructive price cutting is forbidden, and it allows minimum prices to be set during an emergency under the stated process.

6742.s: This order makes tax returns open to inspection by the Special Committee Investigating the Munitions Industry of the United States Senate. The committee is authorized to investigate the manufacture of and traffic in arms, munitions, and other implements of war. The inspection must follow rules and regulations approved by the President and the Secretary of the Treasury.

6744.s: This order allows six named people to be appointed to specific jobs in the Treasury Department. It says these appointments may be made without following the requirements of civil-service rule II.

6743.s: This order delays the effective date of the Baking Industry code until July 9, 1934. It also removes a stay on Article VII, Section G, so that section will be in full force when the code takes effect. The order gives the Code Authority more time to report on the operation and effect of Articles III, IV, and V, extending that deadline to November 15, 1934.

6741.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be used for lookout-station purposes in connection with cooperative forest-protection work. It also says valid existing rights are protected, and the withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6740.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Utah and Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use, subject to valid existing rights.

6739.s: This order revokes part of two 1910 executive orders that created Temporary Power-Site Withdrawal No. 112 and Power-Site Reserve No. 112. It applies to the listed lands in Idaho, including land in several townships and sections near the Bruneau River.

6738.s: This order exempts Curtis F. Marbut from compulsory retirement for age and lets him stay in federal service until July 1, 1935. It applies to his job as Chief of the Division of Soil Survey in the Department of Agriculture.

6737.s: This order cancels part of chapter I of the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers under the heading "Organization of the Department of State." It affects the instructions for diplomatic officers and the Department of State organization section.

6735.s: This order makes $50,000,000 immediately available to the Federal Emergency Relief Administration. The money comes from funds already allocated to that agency for spending during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1935.

6736.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the candy manufacturing industry. It stays some rules about revised price lists, premiums, and one rule on sale terms for a time. It also allows the Administrator to hold further hearings before September 15, 1934, to decide whether the minimum wages in the code are adequate.

6734-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Wheat Flour Milling Industry. It also delays some parts of the code, including one section for 20 days and another section until further order by the Secretary of Agriculture. One article will only take effect if the Secretary of Agriculture finds in writing that an emergency exists in the industry.

6734.s: This order changes a previous land reservation for the United States Bureau of Education for educational purposes at Eklutna and Cordova, Alaska. It removes one described parcel from the reservation and adds two other described parcels to it.

6733.s: This order temporarily withdraws a specific piece of public land in Mississippi from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land will be classified and considered for possible inclusion in a national forest. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6733-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the bottled soft drink industry. It also requires the Code Authority to submit a study of labor hours, pay rates, and other working conditions six months after the code takes effect. The study is to look at revising wages, hours, and other employment conditions in that industry.

6732.s: This order amends the civil-service rules by adding one position to Schedule A, Subdivision XXII. The new position is Assistant Secretary of the Federal Power Commission.

6731-A.s: This order appoints Sullivan W. Jones as the disinterested chairman of the National Construction Planning and Adjustment Board. The board is part of the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry and includes members selected from construction industry and labor nominations.

6731.s: This order delays the transfer of civil-service retirement functions from the Veterans' Administration to the Civil Service Commission. The transfer is postponed until October 1, 1934. It may still be made effective between June 7, 1934, and October 1, 1934, by order of the United States Civil Service Commission with the President's approval.

6730.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the iron and steel industry. The revised code was set to take effect on June 11, 1934, and the earlier code stayed in force until then. It also directs the Federal Trade Commission and the National Recovery Administration to study the basing point system and its effect on prices and competition, and says steps will be taken to let employees choose their own representatives for collective bargaining and mutual aid.

6729.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the canning industry under the National Industrial Recovery Act. It requires the industry to designate a committee, subject to the Administrator’s approval, to help set product quality standards and labeling rules. It also requires the industry to report on the operation of certain provisions by December 1, 1934, to improve the hour and wage rules.

6728.s: This order revokes part of an earlier order that moved federal disbursing functions to the Treasury Department. It does not apply that transfer to the War Department, the Navy Department, and the Panama Canal, except for departmental salaries and expenses in the District of Columbia. The Secretaries of War and the Navy must still provide fiscal reports and other fiscal data to the Secretary of the Treasury, and their facilities may be used for disbursement if requested and approved.

6726.s: This order creates a Division of Territories and Island Possessions in the Department of the Interior. It moves the functions of the Bureau of Insular Affairs, along with its personnel, records, supplies, equipment, property, and unexpended balances, that relate to the administration of the Government of Puerto Rico from the Department of War to that new division. The division is to be run under the supervision of the Secretary of the Interior.

6727.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations under section 4 of Executive Order No. 6166. Those changes, and other provisions tied to section 4, are postponed until December 31, 1934 if they were not already carried out by June 30, 1934. The Secretary of the Treasury, with the President’s approval, may make any of those changes effective between June 30, 1934 and December 31, 1934.

6725-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Baking Industry under the National Industrial Recovery Act. It also stays some rules about revised price lists and Article VII, Section 6 until further order. The Code Authority must investigate and report on the operation and effect of Articles III, IV, and V within 90 days, and those parts may be changed after that.

6725.s: This order appoints six named people as additional members of the Science Advisory Board. It affects those appointees and the board itself. Their terms of office end on July 31, 1935.

6724.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to spend up to $1,000,000 to buy or rent land for emergency conservation work. The land is for refuges for migratory birds and other wildlife, and for work to protect land from forest fires, floods, soil erosion, plant pests, and disease. It also says this work will help restore depleted natural resources and provide employment for unemployed citizens. The order rescinds a previous executive order on the same subject.

6723.s: This order suspends most provisions in the codes for service trades or industries later designated by the Administrator for National Recovery. It keeps in place rules on child labor, maximum hours of work, minimum pay, and the mandatory parts of sections 7(a) and 10(b). Members of those trades or industries may display the National Recovery Administration insignia only while they follow the remaining rules. In some localities, if 85% of members agree to an approved local code, the insignia may be shown only if they follow that agreement too.

6721.s: This order temporarily withdraws a described piece of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be used for lookout-station purposes in connection with cooperative forest-protection work. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6720.s: This order revokes parts of two earlier orders that had withdrawn public lands in California and Nevada. It opens the listed townships first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plats. After that, the lands may be open to the general public under the public-land laws that apply.

6719.s: This order modifies a previous order that had withdrawn public lands in Oregon for classification and in aid of proposed legislation. It allows the Secretary of the Interior to approve Great Northern Railway Co.'s application for station grounds on the listed land in Oregon.

6718.s: The order directs the Federal Emergency Administrator of Public Works to make $93,000 available to the Central Statistical Board. The money comes from funds already allocated for National Industrial Recovery and is for the Board’s expenses through June 30, 1935.

6717.s: This order exempts Charles Y. Dixon from the compulsory retirement rule for civilian federal service. It lets him stay in his job as an engineer in the War Department until June 1, 1935. It affects Dixon and the retirement rule that would otherwise apply to him.

6716.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the feed manufacturing industry. It applies to the feed manufacturing industry and the American Feed Manufacturers' Association, Inc. The association's continued participation in choosing the Code Authority after June 1, 1934 depends on changing its by-laws to the satisfaction of the Secretary of Agriculture and the Administrator for Industrial Recovery.
