6715.s: Each executive department, independent establishment, and emergency agency must file a functional organization chart with the Director of the Bureau of the Budget. The chart must show its bureaus, divisions, sections, and the functions they perform, and updated charts must be filed when changes are made. New executive departments, independent establishments, and emergency agencies must file a preliminary chart within 5 days after their head is appointed.

6713-A.s: This order approves a Code of Labor Provisions for the alcoholic beverage wholesale industry. It applies to people and businesses in that industry. The President says the code meets the requirements of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6713.s: This order corrects the description of the Corundu Military Reservation in the Canal Zone. It says a recent survey found errors in the earlier description, so the boundary lines are rewritten. The reservation includes Fort Clayton, the Panama Arsenal, the Engineer Depot, the Post of Corozal, and Albrook Field.

6712.s: This order makes tax returns open to inspection by the House Committee on the Judiciary. The committee is authorized to use those returns for its investigation of equity and bankruptcy receiverships in federal courts. The inspection must follow the Treasury Department rules and regulations approved by the President.

6711-B.s:
This order approves the Plumbing Contracting Chapter for the construction industry code and changes the earlier approval of the construction code to include it. It applies to the plumbing contracting division of the construction industry.

The order also lets the Administrator review or reconsider one section within 180 days. The Administrator may require changes or grant a stay or exemption in a region or locality if that section causes undue hardship for employers or employees.

6711-A.s: This order says that if a code of fair competition bans homework, some people may still be allowed to do homework at the same wage rate as factory work. That applies when a person is physically unable to work in a factory, or when the person must stay home to care for someone who is bedridden or an invalid, and no contagious disease is present. Employers must keep the certificate on file and report the worker’s name and address to the Code Authority.

6711.s: Employers covered by an approved code of fair competition may not dismiss or demote an employee for making a complaint or giving evidence about an alleged violation of that code. The order also says violations of this rule can lead to a fine, imprisonment, or both under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6710.s: This order changes a prior order under the National Industrial Recovery Act. It exempts certain local retail and service employers that operate no more than three establishments in small towns from rules on hours, pay, minimum prices, and assessments, unless they choose to be bound by them. It also authorizes the Administrator for Industrial Recovery to set rules needed to carry out this change.

6709.s: This order makes $100,000,000 available to the Federal Emergency Relief Administration for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1934. The money comes from a larger amount that had been allocated to that agency for the next fiscal year. It is issued under authority of an act appropriating money to carry out the Federal Emergency Relief Act of 1933 and continue the civil-works program.

6708.s: This order directs John Dickinson, the Assistant Secretary of Commerce, to carry out the duties of the Director of the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce if the director resigns, is absent, or is sick. He would do this until the director returns from absence or sickness, or until a successor is appointed after a resignation.

6707.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Montana from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The lands are tied to the Fort Peck Dam and Reservoir project. It applies to the listed townships and sections, subject to valid existing rights, and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6706.s: This order temporarily withdraws a piece of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is set aside for lookout station purposes in connection with cooperative forest-protection work. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it, and it does not affect valid existing rights.

6705.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Country Grain Elevator Industry of the United States. It says the code was applied for, heard, and found to comply with the National Industrial Recovery Act. It affects the country grain elevator industry and the interested parties who took part in the hearings.

6704.s: This order temporarily withdraws a piece of public land in Washington from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets the land aside for the Department of Agriculture to use as a fire-lookout site for the Colville National Forest. The withdrawal stays in place unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6703.s: This order exempts Theodore A. Hostetler from a rule that would stop certain federal civilian workers from staying in service after reaching retirement age. It lets him continue working as Solicitor of the Patent Office in the Department of Commerce until June 1, 1935.

6701.s: This order allows Mrs. Elizabeth W. Herde to be appointed to a clerical position in the Federal Trade Commission. It says she may be appointed without following the civil-service rules.

6702.s: This order exempts Herman M. Underwood from the rule that required certain government workers to retire at the set age. It lets him stay in service until October 1, 1934. It applies to Underwood, an associate engineer in the War Department.

6699.s: This order moves the counties of Henderson, Knox, Peoria, and Warren from the first internal revenue collection district of Illinois to the eighth district. It takes effect on July 1, 1934.

6700.s: This order amends the rules for the Central Statistical Board and sets out how it is formed. The Board includes a chairman appointed by the President and representatives from several federal offices, with no more than 17 members total. It is concerned with statistical services used for carrying out the National Industrial Recovery Act, and it may plan, coordinate, investigate, and publish data on those services. It is also authorized to hire staff and receive funds needed to carry out its duties.

6697.s: This order reserves certain public lands in Nye County, Nevada, as a refuge and breeding ground for wild birds and animals for the Department of Agriculture. It says people may not hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or take nests or eggs there, unless allowed by rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. It also bans cutting or destroying natural growth, leaving fires unattended, and damaging U.S. property.

6698.s: This order temporarily withdraws a specific parcel of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be used for lookout-station purposes in connection with cooperative forest-protection work. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6696.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry while they are resurveyed. It applies to the listed townships in the San Bernardino Meridian and affects people who might seek to settle, claim, buy, or enter those lands.

6695.s: This order changes veterans’ rules so the Administrator may pay burial and funeral expenses, including transportation of the body, for certain deceased war veterans. The payment cannot be more than $100, and it is not payable if the veteran’s net assets at death equal or exceed $1,000. It also says outside contributions for burial costs do not reduce the allowed amount, but the total from all sources cannot be more than the actual burial and funeral cost.

6694.s: This order abolishes the Office of the Alien Property Custodian and moves its powers and duties to the Department of Justice under the Attorney General. It also transfers the office’s records, property, funds, and personnel to the Department of Justice. Other executive orders that conflict with this order are revoked.

6694-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the retail rubber tire and battery trade. It makes the code effective on May 14, 1934, unless cause is shown before then, and it affects businesses in that trade. It also lets the Administrator act if there is an emergency from destructive price-cutting, including setting a lowest reasonable cost, establishing a uniform guarantee and warranty, and staying the waiting period for revised price lists. The Code Authority must also submit recommendations within 90 days to make the hour and wage rules more consistent with related trades.

6693.s: This order creates the Committee on National Land Problems. The committee is to study national land problems, improve land use, better balance agricultural production, help solve human problems in land use, and develop a national land program. Its members are appointed by the President, and the committee advises the President without pay.

6692.s: This order approves a new official seal for the Department of Justice. It replaces the older seal design with a different one that includes a shield, an eagle, an olive branch, arrows, and the words "Department of Justice." It affects the Department of Justice and the Attorney General's office.

6691.s: This order authorizes the Postmaster General to submit Robert Shultice for nomination by the President as postmaster at Norfolk, Virginia. It allows this to be done without following Executive Order No. 6203, which deals with the appointment of postmasters of the first, second, and third classes.

6690.s: This order delays the effective date of Executive Order No. 6614 until May 21, 1934. It affects the transfer of War Department functions on national cemeteries and memorials in Europe to the American Battle Monuments Commission.

6689.s: This order transfers $75,000,000 to the Federal Emergency Relief Administration. The money comes from funds that had been allocated to the Federal Civil Works Administration. The funds are to be available for spending during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1934.

6688.s: This order exempts John L. Crone from a rule that would otherwise require him to leave federal service when he reaches the retirement age for automatic separation. It lets him stay in his job as a supervising inspector in the Bureau of Navigation and Steamboat Inspection until November 1, 1934.

6686-A.s: This order allows Miss Helen Woodrow Bones to be appointed to an appropriate position in the Department of State. It says the appointment may be made without following the civil-service rules.

6687.s: This order exempts Charles H. Deetz from the rule that would require his retirement for age. It allows him to stay in service as a draftsman under the Coast and Geodetic Survey, Department of Commerce, until May 1, 1935.

6686.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the linseed oil manufacturing industry. It applies to that industry and says the Code Authority must later study labor hours, pay rates, and other working conditions for possible revision.

6685.s: This order amends the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry. It lets members of that industry bottle distilled spirits without rectifying them. It also prohibits the acquisition and sale of distilled spirits or other alcoholic beverages that were produced, transported, imported, or bought, sold, or delivered in violation of any law, except under Federal Alcohol Control Administration rules.

6684-C.s: This order approves the Electrical Contracting Chapter of the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry. It also changes the earlier approval of that code to include the new chapter. This affects the electrical contracting division of the construction industry.

6684-B.s: This order approves an agreement among certain manufacturers and distributors of rubber tires about the sale of rubber tires. It applies to the manufacturers and distributors covered by that agreement.

6684-A.s: The order approves a compact on fair competition for the prison industries of the United States of America. It says the compact may be approved for states that have signed it or may sign it later. It also appoints three members to the Prison Labor Authority to represent labor, industry, and consumers, and gives the Administrator for Industrial Recovery the powers tied to the compact until further order.

6684.s: This order authorizes the purchase or rental of land to create refuges for migratory birds and other wildlife. It says work on those lands will help protect them from forest fires, floods, soil erosion, plant pests, and disease, and help restore depleted natural resources. It also says the land purchases will provide employment for unemployed citizens of the United States.

6684-D.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the household goods storage and moving trade. It also stays some rules about waiting periods for revised price lists and terms of sale. Another part about whether certain vehicles fall under the trucking industry code or this code is left for a later public hearing and further order.

6684-E.s: This order approves the Mason Contractors Chapter of the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry. It also changes the earlier approval of that code so it includes the Mason Contractors Chapter. It affects the mason contractors division of the construction industry.

6683.s: This order amends earlier executive orders about the Federal Alcohol Control Administration. It designates and appoints six named people as the present members of that administration.

6684-F.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the barber shop trade. It says the code will not take effect in any trade area until the area boundaries are approved, a local administrative board is set up, service names and minimum prices are set, and a price stabilization agreement is made and approved. Barbers in a trade area who sign the agreement and follow the code may use the National Recovery Administration Code Insignia before the code is fully effective there.

6682.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of public lands in two townships in Wyoming that had been held pending resurvey. After the resurvey plats are filed, the lands are opened only to entry under the homestead or desert-land laws by qualified ex-service men for 91 days. After that, the lands are open to the general public under the public-land laws that apply.

6681.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Oklahoma from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be classified and held pending legislation that would authorize their disposal and provide relief for bona fide claimants.

6680.s: This order abolishes the United States Geographic Board. It transfers the board’s functions, staff, records, supplies, equipment, property, and unspent funds to the Department of the Interior, where they will be supervised by the Secretary of the Interior. The order applies under the reorganization authority in the act of March 3, 1933, and it can be delayed if the President decides economy requires it.

6679.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn certain public land in Wyoming. It says the land may then be withdrawn by the Secretary of the Interior for use by the Department of Commerce as an intermediate landing field for air-navigation facilities.

6678-A.s: This order offers to extend the President’s Reemployment Agreement to the head of every business establishment for any part of the business not covered by an approved code of fair competition. The extension starts on May 1, 1934, and lasts until that part of the business is covered by an approved code. Employers who already signed before May 1 may accept by displaying the Blue Eagle, and those who have not signed may accept by signing the agreement. It also lets the Administrator for Industrial Recovery make rules to carry out the order.

6678.s: This order says a clause may be added to a code of fair competition if it is applied for and approved. The clause lets the Code Authority raise funds from industry members, with the Administrator’s approval, to cover the code’s expenses and enforce collection if needed. It also says only members who comply with the code and pay these expenses may help choose the Code Authority, use its emblem, or get the benefit of its voluntary activities.

6677.s: This order revokes part of a 1932 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in California. It opens the released lands to entry under the homestead and desert-land laws by qualified ex-service men for a set period. After that, the lands may be open to the general public under any public-land law that applies.

6676.s: This order changes the civil-service rules for certain positions in the Indian Service. It says the jobs covered are those that were not already excepted from examination under schedule A and where applicants are of one fourth or more Indian blood.

6675-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the live poultry industry in the metropolitan area in and about New York City. It applies to businesses in that industry in that area. The order says notice and hearings were held before approval.

6675.s: This order changes the amount paid to carriers in the Rural Mail Delivery Service for equipment maintenance. It sets that payment rate for each mile or major fraction of a mile scheduled for the period beginning April 1, 1934, and ending June 30, 1934.

6674.s: This order abolishes Beaufort, South Carolina, as a customs port of entry in customs collection district no. 16, which has headquarters at Charleston, South Carolina. The change takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

6673.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Oregon from use for classification. The lands are to be studied for their suitability as migratory bird refuge purposes, subject to reservoir and other incidental uses and existing valid rights. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

6672.s: This order withdraws public lands in one township in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry while a resurvey is done. It applies subject to valid existing rights and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6671.s: This order withdraws public lands in one township in Arizona from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It does this while a resurvey of that township is pending. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6670.s: This order transfers civil service retirement duties from the Veterans' Administration to the United States Civil Service Commission. It also transfers the related personnel, records, files, property, and some unexpended appropriations or allotments used for those duties. The order applies to retirement activities under the Civil Service Retirement Act, Executive Order No. 5398, and the Canal Zone Retirement Act.

6669.s: This order cancels Veterans Regulation No. 12 (a) effective March 28, 1934. The regulation concerns a presumption of entitlement to pensions for Spanish-War veterans and certain widows, children, and dependent parents of deceased World War veterans.

6668.s: This order cancels Veterans Regulation No. 1 (d), effective March 28, 1934. It changes the rules for veterans’ pension entitlement under that regulation.

6667.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in township 1 south, range 82 west of the sixth principal meridian in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The withdrawal lasts while a resurvey of the township is pending, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6665.s: This order lets Dr. John Bruce Arnold be appointed as acting assistant surgeon in the United States Public Health Service at the Treasury Department without meeting civil-service rule II requirements. It says he had been on duty abroad with the Public Health Service since February 1, 1921, and had been moved to a similar position in the United States that required civil-service eligibility.

6664.s: This order waives the time limit in civil-service rule IX so Miss Irene C. Claveloux can be reinstated to a position in the General Accounting Office. It affects her and the General Accounting Office.

6663.s: This order exempts Luther L. Browning from the rule that required automatic retirement at the retirement age. It lets him continue working in the Government Printing Office until April 1, 1935.

6666.s: This order revokes a 1928 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Colorado. It says the lands will first be open only to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plats. After that, the lands will be open to the general public under any applicable public-land law.

6662.s: This order amends Veterans Regulation No. 12 to give some Spanish-American War veterans a presumed right to receive a pension without further application. It also covers some veterans whose pensions were reduced or stopped, letting them receive 75 percent of the payments they were getting on March 19, 1933, until the Board of Veterans' Appeals decides their cases. The Board and the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs are directed to review and develop these cases, and the order sets limits for cases that do not meet the service and discharge requirements.

6660.s: This order lets the heads of emergency agencies, executive departments, and other independent establishments spend money already allocated to them for national industrial recovery. It allows those funds to be used for personal services, rent, law books, paper, printing, binding, and passenger-carrying vehicles. It also confirms spending made before the date of the order, and says later purchases, maintenance, and operation of motor-propelled passenger-carrying vehicles must follow another law.

6661.s: This order amends Veterans Regulation No. 1 (a) by adding rules for some pension claims that were disallowed by special boards of review. In those cases, 75 percent of the payments being made on March 19, 1933, shall be paid from the date of the regulation until the Board of Veterans' Appeals makes a decision. If the Board grants service connection on review, pension is payable from July 1, 1933, and the Board and the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs are directed to review and develop these cases.

6659.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the infants' and children's wear industry. It sets rules for manufacturers of infants' and children's wear, including how some businesses that also make products covered by other codes may choose which code to follow. It also gives special rules for infants' and children's bathrobes, girls' coats, and certain other clothing items covered by the order.

6658.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Shoe Rebuilding Trade. It also stays one part of the code, Article VI, Section 6, subsection (i), until the Administrator changes it after further study and a public hearing. The order affects people and businesses in the shoe rebuilding trade.

6657-A.s: This order sets temporary rules for reimbursing officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States who are serving in foreign countries for losses caused by foreign currency rising in value against the American dollar. It defines when a person is considered to be serving abroad and explains how to calculate the loss from salary, pay, and allowances. It also sets basic exchange rates for many currencies and says the order takes effect on April 1, 1934.

6657.s: This order set temporary rules for reimbursing officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States in foreign countries for losses caused by foreign currency changes. It said the rules applied to people serving abroad, including some travel and leave situations, and it set how much salary and allowances would count for reimbursement. It also listed basic exchange rates for many foreign currencies and said the order was later superseded and never actually in operation.

6655.s: This order changes the civil-service rules for the Post Office Department. It adds two exempt positions: assistant private secretary to the Postmaster General and private secretary to the executive assistant to the Postmaster General. It also keeps the listed exempt positions for certain other Post Office Department offices.

6656.s: This order says the Executive Committee on Commercial Policy will keep carrying out its current work to help coordinate the commercial policy of the United States. It also says the Special Adviser to the President on Foreign Trade will work with that committee and add to its work in the areas covered by the earlier order. The committee’s chairman must be a representative of the Department of State chosen by the Secretary of State.

6654.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Lumber and Timber Products Industries. It affects the lumber and timber products industries and follows an application from the Lumber Code Authority.

6653.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the photographic and photo finishing industry. It applies to businesses in that industry. It also stays the rule that would require a waiting period before revised price lists or revised terms and conditions of sale can take effect.

6652.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for Investment Bankers. It says the Administrator may approve later changes to the code after notice and a hearing. Those changes may be made to give prompt relief from hardship or to deal with unforeseen contingencies.

6651.s: This order creates the Office of Special Adviser to the President on Foreign Trade. The Special Adviser is appointed by the President and is allowed to collect and coordinate foreign trade information from federal agencies, and to carry on talks about specific trade transactions. Federal departments and export-import banks are asked to share information and work with the Special Adviser, but existing departments keep their legal roles in foreign trade policy and general trade agreements.

6650.s: This order changes the rules for passport applications and renewals. It sets the fee for a passport application at $9 when filed before a clerk of court and says the fee for a renewal request is $5. It also cancels Rule 99.

6649.s: This order allows Mrs. Elizabeth Bass to be appointed as district supervisor in the Bureau of Narcotics in the Treasury Department without meeting civil-service rule II requirements. It applies only to her appointment to that position. The order says she had been serving temporarily in that job with approval of the Civil Service Commission.

6648.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for grain exchanges and the people who are members of them. It says an application was made, notice and hearings were given, and the code was found to comply with the National Industrial Recovery Act. It applies to grain exchanges and their members.

6647-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Machinery and Allied Products Industry. It also requires the trade associations for the 39 subdivisions of the code to amend their governing documents to the Administrator’s satisfaction, and it directs two code authorities to study the code definitions and recommend changes to remove any overlap.

6647-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the bowling and billiard operating trade. It affects businesses in that trade by putting the code into effect under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6646.s: This order requires federal bidders, contractors, and suppliers to certify that they comply with approved codes of fair competition or with an agreement with the President when no code applies. It also applies these rules to some contracts and purchase orders made by states, local governments, people, or corporations using federal loans or grants. False certification can lead to punishment, cancellation of the contract, and completion of the work at the person’s expense.

6645.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in South Dakota from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be used to provide material for the construction and repair of public roads.

6647.s: This order exempts W. H. Moran, Chief of the Secret Service Division in the Treasury Department, from the rule that would require civilian employees to leave service at the retirement age. It lets him continue in service until March 31, 1936.

6644.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in two Colorado townships from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It keeps that restriction in place while those townships are resurveyed, and it says valid existing rights are still protected. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6643.s: This order revokes part of a 1932 withdrawal of certain public lands in California. The released lands are opened first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead and desert-land laws for a limited period. After that period, the lands may be available to the general public under the public-land laws that apply.

6642.s: This order revokes a 1929 withdrawal of certain public lands in California. It says those lands will be opened first only to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws for a 91-day period after the plats of resurvey are officially filed. After that, the lands will be open to the general public under any applicable public-land law.

6640.s: This order approves Chapter III of the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry. It applies to the Painting, Paperhanging and Decorating Division of the Construction Industry and modifies the earlier code approval to include that chapter.

6641.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the scrap iron, nonferrous scrap metals, and waste materials trade. It also requires the Code Authority or Administration Member for the waste paper trade to report whether a separate supplementary code is needed and to recommend its provisions. If approved by the Administrator, those recommendations would have the same force and effect as the rest of the code.

6638.s: This order creates a banking corporation called the Second Export-Import Bank of Washington, D.C. It is meant to help finance and facilitate exports and imports, and the exchange of commodities between the United States and other nations or their agencies or nationals. The corporation will operate in the District of Columbia, with a board of trustees and capital stock set up for common and preferred shares. The Secretary of State and the Secretary of Commerce are directed to form the corporation and subscribe to its common stock for the United States.

6639.s: This order consolidates executive agencies that enforced the internal revenue laws. It abolishes the Bureau of Industrial Alcohol and the Office of Commissioner of Industrial Alcohol, and transfers their powers, records, property, employees, and certain funds to the Bureau of Internal Revenue under the Secretary of the Treasury. It also transfers some functions and personnel from the Department of Justice to the Bureau of Internal Revenue and revokes parts of earlier executive orders that conflict with it.

6637.s: This order directs the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works to give $50,000 to the National Recovery Review Board. The money is to come from funds already set aside for the National Recovery Administration.

6636.s: This order allows Mrs. Marion Doody to be appointed as a charwoman in the custodial service at the Boston Post Office, without following the regular rules for appointing unclassified laborers. Mrs. Doody is the widow of William Doody, who served many years as a carrier in the Post Office Department.

6635.s: This order abolishes Wichita, Kansas, as a customs port of entry in customs collection district No. 45, with headquarters at St. Louis, Missouri. The change takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

6634.s: This order designates Lawrenceburg, Indiana, as a customs port of entry in customs collection district no. 40, with headquarters at Indianapolis. It also includes the adjoining town of Greendale, Indiana, within the limits of that port.

6632.s: This order creates the National Recovery Review Board and names its members. The board is to review approved competition codes and report whether they are designed to promote monopolies, oppress small enterprises, or discriminate against them. It may also recommend changes to approved codes and use National Recovery Administration facilities and records when needed.

6631-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the anti hog cholera serum and hog cholera virus industry. It says the code was applied for, notices and hearings were given, and the code was found to comply with the law. It affects businesses in that industry.

6630.s: This order restores a tract of land from the Aiea Military Reservation to the Territory of Hawaii for road purposes. The land stays subject to an existing lease and to United States rights-of-way across, over, and under it. If a road is not built on the land within 1 year, or if it later stops being used for road purposes, the land goes back under the control of the War and Navy Departments.

6629.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Louisiana and Mississippi from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be classified while a decision is made on whether to include them in national forests. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6628.s: This order withdraws Short Island in American Lake, Washington, from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets the island aside for use in connection with military purposes of the War Department, subject to valid existing rights.

6626.s: This order temporarily withdraws two lots in the townsite of Anchorage, Alaska, from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lots and the improvements on them for the use of the War Department, and it stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6627.s: This order changes a 1930 withdrawal of public lands in Nevada so an airport lease can be issued to Eureka County, Nevada. It applies to 600 acres of public land in Township 20 North, Range 53 East of the Mount Diablo Meridian. The lands were previously withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, or entry while a resurvey was pending.

6624.s: This order delays the effective date of the part of Executive Order No. 6166 that abolishes the Federal Employment Stabilization Board and transfers its records to the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works. It says the change will be delayed until the board’s functions can be transferred as provided in Executive Order No. 6623.

6625.s: This order appoints Rear Admiral Christian Joy Peoples, Director of Procurement, as a member of the Special Board for Public Works. He is to succeed and act in the place of Assistant Secretary of the Treasury L. W. Robert, Jr.

6622.s: This order changes a previous rule on compensation for government employees in emergency agencies. It excludes most Federal Civil Works Administration employees from that rule, except clerical and administrative staff in the central office in the District of Columbia.

6623.s: This order abolishes the Federal Employment Stabilization Board. It creates the Federal Employment Stabilization Office in the Department of Commerce and moves the board’s functions, director, other personnel, records, supplies, equipment, property, and unspent funds to that office. It also revokes a part of a prior executive order about the board.

6621.s: This order transfers certain lands, buildings, equipment, and furnishings at the Naval Station in St. Thomas to the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Interior. The items are to be used in running the government of the Virgin Islands. The land and buildings must be kept in good repair and returned to the Secretary of the Navy when needed for naval uses.

6620-B.s: This order changes the earlier approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Hotel Industry by striking two of its conditions. It also says the Administrator will review the code by June 1, 1934 to see whether it carries out the policy and purpose of Title 1 of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6620-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Fishery Industry. The code does not take effect right away; it is stayed for 10 days so interested parties can consider objections. After that, it will become effective unless the President changes or extends the stay.

6620.s: This order revokes part of Executive Order No. 6025 that created Public Water Reserve No. 149 for certain lands in Wyoming. The lands named in the order will not be open to disposal under the public lands laws until a later date and after notice is announced.

6619.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Arizona, Utah, and Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use. The order applies only to the specific tracts listed in each state.

6618.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use. The order applies only to the public lands described in it and is subject to valid existing rights.

6617.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The lands are to be used in connection with the Walker River Indian irrigation project, and the withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6616.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for use as an addition to the Cordova Aviation Landing Field. The land is described as about 18.22 acres and is in front of survey no. 1668 and in the bed of Eyak Lake.

6614.s: This order transfers the administration of national cemeteries and memorials in Europe from the War Department to the American Battle Monuments Commission. It also transfers the related civilian personnel, records, supplies, equipment, property, and available unexpended balances for those functions. The order revokes the earlier provision that would have moved administration of national cemeteries in foreign countries to the Department of State.

6615.s: This order exempts Jacob L. Nuber from the rule that requires civilian employees to retire at the set age. It lets him stay in service as Chief of the Printing and Binding Section, Bureau of Internal Revenue, Treasury Department, until February 28, 1935.

6613.s: This order revokes a 1931 withdrawal of certain public lands in Colorado. After the resurvey plat is officially filed, the land would be open for 91 days only to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws, subject to valid rights and existing withdrawals. After that, it would be open to the general public under the public-land laws that apply.

6613-A.s: This order changes earlier approvals for the codes for the Graphic Arts Industries and the Daily Newspaper Publishing Business. It says government members of the Graphic Arts Industries code authority should pay special attention to the rules allowing minors to sell and deliver newspapers, periodicals, and advertising newspapers, and report to the President within sixty days. It also says one comment applies to both codes, but the named parts of the two codes are still approved without change.

6612-A.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about the National Labor Board. It says that if the Board finds an employer interfered with an election, refused to recognize or bargain with employee representatives, or otherwise violated section 7 (a), the Board may report those findings and make recommendations to the Attorney General or the Compliance Division of the National Recovery Administration. The Compliance Division may then take appropriate action based on the Board’s findings.

6612.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 3870 of June 19, 1923. That earlier order set a procedure for classifying officers of the Army under the named law.

6611.s: This order transfers the Bureau of Mines and all of its functions from the Department of Commerce to the Department of the Interior. It also transfers the bureau’s personnel, records, supplies, equipment, property, and unspent funds. The Bureau of Mines will be administered under the supervision of the Secretary of the Interior.

6610.s: This order exempts C. Frank Wittenauer from the rule requiring retirement at the set age for automatic separation from service. It lets him stay in service until August 31, 1934.

6609.s: This order exempts John Bach from the rule that would require his automatic retirement at age. It lets him stay in civilian service until February 28, 1935.

6608.s: This order changes the rules for interest on deposit money orders issued by the Canal Zone Postal Service. It sets different interest rates for orders issued on or after April 1, 1934, and for orders issued before that date. Interest is paid when the order is paid and does not build up for more than 3 years. The Governor of the Panama Canal may set detailed rules to carry out the order.

6607.s: This order temporarily withdraws a piece of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The Department of Agriculture may use the land as a fire-lookout site for the Trinity National Forest. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6606-C.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Advertising Distributing Trade. For 90 days, boys ages 14 and 15 may be employed up to three hours a day, between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m., and not during school hours. It also pauses one rule on working hours for 90 days and requires a report on the hours and pay of office workers within 90 days.

6606-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Graphic Arts Industries. It deletes one section, transfers some duties to Code Authorities and Compliance Boards, and allows the Administrator to appoint a National Graphic Arts Labor Board to hear disputes over wages, hours, and other working conditions. It says the hours rules are not to be treated as a minimum work day or work week, requires the code's hours, wages, and employment rules to be posted at covered establishments, and sets conditions for trade associations to keep taking part in the code's administration. It also delays one part of the code on prison made products for 90 days or longer at the Administrator's discretion.

6606-A.s: This order says codes of fair competition cannot be used to make sales to or through bona fide and legitimate cooperative organizations, including farmers' cooperatives, a violation. It also says these cooperatives may receive and pass on discounts, commissions, rebates, or dividends that are given to other wholesale or middleman purchasers. The Administrator for Industrial Recovery is allowed to decide whether an organization qualifies as a bona fide and legitimate cooperative organization.

6606.s: The order changes the rules for veterans seeking review of disability and death pension claims. It says appeals must be filed within 1 year with the office that issued the denial. If no appeal is filed in time, the decision becomes final, unless new and material official service department reports later allow the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs to reopen the claim.

6606-G.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the daily newspaper publishing business. It also requires that hours and wages for news department workers be set within 60 days and that government members of the Code Authority pay special attention to the rules allowing minors to deliver and sell newspapers.

6606-D.s: This order approves Chapter II of the Code of Fair Competition for the General Contractors Division of the Construction Industry. It also changes the earlier approval of the construction industry code to include that chapter as part of the full code.

6606-E.s: This order amends the approved Code of Fair Competition for the Electrotyping and Stereotyping Industry. It says the maximum hours in the code are not to be treated as a minimum work day or week. If enough employees ask in writing, work hours may be changed by agreement so available work can be shared with bona fide resident unemployed competent mechanics, and disputes can go to a local board and then to the Labor Board.

6605.s: This order changes the rules for commutation of rations and quarters for enlisted men by adding the American Embassy in Moscow, U.S.S.R. to the list in the earlier order. It also sets special subsistence and quarters amounts for the American Embassy in Moscow.

6604-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the restaurant industry. It suspends some parts of the code for certain restaurant employees and for employees of hotel restaurants with not more than 15 workers, while setting limits on hours and pay for those workers. It also says the regular full-time work week for any class of employees cannot be increased, and that no female employee may work more than 48 hours a week except as allowed by the code. The order also suspends the code’s stop loss provision until further review.

6604.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Nebraska and South Dakota from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The lands are set aside for soil classification. It applies only to the townships listed in the order and does not affect valid existing rights.

6604-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the laundry trade for 90 days. It says the Administrator will study the minimum wages in the code and report back. The code does not become fully effective in a trade area until several local steps are completed, including set trade area boundaries, a Code Control Board, approved service names and prices, and an approved petition showing support in that area.

6603.s: This order allocates $500,000,000 to the Federal Emergency Relief Administration from money already appropriated under the Federal Emergency Relief Act of 1933. The money may be used for grants to States and for administrative expenses. Some of the money is available for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1934, and the rest is available for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1935.

6603-A.s: This order lets the House Committee on Naval Affairs, or a subcommittee, inspect tax returns for companies that make or sell airplanes, airplane engines, motors, and related parts and accessories. It applies to companies that have done business with the Navy Department since 1921, including their holding, affiliate, and subsidiary companies. The inspections must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury and approved by the President.

6602.s: This order directs certain disbursing officers to make payment for supplies and services used by the Federal Civil Works Administration, once they are certified by a designated certifying officer. It also allocates $450,000,000 from a $950,000,000 appropriation to continue the Federal Civil Works program. The funds are to be used under the existing rules and regulations of the Federal Civil Works Administration, as they may be changed later.

6601-A.s: This order increases the board of trustees of the Export-Import Bank of Washington from five members to not less than five and not more than nine members. It adds four named people as additional trustees. Any vacancies on the board are to be filled under the bank’s certificate of incorporation and bylaws, with the President’s approval.

6601.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the retail solid fuel industry. It applies to that industry and sets a condition that the Administrator report to the President within 120 days after the code takes effect. The President keeps the power to change or eliminate parts of the code after that report.

6606-F.s: This order says some people with physical or mental handicaps, age, or other infirmity may be employed on light work at wages below the minimum set by a Code of Fair Competition. The employer must get a certificate from the state authority designated by the U.S. Department of Labor, and the employer must file a monthly list of these workers with the Code Authority. It also changes any existing approval orders for these codes if needed so these rules can be carried out.

6600.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Trucking Industry. It also requires certain vehicles owned and operated by enterprises mainly engaged in warehousing furniture and household goods to be registered with the Code Committee, and later with the Code Authority if that code is approved.

6599.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Gray Iron Foundry Industry. It follows an application, hearings, and a report from the Administrator. It affects businesses in that industry under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6597.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Chemical Manufacturing Industry. It affects businesses and workers in that industry by putting the approved code into effect.

6598.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Pleating, Stitching and Bonnaz and Hand Embroidery Industry. It requires the Code Authority to study whether the minimum wages are becoming maximum wages and to report back with recommendations on the wage rates. The Administrator may also hold hearings to look into whether the wage rates are tending to establish maximum wages.

6596.s: This order directs Willis R. Gregg, the Chief of the Weather Bureau in the Department of Agriculture, to perform the duties of Secretary of Agriculture. He would do so during the absence of the Secretary of Agriculture and the Assistant Secretary of Agriculture.

6595.s: This order lets the Director of the United States Employment Service accept and use unpaid volunteer help. It is limited to no more than 15 people for a project on occupational specifications and classifications.

6594.s: This order transfers part of the Naval Reservation at Ediz Hook in Port Angeles, Washington, from the Navy Department to the Treasury Department for Coast Guard purposes. It keeps a right-of-way for the Department of Commerce for a roadway to the lighthouse station and for telephone, light, power, and water lines. If the land stops being used for Coast Guard purposes, control goes back to the Navy Department.

6593.s: This order authorizes the Beet Sugar Committee to accept and use the voluntary, unpaid services of Professor W. Lewis Abbott. It applies to the committee and to Professor Abbott.

6592.s: This order temporarily withdraws a piece of public land in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It does this while Congress considers legislation that would let the city of Forest Grove buy the land for use as part of its watershed.

6591.s: This order directs the Postmaster General, the Secretary of War, and the Secretary of Commerce to work together so air mail service can continue during the emergency. It also directs the Secretary of War to make Army airplanes, landing fields, pilots, and other equipment available for carrying mail on routes and schedules set by the Postmaster General.

6590-A.s: This order gives the Administrator for Industrial Recovery authority to make rules and regulations about changes to approved codes of fair competition under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. It covers amendments, modifications, exceptions, exemptions, stays, and other forms of relief from those codes.

6590-B.s: This order authorizes the Administrator for Industrial Recovery to make rules for people covered by approved codes of fair competition. Those rules can require them to post or display the code terms, or otherwise bring them to the attention of interested persons, including employees. It also authorizes the Administrator to take other steps to carry out those rules. The order says violating any rule or regulation made under it can lead to a fine, imprisonment, or both.

6590.s: This order revokes part of a 1910 executive order that had created a coal-land withdrawal in New Mexico. It applies to the specific land described in Section 4, Township 9 North, Range 16 West, southeast quarter.

6589.s: This order amends a rule about licensing motor vehicles in the Canal Zone. It applies the rule to vehicles owned and operated by the United States Government and certain authorized groups, the Panama Railroad Co., and the Republic of Panama. It also allows the Governor to authorize free official licenses for passenger automobiles for legations in or accredited to the Republic of Panama or the Canal Zone.

6588.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation, subject to valid existing rights. It sets aside those lands for the War Department to use as a bombing and gunnery range. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6587.s: This order withdraws certain public land in Utah from settlement, location, sale, or entry, as far as the land is still owned by the United States. It reserves the land for classification, for aid in legislation, for conservation and development of natural resources, and for use as grazing land. The Secretary of the Interior may prescribe rules and regulations for its use.

6585.s: This order delays the effective date of section 18 of Executive Order No. 6166. The new effective date is April 10, 1934.

6586.s: This order revokes section 18 of Executive Order No. 6166. That section had partly abolished functions involving cooperative vocational education and rehabilitation, payments for agricultural experiment stations, cooperative agricultural extension work, and endowment and maintenance of colleges for agriculture and the mechanic arts. It affects those government functions and funding areas.

6584.s: This order transfers certain land on Sand and Quarantine Islands among the Treasury Department, the Department of Commerce, and the War Department. It says the land is needed for work to widen and deepen the entrance channel to Honolulu Harbor and enlarge the harbor basin. If the Treasury Department or the Department of Commerce stops using land it receives and gives formal notice, that land goes back to the War Department. It also sets aside some land for use by the War Department in connection with the harbor improvements.

6583.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It does this to help the State of New Mexico make exchange selections under the listed laws. The lands remain subject to valid existing rights unless the President or Congress revokes the order.

6581.s: This order creates a banking corporation called the Export-Import Bank of Washington. It says the bank is meant to help finance and facilitate exports and imports and the exchange of commodities between the United States and other nations, or their agencies or nationals. It also directs the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Commerce to form the corporation and subscribe for its common stock for the United States.

6582.s: This order sets aside the Killcohook Disposal Area in New Jersey and Delaware as a refuge and breeding ground for wild birds and animals. It places the area under the Department of Agriculture, but subject to existing valid rights and some War Department uses. It also bars hunting, trapping, disturbing, killing, or entering there except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture, and forbids cutting natural growth, leaving fires unattended, or damaging U.S. property.

6580.s: The order directs the National Labor Board to arrange and supervise union representation elections when a substantial number of employees ask for one. It says the Board will publish the names of representatives chosen by a majority of voting employees. If an employer refuses to recognize or deal with those representatives, the Board must report that to the Administrator for Industrial Recovery.

6579.s: This order removes several listed tracts of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest and restores them to entry under the public-land laws. The tracts are home sites in the Wrangell area, near Auke Lake by Juneau, on Klawak Inlet, and on Revillagigedo Island. It applies to the land areas described in the order.

6578-A.s: This order appoints James H. Pierce of Scranton, Pennsylvania, to the National Bituminous Coal Industrial Board. It is made under the Code of Fair Competition for the Bituminous Coal Industry.

6578.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the construction industry. It says an application was filed, hearings were held, and the Administrator reported that the code met the required parts of the National Industrial Recovery Act. It affects the construction industry and the people and businesses covered by that code.

6577-A.s: This order allows Miss Will Harris to be appointed in the classified civil service without following the usual Civil Service rules. It applies to her appointment and the civil service hiring requirements named in the order.

6576.s: This order changes the rules for the Federal Alcohol Control Administration. It sets the Administration at six people named by the President, gives each member one vote, and gives the Director an extra vote in a tie. It also names the current members and says the Director will assign members to work with certain federal departments and choose one member to serve as Assistant Director.

6577.s: This order exempts Carleton W. Sturtevant from the rule that required automatic separation at retirement age. It lets him stay in civilian service in the War Department until July 31, 1934.

6575.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6237 from July 28, 1933. That earlier order had allocated funds to buy land needed to complete the Great Smoky Mountains National Park.

6575-A.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of State to acquire real or personal property for Department of State projects by purchase or by eminent domain. It also allows the Secretary to sell or lease that property and sign any needed documents for its transfer. The order specifically includes the Rio Grande rectification project.

6574.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Oregon and Washington from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other use. The withdrawal is connected to construction of a dam in the Columbia River near Bonneville, Oregon, for projects 27 and 28 of the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6573.s: This order revokes part of a 1932 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in California. It opens the released lands first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead and desert-land laws for 91 days, then to the general public under any applicable public-land law. Until then, no one may gain rights to those lands except as allowed by this order.

6572.s: This order revokes a 1932 withdrawal of public lands in a township in New Mexico. It says those lands will be open only to entry under the homestead or desert-land laws by qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat. After that, the lands may be opened to the general public under any applicable public-land law. It also says no one may gain rights to the land by settlement before entry except as allowed by the order.

6571.s: This order lets certain Navy medical and dental officers who were attached to the War Department for duty with the Civilian Conservation Corps be relieved from that duty. The Secretary of War may do this when the officers can be replaced or when their services are no longer needed. It affects those naval medical and dental officers and the agencies they were attached to.

6570.s: This order restores part of the Schofield Barracks Military Reservation in Hawaii to the Territory of Hawaii. The land may be used as a right-of-way to build and maintain a territorial road or highway. If it is not used for that purpose within 2 years, or if the governor says Hawaii does not want to use it anymore, the land goes back to the War Department.

6569.s: This order sets up a process for complaints about monopolistic practices under approved codes of fair competition. If a complainant is dissatisfied with a federal agency’s handling of the complaint, the complaint can be sent to the Federal Trade Commission. The FTC may then start a proceeding if it thinks it is in the public interest, or send the complaint to the Department of Justice in some cases.

6567.s: This order changes rules for paying burial and funeral expenses for honorably discharged war veterans who die after discharge. It allows the Veterans Administration to pay up to $100 for burial, funeral, and transportation of the body, but not if the veteran’s net assets at death are $1,000 or more. If a veteran dies in a Veterans Administration facility, the agency will pay the actual burial and funeral cost up to $100 and arrange transportation of the body under the stated rules. The change does not apply to cases where death happened before the order was issued.

6568.s: This order changes Veterans' Regulation No. 10 so that some people working for the United States Government, the District of Columbia government, or certain government-owned corporations cannot receive a pension or emergency officers' retirement pay while also drawing a salary from that job. It lists exceptions for some disability cases, some protected pensions, some lower-paid workers, and widows of veterans. It also says a person entitled to certain monetary benefits may renounce the right in writing, and then those benefits stop and a later application is treated as an original application.

6566.s: This order changes rules for Veterans' Affairs care. It lets the Administrator provide domiciliary or hospital care, including medical treatment, to certain honorably discharged veterans and other discharged service members who meet the listed conditions. It also allows travel and body-transport costs in some cases, limits some pensions while a person is receiving government care, and lets part of a pension be paid to a wife, child, or dependent parent in some situations.

6565.s: This order changes Veterans' Regulation No. 1 so monthly pension amounts are set by disability rating, from $10 for a 10 percent disability up to $100 for a total disability. It also sets a pension rule for the surviving widow of certain deceased service members, with a cap of $30 per month. The order changes pension rules for some veterans of the Spanish-American War, Boxer rebellion, Philippine insurrection, and World War, and it says the changes take effect on the date they were issued.

6564-A.s: This order retires Alfred T. Burri, a Foreign Service officer, on an annuity under the law cited in the order. It says he was found permanently and totally disabled for useful and efficient service because of disease, and that the disability was not due to vicious habits, intemperance, or willful misconduct on his part.

6564.s: This order revokes part of a 1929 withdrawal of public lands in one township in Wyoming. It opens those lands first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws for 91 days after the resurvey plat is filed, subject to valid rights and existing withdrawals. After that, the lands may be used by the general public under any applicable public-land law.

6563.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of certain public lands in New Mexico that were pending resurvey. After the plats of resurvey are filed, the lands are open for 91 days only to entry under the homestead or desert-land laws by qualified ex-service men. After that, the lands are open to the general public under any public-land law that applies.

6562.s: This order gives enlisted men of the Army extra pay if they establish special qualifications in using the arms they may be required to use. The Secretary of War sets the standards and the conditions for the pay. The extra compensation is paid in five classes, from $1 to $5 per month.

6561.s: This order delays the abolition of the volunteer field agencies created under earlier executive orders. Those agencies will keep doing their current work until the Executive Director tells them they are abolished.

6560-B.s: This order appoints John L. Lewis as a member of the National Bituminous Coal Industrial Board. It is made under the Code of Fair Competition for the Bituminous Coal Industry.

6560-A.s: This order appoints F. E. Berquist as a member of the National Bituminous Coal Industrial Board. It applies to the board for the bituminous coal industry.

6559.s: This order changes earlier rules on banks by removing a restriction on foreign exchange transactions in certain licenses. It applies to banks covered by the earlier order of March 10, 1933, and to banking institutions that are not members of the Federal Reserve System. It also says the change does not affect earlier acts or orders, and it does not remove any duty to follow the January 15, 1934 order on the export of coin and currency and foreign exchange transactions.

6558.s: This order says a national emergency exists and sets rules for receiving gold on consignment for sale. It allows U.S. mints and assay offices to receive gold if they are satisfied it was not held in violation of earlier executive orders, Treasury orders, regulations, rulings, or licenses. It also gives the Secretary of the Treasury power to issue rules to carry out the order, and says the order can be changed or revoked at any time.

6560.s: The order says a national emergency continues and sets rules for foreign exchange, transfers of credit, and the export or withdrawal of U.S. currency or silver coin. It generally prohibits these transactions unless a license is issued, with some exceptions for normal business needs, reasonable travel and personal needs, and obligations made before March 9, 1933. It also gives the Secretary of the Treasury authority to issue regulations, grant licenses, require reports and records, and enforce penalties for violations.

6557-C.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Raw Peanut Milling Industry. It says an application was made, notice was given, and hearings were held before approval. The order affects businesses in the raw peanut milling industry.

6557-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the carpet and rug manufacturing industry. It also stays the provisions of Article VII, Section 19(a) until the Administrator finishes further investigation and determination of the issues raised.

6557-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the wholesaling or distributing trade. It applies to businesses in that trade and follows an application, hearings, and a report by the Administrator.

6556.s: This order amends rules on buying and exporting gold coin, gold bullion, and gold certificates. It says no one other than a Federal Reserve bank may acquire gold coin, gold bullion, or gold certificates in the United States unless licensed, with limited exceptions for member banks, certain users of gold in business, and collectors of rare and unusual coin. It also adds a rule allowing the export of certain gold coin with recognized special value to collectors, through an agency the President designates.

6555.s: This order allows Mr. Robert K. McQueen to be appointed as a lockmaster in the Engineer Department at large of the War Department. It waives the usual requirements of Civil Service Rule II for that appointment.

6554.s: This order extends the pay rules in Executive Order 6440 to all other existing emergency agencies and to any emergency agencies created later. It applies to officers and employees whose pay is set without using the Classification Act of 1923, as amended.

6553.s: This order announces cost-of-living index figures for the periods ending June 30, 1928, and December 31, 1933. It says the index for December 31, 1933 was 21.1 percent lower than the base period. It also says a 15 percent reduction applies to the compensation of officers and employees for the period from January 1, 1934, to June 30, 1934.

6551.s: This order changes earlier orders that gave the Secretary of Agriculture certain powers under the National Industrial Recovery Act. It transfers those powers to the Administrator of the National Recovery Administration, but keeps some powers with the Secretary of Agriculture for certain agricultural industries and first processors. It also says some subjects, like prices, brokerage fees, credits, marketing quotas, and plant capacity, cannot be controlled for those first processors without the Secretary’s written approval. If there is a dispute about whether an industry is covered, the Secretary and the Administrator decide it in writing, or the President makes the final decision.

6552.s: This order changes the 1928 order creating Public Water Reserve No. 116 in California. It authorizes the Federal Power Commission to issue an amendment to the license for project no. 923 of the Southern California Edison Company on the listed lands in San Bernardino Meridian.

6549-A.s: This order approves a new Code of Fair Competition for the Wholesale Food and Grocery Trade and puts it in place of the earlier Code of Labor Provisions. It also changes some parts of the code by delaying two provisions for 30 days and eliminating one section. The Administrator must consider the right of the United States Wholesale Grocers Association to representation on the code authority, hold a hearing on the listed questions, and may disapprove any act of the code authority.

6549.s: This order requires accounts of receipts and expenditures by governmental agencies, including corporations, created after March 3, 1933, to be reported to the General Accounting Office. The Comptroller General of the United States may set how, how much, and when those accounts are reported for settlement and adjustment.

6547.s: This order creates a Board of Veterans' Appeals in the Veterans' Administration. It says the board will have a chairman, a vice chairman, up to 30 associate members, and other staff needed to handle hearings and appeals. Members are appointed by the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs with the President's approval.

6548.s: This order stops federal departments, independent establishments, government agencies, and certain government-owned corporations from taking on new obligations from emergency appropriations or other emergency funds until their spending estimates are approved by the Director of the Bureau of the Budget. The Director may, with the President's approval, delay applying this rule for up to 60 days, and the order says it does not apply to the Department of State's regular appropriation for emergencies in the diplomatic and consular service.

6546.s: This order withdraws and reserves a specific 4.94-acre area of public land in the Territory of Alaska for burial purposes. It is subject to valid existing rights. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6545.s: This order changes the name of the customs port of Nyando, New York, to Rooseveltown, New York. It applies to the customs collection district no. 7 (St. Lawrence), with headquarters at Ogdensburg, New York.

6544.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be used by the Department of Agriculture as fire-lookout sites and as a site for storing explosives in connection with the Shasta and Trinity National Forests. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6543-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the household ice refrigerator industry. It applies to that industry and puts the approved code into effect under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6543-C.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Shoe and Leather Finish, Polish, and Cement Manufacturing Industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and puts the approved code into effect.

6543-F.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the cotton cloth glove manufacturing industry. It affects businesses in that industry by putting the approved code into effect under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6543-A.s: This order gives the Administrator for Industrial Recovery the power to approve codes of fair competition, except for codes for major industries and certain codes under the act. It also gives the Administrator power to approve changes, exceptions, exemptions, or removals of parts of those codes. It does not change earlier power given to other government departments.

6543-G.s: This order approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Velvet Industry. It applies to the velvet industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about that code.

6543-H.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Coated Abrasives Industry. It applies to that industry and follows an application and hearings under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6543-J.s: This order approves a "Code of Fair Competition" for the cinders, ashes, and scavenger trade. It adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings for that trade.

6543-K.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Cast Iron Pressure Pipe Industry. It applies to the businesses and workers covered by that industry’s code.

6543-L.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Folding Paper Box Industry. It applies to the folding paper box industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6543-M.s: This order approves a code of fair competition for the blouse and skirt manufacturing industries. It also stays the code for the manufacture and sale of vestees, gilets, and guimpes until a public hearing is held and the Administrator decides whether they should be included. It affects businesses in those manufacturing industries.

6543-I.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Paper Stationery and Tablet Manufacturing Industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and puts the approved code into effect under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6543-N.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the American Match Industry. It applies to the businesses and other people covered by that industry’s code under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6543-O.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Wall Paper Manufacturing Industry. It makes those amendments part of the code. It affects the wall paper manufacturing industry and the group that applied for the changes.

6543.s: This order approves a new Code of Fair Competition for the retail food and grocery trade. It replaces the earlier Code of Labor Provisions for that trade. The order also delays one paragraph for 30 days, removes another paragraph, and gives the Administrator power to disapprove any act of the code authority.

6543-D.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the concrete pipe manufacturing industry. It applies to the companies and workers in that industry. The order says the code met the requirements of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6543-E.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the End Grain Strip Wood Block Industry. It applies to that industry and follows the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6542.s: This order authorizes the United States to buy certain privately owned lands near several national park and monument projects in North Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia, and Kentucky. The land purchases are meant to help protect public lands from forest fires, floods, soil erosion, plant pests, and disease. The order also says the work will provide employment for unemployed citizens of the United States.

6541.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are set aside for flood and erosion control in connection with cooperative Civilian Conservation Corps work. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6539-C.s: This order directs the reinstatement of three former Foreign Service officers who had resigned when they were appointed to positions in the Department of State. Their reinstatement takes effect when the Senate confirms their nominations, and they are placed in the Foreign Service classes listed in the order.

6539-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Commercial and Breeder Hatchery Industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and follows hearings and review under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6539.s: This order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Lace Manufacturing Industry. It makes those amendments part of the code and applies to the lace manufacturing industry.

6539-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the wine industry. It says the Secretary of Agriculture submitted the code, hearings were held, and the code met the requirements of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The order affects the wine industry and the parties involved in those hearings.

6538.s: This order appoints R. B. Paddock as a nonvoting member of the Code Authority for the Toy and Playthings Industry. He is to represent the Administration on that Code Authority.

6537.s: This order appoints named people to serve on a temporary Code Authority for the Motor Vehicle Storage and Parking Trade. The temporary authority will serve until a permanent Code Authority is elected. If a member resigns, the Administrator for Industrial Recovery may appoint a successor.

6536.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the watch case manufacturing industry. It says an application was made, hearings were held, and the Administrator reported that the code met the requirements of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The order affects businesses in the watch case manufacturing industry.

6535.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the commercial refrigerator industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings on the code.

6534.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the paper distributing trade. It applies to people and businesses in that trade and accepts the Administrator’s report and findings.

6530.s:
This order approves a code of fair competition for the medium and low priced jewelry manufacturing industry. It applies to businesses and employees in that industry.

It also delays one provision that requires time and one third pay for hours over 40 a week until March 1, 1934. After that date, the provision takes effect.
