6529.s: This order approves changes to the Code of Fair Competition for the Textile Bag Industry. It affects the textile bag industry and makes the approved changes part of that code.

6528.s: This order revokes part of an earlier withdrawal of public lands in two Wyoming townships. It opens those lands first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws for 91 days after the resurvey plats are filed, subject to valid rights and existing withdrawals. After that, the lands are open to the general public under the public-land laws that apply.

6527-A.s: This order approves changes to the Code of Fair Competition for the Petroleum Industry. It sets hour limits for clerical workers and other employees in drilling, production, refinery, and pipe line operations, and it applies rules to drilling contractors. It also lists several drilling practices as unfair, including secret agreements, rebates, certain bidding methods, payment in anything other than cash or check, and contracts below fair economic cost. The order also requires subcommittees to represent the drilling branch of the industry, with equal representation for drilling contractors or their groups.

6527.s: This order sets up an official bulletin board for the National Recovery Administration in the Department of Commerce building in Washington, D.C. The public must be allowed free access during business hours. Notices of hearings and other proceedings under the National Industrial Recovery Act must be posted there, and that posting counts as notice to interested parties when other notice has not been given.

6526.s: This order denies the Southern Plow Manufacturers Association’s request for an exemption from the minimum wage rules in the Code of Fair Competition for the Farm Equipment Industry. It also changes one part of the Code so that the words “members of the Association” are replaced with “employers who have agreed to the Code.” The order says the wording was too restrictive and was changed to allow more complete sharing of statistics.

6525.s: This order approves changes to the Code of Fair Competition for the Gasoline Pump Manufacturing Industry. The approved changes become part of that code and apply to the businesses covered by it.

6524.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the rubber tire manufacturing industry. It also lets the President cancel or change the approval if needed to prevent unfair trade practices in that industry. The Administrator is directed to investigate possible unfair trade practices and use the Federal Trade Commission to help handle complaints.

6523.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the industry that smelts and refines secondary metals into brass and bronze alloys in ingot form. It adopts the Administrator’s findings and recommendations and makes the code effective for that industry.

6522.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the rayon and silk dyeing and printing industry. It takes effect in place of the earlier Code of Labor Provisions for that industry.

6521.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Rolling Steel Door Industry. It applies to the rolling steel door industry and adopts the Administrator’s findings and recommendations under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6520.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Grinding Wheel Industry. It applies to the grinding wheel industry and follows an application, hearings, and a report by the Administrator.

6519.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for savings, building and loan associations. It affects those associations by putting the approved code into effect under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6518.s: This order waives a rule that generally barred federal officers and employees from holding state or city offices, for Martin Conboy. It lets him serve as United States attorney for the southern district of New York and also as a special assistant attorney general of New York for the matters named in the order.

6517.s: This order extends an earlier order to include employees in the field service of executive departments and independent establishments of the Government, including the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations. It affects those federal employees in the District of Columbia who were not included before.

6516.s: This order closed several executive departments and independent government establishments in the District of Columbia on December 23 and December 30, 1933. It also excused Federal employees in the District of Columbia from duty on those days, except for workers who were needed for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law. The order covered the Government Printing Office, the Navy Yard, and stations.

6515-A.s: This order authorizes Charles E. Wyzanski, Jr., the Solicitor of Labor, to perform the duties of Secretary of Labor. He may do so only when the Secretary of Labor and the Assistant Secretary of Labor are absent.

6515.s: This order extends the President’s Reemployment Agreement for employers from January 1, 1934, to April 30, 1934, or until an approved code of fair competition applies. Employers who already signed can accept the extension by displaying the Blue Eagle, and employers who have not signed can accept it by signing the agreement. It also says earlier substitutions, exemptions, and exceptions still apply, and it authorizes the Administrator for Industrial Recovery to make needed rules and regulations.

6514.s: This order creates a Delaware corporation called Electric Home and Farm Authority, Inc. It gives the corporation a three-member board made up of Tennessee Valley Authority officials and sets aside $1,000,000 to buy its stock for the United States. The board may hire officers and employees without following civil service laws and may use government, State, and local services with consent.

6513-C.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the waxed paper industry. It follows an application, hearings, and a report from the Administrator finding the code complies with the law. The order affects the waxed paper industry.

6513-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Set Up Paper Box Industry. It applies to that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings. It says the code complies with the requirements of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6513-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Knitted Outerwear Industry under the National Industrial Recovery Act. It also gives manufacturers of knitted outerwear for infants and children up to age fifteen a stay from the code until the Administrator decides whether they will be included.

6513.s: This order adds all members of the Special Industrial Recovery Board to the National Emergency Council, including the Attorney General, the Director of the Bureau of the Budget, and the Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission. It says the Council will carry out the Board’s functions and duties. This affects the members of that Board and the National Emergency Council.

6513-D.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the domestic freight forwarding industry. It applies to the businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s findings and recommendations about the code.

6513-E.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the wholesale automotive trade. It follows an application and hearings under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The code applies to businesses in the wholesale automotive trade.

6513-F.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Non-Ferrous Foundry Industry. It applies to that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about the code.

6513-H.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the fur dressing and fur dyeing industry. It applies to that industry and follows an application and hearings under the National Industrial Recovery Act. The order says the code meets the law’s requirements and is approved.

6513-J.s: This order changes the fair competition codes for the men's clothing industry and the cotton garment industry. It changes which clothing items are covered and sets new minimum wages for certain workers, including workers on single pants, men's wash suits, and men's summer clothing. It also creates an inter-code committee to oversee cotton wash suits and single pants and to handle questions about the order.

6513-I.s: This order approves Amendment Number I to the Code of Fair Competition for the Cast Iron Soil Pipe Industry. It affects businesses and workers in that industry by changing the code they follow under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6513-K.s: This order approves an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Automobile Manufacturing Industry. It changes the code’s expiration date to September 4, 1934, unless the President or Congress ends the emergency earlier. It applies to the automobile manufacturing industry under that code.

6513-G.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Refractories Industry. It follows an application, hearings, and a report from the Administrator finding that the code met the required provisions of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6512-A.s: This order appoints Charles Brenton Barnes as the wholly impartial and disinterested Presidential member of the Bituminous Coal Labor Board for Division I, South. The board’s headquarters is in Cincinnati, Ohio.

6511.s: The order keeps the National Labor Board in place and gives it more power to handle industrial disputes and conflicts that threaten industrial peace. It lets the board settle controversies between employers and employees through mediation, conciliation, or arbitration. The board can also create local or regional boards with equal employer and employee representation, review their decisions when the public interest requires it, and make its own rules and procedures.

6510-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Fur Trapping Contractors Industry. It applies to people and businesses in that industry and makes the approved code official.

6510.s: This order changes the Code of Fair Competition for the Men's Clothing Industry. It allows employers to hire learners to replace home-workers for a limited time, sets rules for posting parts of the code, and sets delivery dates for top coats. It also allows some workers with physical or mental handicaps to be paid below the minimum wage under set limits and reporting rules.

6509.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the dry and polishing mop manufacturing industry. It applies to people and businesses in that industry.

6512.s: This order delays the abolition of the volunteer field agencies that were set to end under Executive Order No. 6433-A. It changes the effective date for ending those agencies to January 16, 1934.

6507.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the hair cloth manufacturing industry. It affects the hair cloth manufacturing industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6508.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Stone Finishing Machinery and Equipment Industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report and recommendations.

6505.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the oxy-acetylene industry. It also removes Section 4 of Article VIII from that code. The order affects businesses in the oxy-acetylene industry.

6506.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Rubber Manufacturing Industry. It affects the rubber manufacturing industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about that code.

6504.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Metal Tank Industry. It follows an application, hearings, and a report by the Administrator that said the code met the rules of the National Industrial Recovery Act. It affects businesses in the metal tank industry.

6503.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Valve and Fittings Manufacturing Industry. It says the filed effective price lists must be open to inspection by the trade factors concerned. It affects people and businesses in that industry.

6502.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Can Manufacturers Industry. It also adds rules for territories and possessions and requires certain statistical information to be submitted to government agencies when the Administrator deems it necessary.

6501.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the millinery industry. The code is in effect only until May 15, 1934, and the Code Authority must make recommendations before then about keeping it or changing it. The Administrator is to appoint a special board to decide whether pay scales for a particular area, market, or industry member should be stayed or changed because of great and unusual hardship. It also provides a way for people facing undue hardship to seek relief.

6500.s: This order revokes part of a 1930 order that had set aside land in Arizona for customs and immigration inspection purposes at the international boundary line. The revoked part covers 2.87 acres west of the center line of the Ajo-Sonoyta Highway. The rest of the land, 5.84 acres, remains withdrawn for those inspection purposes.

6499.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The lands are withdrawn while a resurvey of the township is pending. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6498.s: This order extends the trust period on Indian lands, whether tribal or individual, if that trust would expire during 1934. The extension lasts 10 years from the date the trust would otherwise end, except where Congress has specifically kept the power to extend the trust itself.

6497.s: This order changes Executive Order No. 6247 by adding a new paragraph. It says that order does not apply to orders the President may issue approving codes of fair competition under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6496.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it, while the township is resurveyed.

6495.s: This order sets rules for furloughs without pay when a department or office has more officers and employees than it needs. It allows rotative furloughs of 90 days or less for affected employees, and it says furloughs over 90 days must follow other civil service rules. The rules do not apply to carriers in the Rural Mail Delivery Service, and the President may suspend or reduce their equipment and maintenance allowance for fiscal year 1934.

6494.s: This order exempts Charles J. Chamberlain from a law that would require automatic separation from civilian service when he reaches the retirement age. It lets him stay in service as head carpenter for the Senate Office Building until December 31, 1935.

6492.s: This order revokes part of two earlier executive orders that had created coal land withdrawals in New Mexico. It applies to the specific lands listed in the order.

6493.s: This order restores two parcels of land in Honolulu, Oahu, from Navy use to the Territory of Hawaii. The land is to be used for widening and improving parts of Kalanianaole Highway. The parcels were previously transferred to the United States for the use of the Navy.

6491.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Montana from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The lands are set aside in connection with the Fort Peck Dam and Reservoir project. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6489.s: The order amends the civil-service rules by adding a new paragraph to Schedule A, subdivision XIII. It adds six district commissioners of immigration and naturalization to that schedule.

6488.s: This order amends the civil-service rules by adding one Director of Information position and one Administrative Assistant position in the Office of the Secretary. It affects those two positions in that office.

6487-A.s: The order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the alcoholic beverage wholesale industry. It says the Secretary of Agriculture submitted the code, and that notice and hearings were given to interested parties. The order applies to the alcoholic beverage wholesale industry.

6487.s: This order amends the Code of Fair Competition for the Lumber and Timber Products Industries. It also establishes a Broom and Mop Handle Division. It affects the lumber and timber products industries and the new division covered by the amendments.

6485.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Machined Waste Manufacturing Industry. It applies to that industry and confirms the Administrator’s report and findings under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6486.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Asphalt and Mastic Tile Industry. It follows an application, hearings, and a report from the Administrator, and it applies to that industry.

6484.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the pyrotechnic manufacturing industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and puts the approved code into effect.

6483.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the motor vehicle storage and parking trade. It follows an application, hearings, and a report from the Administrator finding the code met the required provisions. It applies to businesses in that trade.

6482.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Excelsior and Excelsior Products Industry. It applies to the businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings. The order says the code meets the requirements of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6481.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Furniture Manufacturing Industry. It applies to the furniture manufacturing industry and adopts the Administrator’s findings and recommendations.

6480.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Paper Making Machine Builders Industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about the code.

6479.s: This order changes approved and future codes of fair competition, agreements, and licenses to require people subject to them to provide statistical information the Administrator may need. The information must be given to Federal and State agencies the Administrator chooses. It also says nothing in a code, agreement, or license removes any existing duty to file reports with government agencies.

6487-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry. It says notice was given and hearings were held before approval. The code applies to businesses in that industry.

6477.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in South Dakota for classification. It says the land will stay withdrawn while the government decides whether to include it in a national monument, and it is subject to valid existing rights.

6478.s: This order revokes part of a 1930 withdrawal of certain public lands in New Mexico, except for land already set aside as White Sands National Monument. It opens the surveyed lands in the released areas first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead and desert-land laws for a limited period, and then to the general public under other public-land laws. It also says no one may gain rights to these lands by settlement before entry except as allowed by the order.

6476.s: This order denies an exemption from part of the Cotton Textile Industry Code for limits on the use of productive machinery used to make tire yarns or fabrics for rubber tires. It ends the stay on those limits, and the code’s rules on that issue go back into full effect for the affected persons.

6475.s: This order allows Miss Anne Stevens to be appointed to a clerical job in the office of the United States attorney in Boston, Massachusetts, without following the civil-service rules. It concerns Miss Stevens and that office.

6473-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Brewing Industry. It says an application was made, hearings were held, and interested parties were given notice and a chance to be heard. It affects the brewing industry.

6474.s: This order establishes the Federal Alcohol Control Administration to help carry out the policy of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The Administration is made up of five officers, and it may investigate and study the taxation, control, and regulation of alcohol and alcoholic beverages. It may also use services from other government agencies to carry out its work. For this order, $500,000 is allocated for the Administration, including the Director's salary.

6473.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal applies to the listed townships and lasts while they are being resurveyed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6472.s: This order assigns radio frequencies to Government radio stations and certain classes of stations. It lists several Army, Navy, and Commerce stations that may use specific frequencies, and it names some independent receiving stations that have no transmitters. It also sets rules for when Government stations may use other frequencies, when mobile stations may use mobile-service frequencies, and when a non-Government mobile station may operate on a Government frequency if directed to do so.

6471-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the alcoholic beverages importing industry. It says the code was reviewed, hearings were held, and the code complies with the National Industrial Recovery Act. It affects businesses in that industry.

6471.s: This order allows Miss Maude McGaugh to be appointed to a position in the classified service without following the civil-service rules. It applies to that appointment and is recommended by the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs.

6470.s: This order designates and establishes the Public Works Emergency Housing Corporation as an agency under Title II of the National Industrial Recovery Act. It authorizes the corporation to help construct or finance public works projects, and to buy or take property by eminent domain for those projects. It also lets the corporation sell, lease, or otherwise handle property and securities connected to the projects.

6469.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of public lands in one township in Wyoming. It opens those lands first only to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws for 91 days after the resurvey plat is filed. After that, the lands may be available to the general public under any applicable public-land law.

6468.s: This order restores part of the Fort Ruger Military Reservation to the Territory of Hawaii for use as a water-reservoir site and related purposes. It keeps a 25-foot right-of-way for a pipe line and roadway for the United States. If the land is not used for that purpose within 1 year, or if the Governor of Hawaii says the Territory does not want it, it goes back under the War Department's control.

6467-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the radio broadcasting industry. It says the code was reviewed and found to meet the requirements of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The order applies to the radio broadcasting industry.

6467.s: This order delays the effective date of article IX, section 4 of the Code of Fair Competition for the Retail Trade until July 1, 1934. It applies to parties affected by the code and gives manufacturers of coupons and other forms of scrip more time to adjust their business. It also says the delay is meant to avoid a reduction of employment among those manufacturers.

6466.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the waterproofing, dampproofing, calking compounds, and concrete floor treatments manufacturing industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s findings and recommendations.

6465.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Structural Clay Products Industry. It applies to that industry and sets its rules under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6464.s: This order interprets commercial bribery rules in approved industry codes. It says no member of an industry may give or offer anything of value to influence or reward an employee, agent, or representative of another without the knowledge of the employer, principal, or party. It also says free and general distribution of common advertising items is allowed unless they are actually used for commercial bribery, and future codes with these rules must follow this interpretation.

6463.s: This order extends a stay on the cotton textile code rules that limit machine hours for making tire yarns or fabrics for rubber tires. The stay will remain in place until the hearings are finished and a decision is made on those issues. It affects parties covered by those provisions in the cotton textile industry.

6462.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the gas appliances and apparatus industry. It applies to the businesses and workers in that industry and puts the approved code into effect.

6461.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Malleable Iron Industry. It applies to businesses in that industry. The order says the code was found to meet the needed legal requirements under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6460.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the wool felt manufacturing industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and puts the approved code into effect.

6459.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the upholstery and drapery textile industry. Certain manufacturers who were already operating under a code of fair competition as of August 15 may choose not to be bound by most parts of this code, except article IX, if they file written notice by the stated deadline. It also stays part of article III, section 4, for 14 days for looms making pile fabrics used only for automobile upholstery.

6458.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Motion Picture Industry. It gives the Administrator power to review or disapprove acts by the code authority and to remove or add members in some cases. It also suspends some parts of the code, including provisions about executive pay and certain rules for writers, authors, dramatists, and other employees in artistic, technical, supervisory, or executive work.

6457.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the chinaware and porcelain manufacturing industry. It applies to that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about the code.

6456.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for investment bankers. It affects investment bankers and sets out the code that applies to them. The order says the code was found to comply with the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6455.s: This executive order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Reinforcing Materials Fabricating Industry. It applies to that industry and sets rules for its board of directors. The order also says the Administrator may review, disapprove, or modify actions taken by the board of directors.

6454.s: This order approves a code of fair competition for the warm air furnace manufacturing industry. It applies to businesses in that industry. It also adopts the Administrator’s findings and recommendations about the code.

6452.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Cigar Container Manufacturers Code. It applies to cigar container manufacturers and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6451.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the concrete masonry industry. It applies to the concrete masonry industry and follows an application and hearings under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6453.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the cement industry. It affects the cement industry and says the code meets the listed requirements of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6450.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the precious jewelry producing industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and sets rules under the National Industrial Recovery Act. One provision for manufacturers and distributors of jewelry for schools, colleges, fraternities, and other educational institutions is delayed for 90 days after the code takes effect.

6448.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the machine tool and equipment distributing trade. It applies to people and businesses in that trade and adopts the Administrator’s report and findings.

6449.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the retail jewelry trade. It follows an application, hearings, and a report from the Administrator finding that the code met the requirements of the law. It affects businesses in the retail jewelry trade.

6446.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the anti-friction bearing industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6445.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the vitrified clay sewer pipe manufacturing industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6447.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Pipe Nipple Manufacturing Industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and puts the approved code into effect.

6444-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry. It says the code was submitted under the National Industrial Recovery Act and that hearings were held for interested parties. The order affects the distilled spirits industry.

6444.s: This order restores certain drill sites in California to Naval Petroleum Reserve No. 2 and puts them under the exclusive control and jurisdiction of the Navy Department. It applies to drill sites 1 to 28 in the original town site of Ford and drill sites 1 to 10 in the addition to that town site. The order also says the county of Kern keeps the rights given by the 1926 act for drill sites 9, 10, 17, and 18, and it revokes two earlier executive orders for these drill sites.

6442.s: This order lets the Federal Emergency Relief Administrator take over relief administration in any state if he thinks it will improve cooperation between state and federal authorities. It also lets him create a state emergency relief administration and advisory committees in those states. The state relief administration would handle the distribution and spending of funds, hire personnel, and set local relief groups, all under the Administrator's direction.

6443.s: This order lets the Administrator for Industrial Recovery change certain agreements made under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The Administrator may also grant exceptions or exemptions in particular cases after investigation if needed to avoid undue hardship. It does not apply to changes in codes of fair competition approved under that law.

6441-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Southern Rice Milling Industry. It says the application was made, notice was given, and hearings were held for interested parties. The order applies to the Southern Rice Milling Industry under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6441.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are set aside for classification and to aid legislation. It says valid existing rights are still protected, and the withdrawal stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

6440.s: This order sets a salary schedule for employees in several emergency agencies that can set pay without using the Classification Act of 1923. It applies to officers and employees now in service and those hired later, and it ties pay to the duties and responsibilities of their jobs. It also allows some salaries to be reduced to match the schedule, with limited exceptions for certain employees.

6439.s: This order gives the Administrator for Industrial Recovery authority to make a seal for the National Recovery Administration and to set more rules needed to carry out the order. It says certified copies of National Recovery Administration books, records, papers, and documents, as well as approved codes, agreements, orders, rules, or regulations, can be used in evidence like the originals. It also lets the Administrator, or someone he designates, certify copies when needed.

6438-A.s: This order allows the named people to be appointed to positions in the Bureau of Internal Revenue in the Treasury Department. Their appointments can be made without following the civil-service rules.

6438.s: This order approves a code of fair competition for the hotel industry under the National Industrial Recovery Act. It removes one subsection from the code and directs the Administrator to hold another hearing within 90 days to review the minimum wages set in the code. The order affects the hotel industry and the people covered by that code.

6437.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Paper and Pulp Industry. It also sets a condition that, within 90 days, the Administrator must hold another hearing to look at whether the minimum wages in the code are adequate. The order affects the paper and pulp industry and the Administrator handling the code.

6436.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Special Tool, Die, and Machine Shop Industry. It applies to businesses in that industry. The order says the code was found to meet the requirements of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6435.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the newsprint industry. It also directs the Administrator to hold another hearing within 90 days to review whether the minimum wages in the code are adequate. The order says the minimum wage for the industry should be at least 40 cents an hour.

6434.s: This executive order approves a code of fair competition for the cotton garment industry. It also sets conditions for prison labor, including limits on hours, prices, payments, and machinery use for prison-made products. The order stays one part of the code for members of the industry in Kentucky and in certain counties in Illinois and Indiana that border the Ohio River for a limited time while the Administrator studies their classification.

6433-A.s: This order creates the National Emergency Council to coordinate and make more efficient the work of government field agencies set up under certain emergency laws. The Council is headed by an Executive Director appointed by the President, and its members serve in an advisory role without compensation. It also abolishes all volunteer field agencies established under those laws, and their needed functions will be taken over by the Council.

6433.s: This order allows Mrs. Josephine B. Wales to be appointed to a classified civil service job without following the usual civil-service rules. It applies to her appointment in the civil service.

6432.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in two Wyoming townships from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while those townships are resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6431-B.s: This order approves the Labor Provisions for the Wholesale Food and Grocery Trade. It applies to people and businesses in that trade and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6431-A.s: This order approves labor provisions for the retail food and grocery trade. It applies to that trade and confirms the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6431.s: This executive order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Mop Stick Industry. It applies to the mop stick industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6429.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the limestone industry. It adopts the Administrator’s report and findings and makes the code effective. It affects businesses in the limestone industry.

6430.s: This order approves a code of fair competition for the all-metal insect screen industry. It applies to people and businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s findings and recommendations under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6428.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Wood Plug Industry. It applies to businesses and workers in that industry. It says the code met the requirements of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6427.s: This executive order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Gear Manufacturing Industry. It applies to the gear manufacturing industry and follows a report and findings from the Administrator under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6426.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Air Transport Industry. It applies to the air transport industry and adopts the Administrator’s findings and recommendations about that code.

6425.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Scientific Apparatus Industry. It applies to businesses and other people covered by that code under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6423-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Imported Date Packing Industry. It says the code was submitted by the Secretary of Agriculture and the National Recovery Administrator, and that hearings were held for interested parties. The order affects the imported date packing industry.

6424.s: This order changes the end date of a stay on limits for machine hours in the Cotton Textile Industry code. The stay applies to the production of tire yarns or fabrics for rubber tires. It extends the end date of that stay from November 13, 1933, to November 20, 1933.

6422.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Hardwood Distillation Industry. It applies to the hardwood distillation industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about the code.

6423.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the crushed stone, sand and gravel, and slag industries. It affects businesses in those industries by putting that code into effect.

6421.s: This order revokes part of an earlier coal-land withdrawal in New Mexico. It affects the listed townships and lands outside grants in the New Mexico Meridian, including some unsurveyed areas and some partial surveys.

6420-B.s: This order establishes a Federal Civil Works Administration to run a public works program called the "civil works program." It gives the Administrator authority to construct or finance public works projects, buy or lease property for them, and appoint officers and employees. It also allocates $400,000,000 to the agency and allows the use of state and local officers and employees with the consent of the state or municipality concerned.

6420-A.s: This order approves modifications to the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Textile Industry. It affects the cotton textile industry and makes the approved changes part of that code.

6419.s: This order exempts James A. Wetmore from a rule that would require civilian government workers to leave service when they reach the retirement age for automatic separation. It lets him stay in service until November 30, 1934.

6418.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the automotive parts and equipment manufacturing industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6417.s: This order approves a supplement to the Code of Fair Competition for the automobile manufacturing industry. It covers fair trade practices for the funeral vehicle and ambulance subdivision and applies to businesses in that part of the industry.

6416-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the cleaning and dyeing trade. It affects businesses in that trade by putting the approved code into effect under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6416.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Machine Tool and Forging Machinery Industry. It also says the Administrator may review and disapprove or modify actions taken by the supervisory agency under article VI. The order affects the machine tool and forging machinery industry.

6415.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Liquefied Gas Industry. It applies to the liquefied gas industry and confirms the Administrator’s findings and recommendations.

6414.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the paperboard industry. It says an application was made, hearings were held, and the Administrator found the code met the needed requirements. It affects businesses in the paperboard industry.

6413.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the shovel, dragline, and crane industry. It applies to that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report and recommendations.

6412.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Ladder Manufacturing Industry. It applies to the ladder manufacturing industry and adopts the Administrator’s findings and recommendations for that code.

6411.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Motor Fire Apparatus Manufacturing Industry. It follows an application, hearings, and a report from the Administrator finding the code met the law’s requirements. The order affects businesses in that industry.

6410.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Printers' Rollers Industry. It applies to people and businesses in that industry and follows the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6409.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Wasatch National Forest to the Ashley National Forest. It also transfers other lands from the Ashley National Forest to the Wasatch National Forest. The lands are in Utah and Wyoming, and the order says it does not give national-forest status to land that did not already have it or remove that status from any land.

6408.s: This order corrects the boundary description of the Fort Ruger Military Reservation in Hawaii. It gives a new legal description for six tracts within the reservation and lists the land, road, lighthouse, and other boundary points that the description uses. The order affects the military reservation and nearby public lands and rights-of-way named in the boundary lines.

6420.s: This order allows Mrs. Mary M. Flanagan to be appointed as a charwoman in the custodial service of the Post Office Department at the Post Office Building in Boston, Massachusetts. It says she may be appointed without following the civil service rules.

6407.s: This order denies an exemption from the machine-hour rule for machinery used to make tire yarns or fabrics for rubber tires. It ends the stay of that rule beginning November 13, 1933. After that, no further exemption or exception can be made except as approved under the process named in the order.

6406.s: The order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Asphalt Shingle and Roofing Manufacturing Industry. It follows an application, hearings, and a report from the Administrator finding that the code meets the requirements of the law. It affects people and businesses in that industry.

6405.s: This order revokes part of a 1911 executive order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 191. It removes the reserve status from the listed lands in Utah. The change applies only to the specific tracts named in the order.

6403-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the fire extinguishing appliance manufacturing industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and sets their code under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6403.s: This order denies an exemption request from the Kaplan Brothers from the Code of Fair Competition for the Artificial Flower and Feather Industry. The request was heard by the Administrator, and the President said no case of injustice and extreme hardship was shown. It affects the named applicants and the code that had already been approved for that industry.

6402.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the leather and woolen knit glove industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and sets the code under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6401.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the washing and ironing machine manufacturing industry. It applies to people and businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6400.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Floor and Wall Clay Tile Manufacturing Industry. It affects businesses in that industry by making the code official under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6399.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the piano manufacturing industry. It applies to that industry and follows an application, hearings, and a report by the Administrator.

6398.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Buff and Polishing Wheel Industry. It also requires that section (n) of article VII be removed. The order affects businesses in that industry.

6397.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Buffing and Polishing Composition Industry. It applies to that industry and follows an application, hearings, and a report from the Administrator.

6396.s: This order approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Office Equipment Manufacturers Industry. It applies to office equipment manufacturers and adopts the Administrator’s findings and recommendations.

6395.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the business furniture, storage equipment, and filing supply industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and follows an application, hearings, and a report by the Administrator.

6394.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Funeral Supply Industry. It affects the funeral supply industry by putting that code into effect under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6392.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for stock exchange firms. It applies to stock exchange firms under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6393.s: This order approves a code of fair competition for the Toy and Playthings Industry. It applies to businesses and employees in that industry. One part of the code, about paying time and one-third for hours over forty a week, is delayed until January 1, 1934.

6391.s: This order approves a code of fair competition for the men's garter, suspender, and belt manufacturing industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and sets the rules they must follow under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6390.s: This order transfers supervision of the District Court of the United States for the Panama Canal Zone from the War Department to the Department of Justice. The court and its personnel will keep the perquisites, privileges, and allowances they already receive, and the War Department will keep providing office, library, and travel facilities in the Canal Zone. The marshal for the Panama Canal Zone must disburse the funds needed for the court’s maintenance and operation and give bond for that duty.

6389.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Soap and Glycerine Manufacturing Industry. It applies to that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings on the code.

6388.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the fabricated metal products manufacturing and metal finishing and metal coating industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and sets out a code that was found to meet the law’s requirements.

6387.s: This order approves a "Code of Fair Competition" for the Copper and Brass Mill Products Industry. It follows an application, hearings, and the Administrator’s report and findings under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6386.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Steel Casting Industry. It applies to the steel casting industry and follows an application, hearings, and a report by the Administrator.

6384.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Crown Manufacturing Industry. It applies to the crown manufacturing industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about that code.

6385.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the American Petroleum Equipment Industry and Trade. It says an application was made, hearings were held, and the Administrator found the code met the required parts of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The order adopts the Administrator’s report and recommendations and makes the code approved.

6382.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the rock crusher manufacturing industry. It applies to that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings on the code.

6381.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Asbestos Industry. It applies to the asbestos industry and follows an application, hearings, and a review by the Administrator.

6383.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the novelty curtain, drapery, bedspread, and novelty pillow industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings. It says the code meets the requirements of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6380.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Nottingham Lace Curtain Industry. It applies to that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about the code.

6379.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the paint, varnish, and lacquer manufacturing industry. It applies to that industry and follows an application, hearings, and a report from the Administrator finding that the code meets the law’s requirements.

6378.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Canning and Packing Machinery Industry. It applies to that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6377.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Terra Cotta Industry. It applies to people and businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report and findings.

6376.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Hair and Jute Felt Industry. It applies to that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about the code.

6374.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the packaging machinery industry and trade. It applies to the businesses covered by that industry and trade.

6375.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the road machinery manufacturing industry. It applies to that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6373.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the motor bus industry. It applies to the motor bus industry and follows an application, hearings, and a report from the Administrator.

6372.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the millinery and dress trimming, braid and textile industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and approves the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6371.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Gas Cock Industry under the National Industrial Recovery Act. It affects people and businesses in that industry by putting the approved code in place.

6370.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the fertilizer industry. It applies to the fertilizer industry and follows an application, hearings, and a report by the Administrator.

6368.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Advertising Specialty Industry. It says that for employees in printing operations, the wage and hour rules in this code will be replaced by the wage and hour rules in the Printing Industry code when that code takes effect. It also creates an advertising specialty industry committee to work with the Administrator on planning and fair practice for the industry.

6369.s: This order approves a code of fair competition for the dress manufacturing industry. It stays part of the wage scale rules for the western area, except for the metropolitan areas of Chicago and Cleveland, until more hearings and a final decision. It also stays the code’s application to certain cotton dresses sold as house dresses or wash dresses, pending more hearings and a final decision.

6367.s: This order revokes part of the 1913 order that created public water reserve no. 12 for the listed lands in Wyoming. The lands named in the order will not be open to disposal under public land laws until a later date and after notice is announced.

6366.s: This order approves the labor provisions for the beet sugar industry under the National Industrial Recovery Act. It says these provisions are to be in effect during the coming season's operations of the industry.

6365.s: This order abolishes Greenwich, Middletown, Norwalk, South Manchester, and Stamford, Connecticut, as customs ports of entry. It affects customs collection district no. 6 in Connecticut, with headquarters at Bridgeport, Connecticut.

6364.s: This order allows Mrs. Jean Springstead Whittemore to be appointed as collector of customs for Puerto Rico without following the civil-service rules. It affects that appointment and the customs position in Puerto Rico.

6363.s: This order revokes parts of earlier coal-land withdrawals in New Mexico for the lands listed in the order. It affects many specific public land sections and townships, including some areas outside named grants and outside the Navajo Indian Reservation. The listed lands are no longer covered by those coal-land withdrawals.

6362.s: This order revokes part of a prior order that had withdrawn certain public lands in New Mexico. It opens those lands, subject to existing valid rights, only to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws for 91 days starting 63 days after the order. After that, the lands are open to the general public under the public-land laws that apply. No rights can be gained by settlement before entry except as allowed by this order.

6360.s: This order allows Mr. Wade Crawford to be appointed as superintendent of the Klamath Indian Agency in Oregon without following the Civil Service rules. It affects that appointment and the Interior Department process for it.

6361.s: This order temporarily withdraws about 1,136,000 acres of surveyed and unsurveyed public lands in California for classification. It says the lands will be reviewed to decide whether to include them in a national monument. The withdrawal is subject to valid existing rights and existing withdrawals, including those connected to the Colorado River storage project.

6359.s: This order revokes an earlier order about the sale and export of gold recovered from natural deposits, while allowing the Secretary of the Treasury to handle gold received on consignment before this order. It authorizes U.S. mints and assay offices to receive such gold, and lets the Reconstruction Finance Corporation acquire it and hold, earmark for foreign account, export, or otherwise dispose of it. It also changes an earlier order to permit the export of articles made from gold, subject to Treasury regulations.

6358.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Steel Tubular and Firebox Boiler Industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s findings and recommendations under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6357.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Plumbago Crucible Industry. It applies to the industry covered by that code and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6356.s: This executive order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Industrial Supplies and Machinery Distributors' Trade. It applies to businesses in that trade and approves the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6354.s: This order changes earlier rules under the National Industrial Recovery Act and makes some small local retail and service employers exempt from the President’s reemployment agreement and related fair competition code obligations, unless they choose to keep complying. It applies to employers that work only locally, do not affect interstate commerce, employ no more than five people, and are in small towns outside the immediate trade area of a larger city. It also directs the Administrator for Industrial Recovery to investigate price increases and handle complaints about price increases from manufacturers, producers, and retailers.

6355.s: This order says provisions in approved or future codes, agreements, or licenses under the National Industrial Recovery Act cannot be used to stop bona fide and legitimate cooperative organizations from paying patronage dividends to members. It applies to cooperatives, including farmers' cooperatives, that are organized under the laws of a State, Territory, the District of Columbia, or the United States. The dividends must come from actual earnings and cannot be paid at the time of purchase.

6353.s: This order sets out how complaints and investigations under section 3(e) of the National Industrial Recovery Act will be handled. The Administrator may make preliminary investigations, receive complaints, and ask for sworn or unsworn information from interested parties. If the matter goes forward, the United States Tariff Commission must investigate, hold any required hearings, and send its findings and recommendations to the President and the Administrator.

6352.s: This order changes the civil-service rules for the Post Office Department by replacing “1933” with “1934.” It keeps temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers in the Postal Service excepted from examination for part-time or intermittent work tied to the holiday or seasonal business until February 1, 1934.

6351.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the retail trade. It applies to the retail trade and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6350.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the cap and closure industry. It applies to the businesses in that industry and follows hearings and a report by the Administrator under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6349.s: This order approves a code of fair competition for the Marking Devices Industry. It also creates a Marking Devices Industry Code Authority to work with the Administrator as a planning and fair practice agency. The committee includes eleven industry representatives chosen by a fair method approved by the Administrator and three nonvoting members appointed by the Administrator.

6347.s: This order gives an additional stay of part I, section 1(c) of the Code of Fair Competition for the Underwear and Allied Products Manufacturing Industry. It affects manufacturers covered by that section while the Administrator decides the issues about whether they should be included under it.

6348.s: This order changes an agreement for the cordage and twine industry. It requires employers to raise pay for hourly and piece-rate workers, and for workers paid by the day, week, or month who now get less than $35 a week, to at least 90% of the rates paid in June 1929 for the same work, unless the code sets a higher minimum. The rest of the agreement stays in effect until a permanent code is approved.

6345.s: This order amends earlier orders that gave the Secretary of Agriculture certain authority under the National Industrial Recovery Act. It adds more trades and industries, including those handling certain agricultural commodities, food and food ingredients, nonfood grain products, inedible oils and fats, naval stores, feathers, hides, furs, brooms, hog-cholera serum, and those crushing cotton seed or flax seed. If there is a dispute about whether a trade or industry is covered, the Secretary of Agriculture and the National Recovery Administrator decide it, or the President decides if they do not agree.

6344.s: This order allocates $386,000 from a larger appropriation and transfers it to the Department of Agriculture. The money is for buying land for forest research in connection with the National Arboretum, including costs related to the purchase. It also revokes Executive Order No. 6223.

6343.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to buy or take real or personal property by eminent domain. The property must be used for construction of projects under allocations made to the Department of the Interior under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6342.s: This order allows tax returns to be inspected by the Special Committee to Investigate Receivership and Bankruptcy Proceedings and Appointment of Receivers and Trustees. The inspection must follow Treasury rules and regulations approved by the President. It applies to the committee named in Senate Resolution 78.

6341.s: This order extends the trust period on lands held in trust for the use and benefit of the Morongo Band of Mission Indians in California. It adds 10 years to the trust period after it was set to expire on December 13, 1933.

6340.s: This order creates a Delaware corporation called the Commodity Credit Corporation. It is meant to help carry out several laws dealing with the emergency, including laws on agriculture, relief, and credit. The Secretary of Agriculture and the Governor of the Farm Credit Administration are directed to form the corporation and subscribe to all of its stock for the United States.

6339.s: This order abolishes Michigan City, Indiana, as a customs port of entry in customs collection district no. 39, which is headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. The change takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

6337.s: This order sets rules under the National Industrial Recovery Act. It bars anyone from falsely saying they are following the President’s Reemployment Agreement or an approved code of fair competition, and it bars misuse of National Recovery Administration emblems or insignia. It also lets the Administrator for Industrial Recovery make more rules, take other steps to carry them out, and appoint personnel. Anyone who breaks these rules may be fined, jailed, or both.

6338.s: This executive order exempts James S. Goldsmith and George G. Hedgcock from a rule that would require automatic separation from service at the retirement age. It allows them to stay in service until October 31, 1934.

6336.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Snoqualmie National Forest to the Mount Baker National Forest. It describes the lands by township, range, and boundary lines. It also says the order is not meant to give forest status to any lands that did not already have it, or to remove any lands from forest status.

6335.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Rainier National Forest to the Wenatchee National Forest in Washington. It applies to lands north and east of a described line in the Rainier National Forest. The order says it does not give any lands national-forest status that they did not already have, and it does not remove any lands from national-forest status.

6334.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Rainier National Forest to the Snoqualmie National Forest. It also eliminates some lands from the Rainier National Forest, and some lands described in the order are transferred to the Wenatchee National Forest by a separate order. The order says it does not give national-forest status to lands that did not already have it, except for the lands described as being eliminated from Rainier.

6333.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Rainier National Forest to the Columbia National Forest in Washington. It says the transfer does not give any lands a national-forest status they did not already have, and does not remove any lands from national-forest status.

6331-C.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Heat Exchange Industry. It applies to the heat exchange industry and puts the approved code into effect.

6332.s: This order sets the amount paid to carriers in the Rural Mail Delivery Service for equipment maintenance. It fixes different pay rates for October 1933, for November 1, 1933, through February 28, 1934, and for March 1934. It affects rural mail carriers whose pay is based on miles scheduled.

6331-A.s: This order denies an exemption request from the minimum wage rule in the Coat and Suit Code. It applies to the named applicants, who said the code was unjust to them. The order says no case of injustice and extreme hardship was shown.

6331-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Compressed Air Industry. It applies to the compressed air industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about the code.

6331.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be used as a State conservation camp in connection with cooperative Civilian Conservation Corps work. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6331-D.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the pump manufacturing industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6331-E.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Throwing Industry. It applies to the Throwing Industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about the code.

6330.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the silk textile industry. It says the minimum wage applies only to the lowest paid class of labor in the industry. It also says weavers, warpers, loom fixers, and other skilled and semi-skilled workers must be paid on a higher wage scale that keeps the wage differences above the lowest paid class as they were on July 1, 1933.

6329.s: This order changes the Code of Fair Competition for the ship building and ship repairing industry. It sets up a committee to work with the Administrator as a planning and fair practice agency. The committee includes representatives of ship builders and ship repairers, plus four nonvoting members appointed by the President, and it may make recommendations to the Administrator about the industry.

6328.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for mutual savings banks. It applies to mutual savings banks and sets the code they are to follow.

6328-A.s: This order approves a code of fair competition for the Automatic Sprinkler Industry. It says an application was made, hearings were held, and the Administrator found the code met the law’s requirements. The order affects businesses in that industry.

6327.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the handkerchief industry. It applies to the handkerchief industry and follows an application, hearings, and a report by the Administrator.

6326.s: The order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the umbrella manufacturing industry. It also creates a Planning and Fair Practice Agency to work with the Administrator, made up of the thirteen members of the Executive Committee and three nonvoting members appointed by the Administrator.

6325.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Optical Manufacturing Industry. It also creates an Optical Manufacturing Industry Committee to work with the Administrator as a planning and fair practice agency. The committee is made up of seven industry representatives and three nonvoting members appointed by the Administrator.

6323.s: This order approves changes to the Code of Fair Competition for the Lumber and Timber Products Industries. It establishes a "Veneer and Plywood Division" within that code. The changes were set to take effect one week after the order unless good cause was shown to the Administrator before then.

6324.s: This order says David H. Morton may be appointed as a personal secretary and law clerk in the United States Customs Court in New York without following the civil service rules. It applies to that appointment and was requested by Judge Brown of the court.

6322.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Glass Container Industry. It affects the glass container industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6320.s: This order amends the oil burner industry code by adding rules for selling distillate burners of sleeve type. It sets material, size, and parts requirements for those burners, and says a sale that does not meet the rules is unfair competition unless permission is first obtained. It also allows existing stocks of noncomplying burners to be sold for 30 days after the change takes effect.

6321.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the motor vehicle retailing trade. It affects businesses and workers in that trade by putting the approved code into effect under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6318.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the luggage and fancy leather goods industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6319.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Women’s Belt Industry. It also sets a condition for the National Association of Women’s Belt Manufacturers to keep taking part in choosing the code authority and its activities, if its constitution and bylaws are amended in a way the Administrator accepts.

6317.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the retail lumber, lumber products, building materials, and building specialties trade. It affects businesses in that trade by putting the approved code into place under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6315.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Saddlery Manufacturing Industry. It affects people and businesses in that industry by putting the approved code into effect.

6316.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Ice Industry. It also creates a code authority to work with the Administrator as a Planning and Fair Practice Agency for the ice industry. The authority must include five representatives of the ice industry and three nonvoting members appointed by the Administrator.

6314.s: This order approves a code of fair competition for the laundry and dry cleaning machinery manufacturing industry. It applies to that industry and follows an application, hearings, and a report by the Administrator.

6313.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Boot and Shoe Manufacturing Industry. It also says article IV must be removed because interpretations of section 7(a) of the National Industrial Recovery Act had caused confusion and misunderstanding. The order affects the boot and shoe manufacturing industry and the people or businesses using that code.

6311.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the knitting, braiding, and wire covering machine industries. It applies to businesses in those industries and adopts the Administrator’s findings and recommendations.

6312.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Builders Supplies Trade. It affects businesses in that trade by putting the approved code into effect.

6309.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Electric Storage and Wet Primary Battery Industry. It applies to that industry and follows an application, hearings, and a report by the Administrator.

6310.s: The President approved a Code of Fair Competition for the Textile Machinery Manufacturing Industry. The order says an application was made, hearings were held, and the Administrator found the code complied with the law. It affects the textile machinery manufacturing industry.

6308.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Boiler Manufacturing Industry. It applies to people and businesses in that industry, and it leaves out subparagraph (a) of article VII.

6306.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Lime Industry. It also requires the National Lime Association to change its bylaws and remove a rule that made membership depend on nomination by two members and approval by a majority of the board of directors.

6307.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the farm equipment industry. It also says the second paragraph of article VIII must be removed. The order affects businesses in that industry.

6305.s: This order approves a "Code of Fair Competition" for bankers under the National Industrial Recovery Act. It affects bankers by putting that code into effect.

6304.s: This order changes the President’s Reemployment Agreement for employers signing on or after October 1, 1933. It changes the work limits so factory or mechanical workers or artisans may not be employed more than 35 hours a week until December 31, 1933, and no worker more than 8 hours in any one day. It says earlier signed agreements are not changed.

6302.s: This order exempts Clayborn L. Gatewood from a law that would have required his automatic retirement because of age. It lets him stay in service as a junior mechanic in the House wing of the United States Capitol Building until September 30, 1935.

6303.s: This order consolidates the Kaniksu National Forest and the Pend Oreille National Forest into one forest called the Kaniksu National Forest. It also transfers administration of certain lands from the Pend Oreille National Forest to the Coeur d'Alene National Forest. The order says it does not give any lands national-forest status that they did not already have, and it does not remove any lands from national-forest status.

6301.s: This order postpones again the effective date for moving the District Court of the United States for the Panama Canal Zone to the Department of Justice. The new date is November 4, 1933.

6299.s: This order approves a revised Code of Fair Competition for the Bituminous Coal Industry. It also approves the revised schedule of basic minimum rates and corrects a wording error in the code. For the National Bituminous Coal Labor Board, it says only the President’s impartial and disinterested representatives may take part in decisions, while the other members act in an advisory role.

6300.s: This order abolishes Chincoteague, Virginia, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 14, which has headquarters in Norfolk, Virginia. The change takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

6298.s: This order appoints Hugh S. Johnson to serve temporarily as a nonvoting member of each code authority under the Code of Fair Competition for the Bituminous Coal Industry. He may name an agent to act for him in any divisional or subdivisional code authority. The President also keeps the power to appoint a member directly instead of this temporary appointment.

6296-A.s: This order allocates $100,000 from a national industrial recovery appropriation for payments to certain contractors with government contracts made before June 16, 1933. The money is to help them finish those contracts and comply with the codes and employment agreements that apply to them. Payments may be made only to contractors who have complied, or agreed to comply, with the applicable codes and agreements and who receive the required certificate and findings.

6297.s: This order changes Reservoir-Site Reserve No. 17 in California to allow the Federal Power Commission to issue an amended license for project no. 966. It lets two sections of a transmission line be moved on certain listed lands, and if those lands are later needed for reservoir purposes, the licensee must remove its project works at its own expense within 30 days after notice from the Secretary of the Interior.

6296.s: This order denies an exemption request from Gem-Dandy Garter Company and the other named applicants under the Corset and Brassiere Code. It says they did not show a case of injustice or extreme hardship that would require special treatment. The order affects those applicants and their request for a wage differential for members of the industry in the southern section of the United States.

6295.s: This order approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Underwear and Allied Products Manufacturing Industry. It also gives manufacturers covered by one part of the code a 14-day stay after the code takes effect so they may show cause to the Administrator why they should not be included under that section.

6294.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the transit industry. It says existing labor contracts may continue until they expire unless the employer and employees agree to changes, but renewed contracts cannot have working hours above the code’s maximum or wages below its minimums. It also requires the American Transit Association to change its constitution and by-laws if needed so there are no unfair limits on membership.

6293.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the textile bag industry. It applies to the textile bag industry and sets that code under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6291.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the linoleum and felt base manufacturing industry. It affects businesses in that industry by putting the approved code into effect.

6292.s: This executive order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Oil Burner Industry. It also creates a Code Authority to work with the Administrator as a Planning and Fair Practice Agency for that industry. The Code Authority must include nine representatives from the oil burner industry and three nonvoting members appointed by the Administrator.

6290.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the gasoline pump manufacturing industry. It also creates a Gasoline Pump Manufacturing Industry Committee to work with the Administrator on planning and fair practice matters. The committee will have five industry representatives and three nonvoting members appointed by the Administrator.

6289-A.s: This order approves a code of fair competition for the bituminous coal industry, with several conditions. Coal producers subject to the code must give statistical information to government agencies designated by the Administrator. It also changes how the code handles the Industrial Board, minimum rates, and the definition of “employee.”

6289.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Flower and Feather Industry. It affects businesses and workers in that industry by putting the approved code into effect.

6284.s: This order abolishes Robbinston, Maine, as a customs port of entry. It also extends the limits of the customs port of Calais, Maine, to include the townships of Calais, Robbinston, and Baring in Washington County, Maine. These changes take effect 30 days after the date of the order.
