6288.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in place until the President or Congress revokes it, and it applies while a resurvey is pending.

6287.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in two townships in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. It keeps those lands withdrawn while a resurvey is pending. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

6286.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the townships are being resurveyed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6285.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain surveyed public lands in California for classification. It also says the lands will stay withdrawn while a decision is made about including them in a national monument, subject to valid existing rights.

6283.s: This order abolishes New Bern, North Carolina, and Manteo, North Carolina, as customs ports of entry in Customs Collection District No. 15. It takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

6284-A.s: This executive order changes the Code of Fair Competition for the Petroleum Industry. It sets or changes work hours and minimum pay rules for workers in drilling, refining, pipeline, market, filling station, and garage operations, and it gives the President and federal agencies more authority over reports, quotas, shipments, and prices for petroleum. It also changes rules for merchants selling petroleum products, adjusts equipment sale rules, and says the code rules do not apply to propane, butane, and other liquefied petroleum gases.

6282.s: This order abolishes Lincoln, Nebraska, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 46 (Omaha). The change takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

6281.s: This order abolishes Knoxville, Tennessee, as a customs port of entry in customs collection district No. 43. It affects customs operations in that district, which has headquarters at Memphis, Tennessee.

6279.s: This order abolishes Sturgeon Bay, Wisconsin, as a customs port of entry in customs collection district No. 37, which has headquarters in Milwaukee. The change takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

6280.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of public lands in two townships in New Mexico that had been held pending resurvey. After the official filing of the resurvey plats, the land would be open for 91 days only to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws. After that period, the land would be open to the general public under the public-land laws that apply.

6278.s: This order revokes part of a previous withdrawal of certain public lands in California. The released lands are opened first only to entry under the homestead and desert-land laws by qualified ex-service men, under the terms of the cited resolution and regulations. After that period, the lands may be used by the general public under any applicable public-land law.

6275.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Cast Iron Soil Pipe Industry. It affects businesses in that industry by putting the approved code into effect.

6276.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It makes exceptions allowed by the named laws and is meant to aid the State of New Mexico in making exchange selections. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6274.s: This order denies a request from the Connecticut Garment Manufacturers Association for an exemption from the minimum wage rules in the Coat and Suit Industry code. The applicants had said the code was unfair to them and asked for special treatment. The Administrator reported that no case of injustice and extreme hardship had been shown.

6273.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the leather industry. It applies to the leather industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about the code. It does not list the code’s specific rules in this order.

6272.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the salt producing industry. It also creates a code committee to work with the Administrator as a Planning and Fair Practice Agency for the industry. The committee must have seven industry representatives chosen by a fair method approved by the Administrator, and three nonvoting members appointed by the Administrator.

6271.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the wall paper manufacturing industry. It also creates an industry committee to work with the Administrator as a Planning and Fair Practice Agency. The committee will have five representatives from the industry and three nonvoting members appointed by the Administrator.

6270.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Motion Picture Laboratory Industry. It affects businesses in that industry by putting the code into effect.

6269.s: This order withdraws and reserves a tract of land in Alaska for use by the Washington-Alaska Military Cable and Telegraph System. The land is subject to any valid existing rights, and the order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6268.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it, and it applies while the township is resurveyed.

6267.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in two townships in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It applies while those townships are being resurveyed and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6266.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the township is being resurveyed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6265.s: The order changes a prior executive order to let the Secretary of Agriculture set aside up to $35,000 for the Bureau of Chemistry and Soils. The money is for soil examination, surveys, and investigations.

6264.s: This order exempts George P. Metzger, a deputy collector of internal revenue in Ohio, from the age-based retirement rule that would normally separate him from service. The exemption lasts until December 31, 1933.

6263.s: This order exempts Joe Smith from a law that would have required his automatic separation from civilian service when he reached the retirement age. It lets him stay in service until August 31, 1935.

6262.s: The order changes the Consular Regulations to let the Secretary of State waive certain requirements and allow the full amount of fees collected to be remitted to the Department of State. It also allows salaries and allowances to be paid by individual drafts to employees. The order updates related references in the Consular Regulations and in Instructions to Diplomatic Officers.

6261.s: The order says a national emergency exists and lets the Secretary of the Treasury receive gold from natural deposits in the United States or places under U.S. control for sale. It allows those sales to people licensed to use gold in the arts, industries, or professions, or for export to foreign buyers. The Secretary sets the price, rules, and charges, and may also issue licenses to export articles made from that gold.

6260-A.s: This order names the Secretary of the Interior as the Administrator for the petroleum industry. It also makes the Department of the Interior the federal agency for that industry. They are to exercise the functions and powers given by the law and the Code of Fair Competition for the petroleum industry.

6260.s: This order sets rules for gold coin, gold bullion, gold certificates, and foreign exchange during a national emergency. It requires many people who hold gold coin, gold bullion, or gold certificates to file a sworn return, and it limits when gold can be acquired, held, earmarked, or exported without a license. It also gives the Secretary of the Treasury power to investigate, regulate, or prohibit foreign exchange transactions and the export or withdrawal of currency. Violations can lead to fines or prison.

6259.s: This order amends an earlier executive order from January 28, 1873. It says mechanics and laborers hired by the day in armories, arsenals, navy yards, and similar places are covered by that order. It also includes master workmen and others who hold appointments from the Government or a department, whether for a fixed time or at the pleasure of the appointing power.

6258-C.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Hosiery Industry. It applies to the hosiery industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings on that code.

6258-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the rayon and synthetic yarn producing industry. It requires each employer in the industry to give the Administrator reports from time to time about wages, hours of labor, and other matters in the form and detail he requires.

6258-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the automobile manufacturing industry. It applies to the automobile manufacturing industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings about that code.

6258-D.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the men’s clothing industry. It applies to businesses and other people covered by that code in the men’s clothing industry.

6258.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in effect while a resurvey of the township is pending. It remains in force unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6256.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the petroleum industry. It applies to the petroleum industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6257.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Photographic Manufacturing Industry. It also creates a Photographic Manufacturing Industry Committee to work with the Administrator as a Planning and Fair Practice Agency. The committee must have seven industry representatives chosen by a fair method approved by the Administrator and three nonvoting members appointed by the Administrator.

6255.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Lumber and Timber Products Industries. It applies to businesses in those industries and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings on the code.

6254.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the iron and steel industry. It applies to the iron and steel industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6253.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the fishing tackle industry. It also requires the Associated Fishing Tackle Manufacturers to change its bylaws by repealing the rule that required a majority vote for election to membership in the association.

6252.s: This order gives the Federal Emergency Administrator of Public Works power to set up agencies, use government and volunteer workers, and help build or finance public works projects. It also lets the Administrator make grants to states, municipalities, and other public bodies, and help finance certain railroad maintenance and equipment. The order bars convict labor on covered projects, sets limits on work hours, requires just and reasonable wages, and requires contractors to post wage rates.

6251.s: This order designates the Federal Power Commission to help the Federal Emergency Administrator of Public Works prepare the public works program for water power and the transmission of electrical energy. It directs the Commission to survey U.S. water resources, the role of water power in other industries and in interstate and foreign commerce, and the transmission and distribution of electrical energy. It also lets the Commission investigate loan applications for public works projects involving electric power and make recommendations to the Administrator.

6250.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the legitimate full length dramatic and musical theatrical industry. It follows an application, hearings, and a report by the Administrator saying the code meets the requirements of the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6249.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Lace Manufacturing Industry. It also creates a Lace Manufacturing Industry Committee to work with the Administrator as a planning and fair practice agency for that industry. The committee must have five industry representatives and three nonvoting members appointed by the Administrator.

6248.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Corset and Brassiere Industry. It applies to the industry and adopts the Administrator’s report, recommendations, and findings.

6247.s:
This order sets rules for how draft executive orders and proclamations must be prepared. It says they must follow government style rules, use approved geographic names and land descriptions, and be typed in a set format.

It also sets a review process: drafts go first to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget, then to the Attorney General, then to the Department of State before going to the President. The Department of State keeps the signed originals and oversees their publication and distribution.

6246.s: This order says federal supply contracts made in the United States must require contractors to follow the approved code of fair competition for that industry, or the President's Reemployment Agreement if no code exists. If a contractor does not comply, the Government may end the contract and buy the supplies in the open market, and the contractor and sureties may have to pay the extra cost. It also says disbursing officers are not liable for payments made under the act or any order issued under it.

6245.s: This order keeps certain employees in their current jobs for now instead of separating them right away under Executive Order No. 6166. It says they will stay in place unless later directed otherwise, and that they will be separated on September 30, 1933, under Section 19.

6244.s: This order delays the operation of certain parts of Executive Order 6166 that relate to the Office of the General Counsel for the Bureau of Internal Revenue until October 10, 1933. It also allows those delayed provisions to be put into effect in whole or in part between August 10, 1933 and October 10, 1933 by a joint order of the Secretary of the Treasury and the Attorney General, with presidential approval.

6243.s: This order postpones the effective date of transferring the District Court of the United States for the Panama Canal Zone to the Department of Justice. The new effective date is October 4, 1933.

6242-B.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the electrical manufacturing industry. It affects the electrical manufacturing industry and sets that code in place under the National Industrial Recovery Act.

6242-C.s: This order denies a request for exemption from parts of the Cotton Textile Code. The request came from the named applicants, who said the code was unjust to them because of limits on the use of productive machinery. The order says no case of injustice and extreme hardship was shown, but notes they may still be affected by a stay of the code granted by the Administrator.

6242-A.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the Coat and Suit Industry. It applies to businesses in that industry and follows an application, hearings, and a report by the Administrator.

6242.s: This order designates Mrs. Alice M. Grove of the General Land Office to sign land patents when the regular clerk is absent. It affects land patent paperwork in the Department of the Interior.

6242-D.s: This order denies Crystal Springs Bleachery Incorporated’s request for an exemption from parts of the Cotton Textile Code. It says the company had hearings, but no case of injustice or extreme hardship was shown. The company may still be affected by a stay of the code already granted by the Administrator, pending final action on a related application from the Rubber Manufacturer's Association.

6242-E.s: This order denies an exemption from the Cotton Textile Code for the applicants who said the code was unfair to them. It covers their request about limits on the use of productive machinery. They may still be affected by a stay of the code under a later order while issues about machinery limits for tire yarns or fabrics for rubber tires are decided.

6241.s: This order lets a special Senate committee inspect tax returns. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury and approved by the President.

6240.s: This order names Winfield W. Riefler as a member of the Central Statistical Board. It also assigns him as Economic Adviser to the Executive Council.

6239.s: This order defers the effective date for abolishing the Federal Coordinating Service to October 10, 1933. It also allows the President to make that abolition effective, in whole or in part, between August 10, 1933, and October 10, 1933.

6238.s: This order creates a Science Advisory Board under the National Research Council. The board can appoint committees to deal with specific problems in different departments, working through the National Academy of Sciences and the National Research Council. It names the board members and appoints them for two years.

6237-A.s: This order gives the Alien Property Custodian the President’s power under the Trading with the Enemy Act over deposits, transfers, and payments of money and interest held by the Treasurer of the United States. If the Custodian cannot serve, the General Counsel and then the Director of Finance and Accounts take that authority. It also lets these officials release and deliver property held under the act, while claims that must go to the Attorney General and the President still must do so.

6237.s: The order allocates money to buy land needed to complete the Great Smoky Mountains National Park. It directs the Treasury to transfer the funds for that purpose, and the land may be bought by the Secretary of the Interior or through authorized state commissions. The order says the land purchases are for the park area in North Carolina and Tennessee.

6236.s: This order allows Henry Roe Cloud to be appointed without a competitive civil-service exam as Superintendent of the Haskell Institute in Lawrence, Kansas. It affects the Haskell Institute and Mr. Cloud. The order says he is a Winnebago Indian and has experience in Indian education and the Indian Service.

6235.s: This order revokes part of two earlier executive orders that had set aside certain Oregon lands for power-site use. It applies only to the lands listed in the order.

6234.s: This order changes rules for pensions and retirement pay for some veterans and widows. It defines who counts as a widow for certain war and peace-time veterans, and it limits pension payments for people who still hold certain government jobs or work for some U.S.-owned corporations. It also limits pension or retirement pay for people living outside the continental United States, with listed exceptions, and defines what counts as Veterans' Administration facilities for hospital care.

6233.s: This order sets a new rule for Veterans' Affairs medical care. It allows the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs to provide medical, surgical, and dental services within Veterans' Administration facilities to honorably discharged veterans of any war and to men discharged for disabilities incurred in the line of duty. It also allows the Veterans' Administration to provide supplies such as dental appliances, wheel chairs, artificial limbs, trusses, and similar items when they are reasonably necessary.

6232.s: This order sets rules for the Veterans’ Administration to provide domiciliary or hospital care, including medical treatment, to certain honorably discharged veterans and service members with service-related injuries or diseases. It also covers some veterans with permanent disabilities, tuberculosis, or neuropsychiatric ailments who cannot earn a living and have no adequate means of support. The order limits when clothing, travel expenses, and pension payments may be provided, and says no one living outside the continental United States or its territories or possessions is entitled to this care.

6231.s: This order amends Veterans Regulation No. 3(a) by canceling Paragraph II. The surrounding law is about rules for rating disabilities and setting pension rates for veterans and their dependents, including different kinds of service-connected and non-service-connected disabilities.

6230.s: This order sets rules for when disability and death pension awards start, when pension payments can be reduced or stopped, and when claims must be filed with the Veterans' Administration. It also creates a Board of Veterans' Appeals to review claims and makes its decisions final in most cases. The order provides for special review boards to look at certain presumptive claims for veterans who served before November 11, 1918, and whose disability was not the result of their own misconduct.

6228.s: This order says certain parks, battlefields, monuments, memorials, and national cemeteries are transferred from the War Department to the Department of the Interior. It lists the specific sites covered by the transfer. It also postpones the transfer of other national cemeteries, including those in foreign countries and insular possessions, until further order.

6227-A.s: This order says the Cordage and Twine Industry must follow the Cotton Textile Industry Code of Fair Competition starting at midnight on the date of the order. It also requires the industry to present its own code for hours, wages, and other working conditions to the Administrator for approval by August 5, 1933. The order says the President can cancel, revise, or change it at any time.

6227.s: This order delays the separation of employees covered by Sections 2 and 15 of Executive Order No. 6166. They are kept in their current status until September 30, 1933, unless changed sooner by later direction.

6226.s: This order sets rules for reporting how public funds are apportioned and what obligations have been made against them. It requires the Treasury Department to keep budget accounts and get reports from executive departments, independent establishments, and governmental corporations that use public funds. It also requires the Secretary of the Treasury to give the Bureau of the Budget reports on the status of appropriations and funds available for spending.

6225.s: This order establishes a Central Statistical Board to set standards and coordinate federal statistical services for the purposes of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The board includes representatives from several federal offices and may add other members. It may review statistics schedules and plans for tabulation and classification, and it is given authority to appoint staff and use $20,000 from the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works.

6223.s: This order allocates money from the National Industrial Recovery appropriation and tells the Treasury Department to transfer it to the Department of Agriculture. The money is for finishing the purchase of land for the National Arboretum, including costs tied to buying the land.

6224.s: This order delays the transfers, consolidations, and eliminations called for in sections 1, 4, and 8 of Executive Order No. 6166 until December 31, 1933. It does not delay the abolition of the Federal Employment Stabilization Board. Any of those changes may still be made effective between August 10, 1933, and December 31, 1933, by order of the Secretary of the Treasury approved by the President.

6222.s: This order postpones the effective date of transferring legal work from the Veterans' Administration to the Department of Justice. The work involves defending suits against the United States under section 19 of the World War Veterans Act, 1924, as amended.

6221-C.s: This order applies to garment manufacturers in the International Association of Garment Manufacturers and Subdivisional Industries Thereof, including producers of light cotton garments. Pending approval of a fair competition code, they must follow certain parts of the Cotton Textile Code and a 40-hour workweek limit, with some workers excepted. It also says productive machinery may run for only one 40-hour shift each week, and that hours cannot be raised or wages lowered below current standards.

6221-B.s: This order put certain proposed rules for the hosiery industry into effect while a final code was still pending. It limits hours for many workers in productive operations to 40 hours a week, sets a five-day workweek for most productive work, and sets minimum wages under the code. It also says employers must respect workers’ rights to organize and bargain collectively and must follow the approved hours, pay, and other work rules.

6221-A.s: This order approves a code of fair competition for the Wool Textile Industry. It also creates a Wool Textile Industry Committee to work with the Administrator on planning and fair practices. The committee must include five industry representatives and three nonvoting members appointed by the Administrator.

6221.s: This order delays the effective date of several parts of Executive Order No. 6166. It delays changes involving co-operative vocational education and rehabilitation, payments for agricultural experiment stations, co-operative agricultural extension work, and endowment and maintenance of colleges for the benefit of agriculture and the mechanic arts. It also delays the abolishment of the Federal Employment Stabilization Board and the transfer of its records to the Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works.

6221-D.s: This order says the National Council of Pajama Manufacturers must follow the Cotton Textile Industry Code while a code of fair competition is pending approval for the industry. It begins on July 26, 1933, and can be changed or canceled at any time without notice. It also says it may not be used to raise hours or lower wages below the standards now in place, and it must not delay submission of a code for the industry.

6220.s: This order reinstates Louis R. Glavis in the Civil Service. It allows him to be appointed to any department, establishment, or office in the classified civil service if he is qualified and there is a need for his services, without following the usual civil service rules. It also says this is done without regard to any charges previously brought against him.

6219.s: This order sets rules for licenses to practice the healing art in the Canal Zone. It says no one may practice unless licensed or exempt, and it sets education standards, exams in the basic sciences, and rules for licenses without examination in some cases. It also creates special rules for midwifery and keeps some earlier licenses in effect unless suspended or revoked.

6215.s: This order changes a Civil Service Rules section to include all positions in the Division of Investigation except fingerprint classifiers. It takes effect on the effective date of Section 3 of Executive Order 6166.

6216.s: This order approves a Code of Fair Competition for the shipbuilding and shiprepairing industry, as amended and submitted on July 25, 1933. It applies to that industry and follows hearings and a report and recommendation from the Administrator.

6214-B.s: This order appoints Colvin W. Brown to temporarily serve as Assistant Secretary of the Executive Council. It says the role was created to help with the orderly presentation of business and to coordinate problems between new government agencies.

6214-A.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to place certain commerce-related jobs under Schedule B, which means they are excepted from competition. It covers commercial attaches, trade commissioners, district managers, experts, commercial agents, and special agents who investigate trade conditions in the United States, Alaska, the Philippines, and other insular possessions. These positions are tied to promoting foreign and domestic commerce of the United States, including some positions that had previously been moved into the competitive civil service.

6214.s: This order exempts Curtis F. Marbut, a Principal Soil Scientist in the Department of Agriculture, from the rule that would automatically separate him from service at retirement age. The exemption lasts until June 30, 1934.

6213.s: This order sets the rental and subsistence allowances for officers of the various services that are entitled to them for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1934. It sets one subsistence allowance at 51 cents per day and one rental allowance for one room at $17 per month.

6212.s: This order temporarily withdraws surveyed and unsurveyed public lands in one township in California for classification. It is to help decide whether the lands should be included in a national monument. The lands remain subject to valid existing claims and to an earlier withdrawal connected with the Colorado River Storage Project.

6211.s: This order appoints Colonel Henry M. Waite to the Special Board for Public Works. He is to serve in place of Colonel George R. Spalding under the public works and construction projects authority in the 1933 act.

6210-A.s: This order makes parts of the proposed Code of Fair Competition for the Silk and Rayon Dyeing and Printing Industry effective. It approves several listed articles, but some parts are left ineffective until a public hearing and final approval. The order applies to members of that industry.

6210.s: This order combines the Natural Bridge National Forest with the George Washington National Forest. The lands covered by those forests will now be known as the George Washington National Forest, and it does not give new national forest status to other public lands or remove that status from any public lands.

6209-A.s: This order says the Textile Finishing Industry will be bound by certain parts of the Cotton Textile Industry Code beginning July 31. It sets the minimum wage at $1.00 per week higher in each section of the industry than the Cotton Textile Code. The agreement can be canceled at any time without notice.

6209-B.s: This order says manufacturers of knitted, woven, and other underwear and allied products must follow the Cotton Textile Industry Code while a fair competition code is pending approval. It applies to underwear mills and related fabrics used for underwear, and it can be canceled at any time without notice.

6209.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to administer Section 208 under Title II of the cited Act. It also lets the Secretary name agents, set up boards and agencies, and make rules needed to carry out that section.

6208.s: This order rescinds parts of two earlier executive orders and replaces them with a new funding plan. It allocates $20,000,000 for the purchase of forest lands for conservation work. The money is to be transferred by the Treasury Department to the War Department, then to the Department of Agriculture for use by the Forest Service to buy land in national-forest purchase areas.

6207.s: This order keeps in effect the authority given to the Secretary of Agriculture under a previous order. That authority covers functions and powers under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act for trades and industries mainly handling milk and its products, tobacco and its products, and all foods and foodstuffs. It does not include rules about hours of labor, rates of pay, or other conditions of employment, and the President keeps the power to approve or disapprove codes of fair competition.

6206-C.s: This order allows Mrs. Bertha Wetherton to be appointed in the Treasury Department as a Special Assistant to the Commissioner of Internal Revenue without following the Civil Service rules. She would be assigned to similar duties in the Bureau of Internal Revenue.

6206-B.s: This order approves certain provisions of a Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Thread Industry. Those provisions are made effective on July 17, 1933, and they are the same as corresponding provisions in the Cotton Textile Code. The approval is subject to the same interpretations and conditions placed on the Cotton Textile Code, and it may be changed after a hearing on the cotton thread code.

6206-A.s: This order gives final approval to the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Textile Industry and withdraws the condition that approval would end after four months unless renewed. It sets work-hour rules for office employees and for repair shop crews, engineers, electricians, and watching crews, and it says wage rate differences for certain employees cannot be reduced. It also limits any increase in work speed beyond the practices in place on July 1, 1933, unless approved, and it applies to the whole cotton textile industry with some possible exemptions.

6206.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It does this to help proposed legislation that would protect the water supply of the City of Los Angeles. It affects the listed lands and anyone who might seek to use them for those purposes.

6205-C.s: This order says certain divisions of the Silk Association of America must follow the Cotton Textile Industry Code beginning July 17. It applies to the Broad Silk and Rayon Weavers, Converters, Special Fabrics, Ribbon, and Woven Label divisions, and the agreement can be canceled at any time without notice.

6205-A.s: This order lets the Administrator for Industrial Recovery hire permanent staff and set their pay, with general approval from the Special Industrial Recovery Board. It also lets the Administrator conduct hearings and carry out other powers under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, except approving codes, making agreements, issuing licenses, and using certain listed powers.

6205-B.s: This order says any approved code of fair competition takes effect on the date stated in the code. People who did not take part in setting up or agreeing to a code, but are directly affected by it, may ask for a hearing if they want an exception, exemption, or change. If they apply within ten days after the code takes effect, they must get a hearing before the code is enforced against them. The Administrator may also pause the code for similarly affected people while the issues are decided.

6205.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for reservoir sites in the East Fork Deschutes River area.

6204-B.s: This order approves certain provisions of a Code of Fair Competition for the Throwing Industry. Those provisions were to take effect on July 17, 1933, and they are subject to the same interpretations and conditions that were placed on the related Cotton Textile Code. The order also says the approved provisions may be revised or modified after a hearing on the code.

6204-A.s: This order approves certain provisions of a Code of Fair Competition for the Rayon Weaving Industry. Those provisions are set to take effect on July 17, 1933, and they apply to the rayon weaving industry. The approval is subject to the same interpretations and conditions used for the related cotton textile code, and it may be changed after a hearing on the code.

6204.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to use the powers given to the President to enforce Section 9(c) of the Act and the July 11, 1933 order. It lets the Secretary appoint agents, create boards and agencies, and issue rules and regulations needed for that enforcement.

6203.s: This order sets rules for filling postmaster vacancies in first, second, and third class post offices. It lets the Postmaster General and Civil Service Commission use nominations, open competitive exams, and a list of eligible candidates for appointment. It also sets age and residence limits for applicants and gives added rating points and age waivers for veterans of the World War, Spanish-American War, and the Philippine Insurrection.

6202-B.s: This order sets who will do the Secretary of the Treasury’s duties if the Secretary is absent or sick. If both the Secretary and Under Secretary are absent or sick, the Fiscal Assistant Secretary will act. If the Secretary, Under Secretary, and Fiscal Assistant Secretary are all absent or sick, the Senior Assistant Secretary on duty will act.

6202.s: This order revokes part of a 1910 executive order that created Phosphate Reserve No. 4 in Wyoming. It applies to the described land in Wyoming, including Mineral Survey No. 553, the Granite Placer claim.

6202-A.s: This order creates a temporary Executive Council made up of top federal officials and other members the President may choose. The council is set to meet each Tuesday at the White House, and the senior Cabinet member present will lead if the President is absent. It also names Frank C. Walker as temporary Executive Secretary and lets him buy needed equipment and hire temporary staff, with funds allotted for those costs subject to approval.

6201-A.s: This order designates Miss Louise Polk Wilson, a clerk in the District of Columbia, to sign the President’s name on land patents. It affects land patents handled by the Department of the Interior.

6201.s: This order makes Puerto Rico part of the Internal Revenue Collection District of Maryland for all purposes allowed by federal internal revenue laws. It takes effect on and after July 28, 1933.

6199.s: This order prohibits transporting petroleum and its products in interstate and foreign commerce if they were produced or taken from storage in amounts above what a State law or valid State order allows. It applies to petroleum producers, storage operators, and anyone moving those products across state or international lines.

6200.s: This order gives the Director of Emergency Conservation Work full authority over how the work is run under the President’s direction. It says no purchase of supplies, materials, or equipment over $2,500 can be made without prior approval from the Director or a person he names. It also directs that services and items be provided for the instruction, recreation, amusement, and welfare of enrolled members of the work.

6198.s: This order appoints Harold L. Ickes to serve as Federal Emergency Administrator of Public Works. It is issued to carry out the public works and construction projects section of the referenced act.

6197.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of 80 acres in Montana that had been set aside for use by the Forest Service as an administrative site. It opens the land first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws for a limited period, subject to valid rights. After that period, the land is open to the general public under the public-land laws that apply.

6195.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of public lands in a township in Wyoming that had been held pending resurvey. After the official filing of the resurvey plat, the land would be open for 91 days only to qualified ex-service men under the rules in the resolution, and after that it would be open to the general public under the public-land laws that apply. No one could claim rights to the land by settlement before entry except as allowed by this order.

6196.s: The order carries out the Emergency Railroad Transportation Act by creating the office of Federal Coordinator of Transportation. It designates Interstate Commerce Commissioner Joseph B. Eastman as the Coordinator and relieves him of his other duties as commissioner, except for duties he chooses to perform and certain voting duties. It also approves the appointment of assistants and agents for the Coordinator, but not at a salary above $15,000 a year.

6194.s: This order revokes a previous order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Oregon pending a resurvey. It affects the lands described in sections 13 to 36 of Township 16 South, Range 9 West of the Willamette meridian.

6191.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn certain public lands in California for use by the Department of Commerce as air mail beacon sites and landing fields. It applies only to the lands described in the order in San Bernardino Meridian, including parts of sections 10 and 11.

6190.s: This order revokes part of an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in California. The released lands are opened first to qualified exservice men for entry under the homestead and desert-land laws for a set period, and later to the general public under any applicable public land law.

6189.s: This order reserves a tract of land below the line of mean low tide in Wrangell Narrows at Petersburg, Alaska, for use as a dock site. The Forest Service may use it in connection with the administration of the Tongass National Forest, along with other Government bureaus. It is subject to all valid existing rights and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6186.s: This order revokes the withdrawal of certain public lands in a township in Wyoming that had been held pending a resurvey. The lands are to be opened first to qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat, subject to valid rights and existing withdrawals. After that, the lands may be opened to the general public under applicable public-land laws.

6187.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of public lands in a township in Wyoming that had been held pending resurvey. It says those lands must first be open only to entry under the homestead and desert-land laws by qualified ex-service men for a 91-day period after the resurvey plat is officially filed. After that, the lands may be opened to the general public under the public-land laws that apply, and no rights may be gained by settlement before entry except as allowed in the order.

6184.s: This order withdraws certain lands in Utah from settlement, location, sale, or entry, while keeping any valid existing rights. It sets aside those lands as Helium Reserve No. 2. The reserve is for producing helium to supply the Army and Navy and other branches of the Federal Government.

6185.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of public lands in two Wyoming townships that had been held pending a resurvey. It says those lands will be opened only to entry under the homestead and desert-land laws by qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the resurvey plats are officially filed. After that, the lands may be available to the general public under the public-land laws that apply.

6183.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of public lands in two townships in New Mexico. After the plats of resurvey are officially filed, the lands may be opened for 91 days only to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws, subject to valid rights and existing withdrawals. After that period, the lands may be available to the general public under any public-land law that applies.

6182.s: This order gives the Secretary of Agriculture the President’s powers under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act for trades and industries mainly handling milk and dairy products, tobacco and tobacco products, and all foods and foodstuffs. It does not include decisions about hours of labor, pay rates, or other working conditions. The President keeps the power to approve or disapprove any code of fair competition, and the order stays in effect until revoked.

6180.s: This order withdraws certain land in Arizona for use by the National Guard of the State of Arizona as a target range. The withdrawal is subject to valid existing rights. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6179-C.s: This order directs South Trimble, Jr., the Solicitor for the Department of Commerce, to perform the duties of the Secretary of Commerce. He would do this when the Secretary of Commerce and the Assistant Secretaries of Commerce are absent.

6181.s: This order changes a previous order so the funds for buying forest lands can be used in the existing National Forest Purchase Units. It also allows those funds to be used in any other National Forest Purchase Unit later set up by the Secretary of Agriculture, with the approval of the National Forest Reservation Commission.

6179-A.s: This order revokes a group of presidential appointments to classified positions in the Department of Labor. It affects named people who had been appointed as special investigators, clerks, a supervisor of detentions, a junior clerk, and a matron. Several of the positions are in the Immigration Service, and others are in the Naturalization Service and the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

6179.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Utah from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while a resurvey of the township is pending. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6179-B.s: This order abolishes the National Committee on Wood Utilization. Its property, files, and records are transferred to the Secretary of Commerce, who may decide what to do with them. If the forest products industries want to keep doing the same work on their own time and at their own expense, the Secretary of Commerce may let them use the committee's records and files.

6178.s: This order excludes certain lands in New Mexico from the Carson National Forest. It applies to the lands listed in the order under the Santa Fe 063408 application.

6177.s: The order revokes a 1930 withdrawal of public lands in one township in Arkansas pending resurvey. After the resurvey plat is officially filed, the unreserved public lands there would be opened for 91 days to qualified ex-service men under the homestead law only, subject to valid rights. After that, the land would be open to the general public under the public-land laws that apply, and no rights could be acquired by settlement before entry.

6176.s: This order sets the amount paid to carriers in the Rural Mail Delivery Service for equipment maintenance. For the period from July 1 to September 30, 1933, they are paid 1.176 cents per mile per day for each mile or major fraction of a mile scheduled.

6174.s: This order appoints Colonel Donald H. Sawyer as acting Federal Emergency Administrator of Public Works and sets up a Special Board for Public Works. It gives the administrator temporary authority to allocate up to $400,000,000 for highway building among the states, territories, and the District of Columbia, and up to $238,000,000 to the Department of the Navy for certain vessels. The public roads money must be approved by the board, and the administrator and board must study and report on public-works projects.

6175.s: This order changes how departmental employees are rated for demotion or separation when there is a reduction in force. It gives service credit based on years of Government service, up to 10 points. Employees who are eligible for retirement after 30 years of service get no credit for length of service when that retirement is authorized by law.

6170.s: This order says the Assistant Secretary of the Interior, Oscar L. Chapman, is authorized to perform the duties of the Secretary of the Interior. He may do so only when both the Secretary and the First Assistant Secretary are absent or unable to serve.

6173.s: This order appoints Hugh Johnson as Administrator for Industrial Recovery under Title I of the act. It also sets up a Special Industrial Recovery Board made up of several cabinet officials and other federal leaders. The Administrator is allowed to hire temporary staff for hearings and other work under Title I, with the board's general approval.

6172.s: This order adds certain lands in Utah to the Cache National Forest. It says the withdrawal will not interfere with lands that are already legally appropriated or reserved for a public purpose, as long as those rights or reservations stay in force.

6171.s: This order revokes the earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in a township in California that were being held pending resurvey. It then opens the unreserved public lands there, subject to valid rights, to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws for 91 days after the resurvey plat is officially filed. After that period, the land is open to the general public under the public-land laws that apply. No rights may be gained by settling on the land before entry except as allowed by the order.

6169.s: This order attaches up to 170 Coast Guard warrant officers to the War Department for duty on new public works projects or with the Civilian Conservation Corps. The Secretary of War may call them when needed, and they will have priority over members of the Army Reserve Corps, the Naval Reserve, and the Marine Corps Reserve. When ordered to duty, they will be paid from the funds for those projects or the Civilian Conservation Corps, and until then they will be on furlough status.

6168.s: This order exempts William A. Taylor, Chief of the Bureau of Plant Industry in the Department of Agriculture, from the rule that would automatically separate him from service at retirement age. The exemption lasts until December 31, 1933.

6166.s: This order reorganizes many parts of the executive branch by moving functions, offices, and records between departments and divisions. It creates or consolidates offices for procurement, national parks and buildings, investigations, disbursement, internal revenue, immigration and naturalization, and some other functions. It also abolishes several agencies and shifts some duties, property, and personnel to successor agencies or to the Treasury Department.

6165.s: This order excludes certain tracts of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It also restores those lands to entry under the applicable public-land laws for the home sites that are occupied there.

6167.s: This order cancels earlier accounting rules for diplomatic and consular officers and replaces them with new ones. It requires their accounts and drafts on the Secretary of State to be stated in United States currency, except for accounts covering special deposits. If disbursements are made in foreign currency, the vouchers must be sent in that currency with evidence showing its value in United States coinage.

6164.s: This order transfers possession and control of part of tract no. 2 at the Charleston Army Supply Base from the United States Shipping Board back to the War Department. The land is to be used for as long as the Charleston Ordnance Depot is maintained as an Ordnance Depot by the War Department. The order says this is to allow a proper firebreak between the Charleston Ordnance Depot and the United States Shipping Board Terminal.

6163.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of certain public lands in Colorado that had been held pending a resurvey. If the lands are otherwise available, they are to be opened first under homestead or desertland laws for qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the resurvey plat is officially filed. After that period, the lands may be open to the general public under applicable public-land laws, and no rights may be claimed by settling on them before entry except as allowed here.

6162.s: This order puts the construction of the Cove Creek Dam on Clinch River under Arthur E. Morgan, without extra pay. It says the work will be done by and through the Tennessee Valley Authority, using engineers as needed under his direction.

6161.s: This order directs the Tennessee Valley Authority Board to make surveys, plans, studies, experiments, and demonstrations. These actions are meant to help the proper use, conservation, and development of the natural resources of the Tennessee River drainage basin and nearby areas related to it. It also says the work is to promote the general welfare of the citizens in that area, within the money Congress provides.

6160.s: This order sets rules for Emergency Conservation Work, including pay, discipline, and camp operations for the Civilian Conservation Corps. It allows limited cash allowances for some CCC members, creates a penalty system for minor offenses, and provides for the enrollment of 25,000 veterans of the World War and previous wars. It also moves money for conservation work on Indian reservations and for the purchase of forest lands, and it lets the Director approve conservation camps on certain federal, state, county, municipal, and private lands.

6158.s: This order sets rules for burial help for deceased war veterans who were honorably discharged. It says a flag must be provided to drape the casket, and the flag is given to the next of kin after burial. The Veterans Administration may pay burial, funeral, and body transportation costs up to $75, but not if the veteran’s net assets were $1,000 or more at death. Claims must be filed within one year after death.

6156.s: This order sets rules for pensions for veterans who were disabled in active military or naval service during the Spanish-American War, the Boxer Rebellion, the Philippine Insurrection, or the World War. It also sets pension rules for widows, children, and dependent parents of veterans who died from service-related injury or disease. The order gives different monthly pension amounts based on the level of disability and the type of family survivor.

6157.s: This order sets a schedule of disability ratings for veterans based on reductions in earning capacity from specific injuries. It directs the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs to use ten grades of disability, from ten per cent to total, one hundred per cent, and to readjust the schedule from time to time. It also says the schedule must not reduce payments by more than 25 per centum for certain veterans who were properly rated on March 20, 1933.

6155.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in New Mexico that had been set aside pending resurvey. It says the unreserved lands in those townships may be opened, subject to valid rights, to qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plats, under homestead or desert-land laws only. After that, the land would be open to the general public under the public-land laws that apply.

6153.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in two townships in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the townships are resurveyed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6152.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Oregon for classification as to whether they are suitable for migratory bird refuge purposes. It applies to the listed lands and waters and is subject to valid existing rights. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6154.s: This order revokes two earlier withdrawals of land in Montana that had been set aside for use by the Forest Service as administrative sites. It then opens those lands, subject to valid rights, first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws, and later to the general public under any applicable public-land law. No one may gain rights by settlement before entry except as allowed in the order.

6150.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of public lands in two New Mexico townships that had been set aside pending resurvey. It says the unreserved public lands in those townships, if otherwise available, must be opened first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert-land laws for 91 days after the resurvey plats are officially filed. After that, the lands may be opened to the general public under the public-land laws that apply.

6149.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of certain public lands in New Mexico that had been held pending resurvey. After the official resurvey plats are filed, the lands may be opened for entry under the homestead or desert-land laws for 91 days by qualified ex-service men, subject to valid rights and the stated rules. After that, the lands may be available to the general public under any applicable public-land law, and no one may gain rights by settlement before entry except as allowed here.

6148.s: This order attaches listed naval medical and dental officers to the War Department for duty with the Civilian Conservation Corps. The Secretary of War is to call them as needed for hospitalization and medical attendance, and they are to be given priority over certain other medical and dental personnel. When they report for duty, they are to be paid from funds for the Civilian Conservation Corps.

6147.s: This order sets up a Treasury fund for emergency conservation work on tribal or other lands within Indian reservations. The fund can be spent for the purposes named in the March 31, 1933 law. It also directs that authorized funds for conservation work on Indian reservations be transferred to the Interior Department and paid out by the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, with separate payrolls and accounts kept.

6146.s: This order exempts Walter L. G. Perry from the rules that would automatically separate him from service because of age. It lets him keep serving as Chief of the Division of Photolithography in the Coast and Geodetic Survey until May 31, 1935.

6145.s: This order abolishes the Board of Indian Commissioners. It directs the Secretary of the Interior to wind up the board’s affairs and to receive its records, property, and personnel. The order would take effect on the 61st calendar day after it is sent to Congress unless changed under the stated law.

6144.s: This order amends a previous executive order about Emergency Conservation Work. It directs that 25,000 veterans of the World War and veterans of previous wars be enrolled as soon as possible under the supervision of the Director of the Emergency Conservation Work.

6143.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It makes exceptions allowed by the listed laws and keeps valid existing rights in place. The withdrawal is meant to aid the State of New Mexico in making exchange selections.

6142.s: This order changes a previous exemption from compulsory retirement for age for Pickens Neagle of the Navy Department. It ends that exemption on May 31, 1933.

6141.s: This order removes special agents employed in collecting cotton statistics from Schedule B and places those positions in the competitive classified service. The current people in those jobs will not get classified status, but if they are between 21 and 60, they may compete to keep their jobs in Civil Service Commission exams. The positions are excluded from the Retirement Act because the work is intermittent.

6140.s: This order revokes two earlier land withdrawals in Montana that had set aside public lands for Forest Service ranger stations. It then opens those lands, subject to valid rights and any phosphate reserve conditions, first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws for 91 days. After that, the lands are open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

6139.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of public lands in two townships in Colorado that had been held pending resurvey. After the official plats of resurvey are filed, the lands may be opened for 91 days to qualified ex-service men under the stated terms and rules. After that, they may be available to the general public under the public land laws. No one may gain rights to the released land by settlement before entry except as allowed in the order.

6137.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Arizona that had been held pending resurvey. It says those lands, if otherwise available, will be opened first to entry under the homestead or desert land laws for a limited period after the resurvey plats are filed. During that time, only qualified ex-service men may enter the lands under those terms, and after that the lands may be available to the general public under applicable public land laws.

6136.s: This order lets Emergency Conservation workers be assigned to county parks and metropolitan sections of municipal parks, with approval from the Director of Emergency Conservation Work. The National Park Service would supervise that work, and it would be limited to cooperative work on forest fires, forest tree pests and diseases, and flood control.

6135.s: This order sets aside money for the Secretary of Agriculture to buy forest lands within 42 existing national-forest purchase areas. The lands are in 20 states east of the Great Plains and are to be bought under the rules already set for such purchases. It affects private landowners in those areas and the federal forest program there.

6133.s: This order allows Mrs. Elizabeth Horter to be appointed to a classified job in the Department of State. It says the appointment may be made without following the Civil Service rules.

6134.s: This order changes the civil-service rules to replace "Federal Farm Board" with "Farm Credit Administration" in Schedules A and B. It adds certain private secretary and confidential clerk jobs, and up to eight jobs in the Governor’s immediate office, to the exempt positions under Schedule A. It also says workers transferred to the Farm Credit Administration do not automatically get competitive civil-service status unless the Governor recommends them and they pass any fitness tests set by the Civil Service Commission.

6132.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in Alaska, subject to valid existing rights, for use by the War Department as a site for an Army radio station at Point Barrow. The tract is described as about 14.1 acres. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6131-A.s: The order attaches listed naval surgeons to the War Department for duty with the Civilian Conservation Corps. The Secretary of War is to call them as needed for hospitalization and medical attendance. They are to be paid from funds set aside for emergency conservation work.

6130.s: This order transfers certain tide lands at the intersection of Mission and Stedman Streets in Ketchikan, Alaska, to the Treasury Department. It reserves the land as a site for Federal buildings, subject to valid existing rights. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6131.s: This order establishes a Treasury fund for work carried out on tribal or other lands within Indian reservations under the 1933 act on useful public work. The fund is to be used by the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, with recommendation from the Director of Emergency Conservation Work and approval of the President. Payments for the Indian Service must go through the bonded disbursing agent for each jurisdiction, with separate payrolls and accounts kept.

6128.s: This order changes the speed rules for vessels traveling through the Panama Canal and nearby waters. It sets different maximum speeds for different canal sections, including the locks, Gatún Lake, Gaillard Cut, Miraflores Locks, and canal ports. It also sets slower speeds for larger vessels in some places and says the order takes effect right away.

6129.s: This order directs the enrollment of 25,000 World War veterans in Emergency Conservation Work as soon as possible. They are to be enrolled under nearly the same conditions as the original enrollment and set up as a separate part of the program. Enrollment will not begin until full plans are agreed on and made public.

6127.s: The order says supplies, materials, equipment, and other property for Emergency Conservation Work should use surplus or excess stocks from executive departments or independent establishments when possible. If those stocks are not available, departments may provide needed items from current issue stocks and be reimbursed from the Emergency Conservation Fund. It also says costs for services and other items that cannot be procured that way will be charged to that fund.

6125.s: This order revokes parts of three earlier executive orders for specific lands in Montana, New Mexico, and Wyoming. Those lands are restored to the public domain if they are not otherwise reserved or withdrawn. They will be subject to disposal under the laws that apply after later notice is announced.

6126.s: The order directs the Director of the Emergency Conservation Work to set up his office in the District of Columbia and hire civilian personnel needed to carry out his duties. It also lets him authorize travel, buy office supplies and equipment, and use money from the Emergency Conservation Fund for those needs. Civilian and military personnel already in United States service are to be used as much as possible, and if needed, additional personnel may be hired without following civil service laws and regulations. A weekly report of those appointments must be made to the President.

6124.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the townships are resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6123.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in place until a resurvey of the township is completed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6122.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in a township in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It applies while the township is being resurveyed. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

6121.s: This order revokes part of a 1930 withdrawal of public lands in California, but not the lands already set aside as Death Valley National Monument. The released lands are opened first only to qualified ex-service men under the homestead and desert land laws, subject to valid rights and existing withdrawals. After that period, the lands may be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

6120.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. It applies to listed townships in the San Bernardino Meridian and lasts while a resurvey is pending. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6119.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal applies to listed townships in the San Bernardino Meridian and stays in effect while those townships are resurveyed. It remains in force unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6118.s: This order places a described piece of land in Alaska under the control of the Secretary of War for use by the Washington-Alaska Military Cable and Telegraph System. It also gives necessary right-of-way for access to the land. The land remains subject to a right-of-way for the Office of Indian Affairs, including free passage for its employees and pipe lines to carry water from the pump house to nearby buildings.

6117.s: This order adds certain lands in South Dakota to the Harney National Forest. It also says the withdrawal will not interfere with lands that were already legally appropriated under public land laws or reserved for a public purpose. Those legal rights and reserved uses can continue so long as they are legally maintained or remain in force.

6116.s: This order withdraws certain public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves that land for public use under the law cited in the order.

6115.s: This order sets up a committee made up of the Secretary of State, the Attorney General, and the Secretary of Labor. The committee is told to review the nationality laws, recommend revisions, especially to remove certain existing discriminations, and put them into one law to send to Congress at the next session.

6113.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The withdrawal is pending a survey and the filing of maps for a right-of-way for a transmission line to carry power from the Boulder Canyon Project to the city of Los Angeles. It affects the lands listed in the order, subject to valid existing rights.

6112.s: This order revokes part of a previous withdrawal of certain lands in California and Nevada. The lands listed in the order are affected, and the change is made for a transmission-line right-of-way.

6111.s: This order prohibits the earmarking for foreign account and the export of gold coin, gold bullion, and gold certificates, with limited licenses allowed in some cases. It also gives the Secretary of the Treasury authority to investigate, regulate, or prohibit foreign exchange transactions, transfers of credit, and the export or withdrawal of currency. People who hold or delivered gold under earlier orders may get licenses for amounts up to what they held or delivered, and willful violations can be punished by fine or imprisonment.

6110.s: This order changes Public Water Reserve No. 52 in Nevada so that Valentine scrip applications may be approved for the land described in it. The land involved is the specific property listed in Mount Diablo Meridian, in Carson City applications 09916 and 09917.

6108.s: This order waives an earlier rule that barred Federal employees from holding office under a State, territorial, or municipal government. It lets Raymond Moley, an Assistant Secretary of State, serve on a New York commission to investigate and collect facts about the State's administration of justice, without pay and without conflicting with his federal duties.

6109.s: This order sets the cash allowance for members of the Conservation Corps at $30 a month from enrollment until final discharge. It also says this allowance will not be subject to the deductions named in the March 20, 1933, act. It affects Conservation Corps members.

6107.s: This order exempts Reuben Perry, the superintendent of the Albuquerque School in New Mexico, from the retirement rule for automatic separation from service. It keeps him in service until June 30, 1933.

6106-A.s: This order sets up how funds for unemployment relief work are handled for useful public work under the Civilian Conservation Work. It names the Army Chief of Finance to receive, spend, and account for the funds. It also says Treasury funds will be transferred to the War Department and that spending from the Emergency Conservation Fund will be tracked under Army accounting rules.

6105.s: This order allows Miss Jessie B. Saunders to be appointed to an appropriate position in the Bureau of the Budget without following the civil-service rules. It is recommended by the Director of the Bureau of the Budget.

6106.s: This order exempts two named Library of Congress employees from automatic retirement for age. It applies to Hugh A. Morrison and David E. Roberts, and keeps them from being separated from service until April 30, 1935.

6104.s: This order combines the Cascade National Forest and the Santiam National Forest into one forest called the Willamette National Forest. It says no publicly owned lands will be given national-forest status if they did not already have it, and no publicly owned lands will be removed from national-forest status.

6103.s: This order says certain temporary appointments in the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency may be made without following Civil Service requirements. It applies to appointments made under the March 9, 1933 Act for relief in the national banking emergency.

6102.s: This order prohibits hoarding gold coin, gold bullion, and gold certificates in the continental United States by individuals, partnerships, associations, and corporations. It requires people to turn over most gold they own or later receive to a Federal Reserve Bank or member bank, with exemptions for certain industrial, professional, artistic, collector, foreign government, and licensed transactions. The Treasury Secretary may extend the deadline in cases of hardship and may issue further rules and licenses. Willful violations can lead to fines, prison, or both.

6101.s: This order sets up Emergency Conservation Work to carry out the unemployment relief act. It appoints Robert Fechner as director, creates an advisory council with representatives from four departments, and establishes a $10,000,000 fund in the Treasury. It also says departments may provide supplies, materials, and other services for the work under the President's direction and with reimbursement under his instructions.

6100.s: This order lets certain veterans of the Spanish-American War, including the Boxer Rebellion and the Philippine Insurrection, keep receiving pensions at the rate they were already being paid. It also covers certain widows, children, and dependent parents of deceased World War veterans who were already receiving compensation. Their injuries or deaths are presumed to have happened in the line of duty, but that presumption can be reviewed and overturned.

6099.s: This order makes Veterans Administration files, records, reports, and other papers about claims confidential and privileged. It allows disclosure only in the cases listed, including to the claimant or the claimant’s representative, to a court, to a government agency, or in certain judicial and competency proceedings. It also lets the Administrator release some information, allow inspections by recognized organizations, and set fees for copies and certifications of records. Anyone who wants a copy must apply in writing and say which record is wanted and why.

6098.s: This order sets rules for veterans’ pensions and related benefits under the law. It defines who counts as serving in the military or naval forces, who counts as a veteran of each war, and who counts as a wife, widow, child, mother, or father for benefit claims. It also sets rules for line-of-duty injuries, misconduct, pension limits for some government employees and people living outside the continental United States, and the authority of the Administrator of Veterans’ Affairs over claims, fiduciaries, representatives, and fees.

6097.s: This order sets rules for paying burial and funeral expenses for deceased honorably discharged war veterans. It allows a burial flag in all cases and lets the Veterans' Administration pay up to $75 for burial, funeral, and transportation costs if certain conditions are met. It also says claims must be filed within one year after the veteran's death, and missing information must be sent within six months after the request.

6096.s: This order sets rules for yearly renewable term insurance for veterans. It lets some people convert that insurance into level premium life or endowment insurance, but they must apply within 31 days and send a premium payment. It also allows some payments to continue for matured contracts and certain court judgments, and says other pending or future claims for these benefits will be disallowed.

6095.s: This order authorizes the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs, within available Veterans' Administration facilities, to provide medical, surgical, and dental services to honorably discharged veterans of any war, including the Boxer Rebellion and the Philippine Insurrection. It applies to veterans who have diseases or injuries incurred or made worse in the line of duty during active military or naval service. It also allows the VA to provide needed supplies such as dental appliances, wheelchairs, artificial limbs, trusses, and similar items.

6094.s: This order sets rules for Veterans’ Administration care for honorably discharged veterans of any war, including the Boxer Rebellion and the Philippine Insurrection. It says who may receive domiciliary or hospital care and medical treatment, and it limits care to veterans living within the continental United States or its territories or possessions. It also restricts when clothing, travel costs, and return-of-body expenses may be paid, and it sets limits on pensions for some veterans who are being cared for by the government.

6093.s: This order sets a rule for some Army, Navy, and Marine Corps officers who served during the World War and had applied for retirement under the 1928 law. It says they may keep receiving retirement pay at the monthly rate they were already getting if their disability came from a disease or injury, or a worsening of a preexisting condition, that happened in the line of duty. It also requires that the person entered active service between April 6, 1917, and November 1, 1918, and that the disease or injury came directly from military or naval duty.

6092.s: This order says certain veterans’ compensation and pension claims are not subject to title I of Public Law 2 if they are already based on a finding that the injury or disease was directly connected to military or naval service. It still allows changes to the disability rate, the time of entry into active service, or payment based on a statutory allowance. It also says this protection does not apply when service connection comes from a statutory or regulatory presumption.

6090.s: This order sets rules for when disability and death pensions start, change, or stop for veterans and their families. It says claims must be filed with the Veterans' Administration, and some claims can be reviewed on appeal once. It also sets rules for who may receive unpaid pension amounts after a person dies, including widows, children, and the person who paid burial expenses.

6089.s: This order sets rules for pensions for veterans and their dependents. It covers disability or death linked to active military or naval service in the Spanish-American War, Boxer Rebellion, Philippine Insurrection, World War, and other service periods, and it also covers some permanent total disabilities not caused by service. It lists who may qualify, how disability is measured, and the monthly pension amounts for veterans and surviving widows, children, and dependent parents.

6091.s: This order directs the Administrator of Veterans’ Affairs to use a schedule of disability ratings for injuries or combinations of injuries. The ratings are to be based, as far as practicable, on average loss of earning capacity in civilian jobs. The schedule must have five grades of disability and be used to set pension payments.

6088.s: This order exempts Harry O. Bailey, superintendent of meters in the District of Columbia under the Office of the Architect of the Capitol, from the rule that would automatically separate him from service at retirement age. The exemption lasts until March 31, 1935.

6084.s: This order reorganizes federal agencies that handle farm credit. It changes the Federal Farm Board into the Farm Credit Administration and moves many farm loan and agricultural credit functions under it.
