It also transfers related records, property, personnel, and funds, and directs the governor of the new agency to handle staff changes and further reorganizations.

6086.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had established the Rio Grande Reservation in New Mexico for the protection of native birds. It reserves certain land and water in Socorro and Sierra Counties for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and wild animals, subject to uses by the Bureau of Reclamation and valid existing rights. It also makes it unlawful within the reservation to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds, or to damage natural growth or United States property.

6087.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in two townships in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while a resurvey is pending and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6085.s: This order announces cost of living index figures for the six months ending June 30, 1928, and the six months ending December 31, 1932. It says the 1932 index was lower than the 1928 base period by 21.7 percent. Because that drop was above the maximum allowed, it sets a 15 percent reduction for the compensation of officers and employees for the stated period.

6083.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules by adding a new item to Schedule A for the Federal Radio Commission. It creates one Secretary position for the Federal Radio Commission.

6082.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in a township in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in place until the township is resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6081.s: This order withdraws 20 acres of public land in California for camp-ground purposes. It says the land is for use by the general public, subject to the listed laws and any valid existing right.

6080.s: This order lets the proper state or local authority appoint an official to conserve the assets of a Federal Reserve member bank if the bank has not been licensed by the Secretary of the Treasury to resume normal banking. The appointment can be made when the authority thinks it is needed to protect the bank’s assets for depositors or other creditors. It also says the bank may not reopen for its usual and normal functions until it gets a Treasury license.

6079.s: This order designates Mrs. Helen V. McLeod of the General Land Office to sign land patents when the clerk usually assigned to do that job is absent. It affects the Department of the Interior’s land patent signing process.

6078.s: This order designates Mrs. Leafie E. Dietz to sign the President’s name on land patents. She had been appointed by the Secretary of the Interior as a clerk to sign land patents, and this order makes that role official as required by law.

6077.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It applies while the township is being resurveyed and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6076.s: The order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It applies to the listed townships and stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it. It is in place pending a resurvey of those townships.

6075.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It applies until the township is resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6074.s: This order amends the civil-service rules to add certain jobs to the list of positions excepted from examination. It covers one executive assistant to the Postmaster General, one special assistant to the Postmaster General, one private secretary or confidential clerk to the Assistant Attorney General, and one to the purchasing agent of the Post Office Department.

6073.s: This order lets the Secretary of the Treasury and state banking authorities allow banks to reopen and carry on their usual banking functions under rules they set. Banks in the Federal Reserve System must apply for a license through the Federal Reserve Banks, and those banks act for the Secretary in receiving applications and issuing licenses. It also restricts the export or withdrawal of gold coin, gold bullion, and gold certificates, limits gold payouts and currency withdrawals for hoarding, and controls certain foreign exchange transactions.

6072.s: This order transfers control of Buildings Nos. 1113, 1409, and 1411 at Cristobal in the Canal Zone from the War Department to the Navy Department. The transfer is under the same conditions as before, with the sites excluded but free use of the sites included.

6071.s: This order allows August A. Gennerich to be appointed as an operative in the Secret Service Division of the Treasury Department without following the civil-service rules. It affects that appointment and the Treasury Department.

10937.s: This order amends the rules for the National Agricultural Advisory Commission. It says the commission is to have twenty-five members appointed by the President, with no more than fifteen from one political party and at least eighteen who are representative farmers. It also sets the terms of the members and says the President will designate the chairman.

10968.s: This order changes the rules for the President's Committee for Traffic Safety. It says the committee may have no more than eighteen members appointed by the President from certain fields, and it adds the Secretaries of Defense, Commerce, Labor, and Health, Education, and Welfare as ex officio members.

10826.s: This order lets the Civil Service Commission grant a benefit to a Federal employee or former Federal employee who met the requirements for an Executive order benefit but lost it because an agency failed to make a timely determination or recommendation. The benefit can be granted only after the required agency action is made, and it does not take effect before the grant date. It also says that getting this benefit does not give a person a right to appeal a reduction-in-force or other personnel action already made effective before the agency is notified. It revokes Executive Order No. 10535.

10834.s: This order sets the design of the flag of the United States, including red and white stripes and white stars on a blue field. It also sets rules for the sizes and use of flags and union jacks by executive agencies. The flag in use under Executive Order 10798 stays official until July 4, 1960, when this order’s flag becomes the official flag of the United States.

10763.s: This order changes the procedure for sharing information about United States citizens who are employed or being considered for employment on the Secretariat of the United Nations. It directs the Secretary of State to send the information to the United States Civil Service Commission, which must do a full background investigation. If the investigation turns up derogatory information, the Commission must send it to the Federal Bureau of Investigation for a full field investigation. For short-term employees whose employment does not exceed ninety days, the investigation does not need to include some of the listed sources.

10692.s: This order changes how the United States members of the Joint Mexican-United States Defense Commission are chosen. It says the Army, Navy, and Air Force members will be designated by the Secretary of Defense, who will also pick the chairman and may name alternate members. It also says the order does not end the terms of anyone already serving on the United States section of the Commission, but the Secretary of Defense may end those terms.

10666.s: This order restores a parcel of land at Humuula, North Hilo, Hawaii, to the possession, use, and control of the Government of the Territory of Hawaii. The land had been set aside for a V. H. F. Link Station under the Civil Aeronautics Administration, but that agency said it was no longer needed for that purpose. The restored land is described as part of the Government (Crown) Land of Humuula and contains 0.92 acre.

10762.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense the President’s authority to order certain reserve members in medical, dental, or allied specialist categories to active duty for up to 24 consecutive months, with or without their consent. It applies to members who have not reached the thirty-fifth anniversary of their birth and who have not done at least one year of active duty other than for training. It also lets the Secretary of Defense set rules for the appointment, reappointment, or promotion of qualified people ordered to active duty as physicians, dentists, or allied specialists. It revokes Executive Order No. 10478, as amended by Executive Order No. 10658.

10622.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Railway Express Agency, Inc. and some of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For that period, and for thirty days after the report is made, the company and its employees may not change the working conditions tied to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

10594.s: This order changes several Selective Service rules. It adds rules about advisors to registrants, possession and replacement of registration papers, and how local boards mail classification notices and review a registrant’s classification after active duty. It also changes the list of medical and physical conditions used in classification and the rules for some U.S. citizens outside the United States.

10589.s: This order changes the membership of the Quetico-Superior Committee. It appoints or keeps Charles S. Kelly, Ernest C. Oberholtzer, and Paul Clement on the committee. The two other committee members will still be chosen by the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of the Interior and serve at their pleasure.

10500.s: This order names the Power Authority of the State of New York as the U.S. designee for building the works for power development in the International Rapids Section of the St. Lawrence River. It also sets up the United States Section of the St. Lawrence River Joint Board of Engineers, with two members from the Department of the Army and the Federal Power Commission. The U.S. section is to work with the Canadian section to review and approve plans and construction programs and to help ensure the works are built as approved.

10392.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Immigration and Naturalization in the Executive Office of the President. The commission must study U.S. immigration and naturalization policies and recommend legislative, administrative, or other action to the President. It must look at admission, naturalization, denaturalization, exclusion, deportation, the national origin quota system, and the effect of these laws on foreign policy. All federal executive departments and agencies are directed to help the commission, and the commission ends 30 days after its final report.

10171.s: This order moves the United States responsibilities and obligations for the occupation of Austria to the Department of State, along with related funds and property. It keeps the United States High Commissioner for Austria as the top U.S. authority in Austria and the chief of the U.S. diplomatic mission, under the Secretary of State. It also keeps certain military matters under direct instructions from the Joint Chiefs of Staff and lets the Commanding General take needed steps to protect U.S. interests, troops, and personnel in Austria.

10131.s: This order designates the Displaced Persons Commission to make or prepare investigations and written reports on the character, history, and eligibility of eligible displaced persons and persons of German ethnic origin seeking admission into the United States. It also directs the Department of State, the Department of the Army, and other agencies to help the Commission when asked. The order took effect at once and replaced Executive Order No. 10003.

10165.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate a dispute between the Railway Express Agency, Inc. and certain of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. From the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, neither the company nor its employees may change the conditions that led to the dispute, except by agreement.

10099.s: This order gives the Secretary of State authority to carry out most of the powers under the Mutual Defense Assistance Act of 1949. The Secretary of State must work with the Secretary of Defense and the Administrator for Economic Cooperation when directing these programs. Aid to recipient countries must follow approved programs, and military stocks cannot be transferred if the Secretary of Defense says it would hurt national security or if the items are needed for reserve training. The Secretary of State may also assign funds to government agencies to carry out these programs.

10063.s:
This order says that, while he serves as United States High Commissioner for Germany, Mr. John J. McCloy will represent the Administrator for Economic Cooperation and the United States Special Representative for Europe in matters involving Germany. He is to work under the Administrator’s immediate supervision, with consultation and ultimate direction by the President.

It also says Mr. McCloy will be helped by a Chief of Special Mission appointed by the Administrator for Economic Cooperation and acceptable to Mr. McCloy. That person will have the rank of Minister and will serve under Mr. McCloy’s immediate supervision and direction.

10052.s: This order enlarges Naval Petroleum Reserve No. 1 to include certain public and private lands in Kern County, California. It withdraws the public lands in those areas from appropriation under the public land laws, including the mining and mineral-leasing laws, and reserves them as part of the naval petroleum reserve. It also revokes part of a 1948 public land order for the lands covered by this order.

10047.s: This order restores a tract of land at Honolulu Harbor, including Piers 5 and 5-A, to the jurisdiction of the Territory of Hawaii. The land is on the west side of Ala Moana Boulevard in Honolulu, Oahu, and includes all improvements on it. The order says the area is no longer needed by the United States for military or naval purposes.

9965.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between National Airlines, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International, and the International Association of Machinists. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report is made, no change may be made by National Airlines, Inc. or its employees in the conditions out of which the disputes arose, except by agreement.

9940.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Railway Express Agency, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, Chauffeurs, Warehousemen and Helpers of America, AFL. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the company and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

9901.s: This order appoints James P. Davis, who was Director of the Division of Territories and Island Possessions in the Department of the Interior, as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration. He is to serve without extra compensation and take over the duties and authority of that office. The order also amends earlier executive orders to reflect this change.

9844.s: This order names the United States Mission to the United Nations and includes the U.S. representative, deputy representative, and other U.N. representatives and their staffs. It makes the U.S. Representative at the United Nations the Chief of Mission in charge of the mission. The Chief of Mission is responsible for coordinating the mission and for its administration, including personnel, budget, and spending, with some limits for the Military Staff Committee.

9773.s: This order revokes an earlier order about the U.S.S. Lafayette, also called the Ex-Normandie. It directs the United States Maritime Commission to dispose of the ship under the Merchant Marine Act and other laws for selling vessels. The ship had been taken over by the United States, and the Navy Department had possession and control of it before it was declared surplus.

9695.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 9243, which dealt with the transfer and release of federal personnel. It says the revocation does not change any reemployment rights already gained under certain other executive orders and directives. It also lets the Civil Service Commission make rules and procedures to protect those reemployment rights and carry out Executive Order No. 9063.

9640.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate a dispute between Railway Express Agency, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, Chauffeurs, Warehousemen, and Helpers of America. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, Railway Express Agency, Inc. and its employees may not change the conditions out of which the dispute arose unless they agree to do so.

9627.s: This order changes the membership of the Advisory Board on Just Compensation. It replaces Judge John J. Parker with Judge Joseph C. Hutcheson, Jr., Judge Charles E. Clark, and Justice Irwin Untermyer. It also says the time period in the earlier order starts on the date of this order.

9549.s: This order lets two named employees of the General Land Office sign the President’s name on land patents. Mrs. Ruth W. Talley is the principal signer, and Mrs. Alice M. Grove is the alternate.

9598.s: This order changes the rules for when a person can get classified civil-service status. It says a person must have been regularly selected for appointment from a Civil Service Commission certificate and entered on duty, or meet the listed older appointment conditions and record requirements. It also says this order replaces Executive Order No. 9506, but does not replace or change Executive Order No. 9538.

9469.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to take possession of and operate the mines, collieries, and preparation facilities of the Philadelphia and Reading Coal and Iron Company in Pennsylvania, along with related property and assets. It says this is because strikes, threatened strikes, and other labor disturbances were interrupting production and could delay the war effort. The Secretary must operate the facilities under the terms then in effect, protect employees as needed to maintain production, and work with other federal agencies. Possession must end after the Secretary decides production efficiency has been restored to its earlier level.

9461-A.s: This order designates and authorizes A. Cecil Snyder to serve as Acting Judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico. He may do this during the judge’s absence, illness, or other legal disability for the current calendar year, and he will receive no extra compensation. It also says this does not affect the case of United States v. Julio Trinidad Geigel.

9402.s: This order lets Dr. R. R. Sayers, the Director of the Bureau of Mines in the Department of the Interior, perform the duties of certain top Interior Department offices when directed by the Secretary of the Interior. He may act as the Under Secretary, First Assistant Secretary, or Assistant Secretary during the absence or sickness of the person holding that office.

9384.s: This order requires executive branch departments and other covered government offices to keep updated long-range programs for public works and improvement projects they plan to fund. It also requires them to submit those programs, related budget estimates, and certain reports to the Bureau of the Budget, and to include the Bureau's advice when reporting to Congress. It applies to a broad set of executive agencies and the District of Columbia government, but not the legislative or judicial branches.

9225.s: The Secretary of War is authorized to take possession of and operate the S.A. Woods Machine Company plant in South Boston, Massachusetts. The plant may be used to produce war materials for the company’s contracts with the United States or as needed for the war effort. The Secretary of War may hire needed employees, including a civilian advisor on industrial relations. This control will end when the President decides the plant can be privately operated in a way that is consistent with the war effort.

9098.s: This order changes a prior order that had withdrawn certain public lands in California for use by the War Department as an anti-aircraft firing range. It removes the listed lands from that withdrawal, except for the main access road crossing those lands. The roads named in the order are kept within the area affected.

9079.s: The order lets the Federal Security Administrator admit insane persons, except those from the District of Columbia, to Public Health Service Hospitals in Lexington, Kentucky, and Fort Worth, Texas, for care and treatment. It also lets the administrator transfer some of those patients from St. Elizabeth's Hospital to those hospitals. The government agency responsible for each patient must pay the same amount it would pay for care at St. Elizabeth's Hospital, and the order stays in force during the war and for six months after it ends.

8959.s: This order designates Mrs. Ruth W. Talley, an employee of the General Land Office, to sign the President’s name to land patents. It also revokes Executive Order No. 7703.

8946.s: This order allows James M. Bayles, John J. Bowe, James P. Boyce, Arthur E. Kelly, John F. Leganey, and Charles W. Moore to be appointed to classified guard positions in the Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency. They may be appointed without following the Civil Service Rules.

8955.s: This order extends the Classification Act of 1923 to certain positions in the War Department and the Navy Department outside the States and the District of Columbia. It applies to jobs filled by citizens of the United States that are needed for national-defense projects in Alaska, British Guiana, Trinidad, Antigua, St. Lucia, Jamaica, Bermuda, the Bahamas, and Newfoundland. It also establishes a salary differential for those positions and says it does not apply after June 30, 1943.

8937.s: This order says time spent in the military or naval forces of the United States after May 1, 1940, will not count against the eligibility period for certain people on Civil Service Commission eligible registers or reemployment or replacement lists. It applies to people who entered active military or naval service while on those lists, or who became eligible during that service. Those people must notify the Civil Service Commission within 40 days after their service ends if they want the benefit of this order.

8765.s: This order allows Alexander M. Knauss to be appointed as a Junior Historical Aide at the Vanderbilt Mansion National Historic Site in the National Park Service. It lets the appointment be made without following the usual Civil Service Rules.

8888.s: This order appoints Guy J. Swope as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration. He is to serve without extra pay and carry out the functions, duties, and authority of that office. It also amends earlier executive orders to reflect the change.

8653.s: This order allows Mrs. Florence Bankhead of Alabama to be appointed as Chief of the National Memorials and Historic Sites Section in the National Park Service. It says she may be appointed without following the Civil Service Rules.

8568.s: This order creates the St. Lawrence Advisory Committee to advise the President on matters listed in the order. It directs the Federal Power Commission and the Army Corps of Engineers to do preliminary studies on navigation and hydroelectric power in the International Rapids Section of the St. Lawrence River, including dam site work, land surveys, title checks, and preliminary plans. It also requires periodic reports to the President and cooperation with Canadian government agencies.

8521.s: This order revokes part of Executive Order No. 4203 for one described tract of public land in California. The land is in the Mt. Diablo Meridian, T. 9 N., R. 13 E., section 9, NW¼NW¼, 40 acres. It affects the public lands covered by that earlier withdrawal in California.

8485.s: This order allows Peres D. Ziegler to be appointed as a rural letter carrier in the Postal Service without meeting the Civil Service Rules requirements. It applies to Mr. Ziegler, who is described as a former crew member of the U.S.S. Panay. The order says he was injured in the line of duty in the bombing and sinking of that vessel.

8467.s: This order changes a prior executive order about the competitive classified civil service. It directs the United States Civil Service Commission to set up a Council of Personnel Administration and name its members and chair. The council must advise the President and the Commission on the merit system, recommend changes in rules and procedures, and may hold hearings and conduct investigations when directed. It also revokes Executive Order No. 5612 of April 25, 1931.

8464.s: This order allows Mrs. Gertrude S. Cooper to be appointed as Superintendent of the Vanderbilt Mansion National Historic Site in the National Park Service. It says the appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

8466.s: This order allows Leland L. Tolman and H. Fred Martin, Jr. to be appointed to legal positions in the Administrative Office of the United States Courts without following the Civil Service Rules. It affects those two people and the hiring rules for those positions.

8418.s: This order allows Mrs. Jeanette M. Priester to be appointed to a classified clerk job at the Navy Yard in Washington, D.C. It says the appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules. It also says she is the widow of Alfred Charles Priester, who died in the line of duty when the U.S.S. Squalus sank.

8356.s: This order sets rules for who takes precedence among Foreign Service officers and other U.S. government officers at diplomatic missions, ceremonies, receptions, and some international conferences. It lays out the ranking of chiefs of mission, counselors, attaches, consuls, and certain medical officers in relation to one another. It also revokes an earlier executive order from 1927.

8341.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 8323. That earlier order had abolished Customs Collection District No. 43 in Tennessee, removed Memphis, Chattanooga, and Nashville as customs ports of entry, and extended two other customs districts to include Tennessee and Arkansas.

8323.s: This order changes the customs field organization. It abolishes Customs Collection District No. 43 in Tennessee and revokes the customs port of entry designations for Memphis, Chattanooga, and Nashville. It also extends Customs Collection District No. 42 to include Tennessee and Customs Collection District No. 45 to include Arkansas.

8288.s: This order changes the customs service field organization in Texas. It moves the headquarters of Customs Collection District No. 23 from San Antonio to Laredo, renames it the Laredo Customs Collection District, and keeps San Antonio as a customs port of entry. It revokes Fort Worth as a customs port of entry and moves several parts of Texas counties to Customs Collection District No. 22 in Galveston.

8201.s: This order changes an earlier order about land in the Virgin Islands. It transfers a tract at Lindbergh Bay, St. Thomas, from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of the Navy. The land is to be used for the establishment, construction, and operation of aviation facilities at the Naval Air Station, St. Thomas, subject to valid existing rights.

7964.s: This order sets rules for citizens of other American republics to apply for instruction at certain schools and educational institutions run by the U.S. government. It says applications must go through diplomatic channels, and the Secretary of State must send them to the proper department or agency for advice. The order also limits how many such permissions may be granted and says they must not reduce admission opportunities for eligible U.S. citizens.

8088.s: This order revokes two earlier orders that had withdrawn public lands in California and Nevada pending a resurvey. It applies to the remaining lands covered by those orders, except certain lands in Nevada described in T. 26 S., R. 58 E. of the Mount Diablo meridian, and it takes effect when the plats of the resurveys are officially filed.

7943.s: This order allows Edgar C. Faris, Jr., William B. Roberts III, and Leonard W. Mosby to stay in their jobs in the office of the Secretary of the National Bituminous Coal Commission. It says they may continue without following Civil Service Rules and without getting classified status.

7920.s: This order allows Mrs. Irene M. Mori to be appointed to a classified Government position without following the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of Alfred H. Mori, who served in the War Department and died on December 18, 1937, leaving his widow and two children without adequate means of support.

7820.s: This order exempts Dr. J. Davis Bradfield from the rule that requires automatic retirement at a certain age. It lets him stay in service until March 1, 1939. It affects Dr. Bradfield and the Health Department of the Government of the District of Columbia.

7737.s: This order allows Mrs. Mary G. Bird to be appointed to a classified position in the Farm Credit Administration without following the Civil Service Rules. It says she would have become eligible for civil service status under Executive Order No. 6758 if she had not been appointed to an excepted position in the Farm Credit Administration on June 1, 1934.

7736.s: This order changes an earlier rule so that an officer or employee of the Municipality of St. Thomas and St. John or the Municipality of St. Croix in the Virgin Islands may be appointed as an Immigration Inspector for the Virgin Islands. It affects those municipal officers and employees and the Immigration Inspector position.

7731.s: This order names Honorable Martin Travieso to act as judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico for the trial of United States v. Julio Pinto Gandia and others. He is authorized to perform the judge’s duties and sign papers, records, and orders needed for the case. The order says this is because Judge Robert A. Cooper is a necessary witness for the Government in the trial and cannot act as judge in that case.

7600.s: This order changes the fees in the United States consular fee schedule for passport and related services. It sets fees for passport applications, passport issuance, renewal, registration, and certain copies or affidavits, and it gives no-fee exceptions for some U.S. officers and employees, seamen, and certain family members visiting the graves of American soldiers, sailors, or marines buried abroad.

7572.s: This order changes an earlier executive order that moved lands between the Roosevelt, Pike, and Arapaho National Forests in Colorado. It keeps certain lands in Clear Creek County from being transferred from the Pike to the Arapaho National Forest and restores those lands to their prior forest status. It also changes one land description from "SE¼" to "SW¼" for Section 32, T. 5 S., R. 71 W.

7559.s: This order revokes part of a 1931 order that had withdrawn public lands in one township in Wyoming while a resurvey was pending. It affects the public lands in that township under the Sixth Principal Meridian. The order takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey for that township is filed.

7488.s: This order names Louis N. Robinson as Chairman of the Prison Industries Reorganization Board. It replaces Joseph N. Ulman in that role and amends Executive Order No. 7202 accordingly.

7479.s: This order directs Dr. W. C. Mendenhall, the Director of the Geological Survey, to perform the duties of the Secretary of the Interior when certain Interior Department officials are absent or sick. It applies to the Secretary of the Interior, the Under Secretary, the First Assistant Secretary, and the Assistant Secretary, and it also modifies Executive Order No. 7277.

7443.s: This order changes the land description in a prior proclamation that established the Talladega National Forest in Alabama. It replaces one listed section with another in the Huntsville Meridian description. The change affects the land described in that proclamation.

7412.s: This executive order changes the land description in the proclamation that established the Bienville National Forest in Mississippi. It changes one tract’s location from T. 7 N., R. 8 W., Choctaw, Meridian, to T. 7 N., R. 8 E., Choctaw, Meridian.

7392.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6014, which had withdrawn public lands in a township in Oregon while a resurvey was pending. It becomes effective when the official filing of the plat of resurvey for that township is made.

7349.s: This order modifies the 1926 reservoir site reserve so the Federal Power Commission can issue an amendment to a license for Project No. 966 on certain lands near a transmission line. If those lands are needed for reservoir purposes, the licensee must remove its project works at its own expense within thirty days after notice from the Secretary of the Interior. It also revokes Executive Order No. 5906, which had authorized a license for Project No. 1209.

7306.s: This order allows Mrs. Hilda McTeer to be appointed to a job in the classified civil service without following the normal civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of a former Treasury Department employee who died in 1935, leaving her and a minor child without enough support. It also says she had served for several years in temporary Treasury Department jobs.

7290.s: This order revokes part of Executive Order No. 5790 for a township in New Mexico, which had withdrawn public lands there pending resurvey. It becomes effective when the official plat of resurvey for that township is filed.

7294.s: This order waives a civil-service time limit so Mrs. Nell J. Kline may be reinstated to a clerical position in the Postal Service. It affects Mrs. Kline, who was a former Postal Service employee and the widow of a Post Office Inspector.

7227.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn public lands in T. 15 N., R. 15 E. of the Mount Diablo meridian in California. The revocation takes effect when the official plat of resurvey for that township is filed.

7253.s: This order allocates federal funds to the Secretary of the Interior to acquire and develop a historic site on the west bank of the Mississippi River near old St. Louis, Missouri. The site is to be developed and preserved through the National Park Service for the purposes named in the 1935 act. The City of St. Louis must make its agreed contribution available before the full amount may be spent.

7216.s: This order lets Mrs. Ella W. Budge be appointed to a position in the Bureau of Public Roads in the Department of Agriculture without following the civil-service rules. It applies to her appointment only. The order says she is the widow of a government employee, has three small children, and does not have enough means of support.

7109.s: This order waives the maximum age limit for entrance to certain civil-service examinations for two employees. It lets them compete for the positions of chief engineman and watchman in custodial service, where they had been serving under temporary appointments.

7100-A.s: This order allows Mrs. Ina E. Swartz to be appointed to a clerical position in the Department of Agriculture without following the civil-service rules. Mrs. Swartz is the widow of Rexford K. Swartz, who served for 22 years in that department. The Secretary of Agriculture recommended this order.

7024-B.s: This order creates the Federal Petroleum Agency No. 1. The agency is set up to investigate tender applications and report to Federal Tender Board No. 1. Its representatives may present evidence, examine witnesses, and administer oaths and affirmations.

7011.s: This order allows Mrs. Anna Jewell Murray to be appointed to a clerical job in the Treasury Department without meeting the civil-service rules. It applies to that appointment in the Treasury Department. The order says Mrs. Murray is the widow of Arthur H. Murray, who worked there for 23 years.

6993.s: This order reconstitutes the National Industrial Recovery Board. It keeps A. D. Whiteside, Sidney Hillman, Leon C. Marshall, and Walton Hamilton on the board, appoints William P. Witherow and Philip Murray, and names Donald R. Richberg as a member and acting chairman after S. Clay Williams retires. It also changes any earlier orders on the same subject as needed to make this order work.

6963.s: This order cancels Paragraph XI of Executive Order No. 6098, as amended by Executive Order No. 6234. It changes Veterans Regulation No. 10 under the authority named in the order. It affects the regulation for veterans.

6947.s: This order allows Mrs. Carmen B. Knox to be appointed as a clerk in the Post Office Department without following the civil-service rules. It applies to her personally and affects a job in the classified service. The order says she is the widow of James H. Knox and had prior service as a translator and typist in the American postal agency at Bordeaux, France.

6941.s: This order lets Mrs. Hannah Curtis be appointed as an under clerk in the Bureau of Supplies and Accounts of the Navy Department in Washington, D.C. It says the appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules. It also says she is the widow of a former chief clerk of the Navy Department and that the order was issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Navy.

6937.s: This order allows Mrs. Anna E. McGurty to be appointed as a clerk in the New York, New York, Post Office without following the civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of Peter A. McGurty and does not have adequate means of support.

6915.s: This order changes the membership of the National Longshoremen's Labor Board. It appoints O. K. Cushing as chairman and Captain Edward MacCauley as a member. It also says the chairman and members may receive travel and subsistence expenses, and most of them will receive a daily payment.

6870.s: This order allows Mrs. Era I. Sexton to be appointed as inspectress of customs in San Antonio, Texas, without following the civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of Harry L. Sexton and has three young children without enough means of support. It also says she is represented as qualified for the job.

6633.s: This order allows Mr. F. Harry Lewis to be appointed as an examiner of merchandise in the Customs Service in New York without following Civil Service Rule II. Mr. Lewis has served in the Customs Service since 1913 as a Chinese interpreter. The order says he can translate and classify Chinese and Japanese invoices and has helped examiners with those documents.

6722.s: The order sets rules for how alien seamen may enter the United States. Some bona fide alien seamen may be admitted temporarily without passports or visas in certain cases, and other alien seamen may use passport visas, transit certificates, or group transit certificates. Masters of vessels must submit a visaed list of alien crew members, and an alien seaman not on that list cannot land unless the Secretary of State gives permission.

6631.s: This order lets Mr. Robert H. Hartenberger and Mr. James B. Morgan, Jr. be appointed to jobs in the War Department without following Civil Service Rule II. It applies to their appointments as an airplane painter helper and a watchman in the Air Corps at large in San Antonio, Texas.

6557.s: This order waives a civil-service time limit so Mrs. Marie E. Summers can be reinstated to a position in the Government Printing Office. It affects her and the Government Printing Office. Mrs. Summers formerly worked there as a pressfeeder and is the widow of Robert W. Summers.

6550.s: This order requires most federal departments, agencies, and government-owned corporations to send the Director of the Budget weekly reports on allocations and obligations made from emergency funds. The reports must itemize money allocated and obligations incurred, including through the issuance of securities. It does not apply to the regular appropriation for the Department of State’s “Emergencies Arising in the Diplomatic and Consular Service,” and it revokes Executive Order No. 6548.

6540.s: This order delays certain transfers, consolidations, and eliminations set out in Executive Order No. 6166. It also delays other related parts of that order until June 30, 1934, unless the Secretary of the Treasury, with the President's approval, makes them effective earlier. It affects the government offices and functions covered by those sections.

6490.s: This order revokes a previous order that had withdrawn certain public lands in New Mexico pending resurvey. It applies to the lands in T. 16 N., R. 11 E. of the New Mexico principal meridian.

6404.s: This order revokes part of a 1918 executive order that created Oil-Shale Reserve No. 1 in Nevada. It affects the listed lands in Mount Diablo Meridian, Township 34 North, Range 56 East, section 19, lots 1, 2, and 3.

6346.s: This order denies the exemption request made by Greensboro Lumber Company and H. A. Taylor. They had asked to be exempt from the minimum wage in the Code of Fair Competition for the Lumber and Timber Products Industries. The order says their application did not show a case of injustice and extreme hardship that would require special treatment.

6218.s: This order allows David A. Gates to be appointed as an Internal Revenue Agent in the Treasury Department without following the civil-service rules for one year. The position he would fill is withdrawn from those rules during his time in office. It affects Mr. Gates and the Internal Revenue Service.

6217.s: This order allows James J. Maloney, John E. Murphy, Roy G. Perry, and Albert R. Vaughan to be permanently appointed as operatives in the Secret Service Division of the Treasury Department. It says this can be done without following the civil-service rules. The order applies to these four men and their jobs in the Secret Service Division.

6229.s: This order changes Veterans Regulation No. 1 (a) to say that, except for listed exceptions, no pension is payable for permanent disability less than total disability. It also adds a rule that Spanish-American War veterans who meet the listed requirements shall be paid a pension of not less than $15 per month.

6193.s: This order revokes a previous order that had withdrawn certain public lands in New Mexico pending a resurvey. It affects the public lands in T. 15 N., R. 18 W. of the New Mexico principal meridian.

6192.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in a township in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it, while the township is resurveyed.

6151.s: This order revokes a previous order that had withdrawn certain public lands in New Mexico pending a resurvey. It affects the public lands in Tps. 11 S., Rs. 14 and 15 E. of the New Mexico principal meridian.

6138.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5166 from 1929. It affects the public lands in Tps. 13 N., Rs. 16 and 17 E. of the Mount Diablo meridian in California that had been withdrawn pending a resurvey.

6070.s: This order allows Mrs. Mary A. McClung to be appointed to an appropriate position in the Department of Agriculture without following Civil Service rules. It applies to Mrs. McClung and the Department of Agriculture.

6114.s: This order allows Mrs. May Cairns Aimone to be appointed to a clerical job in the classified service without following the civil-service rules. It applies to Mrs. Aimone, the widow of Dr. Victor A. Aimone. The order says it was issued on the recommendation of the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs.

6069.s: This order allows John M. Hooe to be permanently appointed as a marine gasoline engineer, qualified as an airplane pilot, on the force of the Collector of Customs at Buffalo, New York. It waives the civil-service rules for this appointment and says he has been serving in a temporary appointment in an essential position.

6068.s: This order allows Mrs. Daphne Mary Byrne to be appointed as a clerk-typist in the classified service under the Veterans' Administration. It says she is the widow of a Veterans' Administration employee who died, and it gives the reason stated by the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs.

6067.s: This order allows Thomas H. Allen to be appointed as a special investigator in the Immigration Service of the Department of Labor without following the civil-service rules. It applies to his appointment and says he has rendered highly meritorious service under difficult circumstances.

6066.s: This order keeps Edwin Sheddan Cunningham, a Foreign Service Officer of Class I from Tennessee, on active duty. It allows him to stay in service for as long as needed, but for no more than five years from July 6, 1933.

6065.s: This order reserves land in Nevada and Arizona as a refuge and breeding ground for wild birds and animals. It puts the area under the use of the Department of Agriculture as the Boulder Canyon Wild Life Refuge. It bars hunting, trapping, disturbing, or killing wild birds or animals, taking nests or eggs, cutting or burning natural growth, leaving fires unattended, and damaging U.S. property. It also says people may enter or use the reservation only under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

6064.s: This order rescinds Executive Order No. 5143, which had restricted the transportation of passengers from certain ports in the Orient to a United States port. It says the unusual prevalence of epidemic cerebrospinal meningitis infection in the Orient has subsided and that ordinary quarantine procedures at United States ports of arrival can now control the danger.

6063.s: This order allows Miss Ellen T. Purcell and Miss J. Elizabeth Williams to be appointed to classified positions in the Department of Labor without following the civil-service rules. It applies to these two women and concerns their jobs in the Department of Labor.

6062.s: This order allows Ruby Mae Webb to be appointed as a rural letter carrier in the classified service without following the civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of a former rural letter carrier, is qualified for the job, and has been serving the route as a temporary carrier since her husband died.

6061.s: This order allows Joseph Gambaro and Solomon Israel to be appointed as special investigators in the Immigration Service of the Department of Labor without following the civil-service rules. It applies only to these two people and the jobs they may be appointed to.

6060.s: This order directs that the records, files, and other papers of the President's Emergency Committee and the President's Organization for Unemployment Relief be transferred to the Department of Commerce. The Department of Commerce must keep and preserve them until a building for permanent Government records is finished. Then it must deliver those records to that building and to the official in charge.

6059.s: This order allows Irvin S. Goldbarth to be appointed as a Clerk in the Custodian Service at the Federal Building in Richmond, Virginia. It says this appointment may be made without following the Civil Service rules.

6058.s: This order allows Mrs. Jessie N. Barber to be reinstated in the classified service and appointed to a clerical position in the General Accounting Office. It says this can be done without regard to civil service requirements related to apportionment. It applies to Mrs. Barber, who is named in the order.

6057.s: This order allows Clara L. Hess to be appointed in the classified civil service without following civil-service rules. It applies to her position in the Post Office Department, where she has been serving since March 16, 1927.

6056.s: This order allows G. Harold Keatley of Pennsylvania to be appointed in the classified civil service without following civil-service rules. It affects his position in the Department of State.

6055.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in effect until the land is resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6054.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. It does this while a resurvey of the township is pending. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6053.s: This order changes Reservoir-Site Reserve No. 17 so the City of Pasadena’s application can be approved. It also allows a patent to be issued for the listed lands in California.

6052.s: This order says Mrs. Marie K. Kaley may be appointed an inspectress of customs in the Office of the Collector of Customs at New York without meeting the civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of a former deputy collector of customs, and that she was left without adequate means of support.

6050.s: This order assigns two parcels of land in the Tongass National Forest near Juneau, Alaska, to the Secretary of War for use as a site for an Army radio receiving station. The land was taken from the forest because of a stated military necessity. When the land is no longer used for that purpose, it will return to the Tongass National Forest.

6051.s: This order says that serving on the Colonial Council of St. Thomas and St. John or St. Croix does not bar a person from Federal employment in the Virgin Islands if the council role is unpaid. It also says the head of the department will decide whether the council service interferes with the person's Federal duties.

6049.s: This order allows Milton Harold Powell to be appointed as an apprentice boy (electrician) in the office of the Director of Public Buildings and Public Parks of the National Capital. It says this appointment can be made without following the civil-service rules, and it was issued on the recommendation of that office's director.

6048.s: This order allows Harry E. Timmis to be appointed to the classified service without following civil-service rules. It applies to his position under the Department of Commerce and was issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of Commerce.

6047.s: This order revokes a Civil Service rule that allowed one confidential clerk to be appointed without a competitive examination for the Collector of Customs at New York, if the Secretary of the Treasury approved it. It also says the person holding that job at the time is placed in the classified service with the position.

6046.s: This order changes the civil-service rules for certain jobs at the United States Military Academy that do not have to go through competitive examination. It adds kitchen helpers and waiters to that exempt list. It also includes head and assistant head waiters when they are promoted from waiter positions.

6044.s: This order withdraws and reserves part of Amaknak Island, Alaska, for the protection of the fishing rights of Alaska Natives. It applies subject to any valid existing rights. The reservation stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

6045.s: This order changes the legal description of the Sitka Dock Site in Sitka, Alaska. The site was reserved for use by the Forest Service in connection with the administration of the Tongass National Forest, and the revised area is 2.50 acres, more or less.

6042.s: This order allows Mrs. Grace F. Smythe to be appointed in the classified civil service without following the usual civil-service rules. It applies to her position in the Post Office Department and was issued on the recommendation of the Postmaster General.

6043.s: This order amends Civil Service Rule IX to say that a former classified employee who is entitled to military preference in appointment may be reinstated without a time limit. It applies to former classified employees with military preference. The order says the change is meant to make military-preference benefits uniform.

6040.s: This order withdraws a listed piece of land in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It also reserves that land for public use. The land is described by township, range, and section in the Willamette Meridian.

6041.s: This order allows Mrs. Adelle B. Freeman to be appointed as a junior bacteriologist in the Department of Agriculture without following the civil-service rules. It applies to Mrs. Freeman, who is the widow of George F. Freeman, and it notes that she graduated from Kansas State Agricultural College with a bachelor of science degree.

6039.s: This order revokes two earlier land reservations on Kodiak Island, Alaska, and places those lands under the control of the Secretary of the Interior. It reserves one tract for the War Department to use as a radio station. It also reserves two tracts for the Alaska Game Commission for pasturage and other purposes.

6038.s: This order allows Laurence Gouverneur Hoes to be appointed to a job in the Veterans' Administration without following the civil-service rules. It says the order was issued on the recommendation of the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs.

6037.s: This order allows Miss Alice Mummenhoff to be appointed in the classified civil service without following civil-service rules. It applies to her position in the Post Office Department and is based on the Postmaster General’s recommendation.

6036.s: This order lets Edmond M. Martin be appointed in the classified civil service without following civil-service rules. It applies to Martin, who has been serving in a Post Office Department position excepted from civil-service requirements.

6035.s: This order allows Kenneth C. Macpherson to be appointed in the classified service without following civil-service rules. It applies to his appointment after his work in the Department of Commerce and the Post Office Department.

6034.s: This order allows Joseph A. Kinnahan to be appointed in the classified service without following civil-service rules. It applies to his position in the Post Office Department and was issued on the recommendation of the Postmaster General.

6033.s: This order lets Mrs. Ann F. Kammerer be appointed in the classified service without following civil-service rules. It applies to her work in the Post Office Department.

6032.s: This order allows Isaac Gregg to be appointed to the classified civil service without following civil-service rules. It applies to Gregg, who has been serving in a Post Office Department position excepted from civil-service requirements, and it was issued on the recommendation of the Postmaster General.

6031.s: This order allows Miss Alice W. Goodwin to be appointed in the classified service without following civil-service rules. It applies to her position in the Post Office Department, where she has been serving since September 8, 1924.

6030.s: This order exempts Charles J. James from compulsory retirement because he has reached the retirement age for automatic separation from service. It lets him stay in his job as chief appraiser of the office of the Register of Wills and clerk of the Probate Court, Supreme Court of the District of Columbia, until February 28, 1935.

6029.s: The order places Miss Mary Stewart in the classified service. It applies to her appointment as Assistant Director of Education in the Indian Office, Department of the Interior.

6028.s: This order allows the listed people to be appointed as special investigators in the Immigration Service of the Department of Labor without following the civil-service rules. It affects the named employees in the Department of Labor.

6027.s: This order exempts John Storey, a gardener for Public Buildings and Public Parks of the National Capital, from the automatic retirement age rule. He may stay in service until February 28, 1935.

6026.s: This order allows Mr. Sterling L. Morelock to receive a probational appointment as a guard in the Department of Agriculture without regard to his civil-service register standing. It says he is a disabled veteran of the World War and was awarded the Congressional Medal of Honor and the Order of the Purple Heart.

6025.s: This order withdraws listed public lands in Montana and Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use. The affected land is described by township, range, section, and lot in the order.

6024.s: This order allows Edward N. Dingley, Jr. to be reinstated in an approved vacancy as an associate radio engineer at the Naval Research Laboratory in Bellevue, D.C. It says this can be done without following the rule about the required length of prior service. The order affects Mr. Dingley and the Navy position named in it.

6022-A.s: This order classifies Harry A. McBride, who had been serving as an Assistant to the Secretary of State without a competitive classified status. It affects Mr. McBride and changes the status of his position in the Department of State.

6022.s: This order exempts Ernest F. Moessner, a scale repairer in the Mint of the United States at Denver, from the rule requiring automatic retirement at the retirement age. It keeps him in service until February 28, 1935.

6021.s: This order sets rules for sick leave with pay for civilian officers and employees of the Government, within the limits allowed by law. It says sick leave may be used when a worker is sick or injured, or in some cases when a family member has a contagious disease or the worker was exposed to one. It limits how sick leave is granted, requires notice and proof in many cases, and says the rules do not apply to some Postal Service, Panama Canal, and Foreign Service employees.

6020.s: This order allows Richard H. Knight to be reinstated as a substitute clerk in the New York, N.Y., Post Office. It says this can be done without following the civil-service rules, and it was recommended by the Postmaster General.

6019.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Oregon and Utah from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use. The order affects the listed parcels in the Willamette Meridian in Oregon and the Salt Lake Meridian in Utah.

6018.s: This order gives the Alien Property Custodian the President’s power under the Trading with the Enemy Act over certain money, interest, and property held by the Treasurer of the United States. If that official cannot act, the power goes to the Director of Finance and Accounts, and then to the Chief of the Legal Division. Claims that must go to the Attorney General and the President under a prior order still must be sent there.

6015.s: This order revokes part of a 1910 executive order that had withdrawn certain lands in Montana for coal land purposes. It affects only the specific tracts of land listed in the order.

6017.s: This order changes the consular regulations on office rooms, requiring approval from the Secretary of State before signing a lease or rental agreement and before changing offices in most cases. It also adds the terms of a proposed rental agreement or lease to the required papers. It directs consular officers to carry out certain Veterans' Administration duties in their districts and to supervise those activities. The order also cancels one section and makes several record-keeping changes in the regulations.

6013.s: This order exempts the named people in the Treasury Department from compulsory retirement when they reach the normal retirement age. It keeps them from automatic separation from service until February 28, 1934.

6014.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it, while a resurvey of the township is pending.

6012.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Utah for use as an agricultural range experiment station. The Secretary of Agriculture is to administer the lands under the cited law. It applies to the listed areas and is subject to valid existing rights.

6011.s: This order excludes certain tracts of land in Alaska, occupied as home sites, from the Tongass National Forest. It restores those lands to entry under the applicable public land laws. The order covers home sites in the areas described in the text.

6010.s: This order changes the boundaries of the Fort Randolph and France Field military reservations in the Canal Zone. It reduces the area of Fort Randolph and increases the area of France Field, then gives the new boundary lines for each reservation. The earlier 1920 order stays in effect except as changed here.

6009.s: This order revokes earlier orders that related to San Nicholas Island, California, including one that reserved the island for lighthouse purposes. It places San Nicholas Island under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy for naval uses. It also reserves sites for the Department of Commerce to build and maintain aids to navigation and related facilities.

6007.s: This order allows Carl R. Shepard of Washington, D. C. to be appointed as a junior construction engineer in the Office of the Supervising Architect of the Treasury Department without following the civil-service rules. It affects Mr. Shepard and the Treasury Department office working on a large building program.

6008.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of certain public lands in Colorado that had been held pending a resurvey. It says the lands, if otherwise available, must first be opened under set rules to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws. After that, the lands may be open to the general public under the applicable public land laws, and no one may claim rights by settling there early except as allowed in the order.

6006.s: This order withdraws United States Survey No. 1946 from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for public use as a source of water for domestic purposes in the community of Unalaska.

6005-A.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 3360, which had approved the specifications for an official flag for the office of the Secretary of State. It affects that official flag specification only.

6004.s: This order exempts Oliver M. Maxain, Chief of the Division of Operations in the United States Coast Guard, from the compulsory retirement rule for age. It applies to him because he reaches the retirement age during the current month.

6005.s: This order allows Mrs. Kathleen M. Glancy to be appointed to a clerical position in the Department of Justice without following the civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of John E. Glancy, who worked in that department for more than 24 years and left her and their three young children without means of support.

6003.s: This order classifies Miss Paula Gillespie, who worked in the office of the Assistant Secretary of the Navy as a senior clerk-stenographer. It applies to her and is issued on the recommendation of the Assistant Secretary of the Navy.

6001.s: This order discontinues the United States land offices in Little Rock, Arkansas; Alliance, Nebraska; Cass Lake, Minnesota; and Gainesville, Florida. It moves their business and necessary archives to the General Land Office in Washington, D.C. and consolidates them there.

6002.s: This order withdraws certain public land in Arizona, along with any buildings or structures on it, from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for use by representatives of the Geological Survey to support existing power-site reservations and to maintain and operate gaging stations on the Colorado and Paria Rivers. The order affects the listed land in Gila and Salt River Meridian, including land near the Colorado River.

6000.s: This order allows Mrs. Josephine Horigan to be appointed to a position in the Department of Agriculture without following the civil-service rules. It concerns Mrs. Horigan, the widow of James B. Horigan, who worked for nearly 23 years in the Government service in the Department of Agriculture.

5999.s: This order lets Martha Owczarzak be appointed as a charwoman in the Custodian Service at the Post Office in Bay City, Michigan, without regard to her standing on the Civil Service register for classified laborer, female. It affects Mrs. Owczarzak and her family, including her husband and their four children, who depend on them for support.

5998.s: This order says Charles Gallagher may be appointed to the classified civil service even though he has been serving in a Post Office Department position that was excepted from civil-service requirements. It applies to Charles Gallagher and was issued on the recommendation of the Postmaster General.

5997.s: This order allows Dirrelle Chaney to be appointed in the classified service without following civil-service rules. It applies to Chaney, who has been serving in a position in the Post Office Department excepted from civil-service requirements.

5995.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of public lands in parts of Wyoming that had been set aside pending resurvey. It opens certain unreserved public lands in one township, subject to valid rights, for qualified ex-service men to enter under the homestead or desert land laws for 91 days after the official plat of resurvey is filed. After that period, the lands may be open to the general public under any applicable public land law.

5996.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of public lands in one township in Wyoming that was pending resurvey. After the resurvey plat is officially filed, the unreserved public lands in that township would be open for 91 days to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws, subject to valid rights and the stated rules. After that, the land would be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5993.s: This order designates the customs station of Baton Rouge, Louisiana, as a customs port of entry. It places Baton Rouge in Customs Collection District No. 20, with headquarters at New Orleans, Louisiana, and says the change takes effect 30 days after the order.

5994.s: This order withdraws the land described in it, subject to valid existing rights, while legislation is pending. It applies to the listed parcel in Minnesota. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5992.s: This order allows Charles Carran to be appointed as a rural letter carrier in the classified service. It says he may be appointed without following the civil-service rules.

5991.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Deschutes National Forest to the Fremont National Forest. It also transfers one tract from the Fremont National Forest to the Deschutes National Forest. If some listed tracts later become national-forest lands, they will become part of the Fremont National Forest.

5990.s: This order withdraws a parcel of public land in Colorado and reserves it for use by the Department of Agriculture. It is for the administration of the Cochetopa National Forest and is subject to any valid existing rights.

5989.s: This order exempts Dr. Charles Orrin Townsend, Chief of the Sugar Division of the United States Tariff Commission, from the retirement rule for automatic separation from service. It keeps him in service until January 31, 1934.

5988.s: This order exempts the listed people from the rule that would automatically separate them from service when they reach retirement age during the current month. It applies to Frank Van Vleck of the War Department and Frederick W. Ashley of the Library of Congress.

5987.s: This order revokes a 1927 withdrawal of certain public lands in California that had been set aside for use by the Department of Commerce as air mail beacon sites and landing fields. It applies only to the listed land parcels in the San Bernardino Meridian area. One listed parcel is excepted for 4.16 acres in a patented mineral entry.

5986.s: This order allows James W. Higgins, Jr. to be appointed as a Special Agent in the Internal Revenue Bureau of the Treasury Department without following the civil-service rules. It says he has served as Deputy Collector of Internal Revenue since April 10, 1922, and has gained knowledge and experience for the investigative work of that job.

5985.s: This order revokes part of a 1910 executive order that had withdrawn certain lands in Montana for coal land withdrawal. It applies to the specific townships, ranges, sections, and lots listed in the order. Some of the listed lands are described as outside the Fort Belknap Indian Reservation.

5984.s: This order changes Civil-Service Rule VII on how eligibles are certified for federal job vacancies. It says certifications should be made without regard to sex unless the commission thinks the duties can be performed only by men or only by women.

5983.s: This order revokes part of a 1930 order that had withdrawn certain unreserved islands, rocks, and pinnacles in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California. It applies to those lands south of the mouth of Carmel River and in the vicinity of Point Lobos in California.

5982.s: This order exempts Charles J. Harlow, a plate printer in the Coast and Geodetic Survey of the Department of Commerce, from the retirement rule for automatic separation from service. It lets him stay in his job until March 31, 1933.

5981.s: This order exempts John T. Crowley, a Vocational Advisor at the Veterans' Administration, from automatic separation from service because of retirement age. It keeps him in service until May 31, 1933.

5980.s: This order changes an earlier withdrawal of certain Oregon lands. It authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to withdraw the described land for use by the Department of Commerce to maintain air navigation facilities. The land is subject to an existing power transmission line reservation, and the timber on it may still be sold by the United States under the 1916 law.

5979.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn public lands in Tps. 1 and 2 N., R. 10 E., New Mexico principal meridian, in New Mexico, pending resurveys. It affects those public lands in New Mexico.

5978.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of public lands in a township in San Bernardino meridian, California, pending resurvey. It opens the land, if otherwise subject to disposition, to entry under the homestead or desert land laws only by qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the official resurvey plat is filed. After that period, the land may be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply. No rights may be acquired by settlement before entry except as provided here.

5977.s: This order closes several executive departments and independent Government establishments in the District of Columbia on Saturday, December 24, 1932, and Saturday, December 31, 1932. It also excuses Federal employees in the District of Columbia from duty on those days, except for those excepted for special public reasons or when existing law would not allow them to be absent.

5975.s: The order transfers custody and control of lot 1 of block 40 in Alva, Oklahoma, from the Department of the Interior to the Treasury Department. The lot is to be used as the site of a Federal building.

5976.s: This order withdraws a specific parcel of land in Washington and reserves it for use by the Department of Agriculture as the Greenleaf Mountain lookout site. It is for the administration of nearby national forests and is subject to any valid existing rights. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5974.s: This order changes the civil-service rules for excepted positions under the Treasury Department. It adds employees who work at psittacosis investigation stations, along with people employed at leprosy, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, and yellow fever investigation stations.

5973.s: This order amends the Consular Regulations on citizenship, passports, and passport fees. It says some naturalized citizens living abroad for set periods may be presumed to have lost American nationality unless they provide satisfactory evidence otherwise. It also sets rules for proving citizenship, listing family members on a passport, surrendering old identity papers, and collecting passport fees with certain exceptions.

5971.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Utah that had been set aside pending adjustment of claims. It does not affect the separate withdrawal of those lands for the Bear River Migratory Bird Refuge, which remains in force.

5972.s: This order allows Miss Geraldine Rollins to be appointed as a junior typist in the Bureau of Internal Revenue without following the civil-service rules. It says she is the daughter of John Lester Rollins, who died leaving his widow and daughter with limited resources. It also says she took a stenographic and typing course in high school and that more typists are needed in the bureau.

5970.s: This order says certain income tax returns filed under several revenue laws must be open to inspection. The inspection must follow rules and regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury and approved by the President. It affects the tax returns covered by those listed acts.

5969.s: This order transfers the administrative duties, powers, and authority of the Employees' Compensation Commission to the Civil Service Commission for the program covering compensation for injuries to civilian Federal employees and employees of the District of Columbia government. The Employees' Compensation Commission will serve in an advisory role. It also transfers the related personnel, records, property, and funds to the Civil Service Commission.

5968.s: This order transfers the activities, powers, and duties of the Alien Property Custodian to the Department of Justice. It also moves the related personnel, records, papers, property, and unexpended funds to that department. The Attorney General will get the supervisory and appellate powers that had been given to the Alien Property Custodian.

5967.s: This order transfers to the Department of Justice the Veterans' Administration's duties for defending court cases involving claims under section 19 of the World War Veterans' Act, 1924, as amended. The Veterans' Administration keeps duties related to getting facts, interviewing witnesses, preparing evidence, and gathering materials needed for those cases. It also transfers certain officers, employees, records, property, and funds to the Department of Justice, and other affected employees are dismissed.

5966.s: This order moves the Immigration Border Patrol from the Bureau of Immigration and the Customs Patrol from the Bureau of Customs to the Coast Guard Service in the Treasury Department. It directs the Commandant of the Coast Guard to work toward a unified border patrol, with the Secretary of the Treasury acting with the President's approval. The transferred agencies keep their powers and duties, personnel, records, property, and unused funds.

5965.s: This order creates an Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Merchant Marine and puts that official in charge of merchant-marine work in the Department of Commerce. It transfers several agencies and functions to the Department of Commerce, including parts of the Coast and Geodetic Survey, the Bureau of Navigation and Steamboat Inspection, the United States Shipping Board Merchant Fleet Corporation, the Inland Waterways Corporation, and the Bureau of Lighthouses. It also lets the Secretary of Commerce consolidate, eliminate, or redistribute offices and functions within the department, with the President’s approval.

5964.s: This order changes one Assistant Secretary of the Interior to Assistant Secretary of the Interior for Public Works. It transfers several public works-related offices, boards, commissions, and activities into the Department of the Interior, including reclamation, roads, public buildings, parks, and some rivers and harbors work. It also lets the Secretary of the Interior consolidate, eliminate, or redistribute those offices and their functions with the President’s approval.

5963.s: This order changes the Assistant Secretary of Agriculture role to Assistant Secretary of Agriculture for Land Utilization. It moves the General Land Office from the Department of the Interior to the Department of Agriculture and places several land use and conservation-related offices under that department. It also lets the Secretary of Agriculture, with the President's approval, consolidate, eliminate, or redistribute offices and functions in the department.

5962.s: This order changes one Assistant Secretary of the Interior to Assistant Secretary of the Interior for Education, Health and Recreation. It puts that official in charge of the Department of the Interior’s education, health, and recreation activities. It also transfers several agencies and functions to the department, including the Public Health Service, the Division of Vital Statistics, the American Printing House for the Blind, and National Cemeteries, Parks and Monuments.

5961.s: This order transfers the Employees' Compensation Commission activities that deal with the longshoremen's and harbor workers' compensation laws to the Department of Labor. It also transfers the related personnel, records, property, and unspent funds to that department. With the President's approval, the Secretary of Labor may also consolidate, eliminate, or redistribute bureaus, agencies, offices, activities, and their functions within the Department of Labor.

5960.s: This order moves several government functions and agencies to the Department of Commerce or its bureaus. It transfers the Federal Oil Conservation Board’s powers to the Bureau of Mines, gives the National Screw Thread Commission and the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics to the Bureau of Standards in an advisory role, and moves the Weather Bureau from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of Commerce. It also says the transferred offices keep their powers, staff, records, property, and funds, and it lets the Secretary of Commerce reorganize parts of the department with the President’s approval.

5959.s: This order transfers certain accounting and audit duties from the General Accounting Office to the Bureau of the Budget. It also transfers the Bureau of Efficiency to that bureau.
