The order says the transferred agencies and activities bring their powers, personnel, records, and funds with them, and that the Bureau of the Budget may reorganize its offices and functions to carry out the changes.

5958.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in one township in Arizona from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in effect while the township is being resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5957.s: This order revokes part of a 1916 executive order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 547 in New Mexico. It applies only to the lands listed in the order.

5956.s: This order replaces a previous instruction on asylum in American embassies and legations. It says asylum is not part of a diplomatic mission and should not be given to people fleeing the legitimate agents of the local government. It allows protection only for uninvited fugitives whose lives are in immediate danger from mob violence, and only while that danger continues.

5954.s: This order exempts John L. Bateman of the Office of the Architect of the Capitol and Mrs. Otilla A. Reagan of the Department of the Interior from the rule for automatic separation from service at retirement age. It applies to these named persons who reach the retirement age during the current month.

5955.s: This order extends the trust period on the allotment of Gertrude Lamb, a deceased Wichita allottee in Oklahoma. The extension lasts for 10 years from the date the trust period would have expired in 1932.

5953.s: This order extends the trust period for Indian allotments that were set to expire during 1933. It applies to allotments on the listed reservations and to other reservations not named here, and it extends the trust period for 10 years from the date it would have expired.

5952.s: This order revokes two earlier orders and sets new rules for the Army ration. It lists the kinds and amounts of food for garrison, travel, reserve, and field rations, and it also covers food for troops traveling on transports. It includes special rules for Alaska, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day, the Philippine Islands, and other remote stations.

5951.s: This order exempts George R. Wales from the rule that would automatically separate him from government service at the retirement age. It applies only to him and changes the compulsory retirement rule under the cited law.

5950.s: This order removes a tract of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It restores the land to entry under the public land laws and says the tract was previously occupied as a home site.

5949.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Montana and Wyoming from settlement, sale, entry, or other disposal. It reserves those lands for the approach road to Yellowstone National Park, subject to valid existing rights.

5948.s: This order changes a prior withdrawal of a specific parcel of land in Michigan from all forms of appropriation. It allows the State of Michigan to select that land under the act of July 31, 1912.

5947.s: This order removes certain tracts of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. The land had been occupied as home sites, and it is restored to entry under the public land laws. It affects the listed home site tracts described in the order.

5946.s: This order exempts three named federal employees from the rule that would automatically separate them from service when they reach the retirement age during the current month. The people named are Thomas W. Maxwell of the Post Office Department, Cornelius T. Finehout of the Treasury Department, and Charles E. Molster of the Department of Commerce.

5945.s: This order sets aside a described area in Siskiyou County, California, as a refuge and breeding ground for wild birds and animals. The land is still subject to use by the Department of the Interior for irrigation and other incidental purposes, and to existing valid rights. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds there, or to damage natural growth, fire safety, or U.S. property. The refuge is to be known as the Tule Lake Wild Life Refuge.

5944.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of public lands in four townships in Nevada that had been held pending resurvey. After the resurvey plats are filed, the unreserved public lands will be opened first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws for 91 days, subject to valid rights and the stated rules. After that period, the lands will be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5942.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in place while the townships are resurveyed. It affects people who might try to settle on, claim, buy, or enter those lands.

5943.s: This order revokes a 1927 withdrawal of certain public lands in two Colorado townships that had been held pending resurvey. It says the unreserved land, if otherwise available, will be open first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws for 91 days after the resurvey plats are filed. After that, the land will be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5940.s: This order exempts William Bertrand Acker, Chief Clerk in the Department of the Interior, from the rule that would automatically separate him from service at retirement age. It lets him stay in federal service instead of retiring under that rule.

5941.s: This order revokes part of a 1919 executive order that had created Public Water Reserve No. 65. It applies to the listed land in New Mexico that is not otherwise reserved or withdrawn. That land is restored to the public domain and will be open to disposition under the laws that apply to it, on a date and after notice that will be announced later.

5939.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5452, which had withdrawn public lands in T. 26 N., R. 11 W., New Mexico principal meridian, New Mexico, pending a resurvey. It affects those public lands in that area.

5938.s: This order adds described land in South Dakota to the Harney National Forest. It says the change will not interfere with land that is already legally used or reserved for a public purpose, as long as those rights stay in force.

5937.s: This order revokes parts of earlier power-site withdrawal and reserve orders for the lands listed in Idaho. It affects the specific parcels described under the Boise Meridian.

5936.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in California for classification as to whether they are suitable for national-forest purposes. It is subject to valid existing rights and an existing power-site withdrawal, and it stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5935.s:
This order revokes a previous withdrawal of public lands in a township in Wyoming that had been held pending resurvey. After the resurvey plat is officially filed, the lands may be opened under set terms and conditions, subject to valid rights.
For 91 days, only qualified ex-service men may enter the lands under the homestead or desert land laws. After that, the lands may be open to the general public under any applicable public land law, and no one may gain rights by settling there ahead of entry except as allowed by the order.

5934.s: This order revokes a 1923 withdrawal of public lands in one township in Colorado. After the official resurvey plat is filed, the lands would be opened under the homestead or desert land laws only for 91 days to qualified ex-service men named in the resolution, subject to valid rights and the stated rules. After that, the lands would be open to the general public under any applicable public land law.

5933.s: This order revokes a 1929 withdrawal of public lands in T. 45 N., R. 87 W. in Wyoming that had been held pending resurvey. It says the lands, if otherwise subject to disposition, must be opened under the terms of a public resolution and related regulations. For 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat, qualified ex-service men may enter the lands under the homestead or desert land laws only, and after that the general public may seek them under applicable public land laws.

5932.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of public lands in two townships in New Mexico, pending resurvey. After the resurvey plats are filed, the unreserved public lands there may be opened to entry under the homestead or desert land laws only by qualified ex-service men for 91 days. After that, the lands may be available to the general public under the public land laws that apply. Until then, no rights may be gained by settling on the land ahead of entry.

5930.s: This order changes the civil-service rules for the Post Office Department. It adds temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers needed for part-time or intermittent work in the Postal Service for holiday or seasonal business through February 1, 1933.

5931.s: This order changes two strips of land on Oahu, Hawaii. One strip from Round Top Military Reservation to Ferdinand Street is restored to its previous status for use by the Territory of Hawaii because it is no longer needed as a right of way. Another 10-foot strip from the reservation to Awapuhi Street is reserved and set apart as a right of way.

5929.s: This order temporarily withdraws specific public lands in Wisconsin from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be classified while officials decide whether to include them in a national forest. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5928.s: This order withdraws 5 acres in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by law. It reserves the land for use by the Forest Service as a ranger station for the administration of the Deschutes National Forest. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5927.s: This order revokes part of a 1919 order that had created Power-Site Reserve No. 706. It affects the lands described in the order in California.

5926.s: This order revokes parts of earlier power-site withdrawals and reserves for specific lands in the Boise Meridian in Idaho. It applies only to the lands listed in the order.

5925.s: This order moves certain lands from the Boise National Forest and the Challis National Forest into the Sawtooth National Forest. It also moves some lands from the Sawtooth National Forest into the Boise National Forest. The order says it does not give national forest status to public lands that did not already have it, and it does not remove any public lands from national forest status.

5924.s: The order lets the Civil Service Commission create rules giving priority for job openings to certain employees who have been recently furloughed or are about to be furloughed because of a reduction in force. This applies to employees with the proper status and without delinquency or misconduct. It also replaces earlier orders and an executive instruction about reemployment and transfers.

5923.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in T. 3 S., R. 7 E. of the Willamette meridian in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. It applies while a resurvey of the township is pending. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5922.s: This order changes Schedule B of the civil-service rules, which lists positions that may be filled through noncompetitive examinations. It adds one position in the Post Office Department: one postal rate expert.

5920.s: This order withdraws public lands in townships 21 and 22 south, range 3 east, of the New Mexico principal meridian from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the townships are resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5921.s: This order exempts three named federal employees from the rule that would automatically separate them from service when they reach retirement age. It applies to Edward M. Hall in the Treasury Department, Walter L. Turner in the Department of Commerce, and Edward J. Wilver in the Government Printing Office. These exemptions cover people who will reach the retirement age during the current month.

5918.s: This order authorizes the United States Civil Service Commission to test the qualifications of applicants for nomination to appointment in the United States Military or Naval Academies. It applies to applicants nominated by any Member of Congress.

5919.s: This order revokes part of a 1917 executive order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 661. It applies to the specific lands listed in the Willamette Meridian in Oregon.

5917.s: This order exempts Albert D. Davis, a cabinet maker at the United States Shipping Board, from the rule that would automatically separate him from service at retirement age. It applies only to him and changes how that retirement rule affects his job.

5916.s: This order revokes parts of earlier orders that set aside certain lands in California for power-site use. The revoked land is in the Mount Diablo Meridian and is described by township, range, and section.

5914.s: This order enlarges the Long Lake Migratory Bird Refuge in North Dakota to include an additional area. It makes it unlawful in the refuge to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds, or to take or destroy nests or eggs. It also forbids cutting or burning natural growth, leaving fires unattended, and injuring or destroying U.S. property.

5915.s: This order revokes part of a 1915 executive order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 471. The revocation applies to the lands described in the order under the Mount Diablo Meridian in California.

5913.s: This order temporarily reserves certain lots and all of block 189 in the Hot Springs Reservation, Arkansas, from other forms of disposal. The land is set aside for the use and benefit of Hot Springs National Park, subject to valid existing rights and the conditions of the cited acts.

5912.s: This order exempts John P. McDowell from the rule that would automatically separate him from service because of age. McDowell is a member of the board of appeals in the Office of the Solicitor at the Department of the Interior.

5911.s: This order exempts John W. Ginder, the Superintendent of the Architectural Engineering Division in the Treasury Department, from the retirement rule for automatic separation because of age. It affects him and the retirement requirement named in the law.

5910.s: This order changes the Tariff of United States Consular Fees. It changes one word in item 1, adds a $9 fee for visaing a Chinese passport or certificate except for persons included in a, b, and c above, and sets a $9 fee for visaing an affidavit of identity.

5909.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in a described area of New Mexico from use so they can be classified for possible wildlife refuge purposes. It applies subject to valid existing rights and stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5908.s: This order revokes part of a 1927 land withdrawal for the listed lands in San Bernardino Meridian. It also opens public lands within 50 feet of a proposed conduit to carry water from the Colorado River for the City of Los Angeles right-of-way application.

5902.s: This order withdraws the listed public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for municipal water-supply purposes. It applies only to the specific tracts named in the order, as far as title remains in the United States.

5907.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Montana, New Mexico, Oregon, and Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for public use.

5906.s: This order changes Reservoir-Site Reserve No. 17 to allow the Federal Power Commission to issue a license for Project No. 1209 on certain lands along a transmission line. If the lands are later needed for reservoir purposes, the licensee must remove its project works at its own expense within 30 days after notice from the Secretary of the Interior.

5905.s: This order allows Mrs. Sarah L. Curtiss to be appointed to a clerkship in the Veterans' Administration at $1,260 a year without regard to civil-service requirements. It says Mrs. Curtiss is the widow of Dr. William W. Curtiss, who was a commissioned officer in the Public Health Service and an employee of the Veterans' Administration.

5904.s: This order withdraws 160 acres of land in Wyoming, subject to valid existing rights. The land is set aside for use by the Navy Department in connection with Naval Petroleum Reserve No. 3 until the President or Congress revokes the order.

5903.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from use so they can be classified for migratory-bird refuge purposes. It applies to the public lands in the described areas and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5901.s: This order changes the civil service rules for the Department of Agriculture. It removes the examination exception for one assistant to the Secretary in the Office of the Secretary of Agriculture and places that position and its incumbent in the classified competitive service.

5900.s: This order temporarily withdraws a described tract of public land in Oregon for classification and to aid legislation. It applies subject to valid existing rights and the conditions of the cited acts, and it stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5899.s: This order revokes part of a 1912 executive order that had created Public Water Reserve No. 2 in Wyoming for the listed land. The land that is not otherwise reserved or withdrawn is restored to the public domain and will be open to disposal under the laws that apply to it after notice is announced.

5898.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Arizona from settlement, location, sale, or entry, while still allowing any prior valid existing claims. It is meant to aid contemplated legislation that would let Arizona secure some of those lands for the use of the University of Arizona, and the withdrawal lasts until that legislation is enacted or the order is revoked.

5897.s: This order gives William Bertrand Acker a further temporary exemption from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service until November 1, 1932.

5896.s: This order exempts the named federal employees from the rule that required automatic separation from service at retirement age. The people listed work in the Department of Commerce, the Department of the Interior, the Navy Department, the Department of State, the Treasury Department, the War Department, the District of Columbia, the Smithsonian Institution, and the Senate Office Building. It says they had already been temporarily exempted before.

5895.s: This order revokes a 1929 order that had withdrawn public lands in two townships in Florida pending resurvey. It affects those public lands in Tps. 14 and 15 S., R. 25 E., Tallahassee meridian, Florida.

5894.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The lands are held back while the townships are resurveyed. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5893.s: This order allows Mr. Lamar Costello to be appointed as Supervisor of Detentions in the Immigration Service at Ellis Island, New York. The job pays $3,000 a year. The appointment can be made without following the civil-service rules.

5892.s: This order abolishes the Radio Division of the Department of Commerce and transfers its duties, powers, and functions to the Federal Radio Commission. It also transfers the division’s records, property, and available appropriations to the commission. Officers and employees judged indispensable may be moved to the commission, and the others are to be dismissed. The commission may also change the titles, designations, and duties of those employees.

5891.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Oregon for classification as to their suitability for migratory bird refuge purposes. It applies to listed areas around Harney Lake and Malheur Lake, including some lands not included in the Lake Malheur Reservation. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5890.s: This order revokes part of a 1927 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in California and Nevada for air-mail beacon sites and landing fields. The revocation applies only to the NW. ¼ of section 20, T. 9 N., R. 2 W., San Bernardino meridian, California.

5889.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the cited laws. The lands are set aside for use with the San Carlos Indian Irrigation Project. It also says any valid rights or claims already started before the order are subject to it.

5888.s: This order sets rules for shipping liquor under seal through the Canal Zone on the highways or waterways. Each shipment must carry a certificate, stay sealed, be shown to officials if asked, and move through the Canal Zone without stopping there. It applies to liquor in transit between points outside the Canal Zone and not meant for use, consumption, or final delivery in the Canal Zone.

5886.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The lands will stay withdrawn while they are resurveyed. The order remains in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5887.s: This order directs federal department heads and the District of Columbia government to furlough employees without pay to stay within the 1933 appropriations. It says higher salaried employees should be furloughed first when possible, and employees should not be discharged if they are qualified for the work that will continue. It also says furloughs should be used only when absolutely necessary and that other ways of avoiding them should be considered first.

5885.s: This order changes the name of the California National Forest to Mendocino National Forest. It says the change is meant to avoid confusion with the State of California, which had the same name as the forest.

5883.s: This order revoked a 1929 withdrawal of public lands in two townships in Colorado, subject to valid rights. It opened the unreserved public lands in one township to entry under the homestead or desert land laws by qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat, and then to the general public under applicable public land laws. No rights could be gained by settlement before entry except as allowed by the order.

5884.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Wyoming pending resurvey. It says the lands, if otherwise subject to disposition, will be opened first for entry under the homestead or desert land laws only, for qualified ex-service men, for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat. After that, the lands may be opened to the general public under any applicable public land law. No one may claim the released lands by settling on them before entry except as allowed by the order.

5882.s: This order changes the name of the Crater National Forest in Oregon to Rogue River National Forest. It is meant to avoid confusion with Crater Lake National Park.

5881.s: This order gives three named Treasury Department employees a further temporary exemption from automatic retirement because they have reached retirement age. It lets them stay in service until August 1, 1932, to give time to appoint successors to their positions.

5880.s: This order changes the boundaries of the Balboa Division of the District Court of the Canal Zone. It adds a strip of land near Madden Road to that division. The area was one where jurisdiction was ceded to the United States by the Republic of Panama during construction of the Madden Dam. It stays in effect while the United States exercises jurisdiction in that area.

5879.s: This order allows Mrs. A. Blondell Howe to be appointed to a clerical position in the Internal Revenue Bureau of the Treasury Department without following the Civil Service Commission rules. Mrs. Howe is the widow of a former Treasury worker, and the order says she has four young children and no adequate means of support.

5878.s: This order sets the rates for rental and subsistence allowances for officers in the various services that are entitled to them for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1933. It sets one subsistence allowance at 52 cents per day and one rental allowance for one room at $18 per month.

5877.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Colorado that had been held pending resurvey. It says those lands, if otherwise available, will be opened for entry under the homestead or desert land laws for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat. During that period, qualified ex-service men may enter the lands, and after that they may be opened to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5876.s: This order revokes parts of earlier executive orders that had created coal land withdrawals in Montana. It applies to many described lands in several townships and ranges. The order leaves the listed lands open by ending those withdrawal restrictions, including land outside the Cheyenne River Indian Reservation except for one lot named in the order.

5875.s: This order temporarily exempts William B. Hamilton of the Treasury Department and William E. Rollins of the Senate Office Building from automatic retirement for age. It lets them stay in service until August 1, 1932, while a decision is made on possible permanent exemptions.

5874.s: This order temporarily lets certain named federal employees stay on the job even though they have reached the retirement age for automatic separation from service. It says they may remain until July 10, 1932. The order applies to people in positions that must stay filled while successors are appointed.

5873.s: This order temporarily exempts the named federal employees from automatic retirement because of age. It lets them stay in service until August 1, 1932. The order says this time is to decide whether permanent exemptions are needed in the public interest.

5872.s: This order exempts the named people from automatic retirement for age. It applies to employees in several federal departments and agencies, including Agriculture, Commerce, the Interior, the Post Office Department, State, Treasury, and others. They are allowed to stay in service despite having reached the retirement age set for automatic separation.

5871.s: This order says the current regulations for sick leave of absence in executive departments and independent establishments will stay in effect for now. They will continue until uniform regulations are later prescribed under the authority named in the June 30, 1932 act.

5870.s: This order keeps the government travel regulations in effect until new ones are approved, with some changes. It revokes reimbursement for actual subsistence expenses and allows per diem instead, up to set maximum rates inside and outside the continental United States. It also says reimbursable transportation charges do not include gratuities or tips, and department heads must set per diem only when justified by the travel.

5869.s: This order sets rules for what documents immigrants and nonimmigrants must show when entering the United States. It requires most immigrants to present immigration visas, and most nonimmigrants to present passports or other official documents visaed by U.S. consular officers, with several listed exceptions. It also gives some U.S. officials authority to issue visas and transit certificates for aliens coming from the Canal Zone, the Philippine Islands, American Samoa, and Guam. The order also covers entry into the Philippine Islands and some other American possessions.

5868.s: This order revokes part of a 1926 order that created Reservoir-Site Reserve No. 17. It applies only to the specific lands described in California’s Mount Diablo Meridian.

5867.s: This order changes the name of the Shenandoah National Forest to the George Washington National Forest. It was done to avoid confusion with the Shenandoah National Park in Virginia.

5866.s: This order changes an earlier rule for enlisted Marine Corps personnel. It says enlisted men who have established special qualifications in using the arms they are required to use may receive extra pay under rules set by the Secretary of the Navy. The extra compensation is set at five different classes, from $1 to $5 per month.

5864.s: This order temporarily withdraws 40 acres of public land in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets the land aside for use as a lookout station in cooperative forest-protection work until the President or Congress revokes it.

5865.s: This order revokes earlier flight regulations and sets new rules for increased pay tied to regular and frequent aerial flights. It applies to officers, warrant officers, and enlisted men in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, and National Guard. It also defines who counts as a qualified aircraft pilot, observer, or student, and sets flight requirements and reporting rules for those groups.

5863.s: This order transfers lands within the Toiyabe National Forest to the Nevada National Forest. It says it does not give national-forest status to any publicly owned lands that did not already have it, and it does not remove that status from any publicly owned lands. The order takes effect on July 1, 1932.

5862.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The lands are held this way until a resurvey of the townships is done. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5861.s: This order allows Eugene R. Capozio to be appointed as a clerk in the Veterans' Administration. It sets his pay at $1,260 a year and says the appointment may be made without following the civil-service rules. The order was issued on the recommendation of the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs.

5860.s: This order sets rules for who may issue passports in the United States and abroad. It says the Secretary of State may issue passports in the United States and may refuse them, while American consular officers issue passports abroad and chief executives issue them in certain U.S. possessions. It also lays out who may get a passport, who can be included on one passport, the fees, and the information, photos, witnesses, and sworn application required.

5859.s: This order revokes a civil-service rule that allowed mounted inspectors in the customs service on the Mexican border to be appointed without a competitive examination. It also says the current people in those positions in the San Antonio, El Paso, Arizona, and San Diego customs districts will be placed in the classified service with their positions if the Treasury Department recommends it and they pass fitness tests set by the Civil Service Commission.

5858.s: This order sets aside several islands and nearby waters in the Semidi Island Group as a refuge and breeding ground for wild birds, game, and fur animals, subject to existing valid rights. It also reserves the area from public land claims and makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, enter, or use the reservation except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. It also forbids cutting or burning natural growth, leaving fires unattended, and damaging U.S. property.

5857.s: This order cancels one section of the Consular Regulations of 1896 and updates several other sections to cite the Tariff Act of 1930 instead of the Tariff Act of 1922. It also changes the rule for invoices, including how many copies are needed for some shipments. Another section is rewritten to require imported articles and their containers to be marked with the country of origin, with a 10 percent duty added if they are not properly marked.

5856.s:
This order removes certain tracts of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. Those tracts had been occupied as home sites and are restored to entry under the public land laws.
It applies to the specific lands described in the order, including areas near Juneau and Prince of Wales Island.

5855-A.s: This order assigns radio frequencies to government stations. It lets listed stations use other frequencies for up to one month if they first give notice to the Interdepartment Radio Advisory Committee and, in some cases, the Federal Radio Commission, and stop if interference is reported. It also says the stations’ listed powers are not limits on those stations and that it replaces a 1931 executive order.

5855.s: This order assigns radio frequencies to government stations and lists several experimental stations that may use miscellaneous frequencies if they do not cause interference. It also says government departments should use existing communication facilities when possible and should avoid closing stations that serve other government departments without making other arrangements. The order says the government will encourage privately owned radio facilities and may use commercial stations when government interests warrant it.

5854.s: This order directs a patrol to be maintained in U.S. territorial waters and on the high seas, including the Bering Sea, to enforce the act protecting the northern Pacific halibut fishery. It says naval or other public vessels may carry out the patrol, and it names several Bureau of Fisheries vessels for that duty. It also designates the masters of those vessels, along with certain Bureau of Fisheries agents, assistant agents, inspectors, and wardens, to use search and seizure powers under the act.

5853.s: This order waives the maximum age limit for George H. Rolfe so he can enter the open competitive examination for postmaster at Concord, New Hampshire. It affects only George H. Rolfe and the postmaster exam for that job.

5852.s: This order allows Mrs. Gladys L. Knight to be appointed to an existing vacancy as a junior typist at the Headquarters of the United States Marine Corps in Washington, D.C., without following the civil service act or rules. It says she is the widow of a Marine Corps officer who was killed in the line of duty. It also says she needs employment to support herself and her minor child.

5851.s: This order allows Mrs. Nesta Stephens Long to be appointed as a clerk in the Customs Service in Arizona for one year, without regard to her standing on the civil-service junior stenographic register. It affects Mrs. Long and the Customs Service position in Arizona. The order says her husband, Carroll Robert Long, is giving up his position temporarily because of serious illness.

5850.s: This order takes federal control of the municipal aviation field in Tucson, Arizona, for military purposes. It says the field had been leased to the city of Tucson and designates the Secretary of War to exercise this control for the United States.

5849.s: This order sets apart a described area in the Canal Zone for use as a naval reservation under the Secretary of the Navy. It says the land remains subject to the civil control and jurisdiction of the Canal Zone authorities, and it keeps rights of way for highways, power and communication lines, lighthouses, and military defense installations. If any part later becomes surplus for naval needs, that part must be restored to Canal Zone control.

5847.s: This order allows Warren Benjamin to be appointed to a clerical job in the Treasury Department without following the civil-service rules. It says he is the stepson of the late Graham Nichol. It also says Mr. Nichol had served in the Bureau of Internal Revenue and left his widow without adequate means of support.

5848.s: This order changes the Tariff of United States Consular Fees. It sets the fee for issuing a passport at $9.00 and the fee for renewing an American passport at $5.00, and it removes references to Form No. 37, Form No. 38, and Form No. 39. It also says there is no fee for certifying copies of certificates of American origin, manufacture, or inspection when done on written orders of the Secretary of State to advance the export trade of the United States.

5846.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands stay subject to valid existing rights and are being held for classification. It also says they will be considered for possible addition to Rocky Mountain National Park.

5845.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn public lands in Township 62 North, Range 2 East in Minnesota pending resurvey. It says all of the lands in that township are within the limits of the Superior National Forest.

5844.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of public lands in township 25 north, range 4 east, in Michigan, that had been pending resurvey. It affects the lands in that township, which are within the Huron National Forest.

5843.s: This order withdraws certain unappropriated public lands in listed California townships from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The lands are withdrawn for classification and in aid of legislation, while valid existing rights stay in place. It also revokes a 1912 order that had temporarily reserved part of the land for an investigation of its suitableness for Indian allotment purposes.

5842.s: This order names Emilio del Toro to do the duties of the Judge of the District Court of the United States for Porto Rico when Judge Ira K. Wells is absent. He is also allowed to sign the needed papers and records as acting judge during that absence.

5841.s: This order changes the boundaries of the Siuslaw National Forest in Oregon. It removes the listed lands from the forest. The order affects the specific tracts named in the land description.

5840.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of public lands in one township in New Mexico that had been pending resurvey. It affects the lands in that township, which are all within the Santa Fe National Forest.

5839.s: This order allows Mr. Ralph A. Vestal to be appointed as a junior clerk in the Department of State. It says this can be done without following the civil-service rules.

5838.s: This order temporarily withdraws 40 acres of public land in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the cited acts. It applies to that land unless the President or Congress revokes it, and it is in aid of proposed legislation.

5837.s: This order adds a consular fee item for certifying copies of certificates of American origin, manufacture, or inspection issued by a U.S. government department or office. No fee is charged when the certified copy is needed to help advance U.S. export trade.

5836.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in California and Nevada from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It does this while the right of way is being definitely located for a transmission line to carry power from the Boulder Canyon Project to the city of Los Angeles.

5835.s: This order extends the limits of certain customs ports of entry in North Dakota, Minnesota, and Washington. It adds the townships of Ambrose, Baxter, and St. Vincent to named ports in North Dakota and Minnesota. It also changes the port limits at Blaine, Washington, by setting out a new boundary area.

5834.s: This order transfers all lands that were part of the Jefferson National Forest to the Lewis and Clark National Forest in Montana. It affects the forest lands covered by the earlier proclamation and later orders named in the text.

5833.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Minnesota for classification. It also holds those lands while a decision is made on whether to include them in a national forest. The withdrawal is subject to valid existing rights.

5832.s: This order reserves land and buildings in the former Fort St. Michael Military Reservation in Alaska for use by the Department of Justice. It covers three parcels of land and includes buildings numbered 5, 14, 16, and 24, plus a coal house. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5830.s: This order lets the Secretary of the Interior hire people needed to help administer the War Minerals Relief Act. Those hires do not have to follow the civil service act and rules, and the work is tied to relief for contracts connected with the prosecution of the war.

5831.s: This order allows Mrs. Ruth Bascot Dartt to be appointed to an existing junior clerk vacancy at Headquarters, United States Marine Corps, in Washington, D.C. It says the appointment may be made without regard to the civil-service act or rules, and notes that she is the widow of a Marine Corps officer killed in line of duty.

5829.s: This order withdraws public lands in a township in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the township is being resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5827.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation, while keeping valid existing rights in place. The lands are held for the exclusive use and benefit of the War Department for military purposes until the order is revoked by the President or by Congress.

5828.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It holds the land for the exclusive use of the United States Navy Department to develop and use as an ammunition depot. The order applies only where valid existing claims do not already exist and where the land title remains with the United States.

5826.s: This order changes the name of the Colorado National Forest to Roosevelt National Forest. It applies to that national forest in Colorado and names it in honor of Theodore Roosevelt.

5825.s: This order changes leave rules for diplomatic officers and consular officers. It allows leave without pay for a longer time if it is consistent with the public interest and there is a good reason. It also lets the Secretary of State add unpaid leave to cover part of a leave period that carries into the next calendar year.

5824.s: This order says income tax returns may be open to inspection by state officers for state intangible property tax purposes. It applies under the rules and regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury, as amended and approved by the President.

5822.s: This order allows Fred Scott of Valdez, Alaska, to be appointed as a guard at one of the Federal penitentiaries in the Department of Justice without meeting the civil-service rules. It says he previously worked at Walla Walla Prison, later worked in Alaska on road construction for the Alaska Roads Commission, and had a hand injury that led to the loss of a finger. The Attorney General recommended his appointment.

5823.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Colorado that had been held pending resurvey. It says the unreserved lands in the listed sections of T. 36 N., R. 13 W. may be opened, subject to valid rights, to qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat. After that, the lands may be opened to the general public under any applicable public land law, and no one may gain rights by settling there before entry. It also states that all the lands in T. 36 N., R. 12 W. are within the Montezuma National Forest.

5820.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn public lands in one township in Arkansas while a resurvey was pending. The lands in that township are part of the Ouachita National Forest.

5821.s: This order waives the maximum age limit for appointment as acting postmaster and for the open competitive examination for postmaster at the post office at Woodward, Oklahoma. It allows Joseph H. Hopkins to be appointed acting postmaster there and to take the examination for that postmaster job.

5819.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Colorado that had been held pending a resurvey. It opens some of those lands to entry under the homestead or desert land laws, and other lands to entry under the stock-raising homestead laws for qualified ex-service men, subject to valid rights and the listed withdrawals. After the stated period, the unreserved public lands in the township would be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5818.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Washington from settlement or other uses so they can be classified for migratory bird refuge purposes. It covers the listed land sections, plus unsurveyed islands and lands within three unnamed lakes. The withdrawal stays in place unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5816.s: This order revokes part of a 1910 executive order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 155. The change applies to the described land in Montana: T. 2 S., R. 20 E., sec. 32, lot 6.

5817.s: This order changes the civil-service rules for some jobs in the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce. It keeps commercial attaches, assistant commercial attaches, trade commissioners, and assistant trade commissioners in the Foreign Commerce Service in excepted status, and after at least three years abroad they may be transferred or reinstated with Civil Service Commission approval. It also puts most other bureau positions in the continental United States, Alaska, Hawaii, and Porto Rico into the classified competitive service, except for the director and assistant directors.

5814.s: This order adds a described tract of land to the Ocala National Forest and the Ocala National Game Refuge in Florida. The land is in Marion and Lake Counties and is described as 10,801.12 acres, more or less.

5815.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain coal lands in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, entry, lease, or other disposal. The lands are reserved for investigation, examination, and classification. It applies subject to valid existing claims and stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5813.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain lands in Alaska from settlement, sale, entry, lease, or other disposal. The lands are reserved for investigation, examination, and classification. It does not affect valid existing claims.

5812.s: This order changes the rules for buying and using postage stamps with official funds. It requires a voucher for postage purchases and says the stamps may be used only for official correspondence and packages. It also requires a strict account of official postage and makes the same change to instructions for diplomatic officers.

5810.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 4426, which had withdrawn certain public lands in Utah pending a resurvey. It affects the public lands in T. 1 S., R. 2 E., Salt Lake meridian, Utah.

5811.s: This order allows Mrs. Wanda Coolidge Carver to be appointed as an under clerk at the navy yard in Washington, D.C., in place of an existing typewriter vacancy. It says the appointment may be made without following the civil-service act or rules. It also says she is the widow of William E. Carver, who was killed in an explosion at the naval magazine in Bellevue, D.C.

5809.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had withdrawn public lands in a township in New Mexico pending resurvey. The lands in that township are in the Santa Fe National Forest.

5807.s: This order withdraws public lands in one township in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the township is being resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5808.s: This order adds land in Burleigh and Kidder Counties, North Dakota, to the Long Lake Migratory Bird Refuge and sets it aside for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and wild animals. It says people may not hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild birds or animals there, or cut, burn, or destroy natural growth or damage U.S. property, except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

5806.s: This order revokes part of a 1922 order that had reserved certain land in Alaska for town-site purposes. It applies only to tract 32, a 140.24-acre parcel in the Anchorage Town Site.

5804.s: This order allows Miss Ann Halloran to be appointed as a stenographer in the Veterans' Administration without following the civil-service rules. It applies to that appointment and is based on the recommendation of the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs.

5805.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in listed townships in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The lands are held this way while they are resurveyed. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5803.s: This order withdraws and reserves a specific piece of public land in Oregon for use by the Bureau of Fisheries. It is subject to an existing withdrawal for power purposes and to any valid existing rights. The withdrawal stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5802.s: This order allows Mr. Sinclair A. Wilson to be appointed as Senior Forest Economist at the Pacific Northwest station of the Forest Service in the Department of Agriculture. The job pays $4,600 a year. It says the appointment may be made without following the civil-service rules.

5801.s: This order transfers certain lands now in the Absaroka National Forest and the Beartooth National Forest to the Custer National Forest. It describes the land by detailed boundary lines and map divisions. It also says the order is not meant to give public lands national forest status if they did not already have it, or to remove any public lands from national forest status.

5800.s: This order transfers certain lands now in the Gallatin National Forest and the Beartooth National Forest to the Absaroka National Forest in Montana. It describes the lands by location and boundary lines. It also says the order is not meant to give new national-forest status to public lands that did not already have it, or to remove public lands from national-forest status.

5799.s: This order withdraws and reserves 80 acres in Nevada for the Department of Agriculture to use as the McClellan Peak lookout site. It is for work connected to the administration of the Tahoe National Forest, and it is subject to existing rights and the terms of the cited laws.

5798.s: This order revokes part of a 1917 executive order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 660. It applies to the lands described in the Willamette Meridian in Oregon.

5796.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Illinois and Wisconsin from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It covers all islands in the Fox River and in the chain of lakes drained by the river, along with all lands in the drainage basin through which the river flows. The withdrawal lasts until the President or Congress revokes it.

5797.s: This order revokes the withdrawal of certain public lands in two townships in Wyoming that had been held pending resurvey. After the official filing of the resurvey plat, and subject to valid rights, those lands would be open for 91 days to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws only. After that, they would be open to the general public under any public land law that applies.

5795.s: This order revokes part of the 1911 order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 190, for the land described in it. It affects a parcel in Wyoming in the Sixth Principal Meridian, Township 38 North, Range 110 West, Section 36, southwest quarter.

5794.s: This order temporarily withdraws 80 acres of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be used as a lookout station for cooperative forest-protection work.

5793.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of public lands in one township in Wyoming that had been held for a resurvey. It then opens the unreserved public lands in that township, subject to valid rights, first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws for 91 days after the resurvey plat is officially filed. After that period, the lands may be opened to the general public under any public land law that applies.

5792.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The land is kept withdrawn while it is resurveyed. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5791.s: This order withdraws public lands in one township in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in effect while the township is pending a resurvey. It remains in force unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5790.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in two townships in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while those townships are being resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5789.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The land stays withdrawn while it is resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes the order.

5788.s: This order sets rules for trucks and other heavy vehicles using public highways in the Canal Zone. It limits vehicle size, weight, tire thickness, and speed, and it gives special permit rules for vehicles that do not fit those limits. It also allows exceptions in some cases and says people who break the rules may be fined or jailed.

5786.s: This order sets aside a bounded area of water off the coast of North Carolina as a defensive sea area for national defense. It says vessels or other craft may not travel in that area unless the Secretary of the Navy authorizes them. Violations are subject to penalties provided by law.

5787.s: This order changes the civil-service rules for the Department of Justice by listing certain jobs that are excepted from examination. It covers prison directors, parole board members, wardens, some prison staff, clerks for U.S. district attorneys, special employees with knowledge of prohibition law violations, certain jobs in the Attorney General’s office, and most positions in the Bureau of Investigation except fingerprint classifiers. It says the change is meant to reduce the number of excepted positions and improve the service.

5785.s: This order revokes a 1929 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in New Mexico from use while they were pending resurvey. It affects the public lands in Tps. 16 N., Rs. 12 and 13 E., New Mexico principal meridian.

5784.s: This order withdraws part of the Fort William H. Seward Military Reservation in Alaska, called the Clay Reserve, for use by the Alaska Road Commission. If the commission no longer needs the land, it must be returned to the Secretary of the Interior for disposal under law.

5782.s: This order reserves land in Albany County, Wyoming, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and wild animals. It adds that land to the Hutton Lake Migratory Bird Refuge. Within the area, hunting, trapping, capturing, disturbing, or killing wild animals or birds is not allowed, and people may not cut vegetation, leave fires unattended, or damage U.S. property.

5783.s: This order sets aside land in Albany County, Wyoming, as an addition to the Bamforth Lake Migratory Bird Refuge. It reserves the area for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and wild animals, subject to existing valid rights. It also makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, disturb, kill, or capture wild animals or birds there, or to damage plants, start or leave fires, or damage U.S. property.

5781.s: This order allows Mrs. Florence C. Brock to be appointed as a junior clerk in the Bureau of Public Roads in the Department of Agriculture. It says the appointment may be made without following the civil-service rules. Mrs. Brock is the widow of Thomas S. Brock, who served for over 30 years in the Department of the Interior and the Department of Agriculture.

5779.s: This order removes certain tracts of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. The land had been occupied as home sites and is restored to entry under the public land laws. It affects the specific areas listed in the order.

5780.s: This order revokes part of two earlier orders that created public water reserves in Arizona and Utah. It restores the listed land to the public domain if it is not otherwise reserved or withdrawn. The land would then be subject to disposal under the laws that apply to it after notice is announced.

5777.s: This order changes the civil-service rules to allow four headquarters messenger positions at the Philippine Department to be excepted from the competitive exam process. These positions are to be filled by honorably discharged enlisted men who have been on duty at those headquarters.

5778.s: The order adds wage and record rules to public building contracts covered by the act. It says wages must be paid in full at least once a week, payrolls and related agreements must be open to inspection, and the wage rate must be posted at the work site. It also says that if a contractor or subcontractor pays less than the prevailing wage, the Government may end the work and take it over, and this applies to contracts with bids invited after the order.

5775.s: This order revokes the rule that had excepted miners in the Bureau of Mines from competitive civil-service examination. It places the positions of miners in the classified service and gives the people in those jobs competitive classified status. It applies to miners working in rescue or first-aid work at rescue stations, on rescue cars, or at experimental mines under the Bureau of Mines.

5776.s: This order changes civil-service exam rules for applicants who are veterans or related to honorably discharged service members. It adds points to exam ratings for honorably discharged soldiers, sailors, and marines, and gives more points to some applicants with service-connected disabilities, widows, and wives in certain cases. It also says time spent in military or naval service during the World War or the war with Spain can be counted in ratings when an applicant's similar work was interrupted and then resumed after discharge.

5774.s: This order changes civil-service rules to allow appointments of members of national soldiers' homes without examination. If those jobs are filled by members of the homes, the Veterans' Administration must think they can do the work satisfactorily; if not, the jobs must be filled under civil-service rules and regulations.

5773.s: This order changes rules for consular officers and their staff. It requires most official correspondence to go through superior officers, allows direct correspondence in a few listed cases, and restates duties toward American citizens abroad. It also sets rules for unclaimed letters, cancels one obsolete section, and amends the consular fee schedule, including one new no-fee item.

5772.s: This order lets the Secretary of the Interior approve Salt Lake City 049347 from the Uintah Railway Co. for a railroad right of way through certain lands that had been temporarily withdrawn in Utah and other States. It affects the company and the withdrawn lands covered by the earlier order.

5770.s: This order designates Port Everglades, Florida, as a customs port of entry. It places the port in Customs Collection District No. 18, with headquarters at Tampa, Florida, starting January 1, 1932.

5771.s: This order makes a strip of land in the Schofield Barracks Military Reservation available for road right-of-way use. It is meant to replace certain road reserve portions that were described in Executive Order No. 2800. It affects road right of ways through the reservation, including parts of the Honolulu-Waialua Road and the Wahiawa-Waikakalaua Road.

5769.s: This executive order revokes part of two earlier orders that created phosphate reserves in Idaho. It applies to the specific lands listed in the Boise Meridian descriptions.

5768.s: This order extends the trust period for certain allotments made in favor of Indians on named reservations. The extension is for 10 years from each allotment’s current expiration date. It applies to the reservations listed in the order, including places in California, Kansas and Nebraska, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Washington, and Wyoming.

5767.s: This order allows Mrs. Hallie D. Stotler to be appointed as a clerk in the Bureau of Prohibition in the Department of Justice without following the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of a prohibition officer who died in the line of duty, and the Attorney General and Civil Service Commission agreed with the appointment.

5766.s: This order allows Mrs. Yetta B. Floyd to be appointed as a clerk-typist in the Bureau of Prohibition in the Department of Justice. It says the appointment may be made without following the civil-service rules and was issued on the Attorney General’s recommendation.

5765.s: This order transfers certain lands in New Mexico from the Datil National Forest to the Gila National Forest. It changes the forest boundaries for the lands listed in the order. It says the order is not meant to give national-forest status to lands that did not already have it, or to remove that status from any publicly owned lands.

5764.s: This order amends Civil-Service Rule V by adding a new subsection. The new subsection applies when two members of an applicant's family are already in public service in the grades covered by the Civil-Service Act.

5763.s: This order closed executive departments and independent government establishments in the District of Columbia on Saturday, December 26, 1931. It also excused Federal employees in the District of Columbia from duty that day, except for those excepted for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law.

5762.s: This order allows Mrs. Florence F. Burton to be appointed as secretary to the Director of Prohibition in the Department of Justice without following the civil-service rules. It affects her position in the Bureau of Prohibition. The order says she had been serving there temporarily with approval from the Civil Service Commission.

5761.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Bitterroot National Forest and the Missoula National Forest to the Lolo National Forest in Montana. It changes the boundaries of the Lolo National Forest for the lands listed in the order. It says the transfer is not meant to give national forest status to any public lands that did not already have it, or to take any such status away.

5760.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Madison National Forest to the Gallatin National Forest in Montana. It also says the transfer does not give national-forest status to public lands that did not already have it, and does not remove that status from public lands already in a national forest. The new forest boundaries are shown on an attached diagram.

5759.s: This order moves certain lands from the Madison, Missoula, and Helena National Forests to the Deerlodge National Forest in Montana. It also removes certain lands from the Deerlodge National Forest. The order says no lands are given national forest status if they did not already have it, and no lands are removed from that status except the lands listed.

5758.s: This order transfers certain lands now in the Lolo National Forest to the Cabinet National Forest in Montana. It gives detailed boundary lines for the land being moved. It says the order is not meant to give national-forest status to public lands that did not already have it, or to remove that status from public lands that already had it.

5757.s: This order transfers certain lands now in the Madison National Forest and the Deerlodge National Forest to the Beaverhead National Forest in Montana. It describes the land areas by township, range, and boundary lines. It says the order is not intended to give any public lands national-forest status that they did not already have, or to remove any such status from public lands.

5756.s: This order transfers certain lands now in the Lewis and Clark National Forest to the Helena National Forest in Montana. It describes the lands by location and boundary lines. It also says the order is not meant to give national-forest status to public lands that did not already have it, or to remove national-forest status from public lands.

5755.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Mississippi from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be classified and considered for possible inclusion in a national forest. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5754.s: This order withdraws a listed tract of land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for public use.

5753.s: This order amends Civil-Service Rule VII on how appointments are apportioned among the States, Territories, and the District of Columbia based on population. It says eligibles with military preference must be certified without regard to apportionment, and some appointments are excluded from the apportionment figures. It also says certain jobs, including listed trades and positions in some offices, will not be apportioned.

5752.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Datil National Forest to the Manzano National Forest. It also changes the name of the Manzano National Forest to the Cibola National Forest. The order says it does not give national forest status to public lands that did not already have it, and it does not remove any public lands from national forest status.

5751.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Colorado for classification. It covers the listed land areas under two principal meridians and is subject to valid existing claims. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5750.s: This order revokes two earlier withdrawals of land in California that had set aside property for lighthouse purposes. It affects the tract at Point Buchon and lots 8 and 9 in fractional section 36, township 29 south, range 10 east of the Mount Diablo meridian.

5749.s: This order revokes a 1923 withdrawal of certain public lands in one township in Colorado that had been held pending a resurvey. The lands were originally withdrawn for the San Juan Forest Reserve, now Rio Grande National Forest, and some parts were later restored and then withdrawn again. After this revocation, the township will not be open under the general public land laws except for valid adverse claims already started before the listed dates.

5748.s: This order revokes the earlier Savannah River Bird Refuge and sets aside three pieces of federal land in South Carolina and Georgia for the Department of Agriculture. The land is reserved as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and wild animals, with existing rights and possible future use in navigation preserved. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or enter the reservation except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture, and it also bans cutting or burning natural growth and damaging federal property.

5747.s: This order changes the area and boundary lines of the Big Lake Reservation in Arkansas. It removes some parcels where patents have been issued and adds some tracts outside the west boundary of drainage district number seventeen. The reservation protects native birds, and it bars hunting, trapping, disturbing wildlife, taking nests or eggs, cutting vegetation, leaving fires unattended, and damaging United States property. It also says no one may enter or use the reservation except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

5746.s: This order extends the trust periods on certain allotments made for Indians of the Yakima Reservation in Washington. It applies to allotments whose trust periods expire during 1931 and 1932, and extends them for 10 more years from the dates they were set to end.

5744.s: This order revokes part of two earlier orders that had set aside certain lands for power-site use. It applies to the lands described under the New Mexico Meridian in section 31 of Township 43 North, Range 6 West.

5745.s: This order revokes part of earlier orders from 1909 and 1910 that created temporary power-site withdrawals and power-site reserves. It applies to the lands described in the order in Wyoming.

5743.s: This order revokes part of a prior withdrawal of certain public lands in Arkansas. The lands released from that withdrawal are opened first only to entry under the homestead laws by qualified ex-service men, under the stated rules and for a 91-day period. After that, the lands may be opened to the general public under applicable public land laws.

5742.s: This order allows Mr. William C. White to be appointed as a naval architect, grade 4, at $3,800 a year. He would serve as chief draftsman in the Office of the Superintending Constructor of the United States Navy in Groton, Connecticut, on work connected with the submarine Cuttlefish. The order says qualified people for this job are limited, hard to find, and usually cannot be obtained through civil-service open competitive examinations.

5741.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of certain public lands in one township in Wyoming that had been pending resurvey. It says those lands, if otherwise available, must be opened first only for entry under the homestead or desert-land laws for 91 days after the official resurvey plat is filed. During that time, qualified ex-service men covered by the resolution may enter the land, and after that it is open to the general public under the land laws that apply.

5739.s: This order revokes parts of two earlier orders that withdrew certain lands in Idaho for a power-site reservation. The change applies to the listed parcels in Boise Meridian, including parts of sections 21 and 22.

5738.s: This order allows Mrs. Louise A. Gallivan to be appointed as a Grade CAF-1 Clerk in the Boston Regional Office of the Veterans' Administration. It says her appointment may be made without following the civil-service rules, and it was issued on the recommendation of the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs.

5737.s: The order cancels section 55 of the Consular Regulations of 1896. It changes section 524 to use a fiscal year beginning July 1 instead of a calendar year. The new rule takes effect January 1, 1932, and for the first half of 1932 it sets how consular agents will settle accounts for tonnage fees on regularly documented American vessels running regularly to or between foreign ports.

5736.s: This order reserves certain public lands in the Philippine Islands for military purposes, subject to any private rights that may exist. It covers Blocks 22 and 23 and part of Sixth Street in the Manila Harbor reclamation area. It also gives the right to build and maintain pipe lines from oil tanks to piers in Manila Harbor, including routes through Engineer Island and any breakwaters and loading heads.

5735.s: This order revokes a 1928 withdrawal of certain public lands in one township in New Mexico that had been held pending a resurvey. After the official filing of the resurvey plat, the unreserved public lands there would be opened for 91 days to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws, subject to valid rights. After that period, the land would be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5734.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to Indians of the Warm Springs Reservation in Oregon. It applies to allotments whose trust period was set to expire during 1931 and extends that period for 10 more years.

5733.s: This order changes a previous coal withdrawal order for a specific parcel of land in Wyoming. It allows that land to be withdrawn and used as an air navigation site. The land affected is the southwest quarter of the southwest quarter of section 4, township 20 north, range 91 west, Sixth Principal Meridian.

5732.s: This order temporarily withdraws 40 acres of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is set aside for use as a lookout station for cooperative forest-protection work. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5731.s: This order changes the civil-service rules for the Post Office Department. It adds temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers needed for part-time or intermittent Postal Service work tied to holiday or seasonal business through February 1, 1932.

5730.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to members of the Walker River Indian Reservation in Nevada. It applies to allotments whose trust period was set to end during 1931 and extends that period for 10 more years.

5729.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It applies while a resurvey of the township is pending and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5728.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to members of the Otoe and Missouria tribes of Indians in Oklahoma. It applies to allotments whose trust period was set to expire during 1931 and extends that period for 10 more years.

5727.s: This order sets aside land in Box Elder County, Utah for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and wild animals, subject to existing valid rights. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds there, or to take or destroy nests or eggs. It also bars cutting or burning natural growth, leaving fires unattended, and damaging U.S. property.

5726.s: This order temporarily withdraws 238.08 acres in the Prescott National Forest, Arizona, from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the cited laws. It reserves the land for use by the Forest Service as a ranger station. The land is to be used in connection with the administration of the Prescott National Forest.

5725.s: This order interprets the boundaries of the Toiyabe National Forest in Nevada based on recent surveys of certain public lands. It says the forest boundaries are as shown on the attached diagram.

5724.s: This order changes civil-service rules for certain jobs at national homes. It allows chauffeurs-truck drivers, elevator operators, guards, messengers, and telephone operators to be hired from members of the homes if the Veterans' Administration thinks they can do the work. If those jobs are filled by others, the hiring must follow civil-service rules and regulations.

5723.s: This order lets the Secretary of the Interior approve an application by the Uintah Railway Co. for a railroad right of way across certain lands in Utah. It changes a prior order that had withdrawn those lands for investigation, examination, and classification.

5722.s: This order accepts title to 15 acres of Government Island in Alameda, California, for the United States. In return, the United States gives up its rights and interests under the July 5, 1918 lease for the island. The duties, rights, powers, and responsibilities for the 15 acres are placed under the Department of Agriculture. Federal agencies already occupying Government Island are not to be disturbed unless the President directs otherwise through the Chief Coordinator.

5721.s: The order reserves certain vacant public lands along the Mississippi River as part of the Upper Mississippi River Wild Life and Fish Refuge. These lands are between Rock Island, Illinois, and Wabasha, Minnesota, and include areas in Wisconsin, Illinois, Iowa, and Minnesota. The reservation is subject to existing valid rights.

5740.s: This order sets aside a tract of land in Wakulla County, Florida, as a refuge and breeding ground for wild animals and birds. It says the land remains subject to existing valid rights and may still be used by the Department of Commerce for lighthouse purposes. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds there, or to damage the land, plants, fire safety, or government property.

5720.s: This order allows Mrs. Gladys W. Eldridge to be appointed to a clerical job in the Department of Agriculture. It says the appointment may be made without following the civil-service requirements.

5719.s: This order withdraws about 1 acre of land on Naubinway Island in Lake Michigan, subject to valid existing rights. It sets the land aside for the Department of Commerce to use for lighthouse purposes. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5718.s: This order revokes two earlier withdrawals of certain public lands in California. It affects the lands described by section, township, range, and meridian in Humboldt meridian, California.

5717.s: This order changes a 1928 order that created Public Water Reserve No. 116. It authorizes the Federal Power Commission to issue a license for Project No. 1123 on the listed lands in San Bernardino Meridian, California.

5716.s: This order transfers the records, files, and other papers of the National Commission on Law Observance and Enforcement to the Department of Justice. The department must keep them until a building for the permanent housing of government records is completed. Then the records must be delivered into that building and to the official in charge of it.

5715.s: This order restores the land known as "Barracks Lot" in Honolulu, Oahu, to its previous status for use by the Territory of Hawaii. It also removes the use restrictions that had been imposed on that land by Executive Order No. 1507.

5714.s: This order withdraws two parcels of land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the law it cites. It reserves the land for the Department of Agriculture to use in administering the Shasta National Forest as Soldier Mountain and Sugar Loaf lookout sites.

5713.s: This order changes a 1910 coal withdrawal for the land listed in Wyoming. It allows that land to be withdrawn and used to maintain air-navigation facilities. The change applies to the specific tract described in the order.

5712.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Arizona, subject to valid existing rights, pending legislation under the 1910 law as amended in 1912. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5711.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain vacant public lands in Montana from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are reserved for classification and to aid legislation. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5710.s: This order sets the airspace and nearby waters in a part of Chesapeake Bay as a naval air-space reservation and a defensive sea area.
