During that time, no aircraft or vessel may enter those areas unless the Secretary of the Navy authorizes it for national defense or other governmental purposes. Surface vessels on regular channels may pass through the defensive sea area, but not within 2 miles of the stated point. Violations are subject to penalties provided by law.

5709.s: The order withdraws certain public lands in San Bernardino meridian, California, from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. This lasts while the township is being resurveyed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5708.s: This order changes a prior land withdrawal so the Secretary of the Interior may approve an application from the Uintah Railway Co. for a railroad right of way. The right of way would cross certain lands in Utah.

5707.s: This order changes rules for foreign service residential and office quarters owned or leased long term by the United States. It says the Department of State will pay to renew and repair office furniture and to clean offices, but the officer must pay for ordinary cleaning in the residence quarters. It also adds language to section 15 about quarters used for residence purposes.

5706.s: The order allows four named women to be appointed to positions in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without meeting the civil-service rules. It applies to Mrs. Mary J. A. Hangliter, Mrs. Margaret B. Hillyard, Mrs. Catherine Lehmkuhl, and Miss Frances N. Kane. The order says each is connected to a former plate printer and describes family support needs in each case.

5705.s: This order designates Adolph G. Wolf to temporarily perform the duties of the Judge of the District Court of the United States for Porto Rico. He is authorized to sign necessary papers and records as acting judge while the regular judge is absent. This affects the District Court of the United States for Porto Rico.

5704.s: This order changes the boundaries of the Canal Zone judicial districts. It sets the Balboa Division to cover a listed area in the Canal Zone, including territory near the Rio Chagres, Quebrada Madronal, and other named landmarks. It sets the Cristobal Division to cover the rest of the Canal Zone territory described here, including Gatun Lake and its islands, except the area along the Rio Chagres upstream from the mouth of the Quebrada Madronal.

5702.s: This order withdraws the rocks making up Port Orford, Blanco, and Rogue River Reefs off the coast of Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves them as a refuge to protect sea lions, subject to existing withdrawals. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5703.s: This order revokes part of two earlier orders that created Temporary Power-Site Withdrawal No. 137 and Power-Site Reserve No. 137. It applies to the land described in the order in Wyoming.

5700.s: This order changes rules so Public Health Service officers may hold office in State, Territorial, or local health organizations if the Surgeon General recommends it and the Secretary of the Treasury approves. It also allows State, Territorial, or local health officials or employees to hold office in the Public Health Service, unless the law forbids it. These changes are meant to let the Public Health Service work with state and local health departments and to let state and local officials serve in the Public Health Service when the Surgeon General and the Secretary of the Treasury think it is needed.

5701.s: This order authorizes the appointment of Mr. John W. Harrison as an Associate Marine Engineer in the Professional Service, grade 3, at the navy yard in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with pay of $3,200 a year. It says he has about 30 years of experience with shipbuilding companies and other private contractors working on vessels for the United States Navy. The order says his experience would be of value to the Navy in inspecting shopwork assembly and installing machinery on a new cruiser to be built at that yard.

5699.s: This order revokes a 1929 withdrawal of public lands in a township in Oregon that had been set aside pending a resurvey. It opens the unreserved public lands there, subject to valid rights, to qualified ex-service men for homestead or desert land entry for 91 days after the resurvey plat is officially filed. After that, the land may be available to the general public under applicable public land laws. No rights may be claimed by settlement before entry except as allowed by the order.

5698.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of public lands in a township in Colorado that had been set aside pending a resurvey. It says the lands may be opened, if otherwise subject to disposition and subject to valid rights, to entry under the stock-raising homestead laws only for 91 days after the official filing of the plat of resurvey. During that period, qualified ex-service men may enter the land, and after that it may be open to the general public under those laws.

5697.s: This order allows Mrs. Caroline J. Skilton to be appointed to a clerical job in the Treasury Department without following the civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of George W. Skilton, who served in government work for more than fifteen years, and that she and their two young sons were left without means of support after his death.

5696.s: This order changes the civil-service rules to add one headquarters messenger job at the headquarters of the Philippine Department. That job may be filled by an honorably discharged enlisted man who has already been on duty there, without a competitive exam.

5695.s: This order allows Mrs. Marie V. Abernethy to be appointed as a clerk in the Treasury Department without regard to how long she has been away from government service. It applies to her and to the Treasury Department position she may fill.

5694.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public land in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the cited acts. It applies to the land described in the order and stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5693.s: This order changes the legal description of the Punchbowl Hill Military Reservation in Hawaii. It says the change was made because a recent survey found differences in earlier descriptions. The tract described in the order contains 35.17 acres, more or less.

5692.s: This order changes the legal description of the Aiea Military Reservation in Hawaii. It says the tract is about 10.53 acres and is subject to rights of way for the Oahu Railway & Land Co. and the Navy Department. It says the net area of the reservation is about 8.85 acres.

5691.s: This executive order changes the civil-service rules for the Veterans' Administration. It excepts certain jobs from examination, including assistant administrators, a solicitor, an executive assistant, a medical director, a director of construction service, a special counsel on insurance claims, head attorneys, control officers, some local physicians, temporary professional or technical specialists, and certain service workers when registers are impracticable.

5690.s: The order reserves and sets apart certain public lands in Zambales, Luzon, because of chromite deposits there. It also places other lands, which were no longer needed for the purpose they had been reserved for, under the control of the government of the Philippine Islands. Those lands are to be administered for the benefit of the inhabitants of the islands.

5689.s: The order changes an earlier land reservation along the U.S.-Mexico boundary line. It authorizes approval of Western Gas Co.'s application for a right of way for a pipe line to transport natural gas across certain lands in that strip.

5688.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of certain public lands in Colorado that were pending resurvey. Subject to valid rights, the lands would be opened under the homestead or desert land laws only for 91 days after the resurvey plat is filed, first for qualified ex-service men covered by the resolution. After that period, the lands would be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5687.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the townships are resurveyed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5686.s: This order changes Reservoir-Site Reserve No. 17 to allow the Federal Power Commission to issue a license for Project No. 966 on certain lands in California. It covers listed tracts in San Bernardino Meridian, California, near two described transmission-line locations. The licensee must move its project works at its own expense if the land is needed for reservoir purposes so they do not interfere with the Granite Dyke Reservoir Site.

5685.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in New Mexico that had been set aside pending a resurvey. If the lands are otherwise available, they are to be opened first to entry under the homestead or desert land laws, subject to valid rights and the terms of the named resolution. For 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat, they may be entered by qualified ex-service men, and after that they may be open to the general public under the applicable public land laws.

5684.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Utah for classification. The withdrawal is subject to valid existing claims and to existing phosphate, first-form reclamation, and power-site withdrawals. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5683.s: This order temporarily withdraws 40 acres in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for use by the State Forest Service of Oregon as a lookout station to help protect nearby government-owned and other timberlands from fire. The timber on the land remains subject to sale by the United States.

5682.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while those townships are being resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5681.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in San Bernardino meridian, California, from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in effect until the area is resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5680.s: This order revokes two exceptions from civil service examination rules. It covers the superintendent of the Hot Springs Reservation and superintendents or officers in charge of national parks or reservations. Those positions and the people holding them are then included in the competitive classified service.

5679.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of public lands in one township in Wyoming, subject to valid rights. It opens the unreserved public lands in that township to qualified ex-service men for 91 days, under the homestead or desert land laws, after the resurvey plat is officially filed. After that, the land may be available to the general public under any applicable public land law. No rights may be gained by settlement before entry or in any other way except as allowed here.

5678.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Utah that had been held pending a resurvey. It says those lands may be opened under the terms of a 1930 resolution to entry under the stock-raising homestead laws only for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat, and only by qualified ex-service men. After that, the lands may be open to the general public under those laws.

5677.s: This order revokes the earlier withdrawal of public land in one township in New Mexico that had been held pending a resurvey. It then opens the unreserved public lands there, subject to valid rights, to qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the resurvey plat is officially filed. During that time, they may enter the land under the homestead or desert land laws only, and after that the land may be open to the general public under applicable public land laws.

5676.s: This order changes the 1911 reserve order for Reservoir-Site Reserve No. 1. It authorizes the Federal Power Commission to issue a license for Project No. 1150 on the listed lands in the Willamette Meridian area.

5675.s: This order revokes a 1926 withdrawal of certain public lands in Utah that were held pending resurvey. After the official filing of the resurvey plat, the lands would be opened under set terms and conditions, first for 91 days to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws. After that, the lands would be open to the general public under any public land law that applies.

5673.s: The order excludes certain tracts of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It restores those lands to entry under the public land laws, and says the tracts had been occupied as home sites or for cannery purposes.

5674.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in California that were being held pending a resurvey. It says the lands may then be opened under the terms of a public resolution and its rules to entry under the homestead or desert land laws only for 91 days after the official resurvey plat is filed, and only for qualified ex-service men. After that period, the lands may be opened to the general public under any applicable public land law.

5672.s: This order withdraws certain listed public lands in Colorado and Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use under the law named in the order.

5671.s: This order withdraws specified public lands in Wisconsin, Minnesota, North Dakota, Montana, Wyoming, Idaho, Washington, and Oregon from settlement, location, sale, entry, or other disposition. It covers land tied to the Northern Pacific Railroad grants and is issued in aid of contemplated legislation. Any prior valid claims on the listed tracts are excepted as long as they are kept under the law and regulations.

5670.s: This order releases a 23-acre parcel of land in Oregon from a reservation that had been made for the War Department. It then makes that land part of the Siuslaw National Forest.

5669.s: This order revokes parts of two public water reserves in Montana and Utah for the listed lands. Those lands are restored to the public domain unless they are otherwise reserved or withdrawn. The land will then be subject to disposal under the laws that apply after notice is given.

5668.s: This order withdraws a specific piece of public land in Wyoming from settlement, sale, location, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It sets the land aside for use as a target range by the Wyoming National Guard. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5667.s: The order withdraws certain public lands in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It applies to sections 13 to 36 in Township 16 South, Range 9 West, and stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it. The lands are withdrawn pending a resurvey of those sections.

5666.s: This order changes an earlier rule that barred people from holding Federal and State offices at the same time. It allows people who hold State, Territorial, or municipal positions to receive appointments under the Department of Commerce, unless another law forbids it. The Secretary of Commerce may do this when the Secretary thinks it is needed for more efficient administration of the department's duties.

5665.s: This order allows A. D. Forsythe to be appointed to an existing vacancy in the Bureau of Construction and Repair in the Navy Department. The appointment is for Subprofessional Service, grade 4, at $1,620 a year, without regard to the Civil Service Act or rules. It also says Mr. Forsythe is the stepson of William G. Hughes, who worked in that bureau for 31 years.

5664.s: This order withdraws certain lands in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of use. The lands are held for the exclusive use of the United States Navy Department as an ammunition depot. The withdrawal lasts until the President or Congress revokes it.

5663.s: This order designates Horace Paul Bestor as Farm Loan Commissioner of the Federal Farm Loan Board. He will serve in that role until otherwise directed.

5661.s: This order changes the Consular Regulations. It cancels one sentence in section 21 and adds rules for who is in charge of a consular office when the principal officer is absent. It also sets the order of seniority among consular officers by grade and by commission date in some cases.

5662.s: This order adds certain temporary Department of Agriculture field jobs to the list of positions exempt from civil-service examination. It covers inspectors, scouts, trap tenders, truck drivers, and operators of mechanical equipment who work with the states to enforce the Plant Quarantine Act. These employees may serve only as long as needed and not more than 180 days in any one year, and their service must be reported.

5660.s: This order places certain lands in Nevada under the control of the Secretary of the Interior. The land had been withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, or entry and had been held for the exclusive use of the United States Navy as an ammunition depot.

5659.s: This order allows Mrs. Florence R. Hopkins to be appointed to a suitable position in the Treasury Department without following civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of Henry I. Hopkins, who served in government for 18 years and died on June 14, 1926, from injuries with an unknown cause. The order was issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Treasury.

5658.s: This order sets rules for how draft executive orders and proclamations must be written and formatted. It says they must follow Government Printing Office style, geographic names, land descriptions, and other draft requirements, and they must be sent to the Department of State in quadruplicate for review. The Department of State is given custody of the signed originals and must supervise their publication.

5657.s: This order amends Schedule A of the civil-service rules for the State Department. It changes paragraph 2 to read “Assistants to the Legal Adviser.”

5656.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in place while the township is resurveyed. It remains in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5654.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain land in Montana from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the cited laws. It reserves the land for use by the Forest Service as an addition to Duck Creek Ranger Station for the administration of the Helena National Forest.

5653.s: This order revokes part of two earlier orders that had withdrawn certain lands from use for power-site purposes. It applies to the specific described parcels in Colorado.

5652.s: The order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. This lasts while the township is being resurveyed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5651.s: This order revokes part of a previous withdrawal of certain public lands in Minnesota that were not reserved by a 1930 act of Congress. The released lands are then opened first only to entry under the homestead laws by qualified ex-service men for a set 91-day period. After that, the lands may be opened to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5650.s: This order withdraws the listed land from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves that land for public use under the named law.

5649.s: This order allows Mrs. Helen Terrill Mays to be appointed to a clerical position in the Treasury Department’s classified service without following the civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of William O. Mays, has served temporarily in the Bureau of Industrial Alcohol, and is the person affected by the order.

5648.s: This order sets new rules for accounts and returns in the Foreign Service and makes them part of the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers. It lets the Secretary of State create fiscal districts and district accounting and disbursing offices to handle the accounts, receipts, and payments of diplomatic missions, consular offices, and Foreign Service posts in those districts. Officers in those districts may have to send their accounts to the district office, and emergency drafts are allowed only in emergencies.

5647.s: This order allows income-tax returns to be open to inspection by State officers for State income-tax purposes. It also allows beneficiaries under a will to inspect returns, if they comply with the related Treasury rules and regulations.

5646.s: This order changes the boundary between the Selway and Bitterroot National Forests in Idaho. It transfers the lands south and east of the described line from the Selway National Forest to the Bitterroot National Forest. It also says no publicly owned lands are being given national-forest status for the first time or removed from it. The transfer takes effect on July 1, 1931.

5645.s: This order gives the Alien Property Custodian the President’s power under the Trading with the Enemy Act over the deposit, transfer, and payment of money and accrued interest held by the Treasurer of the United States, and over releasing and delivering property held under those laws. If the Alien Property Custodian cannot act, the power goes to the General Counsel, and then to the Director of Finance and Accounts of the Office of the Alien Property Custodian. Claims that must still be sent to the Attorney General and the President will continue to be sent that way, and any conflicting former orders are revoked.

5644.s: This order designates a long list of Foreign Service posts as unhealthful posts for retirement purposes. It affects officers who serve at those places, where service is counted at a higher rate for retirement. It also cancels earlier orders naming some of the same posts, with the cancellation effective July 1, 1931.

5643.s: This order sets rules for representation allowances and post allowances for ambassadors, ministers, diplomatic, consular, and Foreign Service officers. It says representation allowances may be used for official receptions, certain functions, tips, flowers, and other approved entertainment, but not for motor vehicles, club dues, printing or engraving, or alcoholic beverages. It also requires monthly accounting for expenses and limits post allowances to the time an officer stays in the assigned district.

5642.s: This order sets rules for the Department of State to administer the Foreign Service and cancels earlier rules that conflict with it. It lays out how people are examined, appointed, rated, promoted, and assigned, and it sets classes and salary ranges for Foreign Service officers. It also creates the Board of Foreign Service Personnel and says its work must be nonpartisan and based on efficiency records.

5641.s: This order revokes a 1906 order that reserved certain land on Yes Lake in southeastern Alaska for a salmon hatchery. It applies to the tract now identified as United States Survey No. 1981, which is 6.33 acres.

5640.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It applies while the township is being resurveyed and stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5639.s: This order changes a prior land withdrawal so the described land can be withdrawn and used as an aviation field. It applies to the land listed in Wyoming.

5638-A.s: This order assigns radio frequencies to government stations. It also lets listed stations use other frequencies for up to one month if they first send notice to the Interdepartment Radio Advisory Committee and, in some cases, the Federal Radio Commission. The order applies to government departments and stations that use radio, and it replaces a prior executive order.

5638.s: This order assigns radio frequencies to Government stations and lets certain listed experimental stations use miscellaneous frequencies if they do not cause interference. It says departments should use existing Government radio facilities when possible and should not build new stations near existing ones unless needed. It also says the Government will encourage privately owned radio facilities and may use commercial stations when Government interests require it. This order replaces Executive Order No. 5197-A.

5637.s: This order restores most of the Keaahala Military Reservation in Hawaii to the Territory of Hawaii for its use. It keeps one part of the land for military purposes and leaves a 10-foot right of way for an irrigation ditch. The United States also keeps certain roadway and water supply rights for the part of the reservation it retains.

5655.s: This order revokes part of a 1920 executive order that affected the land listed in Arizona. That land, if not otherwise reserved or withdrawn, is restored to the public domain and made subject to disposition under the laws that apply to it after a later notice and date are announced.

5636.s: This order removes attorneys of all grades from Schedule B of the civil-service rules. It places attorney positions in the Veterans' Administration in the competitive classified civil service. Veterans' Administration employees in attorney jobs who are certified by the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs as capable and efficient will be included in the classified civil service.

5634.s: This order transfers certain lands from the Mount Baker National Forest to the Snoqualmie National Forest in Washington. The transfer covers the listed areas in the order. It is set to take effect on July 1, 1931.

5635.s: This order allows Arthur B. Landt to be appointed to a temporary field agent job in the Farmers' Seed Loan Office in Grand Forks, North Dakota, without following the civil-service rules. It applies to his work in that office for as long as the work continues.

5633.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Humboldt meridian, California, from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the township is resurveyed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5632.s: This order revokes the earlier withdrawal of certain public land in North Dakota for classification and aid of legislation. It opens the land to entry under the homestead or desert land laws by qualified ex-service men for a set period, subject to valid rights and the stated rules. If the land is still unentered after that period, it may be opened to the general public under applicable public land law, and no rights may be gained by settlement in advance of entry.

5631.s: This order withdraws listed public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for municipal water supply purposes. The order affects the specific tracts described in the document, as far as title remains in the United States.

5630.s: This order returns certain land in Washington from the Navy Department to the Interior Department for disposal under law. It also reserves lot 7 and places it under the control of the Secretary of Commerce for lighthouse purposes. The land had been used for a naval radio compass station, which had been decommissioned.

5629.s: This order withdraws a small piece of land in Montana from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for public use. The land is all land within 50 feet of a well drilled by the Bowdoin Oil & Gas Co. near the east line of the southeast quarter of the southwest quarter of section 35.

5628.s: This order allows Mrs. Amy Cowing to be appointed as a clerk-typist in the Department of Agriculture. It says the appointment may be made without following the civil-service rules, and it was issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of Agriculture.

5627.s:
This order lets executive civil service officers and employees who live in Arlington County, Virginia, run for and hold local office there. It also lets them take part in campaigns for those local offices.

They must keep doing their federal jobs, and they may not take part in national or state politics in ways that break civil-service rules. If they are elected or appointed to a full-time local office, they must resign their federal job; if the local office is part-time, they may keep both jobs if there is no conflict.

5626.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to the Kickapoo Indians of Kansas that were set to expire during 1931. It extends that trust period for another 10 years.

5625.s: The order sets Saturday as a four-hour workday, not counting lunch, for clerks and other employees of the Department of the Interior’s field service. It also cancels any other orders that conflict with this rule. The head of the department may except a bureau, office, or employee for special public reasons, or when the rule would conflict with existing law.

5624.s: This order sets rules for using and caring for certain U.S. diplomatic and consular homes and offices owned or leased by the United States. It makes the ranking American representative responsible for the property, requires inventories and surveys, and says damages from neglect or improper use may be charged to that officer. It also sets rules for repairs, cleaning, furniture, fire precautions, and who may occupy the premises when an officer leaves or is absent.

5623.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It applies to the listed sections in the Mount Diablo meridian area and stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it. The lands are held this way while they are resurveyed.

5622.s: This order allows some federal employees in the Philippine Islands to be given classified status. It applies to employees who were in federal service on the date of the order, had at least seven years of faithful and exceptionally meritorious service in a classified position, and had a civil-service exam rating of at least 40. An employee who had served continuously since March 1, 1904, could be given classified status without an examination.

5621.s: This order amends consular regulations on the naturalization and citizenship of married women. It says a woman cannot be denied naturalization because of her sex or because she is married, and it changes some residence and filing rules for certain women seeking naturalization. It also says a woman citizen does not lose citizenship by marriage unless she formally renounces it, and it repeals older laws that changed a woman's citizenship based on marriage. It also gives certain wives of U.S. citizens rules about admission into the United States, with listed exceptions.

5620.s: This order allows Mrs. Dorothy I. Sinnott to be appointed to an appropriate position in the Department of Labor without following the civil-service rules. It concerns Mrs. Sinnott, who is the widow of former Representative Nicholas J. Sinnott.

5619.s: This order excludes certain lands in Montana from the Deerlodge National Forest. Subject to valid rights, the public lands in the excluded area are opened first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws where applicable, for a limited period. After that, the lands are open to the general public under any public land law that applies.

5618.s: This order removes a described piece of land in Arizona from the Crook National Forest. It reserves that land for town-site purposes, subject to valid existing claims. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5617.s: This order allows Mrs. Elsie K. Demshock to be appointed to a position in the Navy Department without following the civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of a United States Navy aviation pilot who was killed in an airplane crash while on duty.

5616.s: This order changes the boundary between the Pend Oreille and Kootenai National Forests in Idaho and Montana. It transfers some lands from the Pend Oreille National Forest to the Kootenai National Forest, and some lands from the Kootenai National Forest to the Pend Oreille National Forest. The transfers are set to take effect on July 1, 1931.

5615.s: This order transfers T. 41 N., R. 6 E., Boise meridian, from the St. Joe National Forest to the Clearwater National Forest in Idaho. The transfer is effective July 1, 1931.

5614.s: This order requires the Secretary of the Treasury to give the Director of the Bureau of the Budget a detailed report of government expenditures after each fiscal year. It also requires each executive department and independent establishment to send the Secretary a detailed statement of unexpended balances. The reports must be grouped by appropriations and by general fund, special funds, trust funds, and special deposit accounts.

5613.s: This order enlarges Bishops Point Military Reservation in the Territory of Hawaii by adding land between the reservation and the harbor line. The enlarged reservation will include about 4.21 acres in all. It also reserves a right of way for the Navy Department over the reservation to any landing built on the shore if the water there is deep enough for naval launches to moor.

5612.s: This order creates a Council of Personnel Administration in the Federal Government. It is meant to improve employment and personnel management and to promote the welfare of federal employees. The council includes leaders from several departments and agencies, and it will study current personnel practices, share information, and prepare plans for improvement and coordination. Departments may carry out projects approved by the council and assign staff to help with the work.

5611.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Arizona from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the cited laws. The lands are to be used in connection with the San Carlos Indian Irrigation Project, and any valid rights or claims started before March 24, 1931, are protected.

5610.s: This order changes civil-service rules for future examinations. It gives added rating points and higher placement on the register to certain honorably discharged veterans with service-connected disabilities, as well as some widows and wives of honorably discharged soldiers, sailors, and marines. It also requires appointing officers who pass over a veteran for a nonveteran to file their reasons with the Civil Service Commission.

5609.s: This order directs that certain employees of the Bureau of National Homes of the Veterans' Administration, who are not inmates, be placed in the classified civil service if the Civil Service Commission gets general certification that they are capable and efficient. It does not apply to employees whose duties would normally not place them in the classified service, including chefs, cooks, bakers, attendants, and unskilled laborers. Employees appointed within 60 days before July 1, 1931, are not to be classified unless they were appointed under civil-service law and rules.

5608.s: This order designates the customs station at Sasabe, Arizona, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 26. It applies to the customs station at Sasabe and takes effect 30 days after the order is signed.

5607.s: This order corrects the land description in a previous order that restored certain land on Oahu to the Territory of Hawaii for road purposes. It changes the descriptions of two parcels in the Kahauiki Military Reservation (Fort Shafter) and the Hawaii Arsenal Military Reservation. The order gives the revised boundary details and acreage for those parcels.

5606.s: The order reserves certain public lands in Churchill County, Nevada, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and wild animals. The land stays subject to existing valid rights and to use by the Department of the Interior for irrigation and other incidental purposes. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds, take nests or eggs, damage natural growth, leave fire unattended, or injure United States property.

5605.s: This order revokes a 1928 executive order that set rules for paying actual expenses and per diem allowances to civilian officers and employees while they travel on official business away from their regular duty stations. It says those rules, as amended, are set out in the amended Standardized Government Travel Regulations approved on April 21, 1931. The new regulations become effective July 1, 1931.

5605-A.s: This order changes an earlier radio frequency assignment for government radio stations. It deletes the Navy’s assignment of 68 kc.

5604.s: This order allows Mrs. Cecil Alexander to be appointed to a suitable job in the Post Office Department or its field service without following the civil-service rules. It applies to Mrs. Alexander, who was working as a contact clerk in the postmaster’s office in Dallas, Texas.

5603.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the townships are resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5602.s: This order transfers certain government lands, buildings, improvements, and furnishings in the Virgin Islands to the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Interior for use in administering the Virgin Islands government. Items listed in Class One are transferred permanently, while items in Class Two are transferred temporarily after the naval authorities leave, if they are kept in good repair and returned when needed for naval uses. Other naval property in St. Thomas stays under the control of the Secretary of the Navy.

5601.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain lots in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the cited laws. It affects those lands and says the withdrawal is for classification and to aid proposed legislation unless revoked by the President or by Congress.

5600.s: This order withdraws certain lands within the Umatilla Federal Irrigation Project in Oregon and sets them aside for the Department of Agriculture to use as an agricultural field station. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5598.s: This order revokes part of a 1911 executive order that had created the Coal Land Withdrawal in New Mexico No. 6. It applies to the specific lands listed in the order. The revocation is made to aid an authorized exchange of lands under the act of March 3, 1921.

5599.s: The order directs that Captain Washington C. McCoy, master of the U.S.M.V. Kilkenny in the Bureau of Navigation, be placed in the classified service. It says this is based on a recommendation from the Commissioner of Navigation, with the Secretary of Commerce agreeing, and it refers to his record, skill as a navigator, and faithful service.

5597.s: This order revokes part of a 1923 executive order that created Public Water Reserve No. 86 for the listed land in New Mexico. It restores that land to the public domain, unless it is otherwise reserved or withdrawn, and makes it subject to the laws that apply after notice is announced.

5596.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in a township in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it, and it applies while the township is being resurveyed.

5594.s: This order withdraws certain public land in Nevada and Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves that land for public use. The order lists the specific land sections covered in each state.

5595.s: This order directs that flags on the White House and public buildings in the District of Columbia and Ohio be flown at half mast. It applies on the day it was signed and on the day of the funeral service in Cincinnati, Ohio, for Nicholas Longworth, a late Member and Speaker of the House of Representatives.

5593.s: This order withdraws the listed land in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves that land for public use.

5592.s: This order transfers control and administration of certain lands in Wyoming from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of War. The lands are the same lands that were withdrawn to protect the water supply of Fort Francis E. Warren. The transfer is subject to all valid existing easements, rights, and claims on the lands.

5591.s: This order allows Mrs. Grace McMahan Tyndall to be appointed to a position under the War Department. It says this appointment may be made without following the civil-service rules. The order notes that Mrs. Tyndall is the widow of Lieut. Frank B. Tyndall, who was killed in line of duty while piloting an Army airplane during a night flight.

5590.s: This order revokes part of Executive Order of December 6, 1915, that created Petroleum Reserve No. 40 in Montana. It applies only to the specific lands listed in the order.

5589.s: This order reserves the Climax Mill Site and Crown Mill Site lands in Idaho for town-site purposes. The lands are to be handled under federal town-site laws, subject to valid existing rights, unless the President or Congress revokes the order.

5588.s: This order revokes several clauses in Schedule A of the civil service rules. It also adds a rule allowing one private secretary or confidential clerk, without examination, for the head or assistant head of each independent establishment and for each member of certain commissions or boards when those people are appointed by the President.

5587.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of public lands in a township in Colorado pending a resurvey. It says the unreserved public lands there, if otherwise available, must be opened first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws for 91 days after the official resurvey plat is filed. After that period, the lands may be opened to the general public under any applicable public land law.

5586.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in North Dakota for classification as to whether they are suitable for wildlife refuge purposes. It applies to the public lands in the listed area, subject to valid existing claims. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5585.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in effect while a resurvey of the townships is pending, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5584.s: This order changes the civil service rules to include dentists in a rule for physicians and dentists in the Indian Service who are paid no more than $1,200 a year. It also says their outside private practice must be allowed by law and subject to approval by the commission.

5583.s: This order announces the rates to be used for rental and subsistence allowances for officers of the various services entitled to them. The rates are set as effective for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1932.

5582.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain Alaska lands from settlement, location, sale, entry, lease, or other disposal. The lands are reserved for investigation, examination, and classification. It applies only to the listed lands, subject to valid existing claims.

5581.s: This order withdraws a tract of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of disposal. It applies to the described land, except for any prior valid claim that was legally started and kept, and it stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5580.s: This order extends the trust period on certain lands patented to the Agua Caliente Band of Mission Indians in California. The extension lasts for 10 more years.

5578.s: This order changes the customs port name from San Francisco, California, to Port of San Francisco-Oakland. It also extends the port limits to include all points on San Francisco Bay, effective 30 days after the order.

5579.s: This order sets aside a described area in Garden County, Nebraska, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and wild animals. It makes it unlawful there to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds, or to take or destroy nests or eggs, except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. It also bars cutting or burning natural growth, leaving fires unattended, and injuring United States property.

5577.s: This order revokes the earlier rule that made Oakland, California, a customs port of entry. Oakland, Alameda, Berkeley, Emeryville, and San Leandro are placed back within the port limits of San Francisco, California, effective immediately.

5576.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in New Mexico that had been set aside pending a resurvey. Subject to valid rights, those lands may be opened under the homestead or desert land laws only by qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plats. After that, the lands may be opened to the general public under any public land law that applies.

5575.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to members of the Fond du Lac Band of Chippewa Indians of Minnesota. It applies to allotments whose trust period was set to expire during 1931 and extends that period for 10 years.

5573.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Utah for classification. The lands will be reviewed to decide whether they should be included in a national monument. The withdrawal is subject to valid existing rights and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5574.s: This order excludes a tract of land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest and restores it to entry under the applicable public land laws. The land was previously occupied for fish-cannery purposes. It covers about 21 acres.

5571.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Arizona from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. It keeps those lands withdrawn while they wait for a resurvey of the townships. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5572.s: This order changes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Idaho. It allows the Secretary of the Interior to approve L. E. Strout’s application for a right of way for an irrigation project on land in Idaho.

5570.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule IX to allow some employees who were involuntarily separated during or at the end of probation, and were not at fault, to be reinstated. They may serve a new probation in any part of the service in a position they have qualified for, or can qualify for in a noncompetitive examination, if other civil service rules allow it.

5569.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in T. 26 S., R. 31 E., Tallahassee meridian, Florida. It opens those lands to entry under the homestead laws only for 91 days, starting 63 days after the order, for qualified ex-service men. After that, the lands may be open to the general public under any public land law that applies.

5568.s: This order excludes a tract of land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest and restores it to entry under the public land laws. The land was previously occupied for home-site purposes. It covers about 0.92 acres.

5566.s: This order places the administration of the government of the Virgin Islands under the supervision of the Secretary of the Interior. It also gives the Secretary of the Interior control over expenditures and the hiring and salaries of certain government workers. Naval officers, nurses, enlisted men, and clerical employees in the island governments are to stay in their jobs until replaced, and the governor must report to the President through the Secretary of the Interior.

5567.s: This order revokes part of the 1915 order creating Power-Site Reserve No. 512, as modified in 1916, for the lands described in the order. The revocation does not apply to the area within fifty feet on each side of the center line of the installed pipe line of the Public Utilities Consolidated Corporation, successor to the Mission Range Power Company.

5564.s: This order revokes parts of earlier orders that created Power-Site Reserve No. 566 and Power-Site Reserve No. 145. It applies to the specific lands described in Oregon.

5563.s: This order allows Mrs. Margaret Kane to be appointed as an operative in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without following the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of a former bureau plate printer and that she has seven children, five of whom depend on her, and does not have enough support.

5565.s: This order changes the rules for appointments to the Foreign Service. It keeps both written and oral exams, but Foreign Service clerks with five years of satisfactory service are exempt from the written exam. It also says only people in certain age ranges, U.S. citizens, and people of good character and suitable physical, mental, and temperamental qualifications may be certified as eligible, with an exception for some clerks and people specially designated by the President.

5562.s: This order changes an earlier 1900 order to add more land on the eastern end of Hom Island off the coast of Mississippi for lighthouse purposes. It applies to the land described as lots 1, 2, and 3 in section 25, township 9 south, range 6 west, St. Stephens meridian, Mississippi. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5561.s: This order returns about 30 acres of land from a U.S. Department of Agriculture experiment station in Hawaii to the government of the Territory of Hawaii. The land is to be used with nearby land for home sites by the people of Hawaii.

5560.s: This order amends Schedule A of the civil service rules. It adds one private secretary or confidential clerk for each member of the Federal Power Commission to the jobs excepted from the examination requirement.

5559.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The withdrawal is for contemplated legislation that would grant those lands for the benefit of the Colorado School of Mines. It stays in effect until that legislation is enacted or the withdrawal is revoked.

5558.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in three townships in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The lands stay withdrawn while a resurvey is pending. The order remains in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5557.s: This order extends the trust period for allotments made to Indians on the Pine Ridge Reservation in South Dakota. It applies to allotments whose trust period would expire during 1931 and extends that period for 10 years.

5556.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to members of the Prairie Band of Potawatomi Indians of Kansas. It applies to allotments whose trust period expires during 1931 and extends that period for 10 years.

5555.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in T. 15 N., R. 18 W., New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It does this while a resurvey of that township is pending. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5554.s: This order allows Mrs. Helen R. Witt to be appointed to an appropriate position in the Interstate Commerce Commission. It says her appointment may be made without following the civil service rules.

5553.s: This order allows Mrs. Nixon S. Plummer to be appointed to a position in the Federal Trade Commission without following the civil service rules. It says the commission’s chairman recommended her because her husband is ill, she must support herself and her small daughter, and she has the education and experience to be useful to the commission.

5552.s: This order removes certain Utah lands from an earlier withdrawal of federal lands containing oil shale. It says trust patents can be issued to Ma-chook-a-rats (Chester) and Jimmie Colorow, two Uncompahgre Ute Indians, for the lands allotted to them.

5551.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in two New Mexico townships from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the townships are resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5549.s: This order cancels Chapter X of the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers on citizenship and replaces it with new wording. It directs embassies, legations, and other missions to follow the citizenship instructions in Article X of the Consular Regulations.

5550.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, or other disposition. The lands are reserved for classification and to aid the administration and control of government-owned oil and gas deposits in the Kettleman Hills field.

5548.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in two townships in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while those townships are being resurveyed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5547.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in effect until the lands are resurveyed or until the President or Congress revokes it.

5546.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to Indians of the Cheyenne River Reservation in South Dakota that were set to expire during 1931. The extension lasts for 10 more years.

5545.s: This order revokes a civil service rule that allowed advisers, called disciplinarians, in the Indian Service to be appointed without a competitive exam. It says those positions should be filled competitively instead. People already in those jobs who are certified as efficient by the Department of the Interior may be given classified status.

5544.s: This order adds a new civil service exception for certain Public Health Service research associates. It covers research associates holding fellowships for a fixed term of service in the National Institute of Health under the act approved May 26, 1930. Their qualifications must be approved by the commission.

5543.s: This order revokes part of a 1912 executive order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 283. It applies to the land described as Boise Meridian, Township 9 South, Range 14 East, section 11, lot 3.

5542.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in San Bernardino meridian, California, from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It stays in effect while a resurvey of that township is pending, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5540.s: This order sets aside an area in Washoe County, Nevada, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for wild animals and birds. It says the area must be used as the Charles Sheldon Wild Life Refuge. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds there, or to cut or burn natural growth or damage U.S. property.

5541.s: This order revokes parts of earlier power-site withdrawals and power-site reserves for the lands listed in the order. It covers several land parcels in Oregon under the Willamette Meridian. The revoked areas were part of Temporary Power-Site Withdrawals and Power-Site Reserves numbered 24, 60, 61, 64, 65, and 145.

5539.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to Indians of the Ponca Reservation in Oklahoma that were set to expire during 1931. The extension lasts for 10 more years.

5538.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Township 7 South, Range 80 West in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It applies until the township is resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5536.s: This order revokes part of a 1913 order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 397. It affects the listed lands in Montana Meridian areas described in the order.

5537.s: This order revokes part of a 1913 order that created Potash Reserve No. 2 in California. It applies to the listed lands in Mount Diablo Meridian, Township 25 South, Range 43 East, section 31, lots 4 and 9.

5535.s: This order revokes part of a 1915 order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 510. It applies to the described lands in Montana.

5534.s: This order withdraws certain listed public lands in Montana and Nevada from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use. The order applies only to the specific parcels named in the document.

5533.s: This order changes the reserve for land near Odell Lake in the headwaters of the Deschutes River. It lets the Federal Power Commission issue a license for a minor power project on the described land. If the land is later needed for the Odell Lake Reservoir Site, the licensee must move the project works downstream at its own expense so they do not interfere with a dam or other structures.

5532.s: This order changes the 1911 reserve order for Reservoir-Site Reserve No. 1 so the Federal Power Commission can issue a license for Project No. 1129. It applies to the described lands in T. 27 N., R. 16 E., sec. 10, in the Willamette Meridian.

5531.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the township is resurveyed and remains in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5530.s: This order abolishes Two Harbors, Minnesota, as a customs port of entry. It applies to Customs Collection District No. 36, with headquarters at Duluth, Minnesota, and Superior, Wisconsin, and takes effect 30 days after the order.

5529.s: This order designates Mrs. Leafie E. Dietz to sign the President’s name on land patents. She had been appointed by the Secretary of the Interior as a clerk to sign land patents.

5528.s: This order restores a tract of land on the island of Hawaii to its previous status for use by the Territory of Hawaii. The land had been set aside for public purposes as an addition to the Upolu Airplane Landing Field. It covers 57 2/10 acres.

5527.s: This order allows Mrs. Mildred Barnes Mclnturff to be appointed to an appropriate job in the Department of Commerce without following the civil service rules. It says she is the wife of George F. Mclnturff, Jr., a former Department of Commerce employee who recently had to leave because of his physical condition.

5526.s: This order changes several parts of the Consular Regulations to match U.S. laws and simpler administrative methods. It shifts some authority from the Comptroller General to the Secretary of State for certain accounts, claims, and approvals, and it changes a sight draft rule from 15 days to 5 days. It also cancels one consular fee item and sets new rules for final accounts and payments when a Foreign Service officer has resigned, retired, or otherwise left the service.

5525.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Utah from entry for classification and to help with legislation. It applies to the land described in the order and is subject to valid existing claims and an existing stock driveway withdrawal. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5524.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of public lands in a township in Colorado that had been held pending a resurvey. It says the lands, subject to valid rights, will be opened under the terms of a public resolution to qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat. After that, the lands may be opened to the general public under any public land law that applies.

5523.s: The order allows Mr. John W. Martyn to be classified as an administrative assistant and chief clerk in the War Department. It says this is based on his long service in the Office of the Secretary of War, his service in the legislative branch, and his temporary classified service after passing examinations.

5521.s: This order restores several parcels of land from the Fort Shafter and Hawaii Arsenal military reservations to the Government of the Territory of Hawaii. The land is to be used for the proposed extension of Middle Street. It also says fences, fish-pond walls, and other needed work must be done at no cost to the United States and to the satisfaction of the Commanding General, Hawaiian Department. A road for the United States, with a railroad crossing and gates, must also be built at no cost to the United States.

5522.s: This order temporarily withdraws public lands in a described area of Arizona for classification and in aid of legislation. The withdrawal is subject to prior valid claims made under law. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5520.s: This order allows Mrs. Lulie Hunt Turnipseed to be appointed to a suitable position in the Treasury Department without following the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of a commissioned medical officer of the Public Health Service who died while in service.

5519.s: This order keeps Robert Peet Skinner on active duty in the Foreign Service for as long as needed, up to five years from February 24, 1931. It applies to Skinner, who is the envoy extraordinary and minister plenipotentiary to Greece.

5517.s: This order removes a tract of land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest. The land had been occupied as a home site and is restored to entry under the public land laws. It covers about 4.25 acres.

5518.s: The order revokes a previous withdrawal of certain public lands in two townships in New Mexico that had been held pending a resurvey. It says those lands, if otherwise available, must be opened first to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws for 91 days after the resurvey plats are filed. After that, the lands may be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5516.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to members of the Confederated Bands of Cayuse, Umatilla, and Walla Walla Indians on the Umatilla Reservation in Oregon. It applies to allotments whose trust period ends during 1931. The extension lasts for 10 years.

5515.s: This order revokes a previous order that reserved Bird or Hat Island in Great Salt Lake, Utah, for use by the Department of Agriculture. The island had been set apart as a refuge and breeding ground for wild animals and birds.

5514.s: The order closes federal executive departments and independent government offices in the District of Columbia on Wednesday, December 24, 1930. It also excuses federal employees in the District of Columbia from duty that day, except for those excepted for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law.

5513.s: This order amends the civil service rules for certain State Department jobs. It adds some former United States diplomatic or consular officers, or career foreign service officers, who served abroad for at least four years, for work as administrative officers or executive advisers. The jobs must be in positions with salary comparable to the associate professional grade or higher.

5512.s: This order withdraws described public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by law. It is meant to aid a proposed legislative withdrawal of these lands to protect and augment the city of Los Angeles' water supply system. It affects the specific tracts of public land listed in the order.

5511.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Louisiana from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be classified while a decision is made about whether to include them in a national forest. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5510.s: This order revokes part of two earlier orders that created Temporary Power-Site Withdrawal No. 5 and Power-Site Reserve No. 5. The revocation applies to the listed lands in Wyoming.

5509.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of public lands in a township in New Mexico that was pending a resurvey. It says the lands, if otherwise subject to disposition, must be opened for 91 days under the homestead or desert land laws only, and only to qualified ex-service men named in the resolution. After that, the lands may be open to the general public under any public land law that applies. No rights may be gained by settling on the lands before entry except as allowed here.

5508.s: This order temporarily withdraws unreserved public lands in listed townships in Utah for classification. The lands are also set aside for flood control and for protecting watersheds, subject to valid existing claims. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5507.s: This order abolishes Paducah, Kentucky, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 42. The change takes effect 30 days after the date of the order and affects customs operations in that district.

5506.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of certain public lands in two townships in Colorado, pending resurvey. It says the unreserved lands in those townships may be opened, subject to valid rights, to qualified ex-service men for 91 days after the resurvey plats are officially filed. After that, the lands may be opened to the general public under any applicable public land law.

5505.s: This order places Dog Island in the Mississippi Sound, south of Biloxi, under the control of the Secretary of the Interior. The land had been reserved for military purposes, and it is to be handled for disposition under the law named in the order or as otherwise provided by law.

5504.s: This order withdraws certain public land in Idaho from settlement, sale, location, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It sets the land aside for use as a target range by Company A, 116th Engineers, Idaho National Guard. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5503.s: This order allows Mrs. Pearl McIntosh to be appointed to a suitable job in the General Accounting Office without following the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of a longtime government employee, has four children who depend on her, and could be used in sorting and filing postal savings certificates in the Post Office Department division of the office.

5501.s: This order allows Mrs. Eva MacFate to be reinstated to an appropriate position in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing. It says this may be done even though she served slightly less than the five years normally needed under civil service rules.

5502.s: This order lets people in the Virgin Islands who are lawfully allowed to sell, dispense, prescribe, or distribute opium or coca leaves get those drugs from registered persons in the continental United States for legitimate medical purposes. The order must be approved by the Director of Prohibition of the Virgin Islands, and approved orders must be used within two months. The Director must keep records and send reports, and the Governor of the Virgin Islands is responsible for enforcing the order. Shipments that do not follow these rules can be subject to the penalties in the Narcotic Act.

5500.s: This order reserves a tract of land on the Richardson Highway north of Chitina, Alaska, for the use of the Alaska Road Commission. It bars that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The reserved area is about 12 acres and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5499.s: This order revokes part of two earlier land withdrawals made for coal-land classification in Utah. It applies only to the lands listed in the order, after the Director of the Geological Survey classified them. It says other withdrawals or reservations are not changed.

5498.s: This order reserves a described area in Imperial County, California, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and wild animals. The land is still subject to existing valid rights and to use by the Department of the Interior for irrigation and other incidental purposes. It makes it unlawful in the reservation to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds, or to damage the land, fire, or United States property.

5497.s: This order revokes part of a 1916 order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 547. It applies to the specific lands listed in New Mexico.

5496.s: This order revokes part of a 1915 withdrawal of land in Nevada that created Public Water Reserve No. 29. The land within a quarter of a mile of Allen Spring is restored to the public domain, unless it is already reserved or withdrawn. It becomes subject to disposal under the laws that apply there, on a date and after notice to be announced later.

5495.s: This order withdraws certain public land in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the listed land for public use. It affects the specific land sections named in the order.

5493.s: This order places seven parcels of land from the Augur Barracks military reservation under the control of the government of the Philippine Islands. The land is to be administered for the benefit of the inhabitants there. It says the land is no longer needed for the military purpose for which it was reserved.

5494.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Washington. It opens the unreserved lands in those areas, subject to valid rights, to qualified ex-service men for entry under the homestead or desert land laws for 91 days after the resurvey plats are officially filed. After that, the lands may be available to the general public under applicable public land laws.

5492.s: This order revokes part of the 1919 withdrawal that created Public Water Reserve No. 62 for the listed land in Colorado. That land, if it is not otherwise reserved or withdrawn, is restored to the public domain and can be disposed of under the laws that apply after notice is announced.

5491.s: This order authorizes the U.S. Civil Service Commission to use eligible registers from the federal civil service to fill some District of Columbia government jobs. It says appointments are to be made after tests of qualifications and under rules agreed on by the District commissioners and the Civil Service Commission. It also says appointments and promotions in the Metropolitan Police and Fire Departments are already made under the Civil Service Act and Rules.

5490.s: This order revokes part of two earlier orders that had set aside certain lands in Montana as a temporary power-site withdrawal and a power-site reserve. It affects the specific lands described in the order.

5489.s: The order withdraws a listed piece of land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves that land for public use. This affects anyone who might try to settle on, claim, buy, or enter that land.

5488.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in two townships in Colorado that were pending resurvey. It says the unreserved public lands in one township will be opened first to qualified ex-service men for 91 days under the homestead or desert land laws, if the land is otherwise available. After that, the land may be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5487.s: This order amends the description of the Fort Armstrong Military Reservation in the Territory of Hawaii. It sets out the boundaries of two tracts of land and says they cover 83.301 acres and 1.661 acres, with parts above high tide and parts submerged.

5486.s: This order revokes parts of earlier orders that set aside certain lands in Oregon along the McKenzie River and its tributaries for power-site and water-power purposes. It affects the specific listed parcels in the Willamette Meridian.

5485.s: This order revokes a 1927 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in New Mexico while a resurvey was pending. It affects the public lands in Township 20 North, Ranges 6 and 7 East, New Mexico principal meridian.

5484.s: This order withdraws public lands in two townships in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while a resurvey is done, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5483.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in townships 4 and 5 south, range 8 west, in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while those townships are resurveyed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5482.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Idaho from use, subject to valid existing rights, while legislation is pending. The lands stay withdrawn unless the President or Congress revokes the order.

5481.s: This order temporarily withdraws a described tract of public land in Idaho for use by the Department of Agriculture of the United States. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it, and it is subject to valid existing claims.

5480.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from use for classification and to aid legislation. It applies to lands in T. 41 N., R. 116 W. that are not in a national forest and have not already been withdrawn. The withdrawal is subject to the listed laws and to prior valid claims made under law.

5479.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule X on transfers in the nonapportioned service. It allows transfers within an office, within the same branch of the field service of a department or office, among military staff departments, and from the War Department to any military staff department without a certificate from the commission, unless a regulation says otherwise. It also removes the phrases about transfers among different offices of the same customs district and among post offices.

5478.s: This order withdraws certain listed public land in California, Montana, New Mexico, and Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves that land for public use.

5477.s: This order changes Power-Site Reserve No. 377 in Utah so the Secretary of the Interior may approve an application from the Uinta Pipe Line Co. for a right of way for a telephone and telegraph line. The line would cross certain lands within the reserve.

5476.s: This order transfers certain War Department duties to the Veterans' Administration. It covers payment of annuities and duties related to artificial limbs and trusses. It also transfers the civilian personnel, records, papers, and public property tied to those duties. The transfer takes effect on December 1, 1930.

5475.s: This order designates the customs station of Lake Charles, Louisiana, as a customs port of entry. It applies to Customs Collection District No. 21, with headquarters at Port Arthur, Texas, and takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

5474.s: This order extends the trust period on certain homesteads made to named Indians of the Niobrara or Santee Reservation in Nebraska. The extension lasts for 10 years from the date when the trust would have expired. It affects the listed individuals and the homesteads tied to them.

5473.s: This order sets a process for changes the Personnel Classification Board makes to existing job allocations. The board must give the department head notice, and the change takes effect after 30 days unless the department head files a protest. If there is a protest, the change goes to the President and does not take effect unless the President approves it.

5472.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry, with some exceptions under existing law. It is meant to aid proposed legislative withdrawal of those lands to protect and augment the city of Los Angeles' water supply system. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5471.s: This order changes the civil service rules for the Post Office Department. It adds temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers needed for part-time or intermittent work in the Postal Service for holiday or seasonal business through February 1, 1931.

5470.s: This order adds Triangle Island and nearby small islands, rocks, and underwater lands to the Nunivak Island Reservation in Alaska. It sets those lands aside for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for wild birds, game, and fur-bearing animals. The lands remain subject to existing valid rights and to the rules for the reservation only as they apply to wildlife refuge use.

5469.s: This order changes Consular Regulations rules about inventories, office reports, and the transfer of consular property. It requires consular officers to check and report government property, keep detailed inventories, and send transfer forms and office reports to the Department of State. It also says property cannot be removed from an inventory without advance approval from the department.

5468.s: This order changes the instructions for diplomatic officers on keeping track of government property. Each diplomatic representative must keep a detailed inventory of all government property in the mission, and a new inventory must be sent to the department only when a new diplomatic mission is set up or when the department tells the officer to do so. It also sets out how the inventory must be prepared, filed, and checked when an officer is transferred or leaves on home leave.

5467.s: This order revokes part of the June 8, 1926 order that created Reservoir-Site Reserve No. 17. The revocation applies to the described lands in California under the Mount Diablo Meridian.

5466.s: This order extends the trust period for allotments made to members of the Cass Lake, Leech Lake, White Oak Point, and Winnibigoshish bands of Chippewa Indians of Minnesota. It applies to allotments whose trust period was set to expire in 1930 and extends them for 10 more years. One listed allotment, number 902 for Way me no gwon, who was deceased, is excepted.

5465.s: This order withdraws 6.22 acres of public land in Solano County, California, from settlement, location, entry, sale, and other forms of appropriation. It reserves that land for military purposes as an addition to the Benicia Arsenal Military Reservation.

5464.s: This order directs the Secretary of Agriculture to help the Commissioner of Patents carry out the plant patents law. The department may provide information, do research on special problems, or assign officers and employees when the Commissioner asks.

5463.s: This order cancels Chapter XVIII of the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers, which covered how to correspond with the Department. It replaces that chapter with a rule saying the Department of State will set the rules for the form and sending of correspondence from time to time.
