It affects diplomatic officers and their correspondence with the Department of State.

5462.s: This order temporarily withdraws about 10 acres of land in Arizona near the international boundary with Mexico from settlement, sale, location, or entry. The land is reserved for customs and immigration inspection purposes at the boundary line. It does not affect valid existing rights, and the withdrawal stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5461.s: This order revokes part of a 1915 power-site reserve for lands near Solomon Gulch and Uno Creek in Alaska. It affects lands within one-quarter mile of those streams, except for lands included in Project No. 1101 near Solomon Gulch.

5460.s: This order revokes part of the 1918 order that created Petroleum Reserve No. 61 in Colorado for the lands listed here. Those lands, unless they are already reserved or withdrawn for something else, are restored to the public domain and made available under the laws that apply to them.

5459.s: This order places the position of Shipping Commissioner at the ports of the United States in the competitive classified service. It also supersedes Executive Order No. 3807 of March 15, 1923.

5458.s: This order changes a previous order that withdrew certain public lands in Alaska for lighthouse purposes. It updates the land description to match the official survey and names Lot 3 in section 26, Township 59 South, Range 79 East, Copper River meridian, containing 41.25 acres.

5457.s: This order changes an earlier order about part of Amaknak Island in Alaska and keeps some of the land from being restored to the public domain. It revokes an 1901 withdrawal of certain lands and excludes the lands set aside for lighthouse purposes and for the Navy Department’s wireless station.

5456.s: This order revokes part of a 1913 order that had created Power-Site Reserve No. 393. The change applies to the listed lands in Salt Lake Meridian, including parts of Township 10 North, Range 1 East and Range 2 East in Utah.

5455.s: This order extends the limits of Customs Collection District No. 8, based in Rochester, New York. It adds Allegany and Tioga counties in New York to that customs district. The change takes effect 30 days after the order is signed.

5454.s: This order revokes parts of earlier land withdrawal and power-site reserve orders for the lands listed in Uinta Meridian, Utah. The revoked lands are in Township 1 South, Range 4 West; Township 2 South, Range 4 West; Township 2 South, Range 3 West; and part of Township 2 South, Range 3 West under another reserve order. It affects only the specific tracts named in the order.

5453.s: This order designates Wichita, Kansas, as a port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 45, with headquarters at St. Louis, Missouri. It takes effect 30 days after the date of the order. It affects customs processing in Wichita.

5451.s: This order temporarily withdraws 40 acres in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be used as a lookout station for cooperative forest protection work. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5452.s: This order withdraws public lands in Township 26 North, Range 11 West in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the township is resurveyed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5450.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Alaska from settlement, sale, location, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The lands are set aside for use as a radio station for the Washington-Alaska Military Cable and Telegraph System, subject to valid existing rights and prior withdrawals.

5449.s: This order excludes two tracts of land from the Tongass National Forest in Alaska. One tract had been used for home-site purposes and is restored to entry under the public land laws. The other tract includes the village of Loring and is reserved to be disposed of for town-site purposes, subject to valid existing rights.

5448.s: This order revokes part of a 1915 order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 514. It applies to the land described in White River, Arkansas.

5447.s: This order reserves lots 1, 2, and 3 in block 12 of the Federal Addition to the town-site of Seward, Alaska, for the use of the Department of Agriculture. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5446.s: This order revokes a 1923 withdrawal of certain public lands in California that had been held pending a resurvey. It then opens those lands, if otherwise available, only to qualified ex-service men under the homestead and desert-land laws for 91 days. After that period, the lands would be open to the general public under applicable public land laws.

5445.s: This order extends the limits of the port of Marshfield, Oregon. It adds all points on Coos Bay in Oregon to the port limits, along with Marshfield and North Bend.

5444.s: This order designates Lawrence, Massachusetts, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 4, with headquarters at Boston. It also includes the townships of Lawrence, Methuen, and Andover within the limits of that port.

5443.s: This order revokes part of a 1913 order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 364 in California. It applies only to the lands described in the order at Mount Diablo Meridian.

5442.s: This order allows Mrs. James R. Bennett to be appointed to a clerical position in the Detroit post office without following the civil service rules. It says this is because her husband, a former post office carrier in Detroit, was separated from service because of permanent disability before he would have become eligible for a disability annuity under the retirement law then in force.

5441.s: This order reserves four lots in the town-site of Nenana, Alaska, for the use of the Alaska Railroad. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5439.s: This order changes the boundary of the Tongass National Forest near Petersburg, Alaska. It removes certain described lands from the forest and adds nearby lands between those areas and the forest. The excluded public lands are opened to entry under the homestead laws by qualified ex-service men for a set period, and after that they may be open to the general public under applicable public land laws.

5438.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Arizona for classification and to help with legislation. It applies subject to valid existing claims and stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5440.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Utah that had been held pending a resurvey. It says the lands, if otherwise available, will be opened under the terms of a public resolution and the related regulations. For 91 days after the resurvey plat is officially filed, the lands may be entered only under the homestead or desert-land laws by qualified ex-service men, and after that they may be available to the general public under applicable public land laws.

5436.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming for classification and to aid legislation. It applies to the specific land described in the order and is subject to valid existing claims. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5437.s: This order allows Mrs. Frances Kearney to be appointed as a clerk in the classified service of the Bureau of Prohibition in the Department of Justice without following the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of former Federal Prohibition Agent Dale F. Kearney and that she has two young children and no means of support.

5435.s: This order lets the Secretary of State grant diplomatic visas to diplomatic and consular officers of foreign governments in the United States, along with their immediate families, so they can reenter the United States. The visas may be valid for up to two years, and people with these visas do not have to get their passports visaed by U.S. diplomatic or consular officers abroad before returning.

5434.s: This order revokes part of a 1926 withdrawal of certain public lands in Montana. It opens those lands to entry under the homestead or desert-land laws by qualified ex-servicemen for 91 days, starting 63 days after the order. If the lands are still unentered after that, they are open to appropriation by the general public under applicable public land laws.

5433.s: This order revokes earlier withdrawals for certain public lands in Montana. It opens the unreserved lands to entry under the homestead or desert-land laws by qualified ex-service men for 91 days, starting 63 days after the order. If the lands are still unentered after that, they may be opened to the general public under any public land law. No one may gain rights by settling on the land before entry except as allowed by the order.

5432.s: This order revokes part of a 1914 order that had withdrawn certain land in San Bernardino Meridian, California. The listed land that is not otherwise reserved or withdrawn is restored to the public domain and will be subject to disposition under the laws that apply after notice is announced.

5431.s: This order allows Mrs. Robert D. Freeman to be appointed as a clerk in the Bureau of Prohibition in the Department of Justice without meeting the civil service rules. Mrs. Freeman is the widow of a former Prohibition agent and has a 2-year-old son. The order says she does not have adequate means of support.

5430.s: This order revokes parts of two earlier land withdrawal orders for the lands described in Clark Fork, Montana. It affects the listed sections in Township 11 North, Range 15 West, under the Montana Meridian.

5428.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain vacant public lands in Montana from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are reserved for classification and to aid legislation. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5429.s: This order changes the rules for charges at the Army and Navy General Hospital at Hot Springs, Arkansas. It sets medicine charges at 50 cents a day for certain pay patients, including several groups of military and other service members. For patients admitted through the United States Employees' Compensation Commission, it sets subsistence and medicine charges and says no other charges will be billed or collected except certain additional charges for dressings, costly medicines, or appliances.

5426.s: This order sets document rules for aliens entering the United States and the Philippine Islands. It says immigrants must present immigration visas, with some exceptions for certain children, returning lawful residents, and people from specified places. It also sets passport, visa, transit certificate, and crew-list rules for different kinds of nonimmigrants, seamen, and aliens entering other American possessions.

5427.s: This order lets the Secretary of State make agreements with foreign countries so some nonimmigrants can get passport visas for visiting the United States without paying application and visa fees, or with reduced fees. It applies to citizens or subjects of countries that give similar fee breaks to U.S. citizens of the same class. If no agreement is made, the Secretary may reduce or abolish these fees for eligible nonimmigrants, and those fee changes stay in effect until the foreign country raises its matching fees.

5424.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Colorado for classification and to aid legislation. It applies subject to valid existing claims and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5425.s: This order excludes a tract of land in and around the village of Baranof, Alaska, from the Tongass National Forest. The land is about 10.21 acres. It is reserved to be disposed of for town-site purposes, subject to valid existing rights.

5423.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in New Mexico for resurvey. It says the lands may be opened, if otherwise subject to disposition, for entry under the homestead or desert-land laws only for 91 days after the official plat of resurvey is filed. During that period, qualified ex-service men may enter the land, and after that it may be available to the general public under the public land laws.

5421.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of certain public lands in New Mexico that were held for a resurvey. After the official resurvey plats are filed, the lands would be open for 91 days to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws, if no valid rights block it. After that, the lands would be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5420.s: The order revokes a prior withdrawal of public lands in Colorado that had been set aside for a resurvey. After the official resurvey plat is filed, the lands would be open for 91 days to qualified ex-service men under the homestead or desert land laws, if the lands are otherwise available. After that, the lands would be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5422.s: This order revokes the withdrawal of about 80 acres in Colorado that had been set aside for use by the Forest Service as O'Connor Ranger Station. It opens the land to entry under the homestead or desert-land laws by qualified ex-service men for 91 days, starting 63 days after the order's date. After that, if the land is still unentered, it may be taken up by the general public under any applicable public land law.

5419.s: This order transfers a tract of land on Mountain Point in Alaska to the War Department. It sets the land aside for use as a radio station in connection with the Washington-Alaska Military Cable and Telegraph System. The Lighthouse Service keeps the right to build aids to navigation on the shoreward part of the land.

5418.s: This order revokes the withdrawal of certain public lands in Colorado that had been set aside pending a resurvey. It says those lands may be opened under the homestead or desert land laws only, for 91 days after the official plats of resurvey are filed, to qualified ex-service men. After that, the lands may be open to the general public under any public land law that applies.

5417.s: This order changes consular fees for passports, visas, certificates, and bills of health. It also updates rules on the naturalization and citizenship of married women, including when a woman may keep, lose, or regain U.S. citizenship. The order repeals certain older citizenship laws and makes related changes to the Consular Regulations.

5416.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to Indians of the Klamath River Reservation in California that were set to expire in 1930. The extension lasts for 10 more years. It does not apply to the listed allotments.

5414.s: This order corrects the land description of the Waianae-Kai Military Reservation in Hawaii. It says the earlier description was inaccurate and incomplete, and it amends the reservation boundaries with a new survey description. The order also excludes the Waianae Plantation Railroad right of way and Land Commission Award No. 8307 from Tract No. 1.

5415.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to members of the Kickapoo Band of Indians in Kansas that would have expired during the calendar year 1930. It makes one exception for allotment number 191, for Sah gon ko shuck or Albert Zhuck kah o see.

5413.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Wyoming for resurvey. After the official filing of the plat of resurvey, the lands may be opened for 91 days under the homestead or desert land laws only to qualified ex-service men, subject to valid rights and the stated rules. After that, the lands may be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5412.s: This order revokes the earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in New Mexico that had been held for a resurvey. It says those lands may be opened, if otherwise available, for entry under the homestead or desert land laws only for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plats. During that time, only qualified ex-service men covered by the resolution may enter, and no one may claim the lands by settling on them before entry except as allowed in the order.

5411.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Wyoming for a resurvey. After the resurvey plat is officially filed, the lands may be opened for 91 days to entry under the homestead or desert land laws, but only for qualified ex-service men and subject to valid rights. After that period, the lands may be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5410.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of certain public lands in Township 13 South, Range 9 East, Salt Lake meridian, Utah, for a resurvey. It says those lands, if otherwise available, will be opened under the listed resolution and regulations for entry under the homestead or desert land laws only. For 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat, qualified ex-service men may enter them, and after that they may be available to the general public under applicable public land laws.

5409.s: This order excludes certain tracts of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It restores those lands to entry under the public land laws. The lands described were previously occupied as home sites or for fish cannery purposes.

5403.s: This order revokes part of a 1912 order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 316. The change applies to the described land in Mount Diablo Meridian, T. 37 N., R. 7 E., section 34, NW 1/4 of SE 1/4.

5404.s: This order removes certain lands in Arizona from the Crook National Forest. It reserves those lands for townsite purposes, subject to valid existing claims. The lands include specific parcels in Gila and Salt River Meridian township and range descriptions.

5408.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain unreserved public lands in California for classification. The lands are being considered for possible inclusion in a national monument. The withdrawal applies subject to valid existing claims and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5407.s: This order withdraws the listed public lands in Oregon and Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use. It applies only to the specific parcels named in the order.

5406.s: This order restores the Upolu Airplane Landing Field in the Territory of Hawaii to the Territory for aeronautical purposes only. It keeps a small described tract set aside for military purposes. The restored land must still be available, without charge, for the United States to take off and land airplanes or airships, and for temporary use needed for their operation and maintenance.

5405.s: This order restores a tract of land near Puolo Point in the Territory of Hawaii to the Territory for aeronautical purposes only. It keeps a smaller tract set aside for military purposes. The restored land must also remain available, without charge, for the takeoff and landing of United States airplanes or airships, including temporary occupation needed for their operation and maintenance.

5402.s: This order removes a tract of land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest. The land had been used for fish cannery purposes and is restored to entry under the public land laws. The area is described as about 12.57 acres.

5400.s: This order sets rules for representation allowances for diplomatic and consular offices. It says the money may be used for official receptions, dinners, luncheons, tips, flowers, and other expenses approved by the Secretary of State to support U.S. representation abroad. It also lists places where consular offices may receive these allowances and sets accounting rules, spending limits, and barred uses like motor vehicles, club dues, printing or engraving, and alcoholic beverages.

5401.s: This order withdraws listed public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the cited acts. It does this to aid proposed legislation for a legislative withdrawal of those lands. The goal stated is to protect and augment the city of Los Angeles' water supply system.

5399.s: This order allows Mrs. Bell Scarburgh Joynes to be appointed as a clerk in the Treasury Department without following the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of former Lieut. Commander Walker Waller Joynes and that he left her and a legally adopted child without adequate means of support.

5398.s: This order consolidates the United States Veterans' Bureau, the Bureau of Pensions, and the National Home for Disabled Volunteer Soldiers into a new Veterans' Administration. It transfers their duties, powers, personnel, records, papers, and public property to that new agency.

5397.s: This order temporarily withdraws 80 acres of public land in Washington from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for use by the State of Washington as a lookout station. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5396.s: This order directs federal supervisors to grant leave to disabled veterans in the executive civil service when a medical authority says treatment is required. The leave can include annual leave, sick leave, or leave without pay, and it will not count against the veteran’s efficiency rating. The veteran must give prior notice of the days and hours needed for treatment so work can be arranged during the absence.

5395.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in a township in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. It does this while the township is being resurveyed. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5394.s: This order designates Honorable Pedro de Aldrey to perform the duties of the Judge of the District Court of the United States for Porto Rico when Judge Ira It. Wells is absent. He is authorized to sign necessary papers and records as the acting judge during that absence.

5393.s: This order revokes part of a 1913 order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 406. It applies to the lands described in Boise Meridian, T. 6 S., R. 11 E., in Idaho.

5392.s: This order extends Customs Collection District No. 21, based at Port Arthur, Texas, to include Cameron and Calcasieu counties in Louisiana. It also moves the customs station at Lake Charles, Louisiana, from District No. 20 to District No. 21, effective 30 days after the order.

5391.s: This order reserves certain public lands in Alaska for the use of the Office of Education. The lands are at Chitina, Point Hope, and Kanakanak, where school buildings had been built. The reservation is subject to any valid claims that already existed when the order was issued.

5390.s: The order allows Mrs. A. Louise Gilbert to be appointed without following the civil service rules. The appointment would be to a grade 3 position, or another suitable job, in the Bureau of Agricultural Economies of the Department of Agriculture. It also says she is the widow of a former Department of Agriculture employee who died after an accident on an official trip.

5389.s: This order withdraws certain vacant, unappropriated, unreserved public lands that contain a hot spring or a spring with curative waters. It also covers land within one-quarter mile of those springs on unsurveyed public land, except in Alaska. The land is taken out of settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserved for lease, subject to valid existing rights.

5388.s: This order changes civil service rules for certain jobs in the Indian Service. It adds guidance and placement officers, and it adds agricultural extension agents and home demonstration agents in field positions that are financed partly by the Indian Service and outside cooperating persons or organizations. It says these appointments may be made only when a full-time agent is not justified.

5387.s: This order says Mrs. Mildred E. Vincent may be appointed as a clerk in the Immigration Service without following the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of Harry E. Vincent, who died while serving as an immigration patrol inspector, and that she has a 7-year-old daughter dependent on her.

5386.s: This order changes a previous land withdrawal so that it does not apply to lands selected by the State of Michigan under the Act of July 31, 1912. It affects lands in Michigan that have already been selected or may be selected later under that law.

5385.s: This order abolishes St. Michael, Alaska, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 31. It affects customs operations in that district, which has headquarters at Juneau, Alaska.

5384.s: This order reserves a tract of land in Fort Yukon, Alaska, for the use of the Alaska Game Commission in the Department of Agriculture. The land is subject to any valid claims that already existed when the order was signed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5383.s: The order extends the trust period for certain allotments on the ceded part of the Red Lake Reservation in Minnesota. It applies to the named members of the Red Lake Chippewa Tribe listed in the order, and it extends the trust period for 10 more years from the date it would have expired.

5382.s: This order allows the Paymaster of the Panama Canal, under the Auditor’s direction, to advance small sums of cash to bonded employees on the Isthmus of Panama for petty cash disbursements. No more than $200 may be advanced to any one bonded employee at one time, and the Paymaster remains responsible for accounting for the money under his bond.

5381.s: This order approves the transfer of operation of the Hotel Tivoli from the Panama Canal to the Panama Railroad Co. The transfer is to be under the terms and conditions in the Governor's July 1, 1929 memorandum.

5379.s: This order revokes parts of several public water reserve withdrawals in Arizona, California, and Colorado. The listed lands are restored to the public domain if they are not otherwise reserved or withdrawn. After notice is announced, those lands will be subject to disposition under the applicable laws.

5380.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by law. It is meant to help protect and add to the city of Los Angeles' water supply system. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5377.s: This order allows Miss Patia Smith to be appointed to a position in the Department of Commerce without following the civil service rules. It applies to Miss Smith. It also says she is the daughter of Curtis M. Smith, a former Bureau of Standards employee who was seriously injured in an explosion while on duty.

5378.s: This order revokes part of a 1914 reserve order in Alaska for certain lands near Salmon Creek. It applies to lands within one-half mile of part of the creek channel between Gastineau Channel and a point 5 miles upstream, with some lands excepted. It also excepts lands covered by the Juneau 02879 permit and lands within 100 feet of the center line of Salmon Creek from its mouth to the dam at Salmon Creek Reservoir.

5376.s: This order sets the salary for each member of the American Section of the International Joint Commission at $10,000 a year, starting July 1, 1930. It also revokes Executive Order No. 1440 from December 4, 1911.

5375.s: This order enlarges the Minidoka Reservation in Idaho for the protection of native birds. It adds land in the Minidoka irrigation project north of the Snake River, and the land stays subject to the Department of the Interior’s use for irrigation and other incidental purposes, along with any valid existing rights. It also makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, disturb, kill, or take birds or wild animals there, or to damage natural growth, fire safety, or U.S. property.

5374.s: This order allows Mrs. Mary R. Martin to be appointed for one year as a check assorter or another minor clerical job in the General Accounting Office. It says this appointment will not give her classified status or a right to keep working after that. The order notes that her husband was an employee of that office and died, leaving her with two sons and without means of support.

5373.s: The order directs that $421,000 be placed to the credit of the Governor of the Virgin Islands, with $15,000 allowed for public wells and any additional money made available under that appropriation. The money is to be used at the governor’s discretion for necessary expenses tied to the occupation of the Virgin Islands and the temporary government there. It also requires the governor to appoint and set salaries for employees whose positions and pay are not listed in the annual budgets of the two colonial councils.

5371.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5332, which had temporarily changed the order of precedence of the Assistant Secretaries of War. It affects the Assistant Secretaries of War by ending that temporary change.

5372.s: This order revokes parts of earlier power-site withdrawals, reserves, and water power designations for many listed lands in Oregon. The lands are along rivers and streams including the Willamette, John Day, Deschutes, Nehalem, Walla Walla, Hood, Malheur, Crooked, Rogue, Umpqua, Santiam, Clackamas, Columbia, and others. It affects only the specific tracts and lots named in the order.

5370.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico for classification. It applies to the listed areas and is subject to valid existing claims.

5369.s: This order sets apart a tract of land in the Canal Zone for use as the Cerro Tigre Ordnance Depot military reservation. It puts the area under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of War, while keeping it subject to the civil control and jurisdiction of the Governor of the Panama Canal. The order also gives the reservation’s boundaries and says the area is about 257.80 acres.

5368.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of public lands in one township in Michigan that had been pending a resurvey. The lands are within Huron National Forest. The earlier proclamations reserving those lands for forest purposes remain in effect.

5367.s: This order revokes parts of earlier power-site withdrawal and reserve orders for specific lands along the Boise River and South Fork of the Boise River in Idaho. It affects the land descriptions listed in the order.

5366.s: This order revokes part of an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Michigan near the shore of Lake Michigan. It makes those lands available so Joseph S. Cooper’s application to make a homestead entry can be allowed.

5365.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in the Territory of Alaska from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of disposal. It says the land is being set aside to promote the interests of the natives by vocational training, to help them restock the country and protect fur-bearing animals, and to aid in their care and support. It also reserves all oil, coal, and other mineral deposits to the United States, along with the right to prospect for, mine, and remove them.

5364.s: This order reserves certain land on Unalaska Island, Alaska, for the use of the Navy Department. The land is withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except for leasing for grazing purposes. It affects people who might try to settle, claim, or buy that land.

5362.s: This order reserves a parcel of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It does this to protect a hot spring on the land and allow it to be leased under the law named in the order. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5363.s: This order revokes part of the 1913 order that created Power-Site Reserve No. 397. It removes that reserve status from the listed lands in Montana.

5360.s: This order revokes parts of earlier orders that created power-site reserves in Oregon, California, and Idaho. It applies only to the specific listed lands in the Willamette, Stanislaus, Klamath, and Salmon River areas. The order affects the land descriptions named in each section.

5359.s: This order reserves and sets apart coal-bearing land in Alaska for the use of the Office of Education, while any valid claims already on the land are kept in place. The land is about 206 acres near Wainwright, Alaska, and the reservation stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5361.s: This order reserves a parcel of land at Takotna, Alaska, from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets aside the land for the use of the Alaska Road Commission, and it stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5358.s: This order says money made available in the Interior Department Appropriation Act for studying and reporting on the public domain will be paid out by the chief disbursing officer of the Interior Department. Payment requires a certificate and approval from the executive secretary of the Committee on the Administration and Conservation of the Public Domain.

5357.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to members of the Uncompahgre, Uintah, and White River Bands of Ute Indians of Utah. It applies to allotments whose trust period was set to expire during 1930 and extends that period for ten more years from the expiration date.

5355.s: This order says the rental and subsistence allowance rates for officers in the various services will apply for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1931. It affects officers who are entitled to those allowances.

5356.s: This order extends the trust period for allotments made to members of the Prairie Band of Potawatomi Indians in Kansas that were set to expire during 1930. The extension is for ten years. It makes exceptions for certain listed allotments and says the trust period for some of those lands applies only to specific partitioned parcels.

5354.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in place while the townships are resurveyed. It applies to the listed townships and sections in Wyoming unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5353.s: This order closed several executive departments and independent Government establishments in the District of Columbia on Saturday, May 31, 1930. It also excused federal clerks and other employees in the District of Columbia from duty that day, except for those excepted for special public reasons or where absence would conflict with existing law. The order delayed the Saturday-hours rule in a 1927 executive order until the second Saturday in June and said it was not meant to set a precedent.

5352.s: This order reserves certain public lands in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It sets the lands aside for the Bureau of Biological Survey of the Department of Agriculture to use for its reindeer experiment station. The bureau may build improvements there and use timber from the lands for fencing and other improvements.

5351.s: This order revokes part of a 1913 order that created Phosphate Reserve No. 16 in Florida. It restores the listed lands in Florida to the public domain and makes them available under the laws that apply to those lands.

5350.s: This order separates San Diego and Imperial counties in southern California from Customs Collection District No. 27 and creates Customs Collection District No. 25 with headquarters in San Diego. The new district includes the ports of entry at Andrade, Calexico, San Ysidro, and Tecate, and the customs station at Campo will continue under Tecate's supervision.

5349.s: This order sets aside Bird, or Hat, Island in Great Salt Lake, Utah, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for wild animals and birds. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds there, or to take or destroy wild bird eggs. It also bans using or entering the reservation except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture, and forbids cutting or burning natural growth or damaging United States property.

5348.s: This order allows Mrs. Helen Hall York to be appointed as a clerk in the classified service of the Treasury Department without following the civil service rules. It applies to Mrs. York, who is the widow of former Prohibition Agent Lamar W. York and is described as having three small children and without adequate means of support.

5347.s: The order allows Mrs. Florence R. Hopkins to be appointed for one year to a suitable job in the Treasury Department, if the Secretary of the Treasury requests it, without following civil service rules. It says this appointment would not give her classified status or a right to more government work. The order says Mrs. Hopkins is a widow with four dependent children and without adequate means of support.

5346.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Minnesota from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while a resurvey of the township is pending, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5345.s: This order changes the Consular Regulations of 1896 to use more uniform wording and simpler administrative methods. It replaces some uses of “paragraph” with “section” and changes account and return language for consular officers from “quarterly” to “monthly.” It also updates rules for keeping and returning ship’s papers and changes one item in the tariff of United States consular fees.

5344.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Montana, Nevada, Oregon, and Utah from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for public use. In Utah, it also includes land within a quarter of a mile of Queatchupah Creek and other listed tracts.

5342.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Arkansas from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the township is being resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5343.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the townships are resurveyed. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5341.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Arizona from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It applies to the listed townships and lasts until a resurvey is finished or the President or Congress revokes it.

5340.s: This order allows Mrs. Ida K. Marsh to be employed for one year in a position in the Bureau of the Census without following the civil service rules. It also says this does not give her any status for later employment in the classified service.

5338.s: This order lets three named employees stay on with the Federal Radio Commission without following the civil service rules. It applies only while they work for that commission. It does not give them any employment status in any other part of the classified service.

5339.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain unreserved public lands in listed townships in Arizona and Nevada for classification. It also holds those lands while a decision is made on whether to include them in a national monument. The order does not affect valid existing claims.

5336.s: This order revokes part of a 1910 withdrawal for coal land classification in the listed Utah lands. It says the lands were classified by the Director of the Geological Survey. The revocation does not affect other withdrawals or reservations outside the lands named.

5337.s: This order changes how Army ration amounts are adjusted for different kinds of units and mess arrangements. It sets added ration credits for smaller organizations, for individual men who mess separately, and for enlisted men serving and messing on Army mine planters. It also sets no change for some organizations and a deduction for organizations averaging more than 150 men per day, with an exception for recruit depots.

5335.s: This order allows Mrs. Thelma D. Roy to be employed for one year in the classified service of the Treasury Department without following the civil service rules. It says she does not gain any status for later employment in the classified service. The order affects Mrs. Roy and her employment in the Treasury Department.

5334.s: This order allows Mrs. Selma F. Dinger to be appointed to a suitable position in the War Department without following the civil service rules. It affects Mrs. Dinger and the War Department.

5333.s: This order allows Miss Mary Edwina Coons to be employed for one year in the classified service under the Federal Trade Commission without following the civil service rules. It says this does not give her any status for later employment in the classified service.

5332.s: This order directs the Assistant Secretary of War appointed under the 1926 act to perform the duties of Secretary of War while the Secretary of War is ill or temporarily absent from the seat of government. It applies only until further orders.

5331.s: This order reserves certain public lands in California for townsite purposes under federal law. It says the lands are subject to valid existing rights and may be disposed of under an appropriate townsite law. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5330.s: This order allows Mrs. Helen Laddbush, the widow of Frank E. Laddbush, to be appointed to an appropriate job under the Interstate Commerce Commission. Her appointment may be made without following the civil service rules.

5329.s: This order says Mrs. Laura Mae Decker may be appointed to an appropriate position in the Department of Agriculture without regard to the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of Arthur J. Decker, who worked in Government service for nearly twenty-eight years, including twelve years in the Department of Agriculture.

5328.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in effect until the land is resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5327.s: This order temporarily withdraws federal deposits of oil shale and federal lands that contain them from lease or other disposal. It reserves those lands for investigation, examination, and classification, subject to valid existing rights.

5326.s: This order temporarily withdraws all unreserved islands, rocks, and pinnacles in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It applies subject to valid existing rights and is for classification and in aid of legislation. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5325.s: This order allows Mrs. Liza B. Moncure to be appointed to a classified job in the Treasury Department without following the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of Robert K. Moncure, a prohibition agent who died while carrying out his official duties in West Palm Beach, Florida.

5324.s: This order designates Leopoldville, Belgian Congo, as an unhealthful post for Foreign Service retirement purposes. It says duty there, including regular leave, will count as one year and a half for retirement, under the law it cites. It also says this is in addition to other places already listed, upon the transfer of the consulate at Loanda, Angola, to Leopoldville.

5322.s: This order designates San Luis, Arizona as a customs port of entry. It places San Luis in Customs Collection District No. 26, with headquarters at Nogales, Arizona, effective 30 days after the order.

5323.s: This order withdraws public lands in certain townships in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. It stays in effect while those townships are resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5321.s: This order allows tax returns to be inspected by officers and employees of the Department of Commerce for statistical purposes. The inspection must follow the rules and regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury, as amended.

5320.s: This order extends the limits of the port of Niagara Falls, New York, to include Lewiston, New York. It applies to Customs Collection District No. 9, with headquarters at Buffalo, New York, and takes effect 30 days after the order date.

5319.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed under the listed acts. It is meant to aid proposed legislation that would authorize selling these lands to the city of Los Angeles to protect and increase its water supply system. It also covers the unsurveyed parts of several sections known as Bird Island.

5318.s: This order adds Amak Island, Sealion Rocks, and a small nearby island to the Aleutian Islands Reservation in Alaska. It sets them apart for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for birds and wild animals. The added lands are subject to existing valid rights and to the laws, regulations, and orders that govern the reservation.

5317.s: This order suspends indefinitely an earlier order that abolished New Bern and Manteo, North Carolina, as customs ports of entry. It affects those two ports and Customs Collection District No. 15, with headquarters at Wilmington, North Carolina.

5316.s: The order sets aside the Lighthouse Reservation on Wolf Island for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for wild animals and birds, while keeping it subject to lighthouse purposes. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or take eggs of wild birds there, or to enter the reservation except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. It also bans cutting or burning natural growth, leaving fires unattended, and damaging United States property.

5315.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. It applies while the township is being resurveyed and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5313.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Oregon that are not part of a national forest. It is meant to aid proposed legislation in H.R. 3717 and is subject to valid existing claims and the earlier acts named in the order. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5314.s: This order reserves certain public land in Alfalfa County, Oklahoma, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for birds, subject to existing valid rights. It forbids hunting, trapping, capturing, disturbing, killing, or taking eggs of wild animals or birds in the area, unless allowed under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture. It also bans cutting or burning natural growth, leaving fires unattended, and damaging United States property in the refuge.

5312.s: This order revokes parts of several earlier power-site withdrawals and power-site reserves in Idaho. It applies to listed lands along the Patette River, St. Joe River, Boise River, Crane Creek, Blackfoot River No. 2, Payette River No. 4, Snake River, Coeur d'Alene River, North Fork of Coeur d'Alene River, Salmon River No. 5, Marble Creek, Coeur d'Alene Lake, and South Fork of Boise River. The revocations cover the specific land parcels named in the order.

5311.s: This order lets Mrs. Mabel P. Hollister be appointed to an appropriate job in the Smithsonian Institution without following the usual civil service rules. It says she has passed civil service exams for stenographer and typist and for translator in Spanish and French. The order affects Mrs. Hollister and the Smithsonian Institution.

5310.s: This order allows H. Charles Spruks to be appointed to a classified position in the Department of State without following civil service rules. It affects Mr. Spruks and the Department of State. The order says he has unique experience in visa work at two difficult posts in the American Foreign Service.

5309.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Minnesota from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the township is resurveyed and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5307.s: This order adds described public lands in Utah to Fishlake National Forest. It says the change does not interfere with legal rights on lands that are already legally appropriated under the public land laws, as long as those rights are kept in place.

5308.s: This order reserves a tract of public land in Malabang, Province of Lanao, in the Philippine Islands for military purposes. It says the land is subject to private rights, if any, and to an existing public highway right of way for the Province of Lanao. The United States also keeps the right to require changes in that right of way if military authorities decide they are needed for the land’s use.

5306.s: This order extends the trust period on certain land allotments made to members of the Seneca Tribe in Oklahoma that were set to expire during 1930. The extension is for 10 years from the date the trust period would have expired. It does not apply to the allotments and named allottees listed in the order.

5304.s: This order withdraws public lands in one township in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It stays in effect until the township is resurveyed or the President or Congress revokes it. It affects people who might seek to settle on or claim those lands.

5303.s: This order extends the trust period for certain allotments on the Devils Lake Reservation in North Dakota that were set to expire in 1930. The extension is for ten years from the date the trust would have expired, except for allotment number 1188 for Makana, who is deceased.

5305.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to Indians on the Nez Perce Reservation in Idaho that were set to expire during 1930. The extension lasts for ten years. It does not apply to the allotments listed for Lily Viles, Antoine Bronche, Albert John, and Ida John, who are noted as deceased.

5302.s: This order extends the trust period on certain allotments of the Rosebud Indians in South Dakota for another ten years. It does not apply to the allotments listed by number and name in the order.

5300.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the townships are being resurveyed. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5301.s: This order extends the trust period for allotments made to Indians of the Crow Reservation in Montana that were set to expire during 1930. The extension is for ten years. It does not apply to allotment numbers 18, 51, and 274, which are listed as deceased.

5299.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to members of the Prairie Band of Potawatomi Indians in Kansas that were set to expire in 1930. The extension is for 10 years from the date the trust would have expired. It does not apply to the listed allotments and allottee names.

5297.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. It does this while a resurvey of the townships is pending. It affects people who might seek to use or claim those lands.

5296.s: This order revokes earlier withdrawals of certain public lands in Wyoming for one specific tract in the Targhee National Forest. The land is described by set boundaries near the south boundary of Yellowstone National Park and the Idaho-Wyoming state line.

5295.s: This order replaces Chapter XX of the 1927 instructions for diplomatic officers with new rules on how mission accounts are kept and reported. It says who must render accounts, when accounts and returns must be sent, and how disbursements, fees, drafts, vouchers, postage, telegraph charges, salary accounts, and final accounts are handled. The rules apply to diplomatic officers, chiefs of mission, special disbursing officers, clerks, and other employees at missions.

5293.s: This order revokes part of a 1917 withdrawal order for the listed land in Montana. The land not otherwise reserved or withdrawn is restored to the public domain and will be subject to the laws that apply to it after notice is determined and announced.

5294.s: This order revokes part of a 1929 withdrawal of public lands in township T. 19 S., R. 56 E., in Nevada. It applies to sections 25, 26, 35, and 36 in that township. The lands are in the Dixie National Forest, and the earlier orders reserving them for forest purposes still remain in effect.

5291.s: This order abolishes New Bern, North Carolina, and Manteo, North Carolina, as customs ports of entry in Customs Collection District No. 15. The change applies to those ports and takes effect 30 days after the order.

5292.s: This order withdraws the listed land in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves that land for public use. The order applies to the parcels listed under the Mount Diablo Meridian.

5289.s: This order reserves land in listed Alaska Native villages for the use of the Office of Education. The land is limited to tracts of up to 40 acres in each place where school buildings have been built, and it is subject to any valid claims already existing. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5290.s: This order changes consular regulations on how consular officers report accounts, fees, salaries, disbursements, and related records. It requires monthly accounts and sets rules for postage, clerk hire, consular court accounts, prison expenses, seamen records, ship bills, salary accounts, and returns of fees. It also says some fees and surplus money must be sent to the Department of State or the Treasury, and it sets penalties for false or missing reports.

5288.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5256. It restores Executive Order No. 4728 and Executive Order No. 5022 to full force and effect.

5287.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in effect until the area is resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5286.s: This order says H. Percival Dodge may be reinstated without examination as a Foreign Service officer of Class I when a vacancy occurs. It applies to Dodge, who served in the Diplomatic Service and in several foreign posts and roles named in the order.

5285.s: This order says Eustaquio Vallecer may be given a classified status as master in the Harbor Boat Service of the War Department in the Philippine Islands. It recognizes his service to the United States Government in the Philippines since August 13, 1898. It also says he was recommended by the Secretary of War and the Civil Service Commission.

5284.s: This order designates Fort Pierce, Florida, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 18. It takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

5283.s: This order allows Mrs. Mabel V. Birch to be appointed to a classified job in the Treasury Department without following the civil service rules. It concerns Mrs. Birch, who is the widow of Platt H. Birch, and her three minor children.

5281.s: This order sets aside the air space over certain harbors as a prohibited area for civil aircraft. It applies to Tortugas, Florida; Great Harbor, Culebra; Guantánamo Naval Station, Cuba; Pearl Harbor, Hawaii; Guam; Súbic Bay, Philippine Islands; and Kiska, Aleutian Islands. Civil aircraft may not fly in these areas unless they have special authority from the United States Navy Department, and flights that do not follow the order can be punished under the Air Commerce Act of 1926.

5282.s: This order withdraws one lot in Louisiana from public lands use under the cited acts. It keeps the land withdrawn while officials consider whether to include it in a national monument and while Congress considers H.R. 8873. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5280.s: This order temporarily withdraws 40 acres in Montana from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the listed acts. It reserves the land for use by the Forest Service as an addition to the Deep Creek Ranger Station for administration of the Helena National Forest.

5279.s: This order revokes earlier withdrawals of certain lands in Utah that had been made under prior executive orders. It applies to the specifically described tracts listed in the order. The lands were withdrawn in aid of legislation.

5278.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Florida from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be classified while the government decides whether they should be included in a national forest. It applies to the listed parcels in the Tallahassee Meridian unless it is later revoked by the President or by Congress.

5277.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Idaho for use by the Department of Agriculture for agricultural experiment purposes. It applies to the listed land in Boise Meridian, subject to valid existing claims and the conditions in the law. The withdrawal stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5276.s: This order temporarily withdraws public lands in listed townships in New Mexico, subject to valid existing claims. The lands are to be classified while a decision is made on whether to include them in a national monument.

5275.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Utah from settlement, location, sale, or entry, subject to prior valid claims. The land is to be classified and reviewed to decide whether it should be added to Zion National Park. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5274.s: This order withdraws certain public land in Utah from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves that land for public use under the stated law.

5273.s: This order withdraws the listed land in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for public use under the cited law.

5272.s: This order revokes part of a 1917 withdrawal for certain lands in New Mexico. The land not otherwise reserved or withdrawn is restored to the public domain and will be subject to disposal under the laws that apply to it. The change affects the listed tracts in the New Mexico Meridian.

5271.s: This order revokes parts of two earlier orders that had withdrawn certain lands in Colorado for power-site use. It applies only to the specific land sections listed in the order.

5270.s: This order withdraws certain public land in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is reserved for public use. It covers listed areas in the Sixth Principal Meridian, including land near Vermillion Creek.

5269.s: This order lets Jose T. Casanovas be given a classified status in the Army’s Quartermaster Corps in Porto Rico without following civil service rules. It applies to Mr. Casanovas, who has worked there since 1898 as a janitor and as a mason.

5268.s: This order changes the membership of the Board of Surveys and Maps by adding the Bureau of Lighthouses from the Department of Commerce. It affects that board and the bureau named in the order.

5266.s: This order restores a parcel of land that was part of the Fort Ruger Military Reservation to its previous status for use by the Territory of Hawaii. The land is described by boundary lines in the order and covers 8,700 square feet. It affects the use of that specific piece of land.

5267.s: This order sets Judge James Waldron Remick’s salary as War Claims Arbiter at $10,000 a year. The salary starts when he takes office.

5265.s: This order restores a described parcel of land that was part of the military reservation of Punchbowl Hill to its previous status for use by the Territory of Hawaii. It applies to that specific parcel of land, which is described by survey points and boundaries in the order.

5264.s: This order restricts the introduction of parrots into the United States, its possessions, and dependencies from any foreign port. It says parrots may not be brought in for as long as is deemed necessary, except under conditions set by the Secretary of the Treasury. The order is meant to prevent disease that can be communicated from infected parrots to human beings.

5263.s: This order lets the Alien Property Custodian sell 500 shares of preferred stock of the United States Metals Refining Co. at private sale, without public advertisement. The shares are held as the property of a German bank and are subject to rules about returning 80 percent of German property and keeping 20 percent with the Government. The sale is to be made at $115 per share, and the order says the price appears fair.

5262.s: This order revokes two earlier withdrawals of public lands in certain Arizona townships that were pending resurvey. After the official filing of the resurvey plats, the lands may be opened for 91 days under the homestead or desert land laws only to qualified ex-service men of the war with Germany, subject to valid rights and the stated conditions. After that period, the lands may be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5261.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in two townships in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while a resurvey is pending, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5260.s: This order forms a commission made up of commissioners from the Departments of Interior, Agriculture, and Commerce for business in Alaska. It puts the ex officio commissioner for Alaska in the Department of the Interior in charge of the commission. The commission is directed to study which affairs should be transferred to Alaska for administration and what personnel and records should be transferred with them.

5258.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in North Dakota for classification and to aid legislation. The withdrawal is subject to prior valid rights. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5259.s: This order allows Mrs. Mary Bernadine Partridge to be appointed to a clerical position in the Bureau of Prohibition without following the Civil Service Rules. It says her husband became incapacitated, and that she now has the burden of supporting their family, including three young children.

5257.s: This order withdraws certain land in Colorado from settlement, sale, location, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The land is set aside for use as a target range by Company C, 157th Infantry, Colorado National Guard. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5256.s: This order sets daily allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men who are not given quarters or rations in kind. It applies to the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Survey, and Public Health Service. It also sets different rates for men on duty, men traveling on duty, and men in detention, and says no more than $4 a day will be allowed to one man.

5255.s: This order withdraws certain described land in New Mexico from settlement, sale, location, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The land is reserved for use by the New Mexico National Guard as a target range, unless the President or Congress revokes the order.

5254.s: The order revokes a prior reservation of certain land in New Mexico that had been set aside for use as a target range for the New Mexico National Guard. It opens that land, subject to valid rights, for entry under the homestead or desert land laws by qualified ex-service men of the war with Germany for 91 days starting 63 days after the order. After that, any land still unentered would be open to appropriation under other public land laws by the general public.

5252.s: This order revokes part of the 1918 withdrawal that created Petroleum Reserve No. 61, Colorado No. 2. The lands listed in the order are restored to the public domain and made available under the laws that apply to them, unless they are otherwise reserved or withdrawn.

5253.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to Indians of the Omaha Reservation in Nebraska. It applies to allotments whose trust period expires during the calendar year 1930, and extends that period for ten years.

5251.s: The order withdraws certain described land in Colorado from settlement, sale, location, entry, and all forms of appropriation. It sets the land aside for use as a target range by Company "D" of the 157th Infantry, Colorado National Guard. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5250.s: The order lets the Governor of the Panama Canal grant pardons, paroles, reprieves, and sentence commutations for offenses against Canal Zone laws, orders, and regulations. It also says no pardon, parole, reprieve, commutation, fine remission, or forfeiture remission can be granted until an application is sent to a five-member pardon board and approved in writing by most of the board.

5249.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public land in Michigan from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land will be classified and reviewed to decide whether it should be included in a national forest.

5248.s: This order adds the Federal Farm Board to Schedule B of the Civil Service Rules for attorneys of all grades and for experts in several listed fields. It allows these people to be appointed without competitive examination under the civil service rules. For expert positions, the board must get an advisory opinion on salary, but the Federal Farm Board keeps the final decision on compensation.

5247.s: This order keeps Edwin V. Morgan on active duty in the Foreign Service for as long as needed, up to five years from February 22, 1930. It applies to Edwin V. Morgan of New York, who is ambassador extraordinary and plenipotentiary to Brazil.

5246.s: This order changes an earlier order that created Power Site Reserve No. 377 in Utah. It lets the Secretary of the Interior approve an application by the Uinta Pipe Line Company for a right of way for a gas pipe line across certain lands in the reserve.

5245.s: This order changes a 1916 public water reserve in Wyoming to allow the Secretary of the Interior to approve an application from the Uinta Pipe Line Company. The application is for a right of way for a pipe line to carry gas across certain lands within the reserve.

5244.s: This order temporarily withdraws a 40-acre tract of land in Washington next to the Columbia National Forest. It is reserved for use by the Department of Agriculture as a ranger station for managing the national forest. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5243.s: This order revokes part of a 1913 reservation on Amaknak Island, Alaska, except for one area in the southern part of the island that stays withdrawn for the Department of Agriculture, including the Alaska Game Commission. The rest of the island is restored to the public domain and opened to entry under the homestead laws that apply to Alaska for a set period, then under other public land laws. No rights may be claimed to the restored lands except as allowed by the order.

5242.s: This order directs Clarence M. Young, an Assistant Secretary of Commerce, to perform the duties of the Secretary of Commerce when the Secretary is absent. It also applies when the Assistant Secretary of Commerce appointed under the act of February 14, 1903, as amended, is absent.

5241.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It stays in effect while the township is resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5240.s: This order changes the description of the Pupukea Military Reservation in the Territory of Hawaii. It revokes Executive Order No. 5174 and amends Executive Order No. 4679 to give a corrected land description for the reservation. The order affects the lands set aside for military purposes at Pupukea on the island of Oahu.

5238.s: This order closes several executive departments and independent government establishments in the District of Columbia on Tuesday, December 24, 1929, including the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and Stations. It also excuses most Federal employees in the District of Columbia from duty that day, except those excepted for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law.

5239.s: The order uses money from the stated appropriation to help prepare the Government’s case about title to a piece of land within Naval Reserve No. 1 in California. It allows the substitute register to be paid necessary travel expenses for hearings outside Sacramento. It also appoints James G. Findlay as a special disbursing officer, requires a $5,000 bond, and lets him pay witness fees and other approved hearing and deposition expenses.

5237.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain unreserved public lands in listed townships in California for classification. It applies subject to prior valid rights and stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5236.s: This order changes a Civil Service rule for certain positions under the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. It adds assistant national bank examiners and assistant receivers to the list of positions excepted from examination. It affects people in those banking oversight jobs.

5235.s: This order allows Mrs. Marguerite Barrett to be reinstated in the Treasury Department without regard to how long she has been separated from service. It applies to her and concerns her classified service in the War Trade Board and the Public Health Service of the Treasury Department.

5234.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The lands will stay withdrawn while a resurvey of the township is made, unless the President or Congress revokes the order.

5232.s: This order allows Mrs. Maude Williams to be appointed to a classified Government job without following the civil service rules. It says she has given satisfactory service in a temporary appointment in the Treasury Department. It also says she has three children who are partly dependent on her for support.

5233.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry, while keeping valid existing rights in place. It is meant to help proposed legislation that would let the City of Napa buy the lands for protection of the watershed of its municipal water system.

5231.s: This order allows Germaine M. Finley to be appointed to an appropriate job in the classified service without following the civil service rules. It affects her appointment specifically. The order says she is a widow with two children, without means of support, and that she has experience as a clerk and French stenographer.

5230.s: This order amends Schedule A of the civil service rules to add a new exception for Federal Farm Board positions. It allows one private secretary or confidential clerk for each Member of the Federal Farm Board to be hired without the usual examination requirement.

5229.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by earlier laws. It does this to aid proposed legislation that would let the lands be sold to the city of Los Angeles. The stated purpose is to protect and augment the city’s water supply system.

5228.s: This order reserves certain public lands at Benton Lake, Montana, for the Department of Agriculture to use as a refuge and breeding ground for birds. It applies to the lands described in the order and is subject to existing valid rights. Within the refuge, people may not hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds, take eggs, damage natural growth, or injure United States property except under rules set by the Secretary of Agriculture.

5227.s: This order removes several tracts of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest. It restores those lands to entry under the public land laws. The lands were previously occupied as home sites or for fish cannery purposes.

5226.s: This order cancels two earlier rules about diplomatic visas and replaces them with new wording. It says diplomatic visas will be granted under regulations set by the Secretary of State, affecting diplomatic officers and consular regulations.

5225.s: This order allows Mrs. Eliza C. O'Reilly to be appointed to a classified position in the Treasury Department without following the civil service rules. It applies to that appointment in the Treasury Department. The order says it was issued in recognition of Michael J. O'Reilly's long, faithful, and efficient service in the Treasury Department.

5224.s: This order says Mrs. Alice Tasker may be reinstated in an appropriate position in any part of the Veterans' Bureau service. It applies to her former job as a matron in the New York Office of the Veterans' Bureau.

5223.s: This order revokes part of a 1928 withdrawal of certain land in Idaho that had been reserved for air navigation facilities. It opens the land, subject to valid rights, to entry under the homestead or desert land laws by qualified ex-service men of the war with Germany for a limited period. After that period, any land still unentered may be opened to the general public under the public land laws.

5222.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It is meant to allow classification and to support proposed legislation that would let the City of Napa buy the lands to protect the watershed of its municipal water system.

5221.s: This order says officers and employees in the executive branch of the United States Government may not work for any foreign government, corporation, partnership, or individual that competes with American industry. The rule applies even if they are on annual leave or leave without pay. It affects executive branch officers and employees.

5219.s: This order withdraws a described tract of land in the Fort Davis abandoned military reservation in Alaska from other use, subject to valid existing rights under the mineral land laws. The land is reserved for use of the Alaska Reindeer Service.

5220.s: This order sets rules for the style and form of Proclamations and Executive Orders. Drafts must be sent in triplicate through the Department of State, each one must have a title, and spelling, punctuation, and orthography must follow set standards. It also sets paper and margin requirements and says signed originals must be deposited with the Department of State for custody, proofreading, and distribution.

5218.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Township 24 North, Range 6 East, in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5217.s: This order revokes parts of earlier withdrawals for certain lands in New Mexico that were part of Public Water Reserves No. 53, 63, and 86. The listed lands are restored to the public domain if they are not otherwise reserved or withdrawn. They will be subject to disposal under the laws that apply, after notice is later determined and announced.

5216.s: This order revokes an earlier order for certain public lands in South Dakota and restores those lands for resurvey. It opens the lands, subject to valid rights, to entry under the homestead or desert land laws by qualified ex-service men of the war with Germany for a limited period. After that period, any land still unentered would be open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5215.s: This order revokes the earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in a township in Wyoming that had been held pending resurvey. It opens those lands, if otherwise subject to disposition and subject to valid rights, to entry under the homestead or desert land laws only by qualified ex-service men of the War with Germany for 91 days after the resurvey plat is filed. After that, the lands may be open to the general public under any public land law that applies. No rights may be claimed by settlement before entry except as allowed in the order.

5214.s: This order withdraws four described areas of land and water in the Territory of Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The areas are held for the exclusive use and benefit of the United States Navy Department for naval purposes. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it, and it does not affect prior valid claims or other valid existing rights.

5213.s: This order changes the civil service rules for certain jobs in the Indian Service. It keeps many positions exempt from competitive examination, including some clerks, physicians, special officers, hospital attendants, and other workers named in the order. It also revokes several other paragraphs because their positions are now included in the amended list.

5212.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of certain public lands in Washington that had been held for resurvey. It says those lands, if otherwise available and subject to valid rights, shall be opened to entry under the homestead or desert land laws only by qualified ex-service men of the War with Germany for 91 days after the resurvey plat is officially filed. After that period, the lands may be open to the general public under the public land laws. No one may acquire rights to the released lands by settlement before entry or in any other way except as provided here.

5211.s: This order sets apart the airspace over a described area in Maryland for national defense purposes. The area includes the Aberdeen Proving Ground, parts of the Fort Hoyle and Edgewood Arsenal military reservations, and parts of Bush River, Gunpowder River, and Chesapeake Bay.

5210.s: This order allows Mrs. Josephine Jackley to be appointed as a clerk in the Treasury Department without following the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of Dano M. Jackley, who served as a prohibition agent and was killed while doing his official duty.

5209.s: This order allows Mrs. Guilia P. Burke to be permanently appointed to a classified job in the Treasury Department without following the civil service rules. It says she has served in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing and is now a temporary money counter in the Office of the Treasurer of the United States.

5208.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in a Nevada township from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It stays in effect while the township is resurveyed, and it affects anyone who might try to claim or use those lands under those processes.

5207.s: This order revokes two land reservations in Alaska, one along the Unalaklik River and one on Norton Bay.
