It opens those lands to entry under homestead laws that require residence by ex-service men of the World War for 91 days starting on the 63rd day after the order. After that, the lands may be appropriated under other public land laws by the general public. No one may gain rights to the lands by settlement before entry except as allowed here.

5206.s: This order creates the Customs station of Oroville, Washington as a port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 30. It applies to customs operations in that district and says the change takes effect 30 days after the order.

5205.s: This order allows Erwin G. May to be appointed as an Assistant Customs Agent for an assignment to Berlin, Germany. It says the appointment may be made without the competitive requirements of the Civil Service Act and Rules.

5204.s: This order allows Mrs. Estelle Roberts to be appointed as a matron in the Immigration Service without following civil service rules. It applies to her appointment and says the action is recommended by the Secretary of Labor.

5202.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The lands are held this way pending a resurvey of those sections.

5203.s: This order temporarily withdraws a described piece of land in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It is for classification and to help pending legislation, and it stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5201.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain land in Colorado for classification. It also says the land will be reviewed to decide whether it should be added to Hovenweep National Monument.

5200.s: This order transfers the Division of Cooperative Marketing from the Department of Agriculture to the Federal Farm Board. It also moves the division’s work, records, property, office equipment, personnel, and unspent money to the Board. The transfer takes effect on October 1, 1929.

5199.s: This order excludes four tracts of land in Alaska from the Tongass National Forest and restores them to entry under the public land laws. The tracts were previously occupied as a homesite or for fish cannery purposes, and the order applies to those specific lands.

5198.s: This order amends the Civil Service rules by adding a new paragraph to Schedule A, Subdivision IX. It adds two assistants to the Secretary in the Office of the Secretary of Agriculture.

5197-A.s: This order assigns radio frequencies to government stations and lets government departments make some changes in earlier assignments. It also lists certain government experimental radio stations that may use miscellaneous frequencies from time to time. The order says departments should use existing government communication facilities when possible, and it encourages private radio facilities for use in a national emergency.

5197.s: This order revokes parts of two earlier orders that created Power Site Reserve No. 421 in California and Power Site Reserve No. 544 in Nevada. It removes the listed lands in those states from those reserve orders.

5196.s: This order temporarily withdraws 40 acres in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for the Forest Service to use as headquarters for fire patrolmen protecting national forest and other timbered lands nearby. The timber on the land remains subject to sale by the United States.

5195.s: This order revokes part of a 1923 withdrawal of certain public lands in Colorado and restores those lands, subject to valid rights. It opens the listed lands to entry under the homestead or desert land laws only for qualified ex-service men of the War with Germany for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat. After that period, the lands may be available to the general public under any applicable public land law, and no one may gain rights to the released lands except under these rules.

5194.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain described public lands in Arkansas from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are to be classified in connection with areas that have been or may be acquired by the United States for national forest purposes. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5193.s: This order extends the limits of several customs ports of entry in Customs Collection District No. 29. It adds named places in Oregon and Washington to the ports of Astoria, Longview, Portland, and Marshfield. The changes apply thirty days after the order.

5192.s: This order abolishes Lewiston, New York, as a port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 9. The change takes effect thirty days after the date of the order and affects customs operations in that district.

5191.s: This order changes a prior land withdrawal in Florida so one listed parcel is left out of that withdrawal. It is for the sole purpose of allowing Charley McMillan’s homestead entry to remain in place for that land. The land is not to be open to settlement, sale, entry, or other forms of appropriation except through that homestead entry.

5190.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain described lands in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the cited laws. It keeps those lands reserved for classification and for proposed legislation, affecting anyone who might seek to use or claim them.

5189.s: This order sets rules for how the Foreign Service is run. It says vacancies should be filled by promotion based on ability and efficiency, creates boards to handle personnel and exams, and establishes a Foreign Service School for new appointees. It also sets exam and eligibility rules for applicants and revokes two earlier executive orders.

5188.s: This order changes earlier rules so some officers and employees of the Indian Service can also hold state, county, or municipal jobs. It applies to those serving part-time in a medical or sanitary capacity, if the Secretary of the Interior agrees.

5187.s: This order lets the Director of the Census appoint some state, county, or municipal officers as census supervisors. It applies when the Director decides those other public duties do not conflict with census work and that the appointment is in the best interest of the service. It affects people who hold state, county, or municipal office and are chosen to help with the census.

5186.s: This order allows Ida Elizabeth Henning to be appointed to a position in the Department of Agriculture without following Civil Service rules. It says she is the widow of George A. Henning, who died in an explosion at the Department of Agriculture power house, and that she is in urgent need of employment.

5185.s: This order sets apart a parcel of land in the Canal Zone as the Colon Naval Radio Station for use as a naval reservation under the Secretary of the Navy. The area is also subject to the civil control and jurisdiction of the Governor of The Panama Canal. The order describes the land by exact boundaries and says the parcel is 11.7 acres.

5184.s: The order revokes a prior withdrawal of certain public lands in one township in Wyoming. It opens those lands to entry under the homestead or desert land laws only for qualified ex-service men of the War with Germany for 91 days after the resurvey plat is officially filed. After that, the lands may be open to the general public under the public land laws, and no one may claim rights by settlement before entry except as allowed by the order.

5183.s: This order revokes a previous withdrawal of public lands in one township in Wyoming that was pending resurvey. It opens those lands, if otherwise eligible and subject to valid rights, to entry under the homestead or desert land laws only by qualified ex-service men of the War with Germany for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plat. After that, the lands may be opened to appropriation under any applicable public land law by the general public.

5182.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in California and Nevada from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are set aside for classification, subject to existing withdrawals that already apply to some of them. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5180.s: The order allows Jeanette C. Vaughan to be appointed to a clerical job in the Treasury Department without following the civil service rules. It says this was recommended in recognition of her late husband's long and faithful government service.

5181.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in Wyoming that had been reserved pending resurvey. It opens those lands to entry under the homestead or desert land laws only for qualified ex-service men of the War with Germany, if the lands are otherwise available and subject to valid rights. That special opening lasts for 91 days after the official filing of the resurvey plats, and after that the lands may be opened to the general public under the applicable public land laws.

5178.s: This order revokes a previous order that had withdrawn certain public lands in New Mexico pending resurvey. It opens those lands, if otherwise available and subject to valid rights, to entry under the homestead or desert land laws only by qualified ex-service men of the War with Germany for 91 days after the resurvey plat is officially filed. After that period, the lands become open to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5179.s: This order revokes a prior order that had withdrawn certain public lands in New Mexico pending a resurvey. It opens those lands, if otherwise available and subject to valid rights, to entry under the homestead or desert land laws only by qualified ex-service men of the War with Germany for 91 days after the resurvey plat is officially filed. After that period, the lands may be open to the general public under any applicable public land law. It also says no one may gain rights to the released lands before that time except as allowed by the order.

5176.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain described land in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the cited acts. It keeps the land reserved for classification and for proposed legislation unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5177.s: This order revokes a prior withdrawal of certain public lands in New Mexico that were pending a resurvey. After the resurvey plat is filed, the lands, if otherwise subject to disposition and subject to valid rights, must be opened for 91 days only to qualified ex-service men of the World War under the homestead or desert land laws. After that, the lands are opened to the general public under the public land laws that apply.

5174.s: This order changes the boundary description of the Pupukea Military Reservation in the Territory of Hawaii. It says the earlier description was inaccurate and was revised after a resurvey. The change applies to the lands at Pupukea in the District of Koolualoa on the Island of Oahu.

5175.s: This order allows Mrs. Marjorie M. Noone to be appointed to an appropriate job in the Treasury Department without following the civil service rules. Mrs. Noone is the widow of Matthew J. Noone, who worked in the Treasury Department for ten years before his death. The order says she and their three daughters were left without means of support.

5172.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Montana from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It applies to the listed sections and townships while those areas are pending a resurvey. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5173.s: This order extends the trust period for allotments of Indians on the Yankton Sioux Reservation in South Dakota. It applies to allotments whose trust period expires during the calendar year 1929, and extends that period for a further period of ten years.

5171.s: This order revokes an exception from civil service examination for officers helping with important drafting work in the State Department. It gives classified competitive status to ten named employees who were holding those excepted positions. It also adds a new State Department category to Schedule B for certain specialists in foreign relations, political, economic, and financial work who meet set qualification standards.

5170.s: This order changes Schedule B of the civil service rules. It adds certain professional, scientific, technical, or supervisory positions under the Naval Establishment in the Philippine Islands that may be filled by noncompetitive examination, as agreed by the Secretary of the Navy and the Civil Service Commission.

5151.s: This order revokes part of a previous order that had reserved certain unsurveyed islands in Washington for public purposes. It applies to Sheep Island and two islands known as Double Island.

5169.s: This order abolishes Souris, North Dakota, as a port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 34. It takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

5168.s: This order allows Myrtle B. Shely to be appointed to an appropriate position in the classified civil service without having to meet the usual examination requirements. It applies to her appointment and refers to her as the widow of James W. Shely, who served under the Architect of the Capitol.

5167.s: This order allows Robert F. Kerkam to be appointed as a stenographer and typist at the Naval Station in Cavite, Philippine Islands. It says the appointment may be made to fill an existing vacancy without regard to the civil service act or rules.

5166.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It does this while those townships are being resurveyed. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5165.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It applies to the listed townships and lasts until a resurvey is completed or the President or Congress revokes it.

5163.s: This order gives Mr. Howard Fyfe classified status as Assistant Despatch Agent in the United States Despatch Agency in New York City. It says this action is based on his long service and his training and experience in that job.

5164.s: This order allows James Lawrence Bent to be appointed as lieutenant of police in the Industrial Department at Naval Station, Cavite, to fill an existing vacancy. The appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Act or Rules. It says Bent is a chief electrician's mate in the United States Navy, qualified in a policeman examination in the Philippines, and has been acting as chief of the Navy Yard Police for more than four years.

5162.s: This order revokes a 1923 order that had temporarily withdrawn 120 acres in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It also ended the reservation of that land for use by the U.S. Post Office Department as a landing field for airplanes for the Transcontinental Air Mail Service.

5161.s: Louis Bulicek may be appointed to a position in the Department of Commerce without following the civil-service rules. The order says this is tied to helping the department gather information for the Senate from records of the Food Administration and the Grain Corporation.

5160.s: This order changes an earlier land withdrawal rule to let the Secretary of the Interior withdraw the listed land in Oregon for use by the Department of Commerce. The land is to be used to maintain air navigation facilities. The timber on that land remains subject to sale by the United States under the 1916 act.

5159.s: This order creates Reidsville, North Carolina, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 15. It takes effect 30 days after the date of the order and affects customs operations in that district.

5158.s: The order reserves Snake, Dead Man or Bird, and North Keys in Cedar Keys, Florida, for the Department of Agriculture as a refuge and breeding ground for birds, subject to existing valid rights. It makes it unlawful in the refuge to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild animals or birds, or to take or destroy wild bird eggs, unless allowed by rules from the Secretary of Agriculture. It also bars cutting or burning natural growth, leaving fires unattended, and injuring United States property.

5157.s: This order restores most of the Punchbowl Hill military reservation in Honolulu, on the Island of Oahu, to its previous status for use by the Territory of Hawaii. It removes the rule that the land could be used only for park purposes. A portion of the land kept for military purposes is not included.

5156.s: This order designates Harvey M. Hutchison as acting Judge of the District Court of the United States for Porto Rico for September and October 1929. He may perform the duties of that office and sign needed papers and records without extra compensation.

5155.s: This order withdraws a 517-square-foot portion of the Fort De Russy Military Reservation in Honolulu from the military reservation. It sets that land apart for the Territory of Hawaii to widen Ena Road. The order affects that specific piece of land at the intersection of Ena Road, Ala Moana, and Kalia Roads.

5154.s: This order allows Mrs. Birdie E. Gordon to be reinstated as an operative in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing, without regard to how long she has been away from service. It affects Mrs. Gordon, who had worked there before and had resigned because of her husband’s illness and death.

5153.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule IX on reinstatement. It says a person may usually be reinstated only to the department or government establishment they left, and the request must be made within one year of separation. It also lets the Civil Service Commission waive that one-year limit in certain cases, based on how long the person served, and it applies to people seeking reinstatement in the classified service.

5152.s: This order allows Mrs. Lulu M. Davis to be reinstated as an operative in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without regard to how long she has been away from the service. It affects Mrs. Davis and the Bureau of Engraving and Printing.

5151-A.s: This order assigns radio frequencies to stations used by the War Department and the Navy Department. It lists assigned frequencies for stations in Washington, San Francisco, Panama, Hawaii, the Philippines, Cavite, Pearl Harbor, Darien, fleet stations, and other Navy locations. It also assigns a frequency for the War Department’s amateur reserve net.

5150.s: This order says Mrs. Mae A. Krigbaum may be reinstated as an operative in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without regard to how long she has been away from the service. It also says she had served there before through competitive examination. The order notes that she is a widow with three dependent children, and that the oldest child is in poor health.

5149.s: This order allows Frances D. Haldeman to be reinstated as an operative in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing, no matter how long she has been away from the service. It applies to Mrs. Haldeman, who is named in the order.

5147.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 4246, as amended by Executive Order No. 4278. That earlier order had established the Huachuca District of the Coronado National Forest on the Fort Huachuca Military Reservation in Arizona.

5148.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to the Indians of the Omaha Reservation in Nebraska. It applies to allotments whose trust period expires during the calendar year 1929 and extends that period for ten years.

5146.s: This order allows Edna May to be appointed as an Operative in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without following the civil service rules. It concerns her appointment and notes that she is the widow of a former Bureau employee and has minor children and her mother to support.

5145.s: The order lets Ida A. Coffey be appointed to a position in the Department of Commerce without following civil service rules. It says her husband had worked in the Patent Office until he resigned because of ill health and is now in the Naval Hospital with diabetes and tuberculosis. It also says she has three children and a mother who depends on her for support.

5144.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It stays in effect while the townships are resurveyed. It remains in force unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5143.s: This order restricts people from being brought into the United States or its possessions from any port in China, including Hong Kong, or the Philippine Islands. It applies directly or by transshipment, and it can be done only under conditions set by the Secretary of the Treasury. The order was issued to prevent the spread of epidemic cerebrospinal meningitis.

5142.s: This order says Mr. Ralph Ely Stedman may be reinstated to an appropriate position in the classified service, without regard to how long he has been away from service. It also says that if his eligibility for appointment is restored, he is intended to be offered a job in the General Accounting Office as a Junior Clerk, Grade CAF-2, with a salary of $1440 a year.

5141.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from settlement, location, sale, or entry, subject to prior valid claims. The lands are to be classified to see whether they are suitable for game refuge purposes. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5140.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in specified townships in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation. The land stays withdrawn while a resurvey is pending. It remains in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5139.s: This order sets aside certain lands in the Philippine Islands as naval reservations of the Government of the United States. It places those lands under the governance and control of the Navy Department, subject to any private rights that may exist. The lands include areas at Cavite, Canacao-Sangley Point, Baguio, Romblon, Cuyo, Abuyog, Cape Bojeador, San Fernando, and the mouth of the Imus River.

5138.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Wisconsin from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are reserved for classification and for a decision on whether they should be included in a national forest. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5137.s: This order creates Carbury, North Dakota, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 34 (Dakota). It says the port will be under the district headquarters at Pembina, North Dakota, and will take effect 30 days after the order is signed.

5136.s: This order amends Alaska Railroad townsite rules to let the Secretary of the Interior reappraise and sell unimproved lots in Nenana Townsite, Alaska, that belong to the United States. It also allows the Secretary to readjust assessments on those lots for street, sidewalk, alley, sanitation, and fire protection improvements made before August 31, 1921. For forfeited lots with valuable improvements, the rules on collecting unpaid assessments stay in effect.

5135.s: This order allows Walter K. Liscombe to be appointed as Associate Construction Engineer in the Office of the Supervising Architect of the Treasury without regard to how long he has been away from the service. It affects Mr. Liscombe and the Treasury office that would appoint him.

5134.s: This order allows Mary V. Kehoe to be appointed to a position in the General Accounting Office without meeting the civil service examination requirements. It says she is the widow of George D. Kehoe, who had worked for the Government Printing Office, the Treasury Department, and the General Accounting Office.

5133.s: This order waives a civil service rule for Percy W. Phillips, who is a member of the United States Board of Tax Appeals. It allows him to teach in the Summer School of the University of North Carolina.

5132.s: This order restores two parcels of land at Kahauiki, Oahu to their previous status for use by the Territory of Hawaii for road purposes. The land was taken from parts of the Kahauiki Military Reservation (Fort Shafter) and the Hawaii Arsenal Military Reservation. The parcels are described as 3.916 acres and 1.849 acres.

5131.s: This order allows George Henry Malone to be appointed to a supervising clerk job at the Naval Station in Cavite without following the Civil Service Act or rules. It says the appointment is to fill an existing vacancy. It also directs that he be discharged from the Navy.

5130.s: This order extends the port limits of New Orleans, Louisiana, to include part of Plaquemines Parish. It applies to the area east of west longitude 90°1'0" and north of north latitude 29°49'0", up to the middle of the Mississippi River.

5129.s: This order reserves two tracts of public land in the Philippine Islands for military purposes. One tract is in Zamboanga and one is on the Island of Jolo. The Zamboanga tract is subject to private rights if any exist, and it excludes one parcel and an existing public highway right of way.

5128.s: This order allows Joseph B. White to be appointed to a position in the classified service without following the usual civil service rules. It says he is a veteran and that he previously worked for the United States military government in Cuba. It also notes that he passed a Civil Service Commission examination in 1924 but was not appointed to that position.

5127.s: This order changes the rules for leave and travel pay for consular officers. It requires officers to report all absences from their posts to the Secretary of State, and it counts those absences toward the leave time allowed without loss of salary. It also sets limits on paid leave, leave to visit the United States, and salary for transit time.

5125.s: This order withdraws certain described land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, entry, or other disposition. It reserves the land for use with the construction and operation of railroad lines under the act named in the order.

5126.s: This order changes the rules for leave of absence for diplomatic officers. It says leave is granted at the President’s discretion through the Secretary of State, within statutory limits. It sets different paid leave limits for ambassadors, ministers, and other diplomatic officers, and it keeps separate rules for leave to visit the United States and travel time.

5124.s: This order changes a Civil Service Rule by raising the yearly pay limit from $480 to $540 for certain workers whose duties take only part of their time or are needed only for short periods. It also says the employee’s name, job title, duties, pay rate, and work place must be listed in periodic reports. For workers not paid by the year, the total service and how it was spread through the year must also be reported.

5123.s: The order adds an exception for part-time agents in the Department of Agriculture who take and transmit meteorological observations for airways and whose pay does not exceed $100 a month. It says this exception can continue beyond three years only if the Department of Agriculture and the Civil Service Commission agree. It also requires prior consent for certain appointments and a full report to the Commission for appointments under several listed clauses, as well as for changing an agent to different duties.

5122.s: This order sets aside certain United States lands from the former Fort Keogh Military Reservation in Montana as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds. The lands stay under the Department of Agriculture for their primary use in stock raising and forage crop experiments, and they remain subject to other valid existing rights. It also forbids setting fires, leaving fires unattended, hunting or disturbing wild animals or birds, taking eggs, and damaging U.S. property within the refuge.

5121.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It keeps those lands reserved while a resurvey of the township is done, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5120.s: This order temporarily withdraws 160 acres of land in New Mexico. The land is reserved pending archaeological investigation by the Smithsonian Institution. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5119.s: This order amends a previous order that set aside certain land on Oahu, Hawaii, for military purposes. It corrects the legal descriptions of the land at Keaau Ridge and Kaena Point. The order affects those two tracts of land.

5118.s: This order temporarily withdraws 40 acres in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for use by the State of Oregon as a lookout station, and the timber on it remains subject to sale by the United States.

5116.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Arkansas from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It stays in effect until the President revokes it or Congress acts, and it applies while a resurvey of the township is pending.

5117.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry, except as allowed by the cited laws. It does this while waiting for legislation that would let the lands be sold to the city of Los Angeles. The order says the sale would be for protecting the watershed that supplies water to the city.

5115.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. It keeps those lands closed until a resurvey of the township is finished, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5114.s: This order designates Horace Paul Bestor as Farm Loan Commissioner of the Federal Farm Loan Board. He is to serve in that role until otherwise directed.

5113.s: This order allows Mrs. Marie Crossette to be appointed to an appropriate position in the Department of Commerce without following civil-service rules. It says she is the widow of Louis F. Crossette, who served in the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce and handled China Relief work in 1921. The Secretary of Commerce says her services can be used in a permanent position.

5113-A.s: This order gives the Alien Property Custodian the President’s power under the Trading with the Enemy Act over the deposit, transfer, and payment of money and interest held by the Treasury, and over releasing and delivering property held under that law. If the Alien Property Custodian cannot act, that power goes to the General Counsel, and then to the Managing Director of the Office of the Alien Property Custodian. Claims that must be sent to the Attorney General and the President still have to be sent there. It also cancels any earlier orders that conflict with it.

5112.s: This order allows Mrs. Juliette V. Harring to be appointed to a position in the Department of Commerce without following civil service rules. It says she is the widow of Harry K. Harring, who worked in the Bureau of Standards. The order was issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of Commerce.

5111.s: This order changes the rules for reinstating people who left unclassified labor positions without delinquency or misconduct. It allows reinstatement to a similar position after a physical exam, with limits based on time since separation and service length, and the Commission may waive some time limits in certain cases. It also allows certain people linked to the Civil War, the war with Spain, or the war with Germany, and some of their family members, to be reinstated under the stated rules. It revokes one older paragraph of the reinstatement rule and renumbers the remaining paragraph.

5110.s: This order changes the Consular Regulations for U.S. consulates. It says only certain people of the Chinese race who are admissible under the treaty with China, the Chinese exclusion laws, the immigration laws, and another executive order may enter the United States or U.S. territory. It also sets rules for numbering and recording consular fees, lists a new tariff of consular fees, and requires certain record books to be kept at consular offices.

5109.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in effect until a resurvey is done or until the President or Congress revokes it.

5108.s: This order temporarily withdraws a described parcel of land in Washington from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for use by the State of Washington as a lookout station until the President or Congress revokes it.

5107.s: This order changes Schedule A of the civil service rules by adding a new exception to the examination requirement. It allows one private secretary or confidential clerk for each member of the United States Employees' Compensation Commission to be hired without that examination.

5106.s: This order changes Public Water Reserve No. 107 so it does not apply to the Territory of Alaska. It affects the rules for public water reserve land use in Alaska.

5105.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from use under the cited acts. It covers the listed townships and an unsurveyed area east of Timber Mountain, including Fortymile Canyon Pueblo. The lands are held pending a decision on whether to include them in a national monument.

5103.s: The order allows Mrs. Lottie C. Moyer to be appointed to a clerical job in the Office of the Director of Public Buildings and Public Parks of the National Capital without following civil service rules. It says she is the widow of Jacob S. Moyer, who worked there for more than twenty-five years. It also says she has several years of clerical experience with commercial firms and the Arlington Memorial Bridge Commission.

5104.s: This order sets rules for filling vacancies in postmaster jobs in first, second, and third class offices. If a vacancy is not filled by nomination of a qualified person in the competitive classified civil service, the Civil Service Commission must hold an open competitive examination and give the Postmaster General at least three eligible names, if possible. It also sets age and residency limits for applicants, and it says no person over 65 may be appointed acting postmaster unless already in the postal service.

5102.s: This order excludes two tracts of land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest. It restores those lands to entry under the public land laws. The tracts are at Primrose Landing on the Seward-Kenai Lake Highway and at Lawing on the Alaska Railroad.

5101.s: This order allows Mrs. Mary Elizabeth Porterfield to be appointed as an operative in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without regard to civil service rules. It says the Secretary of the Treasury recommended the appointment because she is the widow of Mr. James Porterfield, who served there for more than sixteen years. It also says he died on March 27, 1929, leaving his widow and two daughters without sufficient means of support.

5100.s: This order allows Mrs. Jean N. Edington to be appointed to a classified service position without following the civil service rules. It applies to her, and it notes that she has two children and that her husband is a patient in a state hospital.

5099.s: This order makes the rental and subsistence allowance rates in the 1922 law effective for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1930. It applies to officers of the various services who are entitled to those allowances.

5098.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It applies while those townships are waiting for a resurvey, unless the President or Congress revokes the order.

5097.s: This order allows certain Alaska lands reserved for lighthouse purposes to be leased for fur farming, if the Secretary of Commerce approves. The Secretary of the Interior would handle the leases, but the lands would stay under the control and jurisdiction of the Department of Commerce. Any lease must let the Lighthouse Service build and maintain navigation aids on the land and have free access to them. The lease cannot be renewed if the Department of Commerce wants the land for its own use.

5096.s: This order extends the port limits of Boston, Massachusetts to include Braintree, Weymouth, Hingham, and the waters next to them. It affects the Customs Collection District No. 4 headquarters port for customs port of entry purposes.

5095.s: This order reserves Nunivak Island from settlement, location, sale, entry, classification, and lease. It sets the island apart for Department of Agriculture experiments with reindeer, native caribou, and musk ox, and as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds, wild game, and fur-bearing animals. It also says the reservation will not interfere with lighthouse, military, or naval use, or with certain school and other improvements. It makes it unlawful to set fires or to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill wild birds and certain animals except under regulations.

5094.s: This order allows William A. Kennedy to be appointed as an associate construction engineer in the Office of the Supervising Architect without following the civil service rules. It says he had served the Government on the Lincoln Memorial and the Memorial to the Women of the Civil War, and it applies to his appointment.

5093.s: This order allows Ida Strong to be appointed to a position in the Department of Agriculture without following civil service rules. It applies to Ida Strong and refers to her as the widow of Jacob Strong, who worked in the department for more than thirty years before his death.

5092.s: This order changes the boundaries of Crook National Forest in Arizona by taking certain lands out of the forest. It says the excluded lands are reserved for townsite purposes and will be handled under the townsite laws, subject to valid existing claims.

5091.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in two townships in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while the townships are resurveyed, unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5090.s: This order revokes a 1927 withdrawal of certain public lands in a township in Wyoming that had been held pending a resurvey. If the lands are otherwise available and valid rights are protected, they must first be opened for 91 days to qualified ex-service men of the War with Germany under the homestead or desert land laws. After that, they may be opened to the general public under the public land laws. No rights can be claimed to the released lands before entry except as allowed by the order.

5089.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in described areas of Colorado for classification and to aid proposed legislation. It applies to those lands, but only subject to valid claims and existing withdrawals that already affect some of them. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5088.s: This order places $314,000, and any additional money available under the appropriation, to the credit of the Governor of the Virgin Islands of the United States. The governor may spend it on necessary expenses for the occupation of the Virgin Islands and for the temporary government of the West Indian Islands, and $49,000 may be used for public works projects damaged or delayed by the September 1928 hurricane. It also gives the governor the power to appoint workers and set salaries for positions that are not listed in the annual budgets of the two Colonial Councils.

5086.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in two townships in New Mexico. It says those lands, if otherwise available and subject to valid rights, will be opened first to entry under the homestead or desert land laws by qualified ex-service men of the War with Germany. After that period, the lands may be open to the general public under the public land laws, and no rights may be gained by settling there in advance of entry.

5085.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Wyoming from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it. It applies to the public lands in the listed township pending a resurvey.

5087.s: This order extends the trust period for allotments made to Indians on the Siletz Reservation in Oregon that were set to expire during 1929. The extension is for ten years, except for the allotments listed for the deceased allottees.

5084.s: This order waives the maximum age limit for admission to the general clerical examination in the Eleventh United States Civil Service District that closes April 5, 1929. It allows Mrs. Lessie L. Schaefer of Pendleton, Oregon, to take the examination, and the order says she is in good health and experienced in clerical work.

5083.s: This order allows Mrs. Emma E. Kennedy to be reinstated as an operative in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing. It says her reinstatement may be made without following the civil service time limit rules.

5082.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Oregon for classification and to support proposed legislation. It applies to the specific areas listed in the order, subject to valid claims and existing withdrawals. The withdrawal stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5081.s: This order abolishes Roche Harbor, Washington as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 30. It affects the port of entry at Roche Harbor and takes effect thirty days after the date of the order.

5080.s: This order transfers certain described lands in Montana from the Missoula National Forest to the Helena National Forest. The lands will be managed under the laws and regulations that apply to the Helena National Forest.

5079.s: This order requires certain decisions by the Commissioner of Internal Revenue to be open to inspection. It applies to decisions allowing a refund, credit, or abatement of income, war-profits, excess-profits, estate, or gift taxes over $20,000. People can inspect them only under rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury and approved by the President.

5078.s: This order creates Lincoln, Nebraska, as a port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 46, with headquarters at Omaha, Nebraska. It takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

5077.s: This order designates Viola B. Pugh, of the District of Columbia, to sign the President’s name to land patents. She had been appointed in 1921 as a clerk to sign land patents.

5076.s: This order designates Mrs. Helen V. McLeod of the General Land Office to sign the President’s name to land patents when the clerk who usually does that job is absent. It affects the handling of land patents in the Department of the Interior.

5075.s: This order allows Mrs. William M. Stuart to be appointed to a clerical job in the Federal Service even though she has been away from it for a long time. It says she was in the competitive classified service from July 1, 1902, to December 31, 1918.

5074.s: This order says Raymond F. Mulherin may be reinstated to an appropriate position in the classified service. It removes the usual time limit on his eligibility for reinstatement.

5073.s: This order allows Mrs. Lee H. Garby to be appointed to an appropriate classified service job without following the civil service rules. It says she is the widow of Dr. Carl D. Garby and that she did chemical work in the Departments of Navy, War, and Agriculture. The order says it is for charity.

5072.s: This order allows Miss Virginia Ladd to be appointed to an appropriate clerical job in the classified service without following the civil service rules. It applies to her appointment and changes how those rules are used for that hiring.

5070.s: This order authorizes James W. Girard to be reinstated as a Logging Engineer in the Forest Service. It says this can be done without following the usual time limit on eligibility for reinstatement under the civil service rules. It affects Mr. Girard and the Forest Service.

5069.s: This order allows Jeannette J. Donahue, the widow of Peter A. Donahue, to be reinstated to an appropriate position in the Department of Labor. It does this without regard to the time limit on reinstatement.

5067.s: This order assigns two radio frequencies to Station NAA of the Navy Department at Arlington, Virginia. The frequencies are for broadcasting programs arranged by the Pan American Union.

5068.s: This order amends civil service rules for entrance exams and layoffs in the classified service. It gives extra points to honorably discharged soldiers, sailors, and marines, certain disabled applicants, widows of honorably discharged service members, and wives of injured soldiers, sailors, and marines who are not qualified themselves but whose wives are qualified for appointment. It also says disabled veterans, their wives, and widows of honorably discharged soldiers, sailors, and marines are to be placed above others on the register, and it protects employees entitled to military preference in reductions in force if their record is good or their efficiency rating is equal to that of others retained.

5066.s: The order revokes an earlier withdrawal of certain public lands in a Wyoming township that had been held pending a resurvey. After the resurvey plat is officially filed, the lands would be open for 91 days only to qualified ex-service men of the War with Germany under the homestead or desert land laws. After that period, the lands would be open to the general public under the public land laws.

5064.s: This order allows Miss Elizabeth Gibson to be employed as a clerk or typist in the Navy Department or Naval Establishment without following the Civil Service Act or Rules. It affects Miss Gibson and the Navy Department, and it says the Civil Service Commission did not agree with the recommendation.

5063.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain described lands in Oregon from use for classification. It says the withdrawal is to help with legislation proposed in H.R. 16698 and S. 5529. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5061.s: This order allows Clifford C. Marsh to be reinstated as Assistant Postmaster at Yellowstone Park, Wyoming. It waives the time limit in the civil service rules for his reinstatement. It also says he was a classified employee from 1893 to 1914 and has worked temporarily and satisfactorily at the post office for the past seven years.

5062.s: The order designates the airspace over the District of Columbia as a prohibited area for public safety purposes from midnight March 2, 1929, to midnight March 6, 1929. During that time, no aircraft may fly through that airspace unless the Secretary of Commerce specifically permits it.

5060.s: This order allows Miss Barbara Davis to be appointed to a suitable job in the Department of Commerce without following the civil service rules. It applies to her appointment and relates to the service of her late father, Dr. William H. Davis, who was chief statistician in the Bureau of the Census. The Civil Service Commission did not agree with the waiver.

5059.s: This order allows Oliver H. Clarke to be reinstated to an appropriate job in the Office of the Supervising Architect in the Treasury Department. It says his reinstatement can happen without regard to the time limit on his eligibility. The Secretary of the Treasury recommended it, and the Civil Service Commission said it could not concur.

5057.s: This order allows Mrs. Gertrude L. George to be appointed to a classified position in the Customs Service of the Treasury Department without following the civil service law and rules. It says she is the widow of Samuel W. George, who worked in the Customs Service in Boston for about fourteen years.

5058.s: This order allows Mrs. Julia Behneke to be appointed to an appropriate position in the Department of Labor without following the civil service rules. The Secretary of Labor recommended the appointment, and the Civil Service Commission did not agree.

5056.s: This order allows Mary Scott Mills, the widow of John S. Mills, to be appointed to an appropriate classified government position without following the civil service rules. It says the Secretary of the Treasury recommended the order. It also says the Civil Service Commission was unable to agree.

5055.s: This order changes the civil service rules for certain temporary Forest Service jobs. It adds "scalers" to the list of positions excepted from examination, along with guards, field assistants, foremen, and telephone operators. These workers may be used only as long as needed during the fire season or when special work requires extra help, and appointments should be made from eligible registers when practicable.

5054.s: This order allows Mary E. Kelly to be reinstated in a clerical job in the classified civil service, without following the usual time limit for reinstatements. It affects Mrs. Kelly, who is identified as the widow of John J. Kelly and the mother of a ten-year-old daughter.

5053.s: This order lets Mrs. Anna M. Archibald be appointed to any federal job she is qualified for without following the Civil Service Act or Civil Service Rules. It applies to her alone and says the Civil Service Commission did not agree with the action.

5050.s: This order allows Samuel H. Thompson to be appointed to a position in or under the Indian Bureau without following civil service rules. It says he has had long service in high-grade supervisory positions outside government service.

5052.s: The order says Mrs. James E. Golladay may be appointed to an appropriate clerical position without following the civil service rules. It also says the Civil Service Commission cannot recommend the appointment because of the interests of the service.

5049.s: This order says Anna M. Stack may be appointed to an appropriate position in the classified service without regard to Civil Service rules. It applies to her appointment and says the decision is based on the President's personal knowledge of her qualifications.

5048.s: This order revokes part of Executive Order No. 4889 for one tract of land in Minnesota. The tract is Lot 2 in Section 23, Township 67 North, Range 17 West, 4th Principal Meridian, containing 48.75 acres. It says the land is part of a prior homestead entry, Cass Lake 014610.

5046.s: This order changes a prior reservation of certain lands in California so the Secretary of the Interior may approve a right of way for a tramway. It affects the Little River Redwood Company and the lands covered by the reserve.

5047.s: This order declares the Panama Canal Zone, including the "three mile limit," to be a Military Airspace Reservation. It sets rules for private aircraft in the Canal Zone, including registration papers, airworthiness papers, crew certificates, passenger and cargo lists, and radio licenses. Private aircraft must use prescribed routes, land at designated airfields, and follow inspections and other rules set by the Governor of the Panama Canal. It also bans certain items and limits photography of military and naval installations, and violations can bring fines or jail.

5045.s: This order changes the Consular Regulations. It removes the subsection about keeping a register of correspondence received and sent at inland consulates from paragraphs 604 and 605.

5044.s: This order changes the land description in a prior order about a 13 and one-third acre tract at Rockaway Point, Long Island, New York. The land is reserved and set apart for the use of the War Department in connection with the Fort Tilden Military Reservation. It replaces the earlier description with a new boundary description for that land.

5043.s: This order allows Mrs. Marion Hayes McCarthy to be appointed as a telephone operator in the War Department without following the civil service rules. It affects Mrs. McCarthy, whose husband died in an airplane accident while on duty.

5041.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Utah from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands are being reviewed for possible use in connection with the Bear River Migratory Bird Refuge. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5042.s: This order moves the position of press helper in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing, including the current workers in that job, into the competitive classified civil service. Future openings for that position must be filled under the rules for the classified civil service.

5040.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain described lands in Wyoming for elk refuge purposes. The land is taken out of settlement, location, sale, or entry, except for prior legal claims and land already in National Forests. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5039.s: This order directs that the dam proposed in a report to Congress, and referred to there as Dam No. 3, be named General Joe Wheeler Dam. It affects the naming of that dam.

5038.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain described land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It is subject to prior claims that were legally started and kept in effect. The land is to be classified and considered for possible addition to Pinnacles National Monument.

5037.s: This order temporarily withdraws described public lands in Utah from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The lands will be classified while the government decides whether to add them to Zion National Park. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

5036.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain unsurveyed land on Gravina Island, Alaska, from use under the stated laws. It is meant to protect the water supply of a Department of Agriculture marine station. The land includes areas near a survey line and a small unnamed lake, except for part already covered by U.S. Survey No. 1334.

5035.s: This order abolishes Frenchville, Maine as a port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 1. It applies to customs operations in that district and takes effect thirty days after the order date.

5034.s: This order allows Arthur J. Dahn to be reinstated as a clerk in the Railway Mail Service without following the usual time limit in the civil service rules. It says he was seriously injured in a railroad wreck while on duty and was unable to serve for several years.

5033.s: This order temporarily withdraws a 40-acre tract in Oregon from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for use by the State of Oregon as a lookout station, while the timber on it remains subject to sale by the United States.

5032.s: This order cancels Chapter XII of the diplomatic instructions and replaces it with new rules on passports and visas. It says only the Secretary of State and certain authorized diplomatic missions or consular offices may issue or verify passports, and no one else may do so. It also says visas are handled by consular officers, while diplomatic visas are granted by diplomatic missions only, with reports required on some visa issuances.

5031.s: This order withdraws certain public land in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. It stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it, while a resurvey of the township is pending.

5030.s: This order withdraws certain public land in two Florida townships from settlement, location, sale, entry, and other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal lasts while a resurvey is done of those townships. It stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

5029.s: This order withdraws certain public land in two townships in New Mexico from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all other forms of appropriation. The withdrawal stays in place while the land is resurveyed. It affects anyone who might seek to settle on or claim that land.

5027.s: This order waives a prior rule that required candidates for presidential postmasterships to pass a civil service examination. It allows Ward M. Parker to be nominated as postmaster at Venice, Florida, without examination. The order says the Civil Service Commission had secured only one eligible after three examinations and that more examinations would probably not produce enough eligibles for three names.

5028.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to the Rosebud Indians in South Dakota. The extension applies to allotments that would otherwise expire during the calendar year 1929 and adds a further period of ten years.

5026.s: This order directs several Bureau of Fisheries patrol boats to patrol waters where seal herds and sea otters are found. It authorizes the masters of those vessels, along with certain Bureau officers, to search U.S. vessels suspected of breaking the convention or related rules. It also allows them to seize those vessels and their officers and crew and bring them to Alaska, California, Oregon, or Washington for trial.

5025.s: This order withdraws certain described lands in Roseau and Lake of the Woods counties, Minnesota, from settlement, entry, or other disposition. It is meant to carry out the act of Congress that puts the 1925 convention between the United States and Great Britain into effect. Existing legal rights are not affected, and the withdrawal applies when existing entries are canceled or relinquished or pending applications are finally rejected.

5024.s: This order allows Carrie C. Anderson to be appointed to a clerical job in the General Accounting Office without following the civil service rules. It affects Mrs. Anderson and makes an exception to the usual hiring rules for that office.

5023.s: This order extends the trust period for allotments made to the Iowa Indians in Kansas and Nebraska that were set to expire during 1929. The extension is for ten years, except for allotments 5, 15, and 33, which are listed by name.

5022.s: This order changes Table I in Executive Order No. 4728. It adds a special entry for the Naval Mission to Brazil with set rates for subsistence and quarters, and says the existing special entry does not apply to enlisted men attached to that mission.

5021.s: This order waives a previous rule that required candidates for presidential postmasterships to pass a civil service examination. It allows Dr. Edward V. Sheely to be nominated as postmaster at Memphis, Tennessee, without examination.

5020.s: This order allows James M.E. Brown to be reinstated as a guard in the Treasury Department without following the civil service time limit for reinstatement. It affects Mr. Brown and the Treasury Department position he may return to.

5019.s: This order allows Mrs. Mildred Brown McIntosh to be appointed as a typewriter at the Naval Air Station in Pensacola, Florida, without following civil service rules. It applies to her, and she is the widow of a Navy chief aviation pilot who died in the line of duty at that station. The order was issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Navy.

4986.s: This order withdraws certain lots and blocks in the Osborn townsite in Montana and sets them aside for use by the Department of Agriculture as an agricultural field station. It applies to the listed blocks, lots, streets, and avenues in the townsite. The order stays in effect unless the President or Congress revokes it.

4994.s: This order extends the trust period for four allotments made to Indians of the Winnebago Reservation in Nebraska. The allotments are listed for Young Rogue, Mary Rave, Greenhair, and Jesse White Greenhair, all marked deceased. It says the trust period on these allotments is extended for ten years.

4981.s: This order extends the trust period on certain land allotments made to Indians of the Lower Brule Reservation in South Dakota for 10 more years from the date the trust would have expired in 1928. It does not apply to Allotment No. 335, Big Eagle, deceased.

4979.s: This order extends the trust period for allotments made to Indians on the Winnebago Reservation in Nebraska that were set to expire during 1928. It does not apply to the listed exceptions, including several deceased allottees and part of one allotment devised to named individuals.

4929.s: This order withdraws a tract of unsurveyed land in the Carson National Forest in New Mexico from entry or appropriation under U.S. land laws. The land is to protect the watershed that the Indians of the Taos Pueblo use for irrigation and domestic water.

4898.s: This order extends the trust period for allotments of Pawnee Indians of Oklahoma that would otherwise expire during 1928. The extension is for ten years. It lists several allotments that are excepted from the extension, including some that belong to deceased allottees.

4858.s: This order extends the trust period for allotments of the Prairie Band of Pottawatomi Indians in Kansas that were set to expire in 1928. The extension is for ten years. It does not apply in full to the listed allotments, and some exceptions are tied to specific land parcels and deceased allottees.

4816.s: This order extends the trust period for certain allotments on the Oakland Reservation in Oklahoma for ten years from June 5, 1928. It affects the named Indian allotments listed in the order, including several that belong to deceased people or people who now have different names.

4705.s: This order sets rules for the order of rank and seating among ambassadors, Foreign Service officers, Army officers, Navy and Marine Corps officers, and Foreign Commerce officers. It says who ranks above whom in diplomatic missions, international conferences, and consular districts. It also rescinds earlier executive orders that conflict with these rules.

4628.s: This order sets the west boundary of an Indian reservation in Utah for jurisdictional purposes tied to the administration of the public lands affected by it. It says the boundary runs from the Utah-Arizona line north along section lines in specified townships to the middle of the San Juan River.

4601.s: This order sets rules for awarding the Distinguished Flying Cross. It says who can receive it, including certain U.S. military members, some reserve members, and members of foreign military, naval, or air forces serving with U.S. forces, but not civilians. It also explains how recommendations are made, what proof is needed, time limits for awards, and how the decoration may be given after a person's death or replaced if lost or damaged.

4549.s: The order withdraws certain public lands in Arizona from settlement, entry, sale, or other disposal. It sets those lands apart for use with the San Carlos Indian Irrigation Project, subject to any existing prior rights. The order lists the specific townships and sections covered.

4571.s: This order extends the trust period on allotments made to the Sac and Fox of the Missouri Indians in Kansas and Nebraska that were set to expire during 1927. The extension applies for ten years from the date the trust period was to end, except for allotment No. 19, Que-nah-pe-ah (deceased), and allotment No. 70, Shawnee (deceased).

4527.s: This order allows Alaska Railroad employees who live in towns along the railroad line to run for municipal office there or hold those offices. The General Manager of the railroad must decide that the employee’s railroad duties are not being disrupted.

4538.s: This order sets rules for filling postmaster vacancies in first, second, and third class offices when a person from the competitive classified civil service is not nominated. It requires the Civil Service Commission to hold an open competitive examination, then send the results to the Postmaster General, who submits one of the three highest qualified people to the President unless the applicant is disqualified by character or residence. No person past his sixty-fifth birthday or who has not lived within the delivery of the office for two years before the examination may take the exam. The Postmaster General must also check that the chosen candidate has kept living within the delivery of the post office up to the time of selection.

4476.s: The order sets document rules for aliens entering the United States, the Philippine Islands, and certain other American possessions. Immigrants generally must show immigration visas, while some children, returning residents, and a few others are exempt or may use reentry permits. Non-immigrants generally must show passports or similar papers, but the order lists several exceptions, including some travelers in transit, certain seamen, and some people from named countries and possessions.

4439.s: This order lets State, county, or municipal officers be appointed as prohibition officers for the Treasury Department, at a nominal rate of pay. They would help enforce the National Prohibition Act and related laws, except in States that have rules against State officers holding Federal office.

4359-A.s: This order cancels an earlier consular rule and replaces it with new rules on citizenship, naturalization, expatriation, passports, registration, and protection abroad. It says who is a U.S. citizen by birth, who may or may not be naturalized, and how citizenship rules apply to married women and children. It also sets when U.S. officials may give protection to citizens overseas and when that protection may be withheld.

4268.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Treasury to remit certain payments of the Chinese indemnity to the Board of Trustees of the China Foundation for the Promotion of Education and Culture. The money is to be used to further develop educational and other cultural activities in China. The order also says the funds are for scientific knowledge, technical training, research, and cultural work such as libraries.

4239.s: This order transfers the Bureau of Mines from the Department of the Interior to the Department of Commerce, where it will be supervised by the Secretary of Commerce. It also transfers the Division of Mineral Resources in the Geological Survey, along with its employees, appropriations, records, and public property. Employees doing oil-leasing work and mineral-leasing work, and the related equipment and appropriations, stay in the Interior Department. The transfers take effect on July 1, 1925.

4224.s: This order lets the Secretary of State make agreements with foreign countries about visa fees for non-immigrants. Citizens or subjects of those countries may get passport visas to visit the United States without the application and visa fees, or with a reduced fee, if their country gives similar treatment to U.S. citizens. It applies to people who are not immigrants under the Immigration Act of 1924 and to countries that make similar concessions to U.S. citizens.

4175.s: This order transfers the United States Patent Office from the Department of the Interior to the Department of Commerce. It also moves the office’s appropriations, records, and public property under the supervision of the Secretary of Commerce, starting April 1, 1925.

4128.s: This order changes an earlier order that had transferred certain lands to the Treasury Department for coast guard purposes. It removes lot 7 in Nee-Ah Harbor Abandoned Military Reservation from that transfer, except for a 250-foot strip, and puts the tract under the Secretary of the Interior.

4060.s: This order reserves certain islands, keys, harbors, and shoals near Key West, Florida, for use by the Navy Department for naval purposes. It covers the areas described in the order and is subject to any existing vested rights in those areas.

3949.s: This order takes certain lands in Washington out of an earlier transfer to the Interior Department. It places those tracts under the jurisdiction and control of the Treasury Department for coast guard purposes.

3987.s: This order directs U.S. representatives in foreign countries to meet regularly and share information about American commercial and other interests. It requires officers to exchange economic and trade information, file copies of reports, and avoid duplicating work. It also sets rules for communication between consular officers and other departments and for notifying officials when someone arrives for a special investigation.

3861.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Interior to operate the railroad systems in Alaska that were built or acquired under the 1914 law. It also covers related branch lines, feeder lines, and telegraph and telephone lines connected to those railroads.

3871.s: This order transfers administration of the National Prohibition Act in the Virgin Islands of the United States from the Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of the Navy. It affects the government role for enforcing Prohibition in the Virgin Islands.

3788.s: This order says some named former employees of the Bureau of Engraving and Printing may reenter the classified service in appropriate positions for five years from March 31, 1922, if the Civil Service Commission certifies them. It also says some named people are not eligible to return because they were retired on annuity. The reinstatement of three other named people has already been authorized.

3844.s: This order gives the Alien Property Custodian the powers the President has under Section 9 of the Trading with the Enemy Act for certain claims. It applies to claims where the amount to be returned or paid does not exceed ten thousand dollars in money or other property. The Alien Property Custodian may send any such claim to the Attorney General for an opinion on the law or facts, and other executive orders are changed as needed to match this order.

3773.s: This order creates the Federal Council of Citizenship Training. The council includes one representative and one alternate from several federal offices and departments. Its job is to suggest ways federal offices can work together to improve citizenship training and to cooperate with public and private agencies across the country.

3759.s: This order removes about 13.5 acres from the Navajo Indian Reservation in Arizona. The land is a tract that had been part of the area withdrawn for Navajo Indians in 1901.

3744.s: This order moves the Fort Apache military reservation in Navajo County, Arizona, under the control of the Secretary of the Interior. It says the land is no longer needed for military purposes and will be handled under the law for its disposition.

3721.s: This order creates an Interdepartmental Patents Board. The board is to recommend rules for how the Government handles inventions and patents made by government employees or acquired by the Government, and to share information about patents, applications, licenses, and other rights under those patents. It affects government departments and other government units.

3714.s: This order changes a prior civil service preference for presidential postmaster examinations. It extends the same preference to honorably discharged veterans of the Spanish-American War.

3657.s: The order removes the current Director and Assistant Director of the Bureau of Engraving and Printing and names new officers in their place. It also abolishes several offices in the bureau, renames some others, and says the Director will fill vacancies created by the reorganization. Some people eligible for retirement because of age are to be placed on the retired list.

3637.s: This order temporarily withdraws 386.85 acres of land in New Mexico from settlement, entry, sale, or other disposal until March 5, 1924. If legislation is not enacted by then and no other directions are given, the land will become subject to disposal under any law then in effect. It also replaces Executive Order No. 3351 from November 6, 1920.

3623.s: This order selects the American Relief Administration to receive surplus medicines and medical, surgical, and hospital supplies from the War, Navy, and Treasury Departments and the United States Shipping Board. The supplies are for the relief of the distressed and famine-stricken people of Russia, up to four million dollars in original cost to the United States. It also directs the organization to transport and distribute the supplies in Russia, and requires reports on the amounts delivered and how they were used.

3601.s: This order sets up a commission to buy, transport, and deliver corn, seed grain, and preserved milk for the relief of the distressed and starving people of Russia and for spring planting where seed grain has been used up. It authorizes the United States Grain Corporation to pay the bills for this work, up to $20,000,000. It also directs the American Relief Administration to accept these goods and distribute them in Russia.

3594.s: This order transfers certain historical papers from the Department of State to the Library of Congress. The papers include the Journal, Acts and Proceedings of the Convention that framed the Constitution, the Articles of Confederation, Thomas Jefferson’s draft of the Declaration of Independence, and certain papers of the Continental Congress, James Madison, and Benjamin Franklin. The Library of Congress is to preserve them and make them available for historical and other legitimate uses under its rules.

3578.s: This order sets rules for preparing and sending the federal budget and for how the Bureau of the Budget will handle estimates from government departments. It lets the Bureau revise those estimates and requires the Treasury to provide budget and revenue information, along with recommendations if expected receipts are too low or too high. It also puts routine business coordination across departments under the Director of the Budget and the Chief Coordinator.

3577.s: This order sets a uniform way to date proclamations, commissions, and other similar formal documents. It changes the wording used before the President’s signature and applies to the departments in Washington. It also allows the forms already on hand in the departments to keep being used.

3560.s: This order directs the Civil Service Commission to add five points to the exam ratings of certain World War veterans applying for Presidential postmaster jobs. It also says their time in World War service may count toward the required business experience, and all age limits must be waived for them.

3524.s: This order says certain design matters must be sent to the Commission of Fine Arts for advice before they are approved. It applies to medals, insignia, and coins made by executive departments, as well as statues, fountains, monuments, parks, and public buildings that affect the appearance of Washington, D.C. or the District of Columbia.

3550.s: This order sets rules for preparing and submitting the federal budget and for how the Bureau of the Budget will work. It lets the Bureau assemble, revise, raise, or lower the spending estimates from departments and establishments, under the President’s review. The Director of the Budget sets the plan for the estimates and may consider cuts in working forces, pay, and unnecessary activities. Estimates for the public debt can be revised only with the Secretary of the Treasury’s concurrence.

3489.s: This order sets rules for reserving, surveying, and selling townsites along government railroads in Alaska. It gives the Secretary of the Interior authority over reservations, surveys, public sales, appraisals, and private entry of lots. It also gives certain residents with improvements on reserved townsites a possible preference right to buy up to two lots, and it revokes earlier conflicting orders.

3474.s: This order puts the administration and conservation of oil and gas lands in certain naval petroleum and shale reserves under the Secretary of the Interior, subject to the President’s supervision. It covers naval petroleum reserves in California and Wyoming and naval shale reserves in Colorado and Utah. It says no general policy on drilling or reserving lands in a naval reserve may be changed or adopted without consulting and working with the Secretary of the Navy.

3464.s: This order moves the listed lands at Fort Duchesne, Utah, out of military control because they are no longer needed for military purposes. It places the 150 acres under the full jurisdiction and control of the Department of the Interior. The land is within the Uintah Indian Reservation.

3466.s: This order responds to the death of Edward Douglas White, Chief Justice of the United States. It directs the National Flag to be displayed at half staff on public buildings, and at legations and consulates for thirty days. It also closes the White House and certain executive offices in Washington on the day of his funeral and calls for usual military and naval honors.

3457.s: This order allows certain alien passengers on ships calling at U.S. ports, including outlying territories and insular possessions, to land without visaed passports for a short stop. They must continue on the same vessel and may stay only for the limited time the ship is in port. Anyone who plans to stay longer must present visaed passports, and ship masters must show that temporary passengers will not remain ashore after the ship leaves.

3452.s: This order restores the east half of the northwest quarter of section twenty-nine, township eight south, range twenty-one east of the Mount Diablo meridian in California to its former status. The land had been withdrawn for Indian use by Executive Order 2023.

3439.s: This order directs the War Department to take over the records of the Council of National Defense, the War Industries Board, the Committee on Public Information, and the War Labor Board. It affects those organizations' records and moves them to the War Department.

3455.s:
The order says that when a first, second, or third class postmaster job is vacant, and no one in the competitive classified civil service is nominated, the Civil Service Commission must hold an open competitive examination. After that, the Commission must send the results to the Postmaster General, who submits one of the top three qualified people to the President for appointment, unless the applicant is disqualified by character or residence.

It says people who have passed their sixty-fifth birthday, or who have not lived within the delivery of the office for the two years before the vacancy, cannot take the examination. It also says that if someone in the competitive classified service is to be nominated, the Civil Service Commission must first find that the person meets the minimum requirements.

3374.s: This order ends the United States Fuel Administration’s authority to gather information about coal and coke producers and distributors under the earlier order. It says those powers were restored to the Federal Trade Commission as of January 1, 1920. The change affects the Federal Trade Commission and the former Fuel Administration powers over coal cost information.

3367.s: This order sets maximum punishments for soldiers under courts-martial. It limits forfeiture or detention of pay, confinement at hard labor, hard labor without confinement, and, in some cases, dishonorable discharge.
