u-tr-19061219.s: This order withdraws certain lands in New Mexico from sale and settlement. It sets those lands apart as a reservation for the use and benefit of the Indians of the Jemez Pueblo, except for any tracts already owned by others or covered by valid legal rights.

u-tr-19060205.s: This order withdraws block 77 in Randlett, Utah, from sale or other disposition. It temporarily sets the land apart to the Protestant Episcopal Church for missionary and cemetery purposes for the benefit of the Ute Indians, as long as it is used that way. If the land is no longer used by the church, it will stay a public reservation for church and cemetery purposes for the Ute Indians.

u-tr-19060131.s: This order changes the boundaries of the military reservation at Fort Washakie, Wyoming, based on a new survey. It moves one corner so the reservation does not include part of the land occupied by buildings for the Indian school. The land use remains subject to the Indians’ rights, and it can be vacated if the interests of the Indians require it after notice to the Secretary of War.

u-tr-19051117.s: This order says an officer or employee in the classified service may be removed without a hearing if the President or head of an executive department finds the person is inefficient or incapable and that removal would improve the public service. The reason for removal must be written down and filed. If misconduct happens in the presence of the President or department head, removal may be made at once without notice.

u-tr-19051118.s: This order amends the civil service rules to add a new clause in the Treasury Department. It creates one examiner of tobacco and one examiner of tea in the Customs Service at the Port of Chicago.

u-tr-19051017.s: This order allows the President or the head of an executive department to remove a classified service officer or employee without a hearing if they are found to be inefficient or incapable and the public service would be improved by the removal. If misconduct happens in the presence of the President or department head, the person may be removed right away without notice. The reason for a removal must be written down and filed.

u-tr-19051117-2.s: This order changes civil service rules for removals, reductions, and other punishment. It says penalties for similar offenses must be alike, and a person in a competitive position can be removed only for cause that promotes the efficiency of the service. It also allows some removals without notice, requires written reasons to be filed in some cases, and limits Civil Service Commission review of removals to certain complaints.

u-tr-19051013.s: The order says no government officer or employee may directly or indirectly help instruct people for special preparation for the United States Civil Service Commission exam. If an officer or employee is found doing this, it is enough cause to remove that person from service.

u-tr-19050831.s: This order sets pay and travel allowances for members of the advisory board of engineers on plans for the Panama Canal. Each member is to receive $5,000 when the board’s report is completed, plus $15 per day for personal expenses while on duty and the actual cost of transportation. It also increases the allowance for Gen. Davis and Gen. Abbott by the amount of their retired pay so they receive the same compensation as the other members.

u-tr-19050826.s: This order waives a six-month service requirement for the transfer of W. E. Lackland from the Treasury Department to the Post-Office at Prescott, Arizona. It applies only to that transfer.

u-tr-19050729.s: This order sets aside a large area of public land in the Territory of New Mexico as a reservation for the use and occupation of the Pueblo Indians of New Mexico belonging to the Pueblo of Santa Clara. Any land with valid existing rights under U.S. law is left out of the reservation. If those claims are later given up, lapse, or are canceled, those lands will be added to the reservation.

u-tr-19050725.s: This order approves a special waiver of the rule that normally requires reinstatement within one year. It applies to Mrs. McLanaham, a former Government Printing Office employee who had been separated from her job, later became a widow, and had three children to support.

u-tr-19050722.s: This order approves the recommendations made by the Acting Secretary of War. It also directs the Secretary of the Interior to have the action noted in the records of the General Land Office.

u-tr-19050629.s: This order allows Mrs. Edna K. Hoyt, who is temporarily employed as a clerk in the Department of State, to be permanently appointed without examination under the civil-service rules. Her pay would be at the rate of $1,200 a year.

u-tr-19050721.s: This order moves most of the Fort Shaw military reservation in Montana to the control of the Secretary of the Interior for disposition under law. It also places the land set aside for the Fort Shaw Indian School under that control, but keeps it reserved for Indian school purposes. The order says the reservation had become useless for military purposes.

u-tr-19050310.s: This order withholds certain lands in Utah from sale and settlement and sets them apart for Indian purposes as an addition to the Navaho Indian Reservation. Any tract in the described area that was already settled or occupied, or had valid rights under existing U.S. laws before the order, is excluded from the reservation.

u-tr-19050127.s: This order approves Mr. E. W. Libbey’s appointment as a telegraph and telephone operator in the Department of Commerce and Labor. It also says he may stay in the service without taking an examination under the Civil Service rules.

u-tr-19050515.s: This order cancels a prior order that set apart certain lands in Utah as an addition to the Navaho Indian Reservation. It then sets apart new described lands in Utah for Indian purposes and withholds them from sale and entry as part of the reservation. Any tracts already settled on, occupied, or covered by valid rights under existing U.S. laws before this order are excluded.

u-tr-19050109.s: This order says Mrs. Elizabeth C. Peters may be reinstated as a sewer in the Government Printing Office. It allows her reinstatement without following the part of Rule IX that limits reinstatements to one year after separation.

u-tr-19050104.s: This order allows Mrs. Evelyn M. Ford to be reinstated as a clerk in the office of the Secretary of War. It says this can be done without following Rule IX, which limits eligibility to one year from the date of separation.

u-tr-19041129.s: This order says no one may be appointed or employed in an Executive Department or office to do work like classified employees unless it follows the civil-service rules. If there is doubt about whether an exam is required, the department head must consult the Civil Service Commission. If they do not agree, the case goes to the Attorney-General for an opinion.

u-tr-19041129-2.s: This order says substitute watchmen in the Government Printing Office will be treated as covered by the civil-service rules. It also says the forty named people now serving in that office will be treated as classified under those rules.

u-tr-19041115.s: This order classifies the Isthmian Canal Commission and applies the civil-service act and rules to it. It says people may not be appointed, employed, promoted, or transferred there unless they pass an examination, unless they are specifically exempted. The order does not apply to persons employed merely as laborers, persons whose appointments are confirmed by the Senate, or engineers detailed from the army.

u-tr-19040624.s: This order allows Clarence Reeder to be appointed as private secretary to the Director of the Geological Survey. It says he may be appointed without taking an examination under the civil-service rules.

u-tr-19040623.s: This order makes an exception to the civil-service rules so Dr. William L. Ralph can be appointed without examination. He is appointed as curator of the section of birds' eggs in the National Museum, at a salary of $100 per month.

u-tr-19040617.s: This order makes an exception to the civil-service rules. It allows Samuel D. Amen to be appointed as an internal-revenue agent.

u-tr-19040613.s: This order says a person who is put back into the classified service in a lower grade than before may be promoted back to the former grade without an examination. It affects people who were separated from classified service and later reinstated at a lower grade.

u-tr-19040602.s: This order transfers certain lands in the Grand Forks land district in North Dakota to the Devils Lake land district. It applies to the lands within the boundaries described in the order.

u-tr-19040526.s: This order allows Mr. I. B. Conklin to be appointed as a special laborer, serving as a clerk in the office of the paymaster at the navy-yard in Washington, D.C. It says the appointment may be made without examination under the civil-service rules.

u-tr-19040518.s: This order allows Miss Katherine C. Masterson to be reinstated in the Government Printing Office. It sets aside the year limit in Civil-Service Rule IX for her reinstatement.

u-tr-19040326.s: This order changes a civil-service rule to cover physicians employed by contract in the Indian service. It says physicians in that service, if they are paid not more than $720 a year, may perform their official duties while also keeping a private practice. Each job must still be approved by the Commission.

u-tr-19040310.s: This order directs all government officials, including civil, military, and naval officials, to observe the President's proclamation of neutrality in the war between Russia and Japan. It also tells them to avoid actions or speech that could cause irritation to either side. The order says they should act in a way that gives no just offense to people of any foreign and friendly power.

u-tr-19040304.s: The order allows Mr. Merrit O. Chance to be transferred from clerk to the Secretary of War to superintendent of post-office supplies in the Post-Office Department. He may make this move without taking a noncompetitive examination. The order says this is because he passed the entrance examination for the classified service in the clerk grade, had former service in the Post-Office Department, and has general knowledge of postal affairs.

u-tr-19040301.s: This order says most civil service positions in the War Department in the Philippines will be treated as classified under civil-service rules. It does not include positions filled by skilled or unskilled laborers or by people appointed by the President. Some current workers who are specially approved may stay in their jobs, and after three years in those positions they may be transferred to competitive positions in the United States under civil-service rules.

u-tr-19040227.s: This order says Mrs. Marie L. Baldwin may be certified for appointment as a clerk in the Office of Indian Affairs. It allows that appointment at $900 and says it can be made without following Civil-Service Rule VII.

u-tr-19040225.s: The order allows Mr. Francis Walker of Massachusetts to be appointed as a special agent in the Bureau of Corporations. It sets his pay at $2,000 a year and says he may be appointed without examination under the Civil-Service rules.

u-tr-19040220.s: This order changes a prior order and keeps a tract of land from being entered or settled. It makes that land part of the Pine Ridge Sioux Indian Reservation in South Dakota. The land includes the Pine Ridge Boarding School Irrigation Ditch and the School Pasture.

u-tr-19040205.s: This order revokes a special rule from July 3, 1902, that made certain people who worked for the United States in the military government of Cuba eligible to stay on in the classified civil service. It affects those workers and the classified service positions of a grade corresponding to the ones they held.

u-tr-19040201.s: This order allows Mrs. Kate L. Croggan to be reinstated as a sewer in the Government Printing Office. It says this can be done without following Rule IX’s one-year limit for reinstatement after separation.

u-tr-19040125.s: This order restores a tract of land in Nebraska to the public domain. The land had been withdrawn from sale and set aside as an addition to the Sioux Indian Reservation in the Territory of Dakota.

u-tr-19040107.s: This order allows Mrs. G. W. Shipman to be appointed as a clerk in the Office of the First Assistant Postmaster-General. It says she may be appointed without examination under the Civil-Service rules.

u-tr-19031204.s: This order allows Mr. Francis L. Hawes of New York to be appointed as a special agent in the Bureau of Corporations. It says he may be appointed at $1,600 a year without examination under the civil-service rules.

u-tr-19031228.s: This order allows Mrs. Frank L. Harrigan to be reinstated as a ruling machine feeder in the Government Printing Office. It says this can be done without following Rule IX, which limits reinstatement eligibility to one year from separation.

u-tr-19031102.s: This order allows Mrs. Roy L. Quackenbush, who was working temporarily as a clerk in the Post-Office Department, to get a permanent appointment. It says she may be appointed without examination.

u-tr-19031009.s: This order allows Clarence A. Cook to be appointed as a special agent of the Bureau of Corporations in the Department of Commerce and Labor. It says the job would pay $2,000 a year and would not require an examination under the civil-service rules.

u-tr-19031023.s: This order allows Mrs. Lillian B. Kellogg to be reinstated as a piece sewer in the Government Printing Office. It says she may be reinstated without following the rule that limits reinstatement eligibility to one year after separation.

u-tr-19030915.s: This order sets aside part of the Camp McDowell abandoned military reservation for the use and occupancy of Mohave-Apache Indians living there or nearby. It also allows the Secretary of the Interior to place other Indians there if needed. The reserved land includes areas with Government improvements and certain tracts where valid rights have not attached under the 1894 act.

u-tr-19030820.s: This order allows Dr. William A. White to be appointed to the vacant superintendent position at the Government Hospital for the Insane. It says he may be appointed without an examination under the civil-service rules.

u-tr-19030809.s: This order allows Mrs. Julia W. Wellborn to be permanently appointed as a Clerk in the Geological Survey. It says she may be appointed without examination under the civil service rules.

u-tr-19030817.s: This order lets Allen Hazen continue as an expert and consulting engineer for the Washington filtration plant. His work may continue during construction and the plant’s initial operation, for up to twenty-four months.

u-tr-19030731.s: This order withdraws four tracts of land in southeastern Nevada from sale and settlement. It sets them apart as an addition to the Moapa River or Paiute Indian Reservation for the use of the Paiute Indians.

u-tr-19030730.s: This order allows Luther M. Walter to be appointed as a law clerk in the Interstate Commerce Commission. The appointment would be made after an appropriate noncompetitive examination.

u-tr-19030729.s: This order allows Mrs. Annie M. West and Mrs. Sadie B. Yates to be reinstated to their former jobs at the Government Printing Office. It says this can happen without following the rule that limits reinstatement eligibility to one year after separation.

u-tr-19030708.s: This order says that when unskilled labor tests are used, age must be left out for Civil War soldiers and sailors. Their fitness is to be judged by physical qualifications, moral character, industry, and ability to do manual labor.

u-tr-19030713.s: This order approved the appointment of 10 men to jobs in the Department of Commerce and Labor without civil-service examination. The reasons given included special qualifications, experience, and the need for messengers during the department’s organization. It covered positions such as special examiner, clerk, chief of division, assistant telegrapher, lieutenant of the watch, messenger, and assistant messenger.

u-tr-19030529.s: This order transfers a described area of land in Minnesota from the Cass Lake land district to the Duluth land district. It affects the land within the listed boundaries in that state.

u-tr-19030703.s: The order concerns Charles B. Terry, a former temporary clerk in the Post-Office Department who had been moved to a laborer job in Washington. It says he could be reinstated to his former position only after he filed an application with satisfactory proof of his efficiency and integrity and showed he was eligible under the rules. The order also notes that he had been convicted of a crime in 1894, but had been pardoned and restored to his civil rights.

u-tr-19030328.s: This order moves a federal office from Marshall, Minnesota, to St. Cloud, Minnesota. It affects the office that was then located in Marshall.

u-tr-19030327.s: This order moves the land office now at St. Cloud, Minnesota, to Cass Lake. It also changes the boundaries of several land districts in Minnesota. Parts of the St. Cloud district are added to the Marshall district, and other parts are moved from the Crookston and Duluth districts into the St. Cloud district.

206.s: This order moves the Revolutionary archives from the Department of State to the Library of Congress. The archives include records and papers of the Continental Congress and papers of George Washington, James Madison, Thomas Jefferson, Alexander Hamilton, James Monroe, and Benjamin Franklin. The Secretary of State may keep some parts back if needed for the Department of State records, and the Librarian of Congress will set the rules for access and use.

u-tr-19030326.s: This order extends certain hiring rules for mere laborers and workmen from Washington to executive civil service offices outside Washington, as quickly as practicable. It directs the United States Civil Service Commission to help create and maintain a registration system to test applicants before hiring. The test is to be competitive and open to all United States citizens who meet the age, physical ability, character, and experience requirements.

u-tr-19021126.s: This order reserves a specific parcel of land in California for Indian school purposes. It says the land will be part of the Greenville (Cal.) Indian Industrial Training School.

u-tr-19021222.s: This order restores part of the White Mountain or San Carlos Indian Reservation in the Territory of Arizona to the public domain. It affects the land inside the described boundaries along the Gila River.

u-tr-19020904.s: This order sets aside certain public land in the Territory of New Mexico as a reservation for the use and occupation of the Indians of the Nambe Pueblo. Any land inside those sections with valid existing rights is excluded. If those valid claims later end, those lands will be added to the reservation.

u-tr-19020809.s: This order sets aside two parts of public land in Nebraska for use by the Department of Agriculture. The land is reserved for purposes connected with experimental tree planting.

u-tr-19020801.s: This order directs extra pay of $2.00 per month for certain enlisted naval personnel. It applies to men rated Seaman Gunner before April 1, 1902, or who hold a graduation certificate from the Petty Officers' Schools, Seaman Gunner Class, during current and later enlistments.

u-tr-19020725.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Treasury to retire officers of the Revenue Cutter Service from active service when they reach age 64. It affects officers of that service.

u-tr-19020722.s: This order reserves Miraflores Island in the Harbor of San Juan, Puerto Rico for public use. It may be used as a quarantine station, a site for a marine hospital, or both. The island is placed under the control of the Public Health and Marine Hospital Service of the United States.

u-tr-19020719.s: This order changes passport rules so U.S. diplomatic and consular officers may issue passports to residents of the Insular Possessions of the United States who make a satisfactory application. Applicants must say they owe allegiance to the United States and do not owe allegiance to any other government, and they must provide affidavits from two credible witnesses about their birth, residence, and loyalty. The same fee applies as for passports issued to citizens of the United States.

u-tr-19020710.s: This order says an enlisted person in the Navy cannot be discharged before the end of his enlistment term except for undesirability, inaptitude, physical or mental disability, or unfitness. A discharge must be recommended by the commanding officer of the vessel where the man is serving. Requests that do not come through the commanding officer must be ignored.

u-tr-19020703.s: This order says appointments of all unclassified laborers in the Executive Departments and independent offices must follow regulations approved and issued by the heads of those departments and offices and the Civil Service Commission. Those regulations take effect when they are announced.

u-tr-19020613.s: This order reserves a specific piece of land in Washington for the Navy Department. It sets the land apart to be used as a target range.

u-tr-19020613-2.s: This order changes the boundaries of the Wakeeney and Colby land districts in Kansas. It transfers part of Kansas, including township 10 and ranges 26 to 42, from the Wakeeney land district to the Colby land district.

u-tr-19020512-2.s: This order excuses certain employees of the Executive Departments, the Government Printing Office, and the Navy Yard and Station at Washington, D.C., from duty at noon on Wednesday for the rest of that day. It applies to those who served in the military or naval service of the United States in the Spanish-American War or the insurrection in the Philippine Islands, so they can take part in the statue dedication ceremonies at Arlington.

u-tr-19020512.s: This order excuses certain employees of the Executive Departments, the Government Printing Office, and the Navy Yard and Station at Washington, D.C., from duty on Saturday, the 17th instant. It applies to those who served in the military or Navy of the United States in the late Civil War, so they can attend the reburial ceremonies of Major-General W. S. Rosecrans.

u-tr-19020430.s: This order reserves the north-west quarter of the north-west quarter and lot 4 of section 32, township one south, range 18 west, San Bernardino base and meridian, California, for light-house purposes. It says this reservation is subject to any legal existing rights.

u-tr-19020429-2.s: The order reserves the building known as the "Residence" and a described tract of land within the Fort Yuma Abandoned Military Reservation in Arizona. It sets that property apart for the Customs Service.

u-tr-19020429.s: This order directs that the National flag be flown at half-mast on the White House and other federal buildings in Washington, D.C. on April 30, 1902. It applies as a mark of respect for J. Sterling Morton, formerly Secretary of Agriculture, on the day of his funeral.

u-tr-19020327.s: The President directs that the National flag be flown at half-mast on the White House and other federal buildings in Washington, D.C. This is a mark of respect for Lord Pauncefote on the day of his funeral.

u-tr-19020326.s: This order reserves the building known as the "office" and a 200-foot-square tract of land in the Fort Yuma Abandoned Military Reservation, Arizona, for the use of the Weather Bureau. It affects that building and the surrounding land area set apart for that use.

u-tr-19020324.s: This order changes the Consular Regulations of 1896. It says a consular officer may not accept an appointment from a foreign state as an administrator, guardian, or other fiduciary unless the Secretary of State has first authorized it.

u-tr-19020215.s: This order moves the office of Surveyor-General in the surveying district of the Territory of Arizona to Phoenix, Arizona. It also says the office at Tucson, Arizona, is discontinued and that its records and business are transferred to the office of Surveyor-General at Tucson, Arizona.

u-tr-19020205.s: This order sets up arrangements for the reception and entertainment of Prince Henry of Prussia during his visit to the United States. It names delegates from the Department of State, War Department, and Navy Department to handle the arrangements. They are authorized to make engagements, incur expenses, and draw money from the Secretary of State to cover those costs.

u-tr-19020131.s: This order forbids all officers and employees serving in or under the Executive Departments from directly or indirectly seeking a pay increase for themselves. It also bars them from trying to influence legislation in their own interest before Congress or its committees, except through the heads of their departments, and says violations can lead to dismissal from government service.

u-tr-19011219.s: This order places any public lands on Culebra Island within the listed borders under the Navy Department. It affects those public lands on the island.

u-tr-19020117.s: This order directs departments to consider laws that give preference to veterans in hiring and keeping jobs. It says preference should be given to honorably discharged Civil War veterans when the needs of the service and the law allow it, if they are fit and well qualified for the work.

u-tr-19011209.s: This order sets the classification and monthly pay for Mess Attendants in the United States Navy starting January 1, 1902. It lists pay for Mess Attendants in the 1st, 2d, and 3d class at $24, $20, and $16 each month.

u-tr-19011203.s: From and after January 1, 1902, enlisted men of the Navy who hold a certificate as a credit from the Petty Officers' School of Instruction at the Navy Training Station in Newport, Rhode Island will receive two dollars per month in addition to the pay of their rating. It applies to Navy enlisted men with that certificate.

u-tr-19011115.s: This order reserves San Nicolas Island, California, for lighthouse purposes. It affects the use of that island by setting it aside for that specific purpose.

u-tr-19011126.s: This order allows all enlisted men of the Navy to receive seventy-five cents per month in addition to their rating pay for each good conduct medal, pin, or bar issued for service. This extra pay applies from January 1, 1901 through December 31, 1901.

u-tr-19011111.s: This order reserves the south-west quarter of section twenty-nine and the south-east quarter of section thirty in California for lighthouse purposes. The reservation is subject to any legal existing rights.

u-tr-19011114.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in Arizona from sale and settlement. It stays withdrawn until the Indians living there have been settled permanently under the homestead laws or the general allotment act and related law.

u-tr-19011109.s: This order reserves certain U.S. lands in the provinces of Zambales and Bataan in the Philippine Islands for naval purposes. It places those reserved lands under the governance and control of the Navy Department. The reservation includes the listed lands within the stated boundaries, along with adjacent islands, bays, harbors, estuaries, and streams inside those limits.

u-tr-19011030.s: This order reserves Harbor Island and three nearby islets in Sitka Harbor, Alaska, for the use of the Revenue Cutter Service. It says this is subject to any legal existing rights.

u-tr-19011015.s: This order sets monthly pay rates for petty officers and other enlisted men in the Commissary Branch of the United States Navy starting on January 1, 1902. It gives different pay amounts for Chief Commissary Steward, Commissary Steward, Ship's Cook, and Baker ratings. It also gives landsmen detailed as crew messmen an extra $5 per month, except when they serve as reliefs during a temporary absence of the regular crew messmen.

u-tr-19011001.s: This order gives Thaddeus S. Sharretts authority to meet and confer with people authorized by the government of China or by other governments with treaties with China. He is to agree on a plan to convert ad valorem duties on imports into China into specific duties, as far as possible and as soon as may be. The plan must follow the final protocol signed in Peking on September 7, 1901, and be submitted to the President for approval.

u-mckinley-19010829.s: This order directs Brigadier-General G. S. Gillespie to do the duties of Secretary of War while the Secretary of War and the Assistant Secretary of War are temporarily away from the seat of Government. It affects the War Department during that absence.

u-mckinley-19010827.s: This order cancels part of a previous land reservation in the District of Alaska for the Scotch Cap tract. It sets aside a new Scotch Cap tract on Unimak Island for light house purposes, subject to any legal existing rights.

u-tr-19010923.s: This order restores sections 23 and 24 of township seven south, range 93 west, 6th principal meridian, Colorado, from the Black Mesa Forest Reserve to the public domain. It says this will happen after notice is published as required by law. The order says the land was found to be better adapted to agricultural than forest purposes.

u-mckinley-19010819.s: This order changes the rates used for accepting the Spanish Alphonsino and the French Louis in payment of customs, taxes, public dues, and postal dues in Cuba. It applies to payments made in those coins in the Island of Cuba.

u-mckinley-19010820.s: This order reserves certain United States land on the Puntailla Point peninsula in San Juan, Puerto Rico, for naval purposes. It applies to the land known as Barrio de la Puntilla, or Puntilla Point, as described in the order.

u-mckinley-19010724.s: This order sets apart funds in the Treasury that came from duties and taxes collected under the Puerto Rico revenue act. It directs that the money be used for public purposes in Puerto Rico, including public and permanent improvements and other governmental and public purposes. The funds are to be spent under the sole supervision and approval of the Governor and administrative heads of the island.

u-mckinley-19010625.s: This order changes a previous executive order by replacing the word "Filipinos" with "natives of the Islands of the Philippines and of the Island of Guam." It affects the wording used in that earlier order.

u-mckinley-19010629.s: This order restores two townships in Oregon within the Cascade Range Forest Reservation to the public domain. It says this will happen after notice by publication as required by law. The order says the tracts were found better adapted to agriculture than forest purposes.

u-mckinley-19010621.s: This order changes an earlier executive order from May 3, 1899. It authorizes the appointment of civilians as Collectors of Customs in the Philippine Archipelago.

u-mckinley-19010625-2.s: This order restores certain tracts within the Big Horn Forest Reservation in Wyoming to the public domain. It says these lands were found better suited to agriculture than to forest purposes, and the change takes effect after sixty days' notice by publication as required by law.

u-mckinley-19010621-2.s: This order gives the President of the Philippine Commission authority over civil affairs in the Philippine Islands instead of the military governor. It appoints the president of that commission as Civil Governor of the Philippine Islands. The military governor is relieved of civil duties, except in districts where insurrection continues or public order has not been restored enough for civil government to be set up.

u-mckinley-19010621-3.s: This order changes and re-establishes the boundary line between the Coeur d'Alene and Lewiston Land Districts in Idaho. It affects the land district boundary from the Idaho-Washington line to the crest of the Bitter Root Mountains.

u-mckinley-19010607.s: This order sets a new system for classifying Navy vessels and assigning crews afloat. It rates most vessels by tonnage and divides them into first, second, third, and fourth rates. Torpedo boats, tugs, sailing ships, and receiving ships are not rated, and some special-purpose vessels are treated differently.

u-mckinley-19010610.s: The order says money previously set aside for Puerto Rico is to be used for public and permanent improvements and other governmental and public purposes there. It also says the spending is to be done under the supervision and approval of the Government and administrative authorities of the island.

u-mckinley-19010429.s: If the Secretary of the Navy dies, resigns, is absent, or is sick, the Assistant Secretary of the Navy and Rear Admiral Charles O'Neil are directed to perform the Secretary's duties. They would do so until a successor is appointed or until the absence or sickness ends.

u-mckinley-19010607-2.s: This order lists which Navy ranks are to command or man different kinds of fleets, divisions, ships, and small vessels. It applies to officers from Admiral down to Ensign and sets what each rank may be assigned to command.

u-mckinley-19010415.s: This order restores certain tracts of land in township fifty-eight north, range eighty-nine west, within the Big Horn Forest reserve in Wyoming to the public domain. The land is described as portions of sections thirteen through seventeen and all of sections twenty through twenty-seven. The order says these tracts were found better suited to agricultural use than forest use, after sixty days' notice by publication.

u-mckinley-19010423.s: This order sets aside five hundred thousand dollars from an appropriation made for the benefit and government of Puerto Rico. The money is to be spent on public and permanent improvements in Puerto Rico, under the supervision and approval of the Governor and Executive Council of the island.

u-mckinley-19010405.s: This order establishes the Insular Force United States Navy. It authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to enlist up to 500 Filipinos in set Navy ratings with listed monthly pay amounts.

u-mckinley-19010402.s: This order reserves most of Amaknam Island in the District of Alaska for public purposes. It does not include the tract reserved for light-house purposes or the tract in amended survey M 58 of the North American Commercial Co.

u-mckinley-19010406.s: On Tuesday the ninth instant, certain employees of the Executive Departments, the Government Printing Office, and the Navy Yard and Station at Washington who served in the Military or Naval services of the United States in the late Civil War or Spanish-American War were excused from duty at one o'clock P.M. for the rest of that day. This let them take part in the exercises for the unveiling of the statue to the memory of the late General John A. Logan.

u-mckinley-19010330.s: This order reserves and sets apart two tracts of land in the District of Alaska for Reindeer stations. One tract is the entire peninsula with Cape Denbigh at its southwest end. The other tract is a piece of land near the Unalaklik River, subject to any existing legal rights to the land.

u-mckinley-19010326.s: This order reserves the unsurveyed portion of Eliza Island and Billingham Bay in Washington for light-house purposes. It affects that specific area in section five, township thirty-six north, range two East Willamette meridian.

u-mckinley-19010325.s: This order requires consular officers to collect fees for bills of health and supplemental bills of health issued to foreign war vessels. It also changes the tariff of consular fees to match that rule.

u-mckinley-19010314.s: This order sets apart two hundred thousand dollars from an appropriation for the benefit and government of Puerto Rico. The money is to be spent improving and grading roads across Puerto Rico, including “Neighboring Roads” between small municipalities.

u-mckinley-19010322.s: The order sets aside six thousand dollars from the appropriation for the benefit and government of Puerto Rico. It is to be spent by the Treasurer of Puerto Rico, on accounts certified by the Auditor of the Island, to refund customs duties paid by certain contractors for materials brought into Puerto Rico since May 1, 1900.

u-mckinley-19010312.s: This order changes an earlier order about Cuba. During U.S. military government there, it creates the offices of Auditor for Cuba, Deputy Auditor for Cuba, and Chief Clerk in the Auditor’s office. It gives the Auditor and Deputy Auditor duties for receiving, auditing, signing, and handling official papers, and says the Secretary of War will issue and enforce the needed rules.

u-mckinley-19010309.s: This order moves North Dakota and South Dakota out of the Internal Revenue District of Nebraska. It creates one new district for those two states, to be known as the Internal Revenue District of Newark, South Dakota. The Internal Revenue District of Nebraska would then cover only Nebraska.

u-mckinley-19010311.s: This order approves the recommendation that was made. It also directs the Secretary of the Interior to note the action in the records of the General Land Office.

u-mckinley-19010308.s: This order abolishes the export rates of duty on tobacco listed in the Customs Tariff for Ports in the Island of Cuba. It affects tobacco exports in Cuba and takes effect on April 1, 1901.

u-mckinley-19010309-2.s: The order recommends changing the wood reservation for Fort Fill in Oklahoma Territory. It would move the eastern boundary to match the new 98 meridian, which is the boundary line between the Kiowa and Comanche Reservation and the Chickasaw Nation.

u-mckinley-19010202.s: This order changes a part of a 1899 executive order about the office of Treasurer of the Island of Cuba. It says the office will be under the Department of Finance of Cuba, and it will be filled by a citizen of Cuba appointed by the Military Governor with the approval of the Secretary of War.

u-mckinley-19001219.s: This order revokes part of an earlier order that transferred the Fort Yuma Military Reservation to the Department of the Interior, but only for the land south of the Colorado River. That land, in the Territory of Arizona, is placed under the control of the Secretary of the Interior for disposition under two Acts of Congress. The order says the land had been abandoned for military purposes.

u-mckinley-19001214.s: This order gives the Naval officer in command at Guam the power to act as Collector of Customs for the island. It also lets that officer appoint a deputy if needed. Any customs authority already used under the commandant at the naval station is approved and ratified, and if the commandant appoints someone from civil life, that person must give good and sufficient security for the job.

u-mckinley-19001213.s: This order sets apart $200,000 from a Puerto Rico appropriation to be used for public education in Puerto Rico. It also allows the money to be used to build and equip schoolhouses on the island.

u-mckinley-19001207.s: This order says that when different parts of the Army are serving together and a Marine Corps or militia officer is in command, that officer must report the commander's actions and the force's operations through military channels. The report must go to the Secretary of War and to the officer’s own superiors in the Marine Corps or militia.

u-mckinley-19001130.s: The United States Civil Service Commission is directed to help the Civil Service Board in the Philippine Islands as much as practicable. It may also conduct civil service examinations for the Philippine Islands when the Board requests it, under rules the two bodies agree on.

u-mckinley-19001029.s: This order reserves a specific parcel of land in Florida for light-house purposes. It affects lot 5 in section 31, township 6 south, range 11 west.

u-mckinley-19001013.s: This order transfers the county of Greet from the Internal Revenue District of Texas to the Internal Revenue District of Kansas. It says the county had been declared part of the Territory of Oklahoma by the United States Supreme Court.

u-mckinley-19001010.s: This order assigns a commissioned officer of the Marine Hospital Service to serve on the staff of the Military Governor of the Philippine Islands as chief of the quarantine service. That officer must submit estimates of quarantine expenses, and after approval the needed funds are to be paid through a Treasury Department disbursing officer. The disbursing officer is to be appointed by the Secretary of the Treasury and must account for those payments under the stated rules.

u-mckinley-19000920.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Treasury to take charge of spending under the law for preventing and stopping the spread of cholera, yellow fever, smallpox, bubonic plague, and Chinese plague or black death. It also directs the Secretary to use the Marine Hospital Service and other needed means to carry out the law and any quarantine laws in force. The Secretary must supervise these expenditures and send reports on the work done.

u-mckinley-19001010-2.s: This order reserves Sections 26, 27, 34, and 35 in township 14 south, range 14 east, in the Territory of Arizona for the United States Department of Agriculture. The land is set apart for an agricultural experiment station.

u-mckinley-19000903.s: The order reserves certain lands in Mississippi for light-house purposes. The lands include parts of Round Island, Horn Island, and Petite Bois Blanc Island. It covers the described fractional sections east of Pearl River.

u-mckinley-19000823.s: This order restores certain land in California to the public domain. The land had been withdrawn for the Mission Indians by an earlier executive order.

u-mckinley-19000919.s: This order lets Lieutenant-General Nelson A. Miles do the duties of Secretary of War if the Secretary of War is ill or away and the Assistant Secretary of War is also away. It also lets Major-General Henry C. Corbin do those duties if the Secretary of War, the Assistant Secretary of War, and the lieutenant-general commanding the Army are all away. It affects the War Department leadership when those officials are absent.

u-mckinley-19000802.s: This order assigns the Island of Guimaras to naval jurisdiction and control. It says this is for establishing a naval base and station on the strait of Iloilo, opposite the town of Iloilo.

u-mckinley-19000629.s: This order places a commissioned officer of the Marine Hospital Service on the staff of the Military Governor of Cuba as chief of the quarantine service. The officer must submit detailed estimates of quarantine expenses each month or at other times the Military Governor directs. After approval, the chief quarantine officer must request the needed funds, and the disbursing officer or agent must pay quarantine bills and keep accounts under the stated rules.

u-mckinley-19000802-2.s: This order allots up to $10,000 from the Emergency Fund, Navy Department, 1901, to pay for a survey of the Island of Guimaras. The survey is to locate the coal wharf and shed, the dry dock, and the fleet anchorages, and to appraise private land that may need to be condemned for government use and land defense.

u-mckinley-19000627.s: This order sets the classification and monthly pay for the rating of electrician starting July 1, 1900. It also says no enlisted man may have his pay reduced during his current enlistment below the pay he was enlisted at or is now receiving.

u-mckinley-19000622.s: This order approves the franchise granted by the Hawaiian government to the Hilo Railroad Company. The company was organized to build and operate railroads between and through several districts on the Island of Hawaii.

u-mckinley-19000612.s: This order reserves a specific parcel of land in Florida for light-house purposes. It affects fractional section 11, township 5 south, range 14 west.

u-mckinley-19000526.s: This order reserves and sets apart certain land in Township 13, south, Range one east, Montana. The land is for the use of the United States Fish Commission of Fish and Fisheries as a fish cultural station.

u-mckinley-19000514.s: This order sets apart a parcel of land in Arizona for Indian school purposes for the Hualapai Indians. It adds that land to the Hualapai Indian School Reserve created by an earlier executive order, and it is subject to the exceptions, reservations, and conditions in the deed.

u-mckinley-19000526-2.s: This order allows needed advances of money from funds set aside for the light-house establishment. The money is for Army and Navy officers serving as engineers or inspectors, and as assistants to engineers or inspectors in the third light-house district, to help carry on the Puerto Rican light-house service.

u-mckinley-19000514-2.s: This order sets apart a parcel of land in Arizona for Indian school purposes. It adds that land to the Hualapai Indian School Reserve for the Hualapai Indians, subject to the exceptions, reservations, and conditions in the deed.

u-mckinley-19000501.s: This order directs the Collector of Customs of Puerto Rico to pay the net proceeds of certain collections to the Treasurer of Puerto Rico. The payments must follow regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

u-mckinley-19000321.s: The Secretary of the Navy is directed to transfer the vessels Badger and Resolute to the Secretary of War for use in the War Department’s transport service. The order says these vessels are no longer needed in the Navy’s service.

u-mckinley-19000320.s: This order cancels part of a prior Executive Order from September 1854. It removes the reservation for lighthouse purposes on the tract at Cape Shoalwater in the Territory of Washington.

u-mckinley-19000319.s: The order withdraws a tract of land in Montana from sale and settlement and sets it apart as a reservation for the permanent use and occupation of the Indians now occupying or belonging upon the Northern Cheyenne Reservation. It says the reservation will be known as the Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation. It also excepts certain listed tracts from the reservation boundaries.

u-mckinley-19000319-2.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in Montana from sale and settlement and sets it apart as a reservation. It is for the permanent use and occupation of the Indians now occupying or belonging upon the Northern Cheyenne Reservation, and it will be known as the Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation. The order also says certain tracts of land owned by named people and a mission are not included in the reservation boundaries.

u-mckinley-19000307.s: This order cancels the 1866 reservation of a 20-acre tract in the Territory of Washington for light-house purposes, but only for that described tract. It then reserves a different 3.25-acre parcel in Washington for light-house purposes instead.

u-mckinley-19000119.s: This order changes the rules for the Army and Navy General Hospital at Hot Springs, Arkansas. It says enlisted men on the retired list and honorably discharged soldiers and sailors of the Regular and Volunteer Army and Navy must pay 40 cents per day for subsistence. It affects retired service members and honorably discharged veterans who use the hospital.

u-mckinley-19000212.s: This order allows $400,776.65 to be moved from the War Department’s “Emergency Fund” to the “Substance of the Army 1900” appropriation. It applies to the funds under the War Department and follows a request approved by the Secretary of War.

u-mckinley-19000108-2.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in the Territory of Arizona from sale and settlement. The land is described as lying west of the Navajo and Moqui reservations and is kept withdrawn until further ordered.

u-mckinley-19000108.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in the Territory of Arizona, west of the Navajo and Moqui Reservations, from sale and settlement. The land stays withdrawn until further order.

u-mckinley-19000105.s: This order sets apart about seven acres from a government reservation in Oahu, Hawaiian Islands. The land is for the use of the United States Treasury Department as a site for a United States Marine Hospital for the port of Honolulu.

u-mckinley-19000103.s: This order applies quarantine rules in the Philippine Islands to help prevent the spread of epidemic diseases. It gives the Marine Hospital Service control over examining incoming and outgoing vessels, cargo, crew, officers, and personal effects, and requires quarantine certificates and bills of health for vessels. It also sets up quarantine officers at ports, gives the Chief Quarantine Officer authority over appointments and spending, and charges the costs to the islands’ revenues.

u-mckinley-18991110.s: This order changes the rules for the Army and Navy General Hospital at Hot Springs, Arkansas. It lets enlisted men on the active list who are under treatment or on duty at the hospital have their usual rations paid in money instead. The payment is to be made to the Senior Medical Officer based on monthly accounts certified by the Surgeon-General of the Army.

u-mckinley-18991201.s: This order gives John Hay authority to meet with authorized representatives of the German and British governments. He is directed to negotiate, conclude, and sign a convention to settle questions about the Samoan group of islands. The agreement is to be sent to the President of the United States for ratification.

u-mckinley-18990929.s: The order closes the several Executive Departments, the Government Printing Office, and the Navy Yard and Station at Washington on Tuesday, October 3rd. This is so employees can take part in the ceremonies for the reception of Admiral Dewey and the presentation of the Sword of Honor to him.

u-mckinley-18991104.s: This order allows certain mailed packages and parcels to be sent between U.S. service members and other public employees in Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Guam, the Philippine Islands, and Cuba, and their families in the United States. The packages must be mailable, marked as gifts or souvenirs, and have no commercial purpose or be for sale. It also assigns the Secretary of War and the Postmaster-General to handle the details and safeguards for carrying out the order.

u-mckinley-18990918.s: This order ends the practice of issuing Hawaiian vessel registers that gave vessels the rights and privileges of Hawaiian vessels in the ports of nations or on the high seas. It affects vessels registered by Hawaii under that system.

u-mckinley-18990911.s: The order directs the Secretary of State to tell the President of Hawaii that the government of Hawaii has no power to sell or dispose of the public lands in the islands. It says any sale proceedings now pending should stop. It also says any sales or sale agreements made since the Resolution of Annexation are null and void, and any money paid should be refunded.

u-mckinley-18990902.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Treasury to transfer an additional $5,000 from money already set aside for the Hawaiian Islands annexation resolution. The money is to be used, at the Executive’s discretion, to carry out that resolution and to enforce the Chinese Exclusion Laws in the Hawaiian Islands under its restriction on Chinese emigration.

u-mckinley-18990817.s: The order says the United States will give assistance and supervision as Cuba moves toward an effective system of self-government. It directs that a census of the people of Cuba be taken and says competent Cuban citizens will serve as enumerators and supervisors. It also asks people in Cuba to help those officers do their work.

u-mckinley-18990724.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Treasury to oversee spending to help prevent and suppress the spread of cholera, yellow fever, smallpox, bubonic plague, and Chinese plague or black death. It also directs the use of the Marine Hospital Service and other needed means, including in carrying out quarantine laws in force. The Secretary must supervise expenditures and send reports on the work done.

u-mckinley-18990703-2.s: This order lets customs officers in the Philippine Islands issue a certificate of protection for certain vessels, giving them the protection and flag of the United States on the high seas and in all ports. It applies to vessels owned by a U.S. citizen living in the Philippine Islands, a native inhabitant who takes an oath of allegiance, or certain residents who renounce allegiance to Spain and take the oath. The order also says the master and watch officer must be U.S. citizens or take the oath, unless the U.S. general in the Philippines waives that rule in special cases.

u-mckinley-18990703.s: This order lets customs officers in Puerto Rico issue a certificate of protection for certain vessels, giving them the protection and flag of the United States on the high seas and in all ports. The vessel must be owned by a citizen of the United States living in Puerto Rico, a native inhabitant who takes the oath of allegiance, or a former Spanish subject in Puerto Rico who gives up allegiance to Spain and takes the oath. The master and watch officers must be citizens of the United States or take the oath, unless the commanding general in Puerto Rico waives that requirement in special cases. The Secretary of War is to set the form and process for issuing these certificates.

u-mckinley-18990627.s: This order creates two new offices during the U.S. military government in Cuba and certain West Indies islands evacuated by Spain. It creates an Assistant Auditor to audit the accounts of the departments of Internal Revenue and an Assistant Treasurer in the office of the islands' Treasurer. The Secretary of War is to appoint both officials.

u-mckinley-18990610.s: Consular court fees and fines are declared to be official money. They are to be used to pay the expenses of consular courts, and yearly accounts of the money received and spent must be sent to the Secretary of State. Any money left over after court expenses are paid must be turned into the Treasury.

u-mckinley-18990616.s: Customs officers in Cuba may allow certain vessels owned by residents and citizens of Cuba to clear for foreign ports or ports of the United States under a permit. Those vessels may fly the American flag above their distinctive signal, but this does not give them the same rights and privileges as vessels of the United States. The Secretary of War will set the form and manner of the permits, and Tariff Circular No. 71 is rescinded.

u-mckinley-18990523.s: The order excuses employees of the executive departments and the Government Printing Office from duty at noon on Wednesday, the 24th instant. This is so they can take part in the Civic parade and other exercises of the Peace Jubilee that day.

119.s: This order amends the civil-service rules on hiring, removal, and exceptions. It says a person in the competitive classified service cannot be removed except for just cause, with written reasons, notice, and a chance to answer in writing. It also lists many jobs and employees who are excepted from examination or registration requirements, including certain secretaries, attorneys, and workers in several departments. In some cases, appointments may be made after fitness tests or after the President approves a nomination that waives examination in whole or in part.

u-mckinley-18990513.s: This order directs that the general election set by the Hawaiian constitution for the last Wednesday in September shall not be held. It also says elective officers whose terms end before Congress passes appropriate legislation will stay in office at the pleasure of the President of the United States.

u-mckinley-18990510.s: This order withdraws Baker Lake and the land within half a mile of its shore from the Washington Forest Reserve. It sets that land apart for the United States Commission of Fish and Fisheries to use as a fish cultural station. If that use is abandoned, the land would again be part of the forest reserve.

u-mckinley-18990506.s: The order creates an Auditor of the Islands, two assistant auditors, and a Treasurer of the Islands for Puerto Rico and other islands in the West Indies east of the 74th degree west longitude that were evacuated by Spain. The auditors are to examine the islands’ accounts, including customs and post office accounts. The treasurer is to receive and keep the islands’ revenue money and pay it out only on warrants from the Auditor of the Islands and the Governor-General.

u-mckinley-18990506-2.s: This order creates offices for an Auditor of the Islands, two assistant auditors, and a Treasurer of the Islands during military government in Cuba and other islands in the West Indies west of the 74th degree west longitude that were evacuated by Spain. The auditors are to audit all accounts of the islands, and the Treasurer is to receive, keep, and pay out island revenues only with the proper warrants and countersignature. The Secretary of War is to issue the rules and instructions needed to carry out executive orders for those islands.

u-mckinley-18990406.s: This order restores two land tracts in Oregon to the Public Domain after notice is published as required by law. The tracts are within the Cascade Range Forest Reservation and were found better suited for agricultural use than forest use.

u-mckinley-18990401.s: This order establishes the headquarters of the new Neech Lake Indian Agency in Minnesota. It sets the headquarters on reserved land in parts of township 142, range 31 west, 5th Meridian, as described in the recommendation approved by the Secretary of the Interior.

u-mckinley-18990403.s: This order directs military and naval honors and burial ceremonies for the dead soldiers and sailors brought to Arlington National Cemetery. It also orders the national flag to be flown at half-staff on public buildings, forts, camps, and public vessels, and says government departments in Washington shall be closed at noon that day.

u-mckinley-18990401-3.s: This order moves the Office of the Humboldt Land District in California from Humboldt to Eureka. It affects the land office for that district.

u-mckinley-18990401-2.s: This order sets apart the Fort Stanton abandoned military reservation in New Mexico, with the buildings on it, for the use of the Marine Hospital Service. It does not apply to any land that already had valid claims under the Homestead or Mineral Land Laws before the order date.

u-mckinley-18990203.s: This order moves several Michigan counties from the First Internal Revenue Collection District to the Fourth Internal Revenue Collection District. It affects the counties of Alger, Baraga, Chippewa, Delta, Dickinson, Gogebic, Houghton, Iron, Keweenaw, Luce, Mackinac, Marquette, Menominee, Ontonagon, and Schoolcraft.

u-mckinley-18990131.s: This order sets apart a tract of land near the north bank of Cook Inlet, next to the town of Kenai in Alaska, as an agricultural experiment station. The land is subject to any existing legal rights. The tract is described as about 320 acres, more or less.

u-mckinley-18990120.s: The order appoints a commission to help extend U.S. authority throughout the Philippine Islands and to support military government there. The commissioners are to go to Manila, announce their mission, and study local government, justice, taxes, transportation, and public improvements. They are also to report what changes may help maintain order, peace, public welfare, and the safety of persons and property.

u-mckinley-18990101.s: The President directs General Otis to avoid a conflict if possible. Miller is to contact the insurgents, give them the President’s proclamation, and tell them the Government will assert its sovereignty while aiming to give them good government and protect their personal rights.

u-mckinley-18981222.s: This order says local government authorities in Cuba may not make certain public or corporate grants or concessions unless the major-general commanding the U.S. military forces in Cuba approves them. The approval must be specially authorized by the Secretary of War. Similar orders were also issued for Puerto Rico and the Philippines.

u-mckinley-18981222-2.s: The Secretary of War directs the U.S. Army commander in Cuba and the senior naval officer in Havana to follow the arrangements and ceremonies for the evacuation of Havana on January 1, 1899. They are also told to help carry out those arrangements.

u-mckinley-18981221.s: This order says the United States will take control of the Philippine Islands and extend military government from Manila to the whole territory. It says the U.S. military commander must tell the people that the United States will protect their persons, property, private rights, and religious rights. It also says private property should be respected, taxes and duties will go to the U.S. authorities, and ports will be open to trade with friendly nations.

u-mckinley-18981221-2.s: The President directs General Otis to send necessary troops to Iloilo to preserve the peace and protect life and property. It says there should be no conflict with the insurgents. It also tells him to be conciliatory, but firm.

u-mckinley-18981209.s: This order sets Cuba and certain nearby islands under a customs district while they are occupied by U.S. military authorities. Havana is made the chief port of entry, and several named ports are made subports of entry. Army officers are assigned to collect customs at these ports, with civilian help appointed by the Secretary of War, and customs questions are decided by the chief collector unless sent to the Secretary of War.

u-mckinley-18981204.s: The President directs Admiral Dewey and General Otis to meet early and advise him on what force and equipment will be needed in the Philippine Islands. He also asks them for suggestions on how the islands should be governed by the Army and Navy for some time to come. If the islands are ceded to the United States, he wants peace and order restored and a kind government that encourages industry and protects life and property.

u-mckinley-18980821.s: This order gives thanks and congratulations to Major-General Merritt and the officers and men of his command. It refers to their gallant conduct in the campaign.

u-mckinley-18980821-2.s: The message thanks Admiral Dewey and the officers, sailors, and marines under his command for their gallant conduct. It also gives them the thanks and congratulations of the nation.

u-mckinley-18980817.s: The order directs that there must be no joint occupation with the insurgents. It says the United States, in control of Manila City, Manila Bay, and Harbor, must preserve the peace and protect persons and property in the territory occupied by its military and naval forces. It also says the insurgents and others must recognize U.S. military occupation and the end of hostilities, and that all law-abiding people must be treated alike.

u-mckinley-18980806.s: This order directs that the graves of soldiers at Santiago be permanently marked. It assigns the Secretary of War to carry out the order.

u-mckinley-18980806-2.s: This order changes the rules for consular agents. It requires them to follow the stated requirements for official services and to send quarterly reports in the prescribed forms to the principal consular officer. It also says money due for services to American vessels and seamen will be sent by Treasury warrant to the officer who is owed it, and it makes Forms 190 and 191 official parts of the Consular Regulations.

u-mckinley-18980727.s: This order reserves a tract of land on the Yukon River in the District of Alaska for the uses and purposes of a townsite. The land is to be held under the townsite law or laws that apply to public lands in Alaska. While this reservation is in force, the land cannot be disposed of in any other way.

u-mckinley-18980721.s: This order lets postal communication between the United States and Santiago de Cuba start again under military rules. It also allows postal service in other enemy territory taken by U.S. land and naval forces, under the same conditions. The domestic postal service in occupied territory may continue and be extended as local needs allow, with military supervision. Revenue from the service is to pay its expenses, and United States postage stamps are to be used.

u-mckinley-18980716.s: The President sends thanks to General Shafter and the United States forces at Santiago for their achievements there. He says their actions led to the surrender of the city and all Spanish troops and territory under General Toral. He also sends sympathy to the sick and wounded.

u-mckinley-18980713.s: This order gives instructions for the U.S. military occupation of parts of Cuba after Spanish forces surrendered there. It says the commander should protect the people in their homes, work, and religious rights, and keep local laws and courts in place when possible. It also covers public and private property, taxes, roads and transport, and says ports in U.S.-held areas should be open to trade with neutral nations and the United States for non-contraband goods.

u-mckinley-18980708.s: The President directs that General Shafter and his army be given the nation’s gratitude and thanks for their work in the fight of July 1. It says the officers and men showed valor and heroism, and that the American people take pride in them. It also says the country mourns the men who died in battle and adds them to the roll of heroes.

u-mckinley-18980704.s: This executive order sends gratitude and congratulations to Admiral Sampson. It also thanks his officers and crews for their valor and says they have added new honors to the American navy.

u-mckinley-18980519.s: The order directs an army of occupation to the Philippines and gives instructions for how it should act there. It says the United States should protect the people in their homes, jobs, and personal and religious rights, while keeping order during military occupation. It also says local laws, courts, police, taxes, property rules, and trade should continue in limited form unless changed by the military commander.

u-mckinley-18980519-2.s: This order sends an army of occupation to the Philippines to finish reducing Spanish power there and to keep order and security while the islands are in United States possession. It opens ports in places held by U.S. forces to trade with neutral nations and the United States in goods that are not contraband of war, with duties paid as required. It also directs that duties and taxes during military occupation be collected by military or naval commanders, and it asks for a review of the Spanish laws on duties and taxes.

u-mckinley-18980519-3.s: This order directs that an army of occupation be sent to the Philippines. It says the force is to complete the reduction of Spanish power there and to give the islands order and security while they are in the possession of the United States. It also instructs Navy and War officials to avoid conflict over authority, and says duties and taxes in occupied ports will be handled by military or naval commanders under those departments.

u-mckinley-18980507.s: The President thanks Dewey and his officers and men for their achievement and victory. He says Dewey has been appointed acting rear-admiral. He also says he will recommend a vote of thanks to Dewey by Congress as a basis for further promotion.

u-mckinley-18980328.s: The order temporarily reserves a tract of land on Kadiak Island, Alaska, as an experiment station for the Department of Agriculture. It says the reservation must not interfere with any prior rights of natives or others to land inside it.

u-cleveland2-18970127.s: This order changes the civil-service rules to add one new job to the list of positions excepted from examination in the departmental service. The new exception is the Assistant Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution, who is in charge of the United States National Museum.

u-cleveland2-18970112.s: This order directs the Attorney General to take court action to protect the rights and interests of the United States in the debt owed by the Union Pacific Railroad and the Kansas Pacific Railroad. It also directs steps to foreclose the mortgages or liens of the United States on those companies’ property. For the other aided Pacific railroads, the government says the situation needs further consideration.

u-cleveland2-18970112-2.s: This order divides officers and employees in the Office of the President who are covered by civil service rules into salary classes. It says that people appointed by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, and mere laborers or workmen, are not included, with one exception for some laborers or workmen assigned to the same kind of work as classified employees. It also says no one may be admitted to a covered place until they pass the required civil service examination and their eligibility is certified by the United States Civil Service Commission.

u-cleveland2-18970102-2.s: This order changes the age limits for many classified civil service jobs. It sets different minimum and maximum ages for positions in the departmental, custom-house, post-office, government printing, and internal-revenue services, as well as some other listed jobs. It also says the age limit does not apply to the wife of the superintendent of an Indian school when she applies to be a teacher or matron.

u-cleveland2-18961223.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule III by adding officers and employees in the penitentiary service who are by law subject to classification. It affects those penitentiary officers and employees covered by that classification.

u-cleveland2-18961102.s: This order says the Navy Department rules for hiring labor at navy-yards had been adopted by the Civil Service Commission as a Commission regulation. It also says those existing rules cannot be changed without the Civil Service Commission’s approval.

u-cleveland2-18961102-2.s: This order amends the civil-service rules. It changes how the classified service is defined and adds or removes certain jobs and offices from civil service coverage, including parts of the Ordnance Department, customs service, internal-revenue service, and some Department of Justice workers. It also changes rules for promotions, board of promotion membership, and some exceptions from examination for attorneys and certain other employees.

u-cleveland2-18960507.s: The order places the office of the Interstate Commerce Commission in the classified departmental service and groups its officers, clerks, and other employees into salary classes. It says people appointed with the advice and consent of the Senate, and workmen or laborers, are not included in this classification. It also says no one may be admitted to a classified place unless he or she passes the proper civil-service examination and is certified by the United States Civil Service Commission.

u-cleveland2-18960513.s: This order changes the civil-service rules to include the life-saving service in a rule that already mentioned the light-house service. It also removes an exception for people in the life-saving service from a rule about those serving in the Treasury Department in any capacity.

u-cleveland2-18960328.s: This order revokes the rule that allowed members of the board of pension appeals in the Department of the Interior to be appointed by non-competitive examination. Those positions will now be treated as subject to competitive examination.

u-cleveland2-18960506.s: The order sets new civil service rules and revokes all others. It gives the United States Civil Service Commission authority to make rules for carrying out the civil service act and sets rules for hiring, testing, and classification in the federal executive service. It also bars civil service employees from using official power to affect elections, from discriminating based on political or religious views, and says people who willfully break the rules must be dismissed. The order lists the branches of service covered and says applicants must be U.S. citizens, of proper age, and pass required examinations unless exempt.

u-cleveland2-18960320.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Interior to expand the classified civil service in the Interior Department and the Indian service. It adds certain clerical and school-related jobs at Indian agencies, Indian schools, and the Indian service to positions covered by competitive examination. Indians may be appointed to these jobs on a test of fitness set by the Secretary of the Interior, without Civil Service Commission examination or certification, but they may not be transferred from those jobs to the departmental service.

u-cleveland2-18960328-2.s: This order changes Civil Service rules for the Department of the Interior. It removes assistant attorneys and law clerks from the list of jobs excepted from examination, so those positions will be subject to competitive examination.

u-cleveland2-18960118-2.s: This order amends the customs civil service rules to add another exception from examination. It covers people appointed to jobs that take only part of their time, pay no more than $300 a year, and allow them to keep other regular business or work. It also lists several other customs positions that are excepted from examination.

u-cleveland2-18951202.s: This order changes a civil service rule in the Department of Labor. It removes statistical experts and temporary experts from the list of jobs that were excepted from examination.

u-cleveland2-18960118.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule 5 for vacancies in internal-revenue collection districts. It allows some vacant storekeeper, storekeeper and gauger, or clerk jobs to be filled by temporary designation without examination and certification until a regular appointment can be made. It also allows emergency temporary appointments for a short period and sets limits on how long temporary service may last and who may receive it.

u-cleveland2-18951202-2.s: This order revokes the part of earlier executive orders that allowed special agents in the Department of Labor to be appointed by noncompetitive examination. It affects appointments to those jobs in the Department of Labor.

u-cleveland2-18951106.s: This order extends postal service classification rules to all free-delivery post offices. If a post office is made part of another free-delivery post office, the employees on its approved roster, including the postmaster, become employees of the free-delivery office. The Civil Service Commission must give exams for vacancies in these offices, except for experimental free-delivery post offices, and any revision or inclusion must be reported to the President.

u-cleveland2-18950930.s: This order places Lieutenant-General John M. Schofield on the Army retired list because he reached the age for relief from active military service. It sets his retirement date as September 29, 1895. It also gives him the pay and allowances tied to his rank on retirement.

u-cleveland2-18950920.s: This order sets rules for filling vacancies in U.S. consulates and commercial agencies with set pay ranges. It says openings should be filled by transfer or promotion, by a person who has already served under the Department of State, or by someone who passes an examination. The Secretary of State designates a three-person board to conduct the exams and set the exam subjects and procedures.

u-cleveland2-18950905.s: This order changes Civil Service rules by removing "bookbinders" from the list of jobs excepted from examination in all departments. It affects people applying for those positions in the departments covered by the rule.

u-cleveland2-18950916.s: This order changes Civil Service rules for the Department of the Treasury’s Bureau of Printing and Engraving. It exempts certain compositors and pressmen now temporarily employed there from examination, and says their work must end before March 14, 1896. After that, any vacancies in that force must be filled only by competitive examination under the civil-service rules.

u-cleveland2-18950822.s: This order changes the age rules for jobs in the Government Printing Office. It says any male citizen of the United States who is at least 21 years old and any female citizen who is at least 18 years old may be examined for those positions.

u-cleveland2-18950816.s: This order revokes the rule that allowed compositors and pressmen to be appointed by noncompetitive examination. After this order, they will be appointed by competitive examination.

u-cleveland2-18950805.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule IX for certain subordinate federal jobs. It says people in jobs like engineer, assistant engineer, fireman, messenger, watchman, and similar positions may be transferred to other subordinate positions after absolute appointment, if they are not barred by age limits. It also says they may not be promoted to clerk, copyist, or other clerical jobs, and that printers' assistants and skilled helpers in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing may only be transferred to the operator grade there.

u-cleveland2-18950730.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule I to add one Treasury Department job that is excepted from examination. It applies in the Bureau of Immigration to one statistician and stenographer who may act as an immigrant inspector.

u-cleveland2-18950715.s: This order changes civil service rules for jobs filled by noncompetitive examination under General Rule III. It adds the editor and the photographer in the Geological Survey in the Department of the Interior to those jobs.

u-cleveland2-18950715-2.s: This order changes the civil service rules for transferring employees. It limits transfers from a pension agency in the Interior Department to certain offices and to other pension agencies. It also says a person may not be transferred from a pension agency to a position in the Interior Department if that person would not be eligible for original appointment under the law on apportioning appointments among the States, Territories, and the District of Columbia.

u-cleveland2-18950715-3.s: This order amends Civil Service rules for the Department of the Interior’s Geological Survey. It covers professional experts and special agents hired for short periods, paid at per diem rates, and paid only when they are actually employed.

u-cleveland2-18950715-4.s: This order changes civil service rules for departmental offices. It adds one designated clerk at each pension agency who may sign official checks for the pension agent. It also allows some employees in excepted places to be directly transferred to nonexcepted places in the same office or bureau.

u-cleveland2-18950715-5.s: This order changes civil service rules for appointments at pension agencies. It says appointments to positions at pension agencies shall not be charged to the apportionment, and it allows certification from a register to fill vacancies at any pension agency. It also allows temporary appointments in some cases, but they may not last longer than ninety days, and at pension agencies during quarterly pension payments they may be made for up to thirty days and not extended or renewed until the next quarterly payment.

u-cleveland2-18950715-6.s: The order directs the heads of the Executive Departments to change their civil service classifications. It requires firemen to be included among the employees classified under those rules.
