u-cleveland2-18950715-7.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Interior to change the Department of the Interior’s civil service classification. It adds the officers, clerks, and other employees of the pension agencies to the employees classified under that department.

u-cleveland2-18950625.s: This order revokes the rule that allowed engineers and assistant engineers to be appointed by noncompetitive examination. It says these jobs will now be filled by competitive examination.

u-cleveland2-18950711.s: This order cancels and replaces Customs Rule V for classified customs districts. It sets rules for promotions after absolute appointment. An employee may be promoted on a test of fitness for the next higher class, except for the positions of weigher and gauger. Promotions or transfers to examiner, weigher, gauger, or other grades require passing the exam for that grade.

u-cleveland2-18950613.s: This order sets rules for the classified service of the Government Printing Office. It puts most employees in salary classes, sets age and trade requirements for some applicants, and uses practical examinations to test fitness for jobs. It also sets rules for hiring, probation, promotions, transfers, and reinstatement, and it requires the Public Printer to report appointments and separations to the Commission.

u-cleveland2-18950609.s: The order withdraws certain land in the Territory of Oklahoma from settlement and entry. It sets that land apart for a boarding and industrial school for the Cheyenne and Arapahoe Indians. It also says existing valid rights of any party are not affected.

u-cleveland2-18950528.s: This order directs the executive departments and the Government Printing Office in Washington to be closed on Wednesday, May 29, 1895. It applies to those government offices on the day of Walter Q. Gresham’s funeral.

u-cleveland2-18950528-2.s: This order closes the Executive Departments and the Government Printing Office on Thursday, the 30th instant. It does this so employees can take part in decorating the graves of soldiers and sailors who died in defense of the Union during the War of the Rebellion.

u-cleveland2-18950524.s: This executive order revokes a prior order about how four clerk jobs in the Department of Agriculture’s division of accounts and disbursements are filled. It says those positions will now be filled through competitive examination instead of noncompetitive examination.

u-cleveland2-18950524-2.s: This order changes a civil service rule for the Department of Agriculture’s office of the Secretary. It allows private secretaries to the chief clerk, wood engravers, and certain scientific or professional experts hired outside Washington, D.C., for up to six months. It says those experts may not be reappointed unless the United States Civil Service Commission certifies that they passed a suitable examination and are eligible for the job.

u-cleveland2-18950524-3.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule No. 1 by adding two jobs in the Department of the Interior that are excepted from examination. The jobs are in the Bureau of Education: specialist in foreign educational systems and specialist in education as a preventive of pauperism and crime.

u-cleveland2-18950524-4.s: This order changes the civil service rules on who is exempt from examination in the classified departmental service. It adds limits for certain money-handling and disbursing jobs in the Department of Agriculture, including the cashier, assistant disbursing clerks, and the disbursing clerk in the division of accounts and disbursements. It also makes exceptions for chief clerks and chiefs of division in the Department of Agriculture, and for chief clerks in the Weather Bureau and the Bureau of Animal Industry.

u-cleveland2-18950516.s: This order changes the civil service rules by adding one job to the list of positions that are excepted from examination. It affects the chief of the dairy division in the Department of Agriculture.

u-cleveland2-18950524-5.s: The Secretary of Agriculture is directed to amend the civil service classification for the Department of Agriculture. The change adds clerks, microscopists, assistant microscopists, stock examiners, taggers, agents, and other employees, with some exceptions, in parts of the Department outside Washington, D.C. It also covers all State statistical agents outside Washington, D.C., and all messengers in the Weather Bureau outside Washington, D.C.

u-cleveland2-18950415.s: This order changes several civil service rules so they apply only after November 2, 1894. It says a person appointed to a place under an exception to examination should not be transferred to another place that is not also excepted from examination, unless the rule applies after that date.

u-cleveland2-18950320.s: This order changes the limits of punishment for enlisted men of the Army. It sets maximum punishments for desertion and many other offenses, including confinement, dishonorable discharge, forfeiture of pay and allowances, and reduction in grade for some noncommissioned officers. It also sets rules for courts-martial, including how previous convictions can increase punishment and how summary courts may handle soldiers accused of offenses.

u-cleveland2-18950507.s: This order sets rules for the classified internal-revenue service, including who is covered, how applicants are examined, and the age limits for clerks, storekeepers, storekeepers and gaugers, and gaugers. It also covers how vacancies are filled, how long probation lasts, when temporary service may be used, and how promotions, transfers, and reinstatements are handled. The amendment to Customs Rule IV allows a temporary appointment in a customs district when a vacancy must be filled at once and no eligible person is on the register, but that appointment may last no longer than ninety days.

u-cleveland2-18950318.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule IV for Indian schools. It lets graduates of Indian normal schools and normal classes in Indian schools be hired as assistant teachers or day-school teachers without further examination, if they have the required certificates. It also allows certain senior class graduates from named Indian schools to be covered until July 1, 1896, and says these teachers may later be considered for promotion if they submit satisfactory certificates.

u-cleveland2-18950302.s: This order changes the civil service rules and adds the classified internal-revenue service to the rules. It lets the Civil Service Commission, in its discretion, refuse to examine some applicants who cannot physically do the work or who have been guilty of a crime or disgraceful conduct. It also changes rules on transfers and promotions for certain Treasury and other Department jobs, including messengers, watchmen, pages, and internal-revenue work.

u-cleveland2-18950103.s: This order changes a postal civil service rule by removing one paragraph and renumbering another. It keeps exceptions from examination for certain postal jobs, including assistant postmaster, secretary to the postmaster, cashier, assistant cashier, and capital printers and pressmen, when authorized and allowed by the Post-Office Department.

u-cleveland2-18950212.s: This order changes civil service rules for some vacancies in Departments and post offices that must be filled right away. If there is no eligible person on the proper register, the vacancy may be filled by a temporary appointment outside the civil service until a regular appointment can be made. Such temporary appointments may not last longer than ninety days, and each appointment and its end must be reported to the Commission.

u-cleveland2-18941215.s: This order amends Civil Service Rule VII to let the Commission certify some officers for transfer or reappointment into classified, non-excepted jobs in the departmental service. It also allows reinstatement in the classified service for certain officers who were separated within the past year because their office was abolished or for another reason, if they were not at fault. It does not allow reappointment for officers who came from an excepted place, unless they got that job by promotion from a nonexcepted place.

u-cleveland2-18941204.s: This order changes Special Departmental Rule No. I for the Department of the Interior. It replaces the list of positions in the Geological Survey with a new list of roles, including geologist, assistant geologist, paleontologist, photographers, chemists, engravers, printers, map reviser, and statistical experts temporarily employed.

u-cleveland2-18941117.s: The order changes civil service rules for sea post clerks and railway mail clerks in the Post-Office Department. Sea post clerks must be appointed by transfer from the classified railway mail service or the classified postal service, and they cannot be moved to another department, branch, or place in the Post-Office Department without examination and certification by the Commission. It also removes two clauses from Railway Mail Rule II and allows some clerks on a line, at a transfer station, or on a steamboat to be appointed without examination and certification with the Commission's consent, but those clerks cannot transfer to any other place in the service.

u-cleveland2-18941102.s: This order changes civil service rules for some Department of Agriculture jobs. It adds chiefs of the division of pomology to the list of division chiefs excepted from examination, and it removes the assistant chief of the division of pomology from the list of jobs excepted from examination.

u-cleveland2-18941102-2.s: This order changes civil service rules for Indian assistant teachers. It allows graduation certificates from certain Indian normal classes to be used instead of a required examination for certification. It also adds one normal teacher each at the Salem, Oregon school and the Haskell Institute in Lawrence, Kansas, and says the exception rule will expire six months after approval.

u-cleveland2-18941102-3.s: This executive order changes Civil Service Rules for the postal service. It lists several postal jobs that are excepted from examination, including assistant postmasters, a secretary to the postmaster, cashiers, assistant cashiers, station or branch post-office superintendents, printers, and pressmen. It also says people appointed under one exception may not be transferred to another job that is not also excepted, and it says superintendents of mail must be chosen from employees of the railway mail service or the mailing division of the post office where they will serve.

u-cleveland2-18941102-5.s: The order directs the Postmaster-General to amend the classification of the Post-Office Department. It adds clerks to post-office inspectors to the classes covered by that classification.

u-cleveland2-18941102-4.s: The order directs the heads of the Executive Departments to change their job classifications. It adds messengers, assistant messengers, and watchmen to the employees covered by those classifications.

u-cleveland2-18940725.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Interior to revise the Department of the Interior’s civil service classification. It would include the chief clerk and assistant chief clerk at the Indian warehouse at New York.

u-cleveland2-18940709.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule II and a special departmental rule. It affects the Department of Agriculture by changing which chiefs and assistant chiefs of the entomology and economic ornithology and mammalogy divisions are excepted from examination.

u-cleveland2-18940621-2.s: This order amends Civil Service rules by adding some customs jobs to the list of positions excepted from examination. It affects the customs district of Boston, where one superintendent of warehouses is excepted, and the customs district of Philadelphia, where five chiefs of division are excepted.

u-cleveland2-18940621.s: This order amends Special Indian Rule No. 1 by adding kindergarten teachers to the jobs excepted from examination. It says these teachers may be employed as such, not exceeding twenty in number.

u-cleveland2-18940526.s: The order closes the Executive Departments and the Government Printing Office on Wednesday the 30th instant. This is to let employees take part in decorating the graves of soldiers and sailors who died in defense of the Union during the War of the Rebellion.

u-cleveland2-18940511.s: This order changes civil service rules for some jobs in the Treasury Department, customs service, railway mail service, and Indian school service. It adds certain positions that can be excepted from examination, changes how some railway mail jobs are certified and filled, and allows an Indian nominated as an assistant teacher to take a noncompetitive examination. It also says an Indian assistant teacher who later passes the teacher's examination may be appointed as a teacher.

u-cleveland2-18940511-2.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Interior to revise the classification of the Indian service. It also adds assistant teachers to class 3 of that classification.

u-cleveland2-18940501.s: This order removes the three highest-grade professors of meteorology in the Weather Bureau from the list of excepted places. It also requires noncompetitive examinations for certain inspectors and assistant inspectors in the Bureau of Animal Industry who were employed outside Washington and stayed in service until they could take the exam. The Commission must report the results to the Secretary of Agriculture.

u-cleveland2-18940320.s: This order revokes the exception from examination for the position of clerk to act as appointment clerk in the Department of Agriculture. That position will now be treated as subject to competitive examination.

u-cleveland2-18940306.s: This order makes an exception from civil service examination for one superintendent and up to four teachers needed for a normal school to be established at Albuquerque, New Mexico. The exception lasts for six months after approval.

u-cleveland2-18940120.s: This order revokes the rule that let fish culturists be appointed without a competitive exam. Going forward, fish culturists must be appointed through competitive examination.

u-cleveland2-18940105.s: The order lets the Secretary of Agriculture make a temporary appointment to fill a sudden vacancy in the observer position in the Weather Bureau of the Department of Agriculture if it cannot be filled from the eligible registers of the Commission. The temporary appointment can last no longer than ninety days. Every such appointment and its end must be reported to the Commission at once.

u-cleveland2-18940105-2.s: This order changes civil service rules for the classified departmental service and the postal service. It replaces some clerk and copyist exam rules with a clerk-copyist examination and related special exams, and it changes several rule references to use "clerk-copyist." It also allows temporary appointments in certain post-office vacancies when a regular appointment cannot be made from the eligible registers, but those appointments cannot last longer than ninety days and must be reported to the Commission.

u-cleveland2-18931211.s: This order revokes the promotion rules that had been applied to the War Department under amended Civil-Service Rule VI. After that, promotions in the War Department are to follow Departmental Rule IX, the Secretary of War’s order of March 2, 1892, and any later orders that do not conflict with the civil-service rules or the President’s order on keeping an efficiency record for merit-based promotions.

u-cleveland2-18930911.s: This order withdraws certain lands in Washington from sale and settlement. It sets that land apart as a reservation for Hoh Indians who are not now living on any Indian reservation. It also says any land with title already passed out of the United States, or with valid legal rights attached under existing laws, is excluded.

u-cleveland2-18930819.s: This order amends Civil-Service Rule VIII about transferring people in the federal civil service. It says a transfer cannot happen until after absolute appointment and until the Civil Service Commission certifies that the person has passed an examination for the new place, with a special rule for people appointed from the copyist register.

u-cleveland2-18930616.s: This order approves new people to serve on the board of control and management of the Government exhibit at the World's Columbian Exhibition. The members represent the Department of State, the Navy Department, and the Department of the Interior. It replaces the former representatives for those three departments.

u-cleveland2-18930606-2.s: This order changes the civil service rules by adding certain jobs that do not need to take an examination. It covers some positions in the Department of Agriculture, the Weather Bureau, and the United States Commission of Fish and Fisheries. It applies to the listed assistant chiefs, officers, property clerks, and certain scientific or professional experts hired for investigations.

u-cleveland2-18930606.s: This order changes Postal Rule No. 2 for the classified postal service. It says admission tests may cover spelling, copying, penmanship, arithmetic, geography of the United States, local delivery, reading addresses, and physical tests, with extra subjects for jobs needing special or technical knowledge or skill. It also says no one may be examined for letter carrier if under 21 or over 40, and no one may be examined for any other classified postal service job if under 18.

u-cleveland2-18930526.s: The order closes the Executive Departments and the Government Printing Office on Tuesday, the 30th instant. This is to let employees take part in decorating the graves of soldiers and sailors who died defending the Union during the War of the Rebellion.

u-cleveland2-18930412.s: This order changes the civil service rules for substitutes in the departmental service. It says substitutes now employed may be appointed to regular places by reinstatement under Rule X, in the order they were employed, and they have preference over all other eligibles. The new rule ends when all of those substitutes have been appointed or are no longer eligible for reinstatement.

u-cleveland2-18930508.s: The President says he will stop all personal interviews with people seeking appointments to office unless he invites them. He will still receive people who want to pay their respects, but only on the days and hours set aside for that purpose. He also asks Senators and Representatives not to bring their constituents and friends during their reception hours.

u-bharrison-18930119-2.s: This order announces the death of former President Rutherford B. Hayes. It directs naval stations and Navy ships to fly the ensign at half-mast on the day of the funeral, or the day after the order is received if needed. It also directs guns to be fired every half hour during daylight and requires Navy and Marine Corps officers to wear mourning badges for thirty days.

u-bharrison-18930119.s: The order announces the death of Rutherford B. Hayes and says the public should show mourning. It orders the Executive Mansion and the executive departments in Washington to be draped in mourning, with flags at half-staff for thirty days. On the day of the funeral, public business in the departments will stop, the troops and cadets will be paraded, and special military honors will be given.

u-bharrison-18930105.s: This order extends the postal service classification to all free-delivery post offices. It also requires the Civil Service Commission to give exams to test people for vacancies in those offices. Experimental free-delivery post offices are not included, and any change in classification or inclusion of a post office in the classified postal service must be reported to the President.

u-bharrison-18921128.s: This order approves a survey of land set aside for the Yakima Indians as the "Wenatshapam fishery." It directs that the survey be done under the Yakima agent’s supervision and in a way that does not interfere with the vested rights of settlers or other parties. The survey may vary from the described boundaries if the land’s topography requires it, as long as it covers the whole area meant to be set apart by the treaty.

u-bharrison-18921121.s: The order adds several tracts of land in Minnesota to the Red Lake Indian Reservation. It reserves those lands from entry and sale as public lands for the use and benefit of the Indians of the reservation.

u-bharrison-18921119.s: This order changes an earlier order that had set aside certain lands in Utah and Arizona for Indian purposes. It restores the Utah lands west of the 110th degree of west longitude to the public domain and removes them from that reservation.

u-bharrison-18920923.s: This order changes several civil service rules. It lets certification be made for the reinstatement of a person who served in the military or naval service in the late War of the Rebellion and was honorably discharged, or the widow of such a person. It says this can be done without regard to how long the person has been separated from the service, as long as the other conditions of the rule are met.

u-bharrison-18920916.s: The order closes the several Executive Departments and the Public Printing Office in Washington on that day. It does this so members of the Grand Army of the Republic who work in public service there can join the parade, and so others may honor the Union soldiers and sailors gathered in the national capital.

u-bharrison-18920507.s: This order changes the civil service rules for some jobs that are subject to noncompetitive examination. It adds fish culturists and machinists in the Commission of Fish and Fisheries to that list.

u-bharrison-18920507-2.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule No. 1 to add more jobs that do not need examination. The added jobs are in the Commission of Fish and Fisheries, including the ichthyologist and editor, one scientific assistant, captains, officers, ships writers, crews on the Commission's vessels, and pilots.

u-bharrison-18920505.s: This order puts the office of the United States Commission of Fish and Fisheries into the classified departmental service and applies civil-service rules to it. It sorts the commission's officers, clerks, and other employees into pay classes based on their annual salary or compensation rate. People appointed with Senate advice and consent, and messengers, laborers, workmen, and watchmen, are not included in this classification. People in these classes must pass the proper civil-service examination and be certified before they can be appointed.

u-bharrison-18920223.s: This order changes the Indian civil service rules for transfers, certification for vacancies, and temporary appointments. It allows transfers after absolute appointment from one agency, school, or district to another under rules set by the Commissioner of Indian Affairs with approval from the Secretary of the Interior. It also changes how eligible names are certified for vacancies and lets the Commissioner temporarily fill sudden vacancies in any agency or school during a school term until a regular appointment is made.

u-bharrison-18920120.s: This order amends a civil service rule by adding elevator conductors to the listed jobs. It applies to the departments covered by Special Departmental Rule No. I, alongside bookbinders.

u-bharrison-18911204.s: The order directs each department to put in place a system to keep an efficiency record for all people in the classified service. It says promotions should be based wholly on merit, and that the rule requiring compulsory promotion examinations has been rescinded. It also says promotion examinations, for those who take them, should focus on knowledge of the work and past efficiency records, and that efficiency records should be open to the clerks to inspect.

u-bharrison-18911124.s: This order amends a civil service rule to add one job in the Treasury Department’s Bureau of Statistics to the list of places excepted from examination. The job is a confidential clerk to the Chief of the Bureau.

u-bharrison-18920112.s: This order approves a change to civil service rules so that captains of the watch and lieutenants of the watch can be filled by noncompetitive examination in all departments where those jobs are allowed by law. It affects those watch positions in the departments that use these rules.

u-bharrison-18911016.s: This order extends the Hoopa Valley Reservation in California to include land one mile wide on each side of the Klamath River from the reservation’s current boundary to the Pacific Ocean. Any land within those new boundaries that already has valid rights under U.S. law is excluded. This affects the reservation area and any tracts of land covered by those existing rights.

u-bharrison-18911001.s: This order puts physicians, school superintendents, assistant superintendents, schoolteachers, and matrons in the classified Indian service. It sets rules for exams, age limits, eligibility, and separate registers by district and sex. It also sets how vacancies are filled, how probation works, how promotions and transfers may be made, and how reinstatement and reporting must be handled.

u-bharrison-18911009.s: This order changes the civil service rules so competitive exams for promotion in the classified civil service will be set under regulations approved by the President. It also changes the start date for the civil-service rules for the Indian service from October 1, 1891, to March 1, 1892. In any district of the Indian service, the rules can take effect sooner if an eligible register is ready first.

u-bharrison-18910706.s: This order announces the death of Hannibal Hamlin, who once served as Vice-President of the United States. It directs that the national flag be flown at half-mast on public buildings of the United States on the day of his funeral.

u-bharrison-18910806.s: This order changes the civil service rules and adds the classified Indian service to them. It says competitive examinations should be set up, when practical, to test fitness for promotion in the classified civil service. It also changes several rule sections for departmental, customs, postal, and railway mail service rules, and allows some railway mail clerks at certain lines to be appointed without examination and certification with the Commission’s consent.

u-bharrison-18910525.s: The order closes the Executive Departments and the Government Printing Office on Saturday, the 30th instant. This is to let employees take part in decorating the graves of soldiers and sailors who fell in defense of the Union during the War of the Rebellion.

u-bharrison-18910413.s: This order revokes clause (c) of section 2 of General Rule III in the civil service rules. It also renumbers clauses (d) through (h) as (c) through (g).

u-bharrison-18910403.s: This order changes a civil service rule to add one more job that does not need an examination. It applies in the Treasury Department, in the office of the Secretary, for one clerk in the office of the disbursing clerk.

u-bharrison-18910413-2.s: This order classifies physicians, school superintendents and assistant superintendents, school-teachers, and matrons in the Indian service into four classes. It does not include people appointed with the advice and consent of the Senate, laborers or workmen, or people employed in connection with contract schools. People entering these classified places must pass an appropriate civil service examination and be certified as eligible.

u-bharrison-18910316.s: This order amends a civil service rule to add one job to the list of positions excepted from examination. The job is the assistant superintendent of free delivery in the office of the First Assistant Postmaster-General in the Post-Office Department.

u-bharrison-18910304.s: This order changes a civil service rule to add one more job in the Department of Agriculture’s office of the Secretary to the list of positions that do not need an examination. The job is a clerk who will act as appointment clerk.

u-bharrison-18910221.s: This order changes Civil Service rules by adding two jobs to the list of positions excepted from examination. The added jobs are a clerk in the Coast and Geodetic Survey who acts as confidential clerk and cashier to the disbursing officer, and a confidential clerk in the office of the Assistant Attorney-General in the Post-Office Department.

u-bharrison-18910226.s: This order sets maximum punishments for enlisted men in peacetime courts-martial and says the rules take effect 30 days after the order. It lists punishment limits for desertion and many other military offenses, including absence without leave, disrespect, drunkenness, and certain crimes such as robbery and larceny. It also sets rules for using previous convictions, limits on summary courts, and allowed substitutions for some punishments.

u-bharrison-18910218.s: This order changes a civil service rule to add one job to the list of positions excepted from examination. It applies in the Department of Agriculture, in the office of the Secretary, for the private secretary to the chief of the division of statistics.

u-bharrison-18910216.s: The Navy Department is ordered to close and suspend all business on the day of General Sherman’s funeral. Navy flags at yards and stations will be flown at half-mast until after his burial, and business at navy-yards or stations will be suspended during public expressions of national sorrow so officers and employees can take part.

u-bharrison-18910214.s: This order announces the death of General William Tecumseh Sherman and says the Secretary of War will have the highest military honors paid to his memory. It orders the national flag to be flown at half-mast over public buildings, and it suspends some public business on the day of the funeral. It also directs mourning for the War Department and the Army, including parading troops, reading the order to them, and stopping labor for the day at military posts.

u-bharrison-18910213.s: The President directs that the national flag be displayed at half-mast on all public buildings throughout the United States until after Admiral David D. Porter’s funeral. He also directs that public business in the Departments at Washington be suspended on the day of the funeral.

u-bharrison-18910126.s: This order changes a civil service rule by adding one job to the list of positions that do not need an examination. It applies to one artist in the Department of Agriculture, in the office of the Secretary, division of illustration and engraving.

u-bharrison-18910130.s: This order directs executive departments and their officers to show respect for the memory of William Windom. It also directs the Treasury Department in Washington to be draped in mourning for 30 days, the executive departments to be closed on the day of his funeral, and the national flag to be flown at half-mast on public buildings throughout the United States.

u-bharrison-18910119.s: This order says George Bancroft died in Washington on January 17. It directs flags at all Executive Departments in Washington and public buildings in the cities the funeral party passes through to be flown at half-mast until his body rests in the state that gave him to the country and the world.

u-bharrison-18901031.s: This order changes Section 7 of Railway Mail Rule IV. It adds the words "or until the emergency ceases" after "days," and it applies to the railway mail rule that section covers.

u-bharrison-18900730.s: This order changes the civil service rules for the Department of Agriculture. It adds wood engravers to the jobs excepted from examination. This affects people applying for those positions.

u-bharrison-18900902.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule No. I by adding one job to the list of positions excepted from examination. The added job is a stenographer serving as confidential clerk to the chief post-office inspector in the Post-Office Department, office of the Postmaster-General.

u-bharrison-18900730-2.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule VIII, section I, clause (b). It adds the office of the Solicitor of the Treasury to the places covered by the rule for moving employees between a Treasury bureau that handles customs business and a classified customs district, on request by the Secretary of the Treasury.

u-bharrison-18900714.s: This order responds to the death of John C. Fremont, a retired major-general of the Army of the United States. It says his public services called for national sorrow and appreciation. It directs the national flag to be displayed at half-mast on all buildings of the Executive Departments in this city until after the funeral.

u-bharrison-18900531.s: This order amends Civil Service Rule No. I to add two jobs to the list of positions excepted from examination. The jobs are topographer and hydrographer in the Treasury Department’s life-saving service.

u-bharrison-18900424.s: This order directs the Attorney-General to have a U.S. marshal carry out federal arrest writs in several counties in Florida. If there is resistance, the marshal is to use a civil posse to discourage or overcome it. It says federal officers must be able to carry out their lawful duties and that executive power will be used as needed to protect that work.

u-bharrison-18900527.s: This order closes the Executive Departments and the Government Printing Office on Friday, the 30th instant. It does this so employees can take part in decorating the graves of soldiers and sailors who died in defense of the Union during the War of the Rebellion.

u-bharrison-18900310.s: This order amends Special Customs Rule No. I by adding detectives employed only as detectives in the customs district of New York. It affects those customs employees in New York who work exclusively as detectives.

u-bharrison-18900328.s: This order changes civil service rules for temporary substitutes for clerks, copyists, and other employees in graded jobs. It lets departments certify and hire substitutes when regular employees are absent because of sickness or another unavoidable cause, and it says substitutes may later be appointed to regular grades in the order they were employed. It also says a person cannot serve as a substitute in more than one department at the same time, that substitute service does not count as grounds for reinstatement, and that one special department rule is revoked.

u-bharrison-18900310-2.s: This order changes a Civil Service rule for the Coast and Geodetic Survey. It replaces the job title "general office assistant" with "assistant in charge of office and topography," so the clause now reads "confidential clerk to assistant in charge of office and topography."

u-bharrison-18900129.s: This order changes civil service rules for the Department of Agriculture. It adds scientific or professional experts hired for investigations specially authorized by Congress to the list of jobs that do not need an examination, but it does not include regular Department employees or people whose work is not scientific or professional.

u-bharrison-18900129-2.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules for postal jobs. It adds “reading addresses” and “physical tests” to the clerk examination, and it adds “reading addresses” to the carrier examination.

u-bharrison-18891118.s: This order changes the civil service rules for the port of New York. It adds the chief clerk and law clerk in the Office of the General Appraiser to the jobs excepted from examination.

u-bharrison-18891101.s: This order changes the rules for filling railway mail vacancies. It directs the Commission to certify eligible names from the State or Territory where the vacancy is, with nearby counties or adjoining States or Territories used if needed. It also allows temporary employment of experienced railway mail clerks without examination or certification in a public and pressing emergency, with reporting to the Commission.

u-bharrison-18891029.s: This order changes Civil Service rules for the Bureau of Engraving and Printing. It adds plate cleaners, transferrers, hardeners, provers, pressmen, machinists, plumbers, carpenters, and blacksmiths to the jobs excepted from examination.

u-bharrison-18890820.s: This order changes the civil service rules for the office of the Supervising Architect. It adds engineers and draftsmen of classes 1 through 5, up to ten positions, to the jobs excepted from examination, and says those ten places will stop being excepted after June 30, 1890.

u-bharrison-18890726.s: This order changes the civil service rules to allow temporary appointments in the classified service. These temporary appointments cannot last more than thirty days.

u-bharrison-18890817.s: This order amends Railway Mail Rule II by adding two groups of clerks to Clause 5. It covers clerks employed only as porters handling mail matter in bulk, in sacks, or pouches, and clerks employed only on steamboats.

u-bharrison-18890726-2.s: This order amends Civil Service Rule II for railway mail service jobs. It adds printers, when employed as printers, to Section 5.

u-bharrison-18890618.s: This order changes several civil service rules to allow certification for the reinstatement of certain former federal workers. It applies to people who served in the military or naval service of the United States in the late War of the Rebellion and were honorably discharged, without regard to how long they have been out of service.

u-bharrison-18890610.s: This order changes civil service rules by adding certain jobs to the list of covered positions. It adds foremen of laborers, skilled laborers, elevator conductors, foreman of cabinet shop, and cabinetmakers in the office of the Secretary of the Treasury. It also revises the list of covered jobs in the Geological Survey, including several scientific and technical positions.

u-bharrison-18890607.s: This order says officers and men in the Army and Navy should observe Sunday and keep Sunday labor to strict necessity. It also changes military inspections so Sunday-morning inspection is only of dress and general appearance, without arms. The fuller inspection with arms and all men present is moved to Saturday.

u-bharrison-18890529.s: This order closes the several Executive Departments and the Government Printing Office on Thursday, the 30th instant. It is meant to let employees take part in decorating the graves of the soldiers who fell during the rebellion.

u-bharrison-18890527.s: This order amends Civil Service Rule VIII. It allows a person who has served two continuous years in the Office of the President of the United States to be transferred to a place in the classified service without examination, if the department head requests it and the Commission certifies it. It also changes another rule section to make an exception for this transfer.

u-bharrison-18890506.s: The order withdraws certain lands in California from sale and settlement. It sets those lands apart as a reservation for the Mission Indians. The order excepts land covered by two patents and any other tracts that already have passed out of the United States or have valid legal rights under existing laws.

u-bharrison-18890504.s: This order changes the civil service rules by adding several Treasury jobs to the list of places excepted from examination. It covers the office of the Secretary of the Treasury and certain positions at the Bureau of Engraving and Printing, including the custodian of dies, rolls, and plates, two subcustodians, the keeper of the vault, and the distributer of stock.

u-bharrison-18890417.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule No. I by adding the office of "inspector of furniture" to the places excepted from examination. It also updates the listed exceptions in the office of the Secretary of the Treasury to include the government actuary and inspector of furniture.

u-bharrison-18890423.s: This order sets rules for issuing arms, ordnance stores, quartermaster's stores, and camp equipage to the territories and the District of Columbia. The territories get these supplies on the governors' requests, and the District of Columbia gets them on requests approved by the senior general of the District militia present for duty. It also requires annual returns and forbids issuing more than the amount allowed under the law, and it revokes any earlier rules that conflict with these regulations.

u-bharrison-18890311.s: This order changes the start date for the civil-service rules for the railway mail service from March 15, 1889 to May 1, 1889. It also says the rules can start earlier in any State or Territory once an eligible register for that place is ready. The order affects the railway mail service and the States and Territories where the rules apply.

u-cleveland1-18890226.s: This order directs that part of the money appropriated under the act be used, under the Secretary of State’s direction, to provide transportation to the United States for any citizens of the United States found destitute in the National Department of Panama in the Republic of Colombia. It also says the money was appropriated to help protect the interests of the United States and the security of persons and property of U.S. citizens at the Isthmus of Panama.

u-cleveland1-18890219.s: This order withdraws certain tracts of land in Washington Territory from sale and settlement. It sets the land apart for the permanent use and occupation of the Quillehute Indians, while stating that existing valid rights are not affected.

u-cleveland1-18890211.s: This order amends a civil service rule to add more jobs that do not need an examination. It adds assistant attorneys in the Department of Justice and the private secretary to the Director of the Bureau of Experiment Stations in the Department of Agriculture.

u-cleveland1-18890211-2.s: This order amends a civil service rule to add the position of captain of the watch in the Post-Office Department to the jobs that may be filled by noncompetitive examination. It affects appointments to that position in that department. The head of the department may recommend a person for examination for the job.

u-cleveland1-18890211-3.s: This order revokes the part of a prior civil service order that allowed appointment by noncompetitive examination to the job of inspector of electric lights. It affects that position in the office of the Secretary in the Treasury Department.

u-cleveland1-18890104.s: This order adds the classified railway mail service as a fourth branch of the classified civil service. It also changes rules so people applying for, examining for, or transferring into that service are covered by the same kinds of certificates, examinations, and transfer rules described here. The order also says local boards and customs, postal, and railway mail boards will handle examinations tied to the classified railway mail service.

u-cleveland1-18890104-2.s: This order approves the rules and sets them to take effect on March 15, 1889. In any State or Territory, the rules can take effect sooner if an eligible register for that State or Territory is prepared before that date.

u-cleveland1-18881206.s: This order approves a change to Civil Service Rule No. 1. It adds bookbinders in all departments to the list of jobs excepted from examination.

u-cleveland1-18881113.s: This order revokes the part of a prior order that allowed noncompetitive examinations for seventeen clerks in the Office of the Treasurer of the United States who were employed as expert money tellers. It means those positions would no longer be filled that way. The order says they should instead be selected from the Commission’s eligible registers.

u-cleveland1-18881205.s: This order would add employees in the railway mail service to the classified service and make them subject to examination. It directs the Postmaster-General to revise the Department’s classification to include these employees in one or more classes. It also asks the Civil Service Commission, after talking with the Postmaster-General, to prepare changes to the rules and regulations for that expansion.

u-cleveland1-18881101.s: This order changes Special Departmental Rule No. I for the Department of Agriculture. It lists the offices and jobs covered in the Commissioner’s office and in the Bureau of Animal Industry, including private secretary, superintendent of grounds, division assistants, chief, assistant chief, and chief clerk.

u-cleveland1-18881101-2.s:
This order changes Departmental Rule VII for classified departmental jobs. It says no certification may be made from the clerk or any supplementary register to a department that has promotion regulations applied, if the vacancy is above grade class I.

It affects departments with those promotion rules and the filling of higher vacancies in the classified departmental service.

u-cleveland1-18881101-3.s: This order changes departmental rules for applications and examinations in the classified departmental service. It allows people to apply for printer's assistant in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing if they are at least 18 and not over 35, and it adds that job to the examination and register rules. It also says that when certification is made from the printer's assistant register and more than one vacancy exists, the appointing officer may choose more than one person from the three names certified.

u-cleveland1-18881101-4.s: This order authorizes noncompetitive examinations for certain jobs in the classified customs service. It applies to tellers and three stenographers in the New York collector’s office, and to a Chinese interpreter in the San Francisco customs district.

u-cleveland1-18881101-5.s: This order authorizes noncompetitive examinations to test fitness for certain jobs in the classified departmental service. It applies to assistant photographers in the Department of the Interior’s Geological Survey permanent force and to special agents in the Department of Labor.

u-cleveland1-18881101-6.s: This order changes a civil service rule for people appointed through a noncompetitive examination. It says they cannot be transferred or appointed to another place not excepted from examination for one year after appointment. After one year in that noncompetitive place, they may be transferred or appointed to such a place if the Commission or board of examiners certifies that they passed an examination for it.

u-cleveland1-18881017.s: This order approves a noncompetitive examination for an additional teller at the custom-house in New York City. It affects the appointment process for that position, which the Commission said should be filled by noncompetitive rather than competitive examination.

u-cleveland1-18880814.s: This order assigns Major-General John M. Schofield to command the Army of the United States. It affects the Army of the United States and the officer named in the order.

u-cleveland1-18880825.s: This order approves noncompetitive examinations for assistant jobs at branch hydrographic offices in the Navy Department. It applies to Francis A. Lewis in New York City and Joseph T. McMillan in San Francisco. The order says these jobs need special technical nautical training and are in places far from Washington.

u-cleveland1-18880809.s: The President directs the Executive Departments in Washington, D.C., to be closed on Saturday, August 11, the day of General Sheridan’s funeral. Public business at the national capital is to be suspended that day.

u-cleveland1-18880810.s: This order adds a special exception from examination in the classified customs service for the office of assistant deputy naval officer in the Boston customs district. It applies to that customs office and changes the hiring rules for that position.

u-cleveland1-18880803.s: This order says no new substitute may be employed in any Department. It lets department heads appoint current substitutes to replace a principal or move to a lower-grade place. Any substitute appointed under this order must pass an appropriate Civil Service Commission examination and be certified by the Commission.

u-cleveland1-18880702.s: This order authorizes noncompetitive examinations to test fitness for certain jobs in the classified departmental service. It applies to specific positions in the Departments of the Treasury, the Interior, Agriculture, and the Post-Office Department, as well as jobs in all departments. The listed jobs include engineers, clerks, stenographers, watch staff, librarians, examiners, and other office workers.

u-cleveland1-18880702-2.s: This order adds many jobs to the list of federal positions that do not need to take examinations for the classified departmental service. It covers jobs in the State, Treasury, Interior, War, Navy, Justice, Agriculture, Post-Office, and Labor departments. The listed positions include clerks, lawyers, engineers, scientists, printers, and other office and technical jobs.

u-cleveland1-18880618.s: This order adds an exception to examination in the classified postal service for printers employed as printers. Before anyone is hired under this exception, the Post-Office Department must tell the Commission which post office has authority to hire printers and how many may be hired there.

u-cleveland1-18880605.s: This order approves a noncompetitive examination to fill a vacant teller job in the collector of customs office at the port of New York. The job involves receiving and counting money paid into that office, and the Commission says the position should be filled quickly. It says this approval is not meant to set a precedent.

u-cleveland1-18880323.s: The President announces the death of Morrison R. Waite, Chief Justice of the United States. The executive offices in Washington are to be closed on the day of the funeral, draped in mourning for thirty days, and the national flag is to be flown at half-mast on public buildings and national vessels on the day of the funeral.

u-cleveland1-18880526.s: This order closes the several Executive Departments, the Department of Agriculture, and the Government Printing Office on Wednesday the 30th instant. It does this so employees can take part in decorating the graves of soldiers who fell during the rebellion.

u-cleveland1-18880321.s:
The order asks the Civil Service Commission to be careful in applying a rule that allows certain department employees to be promoted into the classified service after a noncompetitive examination. It says the Commission should create a way to test the merits of these cases and gather the facts needed for review by the Commission and the President.

It also asks the Commission to revise the different department employee classifications and make them more uniform. The order says this should help address cases where a person can enter one department grade without an examination but must pass one in another department.

u-cleveland1-18880301.s: This order places officers, clerks, and other employees of the United States Civil Service Commission into pay-based classes. It says people appointed by the President with Senate consent, people appointed by the President alone, and people hired only as laborers, workmen, or watchmen are not included in this classification. It also makes the classified commission part of the classified departmental service and says the civil-service rules apply to it.

u-cleveland1-18871024.s: This order announces the death of Elihu B. Washburne, a former Secretary of State and former Representative from Illinois. It says the Department of State will be closed for all public business on the day of his funeral and will be draped in mourning for ten days after. It also directs U.S. diplomatic and consular officers in foreign countries to express public sorrow over his death.

u-cleveland1-18880202.s: This order revises the civil-service rules and revokes two earlier sets of rules, while keeping already classified customs districts and post offices from being excluded. It sets rules for the classified civil service, including departmental, customs, and postal branches, and requires most people to pass an examination before appointment. It also bars officials from using their authority to affect elections, from political discrimination in exams or appointments, and from dismissing workers for refusing political pressure or political contributions. It gives preference in some cases to certain eligible applicants, including honorably discharged military or naval veterans and the widows and orphans of deceased soldiers and sailors.

u-cleveland1-18870901.s: This order sets aside a six-square-mile tract of land in Utah as a military reservation for Fort Du Chesne. The land is inside the Uintah Indian reservation, and its use is subject to the Indians' right, title, and interest in the land. It also says the land must be vacated whenever the interest of the Indians requires it, with notice to the Secretary of War.

u-cleveland1-18870825.s: This order directs customs collectors to allow certain foreign soldiers to enter the United States as guests of the city of Chicago. They may bring their personal baggage, uniforms, arms, and equipment without paying customs duties. Customs officers may require steps to make sure those items are sent back out of the country.

u-cleveland1-18870616.s: The order stops the War Department from moving ahead with plans to offer the return of captured Union and Confederate flags to the states. It says the flags should only be examined, inventoried, and preserved for now. It also says any final decision about what to do with the flags should come from Congress.

u-cleveland1-18870607.s: The War Department directs that flags in its custody be returned to the authorities of the states where the regiments were organized. It also says each flag should be given its history, if possible, including the circumstances of its capture and recovery. This affects the state authorities and the former volunteer organizations whose flags are being returned.

u-cleveland1-18870531.s: The order withdraws an earlier offer to return certain flags now held by the War Department to the states. It says the President views that return as not authorized by existing law or by executive action. It says any decision on the flags’ final disposition should come from Congress.

u-cleveland1-18870526.s: The order approves a plan to send letters to governors of the states whose troops carried the flags now held by the War Department. The letters will offer to return those flags. They will also include the history of each flag and how it was captured or recaptured.

u-cleveland1-18870524.s: This order approves setting aside a tract of land in the Wind River or Shoshone Indian Reservation in Wyoming as a military reservation for Fort Washakie. The land use is subject to the Indians’ rights, title, and interest in the land. The reservation must be vacated whenever the Indians’ interests require it, after notice to the Secretary of War.

u-cleveland1-18870509.s: This order closes the executive offices and Departments at the seat of Government, including the public printing establishment, at noon on Thursday, May 12. It lets employees take leave to attend the unveiling of the statue of the late President Garfield, and some may also be allowed time to join a parade or other exercises before the unveiling. It also allows members of the Society of the Army of the Cumberland to be excused from duty on Wednesday, May 11, to attend society meetings.

u-cleveland1-18870430.s: The order suggests returning captured Union and Confederate flags to the authorities of the States where the regiments were organized. It says the flags are now stored in the War Department for safe-keeping. The suggestion would affect the states and the organizations tied to the regiments that carried the flags.

u-cleveland1-18870505.s: This order changes rules for the executive civil service. It sets up and defines boards of examiners for departmental, customs, and postal service exams, and lets the Civil Service Commission add or change those boards. It also requires open competitive exams for entry and, where rules are applied, for promotion. Some jobs are excepted from examination, and certain transfers and promotions still need examination under the rules.

u-cleveland1-18870314.s: This order withdraws certain lands in California from sale and settlement. It sets those lands apart for the use and occupation of the Mission Indians as an addition to the Coahuila reservation.

u-cleveland1-18870422.s: This order sets rules for giving arms, ordnance stores, quartermaster's stores, and camp equipage to the Territories and the District of Columbia. Territories may receive supplies each year up to the quota of a State with the least representation in Congress, and the District of Columbia may receive up to twice that amount. The supplies are issued on approved requests, and the earlier 1855 regulations are revoked.

u-cleveland1-18870211.s: This order sets apart certain public land in the Territory of New Mexico as a reservation for the use and occupation of the Jicarilla Apache Indians. It also says the order will not take away valid rights that any bona fide settler has already acquired under U.S. public land law.

u-cleveland1-18870129.s: The order withdraws certain lands in California from sale and sets them apart for the permanent use and occupation of the Mission Indians. It also restores other described lands in California to the public domain.

u-cleveland1-18870115.s: This order changes the rules for the civil service exam system. It gives the Civil Service Commission authority to set up and manage several boards of examiners for departmental, customs, and postal service exams. It also requires consultation before appointing board members and lets officials use office time to do board duties.

u-cleveland1-18870104.s: This order sets rules for promotions in the customs service in New York City. It says promotions must be based on examinations, with notice posted before the exam, and only people who score at least 75 percent in the written exam can be certified for promotion. It also allows some transfers without examination after six months of service, with required approvals. The Civil Service Commission may amend these rules or replace them with others.

u-cleveland1-18861120.s: This order closes the Department of Agriculture, the Government Printing Office, and other government offices in the District of Columbia on Monday, the day of the funeral of Chester Alan Arthur. It applies to government offices in Washington, D.C.

u-cleveland1-18861118.s: This order announces the death of Chester Alan Arthur, a former President of the United States. It orders the Executive Mansion and departmental buildings to be draped in mourning for thirty days, and it says public business in the departments will be suspended on the day of the funeral. It also directs military and naval honors, half-staff flags, and other mourning observances at military posts.

u-cleveland1-18861116.s: This order puts the statue “Liberty Enlightening the World” under the care and superintendence of the Light-House Board. The board must maintain, light, and tend the statue as a beacon under existing or new rules it sets. It affects the statue on Bedloes Island in New York harbor.

u-cleveland1-18861001.s: This order restores a tract of land in Washington Territory that had been reserved for the Chehalis Indians to the public domain. It also withdraws part of that land from sale or other disposition and sets it apart for the use and occupation of the Chehalis Indians.

u-cleveland1-18860813.s: This order changes the rules for applying for regular competitive exams to enter the classified civil service. It requires applicants to use blank forms prescribed by the Civil Service Commission and to send requests for those forms to the proper office. For the classified customs and postal services, the requests must be made in writing by the person seeking the examination, and the forms may not be given to other people.

u-cleveland1-18860714.s: The order warns federal officeholders not to use their official positions to control political movements in their local areas. It says they should not manipulate political primary meetings or nominating conventions, or use their offices to help choose themselves as delegates or run political campaigns. It also says officeholders may still take part in political affairs as private citizens.

u-cleveland1-18860703.s: This order says the Executive Departments, the Department of Agriculture, and the Government Printing Office must be closed on Monday, July 5. It applies to those government offices because Independence Day is being generally observed on that day.

u-cleveland1-18860504.s: This order withdraws certain lands in the Territory of Idaho from sale and settlement and sets them aside as an addition to the Duck Valley Reservation. It says the land is for the use and occupation of the Paddy Caps band of Pi-Utes and other Indians the Secretary of the Interior may choose to settle there. It does not apply to land where the title has already passed out of the United States or where valid homestead or pre-emption rights already exist.

u-cleveland1-18860424.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in the Territory of New Mexico from sale and settlement. It sets that land apart as an addition to the Navajo Indian Reservation.

u-cleveland1-18860520.s: This order closes the several Executive Departments, the Department of Agriculture, and the Government Printing Office on Monday, the 31st instant. It does this so employees can take part in decorating the graves of the soldiers who fell during the rebellion.

u-cleveland1-18860323.s: This order cancels part of a previous 1883 order that had set aside certain lands in California for Indian purposes. It applies only to the specific described land portions in section 28, township 4 south, range 1 east, San Bernardino meridian.

u-cleveland1-18860412.s: This order amends the rules for the executive civil service. It allows a person in the classified departmental service to be transferred to another place in that service if certain conditions are met, including a written request from a department head and proof of service and required examinations. It also says a person who served for three years as a clerk in the President’s office may be transferred or appointed to any place in the classified service without examination.

u-cleveland1-18860209.s: The President orders the national flag to be displayed at half-mast on all buildings of the Executive Departments in this city. This is to honor the memory of Winfield Scott Hancock until after his funeral.

u-cleveland1-18851212.s: This order says people who are entitled to part of the 400,000 pesetas fund must present their claims to the Secretary of State within six months. If they do not, they will be barred from the fund. Any money left unclaimed after that period will be divided pro rata among the beneficiaries under the original distribution, if they or their heirs or representatives ask for their shares within the next six months. The Secretary of State is asked to give public notice of these directions.

u-cleveland1-18851128.s: This order closes the Department of Agriculture, the Government Printing Office, and other government offices in the District of Columbia on Tuesday, December 1, 1885. It applies on the day of the funeral of Thomas A. Hendricks, the late Vice-President of the United States.

u-cleveland1-18851127.s: This order changes rules for the executive civil service and the Civil Service Commission. It requires applicants to give information under oath about their identity, citizenship, age, birth, health, work history, and education, and it bars some people from examination based on age, prior dismissal, or certain service status. It also sets rules for hiring, probation, certifications, transfers, and some jobs that are excepted from examination.

u-cleveland1-18851125.s: This order publishes a presidential proclamation for the information and guidance of all concerned. It is directed to those who need to follow or use that proclamation.

u-cleveland1-18851125-2.s: This order announces the death of Thomas A. Hendricks, the Vice-President of the United States. It directs the national flag to be flown at half-mast on public buildings, at U.S. legations and consulates abroad, and at military posts. It also orders the Executive Mansion and executive departments in Washington to close on the day of the funeral and sets mourning observances for the Army and military units.

u-cleveland1-18851125-3.s: This order announces the death of Vice President Thomas A. Hendricks. It directs the ensign at each United States naval station and on each United States naval vessel in commission to be hoisted at half-mast from sunrise to sunset the next day. It also orders gun salutes and requires officers of the Navy and Marine Corps to wear the usual badge of mourning for three months.

u-cleveland1-18851029.s: This order responds to the death of George B. McClellan, who was once the Major-General Commanding the Army of the United States. It directs that the national flag be displayed at half-mast on all buildings of the Executive Departments in the city until after his funeral. It affects those federal department buildings in the city.

u-cleveland1-18851024.s: The order details Major S. M. Mansfield, Corps of Engineers, to work with other officers named in an earlier order. He is to work with people appointed by the State of Texas to find and mark the point where the one hundredth meridian of longitude crosses the Red River.

u-cleveland1-18851001.s: The order sends Dr. E. O. Shakespeare to Spain and other parts of Europe where cholera exists. He is to study the causes, progress, prevention, and cure of cholera and report back to Congress. It also directs that his reasonable travel and living expenses be paid from the money made available under the 1885 law.

u-cleveland1-18851001-2.s: This order revokes Special Rule No. 2 for the executive civil service. It also says applicants on any register for the postal or customs service who have been on it for one year or more by November 1 will no longer be eligible for appointment from that register.

u-cleveland1-18850923.s: This order details three Army engineers to work with people appointed by the State of Texas. Their job is to find and mark the point where the one hundredth meridian crosses the Red River, as part of marking boundary lines between a portion of the Indian Territory and Texas.

u-cleveland1-18850806.s: This order closes the Executive Departments, the Department of Agriculture, and the Government Printing Office at 3 o'clock p.m. on Friday, August 7. It is so employees who want to can attend the funeral of the late ex-President, General Grant, in New York.

u-cleveland1-18850805.s: This order changes Rule XIX for the executive civil service. It says that people whose work is exclusively professional are covered, but medical examiners are not included in that group.

u-cleveland1-18850723.s: The order says that, because of the death of ex-President Ulysses S. Grant, the offices of the Executive Departments in Washington, D.C. must close at 1 o'clock that day. It affects the heads of government departments and the Executive Departments in the city of Washington.

u-cleveland1-18850723-2.s: This order tells Army posts to parade the troops and cadets on the day of the funeral and read the order to them, then stop all work for the day. It directs that the national flag be flown at half-staff and that guns be fired at set times during the day. Army officers will wear mourning bands, and certain military colors will be put in mourning for six months.

u-cleveland1-18850723-3.s: This order directs Navy stations and ships in commission to hoist the ensign at half-mast for the funeral of former President Ulysses S. Grant. It also directs a gun to be fired every half hour from sunrise to sunset at each naval station and on board certain ships on the day of the funeral, or the day after if needed. Officers of the Navy and Marine Corps will wear the usual badge of mourning for thirty days.

u-cleveland1-18850716.s: This order sets a special rule for appointments to 150 places in the Pension Office. It says those appointments, except for promotions or transfers, must be separately apportioned in line with the civil service act as closely as prompt hiring and the applicants’ residence and qualifications allow.

u-cleveland1-18850615.s: This order changes Rule XIX for the executive civil service. It adds chief clerks, deputy collectors, deputy naval officers, deputy surveyors of customs, and superintendents or chiefs of divisions or bureaus to clause 8.

u-cleveland1-18850526.s: This order closes the several Executive Departments, the Department of Agriculture, and the Government Printing Office on Saturday, the 30th instant. It is so employees can take part in decorating the graves of the soldiers who fell during the rebellion.

u-cleveland1-18850602.s: This order changes the rules for applying to the executive civil service. It requires applicants to give sworn information about their identity, citizenship, age, birth, health, military or naval service, past work, residence, education, and family members in public service, and to say they are not barred under the civil-service act for habitual use of intoxicating beverages to excess. It also bars people dismissed for misconduct from taking an exam for two years, limits examinations for people under Army or Navy enlistment, and lets the Commission set rules on ill health, physical incapacity, misrepresentation, and bad faith.

u-cleveland1-18850512.s: This order appoints a board to examine and report on which ports most urgently need fortifications or other defenses. The board must also report on the kind of defenses best suited for each port, with reference to armament and the use of torpedoes, mines, or other defensive appliances. It affects the planning of defenses at ports.

u-cleveland1-18850425.s: The order names Major George M. Sternberg as the U.S. delegate to a sanitary conference in Rome on ways to prevent the spread of cholera and lessen its effects. It also directs the Secretary of War to detail him for that service with full pay and allowances, and says his travel and stay expenses may be paid from the stated appropriation. The order affects Sternberg and the departments involved in his assignment and expenses.

u-arthur-18850303.s: This order closes the several Executive Departments, the Department of Agriculture, and the Government Printing Office on Wednesday the 4th. It does this so employees can witness the inauguration ceremonies on that day.

u-cleveland1-18850318.s: This order changes the rules for transfers and appointments in the classified executive civil service. It allows some employees who have served in the classified departmental service for one year or more to be moved to another place if the needs of the service require it and they have a Civil Service Commission certificate. It also allows a person who has served as a clerk in the President’s office for three years to be transferred or appointed to any place in the classified service without examination.

u-arthur-18850227.s: This order amends civil service rules for federal appointments and exams. It requires four names to be certified for a vacancy, with regard to preference and the apportionment of appointments among States and Territories, and it says sex should be used in certification only when requested or required. It also limits how often a person may be certified or retake an exam, and allows some dismissed or separated employees to be reappointed or reemployed within one year without another examination.

u-arthur-18850303-2.s: This order changes the earlier order that extended the boundaries of the Zuni Indian Reservation in New Mexico. It says that lands in the added area that were already settled upon and occupied in good faith under the public-land laws of the United States are excluded from the addition.

u-arthur-18850226.s: This order sets rules to enforce a law for Alaska that bans importing, making, and selling intoxicating liquors, except for medicinal, mechanical, and scientific purposes. It requires a permit to land liquors in Alaska and a license to manufacture or sell them there. It also says violators and the vessels carrying the liquor can face penalties and forfeiture, and it assigns enforcement to the proper officers in Alaska and customs officers.

u-arthur-18850217.s: This order closes the several Executive Departments, the Department of Agriculture, and the Government Printing Office on Saturday, the 21st instant. It is meant to let employees take part in the ceremonies for the dedication of the Washington Monument.

u-arthur-18850211.s: This order amends rules for the federal civil service. It says appointing officers must choose from a list of four certified names for a vacancy, with rules for how those names are chosen and how appointments are spread among States, Territories, and the District of Columbia. It also says sex may be considered only when required by the request or law, limits how often a person may be certified, and allows some people who were dismissed without fault to be reappointed or reemployed within one year without another examination.

u-arthur-18850209.s: This order restores certain lands in the Niobrara or Santee Sioux Indian Reservation in Nebraska to the public domain. It does not apply to lands used for agency, school, or missionary purposes, and it makes the rest subject to settlement and entry on and after May 15, 1885.

u-arthur-18850124.s: This order changes the rules for the executive civil service. It sets up classified departmental, customs, and postal services and lists the offices and districts covered. It also sets rules for applications, examinations, and how names are certified for vacancies.

u-arthur-18841205.s: This order amends the rules for the executive civil service. It classifies certain jobs in the departments at Washington, customs offices, and post offices, and it sets rules for exams, applications, and appointments to those jobs. It also sets a probation period, allows some transfers and reappointments, and says violations of the rules can be cause for removal.

u-arthur-18841126.s: This order withholds a described area in the Montana Territory from sale and settlement and sets it apart as a reservation. It is for the use and occupation of the Northern Cheyenne Indians living in the southern part of Montana Territory, and for other Indians the Secretary of the Interior may place there. Land inside the boundaries that had already been occupied and improved by bona fide settlers before October 1, 1884, or that had valid rights under public land laws, is excluded from the reservation.

u-arthur-18841126-2.s: This order withholds a described area in Montana from sale and settlement and sets it apart as a reservation for the use and occupation of the Northern Cheyenne Indians living in southern Montana Territory. It also allows the Secretary of the Interior to place other Indians there. Land inside the described boundaries that was already settled and improved by bona fide settlers before October 1, 1884, or that had valid rights under federal land laws, is excluded from the reservation.

u-arthur-18841110.s: This order changes the rules for the executive civil service by adding more jobs that are excepted from examination. It lists certain clerks, cashiers, money-order workers, secret service workers, translators, interpreters, stenographers, professional workers, and some division and bureau chiefs. It also says people in these excepted jobs still need an examination before they can be transferred, appointed, or promoted to a non-excepted place.

u-arthur-18841004.s: This order reserves a tract of land in Bernalillo County, New Mexico, for Indian purposes. The land had been conveyed to the United States as a site for an industrial school for Pueblo and other Indians, along with buildings and other improvements for that use.

u-arthur-18840905.s: This order announces the death of Charles J. Folger, the Secretary of the Treasury. It directs the executive branch to honor his memory by draping the Treasury Department in mourning for thirty days, closing the several Executive Departments on the day of the funeral, and displaying the national flag at half-mast on public buildings across the United States.

u-arthur-18840722.s: This order sets a special rule for filling 150 places in the Pension Office. It says appointments, except those filled by promotions, must be separately apportioned as closely as possible to the civil service rule, while also considering how quickly the jobs need to be filled and the applicants' residence and qualifications.

u-arthur-18840718.s: This order sets a special rule for the executive civil service. It lets the names of people who passed the civil-service examination before July 16, 1884 stay on the register of people eligible for appointment for two years from their registration date, unless they are appointed sooner. It affects those people on the eligibility register for appointment.

u-arthur-18840716.s: This order says there was no specific money for the Bureau of Education to take part in three expositions in New Orleans, Cincinnati, and Louisville. The Bureau’s representative on the board is relieved from further duty. The Bureau’s display will instead be included in the Interior Department’s exhibit using money already appropriated for that department.

u-arthur-18840710.s: This order puts the participation of several Executive Departments, the Department of Agriculture, and the Smithsonian Institution in the Cincinnati Industrial Exposition and the Southern Exposition under the management of a board named in a July 8, 1884 executive order. It also extends that earlier order’s rules to cover those two expositions.

u-arthur-18840708.s: This order continues the board in charge of items to be shown by the Executive Departments, the Department of Agriculture, and the Smithsonian Institution at the World's Industrial and Cotton Centennial Exposition of 1884-85. It sets rules for how the money will be drawn from the Treasury, paid out, and audited. It also says an Army officer and a Navy officer will serve as disbursing officers, and each department representative will be responsible for the public property in his care.

u-arthur-18840612.s: This order sets a special rule for the executive civil service. It lets certain people who worked in an Executive Department at Washington before January 16, 1883, and have stayed in clerk or copyist work, be treated as part of the classified service. That can happen if the department head chooses and the person has passed, or later passes, a civil-service examination with a grade of 65 percent or higher.

u-arthur-18840603.s: This order changes an earlier land order for certain lands in the Territory of Dakota used by the Turtle Mountain band of Chippewa Indians. It keeps one township set aside for their use and occupancy instead of another township. The township that is no longer set aside is restored to the public domain and may be sold or settled.

u-arthur-18840526.s: This order closes the Executive Departments, the Department of Agriculture, and the Government Printing Office on Friday, the 30th instant. It is so employees can take part in decorating the graves of soldiers who fell during the rebellion.
