u-arthur-18840517.s: This order changes an earlier 1880 order that had added certain lands to the Navajo Reservation in New Mexico and Arizona Territory. It excludes certain portions of townships 29 north, ranges 14, 15, and 16 west of the New Mexico principal meridian, south of the San Juan River, from that reservation.

u-arthur-18840517-2.s: This order sets apart certain lands in the Territories of Arizona and Utah as a reservation for Indian purposes. It withholds those lands from sale and settlement. Any tracts already settled on, occupied, or covered by valid rights under existing U.S. laws before the order are excluded.

u-arthur-18840515.s: This executive order removes the Jicarilla Apache reservation in the Territory of New Mexico from its reserved status and restores the land to the public domain. It affects the tract of country that had been set apart for the Jicarilla Apache Indians by the 1880 executive order.

u-arthur-18840423.s: This order changes the rules for the executive civil service and the classified postal service. It lets the Civil Service Commission set rules for excluding people from examination, grading, or certification because of ill health, physical incapacity, misrepresentation, or bad faith, and it may require medical certificates in proper cases. It also says no one may be examined for the classified postal service if under 16 or over 35, except messengers, stampers, and other junior assistants, who must be at least 14. It further says no person coming from outside the classified Civil service may be admitted without examination and certification, unless excepted under Rule XIX.

u-arthur-18840513.s: This order directs the people named by several executive departments and the Smithsonian Institution to meet at the Department of State in Washington and organize a board. The board is for articles and materials to be exhibited at the World's Industrial and Cotton Centennial Exhibition. It also names W. A. De Caindry as secretary of the board.

u-arthur-18840423-2.s: This order changes the civil service rules for people enlisted in the Army or Navy. They can be examined under these rules only for a Department job that needs special qualifications, and only with the written consent of the head of that Department.

22.s: This order creates a board to manage articles and materials from Executive Branch departments for the World's Industrial and Cotton Centennial Exhibition in New Orleans. The board includes people named by the heads of the departments with items to show, plus one each named for the Smithsonian Institution, the Department of Agriculture, and the Bureau of Education. It is charged with preparing, arranging, and keeping the items safe, and may confer with the exhibition's executive officers under the President's direction.

u-arthur-18840329.s: This order restores a tract of land in the Territory of Dakota to the public domain. The land had been set aside for the use and occupancy of the Turtle Mountain band of Chippewa Indians, except for townships 162 and 163 north, range 71 west.

u-arthur-18840320.s: This order returns three listed areas of land in Dakota, east of the Missouri River, to the public domain. These lands had been part of the Great Sioux Reservation and had been kept out of sale and settlement.

u-arthur-18840208.s: The order places General William T. Sherman on the retired list of the Army because he has reached age 64. It says he will keep his current pay and allowances, and it affects his active service in the Army.

u-arthur-18840312.s: It directs United States district attorneys and marshals to work against the shipment of explosives to foreign ports. It says they should be diligent in preventing those offenses and in detecting and prosecuting people who have committed or may commit them. It also points them to federal statutes that regulate the shipment of explosives and the punishment for breaking those rules.

u-arthur-18840109.s: This order cancels a previous reservation order for lands in Arizona. It sets apart a tract in California, except land in the Fort Yuma military reservation, as a reservation for the Yuma and other Indians the Secretary of the Interior chooses to settle there. The land is withdrawn from settlement and sale, and any land with valid legal rights is excluded. It also transfers the Fort Yuma military reservation to the Department of the Interior for Indian purposes.

u-arthur-18831217.s: This order creates a board of Army and Navy officers to consider an expedition to help Lieutenant Greely and his party, known as the "Lady Franklin Bay Expedition." The board is to recommend to the Secretaries of War and the Navy what steps are needed for the relief expedition’s equipment, transportation, control, conduct, and personnel. It names the officers who will serve on the board and says they will meet in Washington, D.C.

u-arthur-18840118.s: This order changes rules for promotions and reappointment in the executive civil service. It requires some employees to pass an examination before being promoted, and it allows certain dismissed employees to be reappointed or rehired in the same part or grade within eight months without another examination. It also renumbers two existing rules.

u-arthur-18831205.s: This order changes the rules for applying to the executive civil service. It requires regular applicants to submit certificates of good moral character, health, and physical and mental capacity for the work. It also sets age limits for exams in the classified postal, customs, and departmental services, with an exception for people honorably discharged from the military or naval service who are otherwise qualified.

u-arthur-18831115.s: This order sets aside a tract of land in the Territory of Arizona for the use and occupancy of the Pima and Maricopa Indians. It withdraws that land from sale and settlement. Land with private title, or land with valid homestead or pre-emption rights already attached before this order, is excluded.

u-arthur-18830815.s: This order sets apart a tract of land in the Indian Territory for the permanent use and occupation of the Iowa Indians. It also allows the Secretary of the Interior to place other Indians there as well.

u-arthur-18831013.s: The order changes Army command assignments and says General William T. Sherman will be relieved from command and retire. It also merges the Department of the South into the Department of the East and assigns several other generals to new commands. The rest of the order amends civil service rules, including open competitive examinations, rules for promotion, limits on political or religious questions, application requirements, and certain excepted jobs that do not need examination.

u-arthur-18830717.s: This order sets apart a tract of land in Indian Territory as a military reservation for Fort Reno. The land is within the Cheyenne and Arapaho Indian Reservation and is to be used for military purposes only. The Secretary of the Interior is directed to note the change in the General Land Office.

u-arthur-18830706.s: This order sets aside a tract of land in the Territory of Arizona as a reservation for the Yuma and other Indians the Secretary of the Interior chooses to settle there. The land is withdrawn from settlement and sale. Any land inside the borders that already has valid rights under U.S. law is excluded.

u-arthur-18830630.s: This order sets aside a township of land in Minnesota for the perpetual use and occupancy of the Boise Fort band of Chippewa Indians. It also says that any parts of that township with valid rights already attached under U.S. land laws are excluded from the reservation.

u-arthur-18830619.s: This order withdraws certain lands in California from sale and sets them apart for the permanent use and occupation of the Mission Indians in California. It also says the withdrawal will not affect any existing valid rights of any party.

u-arthur-18830613.s: This order cancels an earlier order that had set aside certain lands north of and adjoining the White Earth Reservation in Minnesota for Indian purposes. It says those lands are no longer needed for the purpose for which they were set apart.

u-arthur-18830521.s: This order closes the Executive Departments, the Department of Agriculture, and the Government Printing Office on Wednesday, the 30th instant. It is so employees can take part in decorating the graves of soldiers who died during the rebellion.

u-arthur-18830507.s: This order sets rules for the executive civil service and limits political activity by government workers. It bars employees from using official power to influence elections or being forced to give money or service to political funds. It creates classified departmental, customs, and postal services, with open competitive exams, age rules, applications, records, and probation for appointments. It also lists some jobs that are exempt from examination and says violations can lead to removal.

u-arthur-18830501.s: This order changes the boundary description of the reservation set apart for the Zuni Pueblo Indians in the Territory of New Mexico. It says the revised boundary is meant to include the lands named in the earlier order, especially Nutria Springs, Ojo Peseado, and the Zuni settlements in the region of Nutria, Nutria Springs, and the Pescado Springs.

u-arthur-18830326.s: The President directs executive departments and offices dependent on them to use customary and appropriate observances to honor the memory of Hon. Timothy O. Howe, who died in Kenosha, Wisconsin. The Post-Office Department and its dependencies in Washington are to be draped in mourning for thirty days. The executive departments are to be closed on the day of the funeral, and the national flag on public buildings across the United States is to be draped in mourning and flown at half-mast.

u-arthur-18830402.s: This order creates a board of Army and Navy officers to study where a Government foundry should be located. The board must report to Congress which navy-yard or arsenal has the best location and is best suited for making heavy ordnance for the Army and Navy, or what other method should be used. It must also estimate the cost of the buildings, tools, implements, and equipment needed for that work.

u-arthur-18830324.s: This order cancels an earlier order from May 19, 1882, that had set apart certain land in New Mexico for the Mescalero Apaches. It withdraws a described tract of land from sale or other disposition and sets it aside for the Mescalero Apaches. The Secretary of the Interior may also place other Indians there.

u-arthur-18830223.s: This order restores a tract of land in Washington Territory to the public domain. The land had been set apart for the use of Chief Moses and his people by earlier executive orders.

u-arthur-18830205.s: This order restores certain lands in California to the public domain. The lands had been withdrawn for the Mission Indians by an earlier executive order.

u-arthur-18830104.s: This order sets aside a tract of land in the Territory of Arizona for the use and occupancy of the Hualpai Indians. It gives the boundaries of the reserved land, using points along the Colorado River, Tinnakah Spring, Peach Spring, Pine Spring, the Music Mountains, and a high mesa.

u-arthur-18821221.s: This order sets aside a described area in the Territory of Dakota for the use and occupancy of the Turtle Mountain band of Chippewas and other Indians of the Chippewa tribe that the Secretary of the Interior chooses to settle there. It also withdraws that land from sale and settlement.

u-arthur-18821216.s: This order sets apart a tract of land in the Territory of Arizona for the use and occupancy of the Moqui (Hopi) tribe. It also allows the Secretary of the Interior to settle other Indians there. The land is withdrawn from settlement and sale.

u-arthur-18821212.s: This order sets aside a tract of land in the Territory of Arizona for the use and occupancy of the Papago and other Indians already settled there. It withdraws that land from sale and settlement, and lets the Secretary of the Interior place other Indians there as well.

u-arthur-18820724.s: This order cancels part of a prior 1875 order that had set aside certain lands in California for the use and occupancy of the Mission Indians. It removes that protection from two described parcels in section 34, township 9 south, range 2 west of the San Bernardino meridian.

u-arthur-18820804.s: This order restores two tracts of land in Colorado to the public domain. One tract had been set apart for the several tribes of the Ute Indians, and the other had been set apart as a reservation for the Muache, Capote, and Weeminuchee bands of Ute Indians.

u-arthur-18820713.s: The order says the Military Department of West Point will be discontinued on September 1, 1882. It also changes the rules for the United States Military Academy so the General of the Army, under the War Department, will supervise the Academy and watch over its administration, discipline, and instruction of the Corps of Cadets. The Superintendent will have the immediate government and military command of the Academy and will make required reports, returns, and estimates through the Adjutant-General.

u-arthur-18820627.s: This order sets aside certain lands in California for Indian purposes. It withdraws those lands from sale and settlement. It also excludes any tracts where title has already passed out of the United States or where valid legal rights have attached under existing federal land laws.

u-arthur-18820526.s: The several departments of the government will be closed on Tuesday, the 30th instant. This is to let employees take part in decorating the graves of soldiers who fell during the rebellion.

u-arthur-18820519.s: This order cancels a prior order that had set aside land in New Mexico for the Mescalero Apaches. It then withdraws a tract of land in New Mexico from sale or other disposition and sets it apart for the Mescalero Apaches and for other Indians the Department may choose to locate there.

u-arthur-18820519-2.s: This order cancels a previous order that had set aside land in New Mexico for the Mescalero Apaches. It withdraws a described tract of land from sale or other disposition. The land is set apart for the use of the Mescalero Apaches and other Indians the Department may choose to locate there.

u-arthur-18820505.s: This order withdraws certain lands in the Territory of Arizona from sale and settlement. It sets those lands apart for the use of the Pima and Maricopa Indians as an addition to their present reservation. Lands already owned by others, or covered by valid homestead or preemption rights before this order, are excluded.

u-arthur-18820505-2.s: This order withdraws a described area of land in the Territory of Arizona from sale and settlement. It sets that land apart for the use of the Pima and Maricopa Indians as an addition to their present reservation. Land that already left U.S. ownership, or land with valid homestead or preemption rights already attached, is excluded.

u-arthur-18820331.s: This order withdraws a described area in Arizona from sale and settlement. It sets the land apart for the use and occupancy of the Yavai Suppai Indians. It also revokes an earlier order from November 23, 1880, that had set apart a reservation for those Indians.

u-arthur-18820330.s: This order changes the rules on breech-loading rifles and ammunition in Alaska. It lets certain emigrants and actual bona fide residents of the mainland ship limited firearms and ammunition for personal protection and hunting, with approval from the collector of customs, and it limits who may sell them. It also grants Fitz John Porter full remission of the continuing penalty that barred him from holding office under the earlier sentence.

u-arthur-18820124.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in Nebraska from sale. It sets that land aside as an addition to the present Sioux Indian Reservation in the Territory of Dakota. The reservation status will continue at the President’s pleasure.

u-arthur-18820105.s: This order sets aside a tract of land in the Territory of Utah as a reservation for the Uncompahgre Utes. It withholds that land from sale and describes the boundaries of the reservation.

u-arthur-18811019.s: The order directs the Army and Navy forces at Yorktown to salute the British flag at the close of the ceremonies. It applies to the forces of the United States Army and Navy then at Yorktown. The Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy are told to give the needed orders.

u-arthur-18811220.s: This order withdraws certain land in Minnesota from sale or settlement. It sets the land apart as a reservation for Indian purposes. The land is for the use of the Boise Fort Band of Chippewa Indians and is to be called the Vermillion Lake Indian Reservation.

u-garfield-18810528.s: The order says the several departments of the government will be closed on Monday, May 30. This would let employees take part in decorating the graves of soldiers who fell during the rebellion.

u-garfield-18810309.s: This order withdraws the unsurveyed parts of a township in California from sale and settlement. It sets that land apart as a reservation for Indian purposes, except for any tract whose title has already passed out of the United States Government.

u-hayes-18810302.s: This order withdraws certain lands in California from sale and sets them apart as a reservation for the permanent use and occupancy of the Mission Indians in California. It says the withdrawal does not affect any existing valid adverse rights of any party.

u-hayes-18810222.s: The order directs the Secretary of War to take steps to prevent the sale of intoxicating liquors as a beverage at Army camps, forts, and other posts. It says to do this as far as practicable and in a way that is consistent with vested rights. It applies to Army locations and affects the sale of liquor there.

u-hayes-18801123.s: This order withdraws a described area in Arizona from sale and settlement. It sets the land apart for the use and occupancy of the Suppai Indians. It also revokes an earlier executive order that had set apart a reservation for those Indians.

u-hayes-18800921.s: This order sets aside a tract of land in the Territory of New Mexico as a reservation for the Jicarilla Apache Indians. It also withholds that land from entry and settlement as public lands.

u-hayes-18800713.s: This order restores a tract of land in the Territory of Montana to the public domain. The land had been part of an addition to the Blackfeet Reservation set aside in 1875 for the Gros Ventre, Piegan, Blood, Blackfeet, and Crow Indians. It applies to the land within the boundaries described in the order.

u-hayes-18800723.s: This order cancels the Fort Harney military reservation in Oregon. It makes the lands in that reservation subject to the order that established the Malheur Indian Reservation, and directs the Secretary of the Interior to note the change in the General Land Office.

u-hayes-18800608.s: This order sets aside a described area in the Territory of Arizona for the use and occupancy of the Suppai Indians. It withdraws that land from sale and settlement. The order covers the settlements and improvements of the Suppai Indians.

u-hayes-18800527.s: The order directs that several government departments will be closed on Saturday, the 29th instant. It says this is in remembrance of those who fell in defense of the nation and to let employees take part in the commemorative ceremonies.

u-hayes-18800306.s: This order adds a tract of land in Washington Territory to the reservation set apart for Chief Moses and his people. The land is withdrawn from sale and settlement. It is for the permanent use and occupancy of Chief Moses and his people, and other friendly Indians may settle there with his consent and the Secretary of the Interior's consent.

u-hayes-18800117.s: This order cancels part of a previous order from December 27, 1875 as it applies to the Agua Caliente Indian Reservation in California. It also cancels part of that earlier order for the Santa Ysabel Reservation, but only for certain land in sections 25, 26, and 27 of township 11 south, range 3 east. The rest of the Santa Ysabel reservation order is not canceled by this order.

u-hayes-18800106.s: This order withdraws a described area in the Territories of New Mexico and Arizona from sale and settlement. It sets that land apart as an addition to the present Navajo Reservation in those Territories.

u-hayes-18790809.s: This order restores certain land in Dakota Territory from the Sioux Indian Reservation to the public domain. It covers the lands within the boundaries listed in the order, including areas near the Missouri River, several military reservations, and parts of old Sioux, Crow Creek, and Winnebago reservation boundaries.

u-hayes-18790614.s: This order cancels an earlier order from January 10, 1879, and sets aside certain lands in Arizona for the Pima and Maricopa Indians. It withdraws those lands from sale and settlement as an addition to their reservation. It also temporarily withdraws some land south of the Salt River that is occupied and improved by those Indians until they sell the improvements and are paid for them.

u-hayes-18790528.s: The order says several government departments will be closed on Friday, May 30. It is meant to honor those who died defending the nation and to let employees take part in the commemorative ceremonies.

u-hayes-18790419.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in Washington Territory from sale and sets it apart as a reservation. It is for the permanent use and occupancy of Chief Moses and his people. Other friendly Indians may settle there with the consent of Chief Moses and the Secretary of the Interior.

u-hayes-18790318.s: The order withdraws certain lands in Minnesota from sale and settlement. It sets them apart as a reservation for Indian purposes. Land that had already passed out of U.S. ownership, or where valid homestead or pre-emption rights had attached, is excluded.

u-hayes-18790207.s: The order withdraws a described tract of land in Colorado from sale and settlement. It sets that land apart as a reservation for the Muache, Capote, and Weeminuchee bands of Ute Indians.

u-hayes-18790204.s: The order directs that the office be run on business principles and according to civil service rules. It says appointments and removals should not be based on recommendations or influence from the President, the Secretary of State, members of Congress, or other influential people. It also says patronage should be kept to the narrowest limits, with only a few trusted people in certain jobs.

u-hayes-18790116.s: This order cancels the 1877 reservation set apart for the Northwestern Shoshone Indians of Nevada, known as Carlin Farms. It restores those lands to their original status.

u-hayes-18790110.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in the Territory of Arizona from sale. It sets those lands apart for the use of the Pima and Maricopa Indians. The lands are added to their present reservation in that territory.

u-hayes-18781029.s: This order sets apart a tract of land in the Territory of Arizona as an addition to the Navajo Indian Reservation. The land is withdrawn from sale and settlement. It affects the land inside the boundaries listed in the order and the Navajo Indians.

u-hayes-18780803.s: This order restores a described portion of the Tule River Indian Reservation in California to the public domain. It applies to the land inside the boundary listed in the order.

u-hayes-18780527.s: This order says the several departments of the Government will be closed on Thursday, the 30th instant. It is meant to honor the memory of those who fell in defense of the Union and let employees take part in the commemorative ceremonies.

u-hayes-18771231.s: This order directs the U.S. Marshal for the District of Rhode Island to take possession of the steamer Estelle, which was then or lately at Bristol, Rhode Island. It also tells the marshal to hold the steamer until further orders and to use as much of the U.S. land and naval forces as needed to do so.

u-hayes-18771102.s: This order announces the death of Oliver P. Morton and expresses public respect for his service. It directs that the Executive Departments be closed on the day of his funeral and says the nation should pay appropriate honors to his memory.

u-hayes-18770929.s: This order withdraws certain lands in California from sale and settlement. It sets those lands apart as a reservation for Indian purposes for certain Mission Indians, except for sections 16 and 36 and any tracts whose title has already passed out of the United States Government.

u-hayes-18770825.s: This order cancels the 1875 order that set aside certain lands in New Mexico as the Hot Springs Indian Reservation. It restores those lands to the public domain.

u-hayes-18770825-2.s: This order withdraws certain lands in California from sale and settlement. It sets those lands apart as a reservation for Indian purposes, except for sections 16 and 36 and any tracts whose title has already left the United States Government.

u-hayes-18770807.s: The President may stop goods or certain articles from being brought into the country of an Indian tribe and may revoke or reject trade licenses with that tribe. The order also bans breech-loading firearms and special ammunition from being sold or brought into Indian country for trade with Indians, and it bans arms or ammunition from being sold to hostile Indians. U.S. military forces may be used to help stop people and property from entering Indian country against the law, and military commanders must help carry out the order.

u-hayes-18770622.s: This order tells federal officers not to take part in political organizations, caucuses, conventions, or election campaigns. It says they may still vote and share their views on public questions, as long as it does not interfere with their official duties. It also says no political assessments should be collected from officers or subordinates, and that the rule applies to every part of the civil service.

u-hayes-18770526.s: This order says the collection of revenues should be free from partisan control and run on a business basis. It says party leaders should have no more influence in appointments than other respected citizens, and no assessments for political purposes should be allowed on officers or subordinates. It also says officers should not be required or allowed to take part in political organizations, caucuses, conventions, or election campaigns, but they may vote and express their views if it does not interfere with their duties.

u-hayes-18770510.s: This executive order sets apart a tract of land in Nevada known as the Carlin Farms as a reservation for the Northwestern Shoshone Indians. It withdraws that land from sale or settlement. The order gives the boundaries of the land and says it contains 521.61 acres.

u-hayes-18770509.s: The order says the several departments of the Government will be closed on Wednesday, the 30th instant. This is so employees can take part in decorating the graves of the soldiers who fell during the rebellion.

u-hayes-18770416.s: This order withdraws a described tract of land in Idaho and Nevada from the public domain. It sets that land apart as a reservation for the Western Shoshone Indians, with the boundaries subject to later modification when the limits are located.

u-hayes-18770503.s: This order restores certain lands in California to the public domain. Those lands had been withdrawn earlier for the Mission Indians. It affects the specific townships, ranges, and sections listed in the order.

u-hayes-18770331.s: This order restores part of the White Mountain Indian Reservation in the Territory of Arizona to the public domain. It applies only to the land within the boundaries described in the order.

u-hayes-18770316.s: The order withdraws a tract of land in the Territory of New Mexico from sale. It sets that land apart as a reservation for the use and occupancy of the Zuni Pueblo Indians.

u-grant-18761128.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in the Territory of Dakota east of the Missouri River from sale. It sets that land apart for the use of the Sioux tribes as an addition to their present reservation. The order affects the land described in the boundaries and the Sioux Indians using the reservation.

u-grant-18770126.s: This order removes a described part of the White Mountain Indian Reservation in Arizona Territory from the reservation. It restores that 7,421.14-acre area to the public domain.

u-grant-18761030.s: This order cancels the 1872 order that set aside certain lands in the Territory of Arizona as a reservation for certain Apache Indians. The lands described in the order are restored to the public domain.

u-grant-18761123.s: This measure prohibits traders or other people from selling fixed ammunition or metallic cartridges in Indian country occupied by hostile Indians or where they roam. It also authorizes the President to take steps to stop special metallic ammunition from reaching those hostile Indians and to declare it contraband during hostilities. The ammunition may be seized and confiscated, and the rule applies in Indian country within Montana, Dakota, Wyoming, Nebraska, and Colorado.

u-grant-18760831.s: The order withdraws certain lands in the Territory of Arizona from the public domain. It sets those lands apart as an addition to the Gila River Reservation for the use and occupancy of the Pima and Maricopa Indians.

u-grant-18760817.s: This order withdraws a described portion of land in Colorado from the public domain. It sets that land apart as part of the Ute Indian Reservation. It applies to the area within the boundaries listed in the order.

u-grant-18760810.s: This order appoints General W. T. Sherman and Brigadier-General M. C. Meigs to a commission. The commission will examine the whole subject of reform and reorganization of the Army of the United States.

u-grant-18760726.s: This order revokes the military reservation at Camp Wright in California. It keeps the land, buildings, and improvements from public sale. The land is reserved for the use and occupancy of the Indians located on the Round Valley Reservation as an extension of that reservation until changed later.

u-grant-18760718.s: This order cancels a previous order that set aside certain lands in the Territory of New Mexico as a reservation for the Jicarilla Apache Indians. It says those lands are restored to the public domain.

u-grant-18760623.s: This order declares the exterior boundaries of the Hoopa Valley Indian Reservation. It withdraws the land inside those boundaries from public sale and sets it apart for Indian purposes in California.

u-grant-18760623-2.s: This order sets the exterior boundaries of the Hoopa Valley Indian Reservation. It withdraws the land inside those boundaries from public sale and sets it apart for Indian purposes. It affects the land included in the reservation.

u-grant-18760520.s: The order says the several departments of the government will be closed on Tuesday, the 30th instant. This is to let employees take part in decorating the graves of soldiers who fell during the rebellion.

u-grant-18760515.s: This order says land withdrawn from sale by earlier orders is still set apart for Indian purposes. It also declares the boundaries of the Colorado River Indian Reservation in Arizona and California. The order affects the lands covered by the earlier reservation orders.

u-grant-18760308.s: This order revokes an earlier order that had set aside a tract of land in Montana Territory for the Crow tribe of Indians. The land described in that earlier order is restored to the public domain. This affects the Crow tribe and the land they were to use for their reservation.

u-grant-18760427.s: This order changes the boundary of the White Mountain Indian Reservation in Arizona Territory. Land west of the described line is restored to the public domain.

u-grant-18751227.s: This order withdraws certain lands in San Diego County, California, from sale. It sets those lands apart as reservations for the permanent use and occupancy of the Mission Indians in Lower California.

u-grant-18751221.s: This order sets aside a tract of land in the Territory of New Mexico as the "Hot Springs Indian Reservation." It is to be used and occupied by the Southern Apache and any other Indians placed there, and the land is withdrawn from sale. Land set apart by an earlier order that is not inside this tract is restored to the public domain.

u-grant-18751123.s: This order announces the death of Vice President Henry Wilson. It directs that the ensign be flown at half-mast at United States naval stations and on United States naval vessels, and that guns be fired at set times. Officers of the Navy and Marine Corps are required to wear the usual badge of mourning for three months.

u-grant-18760128.s: The order sets aside a tract of land in Oregon for the use and occupancy of the Piute and Snake Indians as the Malheur Indian Reservation. It also restores the part of the earlier reservation area that is not inside those boundaries to the public domain. Some lands within the boundaries that have passed or may pass to two military roads are excepted.

u-grant-18751122.s: This order announces the death of Henry Wilson, Vice-President of the United States. It says the government departments will be closed on the day of the funeral, and the Executive Mansion and other executive departments in Washington will be draped with mourning for thirty days. It also directs military posts to parade troops, read the order, fly the national flag at half-staff, fire guns, and wear mourning for a set period.

u-grant-18751122-2.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in the Territory of Colorado from sale. It sets that land aside for the use of the several tribes of Ute Indians as an addition to the present Ute Indian Reservation. The order affects the land within the boundaries it describes.

u-grant-18751020.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in the Montana Territory from sale and sets it apart for the Crow tribe of Indians as an addition to their present reservation. It says the change should not interfere with the rights of any bona fide settlers who may have already located on that land.

u-grant-18751020-2.s: The order cancels an earlier order from February 2, 1874, that had set aside certain lands in New Mexico for the Mescalero Apaches. It withdraws a tract of land from sale or other disposal and sets it apart for the use of the Mescalero Apaches and any other Indians the Department chooses to locate there, except for the land in the Fort Stanton reduced military reservation.

u-grant-18750821.s: The President announces the death of the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Michael C. Kerr of Indiana. He invites the people of the United States to a solemn recognition of Kerr’s public and private worth and his service.

u-grant-18750802-2.s: This order announces the death of Andrew Johnson and says he will be long remembered for his public service. It orders the Executive Mansion and some government departments in Washington to be draped in mourning, and it suspends all public business on the day of his funeral. It also directs the War and Navy Departments and Army posts to pay honors, fly the flag at half-staff, and follow mourning practices.

u-grant-18750802.s: The order announces the death of former President Andrew Johnson. It directs the ensign at each naval station and each United States Navy vessel in commission to be hoisted at half-mast from sunrise to sunset, and it directs guns to be fired every half hour from sunrise to sunset at each naval station and on board certain vessels. It also requires Navy and Marine Corps officers to wear the usual badge of mourning for thirty days.

u-grant-18750727.s: The order puts an Army engineer in charge of supervising the work connected to the grant for jetties at the mouth of the Mississippi River. It says James B. Eads and his associates must get permission from the Secretary of War before taking material from public lands, and they must stop if that permission is withdrawn. It also lets them build needed shops, dwellings, storehouses, and wharves on the military reservation, as long as they do not unnecessarily interfere with navigation or other United States interests. No one else may build or live on that reservation, and the new rules go into effect on September 1, 1875.

u-grant-18750703.s: This order forbids bringing breech-loading rifles and fixed ammunition for them into the Territory of Alaska. It also tells customs collectors to refuse clearance to any vessel carrying those arms or ammunition for Alaska. If a vessel is only passing through or stopping in Alaska on the way to another port, the master must give a bond to make sure the arms or ammunition are not landed or sold in the territory.

u-grant-18750524.s: The order closes the several departments of the Government on Saturday, the 29th instant. It is meant to let employees take part in decorating the graves of soldiers who fell during the rebellion.

u-grant-18750518.s: This order sets the boundaries of the Round Valley Indian Reservation in California. It follows an act of Congress that defined some of the reservation lines and directed the Secretary of the Interior to appoint a commission to report the north boundary. The order applies to the reservation and the lands around it that are described in the boundary line.

u-grant-18750515.s: This order adds a tract of land in Oregon to the Malheur Indian Reservation. It withdraws that land from sale or settlement, except for lands already passed or that may pass to two military road companies under earlier acts of Congress.

u-grant-18750413.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in the Territory of Montana from sale. It sets that land apart as an addition to the present reservation for the Gros Ventre, Piegan, Blood, Blackfeet, and Crow Indians.

u-grant-18750325.s: This order creates a board to test the strength and value of iron, steel, and other metals for construction and machinery use. The board is also told to prepare tables of the test results and arrange for a testing machine to be built and kept at Watertown Arsenal. The funds for these tests will be handled by the Ordnance Department of the Army, and the board will report to the Chief of Ordinance.

u-grant-18750325-2.s: This order cancels the earlier withdrawal of the land set aside for the Crow Indians. It says the Crow Indians have not removed to the country and are not likely to make it their home. The tract is restored to the public domain.

u-grant-18750316.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in Dakota Territory from sale. It sets that land apart for the use of the several tribes of Sioux Indians as an addition to their present reservation.

u-grant-18750309.s: This order keeps in place a board to manage articles and materials for the International Exhibition of 1876 from several Executive Departments, the Smithsonian Institution, the Agricultural Department, and the United States Commissioner of Food Fishes. It sets rules for how the funds will be drawn from the Treasury and spent, and it names an Army officer as the board’s disbursing officer. Each department representative is responsible for the public property given to that department for the exhibition and must account for it until it is returned.

u-grant-18750309-2.s: This order abolishes the civil-service rules under the Treasury Department that governed appointments and promotions. It says future appointments will be made under section 164 of the Revised Statutes. It also directs the Board of Examiners to turn over its books, papers, records, and public property, and says its clerks and other employees will report to the chief clerk for duty assignments.

u-grant-18750212.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in the Territory of Idaho from sale and sets it apart for the exclusive use of the mixed tribes of Shoshone, Bannock, and Sheepeater Indians. The land is to be known as the Lemhi Valley Indian Reservation. It says the tract is in place of land provided for in an unratified treaty made in 1868.

u-grant-18741124.s: This order revokes and annuls all orders that set apart the Tulerosa Valley in New Mexico as an Indian reservation. It restores the described tract of land to the public domain.

u-grant-18741116.s: This order withdraws a described tract of land from sale. It sets that land apart as a reservation for the Indians of the Colorado River and its tributaries. The land added to the reservation lies within the listed boundaries in Arizona and California.

u-grant-18740831.s: This order extends the civil-service rules to several Federal offices in the city of Boston and in the customs district of Boston. It says proper steps must be taken to carry out the order and says the change will promote the efficiency of the public service.

u-grant-18740819.s: This order restores a tract of land in Montana Territory to the public domain. The land had been set apart by an earlier executive order, except for the part already included in land set apart by an act of Congress for the use and occupation of the Gros Ventre, Piegan, Blood, Blackfeet, River Crow, and other Indians.

u-grant-18740701.s: This order withdraws a tract of land around San Xavier del Bac in Arizona from sale or entry. It sets that land apart for the use of the Papago and other Indians who may be placed there. The tract is to be known as the Papago Indian Reserve.

u-grant-18740621.s: This order restores the part of the White Mountain Indian Reservation in Arizona Territory that lies east of 109 degrees 30 minutes west longitude to the public domain. It affects that portion of the reservation and changes its status from reservation land to public land.

u-grant-18740529.s: This order approves rules for the government of the Light-House Service of the United States. It says the rules will be enforced by the proper officers.

u-grant-18740527.s: The order directs that the several departments of the Government be closed on the 30th instant. This is so employees can take part in decorating the graves of soldiers who fell during the rebellion.

u-grant-18740526.s: The order withdraws certain lands from sale, entry, or other disposition. It sets those lands apart for the use of the Pillager and Lake Winnebagoshish bands of Chippewa Indians in Minnesota.

u-grant-18740409.s: This order sets apart certain land in Washington Territory as the Muckleshoot Indian Reservation. It withdraws those lands from sale or other disposal and says they are for the exclusive use of the Indians in that locality.

u-grant-18740409-2.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in the Territory of New Mexico from sale. It reserves the land for the use and occupation of such Indians as the Secretary of the Interior may choose to locate there.

u-grant-18740325.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in the Territory of New Mexico from sale and settlement. The land had been set apart as a reservation for the Jicarilla Apache Indians, subject to the action of Congress. It describes the boundaries of that tract by reference to the San Juan River, the Navajo Reservation, and the Territory of Colorado.

u-grant-18740323.s: This order withdraws the Pyramid Lake Indian Reservation in Nevada from sale or other disposal. It sets the land apart for the Pah-Ute and other Indians living there. The reservation is identified as the tract surveyed by Eugene Monroe in January 1865.

u-grant-18740319.s: This order withdraws the Walker River reservation in Nevada from public sale or other disposition. It sets the land apart for the use of the Pah-Ute Indians living there. The order applies to the reservation as surveyed in December 1864 and shown on the map.

u-grant-18740309.s: The order announces the death of former President Millard Fillmore and calls for mourning for him. It directs the Executive Mansion and government departments in Washington to be draped in mourning, and says all business will stop on the day of his funeral. It also requires military and naval honors, including flags at half-staff or half-mast and mourning badges for Army, Navy, and Marine Corps officers.

u-grant-18740225.s: This order withdraws a tract of land on Hood’s Canal in Washington Territory from sale or other disposition. It sets the land apart for the use of the S’Klallain Indians. The land includes six sections at the head of Hood’s Canal that were reserved by treaty in 1855.

u-grant-18740212.s: This order cancels an earlier order about land in Nevada and sets aside a described tract of land for the use of the Pah-Ute Indians. It also allows the Department to place other Indians there if it chooses. The land is withdrawn from sale or other disposition.

u-grant-18740204.s: This order cancels a previous order that had withdrawn certain lands in Michigan from public sale for Indian purposes. It says the lands in the named townships are restored to the public domain. It affects the undisposed-of lands in those Michigan townships.

u-grant-18740131.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in the Territory of Montana from sale and settlement. It says the land is set apart as a reservation for the Crow tribe of Indians, subject to the action of Congress. The boundaries are described to include the country drained by the Judith River, Arrow River, and Dog River.

u-grant-18740123.s: This order sets up a board to prepare, arrange, and keep safe articles and materials from executive departments for the International Exhibition in Philadelphia in 1876. Each department with items to show would name one person to the board, and the Smithsonian Institution and the Department of Agriculture would each name one person too. One member chosen by the President would serve as chairman, and the board would work under the President’s direction with the exhibition officers.

u-grant-18731231.s: This order changes a previous order that added lands to the Santee Sioux Indian Reservation in Nebraska. It exempts lots 1, 2, 3, and 4 of section 3, township 32, range 4, which had been patented to Thomas J. Quinn, from that earlier order.

u-grant-18731223.s: This order sets the boundaries of the Snohomish or Tulalip Indian Reservation in the Territory of Washington. It describes the boundary line by reference to low-water marks, township lines, and section lines along Steam-boat Slough, Port Susan, Tulalip Bay, and Port Gardner. It affects the reservation area covered by the treaty with the Dwamish and other allied tribes of Indiana.

u-grant-18731122.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in Washington Territory from sale. It sets the land apart for the use and occupation of the Dwamish and other allied tribes of Indians. It also says part of the land south of the west fork of the Lummi River is part of an island already set apart by an earlier treaty.

u-grant-18731122-2.s: This order takes a tract of land in the Territory of Arizona out of sale. It adds that land to the reservation set aside for the Indians of the Colorado River and its tributaries.

u-grant-18731108.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in Idaho Territory from sale. It sets the land apart as a reservation for the Coeur d’Alene Indians. The order describes the boundaries of the reservation and says the Coeur d’Alene Mission lands are not included.

u-grant-18731104.s: This order changes the description of a tract of land reserved for the Pillager and Lake Winnibigoshish bands of Chippewa Indians. It says the added land must be withdrawn from sale, entry, or other disposition. The land is set apart for the use of those Indians.

u-grant-18731104-2.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in Washington Territory from sale and sets it apart for the use of the Quinaielt, Quillehute, Hoh, Quit, and other tribes of fish-eating Indians on the Pacific coast. It also describes the boundary lines of the land included in the reserve.

u-grant-18731029.s: This order withdraws a tract of land in Minnesota from sale, entry, or other disposal. It adds that land to the reservation provided for in the 1867 treaty with the Chippewas of the Mississippi for the use of those Indians.

u-grant-18731010.s: This order says soldiers who deserted can surrender at a military station on or before January 1, 1874, and receive a full pardon. They would lose the pay and allowances due at the time of desertion, and if they faithfully serve through the rest of their enlistment, they would be restored to duty without trial or punishment.

u-grant-18731003.s: This order withholds a tract of land from sale and sets it apart as a reservation in California. It is for the Tule River, King’s River, Owen’s River, Manche Cajon, and other scattered bands of Indians. The new reservation replaces an earlier one for those Indians, and that earlier order is canceled.

u-grant-18730909.s: This order sets the northern boundary of the Swinomish Reservation in the Territory of Washington. It describes the boundary line from Similk Bay to Padilla Bay and affects the reservation’s land boundary.

u-grant-18730906.s: This order extends the Puyallup Reservation in Washington Territory. It adds the part of section 34, township 21 north, range 3 east, that was not already inside the reservation. It affects the land described in the order and the reservation boundary.

u-grant-18730805-2.s: This order directs that part of the valley of the Gila River in Arizona be restored to the public domain. The land had been included in the San Carlos division of the White Mountain Indian Reservation and lies east of and above the site of old Camp Goodwin. It affects that described land in the Territory of Arizona.

u-grant-18730705.s: The order withholds the described land in Montana from entry and settlement as public lands. It sets the land apart as a reservation for the Gros Ventre, Piegan, Blood, Blackfeet, River Crow, and other Indians. The land is described by boundaries in the order and includes existing military reservations excepted from it.

u-grant-18730805.s: This order approves new rules for the government of the civil service of the United States and says they will be enforced as soon as proper arrangements can be made. The rules limit how recommendations for appointments are considered, say removal should not be used just to make room for someone else, and set out duties for the Civil Service Commission and examiners. They also create examination rules, district groupings, and records for applicants and eligible persons for appointment.

u-grant-18730529.s: This order sets aside a described tract of land in New Mexico as a reservation for the Mescalero Apache Indians. It also withholds that land from entry and settlement as public lands.

u-grant-18730521.s: The order closes the several departments of the Government on the 30th instant. This is so Government employees can take part with the Grand Army of the Republic in decorating the graves of the soldiers who fell during the rebellion.

u-grant-18730408.s: The order withdraws the lands described in the third section of the March 3, 1873 act from sale and entry. It applies to part of the Round Valley Indian Reservation in California.

u-grant-18730314.s: This order changes how the Department of State may fill vacancies in consulates or clerkships. It allows those jobs to be filled by transfer, by someone who has already served there to the department’s satisfaction, or by an applicant who has proper certificates and has passed an exam. The change applies to clerical, consular, and diplomatic service under the Department of State.

u-grant-18730509.s: The President announces the death of Salmon P. Chase, Chief Justice of the United States. He says Chase also served as a Senator, governor of Ohio, and Secretary of the Treasury. The order directs that public offices in Washington be closed on the day of the funeral, draped in mourning for thirty days, and that flags be flown at half-mast on public buildings, forts, and national vessels on that day.

u-grant-18730128.s: This order explains that people holding Federal offices may not also hold certain city or town offices, whether by election or appointment, and whether paid or unpaid. It says Federal officers may serve on boards of education, school committees, public libraries, religious or eleemosynary institutions, and as professors in colleges, if the work does not interfere with their Federal duties. It also says they may be officers of the state militia and may do unpaid service in local fire departments, while day laborers and mechanics in armories, arsenals, and navy-yards are not covered as offices. Master workmen and others with Government appointments are covered by the order.

u-grant-18730312.s: This order sets apart certain lands in southeastern Nevada for the use of the Indians in that locality. It describes the boundary using the Colorado River, the eastern line of Nevada, a point one mile north of Muddy Springs, and the one hundredth and fifteenth meridian of west longitude.

u-grant-18730109.s: The order sets apart the lands described in the letter as a reservation. It is for the bands of Indians in California named in that letter, as recommended by the Acting Secretary of the Interior.

u-grant-18730117.s: This order says people holding a Federal civil office should not also hold an office under a State, Territorial, or municipal government. If they accept or keep one of those other offices, it will be treated as a resignation from the Federal office, except for the offices listed as exceptions. It also directs department heads and other officers to enforce these rules for people serving under them.

u-grant-18730102.s: This order replaces an earlier addition to the Makah reservation in Washington Territory. It withdraws a described tract of land from sale and sets it apart for the use of the Makah and other Indians. The order also gives the boundaries of the added land.

u-grant-18721214.s: This order set aside land in Arizona as the Chiricahua Indian Reservation for certain Apache Indians. It also returned the Camp Grant Indian Reservation to the public domain. In addition, it added land to the White Mountain Indian Reservation and named that addition the San Carlos division.

u-grant-18721026.s: This order adds a tract of land in Washington Territory for the use of the Makah and other Indians. The land is withdrawn from sale and its boundaries are described in the order. It also says part of the boundary matches the reservation set aside for the Makah tribe in the 1855 treaty.

u-grant-18721011.s: This order announces the death of William Henry Seward, who served in several public offices, including the Department of State. It directs the Executive Departments to give appropriate honors to his memory at home and abroad.

u-grant-18720912.s: This order sets apart land on the headwaters of the Malheur River in Oregon as a reservation for the Snake or Piute Indians. The land is described by set boundaries and includes all land within those boundaries except land already granted for military or wagon-road purposes.

u-grant-18720527.s: The order directs that the several departments of the Government be closed on the 30th instant. This is so Government employees can take part with the Grand Army of the Republic in decorating the graves of soldiers who fell during the rebellion.

u-grant-18720416.s: This order approves rules for filling civil service jobs and amends an earlier rule. It says applicants must show fidelity to the Union and the Constitution, and many jobs will be filled through written papers and examinations. It also forbids political assessments in the departments and says honesty and efficiency, not political activity, will determine whether people keep office. Some top posts and certain other jobs are excepted from the rules.

u-grant-18711114.s: This order says the Bitter Root Valley would not be set apart as a separate reservation for the Indians named in the treaty. It directs that all Indians living there be removed as soon as practicable to the reservation in the treaty, and that their substantial improvements on the land be fairly appraised. After the removal, the valley would be open to settlement. It also allows any of those Indians who want to become citizens to stay on the land they now occupy, if they meet the stated conditions.

u-grant-18710331.s: This order tells department heads to give leaves of absence to Territorial officers only for the most urgent reasons and for the shortest possible time. It says these officers should stay in their Territories and attend strictly to their official duties. The order affects Territorial officers and the departments that approve their leave.

u-grant-18710314.s: This order directs that certain public lands in Oregon be withdrawn from market for a limited time. The lands are to be set aside to establish a reservation for Indians in that state east of the Cascade Mountains, except those who choose lands in severalty on the reservation where they are now located. The order also notes exceptions for land already granted for military or wagon-road purposes.

u-grant-18700412.s: The order sets apart the lands shown in the diagram as a reservation for the Arickaree, Gros Ventre, and Mandan Indians. It follows a recommendation from the Secretary of the Interior based on a reported selection of the reservation by Captain Wainwright.

u-grant-18700331.s: This order ends the Fifth Military District and makes it a separate military department with headquarters in Austin, Texas. It also breaks up the Department of Louisiana and adds Louisiana to the Department of Texas and Arkansas to the Department of the Missouri. The new Department of Texas is made part of the Military Division of the South.

u-grant-18700226.s: The order says the Fourth Military District has ended because Mississippi’s Senators and Representatives were admitted to Congress. Mississippi is attached to the Department of the Cumberland, and officers and troops in the former district must report to Brevet Major-General Cooke. It also directs the former district commander to finish the records and send them to the Adjutant-General, except for records kept at department headquarters.

u-grant-18700131.s: This order sets apart certain lands in southern California as reservations for Indian purposes. The lands are described as the San Pasqual and Paia Valleys and nearby townships in the San Bernardino meridian area. It is for the Mission Indians in that part of California.

u-grant-18700129.s: The order says the First Military District has ceased to exist after Virginia’s senators and representatives were admitted to Congress. It places Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia, and North Carolina in a new Department of Virginia under Brevet Major-General E. R. S. Canby, with headquarters at Richmond. Commanding officers in that department must report to General Canby, and the companies of the Eighth Infantry in North Carolina are to be relieved and report to Brevet Major-General A. H. Terry.

u-grant-18691224.s: The order appoints Brevet Major-General A. H. Terry to exercise the duties of commanding general of the District of Georgia. He will do this in addition to his current duties as commander of the Department of the South.

u-grant-18700104.s: This order cancels parts of two earlier Army orders as they apply to Georgia. It says Brevet Major-General Terry will, until further orders, exercise the powers of a military district commander within Georgia under the act of March 2, 1867, and later related acts.

u-grant-18691224-2.s: This order announces the death of Edwin M. Stanton, who had served as Attorney-General and Secretary of War. It directs the Executive Mansion and the several Departments at Washington to be draped in mourning and says business will be suspended on the day of the funeral.

u-grant-18691019.s: Written communications about public business must be sent through the department that handles that subject. This includes messages about legislation, claims, contracts, employment, appointments, removals from office, and pardons, and other communications will not be handled.

u-grant-18691009.s: This order announces the death of former President Franklin Pierce. It directs Navy yards, stations, and fleet flagships to fire twenty-one guns at noon on the day of the funeral, or the next day if the order arrives too late. It also requires flags at Navy and Marine Corps locations to be flown at half-mast and officers to wear mourning badges for thirty days.

u-grant-18691009-2.s: This order announces the death of Franklin Pierce and says he died at Concord early that morning. It orders the Executive Mansion and departments in Washington to be draped in mourning, with all business suspended on the day of the funeral. It also directs the War and Navy Departments, and Army posts, to pay military honors, lower the flag to half-staff, fire guns, and wear mourning.

u-grant-18690831.s: This order approves a recommendation about proposed changes to the Santee Sioux Indian Reservation. It calls for some lands to be restored to market and other lands to be withdrawn from sale.

u-grant-18690603.s: This order sets rules for a citizens’ commission working with the Bureau of Indian Affairs. The commission may inspect Indian Office records, visit Indian agencies and superintendencies, watch annuity payments and goods purchases, and give advice through the Commissioner of Indian Affairs and the Secretary of the Interior. Government officers connected with Indian service must give the commission access to records and help them carry out their duties, and any spending must follow the usual Treasury rules and required approvals.

u-grant-18690907.s: The President directs the Executive Departments to honor the memory of the Hon. John A. Rawlins, who died on September 6, 1869. The departments are to be draped in mourning and closed from the morning of September 8 until after the funeral. His remains are to be interred with military honors, and flags are to be kept at half-mast on the day of the funeral.

u-grant-18690331.s: The order assigns Brevet Major-General A. S. Webb to command the First Military District until Brevet Major-General Canby arrives to relieve him. It also relieves Brevet Major-General George Stoneman from temporary command of that district and directs him to accompany his regiment to the Military Division of the Pacific.

u-grant-18690326.s: This order rescinds part of a March 5, 1869 War Department order, except the part that directed General W. T. Sherman to assume command of the Army of the United States. It says official business that needs action by the President or Secretary of War must go to the Secretary of War through the chiefs of staff corps, departments, and bureaus. It also says orders and instructions about military operations from the President or Secretary of War must be issued through the General of the Army.

u-grant-18690316.s: This order changes several Army military division and department commands and assigns new commanders to them. It also transfers Illinois and Fort Smith, Arkansas, to the Department of the Missouri, and adds the First Military District to the Military Division of the Atlantic. The Department of Washington will be discontinued and merged into the Department of the East, and the Department of the Cumberland will later be discontinued and its states added to other departments.

u-grant-18690309.s: This order assigns Brevet Major-General Adelbert Ames to command the Fourth Military District. It says he is to serve according to his brevet rank.

u-grant-18690308.s: This order puts General William T. Sherman in command of the Army of the United States. It says the chiefs of staff corps, departments, and bureaus must report to him and follow his immediate orders. It also says official business that needs action by the President or Secretary of War will go through the General of the Army.

u-grant-18690305.s: This order changes command assignments in the Army and tells several officers to take new posts. It assigns officers to command the Department of the South, the Military Division of the Atlantic, the Department of Louisiana, the Department of Dakota, the First Military District, the Fourth Military District, the Fifth Military District, and the Department of Washington. It also directs some officers to turn over their current commands, move their headquarters, or return to their regiments.

u-ajohnson-18681104.s: The order assigns Brevet Major-General E. R. S. Canby to command the Fifth Military District and the Military Department of Texas, which consists of the State of Texas. It tells him to give up his current command and take the new one without unnecessary delay. It also says he may use the powers given by acts of Congress to district commanders and military department officers when needed to carry out the laws. Brevet Major-General J. J. Reynolds is relieved from command of the Fifth Military District.

u-ajohnson-18681010.s: This order publishes constitutional and legal rules about choosing the President and Vice President. It also says military and naval officers and other people in U.S. service must not interfere with elections in any state. The rules cover how electors are appointed, how they vote, and how the votes are counted.

u-ajohnson-18680912.s: This order assigns Brevet Major-General L. H. Rousseau to duty according to his brevet rank of major-general when he assumes command. It also revokes an earlier order for Brevet Major-General R. C. Buchanan and assigns him to duty according to his brevet rank of brigadier-general so he may command the District of Louisiana.

u-ajohnson-18680728.s:
The order says several Southern states had complied with the Reconstruction Acts, so the military districts there were changed and new departments were set up. It also says the Second and Third Military Districts ended, and other districts were reduced or reassigned to different commanders.

The order also establishes Sitka as the port of entry for Alaska. It prohibits the import and use of firearms, ammunition, and distilled spirits in Alaska, except for limited shipments to Sitka under rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

6.s: The proclamation announces that Alabama’s legislature ratified the proposed Fourteenth Amendment to the Constitution. It is issued under an act of Congress that required the President to make that announcement after receiving official notice.

u-ajohnson-18680713.s: This order assigns Brigadier and Brevet Major-General Irvin McDowell to command the Department of the East. It also moves the department headquarters from Philadelphia to New York City.

u-ajohnson-18680630.s: This order relieves Brevet Major-General Irvin McDowell from command of the Fourth Military District and requires him to report to the War Department without delay. It assigns Brevet Major-General Alvan C. Gillem to command the Fourth Military District and directs him to take command without delay.

u-ajohnson-18680603.s: This order announces the death of former President James Buchanan. It directs thirty-minute gun salutes at navy-yards, naval stations, and on board flagships at set times after the order is received. It also directs flags at navy-yards, naval stations, marine barracks, and naval vessels in commission to be flown at half-mast until after the funeral.

u-ajohnson-18680603-2.s: This order announces the death of James Buchanan and says the nation will mourn his loss. It directs the Executive Departments to be placed in mourning and to stop business on the day of the funeral. It also requires the War and Navy Departments to give military and naval honors, and tells troops at each military post to parade, hear the order read, and stop work for the day.

u-ajohnson-18680528.s: This order lets people employed in the Executive Departments who want to take part in the ceremonies be absent from their duties on Saturday, if it is consistent with law and the public interests. It applies to those government employees who wish to join their fellow-citizens in honoring the memory of the men buried in the national cemeteries.

u-ajohnson-18680601.s: This order relieves Major-General John M. Schofield from command of the First Military District and names him Secretary for the Department of War. It assigns Brevet Major-General George Stoneman to command the First District and the Military Department of Virginia. The Secretary of War is told to give the needed instructions to carry out the order.

u-ajohnson-18680328.s: This order relieves Major-General W. S. Hancock from command of the Fifth Military District. It assigns him to command of the Military Division of the Atlantic, which was created by earlier General Orders.

u-ajohnson-18680221.s: This order authorizes Lorenzo Thomas to act as Secretary of War after Edwin M. Stanton is removed from that office. It also tells Stanton to turn over the records, books, papers, and other public property in his custody and charge.

u-ajohnson-18680221-2.s: This order removes Edwin M. Stanton from his job as Secretary of War. It also tells him to turn over all records, books, papers, and other public property in his custody to Lorenzo Thomas, who is authorized to act as Secretary of War ad interim.

u-ajohnson-18680212.s: This order creates a military division called the Military Division of the Atlantic. It is to include the Department of the Lakes, the Department of the East, and the Department of Washington, and it is to be commanded by Lieutenant-General William T. Sherman with headquarters in Washington. It also says no officer should be permanently assigned to command the Military Division of the Missouri until further orders from the President, and Major-General P. H. Sheridan will do those duties temporarily.

u-ajohnson-18671228.s: This order changes command in the Third and Fourth Military Districts and in the Department of California. It relieves and assigns named Army officers to those commands and tells them where to report. It also says the officers commanding the military districts may use the powers given to district commanders and military-department commanders by Congress.

u-ajohnson-18671115.s: This order sets aside certain lands in Nebraska near the Sioux Indian Reservation for the use of the Santee Sioux Indians. It also withdraws those tracts from sale and market. Another tract that was already part of the reservation is restored to market.

u-ajohnson-18671217.s: This order says written communications about public business should be sent first to the head of the department that handles the subject. It covers suggestions for legislation, claims, contracts, employment, appointments, removals from office, and pardons. It applies to people sending these communications to the executive department of the government.

u-ajohnson-18670904.s: The heads of the executive departments are instructed to give each person holding an appointment in their department an official copy of the President’s proclamation. It also directs those people to strictly follow its requirements for support of the Constitution and faithful execution of the laws.

u-ajohnson-18670826-2.s: This order assigns Brevet Major-General Edward R. S. Canby to command the Second Military District and the Military Department of the South, which includes North Carolina and South Carolina. It relieves Major-General Daniel E. Sickles from command of the Second Military District. It also says Canby may use the powers given by Congress to district commanders and military department officers when needed to faithfully execute the laws.

u-ajohnson-18670826.s: This order changes Army commands because Major-General George H. Thomas is in poor health. It assigns Major-General Winfield S. Hancock to the Fifth Military District and the military department for Louisiana and Texas, and it directs Major-General P. H. Sheridan to turn over his current command and go to Fort Leavenworth. Major-General George H. Thomas is to remain in command of the Department of the Cumberland until further orders.

u-ajohnson-18670817.s: This order assigns Major-General George H. Thomas to command the Fifth Military District. It also assigns Major-General P. H. Sheridan to the Department of the Missouri and Major-General Winfield S. Hancock to the Department of the Cumberland. The Secretary of War is directed to give the needed instructions to carry out the order.

u-ajohnson-18670812.s: The order authorizes General Ulysses S. Grant to act as Secretary of War while Edwin M. Stanton is suspended. It also directs the Secretary of War to transfer all records, books, papers, and other public property in his custody and charge to Grant.

u-ajohnson-18670812-2.s: This order suspends Edwin M. Stanton from his office as Secretary of War and says he must stop carrying out the duties of that office. It also directs him to turn over all records, books, and other property in his custody to General Ulysses S. Grant. Grant is authorized to act as Secretary of War on an interim basis.

u-ajohnson-18670620.s: This order gives military commanders instructions on how to apply the reconstruction acts for voter registration and elections. It says who can register and vote, including rules about citizenship, residence, age, and who is disqualified because of past officeholding and participation in rebellion. It also says the registration and election boards must use the registration list, accept votes by ballot, and keep records of the election.

u-ajohnson-18670315.s: The President directs a change in the assignment of commanders of districts under the act of Congress for the more efficient government of the rebel States. Brevet Major-General John Pope is assigned to command the Third District, which includes Georgia, Florida, and Alabama. Major-General George H. Thomas is assigned to command the Department of the Cumberland.

u-ajohnson-18670311.s: The order divides Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Florida, Alabama, Mississippi, Arkansas, Louisiana, and Texas into military districts. It names commanders for each district and gives them the powers of departmental commanders.

u-ajohnson-18661102.s: The President says there is reason to fear an insurrection in Baltimore around an upcoming election. He says the United States might be called on to help under acts of Congress if that happens. He also says he does not want any military action that would interfere with free voting or local matters, and he asks Secretary of War Edwin M. Stanton to bring the matter to General Grant for any needed preparation and precautions.

u-ajohnson-18661101.s: The order says the troops then stationed in the Military Department of Washington were not enough to protect the seat of Government. It asks the Secretary of War to take measures to make the seat of Government safe and discourage any attempt by insurgent or other illegal combinations to seize it.

u-ajohnson-18661030.s: The order relieves General Ulysses S. Grant from the duties named in a prior letter and gives those duties to William T. Sherman. It also directs the Secretary of War to give Sherman copies of the special orders and instructions mentioned. Sherman is told to begin his duties without delay.

u-ajohnson-18661026.s: The order directs the Secretary of War to ask General Grant to go to the Mexican frontier or, if he thinks best, to travel with the U.S. minister to Mexico. Grant is to help the minister with advice while carrying out instructions from the Secretary of State. He is also to report to the Secretary of War on matters he thinks should be shared with the department.

u-ajohnson-18660720.s: This order reserves certain townships in Nebraska from sale and sets them apart as an Indian reservation for the use of Sioux Indians. It also names the specific township areas covered by the reservation.

u-ajohnson-18660922.s: This order reserves a tract of land from sale and sets it apart for Indian purposes. It applies to parts of sections 2 and 3 in township 14 north, range 11 west in Washington Territory.

u-ajohnson-18660618.s: The President announces the death of Lewis Cass. The executive departments are directed to give appropriate honors to his memory at home and abroad wherever the national name and authority are acknowledged.

u-ajohnson-18660605.s: This order directs U.S. district attorneys and marshals to arrest prominent, leading, or conspicuous people called “Fenians” if there is probable cause to believe they have broken the United States neutrality laws. It affects people identified as Fenians who may have violated those laws.

u-ajohnson-18660529.s: This order announces the death of Winfield Scott, who was the late Lieutenant-General of the Army. It says the Executive Departments of the Government will be closed on the day set for his funeral. The heads of the War and Navy Departments are told to give orders for appropriate honors to his memory.

u-ajohnson-18660501.s: This order says that when civilians commit offenses and civil courts are available to try them, their cases should be sent to the proper civil authorities instead of military courts-martial or commissions. It does not apply to camp followers, contractors, or other persons named in the cited laws. It also says that people and offenses covered by the Rules and Articles of War and the cited acts of Congress will still be tried and punished by military tribunals.

u-ajohnson-18660413.s: This order directs that public offices be closed the next day in commemoration of Abraham Lincoln’s assassination. It affects public offices and the people who use them.

u-ajohnson-18660407.s: This order directs federal departments and related public service branches to give preference in appointments to honorably discharged soldiers and sailors who have the proper qualifications. It gives special preference to those disabled by wounds or diseases received in the line of duty. It also says these veterans should be preferred for promotions when they are equally eligible and qualified.

u-ajohnson-18651124.s: The order tells people claiming rewards for the arrest of John Wilkes Booth, Lewis Payne, G. A. Atzerodt, David E. Herold, or Jefferson Davis to file their claims and proof with the Adjutant-General before January 1. It also revokes the rewards offered for the arrest of Jacob Thompson, Beverley Tucker, George N. Sanders, William G. Cleary, and John H. Surratt.

u-ajohnson-18660227.s: This order withdraws certain lands in Nebraska Territory from the market and keeps them in reserve. It is for the purpose of setting those townships apart as a reservation for the Santee Sioux Indians now at Crow Creek, Dakota. The lands are to be held until Congress acts.

u-ajohnson-18651011.s: The order releases John A. Campbell, John H. Reagan, Alexander H. Stephens, George A. Trenholm, and Charles Clark from close custody on parole. They must appear at a time and place the President may choose if charges are brought, and they must stay in the states named for each of them until further orders. If the President pardons any of them, that person's parole ends.

u-ajohnson-18651111.s: This order directs civil and military government agents in Alabama to transfer the use and custody of certain property, except cotton, to the assistant commissioner of the Bureau of Refugees, Freedmen, and Abandoned Lands for Alabama.
